reviews.comment: She is a great professor but she refuses to record lectures which I feel is very important for a hard class

Dr. Bahamonde was very kind and professional throughout the entire quarter, and clearly enjoys teaching chemistry; she was very, very soft spoken though so classes seemed to drag on at times. The class was hard but, she gave students lots of practice problems to work on concepts. STAY ON TOP OF STUDYING and this class is an easy pass (or higher)
This was the hardest class I've ever taken and the professor did not make it fun.
Wish she made practice exams other than problem sets. Can be a tricky class, and she is approachable. I took the final, but heard the midterm was harder.

shes one of this best professors I have had. approachable/ easy to access in office hours. lectures are content heavy but she is clear on what is/isnt on the exams. exam gradingnis weird, 1 midterm and the option to take midterm 2 or the final. her exams are short, dense but simple. average for the final was 37%. need 35% is a C- in the course.

Great Prof. IF u want any chance of getting a good grade just take the risk and take the final. Persevere adapt and overcome by taking that 94% final. Be the best version of yourself. Show them how great you are.

Be a risk taker. Take the final and gamble everything. You are only as good as you believe yourself to be. You miss 100% of the shots that you don't take. Do not consider the future with failure in mind, but with the desire to succeed. Dear basketball.

She's really funny, nice, and does not gatekeep what will be on the tests. If something doesn't make sense, she'll re-explain during lecture or in office hours. Anything she'll test you on will literally be in either her lecture notes or her problem sets. So yeah, you kinda gotta put in the effort, but it's not impossible.

final can either be worth 47% of your grade or 94%. grade based on either 1 midterm and final, or just the final. be prepared to teach yourself the majority of the content, handwriting is pretty illegible so if you don't go to class and look at her uploaded slides, you will be confused. The only practice given is 30 question problem sets
Problem sets are nothing like exams, most points for the exam are explaining why versus the product and the mechanisms.
She is just an amazing professor nothing else to say
Unbelievably good Ochem professor. Super approachable during office hours and tests are similar to her practice problems. Lecture notes are clear/concise.

Maybe it was because she doesn't usually teach Chem008A but when I took it, I had to rely on the slides as she sometimes went on tangents and was kind of hard to understand. I was still clueless in the end was surprised I passed.
Bahamonde is such an understanding professor. Take advantage of her office hours, and do not be scared to ask for help! Gives helpful practice problems that reflect the exams

Super nice professor & pretty good at teaching, but tests are SO HARD. Ur whole grade is made up of 2 tests which are all free-response. The avg on the final was 34% - I studied a lot & still had a rly hard time. She also doesn't curve like other CNAS teachers, has a set grading scale. Has high expectations & expects u to memorize all mechanisms
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: As a transfer student, I can say that professor Bahamonde is a really good Ochem professor. To get a good grade, go to her lectures, go to her office hours and write down all the mechanisms till you can do it with your eyes closed. She also provided us with problem sets that somewhat reflected her tests. if you study, you will be fine.

You MUST go to office hours and practice the optional posted problems. When I took her class I would do the practice problems before office hours then go and finish the difficult ones with her help. 6 tests with 3-6 problems each, typically 2 minutes per problem with some exceptions. Do well on the tests so you don't have to take the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: by far my favorite chem prof ive taken at UCR so far. she was very clear in her grading criteria and if you knew everything then you would do fine on the tests. for her first year teaching she was a great lecturer and also super sweet. grade is 100% dependent on tests though so don't underestimate the class and it gradually got difficult.

Professor Bahamonde was fair throughout the quarter. There were chapter tests instead of midterms with about 4-5 questions on them and 10-20 mins to finish, depending on how time-consuming the questions were and the final was optional. If you're confident in being able to solve any ochem problem promptly then I would recommend this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Jia is a generally good professor, but a significant portion of his lectures are not tested. He is reachable by email and always willing to help outside of class. Curve is not very good but midterms/final are not extremely difficult. He tries to relate the content to real life examples that helps you understand the material.

lectures are not helpful i never referred to the slides. in order to fully understand the concepts AND math you need to read the txtbk and do the pp. do not rely on txtbk for quizzes the readings and pp do not match with the lectures. discussion slides are the quiz. i've learned everything from my TA Ethan and the txtbk. all exams are equal
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He's a very nice professor and is always willing to help explain concepts after class or during office hours. The only problem is that his lecturing style was a little hard to follow sometimes, but the content is easy enough to review on your own with the slides. Practice exams are pretty similar to the real ones

Very sweet prof. Sometimes hard to follow in lecture. Makes it very clear what math you need to know, but not concepts. Expects you to read the textbook. Lecture slides aren't great if you don't go/take notes. Exams all weighted the same. Lots of office hours. Bonus pts on each exam. Curve helps most people pass, but doesn't widen the A range much.

Great professor. 2 midterms noncumulative, 1 final cumulative, all exams MCQ. Discussion quizzes are based on suggested HW, but HW is optional. Quizzes and HW are very helpful for exams (one appeared word-for-word on final). XC on all exams & some bonus here and there if you attend lecture.  Lectures are great and useful; highly suggest this class.

Professor Jia is really kind! There are optional readings, and it is really easy to self-study. Discussion sessions have short quizzes, and were super helpful. Practice midterms look a lot like the midterm. Midterms are challenging but fair multiple choice, 25/28 is a 100%, and the class averaged 80%. Overall a great professor!

Professor Jia was the sweetest most caring professor I had at UCR who really cared about the success of his students. Genetics is a difficult class but Professor Jia made the class very enjoyable. His tests were very fair, and there was also a very generous curve at the end of the class. Highly recommend Professor Jia.

Great prof! Clear grading scale & tells you what lectures are covered on what dates. Constantly tells us what to expect on exams, virtually no surprises on exam day. Some concepts tough to understand & require practice but nothing too difficult. Caring prof, makes genetics fun to learn. Won't know grade until end of quarter after he curves though.

If you're okay with not knowing your grade the entire quarter, learning all the material on your own and getting proctored during every exam, then this is the class for you. Prof Jia didn't even give us a grading scale or anything to base off of. Many students are failing his class and when asked if he's gonna curve he says "Don't know."

He was a great teacher and explained the material well. BUT he changed the grading curve the day after our final and everyones grade was shifted by 2 grades (from A to B+). He didnt warn his students and did it to satisfy the univ grading scale. He blindsided the class. If you take him plan on doing better by at least 25 points above his scale.

Professor Jia is kind and really cares about his students. He tells you what to expect on his exams and his quizzes are straight forward. He tests from his notes so a book is not mandatory although the hw problems in the book can give you good practice. He is generous with extra credit and made genetics one of my favorite classes. Take him!!!

This is the sweetest professor I have ever had! Really wants students to do well in his class, and gives a ton of extra credit. He's an ok lecturer (he sometimes gets sidetracked or just reads off the slides) but he tells you exactly what is going to be on his easy exams. Homework is optional but he uses them for the exam. Doesn't curve the class.

For Bio 102: Intro to Genetics: Best professor I've ever had at UCR! Great lecturer, big sense of humor, made class enjoyable, Professor Jia made sure all students understood the material before moving on. Gives a ton of extra credit just for answering a question in class. Great in office hours. 10/10 would take classes with Professor Jia again.
His TA does all the work. Readings are interesting but I wouldn't take him again.

Funny guy, clearly loves what he does. Gets very mad about laptops/students not paying attention. Extra credit grammar test. 4 essays, 2 creative 2 about books. Must be in class to understand in class assignments, no excused absences no matter what. 3 hr lecture but gives breaks. Put in effort and you will do well, go to lecture. Annoying canvas.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The previous reviews are kind of outdated but Professor Aslan is a great professor. His TA's grade everything but he is very reachable through office hours. Go to lecture or create a discord with people who go to lecture. He does pop grammar quizzes and during the final week he gives an extra credit grammar quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Aslan is clearly passionate about writing and he was pretty flexible, lectures were pretty interesting but it kind of just felt like another intro to creative writing class and there was nothing about him outstanding enough to give a 5. Average amount of work, a couple weekly readings and a few bigger writing assignments.
He supports terrorist regime in Iran, he should not be even working at UCR!!
Pretty smart in his field but unyielding and egotistical. Lectures drag on and pretty rude up close.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Reza is a great teacher and has a good sense of humor. The only issue I had with this course was that the writers never had a clear sense of feedback from their stories. He doesn't grade our work; the ta does. Reza's lectures are interesting and he Skyped professional writers in class so we could discuss the ins and outs as writers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Very good
Reza Aslan has a big ego but his classes mostly revolve around him talking about how great he is and how many celebrities he's talked to. He needs to do more teaching and less self-praising.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--SO MANY PAPERS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: full of himself, memorized intellect not real that much depth

Professor Aslan is inspiring to be around because he's a public figure. That said, his teaching is aloof and minimal. He's more caught up in advancing his own career than helping students with theirs.

He's an okay person not that terrible but not that awesome. The whole class is like 100 points so manage ur points! Study for the vocab quiz, write the essays and the story (not sure if they read them, so dont stress but just don't make obvious errors). Easy A.
Great professor! Open minded and highly engaging in lectures, the reason I am an English major!
very good course and professor. teaches how to survive being a writer. Amazing discussions and gives good advice for budding writers.

Its not that this guy was a hard professor but as a student I enjoy a professor who is investing in my learning and cares about me as a student. And this guys is so arrogant and full of himself, it's portrayed when he teaches. I think he cares a lot more about his career as a writer than professor.

Best class ever! If you attend every class (or at least email him beforehand if you're going to miss) and use proper grammar (learn it if you don't know it) you will get an A, AND you will learn a tremendous amount.

Reza knows his stuff. He's a very accomplished writer (he's spoken on the Daily Show!) and his class is super easy. If you do the assignments and don't miss a day, you'll get an easy A. Favorite part: he brings in speakers each week to talk about their work. Also, he wears interesting shirts.

His class goes by quickly it doesn't even feel like 3 hours. It was fairly easy just do your reading and you'll be fine. I disliked that the TA's never post grades and are very unorganized. Other than that this class was easy and fun!
Repeats a lot but he just wants to make sure you understood the concept and know the homework.

This professor is the absolute goat. We didn't have to use a textbook and he is very good at explaining the material. His office hours are a cheat code especially if you are struggling. And overall, Prof. Allen is just an awesome guy to talk to.
Staying on top of the material and completing the problem sets really helps with understanding the course.

Allen is super nice and pretty funny. I would highly recommend going to his lectures because of the extra credit (attendance). He only has one midterm and a final so it isn't so bad. However, do not procrastinate on problem sets or studying. Please don't.

To pass midterm (30% of grade) and final (40% of grade) you should definitely study since the questions are conceptual and not open book. TA gives answers to weekly assignment during discussion so i suggest going. He post videos explaining every question on assignment after due date. Great and understanding professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He was nice even though i hated macroeconomics
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Easy to follow and very informative. Just show up to lecture and the class is easy. Attendance is not mandatory, but he does give some extra credit for poll evs given during class.

He is a super engaging and funny lecturer. Midterm is 30% final is 40%. Attendance is 3% extra credit. He posts his notes and videos reviewing every assignment after it is due to help you study. No real curveballs on exams. Uses current examples to make things easier to understand. I took this as a breadth but would still take him again.

funny, ruggedly handsome professor. the midterm makes up 30% of your grade while the final makes up 40%. lecture attendance is not mandatory, however, you get up to 3% extra credit if you do attend. discussions are not mandatory. you need to do well on the two tests in order to do well in the class.
Great class, I'm very bad at econ but I managed to pass with an A. He has good resources available and the midterms/final are relatively easy. Just study the notes and you'll be fine
Ruggedly handsome man I have to say. W teacher. He's 6'7. Chill guy

To get on his good side, you MUST like gravy. 
One of the best professors. If you attend lecture and take his weekly assignments seriously, you will 100% pass. His guided notes HELP SO MUCH. I definitely recommend office hours, even go to sit and listen. I always walked in knowing nothing, and walked out basically understanding everything.

Took him at Pepperdine for Micro. A very hard class but such a great professor. Every lecture was top notch and engaging—he always paused to make sure students understood, related Econ to real-life examples, and was always helpful in class and OH. His tests, especially the MCQs, were very difficult. Even with a curve, this class is challenging.

Jeff Allen has been one of my favorite Econ professors. His lectures are engaging and the assignments he puts out as homework are simple. His tests are a large portion of the grade and he makes them difficult though. Free response q's are the same as he covers in class but be prepared to study and understand material to answer his MC q's.
Great lecturer. Go to class and you'll do well. There are a ton of resources on his canvas that help you prep for the exams. Go to office hours, it's a cheat code. Would take him again.

Prof. Allen is an extremely entertaining lecturer with a deep passion for his subject. For the most part, Allen is organized and flexible with the class. I am personally horrible at econ and barely understood anything past the halfway mark, but still passed this class with flying colors. The major exams are online and one can certainly make do.

Jeff is a cool guy and tries to be down to earth during his lectures. There are quizzes and homework every week but his tests are probably the hardest. He would not round my 89.8% so, would not take him again probably.
Jeff was a pretty cool guy , his classes were interesting and he never felt degrading . However , his test are difficult and confusing !  Plus they take up majority of your grade .

Honestly the only professor I have woke up at 8 am in my entire undergrad career for because class is super engaging and he is so funny. Makes learning the easy to digest and puts out so many resources to help you succeed, there is no chance you will dislike his classes, highly recommend :)

Amazing professor. Made me laugh my depression away. Uploads class notes after lecture, but I HIGHLY recommend you attend lectures because he makes sure everybody in the room understands the concept. Attendance was not mandatory, but 2-minute extra-credit quiz questions were offered every lecture. Homework was easy because of discussion practice.

professor allen is hands down the best econ professor at ucr. he made class fun and interactive. the course content itself is kinda hard, but he tries to break it down to make it a little easier to understand and will go over a topic as many times as requested.

I loved Jeff, a very down to earth and informative professor. He will clarify after clarifying until we all understand the material and concepts. Hes also very funny, makes class go by fast. He does grade for attendance but it offers a big chunk (at least for my quarter). Just showing up have me 10% in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He makes everything straightforward for this class. There are isn't much homework, but there are some podcasts you have to listen and write about. The harder part of this course is defintely the exams, mainly because of the amount of material you need to cover and understand.

During a time where classes were going from online back to in person. He made it easy for the students by providing a hybrid course. Which none of my other professor did. His exams are not easy and the class averaged 70 on it but he understood that he made it a little to hard so he choose to curve. His class is fun definitely recommend

I would say definitely take his classes he gave study guides for both final and midterm with the exam question on them 2 weeks in advance. The lectures are directly tied to the readings. There are weekly reading quizzes. Discussion attendance is mandatory even though lecture technically isn't. No phones out during class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really fosters conversation in lectures, if anything he takes too many questions but it leads to interesting places. Just go to lecture and listen, participation isn't graded but it really helps with grasping the material. And he does look like Alexander Hamilton.

Had him for biomedical ethics (PHIL007) and he's respectful, funny, and looks like alexander hamilton.

He explained material well. His lecture slides are vague so you must listen and take note of what he says during lecture. If you don't wanna do all the readings, just listen attentively during lecture. Midterm and final questions are given ahead.

Professor Ganesh was an amazing professor, this subject is heavy but he was able to lecture it in a way that explained it all so clearly. He is very understanding as long as you communicate with him. He does online quizzes, reading responses and only one final exam which was difficult but you can pass as long as you study.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Ganesh is awesome and unbiasedly teaches the philosophy of race and gender, allowing you to think critically and form your own opinions on issues. His lectures were great at breaking down the material, which can be heavy sometimes. Although I'm not a Philosophy major, I enjoyed this class and would take more classes taught by him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Took in the Fall quarter, Professor Flores is a very caring/understanding person. Lectures early in the morning but she posts videos on canvas + attendance isn't mandatory. Notes she takes in lectures are very important for understanding class however she explains it very well and organizes the notes so they are easy to read. Def would take again.

Professor Flores was amazing. Her practice exams were very similar to the real exams and she's very caring for her students and truly wants them to succeed. As long as you stay on top of the material and practice the study exams then you will do well.
Easy to follow lectures, which are recorded and promptly uploaded. Very clear on grading and gives reminders. You get credit for doing very simple assignments too.

Really good professor that does a really good job at explaining stats. Very kind. She even records every single lecture. There was a decent amount of HW along with the labs but if you get them done the same day your chilling. Practice tests were very similar to the actual test so use them. Overall really great professor and 100% recommend
this's online class, so she allows open note book, or homework, any source included in the courses. the quizzes and tests are not too heavy.
discussion attendance mandatory, did not attend lectures. one midterm one final, easy class.

She's a great professor. She is very clear, direct, and helpful. All lectures are recorded and posted on Canvas. For full credit, you only have to attend a certain number of discussions and labs. She provided practice exams before each exam, which helped a lot because the practice exam was usually very similar to the real exam.

This professor is one of the best at UCR. She is very nice and is very helpful in office hours. She records all the lectures and post them on canvas. Her test are very fair and provides a very helpful practice exams. I honestly think the hardest part of the class were the labs but not hard either just time consuming.

Professor Flores is amazing! She really cares for her students! 2 midterms and a final which wasn't bad, and she gives a few extra credit points after each exam. 5 homework assignments total and 2 labs/week which are mainly completed in lab section. Only lab and discussion sections have attendance taken. She's the best!
professor genuinely cares and gives all the tools to help you learn.
Best teacher for a math class ever. Cares about the teaching and the student. Really great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Took this class a while ago, but from what I remember Ms. Flores is super nice, well liked, and a good teacher. I probably should have done better in the class, but I was a first year and I lacked focus. Go to class cause it helps a good ammount.

Professor Analisa Flores is the best professor that I've had since the start of college. The professor offers a detailed note outline which she will walk you through step by step during lectures. The professor also offered online lecture recordings for people to review. Labs are easy but time-consuming and if you study, you will get a good grade.

Efficient, streamlined, and organized; Dr. Flores runs her class like the Navy. With pre-made lecture notes, hybrid lectures, and a lesson calendar she actually sticks to, you never miss anything. Super kind and approachable and can always break stuff down for you. Stats is NOT my strong suit, but keep up and focus on both exams and you'll be fine.

If you watch the lectures (she records it too!) and understand everything that's said on there, look over all the examples, you should be able to pass! Drops lowest HW and quiz, one of the most doable and most reasonable classes in terms of what's expected out of you.

Only discussion attendance is required, lectures are recorded.

Prof Flores is how I imagine a prof to optimize their teaching after many years of doing so, and she is still very accommodative and actually wants us to succeed. STAT 155 is still an upper div course, so expect to need to listen to lecture, study, and work for your grade.

Labs are easy at first, complicated at the end.Need to go to 10 out 15 labs for credit, and 7/10 discussions. Her teaching is good, I understood, and she gives a formula sheet during exams. Know where to put everything. Exams are kinda hard (kinda) but if you get it you should be good. Lectures are also recorded. Honestly not a bad class overall.
Very good professor, labs are not too bad, exams are very similar to practice tests, final is not cumulative, lectures are recorded and posted, some Friday lectures are held on zoom.

8AM lectures are recorded and posted on Canvas. Material is pretty easy to pick up as long as you follow the lectures. Test questions are very similar to those on the note outlines. Labs can be completed at home, but you need to attend a certain amount of labs/discussions for full participation. Lowest Webassign HW and lab grades are dropped!

Goated professor. It is an 8 AM class but she records and posts lectures! Very lenient on the grading exams. Pretty test heavy but for all exams, you're able to learn the day of. Super generous with homework and disucssion & lab attendance! Final is not cumulative. Would definitely take again!!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Stats isn't easy but she is a good professor, teaches well. She posts the lectures online, u should watch if u dont go to class, the notes are really helpful to study for exams. 3 exams mostly non-cumulative. If u do bad on an exam u still have some room to get a good grade.  She cares for students! One of the best instructors I've had.

Amazing professor, super forgiving and cares about her students succeeding. Course is heavy on 2 exams that are not cumulative but thorough. Lecture notes are not posted online so you should try and go to lecture if you cannot self teach. Always hosts office hours before where she reviews important topics, go to that. Super easy to talk to and nice

Great professor. She doesn't post completed notes online so going to lecture is basically mandatory, but she explains concepts very well and provides an outline for notes. 60% of your grade is determined by the midterm and final. If you do the homework on time and pay attention in class, the tests aren't difficult and she grades very generously.

reviews.comment: Prof. Flores is a pretty solid professor. Lectures were smooth and easy to understand. I do not advise missing out on a lot of lectures as her exams are lecture heavy. The amount of homework she gives out can be tedious and the labs are also time consuming, but as long as you know what you're doing you should be fine. Highly recommend.

Profesor Flores is great, honestly i's cool how she provided pdf outlines of the chapters for ach chapter. I just have to be honest that be ready to study! This is a very material heavy course and it goes by flying. I wish exams were a bit easier. However if you attend dicsussion, office hours, and labs I think you'll do great. Just be ready to stu
A decent professor that is accommodating

reviews.comment: Great caring professor, just take your notes and do the practice tests and it's an easy A.

During Fall 2021, the course was held asynchronously. I really can't give much feedback for her improvement. The course was well-structured, and there were no problems with her lectures. Her recordings are easily accessible, and her notes are great. Just beware the last chapter (6). Many people tripped up on it, so make sure to go to discussion/OH.

I appreciated how Prof. Flores gave us notes to print out, and the labs were pretty helpful in learning the material. I know lots of people struggled, but my advice is to just make sure to attend every class, do the homework, ask questions when you have them, and find a good study group!

reviews.comment: One of the worst classes Ive ever taken in UCR. I dont know about in person lecture but she has habit of making things complicated in the online recoded lectures. Her tests looks nothing like her examples and the practice exam. Just an overall chaos. Invest that money in crypto rather than taking her class .

She was very arrogant and refused to make her notes available for her students when I took her. She spent too much time copying down paragraphs of information versus having sample lecture problems ready for lecture.

I've always been bad at math, but her class was one of the few math classes where I actually understood the material and felt confident. Prof. Flores is very accessible outside of the classroom and she replies to emails promptly. Don't be afraid to ask her for help, I promise she explains things so well and makes sure you understand the homework.

Professor Flores does a great job engaging students during lectures by asking questions. Requires every student to buy her textbook and the only way to get notes is by going to class. This class also requires students to attend labs and discussions. Make sure you take advantage of all the time given during the exams. Also, study the practice exams!
Really easy class, go to lecture as she doesn't post notes online. Do the practice test and questions she provides. Final is not cumulative. She is super helpful during office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof Flores was amazinnngggg! I attended lectures and visited her in office hours a few times and she was so so so nice in helping me understand and as a result I got an A on every single exam. I'm not even great with math but she really takes the time to make sure you get it. DO THE PRACTICE EXAMS, they're literally just like the exam :)

reviews.comment: Went to fast with notes in class and the lectures were not useful in understanding the material

Attend Lecture because she doesn't post the slides online and make sure you write down everything she writes down too. Also do the practice problems from the textbook even though they're optional because those problems are very similar to the problems that show up on the midterm/final. Final isn't cumulative too.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Professor Flores is a great instructor! She clearly lays out what is expected of you and she even drops one lab and one quiz. I recommend doing the labs beforehand because some of them do take a while to complete. Make sure to attend lecture because that's the only place you're going to get notes!

The class is easy, however the professor makes it much harder than it needs to be. It's as if she understands everyone knows introductory statistics to be ridiculously easy, so she makes it harder to make it seem like the class is more important than it really is. Besides that, do ALL of the practice problems, attend lecture, and you'll be fine.
the worst class ever! spend 70+ dollars on an empty textbook which you have to copy down your own notes seriously?!!

No homework for her class., just study for tests and quizzes. Her notes are really clear and easy to follow. Her tests are really similar to her sample exams and notes. I would recommend her to everyone to take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Flores is really knowledgable and I like how she writes out the notes with you (don't skip class). Her tests are fair, everything is in the notes. The textbook also helps a lot for practice (recommended). No curve, the final isn't cumulative. The material isn't too hard and she's very clear in her notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Honestly one of the best professors I've had at ucr! Attendance is mandatory because she don't post notes online, but as long as you're doing the homework and attending lecture you should do well. We had an assigned textbook but I never used it and just used her lecture notes and homework to study.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Do need to put in effort but professor's clear in teaching the material. You do need to memorize for midterms & final but the final isn't cumulative & a formula sheet is given. Her textbook is mandatory to buy but inside is her a fill in the blank notes, midterms & final practice tests (aka the study guides), formula sheets, lab worksheets, etc
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors because of her teaching style. Shes very straight forward. Go to class & do the practice tests to do well. As long as you go to class,pay attention & do the labs it shouldn't be too difficult. No extra credit or rounding of grades so beware.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Really good teacher. Her notes are fairly long with a lot of useless definitions but her examples are very helpful. Also all her notes are handwritten and she doesn't upload the online so you HAVE to go to class to get the notes. Tests are extremely easy,just make sure you study every single one of her practice problems; they are similar to test q.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very cut and dry professor for statistics. Made the class very bearable and easy. It was a BLESSING to have the final non-cumulative. Her lectures are very organized and she tries to explain it as best she can, always an opportunity for questions. Her tests are straightforward if you study examples in lecture and in hw.  Easy A if you kinda study

She clearly explains everything. There are weekly quizzes in discussion and two labs per week. She clearly explains what is going to be on the midterms and finals. They are a lot like the in class practice problems  practice exams that she gives you.  I think that she is super organized with the way she teaches us and she's very knowledgeable.

1 midterm and a final that is not cumulative. Tests are majorly based on notes, which are organized and effective. Study the homework and labs. The class somewhat requires effort, but the material is easy to learn. Dr. Flores is easy to approach and quick to respond to emails.

No Curve. Only two exams worth 30% each. Labs, HW and quizzes don't help at all even with the lowest ones dropped. Not enough time on exams.  Make sure you can do the problems in your sleep or you'll fail.

Class is pretty easy as long as you study. Book is mandatory cause you need it for notes and labs. She randomly collects notes in lectures for credit especially when attendance is low. I rarely took notes but just do the practice problems before exams and you should be good. Don't f up on any of the tests or it'll be impossible to get an A.

I read the reviews before taking her class and I thought I would hate it but I ended up loving it! She is one of the best professors I had at UCR. Its not an easy A but if you go to all the lectures and study for all tests then you can get an A. He test are not that hard and most quizzes and labs are easy. Just make sure you pay attention in class
She is a really great professor, and likely one of the best for statistics. Her notes are clear, and she seems to genuinely care about student progress. I would absolutely recommend her!

She's a good professor. She is very clear in her notes and the material is repetitive as well as simple. You need the textbook for homework. You can do well on the exams if you can do her in class examples and the homework.
Requires text book for  grade. Her lectures are clear and reflect the material that are on the exam. Her exams are straightforward if you study, but the final is tricky...
She was a great professor, she explains the material clearly.  Sadly, a book is mandatory for a grade. Her exam are tricky if you don't study.

She is not a bad teacher like everyone makes it seem. She explains the material really clearly and makes use everyone understands or else she'll stop lecturing. You need to buy her book it's mandatory but in the end it's worth it. She collects pages but on days students miss a lot like on days before/after holidays. Her tests are not hard, study!

Not an easy class, you need to attend lectures. The homework is not mandatory but it helps you with midterms and finals. She collects pages of textbook on random days. Matt was my TA and he was so helpful. Best professor by far at UCR cares about you understanding and learning.

Seriously not a good teacher. Her tests are really difficult and there is never enough time to finish them. She collects pages of the books on random days and won't collect a copy of it. So lame because I do attend class everyday but sometimes I forget my book! She wants us to BUY HER book not just attend class. Going to give her a bad iEval!!
I absolutely love Dr. Flores. Her lecture style is wonderful and easy to follow. If your lazy and dont go to class, then you wont like her style. Currently taking her again for 100B!

Go to class, if you don't you can't get the notes, without notes youll do bad on the midterms. Since her final is possibly the most difficult final ever you're going to need those midterms to beef up your grade. Yes class is boring but it's pretty essential to getting a good grade and actually understanding the material. Not an easy a.
Avoid. Very boring, book is useless, and lab is repetitive and boring. No curve whatsoever. Avoid!
Very clear.  Loves to teach and it shows.  She is very understanding and reasonable.  Her midterm felt overwhelming but her final was very easy.  Just do the homework and you'll get an easy A

GO TO CLASS. Don't expect to get a good grade if you miss lectures. Since she writes the notes it's kind of impossible to get them otherwise. If you do well on the first two exams you'll be alright. But the final is brutal. On the bright side she explains things in detail, and is happy to answer any question you might have.

Im an avg C math student and thats basically what i got in this class. 69.88, yes d+ no curve whatsoever. I attended all lectures, labs, and discussions, got mid 70's on midterms which made getting anything other than a c or d impossible. great teacher but the weights of the tests makes it difficult for average students to pass.  I had a 3.6, had..

Prof. Flores does not have lecture slides, but rather writes the notes out during lecture, so if you want to get an A, DO NO, AND I REPEAT, DO NOT MISS LECTURE. She explains concepts very clearly and seems very down to earth. Three non-cumulative midterms, all weighed equally. Pay attention during lecture and lab. There is generally no curve.

She is not easy at all. It is impossible to receive an A in her class because if you receive a C on one exam then kiss the A goodbye. There is three midterms and no final. The midterms were fair but hard. Homework takes at least four hours or more. The only reason people attend class is for the notes, other wise, class is useless.

She writes her notes as she speaks so attending class is mandatory if you want to pass. She is very clear and precise. However if you do bad on any exams its going to be hard to get an A because she does not curve anything. You basically have to get an A on everything in order to receive an A for this class.
She is very easy to understand and her tests are very fair. You are allowed to bring a full sheet of paper with whatever you want on it to every exam. Best stats professor at UCR for sure.

Professor Allen is a really chill guy. Found this class to be very interesting and his notes really helped guide me to success. Class lectures structured through filling note outlines, however he does a good job keeping the class engaged through his quips and examples. Tests weren't too difficult, provides practice exams and all material in notes.

Cool guy, crackes jokes to lighen everything up. as long as you study a little bit before midterms and finals youll do fine. the material is very easy to read through and the questions arent super difficult.

Organized and easy to follow along. Discussion section attendance not mandatory but discussion assignments are. Homework is super helpful for understanding how to apply concepts. Exams are the same level of difficulty. Overall great. He's funny and honestly, ruggedly handsome.

Very chill professor! The class is fairly simple, just do your DSAs, Problem sets and study for the exams. Make sure to study for the exams because thats where most of the grade weight comes from. Also I would go to lecture because if you keep missing you'll probably get lost. Other than that, pretty chill. (P.S. he offers extra credit!!)

Lectures are straightforward, but are cumulative so don't get stuck behind. The homework assignments are the best way to study for the midterm and the final. Great professor and knows the material really well. If you miss a few lectures, it's alright because it's for extra credit, but don't get stuck behind.

Very great professor. He really cared about the class and was really funny. Pretty lecture heavy, I wouldn't want to miss his class. Final is worth 40 percent and midterm is worth 30 percent of your grade, however if you do better on your final than your midterm, he will raise your midterm score.

Lecture is required because you have to do a notecard problem at the end, but its easy points, just go to class. Uses PollEv. Wish he did more practice problems in class but the test was similar to those, just different numbers. Not a bad professor overall. Participation (lecture + discussion) is 25%, HW is 10%, midterms 30%, final 35%.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He's a nice professor. Go to office hours and he'll help you understand concepts. You just have to ask. Most complaints are about the 25% participation (lecture + discussion), but it's EASY points if you do the bare minimum of attending lectures + discussion. Notecards are simple. Exams are easy. Just do the practice exams. Curve most likely.

He's honestly a great physics professor. His slides are clear and straightforward. Must attend lectures. Participation (lecture + discussion) is 25%, HW is 10% (no late policy), midterms 30% (scores averaged), final 35%. Exams are basically copies of the practice exams and if you actually understand them, you'll be fine. Very doable.

Honestly this class was one of the easiest classes I've taken. Exams are direct copies from the homework and class activities but with different numbers. He gives better curves if the class is quiet, so if you get a loud section then good luck.

Mandatory lecture attendance but he doesn't actually teach anything in lectures, just bombards you with Polleverywhere questions; you can't get away with doing them from home either cause he also makes you do a problem on a notecard each lecture and turn in the notecard. You'll have to self-study the material, only silver lining are the easy tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Decent exams, but bad teaching style. Attendance mandatory, "lectures" are very little lecturing and mainly examples that he briefly explains. So get ready to teach yourself.
easy tests, but probably the worst way of teaching I've ever seen in a college class. Attendance is mandatory.

One of the best profs!! He truly wants you to learn, and if you do the pre-lectures and hw you will. Highly recommend office hours, he's super sweet and cares a lot, BUT he will make you work, hes not just going to give answers. A lot of ppl don't like that but it works. I suck at physics but learned a lot. Tests are very fair if you try!

Just do/understand the activities and you'll do well! Practice exams similar to actual exams. Lecture slides are very good. Clickers and in class activities. Attendance is mandatory. 4-5 HW questions 3x a week, occasionally the questions show up on the exams. Go to SI and office hours! He curves. Just read the prelectures, don't read the book.

The class itself wasn't that hard as all of his midterms and finals were very similar to the activities that he did in class. However, he expects you to do all the prelectures before his actual lecture to be able to understand the content so a lot of self-teaching is expected in his class.

Anderson knows how to teach students, unlike many other physics professors. His exams are basically his in class activites with different numbers. The activities are challenging but he takes all class to explain them. If you understand what is going on in class you will definetley pass with an A. He loves to teach in office hours too, very helpful.

He is an average professor.  His teaching in lecture is not clear, so read the prelecture material before lecture so you catch up.  He doesn't give a lot of homework in mastering physics (only 5 problems after every lecture).  His tests weren't that challenging, but if you want to get a good grade, self-teach.
Bro spent every paycheck on flashcards for attendance, also no curve at all.

Probably one of the most overhated professors. He's a really nice guy, and is always willing to help you out. Visit office hours, pay attention and answer polls. The grading scale was well laid out, and I really appreciated how he was able to address a pool of over 400 people day by day.
If you care and put in effort you will do good fs
The goat fr fr
He's really good. I recommend

Oh boy oh boy where do I even start. I've had Anderson for multiple classes and I love him. He genuinely cares about the material, tests are fair. If you want to do good and actually understand the content then choose him. I had him for 2a as well and loved him. Although I felt that 2c was easier.

Anderson is really not a bad professor as others say he is. I've taking him for multiple classes, and he is consistent in how he teaches. 35% of your grade is hw/discussion/lecture participation which is easy points if you just stay on top of it. Also has prelectures you should do. Exams are fair, follow almost exactly to the HW/Lecture questions.

Anderson is one of the worst professors I've had so far. Not clear on the grading scale and has not answered any questions about it. Lectures and prelectures don't prepare you for his exams, you have to self study. The TA's also don't care, they limit you to ONLY 1 question and bring up irrelevant material. Choose any other physics professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Definitely not the worst Physics professor. His in class activities are fine if you do the pre-lecture reading. All of his tests are fair on the material, similar to the homework and in class activities. Labs are tedious, but not too complicated. Only difficulty was most of the class is self-study.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: We had clicker questions and at the end of class he made us answer one of the in-class activities as a group on a notecard. He wouldn't give us the question for the notecard until almost the end of class which was really annoying. His lectures aren't the best and you have to rely on reading through the pre-lectures and self-learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Just do the reading, attend lectures, stay consistent with performance in discussion/lab. You'll end with an A. The grading scale is extremely lenient. Winter 2025 Quarter seemed to have a 85% minimum for A grade. He always answered my questions during lecture; don't know what the other reviews are talking about.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lecture was kind of boring and grade was based on PollEvs and exams. Warning, the exams are nothing like the practice exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: go to every lecture, lab, discussion (partcipation matters). do every homework yourself. midterms and tests are exactly like the homework questions so make sure u know how to do them urself. EVERYthing is graded on accuracy. anderson gives prelecture readings so it is kinda "self study" but if u actually do it lectures are way more understandable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Not sure why he's rated so low. He's clear about grading. Attendance is mandatory (poll everywhere + notecard u turn in). Two midterms and a final—literally homework questions with different numbers. Got a 6/15 on midterm and 21/27 on the final due to a terrible flu, but he was really understanding abt my situation. Thankfully I got a B :)

Could have been worse. I didn't attend probably of his lectures, discussions and lab which let me to have a bad lab grade (43%) yet I did pass somehow because I did well on the exams. This was definitely self taught class cause whenever I went to lectures, I didn't get it. It did help that the practice exam were closely related to the actual exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Such a rude guy honestly and grades are based heavily on the exams alone. don't take this class unless you're up for it being self taught! lectures are unhelpful and most of the time i had to teach myself outside of class to keep up. but at the very least the grading scale is generous.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Anderson is a decent professor he just sometimes makes the lectures a lil confusing so you gotta do extra learning outside of class.  He has polls and a lecture attendance that can only be completed in person.  The hw is not forgiving so make sure ur doing it properly cuz otherwise thats easy points lost.  He's lowkey just a mid prof, nun special.
You really have to self study, he does not know how to teach or just enjoys seeing students struggle. He writes the labs and it's so scattered, disorganized, and plain frustrating to do.

When midterms came, he rejected my ask for help after class to go over answers. Then, during finals, I tried to catch him outside the library and was shunned. It seemed very disrespectful to walk past me as if I wasn't there the day before the final. This professor shows zero empathy to  students and you have to rely on self-study and lecture notes

Just leave!!! What a mean guy he is!!! He rejects communicating at all. 

Worst professor I've ever met in UCR. Just don't take his course!!!

This guy is terrible at teaching. The entire course he puts up clicker questions for every lecture and grades them based on accuracy. Once it's over he doesn't explain any answers or concepts. YT heavy class. You can't teach a class by making students do work wroksheets in lecture. Sad to see someone say they care about teaching and not reflecting.

This man does not care about your learning. He barely teaches in lecture, most of your time is spent doing activities that he doesn't explain how to do and 6-8 clicker questions that are graded on correctness. Brushes over topics extremely quickly and relies on you reading 30 page pre-lectures and long textbook sections. Be ready to self study.
Use the prelectures for the exam study material. He doesn't really teach, so if you're willing to "self-study" then take him. In class activities and HW really help too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Incredible no nonsense type of professor. PHYS 40c is intense during the summer but he made it very clear and direct to the point. Concepts are reinforced through reading before class and polls during the class. I'm not a good physics student but pulled an A on his final. First physics class I got an A in because of him and his teaching style.

He's not terrible, that's really all I can say. He does seem to care about you understanding physics so long as you ask him questions but he isn't great at explaining concepts and mostly relies on walking you through PollEv questions (that he grades you on before explaining how to solve them).
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Michael Anderson makes you self study everything. If you want to have a better professor, choose someone else. His lectures are mandatory and he keeps track of attendance through Poll Everywhere. Tests are very difficult but look similar to the practice exams that he assigns to do.

Great professor and teaching style! I would recommend him to anybody. The exams are all very FAIR and doable as long as you understand the in class activities. Go to office hours to clarify hw problems and in class activities.

Tests are reasonable as long as you understand the questions he does in class. Didn't like that he made students try problems without knowing how to do them, that only works for easier concepts. Most of the class is self study. If you read pre-lectures & textbook, his lectures become a little easier. Barely teaches anything tho.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He was okay, study the hw, his in class activities and the practice tests. His tests are representative of the material. His lectures were alright but he may come off as slightly rude at times. Participate class and do not ditch a single lecture or discussion, it will help you and your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor doesn't teach. He posts "pre-lectures" and expects students to fully teach themselves. When asked questions, he gives vague answers or none at all, saying "sure" while you work through problems wrong. His lecture activities mimic exams, but he NEVER provides answer keys, so students can't confirm their work is correct. GO TO ARC

"Easiest professor in the Physics 2b series, but hardest to self-study in terms of content". He's not good in terms of teaching the content but the exams were extremely fair, based on the practice. I self-studied all the way to the end for this guy. Apparently, curve after taking the final must have been crazy good. Pretty happy with the results.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: class is easy to pass and i probably couldve gotten an A if i studied but this guy basically doesn't teach and expects you to know everything by the time you enter the class, lecture consists of clickers and worksheets and he goes over like 1 or 2 problems in it, tests are fair but literally just get ready to teach yourself if you take his class
Participation is mandatory. His midterms are ONLY 11 questions, so make sure to study for them well. Like a previous review says, pretty much if you get more than 3 wrong you're screwed.

Overall a very awful person. I only talked to him twice about my grade and improvement and the interactions were far from pleasant. Attendance is mandatory if you want to get full credit on participation which is easy points but lectures were not very insightful. Be ready to teach yourself.

Hi averages for the tests are pretty bad but the scaling of his course is also very wide. Just do everything the class requires you to do but make sure you do the prelecture stuff cuz its vital if you want to actually understand what hes talking abt in a sense where you could apply it on a test.

Crappy at teaching, but as long as u do his pre-lectures it's manageable, ppl just balance this class with other hard classes so it becomes almost impossible. Two midterms, one final, midterms reflect practice exams, and the final was basically the two midterms plus new content. Takes attendance with notecards every lecture, plus polls.
this guy is literally so bad. All I'm going to say is get ready to teach yourself the material
Lectures are almost pointless to go to, youll learn more on youtube.
Idk why his rate my prof is bad. He is a good teacher and his tests are accurate to the hw/practice test/activities done in class.

He is alright, somewhat easy class for Electricity and Magnetism. Just show up and do the work, and you should be fine. Only thing is that he is condescending during office hours. Just do the prelecture stuff and you should be fine.

Took this class this summer and the course wasn't too bad. Decent professor and was able to explain concepts in depth. Just gotta listen if you wanna do well in the class. He gave us a quiz at the end of every lecture which was basically our midterm score. As long as you listen in class, then you'll do well in the class. Final wasn't too bad either
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This professor is a very mean spirited person, I emailed him regarding a reevaluation of my grade and was met with a harsh reply as if I was insulting him. I did not think I asked anything rudely, yet he seemed offended. LSA is difficult and worth 40% so I suggest you try to prepare well for it. Grade adjustment is unhelpful if you do poorly.

Work in groups. Tedious labs. LSA is rough. Understand physics on deep level to do well on LSA, even if phys/engin isn't your major. Something mean-spirited about pre-lab 8 grading. 2 attempts but the problems are changed on second attempt. This is the only time they change the problems. He tries to trick you on pre-lab 8/LSA so be careful.

Great prof to explain materials, but you have to teach yourself something before taking each class. Exams are not hard if you prepare well by going through the slides and click Q questions. He's nice if you're a good kid.
extremely difficult, you have better chances trying to teach yourself
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is the easiest 2B professor in terms of content but the hardest in terms of self teaching. He has pre lectures that are 30+ slides you need to do before class. Almost all class is activities to help learn but they arent very good. Exams are easy. Will make exams harder if your class wont shut up. If youre a good kid, he will be lenient w you
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Had him for 2A and took him again for 2B because he curves very generously. Midterms are only 10-11 questions and are very similar to homework questions. Lectures are pretty straightforward as long as you read the pre-lecture slides that he puts on Canvas. The textbook is unnecessary tbh and sucks that you have to pay like 100 bucks for HW access.

Anderson's lectures do not really reflect the content on the homework and exams. I did not really like his teaching style but his exams are just like the practice exams on Canvas. If you are looking to earn a good grade, you can take Anderson's class but be aware that you will have to teach yourself the content.

teach yourself everything because he expects you to know everything by the time you walk into class. lecture is basically doing problems that he gives you no time on. his midterms are 10 questions meaning you're screwed if you miss 3 questions + 90% of them are calculations so you run out of time. threatens class saying he'll make the final hard.

DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR! Literal text-to-speech bot, can't teach. Makes you read 30 slides before lecture and 50 textbook pages. Lectures for 10 minutes, rest of class is you and your partners doing "activities", most of which he will not help you figure out. Tons of clicker questions, no stopping for solutions. "You got one wrong?" oh well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Yes, Dr. Anderson is a tough professor so YOU NEED TO APPLY YOURSELF! Go to his office hours! He does not show you how to solve the problems. You need to try it on your own then ask questions. His exams are like the hw, clicker Q's, and activities. Do not fall behind! His class really helped me learn the concepts of physics. I enjoyed this class!

Dr. Anderson gives three exams, 2 midterms and 1 final, but they are very predictable and easy if you participate in the in-class activities and do the Mastering Physics homework. The exam questions are exactly like the in-class activity and homework questions. Also, he provides practice exams which again, the exam questions are exactly like them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Make sure you read the assigned reading before lecture or you will not understand. He explains little things in the lecture and you'll have to read to remotely know what's going on. Exams have very few questions and are mostly based on the sample problems he did in class.  A little annoying that he makes you buy Pearson textbook.

PHYS040B - You will never be surprised by his exams. You will have seen them through lecture activities, clicker questions, or discussion problem sets. During lectures, work with people who are actively engaged with the activities instead of Mr. Manga Reader or Shopper Susan. That's when you learn the most and Anderson tests on.

His tests are extremely predictable if you do the clicker questions, homework, and exams. The most important aspect of his teaching style is he emphasizes working on problems in class. This class becomes exponentially better if you take it with a group of friends to work on in-class activities with and are actively engaged in lectures.

A walking text to speech bot, who flings mandatory clicker questions at you because he read somewhere that engagement metrics means learning. He adds very little substance to the course and he won't be elaborating on 80% of the clicker questions. Click and go, click and go, did you get it right or wrong? who cares, click and go....
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Overall he's a nice guy with terrible teaching methods. No partial credit on exams and participation is graded on accuracy. He doesn't really teach because he just reads from power points, puts you into breakout rooms for 60% of lecture, and doesn't even review WS. Goes over conceptual ideas and doesn't go over any sort of calculations.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Make sure to do all of the practice tests and examples! He doesnt post any answer keys to them but he will check your work and give you feedback if you email him, which is actually very helpful.

Terrible prof does not explain how to do the problem he gives and expects us to figure it out on ourselves despite not even teaching the material. His "teaching style" is for you to teach yourself the material and he gives you a worksheet to do to "practice". THAT'S IT. If you can have the option to switch profs then do not take this man.

The grading for online class was tough: no partial credit in problem solving because of the site he used. He explained concepts fine but his examples did not help prepare for the exams at all. Didn't explain the math well. Plus he really began to lose energy teaching throughout the quarter so it was difficult to pay attention in lecture.
all the "activities" he did was useless to the final. paid the same tuition for a useless online course RIP

From the start he made it very clear to me through email that he will not be telling us any correct answers or any explanation on them (activity slides, practice tests) He verbally explained things in class with few diagrams. This made it extremely difficult for me to learn, as I learn better when things are written down in front of me! Beware!!

Professor Anderson is one of the BEST professors that I have taken at UCR. Very organized and approachable should you have a question. Intelligent and has standards for himself and his students >> you have to pay attention! He cares if you care to ask. Tough class, but that's physics you have to push through and understand what you get wrong.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Honestly, this guy is underrated. He has high standards for his students and expects them to read his notes daily before class. So, yes it's more demanding than other profs (who just want you to get one concept, move on + forget) - but I did end up retaining a lot more info for being on top of my feet and tutoring my peers in subsequent quarters.

I didn't like him at first, especially with the clicker questions but he is honestly extremely fair. His test are based off the in class activities you do in some way or another, and everything else minus the test are easy points. My advice is go to his office hours and solve the activities with him, youll be prepared for the test.

He teaches by putting up Activity slides and clicker questions. Hardly lectures about anything. He quizzes you with clicker questions expecting you to master the material as he just taught you seconds ago which he took for a grade. Likes to throw in trick questions on his exams and clickers. Don't take this guy unless you have to or not at all.

I had prof. Anderson for my 2 quarters (2B and 2C) and I did really well in both the quarters. You just have to make sure you understand the in-class activities nicely and practice enough problems before the tests. As long as you know your concepts and the in-class activities you are good for his class.

Prof. Anderson doesnt deserve such a low rating. Yes, he has high expectations when arriving to class and expects you to read the material ahead of time which is why some might find it difficult because he doesnt go into too much detail during lecture. If you prepare ahead of time you will be fine. Very generous curve & exams are based off lecture.

probably the worst prof ive ever had at UCR. He doesn't teach at all, he just gives clicker questions and doesnt explain the answer at all.
