She may not be clear at first, but if you ask her to she will clarify what she means. She actually uses books that are required so make sure you buy them!
She is probably the cutest english teacher on campus. take her class she is pretty easy and she is cute so its an incentive to to go classs
Miss B. is very cute in my opinion, she's very sweet and helpful, she might not be the funniest teacher in the campus but her smile melts my heart. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED
Ms. Brownell is wonderful!  She is helpful, caring and kind.  Her class is really fun and interesting.  I highly recommend her!!

She is a great English teacher. She's sweet, nice, and helpful. The homeworks may seem a little heavy but it's obvious its all in good intentions. Very helpful. you will learn alot from her teachings.

Lectures were pretty boring, basically just read off slides. Mandatory attendance through pollev and make sure you answer them quick because he closes them fast. What brings rating down is the final, so many questions each requiring time it made my head spin. Overall wouldn't take again.

got mad at me during office hours 3 days before the final for asking questions in front of several other students. several students cheated in his class, the material isnt hard, but he does NOT care abt his students nor abt their success. final and midterm were fair, mirror of his practice exams. but super average, unkind prof. take someone else

yall don't take this save yourself he so rude omg. Literally clocked a kid for his tech issues like huh? discussion is 10x more helpful then his boring, long lectures. But prepare yourself...you have been warned.......
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Pretty straightforward class. Class  made me sleepy even after 2 celsius drinks. The Smartworks assignments are purposely harder than exams. Redemption points are pretty useful and bump up your grade. Take advantage of office hours, he's accessible. Will respond to any concerns with respect.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Did not like this class whatsoever. The midterms were fair but the final felt like the material came out of nowhere and was very unfair. Wish there were more resources like more practice questions as that would've prepared the class more.
crazy hard and his accent is, unfortunately, extremely difficult to understand
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor is absolutely terrible at teaching. The lectures are awful and he can barely explain one topic at a time. The class averages were well below a B- on every midterm and the final but chooses to blame the entire class for their work ethic instead of the test difficulty or teaching. Absolutely stay away from him, especially premeds

I was 1 point away from an A-, don't expect him to round because he won't. Some stuff you have to teach yourself but it's definitely possible to get an A. His lectures are a little boring and there's ICQ's that you technically have to be there for but can do anywhere. Don't take discussion quizzes lightly. He gives curves for every exam.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Bruh plz drop this class before its too late. Granted I haven't heard of any good chem 1a profs here but Fokwa is so boring to listen to and I felt like i didnt learn anything in his class bc he was terrible at teaching. I was always at the ARC and learning by myself and it was just really bad. Sincerely apologize if your LC placed you in his class

Not a good lecturer, but content can be self taught, as he posts all the slides. Midterms and finals tests on exceptions he only mentions in lectures. In-class quizzes can be completed from home during the lecture. Tests mostly cover concepts, rather than math.

Don't be put off by his ratings! He reads off of slides but does practice problems and gives 30 points of extra credit. For our class, he curved one midterm and final. There's an exam redemption system as well. Has PollEVs and Smartwork 5 HW. Read the textbook, somewhat understand the material before class, and you'll get that A.

Took this class as an incoming freshman and had a pleasant introduction to how university classes are structured. The class is what you make of it, that is if you put in the time to go over material before lectures, do the homework, and ask for help when it is needed, then you will succeed.
Easy class. Assignments aren't graded, you can take tests max 3 times and they are curved heavily. My first midterm I got a 37% and it curved to a 95%.

Couldn't understand what he was saying most of the time. Nice guy, but doesn't know how to explain things. Had to read the textbook chapters and watch youtube vids to understand most concepts. Final is worth 40% of your grade so make sure to do well on that. Curve is not by much unless you get the redemption points.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Drop the class if you were forced to have him as your chemistry professor. Does not care about learning. Refused to re-check midterms and final. Very rude and disrespectful.

Professor Fokwa is okay. The only thing about him is that it is really hard to understand his accents and his handwriting. I recommend sitting in the front because he talks pretty quietly. The actual exam is harder than the samples, and it is not an easy A. Ask a lot of questions because it does help. Also, it kinda requires self-teaching.

The class isn't for an easy A. The professor is knowledgeable, but lectures were challenging, requiring self-study. Supplemental classes and bonus questions were helpful. It's important to note that sample exam's difficulty may not match the actual exams.

Very unorganized. I started learning more when I stopped attending lectures and studied. Mandatory ICQs during lecture unfortunately. His office hours are useless. He spends 45 minutes explaining something to one student and leaves 15 minutes for the other 10 students remaining. You basically have to teach yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are difficult to understand so attend discussions & TA office hours. ICQs are conducted with poll everywhere so be ready to answer them he gives ~30 seconds. You need to be on time and stay until the very end to get these points, sometimes he kept us overtime, it is 15% of the grade. There are 2 midterms worth 25% and the final is 40%.

Fokwa is alright, it's maneagable to get an A but you do have to study a good amount and know what you are doing. Lecture's not super helpful. Our final was not very similar to the practice final and it threw me off. Make sure you study outside things like the HW and past ICQ's. Offers 3% of extra credit in the form of bonus questions on tests.

Handwriting was hard to understand and lectures are very boring. Homework load was pretty light. His class is pretty difficult but I appreciate that he gives study guides and also replaces midterm grades if you do better on the final.

He's an okay teacher. He's quite dismissive, so he won't take you as seriously as he should. I fell asleep during his lectures because it was very boring and he just spoke without explanation. I had to teach myself a lot of the chemistry even after taking a lot of notes. Discussion class helped. Participation is mandatory during lecture/discussion.

Getting an A in the class isn't impossible but leans more towards difficult than not. Taking this professor really showed me the importance of looking at other options during registration in terms of instructors. As an instructor he isn't too bad but his lectures are sometimes hard to understand.
Makes countless mistakes on exams and has frequent errors in grading, personally lost around a few percentage points due to IcQ grading problems.
We have study guides but they are nothing like the exams. He is a tough grader. Final exam was super hard. Very hard to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Although the attendance was not mandatory, 15% was in-class quiz (IcQ). Midterms and the final were not too hard, and each of them has bonus points. If you find your test grade was lower than your thought, it might not your fault, since TA sometimes set the answer wrong. So, recheck the questions after the testing grade came out.
Average Professor. Has two midterms and a final. Make sure to study outside of class because lectures are not going to get you an A.

He's kinda mid. His lectures are not too informative as he expects you to read off the lecture slides before lecture starts, and he tests your knowledge of the lecture slides through clicker qs. Exams are kinda tough as there's few trick questions not mention on the practice exams, but he do offer extra credits. Seek outside resources for more help
lectures are hard, always learn the material on your own by reading. Do the practice tests, almost identical to his actual tests and make sure to finish hw and participate in class icq

Fokwa is a nice guy, but a bit hard to understand. I gained a better understanding once I started to attend in-person lecture, but I had trouble the entire quarter. ICQs most classes, but if 80% of the class gets the answer correct, everyone gets points. Will curve exams & has bonus questions worth 5 points. HW is manageable. SI helped a ton

Getting an A would be tough w/o chem background. Clicker questions almost every day, so if you don't come to class you lose tons of points. 2 midterms and 1 final that make up over half of your grade. Doesn't curve but our avg on the final was failing so he made an exception. Homeowork is harder than the midterms overall though.

Took him for chem 1a in fall 2021. Overall a great professor. Homework had unlimited tries w/ no penalty. In class quizzes points were given to everyone if at least 80% of the class got the question right. Overall lots of opportunities to improve your grade. Tests were like the samples, they were generally easy.

Summer session A. Had to lecture myself thru textbook & YouTube. Polleverywhere quizzes for credit, make sure u get those points. Offended by the prof's reaction to students' questions. Prof mumbles a lot, and he ridiculed students for asking about concepts. Said we did bad cuz we don't ask questions / discuss. Really bro? Struggling experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Took CHEM001A for Session A of Summer 2021, not the best experience, but its also not the worst. Attend every lecture if you plan on getting past this class, and make sure to attend office hours with questions. Lectures were okay, but a lot of the time, the professor didnt want to address a lot of the questions that students had. 7/10

The concepts in this class are basic chemistry concepts and are not overly difficult. I personally had trouble following the professor though and relied heavily on the book for the few concepts that were challenging.

Theres no makeups offered for ICQs given in lecture so dont miss those. His lectures are all over the place/not always helpful so I just watched youtube videos and read the book. Preview the slides before lectures so you have some understanding because he moves very fast. The sample exams are similar to the actual ones so make sure you do those.

Fokwa's lectures are all over the place and it's hard to find some way to connect all the dots. He doesn't explain the concepts clearly and sometimes skips over all the important details that I have to khan academy in the end. If you want to just pass the class that's great, but if you're planning on taking the rest of the series get another prof.

I hope this isn't too mean, but to be honest, Fokwa's accent drove me nuts. I could barely understand anything he was saying, and even when I did it was hard for me to comprehend the material he was teaching because he wasn't the best explainer. First midterm should be easy, second gets messy, but the final was something uncalled for.
If you want to pass, take his class. If you want to learn, avoid him. He doesn't teach AT ALL. TAs teach way more than he does

Powerpoints posted alone, attendance not mandatory. Do all clicker questions, that will raise your grade up a lot. Scoring based on point system and not very friendly. Tests were hard, trick questions and did not curve the class. I got 799/1000 and he stressed how hard the class would be and refused to round me up 1 point. I did much better in 1B.

Started by using powerpoints, then would just lecture off the top of his head then refer back to the powerpoint again n would skip over major topics that were then on the exam even though he never talked about them final exam was horrible had a study guide didnt post key until around midnight everyone thought it was difficult overall bad experience
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He might be a bit difficult to understand, but he's a fairly decent teacher. I would recommend doing all of the clicker questions. The curve did help my grade a lot but don't expect it to save a terrible grade. Overall, the class was not too difficult but should not be underestimated.

His lectures are easy to understand. He made it easy to pass with his grading scale. There is no curve, only redemption system which, in my opinion, is better than a curve. He is very caring and fair and really wants everybody to pass. I really recommend him, especially if chem isn't your best subject.

Honestly hated him as a chem professor. I understand that your not necessarily supposed to have a connection with a professor, but his teaching style made me hate chem. Says not to write what's on his slides but he LITERALLY READS OFF THE SLIDES. Expects us to know everything about the topic he would discuss in the class too.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Out of all the chem professors UCR has to offer, Boniface is comparatively a more generous grader. His tests are alright as long as you are actively learning the material outside of class. He offers curves and extra credit throughout the quarter, so take advantage of it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This professor does not explain the concepts efficiently enough for you to clearly understand. He expects you to know rather than to teach it and break down the material for the students. Be ready to put in a lot of unnecessary effort when taking this class and teach yourself everything that should be taught in lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: One of the best chemistry professors, hands down. His midterms are almost the same as his practice midterms. The final was pretty much the two midterms + the practice final. I missed out on a lot of clickers, but I still ended up with an A. In my opinion, he's good at teaching the material. Absolute gem.

Two midterms, one final, the tests are fairly straight forward but do have a "gotcha" components. Its a bit tense asking questions as he expects his students to see the answers he sees. I didn't feel as though I was able to connect with him personally.

Dr Fokwa is excellent. Homework is fairly difficult and his exams were OK (multiple choice). Has a redemption system as opposed to a curve. A bit confusing with the way he explains some topics but nothing office hours cant clear up. Stay on top of your stuff or you will not do well!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: ABSOLUTE LEGEND
Great lectures as they are easy to understand! Tests are reasonable as long as you do enough practice problems.
Study really hard!!!
he writes his notes in class so fast. pretty easy to understand though.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Understand concepts and details taught in class. Some details not taught in class unnecessary. Rewatch lecture videos if needed for details. Put in the work and u will do well
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Had him for A and will be taking him for C. He is truly the goat of ochem. He prepared me for B with his great teaching style. Just make sure to review IR before entering B because he doesn't teach it for A.

honestly amazing professor. so so much extra credit. gives so many worksheets. if you take his class, just practice all the worksheets and activity preps he gives you before the exam. for the final do everything all over again and you will be good, its a lot of work but once you practice it is really not that bad.

He is a great lecturer, but I had to go back and watch recordings because I found the material hard to process so quickly. He offers a lot of extra credit opportunities and the grade scale was recently changed to make it easier to pass the class. He is great for Ochem A, definitely take his lectures, and study as you learn or you'll barely pass.
he somehow grades all midterms and final in 1-2 days. super nice guy. good lectures. funny and caring. just watch chads prep to supplement instruction. easy class!
If only every professor could be like him
THE GOATTTTTT

Great professor, really good lectures, and gives ample extra credit at the end of the course. Definitely take if you want to learn and set yourself up for ochem b and c. Put in the work and it is an easy A.
i wish i could marry him

This is one of the BEST professors you can have for ochem! There was a total of 34 extra credit points, and the tests were completely fair. Casselman also has amazing lectures, and if you supplement his teaching with Ochem as a second language, you will do great!

The best prof you can get for ochem. Attend office hours consistently and do ochem as a second language. A couple days before the midterm, spam practice problems and you'll be set. All exams are fair content wise. It's really hard to finish the midterms in 50 min lwk unfair but final makes up for that as plenty of time is provided. effort = A
The absolute goat.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Best professor for 008A, but doesn't curve. Concepts build up over the quarter, but aren't difficult if you study. Midterms have many questions so you have to know the content well. Did bad on midterms (61%, 50%) but locked in and got a 90% on the final. Ending with a A- with EC(~14pts) and redemption points(max 20pts)

Ochem is difficult, he's one of the better professors who teaches Ochem but don't expect to get a good grade without studying. From week 1 you should do one or all of these three things: office hours, si, ochem as a second language. You aren't tested on the exceptions which is good. Know your material and understand how to apply it in the exam.

The bad reviews are from people who didn't study. The class is time-consuming, but Casselman offers numerous resources, including lots of practice problems and lots of office hours. stay on top of weekly self-assessments (these reflect the exam problems). He does not curve, but 85% is an A. Casselman is a great lecturer and a good person overall.

From week 1, lock in. You can't cram. Do lots of practice problems; exam time is limited. It's a hard class. The professor is fair but doesn't curve; 85% is an A-, 60% is a C. Final exam (40%) offers redemption points on midterms (20% each), but only if you do well, so don't bank on it. Last 20% is hw/polls, you should have 100% in this category.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Reasonable professor who teaches a lot of very important concepts. What Casselman taught in his class and focused on is the present in the core of many other upper-division classes. Obviously it's a challenging class but Casselman did a really good job setting me up for success and a better level of understanding in many of my other classes.

Best O Chem prof. Great lectures, and all assignments helped me learn better. Tests are very hard, go to OH if you have any gaps in learning. I still remember all he taught because he cares about student learning. HW is graded as complete, poll ev in class.

Casselman is an amazing lecturer and is the best professor to learn ochem from. He does practice problems in class and is very helpful during office hours. I explains things in an easy way to understand, and his tests are fair and things you have seen in class. I am taking 8C with him over the summer.

structure of the class + lectures make it easy to understand the material and get an A, but you definitely have to want it or neither will be possible.  leaving this a year after taking 8a/b with dr casselman; don't be afraid to ask him for help, he is an understanding guy.  and do the practice exams!

Casselman is a good professor. It's just that his tests are extremely hard, and he grades even harder. 80% of your grade will fall on the exams, and 20% will fall on HW (graded by completion). He doesn't curve. He does give some EC but not much. Honestly, the best tool you have is gonna be the OCHEM tutor and studying your old midterms. Good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing supportive professor, provides lots of supplemental instruction to learn, study, practice etc. Material is fairly difficult but with practice a lot can be memorized/understood especially with the practice he gives. Tests are a fair reflection of what is taught. Genuine professor that tries to help his students. 10/10 class (tough material).
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Honestly I could have achieved a higher grade if I didn't try to rush all my studying for the weekend and then the exam would be on Monday. Guys a decent teacher but I think if you pair yourself with the "O Chem As A Second Language" book, you are in really good shape to get an A, no doubt.

very good professor. be sure to go lectures, especially when there's an activity and work with peers, it helps a lot. there was definitely some self study that had to be done, but u should lwk be doing that anyways, has a lot of resources practice problems, self assessments, practice exams etc. just stay on top of things and attend SI and ur good
Chill teacher, while the class was difficult I feel like he made things pretty easy to understand.

Records lectures, and puts slides up in Drive. Make sure to attend class on days with the practice papers. Very similar to what he has on the midterm. 
Rushes in the last half. Throws a ton of reactions at you.
You have to study on your own.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Casselman lectures are packed with info, but yeah, it's just the basics. Part of the class is learning what to do with those basics. He gives lots of practice problems so there's no excuse not knowing what's on the exams. Keys to success: 1) show up, 2) practice. If you coasted through gen chem with no work, you will struggle with ochem.

ngl, while casselman is certainly a great professor (especially for STEM standards), and cares about his students, I still think his teaching his pretty bad and you're going to have to self-learn a lot of this stuff so that sucks.

He teaches better than the other professor and he explains certain concepts thoroughly but he rushes the content at times because he didn't have enough time and he won't be clear about certain things he will grade on. Overall, a good teacher but isn't the most organized. I had to do quite a bit of studying on my own.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Two years on, I can say he is one of the best instructors I've had. He clearly explained the grading and exam format. Attending his office hours when in doubt is key, and extra help is invaluable. USE OCHEM as a second language to succeed; the exams, though tough, mirror his lessons. The class structure will help you even outside of his class.
Maybe stick to modeling instead of teaching? Really hard professor

Professor Casselman cares about the success and understanding of his students. Come to lecture and be proactive. He moves at a fast pace and gives good examples in class. Be sure to stay on top of work and the self study material. Very test heavy. Be sure to understand the material, not just memorize it. Good luck guys!

Casselman's lectures are straight-forward and very helpful. Self assessments and any videos posted on Canvas are super helpful so take advantage of the materials he provides!! Tests are very reasonable, never had any content that was not learned. Only complaint is that he crammed reactions before the 2nd midterm. Be prepared to study a lot.

LOVE CASSELMAN! I would say though that his exams are very similar to the optional homeworks he gives you. People fall quarter did get an advantage during their exam with the fire alarm, ruining the curve. overall he is nice

not sure why others complain about his tests, most of the questions are just repeated homework and worksheet problems. He has standards, but they are very reasonable. lectures are easy to digest and he's very open to questions. go to office hours! he teaches you how to solve problems there, otherwise you're on your own

His lectures don't make sense and his exams are ridiculously hard with very little partial credit. His homework makes sense with the content but you have to self-study because his lectures give you next to nothing.
other than being a massive turn on please avoid. he tests us like we have savant like come on man the school has a 70% acceptance rate

I LOVE Casselman! He is such a well thought out and thorough professor for his course material and ensures that we have no problem with the content. His exams are representative of what is taught during lectures as well as the homework assignments provided. He wants students to understand orgo vs memorize. Go to SI, helps alot. 10/10 Would Rec.

Class grade is based upon 2 Midterms (35%), Non-graded worksheets (20%), and a final (45%). EC offered (about 8%) boost. Exams are a mixture of MCQ/FCQ; not difficult, they are just tedious because Casselman looks for minute details in explanation and specific drawings. Going to SI or having a past exam is literally the only way of getting an A.

The class is really hard, but he is an AWESOME PROFESSOR. I think the exams though can be pretty hard, you really need to study ahead and beyond the lectures to pass. There is an assignment every week which helps. but go to SI. Also more improtnaly he's CUTE

AMAZING professor! def the best choice for chem008a. His tests are very fair and doable however his grading policy is a bit harsh. But honestly, he's very kind and approachable and really wants his students to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a great professor and his lectures were SUPER clear, but be ready to practice a bunch and do some self learning because he only really teaches you the basics/what you need to know. The way he grades his tests were probably my least favorite part about taking the course, but as a professor he's really good. His tests again were just horrific.

Casselman is an okay professor. He did his best to be informative and seemed to care about students' understanding. However, his tests were a poor reflection of his lectures. I studied like crazy, attended SI sessions, got extra tutoring, and still struggled to get just average marks. On top of that, he is a tough grader, and he does NOT curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: four words. GREATEST OF ALL TIME. literally the MJ of organic chemistry. its up to you to do the work. his tests are very easy, you just have to know your stuff 100% and ask him for help if you do not.
Casselman makes this class doable with his clear explanations and tons of practice problems. Unstuck ai was a great supplementary tool for me. Definitely put in the work, but it's very manageable.

Best organic chemistry professor. He is caring, supportive, clear and hot. His test though are otherwise difficult. Weekly homework assignments is helpful for this. Other than that, he is one of the best professors I had at UCR.

Casselman is great but be prepared to have to study outside of class heavily. His lecture slides are helpful with learning the material but to pass the class you need to learn how to apply the different mechanisms and reactions. Reaction maps are helpful and find YouTube videos with practice problems and you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's good, easy to get a good grade with work. More work than you think but it's not terrible. Exams are mostly worksheet and homework problems ina different form. Practice lots and you'll be fine!
He is very fair and gives you everything you need ti know for exams. Not an easy A but a doable one. He really cares about teaching and tries his best to give as many A's as possible.

This is my second time having Casselman. His class is not easy but if you put in the work it's very doable I would take him again. Watching YouTube for me helped a lot since I don't just like relying on lecture notes. Making notecards is a must. Find a study habit I had him 8A got a C-(barley passed) and this time I got a B with better test scores.

I feel confident in what I have learned in this class and feel good about the grade I earned. I am extremely thankful I had the opportunity to have Casselman as my professor. He doesn't need to hold office hours or give all the information needed on the test. All you need is true effort to see yourself succeed! Understand don't memorize!! :)
ngl he is the easiest ochem prof at ucr, if you are complaining about his difficulty then you're doomed for future premed classes

Goat. He gave almost 40 point of extra credit for just a 400 point class. and 60 points for just turning in the homework. Anybody who complains about Casselman being hard isn't trying. That final? literally everything from worksheets and homework. Super fair. Lectures are good, and activities are super helpful.

Casselman makes 8B doable. Lots of NMR at the beginning, but he makes it fun and a puzzle. The rest of it is tons of mechanisms, but he tells us what is most important to know for exams. Also does a great job of explaining why things happen, not just telling us what happens. Lots of practice problems. tons of extra credit.

Recorded lectures. Do not cram OChem. Practice exams reflect what is expected on the exam. Textbook problems are overcomplicated. 80% participation in PollEvs for 4 pts e.c. 50% for 2 pts. Refund policy on final: Do good on MT1, MT2 material on final for extra pts. Grading: - MT1 80pts - MT2 80 pts - Final 180 pts* - Self assessments 60 pts. -Q

Casselman is a fun prof. Lectures are interesting and easy to follow, not a lot of things that are extra and not tested. Office hours are low key helpful, he's good for advise about grad school and life too. Or just talk about anime

Hard but not too hard class. It's super clear how to get a good grade in his class. Tests are exactly what is taught. not sure why ppl say that his tests aren't fair, all the same content from lecture and the problems come from the homework. Homework isn't graded, but worth 15% of ur grade. Clickers are extra credit, 20 pts of EC from final too.

Organic Chemistry, the major killer. Haha I don't know it wasn't bad and I think Casselman is cool but I found myself getting lost with trying to study too much and learn too many things at the end. Next time for CHEM008B I'm going to try to make sure to keep it simple and stick with what is being taught and don't ask why and just memorize.

Pro Tip: Do the Organic Chem as the Second Language Book up until alkyne and addition reactions and you will get at least an A-. Fair professor but some topics will require you to watch his short video lectures. I also recommend going to SI as well! Extra credit on the final can bring your grade up a lot depending on how well you do.

you will learn ochem with him. most of the people that don't do well just don't know how to study. he gives you every resource possible to excel in his class. he has no explicit curve but the grading scale  +  extra credit basically gives you about 8-10%. its ochem, itll be hard, so expect to struggle and learn

His lectures don't prepare you for exams fully, they introduce the basic concepts. You NEED to practice independently, for at least an hour a day. He explicitly tests for understanding of reaction mechanics AND theory, so practice both of them.  If you do that, his exams are pretty chill. Harsh grader, grab any EC he gives. SI is invaluable.

It's so hard to rate because he is a great lecturer, he really cares about your understanding, but omg his tests and grading is harsh af. His grading expects you to put what he wants word for word so it can be a struggle. He has great lectures and offers plenty of resources that you NEED to take advantage of to pass. good luck and do all evrything

If you're not a mind reader that can tell what he wants you to say on the exam don't take him. If you don't give him the answer he wants you will not pass, mind you his questions are not specific. reviews.comment: Though he doesn't explain as much as he should, he's a really good ochem teacher and it shows. there was 3 midterms and a final. As long as you do average or above you should pass.
He gives four midterms, no final. He is funny and nice. He gives activity mostly once a week, he really teaches things. Very helpful.

BEST PROFESSOR EVER. Videos are super helpful. Don't be afraid to approach him in office hours, he's really kind and will answer all your questions. Chill dude. Exams are tricky though so you have to study a lot. Made me like a chem class for once. Don't need the book. Make sure you understand his practice tests and lectures as well as videos

Great professor!!!. Lectures are helpful because he explains well. Very helpful during office hours. reviews.comment: Can't deny that he's a good professor, but he's over-hyped.

However, his tests are hard and they are all free response.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Amazing lectures--Would take again

reviews.comment: You must attend every lecture because although he posts ppts, they are lacking the details he gives in class. The tests are straightforward and not meant to trick you like other ochem profs. He does clickers and online quizzes too and makes his own cute videos explaining stuff. Definitely one of the easier ochem professor choices. I'm sad to leave

Best chem teacher ever. He does not trick you on his exams, you won't get anything that he didn't specifically go over in class. Don't need the book to study. Tests are fair and pretty simple. Love this guy and this subject

By far the BEST professor I have ever had for any class ever in my whole life! Highly recommend him!  He really cares about the success of his students. He explains difficult concepts so clearly and well, and is so approachable. His tests are hard (It's ochem so come on) but very fair. Don't take anyone else for Ochem!!!!!

He is the best alchemy teacher in the department! He explains everything really clearly and posts all of his notes online if you miss s also super nice and will add points to your tests if he thinks the TAs were being too hard (which is always). He truly cares about the students.

Honestly, Pro. Cassleman is a great professor! He is really good at explaining concepts clearly. Also, he is patient. He has just 3 midterms and no final. During finals week you take the last midterm. I wish I could take him for chem 12B.  He is the best professor out of all the other professors who teach ochem. Make sure you take him if you can!

Dr. Casselman was the best professor I have ever had at UCR, even though I tend to struggle in chemistry. He went out of his way to help me succeed and went above and beyond to help. If you're going to take OCHEM at UCR, take Casselman. You won't regret it. HE GENUINELY CARES AND WILL HELP YOU PASS if you ask for help. Amazing professor.

Amazing professor would definitely recommend. There are three midterms, no final. The third one is given during final time, but it's weighted the exact same as the other two midterms.  His curves changes depending on the averages of the tests and the practice problems he gives actually help and are not mandatory!

Believe me folks, Matt Casselman is a TREMENDOUS professor. He is a smart, incredible guy. VERY high energy. He wants you to succeed BIGLY. He hosts 2 review sessions per exam, creates supplemental videos to help you, and does in-class activities to help you get proficient with the material. He is truly going to MAKE OCHEM GREAT AGAIN.

Casselman is honestly an angel. Ochem is not an easy course no matter who you take, but he does the best he can to get you prepared for the rest of the series. His lectures are very organized & detailed. He always posts all the notes online and he'll post supplementary videos online to help. His midterms are very fair. 10/10 would recommend.

Great professor who cares about the progress of his students. He moves at a good pace and even uploads supplementary material just to make sure you don't feel left behind. Clicker questions are challenging and helpful. Very patient professor and gives great feedback. Work hard and you'll get the grade you deserve.

The absolute best professor for the subject. Extremely fair grader and very clear in his lectures. Don't be afraid of Organic Chemistry, it requires hard work but it is definitely possible to get a B or higher. Think of it as puzzle solving and less strict memorization.

Good teacher! Cares for student! Do hw, attend lecture and get your clicker points. Get at least a B. Nice curve. Got a C because of finals and midterms being on the same day as BIO. But he is really nice, go to office hours if help is needed! Great guy!

If I  could take Professor Casselman for the entire 12 series, I would. Awesome professor who will do everything he can to help his students succeed. If you're trying to decide between which professor to take for ochem, do yourself a favor and choose Casselman. Grade based on: 3 exams (equally weighted including the final), lab, and participation.

One of the best organic chemistry teachers you will have. Explains everything in great detail and makes sure everyone understand no matter how many questions are asked. He is hard, but only if you make it hard. Do all the reading and all the homework and understand it all, you should be good. THIS IS THE TEACHER YOU WANT FOR ORGANIC CHEMISTRY.

reviews.comment: Great guy, responds to student feedback, puts in the extra hours to make sure students get the material. OChem is a hard class, but this man makes it simple and straightforward.

Straight A's before this class. If you don't have to take this class then don't. TA's were okay. Make sure to study because he does post stuff to prepare you but the grading is what makes passing this class difficult.

Everyone complaining is exaggerating, just work for your grade like you're supposed to. Homework assigns daily however it takes 5 mins max. Do ALL clicker questions and try. LOVED BARTELS. He makes intro to chemistry so interesting. Easy to pass with an A+ if you study and tell your group to do all their parts during discussion. Dont slack off! Hard Professor. Barely got away with a B-. He teaches stuff that are not really applicable for Chem 1A. There's written assignments that you'll need to work with with a TA because they are extremely hard. Office hours, study groups, and practice are the only solution for getting B- or better in this class.

Probably the hardest class I have ever taken. Any opportunity to make the class more work, harder work, or more complicated, Bartels will take it. It left me extremely prepared for the next chemistry but if you have a life outside of chemistry, perhaps a job, other classes, any friends, or if you enjoy sleeping, then be prepared for a hard quarter
How does it feel to be on teaching probation again?  Bartels+Teaching Probation should say it all!

HARD CLASS, but doable. Hard teacher but knows material. teaches to a higher standard than other teachers but gives extra credit and practice tests at end of class. German accent but still quite understandable. ask him a question he will tell u how to do it (but not show).  Overall a decent teacher.  COLLEGE LEVEL CLASS.

He Teach too many things that won't be on the final and the final and midterm is way harder than the other chem class..it will help if you get a good TA ,cause the office hour and written homework will kill you

Bartels was definitely a hard teacher.There was online and written homework, weekly quizzes in discussions and clicker quizzes every lecture, and mandatory office hours.I didn't start to work my butt off until I failed the midterm and ended up getting a B+ in the class because I studied a lot.Get a better teacher if you can though.

I'm going to go ahead and go against the consensus here, at least partially. First off, yes, Bartles is extremely difficult: homework, daily+weekly quizzes, tests. But, he does provide all the information you need to pass. Students who complain about how they were cheated by Bartels are, simply put, inadequate. You will pass if you study, FACT.

First, he has a strong German Accent. Can barely understand him, but still clear at times. He has clicker quizzes that you have to answer at each lecture & mandatory office hours!! This is a HARD CLASS! He taught us Chem 1B & O. Chem in a Chem 1A class! WOW!! Stay away from him!!! It's a hard battle to pass. I barely got a C-

I'm not going to repeat what has already been stated by other reviewers, but it is noteworthy that Prof Bartels makes exams extremely unfair. On the exams, rather than having the same problem but with different constants, you can have a completely different set of problems than the person next to you. This does not fairly evaluate each student...
Super hard professor.  No curve, useless extra credit.  Drop the class if you have a chance.

OMG NO JOKE..BARTELS IS THE HARDEST TEACHER IN THE WORLD..BUT HE TAUGHT ME SOO MUCH AND I WORKED MY BUT OFF TO PASS THE CLASS... I THINK THOSE WHO DROPPED THE CLASS DIDNT WORK HARD ENOUGH BECAUSE THIS IS COLLEGE..NOT HIGHSCHOOL.. WE ARE HERE TO LEARN AND IF YOUR NOT STUDYING TO YOUR FULLEST POTENTIAL.. THEN I DONT KNOW WHAT YOUR DOING HERE.

If you plan to go to med school and you have this professor, think of it like this...Your dream of going to med school is the Titanic...Bartels is the large iceburg...You will sink to the depths of no return and your GPA is sunk as well.

This professor does not treat his students like adults.  He assigns daily homework and required colored pencils on tests.  Forces you to ask a question every week or else you fail.  Average of first midterm was a 33%.  Go to officer hours and you'll get TAs who say use Google cause they don't know how to do anything.(not all of them)

Best C+ I have ever gotten in my life.  I feel bad for all the people that actually worked their asses off and failed.  Also the people who were close to passing but failed since there was no curve.  The evidence is clear in that Bartels doesn't care about his students.  Please pray for the students and their family who paid so much money to fail.

Worst teacher I have ever had. can not teach at all and his office hours consists of 200 people in a small office trying to get help. my friend who had 1a with another teacher got a B and im way smarter than her. his midterms and finals are curved down. example. the minimum requirement is 40 points for a d.if u get 39 points u automatically get a 0
Extremely difficult teacher.  You learn a lot of Chemistry, but your GPA will suffer in return.  Does not curve at the beginning, middle, or end!

I liked Batels because he seemed genuinely interested in what he taught, but he is VERY hard! Be prepared to study and be doing homework ALL the time! I learned more about chemistry than I ever thought I could.  VERY hard midterm but offers a practice final which is exactly the same as the final.  Offers extra credit towards the end of the quarter.

He is a good teacher if you are ready for college. He is indeed difficult but not impossible. You learn an immense amount of Chemistry. Only thing is he is not available during office hours. I suffered through this course but it was well worth it.
Thinks all of his students are chem majors. Gives tons of HW. Teaches material from the entire chem series plus organic chemistry. Worst teacher for and introductory course.

Seriously, Bartles is a really tough professor. He does not kid around when he says only 1/3 of the class will pass. He has mandotory class attendance, due to his idiotic clicker ?s, and if you miss 3 days you automatically fail the course. He doesn't prepaire you well for the midterms.I had a F in the class so I dropped.I would study 20 hrs a week

Hardest chem teacher in the world..avoid his class..if you are in the LC, YOU ARE SCREWED..seriouslly avoid him at all cost..he has a thick accent and is horrible at teaching..gives more homeowrk than necessary..

Horrible professor. You have to attend lectures because there are clicker questions. There's so much homeowrk. Online homework is assigned every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday. Online homework is due before the next one is assigned. Written homework is assigned every Wednesday. Hard midterm. Doesn't curve. HORRIBLE TEACHER!
His class is SUPER hard and some of his TA even say that he's teaching stuff from organic chemistry.
Most difficult chemistry 001A professor. Class average for midterm was 33% and he WILL NOT CURVE ANYTHING! If you choose to take him, good luck.
Hardest Chem001A chemistry professor in Riverside. Midterm was extremely difficult and he doesn't prepare you for any of it.

Bartels...I hated/ and still hate him so much! I swear you think he's out to get you and I was hearing so many bad rumors that he didnt care about his students. the midterm average: 33% and when someone asked whether he would curve if the average was low...he laughed!! this is true, i was there!! Seriously...dont take him, it will lower your gpa! D

Ok im not gonna lie, bartels is a seriously tough teacher, but in order to pass his class you HAVE HAVE HAVE to study hard.  do homework and begin to love ur TA, he will help u!  This professor isnt out to get anyone, he just has COLLEGE expectation. If u get this professor, be ready to work :) He knows what hes talking about and he is super smart!

Worst teacher Ive ever had. Drop this class. There are much easier chem teachers and it sucks sitting there watching others breeze by when you are failing and still having to work 20 hours a week for his class

He is one of the worst professors i have ever has. His extra credit is useless. His midterms are hard because of the amount of material it cover in 50 minutes. If you get bartels you are screwed, it is better to drop the class instead

One of the worst professors I've ever had. He is extremely hard, teaches his class at a ridiculously fast pace, and expects everyone to know everything before he goes over anything. This class caused me so much stress. I felt as if I never had enough time to catch my breath. At times, he lectures on material completely different from the hw assigne

Mr. Ludwig Bartels is without a doubt the worst teacher I have had at this school.  He teaches intermediate aspects of chemistry without even bothering to teach the basics.  He rushes through PPT's and the midterm tests your ability to understand concepts not taught by himself.  Don't take this professor, unless you want a lower GPA.

I believe Mr. Bartels is confusing Chem 1A with an upper division class.  He tries to lower your grade in every way possible until you fail.  No I am not exaggerating; every little thing drops your grade...  Oh! for the midterm...Don't even try. -James H 11AM Class

Very difficult to understand. Can't explain concepts well at all to students. If you want to do well in this class, read the textbook. Flips through his ppt slides without explaining much and tests you on stuff he doesn't go over. Organic chemistry for the first midterm watch out.

All he does it flip through a powerpoint and give us a clicker quiz everyday.  Impossible midterm...It is irrelevant to want he tells you to study.  45 minutes to complete 35+ questions.  Ridiculous amount of homework that is close to impossible to complete on your own.  101 ways to fail. GG

Professor Bartels was AWFUL. I had no idea what we were learning in the class the whole time despite going to SI, office hours, and having an extra study group. His grading was very unfair and he didn't curve that much. He had demos in class that were USELESS, and wasted about 30 minutes of class time. DON'T TAKE HIM!

Bartels is a tough professor. One, during lecture he talks too fast and on top of his heavy German accent it makes it hard to understand him. Two, he makes you attend office hours which I think is a waste of time. Three, he gives a lot of hw, Aris and really hard written hw. And lastly his quizzes and final are super hard.

probably one of the worst teachers in science I've encounter. The structure of the class is horrible, he skips around chapters. If you look at his syllabus compared to other chem classes, its completely different. lectures are completely boring, you constantly see people disrespecting him and leaving class. Even the TAs agree that he horrible!

sure he does fun and appealing experiment now and then but other then that wow his class is a bore for me. the whole mandatory participation is lame and it doesn't even count towards your whole grade it can drop it tho.  he has hw every week aris (online) and written. the written hw is CRAZY intense. final is tough. imo he is a no for me.

If you're a visual learner, this might be the class for you. His lectures consist of demos & videos mostly. Homework&Quizzes are mostly calculations. Don't slack off, it'll hurt you! read read read! study study study!!!

This class goes two ways, if you study and keep up you'll actually learn a lot. His method of teaching by giving weekly quizzes and hw is way better than midterms. Yet you can do practically nothing and still pass. I got a C+ and had NO idea what was going on all quarter. The final is crazyy hard, not multiple choice but was curved. Get him!

The easiest chem teacher out there I have no clue what was going on all quarter and I still got a B+. HW was easy just go to mandatory office hours and they do it for you. There were no midterms only a final worth 1/3 your grade but he tells you everything on it and gives you examples. The curve was ridiculous it was out of 250 and 100 was a B-.

He was such an easy teacher! I did nothing basically for the whole quarter except go to class and get extra credit his class was so freaking easy!!! Gives lots of extra credit but accent and stuttering is very annoying!

Dr. Bartels is a great professor. I definitely recommend taking him. If you are stuck between taking Webster or Bartels, take Bartels, he is MUCH better. Be aware, however, that you need clickers (mandatory attendance) and homeworks are hard. He posts previous midterms, which are very similar to real midterms. Overall, he is one of my favorite.

He is a great teacher! All the hard work he makes you do help out a lot in preparing for the midterms and final. Theres 3 midterms and 1 final and because there are so close to one another, it keeps the material fresh in your mind. Only bad thing was his accent, but you get used to it within the first couple of weeks. = )

Comes off as a difficult class and professor, but as the quarter goes on, he cuts the class a bit of slack. Good professor, but homework questions (as well as test questions) are somewhat ambiguous. Do the homework, because its an easy 30% of your overall grade. Not a bad class, and a pretty good professor.

Bartels does a fairly decent job of explaining things. He's hard to understand the first couple lectures until you get used to his acent. But his demos are REALLY COOL (explosions, burning stuff etc.)

Professor Bartels is an amazing professor. During the course of the quarter, you might think he is hard, but in all honesty, you will appreciate it in the end. The best part about his class is that he makes the otherwise dull topic of Chemistry interesting, and lectures are entertaining. If you study, you will do well. I got an A+.

Professor Bartels is an amazing professor. During the course of the quarter, you might think he is hard, but in all honesty, you will appreciate it in the end. The best part about his class is that he makes the otherwise dull topic of Chemistry interesting, and lectures are entertaining. If you study, you will do well. I got an A+.

Bartels is hard to understand. Yeah, it's hard to work with him at first, but all that extra credit we had really helped me out. The previous years exams really helped a lot too. The Powerpoints are pretty useless sometimes, but read the book. That's basically all it's from.

Bartels is Brutal. His class is so hard. His accent can make things hard also. He doesnt explain things well either. He is really mean and intimidating. The only saving grace for this professor is his insanely generous curve. If you have a choice dont take him. It isnt worth stress.

He's an ok professor...if you can avoid him do it. You won't learn anything from his class. He's eager to help out and ok at office hrs. but overall you walk away without learning anything. Do ALL the extra credit...and do well on the quizzes and homeworks. Plus get A's on atleast three of the exams and your good to go. But again AVOID him if you c

Not a bad professor but can be hard. He does a lot of demonstrations that can help to visualize some of the concepts but does expect students to have a certain understanding of the material prior to coming to the lecture. However, if you get confused go to his office hours. Seriously, it helps!
he sucks, he is not a good general chem teacher, you probably wont learn anything from his class and his homework are horrible...too hard, including his tests and midterms.
Bartels is a difficult teacher, avoid him if you can.  If you do get stuck with him, be sure to attend all his lectures and discussion as this class is very difficult.

He is only easy because of the extra credit he gives you. However, you are going to have to fight for those points as they are usually contests in the class so you're going against 100+ people trying to get 20+ pts for midterms. He stutters way too much and he doesn't help you much, he tells you to Google it instead of explaining it.

Top notch professor. Good class if you actually are in college to learn something rather than waste your time and your parents' money; not so good if you like to come to class smelling of brandy. I dunno, people who say his exams are too hard must be of the brandy variety 'cause I got over 100% on the final. In summary: he's too hot to handle!
not really hard class, you can make up with extra credit points
bartel was not that bad of a professor, midterms and final exam are very similar to the actual one, gives alot of extra credit points, only bad thing was his accent

Seriously, Ludwig is not a bad professor and this is not that hard of a class. he kind of makes the class entertaining. there is a lot of extra credit points that you can get. he covered some basic o-chem stuff like naming, but it does help in chem 112a. overall,  don't try to avoid him.
Strict Attendance/Homework Policy. Thoroughly covered all topics and tests were fair. Unfairly given low marks

Very hard be ready for alot of reading and individual studying. Becuz what he lectures is pointless and isnt on the exams. you must read the book,and teach urself most of the stuff.There are a lot of Ochem questions midterms so be sure and study that. Find some some old midterms if possible, because there are exactly the same. GOOD CURVE at end.

Take someone else, unless of course you like to read the chem book, and in addition to that love to read powerpoint slides. He should stick to his research and leave the teaching to people who actually care if the students understand or not
Make's you memorize the periodic table and makes you use color pencils. enough said. I had to work my ass off to get a B. The other subjects I had taken suffered as a result.
He is a nice guy and makes a strong effort to making sure you know what you are doing.

He is a hard teacher but if you study enough you will do fine. Do the practice quizzes because they are just like the real ones. If you read the chapter thoroughly and do every exercise and example throughout the chapter, you'll do fine. I got an A in his

The demotion of your grade after missing either lecture or homework put me in a hole quick. I had missed so much that I had an F after the first 3 weeks. But all I had to do was talk to him, he actually listened. I ended up with a B, happy ending.
hate his class and could not understand a word he was saying, good god get someone that speaks English! Plus he's lectures not helpful : you practicly teach yourself. Come on! HE sucks #*^&
His class is really hard, but his curve is weird. I just got barely a couple more points than the class average (which were always low low F's) and oddly pulled a B in his class.
terrible teacher w/ thick accent and monotone lectures. super hard midterms and even more impossible final. only gave 95 min. to complete final out of required 180 min. avoid at all costs.

this guy is really hard... i studied my *** off for this class and ended with a C+, u really have to study ALOT for this class. and he is not helpful at all. So you have to really teach urself and its pointless to go to lectures cause he has a really thick accent.  gives some ec but its hard to get. good luck

his class if ridiculous.  he gives extra credit, but in order to receive extra credit, you have to earn over 2o pts on the webquiz.  each question is worth 4 pts.  therefore, receiving extra credit on the webquiz is impossible at times.  his lectures are boring and no one pays attention because he has a thick accent.
No Comments

Like what the last person said.. he's a very hard teacher. Midterms are really hard..has  few o-chem questions.  Lectures are very boring. Impossible to get an a really good grade.  Take wilson.avoid this guy. You cant use a periodic table on tests. Screwed my grade over

Accent is horrible. Lectures are boring. If you go to his office hours, it seems like he doesnt want to help you. He goes over o-chem**** in 1b! stupid. I dont like the class. Wish i had wilson or even webster.

This class is hard work. Homework is assigned everyday and you turn it in next class meeting. Welcome back to high school huh. His exams are nightmares also, one midterm is a take home that took a weekend to complete and the other is 3 hours long. If you have old exams use them.
tests are like his practice tests!!! easy class!!! and he gives extra credit!!!

Tests are undescribably difficult.  Get practice tests and do them, then ask him and T.A. for help if you are confused.  work together on homework if you know smart ppl.  Difficult to pass class or get a high grade unless you are dedicated to trying!
This was the easiest class I had all quarter. It only took 2-4 whole days to finish the homework. Lecture notes do not prepare you for exams by any means.
He failed me.  I was only 5 points from a C-. He sucks.

Not a hard class to pass. Practice ALL the free responses and time urself to make sure u can get through them easily during the midterms and final. The multiple choices are fairly hard. Dont sit too close to the front... he does a lot of in class experiments!
His practice exams are exactly like the real tests...people who complain just didn't study because that class was a piece of cake.
tests are hard, accent is thick, lectures are boring, this lower division course is almost like an upper divisin couse cause it's so hard.
I took his Chem 1B class for spring of 04.  I think he class is really easy.  The pratice tests are almost the same as the real ones.
the material he teaches in class isn't on the test. the test is comepletely different from the material he explains, and the practice tests he gives as examples.
Very very tough... you've really gotta learn those materials if you wanna get a decent grade in his class. But I suppose he prepares us well for Chem IC. =)
Very smart, helpful, although the accent is a little tough to get around sometimes, especially at 8am. homework and tests are frighteningly difficult - work together and you'll do better.
couldn't understand a word he said
He has hard exams, but he lets you gain points in class games that can greatly help.
No Comments

we was hasing problem too muching in his classing. this professor killing the**** outing of us. dude he is extremely tough, if you take him that means you are basically analytically, experimentally, theoritically and .... ****ed
he gives horrible advice. "don't see me unless u want to study abroad".
He's a really good professor but hard on grading. You have to go to office hours if you need help. He's very cooperative on helping students.
He is tough.
man he is hard and i think his test are hard too. but good teacher, we knows his stuff
No Comments

The only options for grading on certain assignments are 100% or 70%. Sometimes, he grades an assignment as a 70% then will give short, but positive feedback. He grades drafts the same as finals, so you have to write finals instead of drafts. I will admit this difficult grading style has improved my writing, but it has made me dread writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: This teacher is tough. I had an emergency surgery, he said that he would give me extra time to do assignments, and locked me out and gave me 0's. It wasn't until I emailed him every day and contacted the dean that he gave me an extension that he said he would, and even then, he didn't update my grade for another semester.
Stressful and assigns an unreasonable amount of online work per week.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Ive never enjoyed writing in general, but this professor really motivated me. His class got me thinking a lot about the world, and made me want to read the assigned readings everyday. This class is not easy, but he is very willing to help out during office hours. I give him so much respect for all that he does!
He's a good teacher but a hard grader. His instructions are vague but if you ask him after class or email him you should be all set.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof Crago made class SO enjoyable, and I'm someone who HATES english. He's extremely reasonable & lenient. You can still get participation credit when you're gone if you let him know ahead of time. GO TO OFFICE HOURS. He gives you all the advice on how to improve essays. For summer: Final was ONLY a 5-10min presentation of the last essay.

I'm terrible at english so I was dreading to take this course (I've gotten a C+ in 1B) but Professor Crago made it easy and worth while. He's an interesting person to converse with and super laidback. He doesn't require you to buy any books!! Attendance is mandatory for a good grade but I'm glad I made the effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Crago is the best professor for English I ever had. As someone who hates writing and received Cs in both my previous 1A and 1B classes, I can honestly say he is a gem. He makes writing more about the process rather than caring about minor grammatical issues and syntax. Go to lecture, office hours are greate discussions and you'll love it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: amazing professor. really enthusiastic and smart which made lectures interesting and worthwhile. approachable and totally willing to work with you in his office hours. probably wrote some of my best papers in his class thanks to his help and suggestions

Rly nice guy, he wants u to always improve & write the best essay possible. Very good, constructive criticism on essays. Very hippie guy, but he's rly woke & makes class interesting. He has a sense of humor & I appreciated him making me a better writer. Would take him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Would take again

reviews.comment: Great professor. If you don't like English that much, he's the right professor because he does not make it very English oriented. More like he discusses topics which inspire ideas to write. I hate English but his class is very enjoyable.

I took her class last year, and I loved her class. Her lecture slides are well-structured and easy to understand. There was an in-person midterm and an online final, and both of them were not difficult as long as you understood the lecture slides.

I honestly wouldn't recommend you take this class with her. Even tho this is an econ course, like 50% of the assignments are doing excels. Her lectures are not very helpful and most of the time i dont understand what shes trying to explain. There is one project split into 3 parts that basically replace the final and midterm.
didnt teach anything and didnt the final exam grade. Its up to ta for your discussions grade and if they are strict you are
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: there is no structure of this course you didnt know your grade until the last day before grades were due doesn't even releases the final exam grade
didn't take for Econ 002 but for an Econ elective. just steer clear, professor didn't teach us anything.

Homework is easy and could be done in minutes. Lectures are not mandatory, but they contained PollEvs that were extra credit, so I recommend going! . The material isnt that hard to learn i promise and the math is extremely easy. Professor was pretty cool and had some nice jokes here and there. Just go with the flow of the class and youll be chillin

Pretty noticeable Korean accent. Lectures got very mind-numbing at times, but she can be entertaining with the occasional pop culture references. Her notes don't reflect her lectures well, so if you want a full understanding as to what her notes are saying, go to lecture. Midterms (2) and final you're allowed a cheatsheet. Final was pretty hard

Didn't want to take the class but is required. Easy honestly didn't study just used cheatsheet she would allow us to have. Homework isn't hard double with optional discussion. Was worried for the math portion very easy.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The content of this course in general is straightforward, as it is ultimately an introductory course. However, I think some of the concepts could have been explained in a substantially different way that would have been universally more receptive to students.

Honestly my GOAT. Great lectures, and caring professor. Definitely agree with people saying that her accent sometimes were difficult to understand. But overall one of the best lectures I've been taken this year and definitely no regrets.
She was alright.
she's a good lecturer just a little hard to understand sometimes with her accent. final was kind of weird she pulled out questions that were odd but it wasn't that bad.

I found what little I did see of her to be kind of rude. Lots of her announcements included her saying "not to email her about this" and that she wouldn't reply even if you did. Well, let's just say she didn't reply to *any* emails, not just the ones about the announcements. Her in-class demeanor was similar and she was hard to understand.
Very good teacher, test heavy but just attend every lecture and you'll be good. Generous with extra credit if you put the work in

Professor is great and provides good examples. Attendance is required for lectures (pollev) and there is extra credit opportunities. Discussion attendance wasn't required for this quarter but it is helpful to go because TA's give practice questions. Most of the grade depends on two midterms and the final, the rest is homework and participation.
She was amazing. One midterm, one final, weekly homework that was super easy and quizzes. Her exams are very fair and if you study the slides and homework you will do great.

2x Midterms worth 25% of your total grade EACH, with 1x Final exam worth 30%. Last 20% being Homework and Participation. Extremely difficult to get a high score unless you score very well all 3x exams. And not many opportunities to make back points other than one 5 point extra credit opportunity for attending EVERY lecture. Not an easy class at all

Very good professor! She is great at explaining concepts and posts her slides online. I would still go to lecture because she explains her notes thoroughly and she does random attendance checks. The homework and discussion sheets are helpful. Just make sure you understand concepts and it will be easy!
Very good professor, though difficult to understand at times. Nonetheless, Professor Choi is very kind and gives out several extra credit opportunities.

Really nice and chill professor. Her tests are quite easy if you study and the homework hardly took like 10 minutes to finish. Her study guides and HW's are pretty much like the tests so use those! If you don't get something, just show up to her office hours and she's more than happy to help and just simply talk with you about random things.
Really easy class, gave a lot of extra credit! She also gives practice material that is similar to the quiz, midterm, and final.

The subject and class itself should be fairly easy so I don't understand how a professor could be so hard to understand from. She does have an accent however it's more than that. She teaches the subject as if we are already experts? She's also not open to constructive criticism or complying with anyone's needs for more explanation.
Really good lectures and engaging overall. Gives lots of study guide material and practice problems for upcoming exams and quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great econ professor at UCR! Lectures are very imformative but heavy with info. Would recommend to write down hw's in your notes as they are a key to doing well in quizzes, midterms and final. Overall the best professor I had for econ at UCR!
Makes very easy concepts very hard to understand.

This was probably my favorite class that I've taken at Berkeley. Learning how to run a research model on the supercomputers, applying the theory we learned was an incredibly valuable experience! Thank you so much Dr. Ivey!!

Honestly she is a very nice person but as a professor she isnt even decent. She will be late to class everyday. Sloppy handwriting. Was not able to cover all of the material she was required to go over. This made a whole generation of ChemEs fall behind on their basic learning. Where ever she head off to next, i wish you guys luck.

heard mixed reviews about Ivey coming in. She was definitely the best prof of online classes I had this summer (school all online bc of covid). Class was pretty interesting. She had pictures of some of the controls from her own experiences working in industry that were pretty cool.

Overall one of the better profs in the department. She made class expectations very clear and was always accessible outside of class. I couldn't always follow the in-class lectures (even though she had great energy for an 8 am class), but she responded to every single email and made accommodations for me outside her given office hour

Ivey doesnt post her lectures beforehand (usually the morning of class) so be prepared to take notes quickly since she goes fast. The material is simple and she allows cheat sheets. Her exams were easy and homework is easy as well. She isnt the best lecturer but you should pass by doing homework, participation, and studying formulas.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Amazing Professor! A solid grade breakdown and posts every lecture! Super friendly and accessible outside of class!

With all do respect she is a really busy professor and human so she makes mistakes. However she arrives to class late and her lectures are plagued by bad handwriting. Examples often take too long or sometimes she does problems and says the textbook is wrong. It made me want to change my major.

reviews.comment: I really like Dr. Ivey. I could tell she really cared about the students. Sometimes lectures were tough to follow (it was more the material getting more challenging) but overall this was a great introductory course to the department

She mentioned it was her first time as a professor, but I thought she was a great lecturer. Some of the material was tough, and she did a good job of simplifying it for us. On exams, if you did the homework, you'd be prepared for the exam
Super nice professor, homework is not too hard or too much, tests are basically as what she told you to review and kind of similar to the sample questions

If you in this for film, then you are out of luck . She doesn't teach anything and only teaches one topic. She then pair us in groups with little to no roles and its completely unorganized. She doesn't bother giving good criticism on your assignments so you don't know if you did good or not. she just grades. Would not recommend taking her.
Only one group project of 8 students. You need to make a short film of 10-15 minutes. Really few things to work on other than this.

She's super sweet. Attendance is mandatory. Need to speak twice per class to get full participation credit. Five group video assignments that are easy to do. A short writing response in which you write about the element covered in class that week that you see in the assigned film. No midterm, no final, no quiz. Please take her if you get a chance.

The class is project-based. You have nothing to read or write outside of class. All assignments aim for one thing: shooting films. The first two projects are short 1-2 minute individual films. The third project is a group assignment and serves as the final. It's broken down into different parts, but it's easy as long as you follow the instructions.

This is a large class so most of the work is graded by your TA. This class is lecture-based, with no tests or quizzes. There's no reading or textbook. The assignments are also straightforward: you need to watch a film each week and write a film review. The midterm and final are two super fun individual projects graded more on completion and effort.

She is super sweet and always gives good feedback. We did three projects: two by individuals and one by a group. The group project is also your final. No tests or quizzes, no reading, the only thing you need to do is make some short films. The course is designed to be in person, but she did several online sessions in the latter half of the quarter.

You can tell Professor Catano is passionate about her job through her effort. Her canvas is very organized with posted videos based on topics, lecture slides, and posted readings. In class activities are a big part of the lecture due by the end of the week. Tests moderately difficult, I think the class average for some was a C.

Overall, the class is more tedious than hard. There is mandatory lectures and participation, as well as homework reading and worksheets. But the tests (which there are 4 of) aren't too difficult and aren't cumulative. If you show up and do the work you'll be set up for a good grade.

Lectures are discussion heavy, lots of participation. 4 exams(40MCQ, 50min), non-cumulative, drops lowest one. Provides readings, videos, pre-lecture and lecture slides, and muddiest notes. It may seem like a lot of material, but just learn based off LO's and you'll be fine. Hardest part were exams, questions are written weirdly, mostly conceptual

Her lectures were very fun to attend and its pretty important you show up since she has PollEvs, attendance codes, and in class assignments. There were 4 exams and no cumulative final. She allowed one exam score to be dropped. Study slides and muddiest points. SI sessions were good.
Overall a very easy class. It's very difficult to fail this class, so as long as you show up to lectures, you should at least be able to get a B.

BIOL003 not 005B! She was nice BUT there's a lot of information she goes over for a GenEd class. Not a bio major and this was a lot of work with pre-class, in-class, post-class, lab. She does PollEv for participation and not going to class is what prevented me from an A despite good scores. Study for exams days in advance bc so much material.

reviews.comment: Easiest bio teacher ever. Laura Catano is an excellent teacher who cares for her students. Though she has pre-lecture assignments before every class, it can be quite time consuming. The worst bio professor at UCR, she's like a machine who only cares about how much bio you do in life.

To prepare for exams, go through all the learning objectives and put them in a google doc, and answer them and actively recall them. To help answer the questions go through lecture slides and the “muddiest points” of each lecture. Overall four exams, she drops the lowest one. If you study like this, you will be fine. And she has extra credit.

Honestly easy class if you put the work. Lots of extra credit. easy and fair class, everything on the 4 exams are things that can be found in lecture or pre-learning, and drops the lowest exam and she semi-curves it too, splits the class into half lecture half worksheet, also there is no final exam for this class, overall great professor

this professor dont get me wrong she has good intentions but she is a new professor who thinks we are already in medical school learning about different case studies and things that u dont even need to know for anatomy. She knows how to lecture and answer questions clearly. She does extra credit before every exam. She is easy to talk to and caring. Her assignments are well organized on Canvas. She was very kind and friendly.
Grades too easily.
