reviews.comment: Very transparent about what to expect on exams. If its your first time taking calculus, do yourself a favor and show up to class and pay attention. He makes calculus easy to understand. Honestly, straight up a decent teacher. Would recommend!

A good grade in this class is possible to achieve, but it requires a lot of hard work and dedication. Do not skip discussion and do all of the homework! Prof. Curtis talks pretty fast and moves on pretty quickly in his lectures so make sure to keep up. Generally speaking, this class with Curtis is extremely time-consuming, but not too challenging.

I am not a math person but Prof. Curtis was great at leading lectures in a way that was easy to follow. He is friendly and gives great feedback after every exam. Don't be afraid to ask him questions, he has a 100 ways of explaining a single concept! Exams consist of questions similar to the hardest questions on the homework; you have been warned.

Prof. Curtis is a great teacher! Yes, the course is rigorous but if you do all the problems he assigns for hw (optional but RECOMMENDED), you will do very well in the class. Also, go to his office hours because they are extremely helpful!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Curtis goes extremely fast during lectures. If this is your first time taking calculus, I recommend taking fewer classes. There is a quiz and worksheet (basically every week), two midterms, and a final. The tests were very hard and homework/practice exams did not help.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: If you have no experience in calculus then I sympathize the struggle you will endure. Curtis will make you feel as if you are understanding the topic & makes it seem so simple until the exams which are very difficult and only free response. The class is based on the success on your exams. He admits he does not do a good job teaching the subject.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I wish that he could actually help students by going over topics. He really needs to put more effort on helping students understand. This class is really difficult and make sure to go to lectures. He goes really fast.

Professor Curtis is hard. He goes very fast and tries to complete as many topics as he can which makes it very hard to understand each and every concept. There is a quiz every week and the discussion sections are heavily weighted. The midterms are hard and it makes you work a lot. Take all other easy classes if you have to take math 22 with Curtis.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Curtis is alright. Work hard and do all the practice problems and go to SI and you will pass with a high grade. He curves the grade and so his passing rate is high. If you put in all the work you should be able to pass the class. His class goes so fast that sometimes students need the practice so always go to office hours to get help.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is pretty old school so all of his slides are handwritten and not posted online. His joke are not funny at all and he it's almost like his goal is to fail every student. The homework is nothing like what he shows in class and is extremely time consuming. Weekly quizzes are doable if you study but the score you get is based on the TA's.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Do the online hws, go to discussion, and go to lecture and you will pass with at least a B. He's sarcastic and tries to make math fun. Tests are easy if you go over the notes and online hws.
Go to lecture and office hours, do the all the homework he assigns and you will pass the class. I did bad on the second midterm but still passed the class with an A-

Lectures are notes he made 10 years ago that barely help you with your homework. You basically have to teach yourself the lessons and good luck on the midterms because they don't look like the homework at all. If you do take the class, take easy classes with it because this is extremely time consuming.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Professor Curtis is honestly one of my favorite professors at UCR and I am not even a math major. He had office hours in a room full of white boards and he was kind enough to let myself and my study group use that office till 11pm to study for the final. He is so kind and wants you to do well! I highly recommend. Yes, his tests are hard though.

Most of the students at UCR that have had him dislike him because of his class. More than HALF fail his class. He assigns 3 midterms, quiz every week, online homework, and the final! His class needs ALOT of time. He will be the ONE that will make you leave UCR, change your major, and dislike your life at the moment. Wish I NEVER took/ came to UCR.

his class you need special effort. In his class you need to learn very hard by yourself, he can not give you any help. He has a lot of homework to complete, but he does not explain these operations. when you ask him a question he alway answers you "I think you are right". if you send an email to him, you will wait for a long time, and you can't get

Honestly, Curtis gives you all the tools to get an A in the class, it's just a matter of whether or not you make the effort to use those tools. He pretty much tells you exactly what's going to be on each quiz, and he gives you clear outlines of what's on each exam. He's not hard as long as you do all the work.

I hated how he taught Calculus. He reuses his notes from last quarter or year and only goes over easy problems. He does give you study guides for midterms and final but some of the study guides, he doesnt give you the answer sheet. I struggled so hard. I would recommend taking three classes instead of four if taking Calc with Curtis.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I honestly did not think I would pass because 1) I have never taken Calc before 2) I heard Curtis was difficult. I honestly was terrified so I got all the help I could get. It's not that bad of a class if you go to SI Sessions (if available), ask your TA, or ask the professor for help. Definitely, do the recommended hw questions. They help a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Love him! His class is easy if you know basic calculus. He gives you study guides and practice questions. I thought ut was an easy class.

This class & its lectures are fast-paced since it's 16 weeks of math (semester) crammed into 10 weeks (quarter). I hated Webassign problems but they were selected by the math department & not him. Quizzes are okay since problems are literally from assigned practice book problems. Funny guy. Class is curved with about an 88% as an A.

I love math but after taking him I hate it. He stands in the front and reads off his notes he already has. Always jokes around and makes fun of students. His midterms and final are soooo hard. He gives study guides for them but never puts those types of questions. If you want to pass avoid him!

Absolutely the worst professor I've ever had. I am an A student, and he just failed me. He won't help during office hours. His teaching style is awful--he just stands at the board and points rather than explaining. His TAs don't understand the material either because it's so difficult. Hard exams. I truly believe he enjoys failing students.

You must be ready to put in time on the class the self. It goes by pretty quick due to the Prof. teaching one section in lecture and learning another with your TA. There's quizzes every week(assigns possible problems) except for when a midterm or final is coming up. If you do not take a quiz in discussion a worksheet is provide not impossible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: If math wasn't a requirement for my major, I would have loved to avoid it, but Curtis made it semi-enjoyable. He is very clear in his examples and is really patient with his students. Yeah, he can be snarky, but chances are if he is snarky with you, you deserve it. He is exam heavy, but does a ton to prepare you, even by outlining them beforehand
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Of all the math professors i've had, Mike curtis is the absolute worst. Am i mincing on words? Far from it. He doesn't exactly work through the problems with the students during lecture, as he simply just points and talks. Rather than helping students out with what's going to be on the midterm he keeps things vague as well. Incredibly frustrating.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Lectures were boring and everyone seemed lost. Only 1/3 of the class would pass his midterms, yet he didn't curve.

I took calc my senior year of high school, and seeing the material before definitely gave me an advantage since the course is so quick. His class is not impossible, but it is improbable to pass if YOU fail to put the work in. He's very generous by giving quizzes based off of assigned homework problems, and there's plenty of supplemental help.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Did well because I took Calc in high school. Class was relatively easy for me but I can understand why so many people were struggling. He goes at an incredibly fast pace, esp for ppl that have never learned calc before. Goes on tangents during lectures, b/ still smart to go to all lectures/discussions. Definitely have to try to pass.

A lot to learn and can be difficult, if you have never seen the material because he tends to review the material very quickly and uses discussion sections to teach an additional topic/quiz/worksheet. He gives extra credit in his midterms and final. Discussion and online hw was slightly curved. If you work hard, its not impossible.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: As long as you go to the lectures you should be fine. His notes in class are very clear, and as long as you pay attention, you should be able to do the homework. He accepts questions during class and will slowly go over practice problems so that it is easier to understand. By no means is his class easy, but it is reasonable for a calculus course.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Curtis was a great professor and his lectures are pretty easy to understand. If you go to discussions and lectures regularly, then I think you will do fine. Math 22 should also be a bit easier than any other Calculus course because it also doesn't go over any trig like a regular Calculus course does.
His exams are nothing like his homework and review. Concepts are the same but he mixes too many topics together to make the test shorter.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Hard grader. Take this class with another professor. I wish I had done that.

This professor really outlines each and every step involved in math, sometimes it's a nuisance, but in the end super helpful. He really cares about you learning thee material. Very picky on how to grade, so really pay attention & try/study.   Definitely attend office hours!

Curtis is a very tough grader. He is by far the hardest math instructor I've had.  I wouldn't recommend this class. No matter how hard you try in his class the midterms and the final are simply way to hard. He is also not very approachable which makes it very difficult.

At first Curtis seems like a laid-back clear-cut professor, but once you take his first midterm you realize that it's a very hard class. His midterms are way harder than his examples or review problems. I am pretty good at math and I struggled in his class. I wouldn't take him again honestly.

Curtis is an amazing professor. He is clear and organized in his lectures. I really learned a lot from him and he really cares for his students. The class however is not easy. You need to go to lectures, do the book problems, get help if your are stuck on something, and practice! His midterms and final are hard but they are passable.

Professor Curtis was an excellent professor! He taught precalculus differently than the teacher I had in high school. Mathxl was a pain because I don't like doing math online, but its easy to get a 100% on the homework. His exams are tough, but do all the mathxl problems and book problems you should be good. He is always available in office hours.

This class is easy as long as you put in the effort. I did all the practice problems from the books before the quizzes and redid them before every midterm and I got high As on both the midterms and a 105 on the final. Make sure to really review the subjects you are unsure about and go to office hours if you need help. He is a pretty funny guy

He was an alright professor, old handwritten slides, talks a lot, thinks he's all that, but knows his math. I didn't pass his class but I always did the homework and more- the midterms were killer hard. Best advice: don't try to memorize the math, try to understand it for the tests.

He was one of those professors who would give you easy homework, but give you hard problems on a midterm.... And he takes videos of student when taking a final... He literally whipped out his GoPro. Extremely rude and thinks he is the smartest professor known to man kind.

Make sure you go to lectures! You will have to resort to the textbook and it can be unclear at times! You can get an A in the class if you take the quizzes seriously! Prepare two days before the quiz and you should be good. Exams are sort of difficult, but if you do well on the quizzes, then the exam should be no problem.

Of all the math teachers I've had, Curtis is probably the worst. He only teaches the bare minimum concept and sometimes the homework from that section is completely different than what he teaches. He probably does this because he expects you've taken precalc recently, but if you tend to forget math from 2 years ago you'll need to work harder

His lectures make sense. If you skip class you better ask a friend for notes and an explanation or go to his office hours. In office hour he is VERY CLEAR AND EXTREMELY HELPFUL. You should do the non-mandatory book problems it helps. He makes the tests with them. He is funny and nice, may come off as sarcastic at first. TESTS ARE HARD SO STUDY

He's makes concepts a lot easier. If you do the hw you should do great on quizzes. For midterms leave time to double check you work, it can make the difference. Everything is fairly straightforward but he does try to confuse you at times. I never got a textbook I just rented it from the library and scanned the pages. Overall hes a good teacher

You will have to work for your grade in this class. Lectures are strait forward, but the midterms and final will be tough. On the bright side he pulls quiz questions strait from the practice problems that week, so be sure to do those. Lecture is not mandatory, but discussion is there is a POTD worth 3 pts each and quizzes once a week.

Curtis is pretty helpful when you need help clarifying material . Most lectures, he tries to squeeze in a 5 min break or dismiss you 5 mins early. If you took precalc in high school and are familiar with the material, you'll get a B/A. Textbook q's are quiz questions, so borrow or rent the book!
One of my favorite teachers. His lectures are super clear and great to attend.
Curtis is a great professor, and he was always willing to help if you were willing to put in the effort.

At first I thought I was going to do really well in his class because I was acing all my quizzes. But then I take the midterm and he throws the hardest possible questions at you. He's helpful if you go to office hours. I do like that he changes the grading scale though so that a 76% is still considered a B- and he drops your lowest three hw grades.

Makes everything look easy during lecture, but then goes and  then gives the hardest problems he possibly can. Hadn't taught the course in about 5 years until now, and made mistakes in class. Almost half the class failed.  Really egotistical and arrogant man. Have no idea why there are any good reviews about him. Good luck if you have him.

Overall, he is an alright professor. Make sure you shut off your cellphone during an exam because he WILL fail you. He's highly insensitive  and unnecessarily "strict." He's not even strict! He's actually just mean.

He is a very arrogant and rude professor. Give long lectures, however half of the time is spent joking around and giving irrelevant information such as his hobbies and opinions on his other classes. Rude, profane, and not a good professor

Curtis is an awesome professor. I would suggest buying the textbook and going to class. Curtis assigns problems from the book but he does not collect it. Also, by doing the problems, you will most likely do  great job on your quizzes and midterms.

Straightforward and student-friendly. If you attend lecture and discussion, you'll pass! Highly suggest you get the book because although the book work is not collected it is SO helpful, seriously, if you do the book practice you'll do so much better on the quizzes, exams and final. I got ABs on my exams! I'm not even good at math, def recommend!!
He and his TAs do a great job of explaining concepts. If you have questions, don't be afraid to ask or go to office hours

Curtis is a passionate teacher and he will help you if you ask. He will not go over something once he feels that he has made it clear so ask questions in lecture! His midterms were so difficult to me! I got a D on the first one and a low C on the second, but his final was so easy! I only got one wrong and got an A in it. His jokes are not funny lol

Prof Curtis was honestly one of the best math teachers I've ever had. My advice: go to each and every lecture because that's how you'll learn how to do the problems in the easiest way possible (how it'll look on the midtermsfinal too). There's a lot of homework, but you will actually learn math if you commit your time to this class.

I took his class, I liked it but when it came to the final exam it was surprisingly harder than the midterms. I had a B average on midterms but I got a 65% on final exam, which is a C- in his class. I studied a lot in his class. He'll make you understand the material, but he'll challenge you to it. He won't be easy, but he'll make you enjoy math.
He honestly made me love math
didn't like him to much

He is a terrible lecturer. I failed the equivalent to this class in high school and I'm failing again because he is a distracted lecturer. He doesn't explain material thoroughly and doesn't seem to care about the concerns of the students. His tests are extremely hard and are very different from MathXL and his lectures.

He is ok. Exams are VERY hard, much more than the homework or quizzes. Explains the material very good. Lots of homework, TA sessions are mandatory. Quiz every week and also a graded problem in class every week.

Curtis is a great teacher. Although he does make mistakes and rarely typos on midterms (which he did once to our class) he is an excellent teacher. During midterms and finals he is very strict about UCR's test taking policy, but as long as you study and do the HW on Math XL, it will be a piece of cake.

He's funny and talks about his life experiences in poker and buying cars while he lectures just to keep the class from sleeping. He gives 5 minute breaks, and he uses good examples to explain the concept. Really good at explaining and gets to the point.

He is a very rude and arrogant person. While he explains math decently, his personality is such that it detracts from the overall experience. He is very disorganized with his test taking, and and is lazy. His tests are hard, and math xl is a whack system to do hw on.

He is clear and consistent with his teaching but he can be really annoying and rude. He makes the lessons harder than they actually are. Quizes are super easy. Midterms are okay just study for them. Do ALL of the homework he assigns. Other than that his okay..

He was funny and often talked about gambling and poker. I was terrible at math, but got an A in his class. Make sure to study for quizzes and do the practice problems to study for midterm and final. Lecture attendance does help.
He was clear, and taught very well. He was funny, and very chill. The tests were very clear and everything we were tested on he had already gone over.

hated the professor. he was extremely arrogant, annoying, and straight up rude. however, the material wasn't too hard. i hate math and ended up with a B+ just make sure you have a good ta and do the hw and youll succeed.

He is an awesome teacher! very funny and tries to keep the class interesting! do the practice problems he assigns and you will ace the quizes and midterms! Easy to get an A if you put the work and effort in!
does not care about class or the students and very unorganized

Curtis, is a very helpful and funny teacher.  He tries his best to make everyone comfortable in class. Even though I hate math I did not really hate the class. Do the practice quiz problems he provides you with before quizzes and you should ace them.

I took his class last quarter and all I have to say is that he is a bomb professor! He explains everything very well and makes class fun as well! he makes sure that you comprehend the material, if not he's always open to meeting with you during his office hrs. Great teacher and wish i had him for math 22! highly recommend taking his class!
Great professor
Really funny guy and a good lecturer, I used to really hate math but he made me comfortable with it, buy the textbook the quizzes and practice problems for exams come from it and it helps your grade

really hate math but Curtis really made me hate it much less. he is really helpful and his way of explaining is really weird but really helps because he of the real life examples he  does using the students. one big word of advice is to get get the book! if you get the book youll have an advantage. over all not to bad.
Professor Curtis is an amazing instructor. One of the best math teachers I've ever had. The material is taught very well, and super easy to comprehend. Great experience.
Curtis is a phenomenal teacher! By far the best math teacher I have ever had! He really makes you understand the material. Try and get him for every math class you take!!!!! I wish he taught 8B...

I actually understand math!! its HARD but u need to STUDY and keep practicing, best math professor coz u actually learn, w/other math classes ur on ur own but not here. in order to do good u have to know some precalc if not ull have to put more time in it. I loveeee the curve

He is overall a great teacher. He knows what he is taking about and clearly explains everything and will answer any question. The midterms and final are challenging, but he provided book problems for practice. He is a bit arrogant, but he is not boring. take his class!

The coolest math teacher I've had.  Very funny, approachable, and makes going to class fun.  Be warned its not an easy class.  His exams are difficult and require you to put time into really grasping the material.  He is fair in his grading though and also curves some tests.  Quizzes are from the book.  Overall, the best math teacher I've had!
worst math teacher ever!!all he does is talk about his cars!!very hard to approach

This teacher is one of the clearest math teachers I have ever had in my life. If this man was my teacher for high school math I might be a math major now. He is very clear. Very concise and some of his lectures are really funny and amusing if he gets into one of his stories. A very good teacher.

Very fair teacher. He explains everything with clarity and gives many examples. He makes himself available for help. He gives helpful math problems before midterms, quizzes, and final. I am not saying that it is an easy A. The class is fair and has an appropriate level of difficulty.If you work hard in the class, you will see positive results.
Awesome professor!! Quizzes/Exams are based on practice questions from the book. Very great at explaining things as well.

Professor Curtis is a really informative teacher. He is very fair in grading and assignments. Attendance is mandatory in order to pass the class. Quiz every Friday in additional lecture. Takes the time to review midterm and final. Quizzes are based on same homework problems. Very approachable!

This professor was definitely one of the worst math instructors I've met and encountered throughout my academic career as a student... His grading in regards to midterms and finals are ridiculously difficult, Good luck passing.
One of the best math teachers I've ever had.  The midterms and final are a bit difficult, but as long as you study hard you should have no problem passing the class. Use office hours!

Great professor. Lectures are very neat, organized and clear. Do the recommended problems. His exams and final are a bit challenging but you'll be fine if you study. Curve is alright. Overall, he is an awesome professor.
Best math teacher I've ever had. Made trig crystal clear and is hilarious.

Seriously, this guy is a big meannie.  I went to all his lectures and only some stuff made sense. I often had to refer to the book to understand it. He also had a problem with people sitting in the back row. He even yelled at a few people during midterms/final because of it. He seriously needs to take a chill pill. SERIOUSLY!
he loves B==D

Best math teacher I've ever had! Attend lecture and pay attention! He goes over everything with clear notes. Plus, he tells stories and jokes :) DO THE HOMEWORK. Even though he doesn't check all of it, he takes quiz questions from it and bases tests off of it. THIS IS A TIME-INTENSIVE COURSE. But if you put in the effort, it will definitely show!

A great teacher, go to his office hours if you are having trouble. His tests are bit hard but nothing he did not go over. I suggest going to class, he uses different examples that are not from the textbook examples. And he's funny, so the class isn't always a drag.
difficult, but you learn the material.
dont take this guy
One of the best math teacher I have ever had. His tests are somewhat challenging.

I went to class about 90% of the time and thought I really understood the material, but come test time, I never did as well as I thought. He makes fun jokes which kept me awake, but if you take him, do all the book problems for your OWN BENEFIT!

So, I didn't always go to class but when I did I thought I understood the material and I still do horrible.  Went to one review and didn't always make it to LCA, so I guess if you are good with attendance then you might actually do well.
loved his class. he explains things very well. one of the best prof i've ever had.

GREAT PROFESSOR!! Lecture is mandatory to do well. Do all of the homework before the quiz, it will help you get a good score. He picks quiz questions directly from homework! Midterms and final are a little tough, but if you study and go to review in lecture you WILL get a good grade. Pay attentionb in class, and do the extra work. Thats how I earne

So I showed up to every lecture, attended every discusssion, and came to every review session. I ended up getting a D. Math 22 was a pain like no other. The tests were very challenging. He tries to amuse people and goes off topic a lot. If you can keep up with the material you should be able to pull a C. The book is essential as well. ESSENTIAL.

I thought this class was great. Quizzes in discussion came directly from practice problems he gave out in the book for homework, but honestly if you did the mathxl and went class, you didn't need the book. I wish I would have been able to take him for 8B
creates the hardest test he possibly could

Curtis, Exams/Quizzes: Extremely Painful  consist of 50% basic concepts/techs, 50% advance. Average on Midterms are C+, Average on final are D-, Few Quizzes. Preps you well for Midterms and Finals.  Presentation: Funny, Clear, Prepared, easy to follow,   Uses Analogies, slows down for others. Misc: Rarely had Homework, Few Quizzes, HARD Finals/MidT

He is super funny and he really makes math lecture worth going to.  I went to class just to hear his cheesy jokes and his sarcastic remarks.  He also really cares about his students. He spends a lot of time making sure his students understand the material.

He is super funny and he really makes math lecture worth going to.  I went to class just to hear his cheesy jokes and his sarcastic remarks.  He also really cares about his students. He spends a lot of time making sure his students understand the material.

He was my professor for 8A and my TA for 8B. All around great teacher, helpful, goes at a good pace for those who aren't as strong in math. As a TA a little lazy, didn't grade, post HW, or hand back HW on time, but did so with the quizzes. Sarcastic at times but his bark is worse than his bite. I'd take him again if he was teaching 9B. TAKE HIM!

Great professor!! Tough but he know's his stuff. He has a great way of teaching and tell you everything that will be on the tests. 2 midterms and a final, challenging! I aced the final though. GREAT CURVE since the test are hard. Overall great professor, I'd take him again anytime.

HES A VERY GOOD TEACHER, KNOWS HIS STUFF..JUST DO THE QUIZ LIST PROBLEMS AND YOULL BE FIND IN DISCUSSION. HIS TEST ARE HARD SO JUST STUDY AND USE THE OFFICE HOURS, IT HELPS! HES VERY ORGANIZE, ONCE YOU HAVE HIM ITS HARD TO GET USE TO A DIFFERENT PROF. NOTES!
he's a really good teacher, but his midterms and final are soo hard! he picks like the hardest possible questions because "it's about the process." pshhhhh.
I genuinely just don’t like the guy. He acts arrogant, and gives really hard finals. He is clear with his examples, and offers additional help. He just wasn’t my type of teacher.

Great teacher! loves his job, very helpful when you go into office hours. Grading scale 90% is an A 77% B 66% C 55%D. Tests are straight-forward but intimidating. Quiz every week. MUST GO TO LECTURES!! Overall great teacher. Sarcastic and uses some fould language, but is entertaining!
tests are hard, but curve is big. explains problems well in lecture
Pretty easy guy if you know your stuff.  Go to lectures and go to discussion.  Just takes a little work to understand stuff.  He's clear on what he says.  I took it in Fall Quarter 2005.

Curtis' class was easy (as long as you took Pre-Calculus in high school) and I barely went to his lectures. However, attending discussions was important and cleared up troubled areas. Jenn Burke was very helpful as TA for MATH4. However, the class got a little difficult the past 2-3 weeks of class. I still didn't go to the lectures, B+.

Pretty good teacher. I remembered most everything from highschool and i have an A+ now.  Somewhat entertaining guy. I'd take him again.

Curtis is tight.
thought i could keep up in the class, he made everything seem easy, but still failed the class unfortunately. Funny guy though.

I got a B+ in Math 5 simply because the math wasn't extremely difficult. Math 22, though, was a different matter. His tests are so difficult. And I couldn't stand his lectures; all he does it talk about himself and go through the material very quickly.

Really obnoxious!!! Enjoys hearing himself talk, but is hard to understand..... and his tests are a gy-normous pain in the ass, a 64 percent earns a C, but busting your ass does not guarantee a C in his class.

reviews.comment: Professor Ross is by far one of my favorites in the Linguistics department. He tends to go over lecture time but it's entirely because of his passion for the subject. Cons: (I say this lovingly) he's a bit of a yapper, NEVER ends class early; lectures are sometimes irrelevant to remember; LOTS of Perusalls.
Pros: VERY lenient grader, often gives full points for late work; never makes you feel stupid for questions; LOTS of extra credit assignments + goes out of his way to make up reasons to give out free points.

reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

It's shocking at how disorganized she can be. It's been 4 weeks of her accusing us of cheating and still has not updated us about anything, half of us don't know if we will fail or not.

The worst professor at UCR. Please avoid her at all costs. You will not pass this class with the grade you desire.
Strict on every single thing. Yells in lectures and takes forever to respond.
Gave out a BUNCH of Fs just because she thought students were using AI.
AVOID HER!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 50% Quizzes, 20% Homework. There are no examples for the Homework and the Quizzes are harder than the practice quizzes given by a decent amount. Be aware that extra credit makes up 1% of your total grade. 25% on Final and 5% on Final Assessment.

The professor mostly reads off the slides. The slides provide information, but not the information you are desiring. The quizzes somewhat relate to what you learn. However, the exams are completely different from what she teaches and emphasizes in class.

Idk about her in-person lectures, but her online lectures have been horrible since she switched to online.  Unreadable computer handwriting, dumps all info onto the slides and reads it, while doing minimal work herself. Also, dont go into this class expecting curves to save you. Her curves are practically nonexistent. Hyperfocused on cheating too.

I think a lot of the negative reviews are from students who didn't have the chance to talk to her. In class she's strict, but she does care about her students and responds very quickly. The class is hard, but she was always there to help. The homeworks and quizzes are difficult, but she was always available when you needed clarifications

This professor is regularly late, disrespectful, and unfair in grading(One from our 5HW, the lowest grade is negative). 

She likes to threaten students, "If you do not reply to me by voice in online class, I will be meaningful to your final", this sentence comes from the start of her lecture of week 10.

Yeah just don't. I don't think any of these positive comments are real. She is way to fixated on cheating and how her ratings come from pissed off students. When in reality she needs to chill. Her graders or whoever grades the assignments, acts like your supposed to teach em how you got the answer too. Which is insane.

Took her for 2 courses. Offers EC, extended deadlines for us as much as the hair on my scalp. Prioritizes all students over herself available on Slack 24/7. Instant feedback and support. For the review about her romantic life & cheating, as a student myself, the only image ruined here is yours, not the professor's for such a low class metaphor.

The professor lacks the vocabulary and desire to give feedback. Most of the feedback given, if any, has been vague or a poor attempt to nudge a student into the correct direction. It has yet to work, as most people are confused and have to ask the teacher assistant. Good luck.

I've taken her a few times already (3 CS 111's, whoops). She's gotten better and much less abrasive in her lectures.
I appreciate that she explained her lecture style at the beginning of the semester [She's been teaching this class for years and knows how to pace it]. Also her comment to speak up if we don't know something, so we don't flounder.

Elena was nice but can sound a bit harsh, tbh she just seems to want students to let her know how she can help them and gets frustrated when no one answers and then asks last minute. for us, she was available through Slack, gave ec opportunities, extended deadlines multiple times, and left a lot of the due dates to student suggestions.

I think her bad CS111 reviews are unfair. It's just a tough class but she explains things well, and if you go to lecture you'll do fine on quizzes. It's pretty much just math which ig isn't for everyone

I went to her Office Hours a lot and she is very sweet and approachable. I learned a lot. Every quiz and homework is important because I have seen those topics come up in future classes. I like her teaching style, and I really appreciate when she stops to make sure that no one is lost. She *cares*, and she is very knowledgeable.

I LOVED her class. It is a hard class, no question about it, but she does her best to make sure that she can provide maximum resources to make it smoother. She is very fair, and despite what some things people say, extremely caring. In all, she is an awesome instructor, and I was really grateful to be able to take classes with her.
Tough grader. Hard to access outside of class. Can be scary/strict sometimes, lectures are okay but dry. Kind of stingy with grading.

Lectures are often useless. Does not to go over review topics in class that's essential for upcoming material. Grading is alright, but can sometimes be extremely stingy when you least expect it. She clearly has a love for teaching, but her teaching method is incompatible with most students.

If you have the option to avoid this professor, I would do it. The quizzes are written in a way where you have never seen the problem before, or you might get lucky and have studied it. It doesn't encourage problem solving but rather memorization of problems. Also this professor is the first one I have taken where they grade in a predatory way.
Elena cool, but I hate this class. The people who grade also are stingy and will dock you off on small or non existing mistakes. Sadly, you have to take this class as a prereq.

She's funny and an interesting lecturer. The projects we did were fun and helpful. The only downside was that her final was incredibly hard and felt a little unfair. She tested us on a lot of material that she sped through in class since most students were seniors, but if it was new to you, you were kinda screwed.

Prof. Elena truly cares about her students from her heart. Wouldn't sit on her chair during OH's till she makes sure that every student gets the answer/support they need. Fair grader. If you show that you understand or at least really want to, she'll know. Straight forward in lecturing, would never go in circles. Sample quizzes help. Respected.
I love Elena, she cares very much for her students. Just do your work, go to office hours when needed, and discussions are vital. Study homework for quizzes.

Here are my tips for this class, DON'T PROCRASTINATE, she is very strict and is very clear on what she expect on her quizzes. TA's will be your friend for this class. I never relied on her lecture as I take notes before hand and relied on discussion heavily. Overall, she is very accessible and she helps you if you need help on Slack.

Terrible priorities. She's more focused on scaring students and cheaters than she is on teaching. And she takes pride in it. Lecture is horrible, she is always aggressive and demeaning. Had to teach myself everything. She does not fit in with the rest of the CS department. She should consider an academic disciplinary position, not teaching.

Teaching style is repeating the lecture slide in a slower voice to get her point across. If you're lucky she might even mix up a few words. Passive aggressive and chastizes the class for not being ready despite always being late. Only reason she gets a 2 is bc she likes questions. Unfortunately though, her answers don't help. TA's are your savior.

Her teaching style is extremely confusing and not helpful whatsoever and not to mention, her lectures are extremely boring and nonengaging. She is mainly reading off the slides and then tries to explain differently which becomes more confusing than it already is. Your best friend taking this class will be doing the practice quizzes and your TA.

"Just go to office hours," has been said on here.The thing is, not all of us are without a job or involvement in school, we don't have unlimited time. Treats all material as a prerequisite even if it is not a prerequisite it is all taught the same. Learn to self-study using the quiz study guides, I never went to class but studied for hours on that.

Professor Elena is a fantastic professor who made me a better student overall. Not only would she deeply cover lecture material and concepts, she didn't just simply read off slides, but would actually engage with students. I've taken multiple classes with her, and over that course of time she taught me how to teach myself which is invaluable, 10/10

I have had Professor Elena for CS010C, CS111, CS141, and CS105 and I think she's one of the best professors. It's funny that her OHs are so empty except the last week when everyone goes to bump up their grade and then have the audacity to complain after literally zero attendance or participation. Go to lectures, attend OH, do the HW. She's great.
Avoid!

The worst professor I've taken so far. Her lectures just consist of her telling you to do/learn everything at home. Just go for the extra credit attendance. She gets aggressive at times and legitimately just can't teach. You need to rely on the TAs.

"I will not cover anything" "its simple just play with it at home" "you should have done the example at home" Real things she said so avoid teaching. She only reads off slides which would be fine, but her slides are terrible. Shes super strict with grading and the material is difficult, but its made even more difficult because elena doesn't teach.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Elena is a tough professor. If you want to suck at algorithms and pass 141 without using your brain, take another professor. If you care about being good at the material, learning it thoroughly, and being a good engineer, take Elena. She will force you to think and learn, she is a great professor when you give effort.
Seriously, Avoid her!

wont say she is an awesome professor because I got an A. Her lecture is not helpful. 80% of the time in her lecture she just read from her slide, the rest of 20% she repeats the same thing in other words. I just skipped her lectures since I realized that. But she offer really good material like sample/practice quiz and some ec to boost your grade.

Its very unfortunate how much hate Professor Strzheletska gets. Not only does she care about her students, but she is always more than happy to clarify. In lecture she constantly encourages us to learn rather than memorize.  If you won't attend lecture at least study her notes, they are very detailed and her tests are similar to them. You can pass.

Before taking this class, I was fearful of Elena because of what everyone would always say of her. After taking her for the first time, my opinion completely was the opposite. Not only is she really lenient, she truly wants us to pass and will give us as many opportunities we want to succeed.
Go to lecture, do the homework, do the samples she gives

Every bad rating in this section is students who don't attend lecture and don't do homework. She gives so much extra credit opportunities it's silly. She's so caring in office hours. It is ridiculous the amount of students who don't show up to a single lecture and expect an A+. Then they show up here blaming the professor for their own stupidity.

I think shes calmed down a little judging on past reviews but she gave 5 hw's worth 4% each and 6 quizzes worth 10% each with one dropped. Hw's took a while but helped a lot for quizzes. I thought the quizzes were fair cuz she gave good practice ones that were similar. The final was a lot harder and surprized the whole class with the difficulty.

If you're looking for an easy A, look elsewhere. For the most part Elena is very attentive to her class and her students' needs. Lectures are pretty intense, but the class gets significantly easier after the first quiz. Only real problem I had with her is that she seems to assume the worst of her students

Makes jokes during class that I find somewhat funny, but it can also come off as harsh and petty. When we had hybrid classes, she offered zoom, but would get upset when we used it. As for lectures, she moved REALLY quickly, but I guess it's fair since class was only 50 min. Despite this, she is easily accessible in office hours & happy to help

Did CS111 & CS141 w/ her. The most devoted & caring professor I know. I had an OH with her until 11PM. If you show that you want the help *consistently*, she will help. But you need to put in the effort. Complaints feel misconstrued & like they're from students who didn't even try except for when they realized they were failing.

I think students who rate her bad are people who want to get grades for free. CS141 is the hardest class in CS majors and have to study hard to understand the content. She knows students getting hard on this and cares about us so much. Give a lot of hints for homework, due date extension, huge curves in your grades, and good feedback on your work.

Everyone knows her class is hard but she is also not very helpful and makes things harder than they need to be. She made the syllabus and then completely changed it during the class. Often with very little notice. Deadlines were confusing and kept moving. When ever I asked questions she had condescending answers.
She is not caring about students' grade.
hard to contact outside the class, made important announcements very late spontaneously with little time, the topic is not hard but she makes it hard.

Expectations are not very clear and elena is hard to reach outside of class. She told our class she would refuse to answer questions about an assignment on slack one time because nobody had questions at the time in class. Makes last minute announcements expecting all students to comply and lectures are dull and not helpful. Very unorganized class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Not as bad as other people have been saying, but certainly not perfect. Lectures were not helpful for me. I learned best from youtube videos and reviewing the material on my own. Do well on the quizzes and the homework and you'll do fine in the class.

Is Elena harder than other professors? Apparently, but she teaches the two most important CS classes. Put consistent effort in. Trying to study for midterms the night before will get you a C if you’re smart. Start assignments early and go to OH for clarification. She is very understanding if you make any effort to speak to her outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Accessible only through slack, not by email. She sometimes assigned quizzes after 11pm. Not worth going to lecture, just watch youtube vids about the concept and read the slides/watch the recording.
Proof heavy, tough grader, class average is low, but she curves at the end. Get as many points as you can on take homes and hw. Hws are very long.

As others have said, lecture and lecture slides don't prepare you for homework, and homework doesn't prepare you for tests. Class average scores for assignments were visible on gradescope and almost every assignment had an average between 40-50%. She is a very harsh grader, criteria is unclear, and she doesn't test on what is taught.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you put in the work you will be just fine. Elena actually cares about her students. If you go to her OH you will see that. OH are super helpful!

Literally, you have to put so much time into this class to get any sort of return. It's either you prioritize this class or your three other courses. Her slides & lectures don't help you prepare for the homework and the homework & study guide don't come close to prepping you for the exams. The god-complexes in this class don't make it any better.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The content of this class is hard but Elena does her best to teach it in a way for students to understand. If you put in the effort she does the same. Has multiple office hours and if you want more help she offers it. She actually cares about her students.

Worst professor I had so far at UCR. Randomly decided to move final earlier. Asked a "no credit" qestion on the last quiz before the final asking if the given time slot for the final was available. You got -33.3% off the quiz if you didn't know, and -3.33% off the quiz if you had a time conflict. Final was also moved two days earlier at 8 AM.

Is she the best explainer? I don't think so. But is she caring towards her students? Definitely. Go to her office hours and she will ask you questions and make you think, but they will definitely give you a better understanding. She even asks her readers to hold study sessions for the students. They're super helpful, and you should really go.

Elena is a great prof. I think the problem is honestly just the course content. Discrete math is hard for most cs people from what I can gather online and it's a lot easier for math majors and the same goes for 111 and Elena. If you just listen and practice, 111 isn't impossible or anything and Elena is actually super helpful in office hours.
Entire class format doesnt make any sense: every homework is graded long after quizzes are taken so you don't have any feedback going into the exams when the material is already complex enough

You will probably have to take this professor if you are pursuing anything computer science-related at UCR. If you do, I pray for your success as she is probably the most unfair professor I ever had in my 4 years in undergrad. She grades extremely tough, partial/pity points do not exist with her. If you wish to pass you must grind.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She is a terrible professor. Can't speak clearly during lectures and skips many slides. Her content is unclear and incohesive. This subject is hard enough as it is, and Elena does not make it any easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The class is hard but she is really nice. You really have to work to get an A but there may be some extra credit if she likes your class. Overall she is really nice and will answer any of your questions, but it's really up to you on how much work you put into the class because that's the grade you get.

I will be honest. The next time I interview for a job, I will probably have Professor Strzheletska to thank for the knowledge I currently have. She is a very good lecturer, so much so that I can still retain a lot of the material in CS111 because of that. She cares a lot about her students and it is not hard to see that she wants the best for us.

The course material in this class is very hard, regardless of the professor. The quizzes and homework are important and ask her for help IMMEDIATELY if you start getting confused. Elena is willing to help you out as much as possible. Going to lectures helps and if you can go to her office hours as well.

Elena is a wonderful professor! I don't understand why she got so many bad reviews. She is a very knowledgeable professor and is a kind, caring person. She is willing to help students during office hours and while the course work is very difficult, her quizzes and tests are fair. If you put effort into studying, you'll do well.

CS111 as a course is very hard but if you put in the effort to study and ask questions, you'll be fine. Along with extra credit, she is very helpful during office hours as well and sometimes even gives hints about the questions asked in quizzes and exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Skips a lot of steps on her slides so you won't understand anything if you zone out at least once. This is a math class and there is a difference between listening to somebody read off slides with all the work already done and doing it step-by-step from the beginning on a whiteboard and explaining as you go. Good luck trying to take notes.

Elena's 111 has a reputation for being hard but I think it's just the shock as one of our first upper-divs, along with learning LaTeX. Attending office hours is one of the best things you can do because not only is Elena super helpful in OH, you'd also know that she's pretty funny and cares a lot about her students; with high expectations, however.
If you have another option to take the class with anyone else, go ahead and do so; trust me...

The class as a whole is incredibly difficult, with difficult situations regarding quizzes and exams. The quizzes are incredibly difficult with quiz practices that do not reflect the quiz questions and lack answers. Homework is incredibly difficult and is not graded based on completion but rather very harshly graded on content. She lacks empathy.

Her lectures are confusing at best, with homework assignments being extremely difficult. Practices for the quizzes (which account for 40% of the grade) are provided, but solutions are only provided for some of the problems, and there are often questions on the quizzes that resemble nothing that was on the practice. Be prepared and ready for this.

If you've taken CS 111 or 141, then you pretty much know what to expect. Elena is very vague when it comes to what she expects from you, so be prepared to spent lots of time going back and for with her (especially for the final project). She likes to keep the TAs in the dark as well so its no use expecting any help from that department.

Elena is a GOOD person, and she cares if you are learning or not. If you ask questions during the lecture(which u should attend otherwise will have a hard time), she is willing to answer them. Also, quizzes are 40&, which is super HEAVY. Quizzes are hard and not ez to get 90%. Heavy study class overall. Ready to drop it if u dont study.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Quizzes make 40% of the total grade and if you fail once, you are likely to get B. Homework grading is crucial, there are always strange reasons to take points off. Lectures are not that helpful, it takes so much time to learn by yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Getting a bad grade in her class has become a self-fulfilling prophecy that results in most students giving up early. Yes, CS111 with Elena is difficult, but it is very doable with her instruction. She is a knowledgeable, caring, and fair professor. The math is not hard. That being said, you will study for this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Participate in class and show up to office hours; she'll remember you and often drops hints to homework if you care enough to ask. If you show a clear intention on trying to understand content, she'll help you through it. If you have a bad math/logic background, be prepared to watch YouTube videos to refresh yourself on certain concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Course material isn't the hard part. Her quizzes are timed and if you want an A on them, do her practice quizzes and literally time yourself so you finish and are confident in your answers to not double check. She explains concepts by repeating procedures/steps. Slides are contradictory & DOES NOT INCLUDE NAMES OF THEOREMS. In a math class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Elena gets a lot of hate but she definitely cares about students. This wasn't an easy class, but I learned a lot more in this class than previous courses. This quarter was online and she implemented a group project that was interesting and a fun way to incorporate algorithms. I did have an issue with dense exams with a short time to complete.

Elena is a profoundly nice person and you can tell that at all times she just wants her students to learn. However, she is also a profoundly terrible teacher. As in, I've never learned anything as a result of her attempts at instructon and I haven't met a classmate that has either. She is also very obviously on the spectrum and lacks social cues.

The professor is a tough grader and so are her grader(s). It seems like theres always random points taken off of homework for the simplest things. Skipped a step? Goodbye 20% of your homework grade even though the final answers are correct. The quizzes and tests are easier than homework, the catch is that you are racing against the clock.

The material in CS111 is not too difficult, if you study, like any student should. HOWEVER, Strzheletska makes it difficult. She gives unreasonable amount of questions for every quiz and test. When students disclosed their concerns with the amount of questions, Strzheletska simply said "study more". Avoid this unreasonable instructor at all cost.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Elena is indeed passionate of the subject. However, she is too passionate to the point she doesnt put into account that her students are students and not expert mathematicians. Course materials are easy to learn if you practice, but quizzes are a complete 180. Throws more complicated materials compared to materials presented on slides and hw.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: SHOW UP TO CLASS AND TRY ON THE HW IF YOU WANT TO PASS!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Elena is strict because she truly cares about students learning the material. Lectures can be confusing as she often just reads off the slides but she is very helpful during office hours, and is more than willing to move/extend them if needed. Provides practice material for quizzes (rely on the quiz syllabus more). Many extra credit ops.

Elena is a very good teacher. She is very passionate about the class, and is clear in what she teach. She is a fair grader. The class is difficult, so put in the effort. Attendance is not mandatory, but is helpful. The quizzes and final are straight forward if you do the HW and participate in class. Also review the proof, and focus on learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Prof Strzheletska is truly passionate about her teaching. Shes strict with her grading to help you better understand the fundamentals of the material. Go to office hours, put time and effort into this class  its rigorous but doable and very rewarding. She challenges you to think outside the box & amply prepares you for concepts covered in CS141.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Course material is hard. Though attendance isnt mandatory, youll do well just by attending and paying attention to lecture, discussions and office hours. Clear expectations for the quizzes and final. Elena was very fair grader. Its easy to say attending class is waste of time, but, like I said, material is hard. Show up. Pay attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Class is hard, make sure you study all the theorems and proofs a lot. Don't fall behind in the class. You should also do all the homework and practice quizzes.
toughest grader I've ever seen

In this class, lectures are fragmented, explanations are never thorough, and expectations are not clearly defined. She will always start lecture and quizzes late. Her quizzes are very strange, given that, she gives you like 30 minutes for 12 problems, and there are questions in the quizzes that don't resemble any of the HW, slides, or discussions.

The course is based on UCR math department guidelines. The math department requires cs111 to be taught on 4 quizzes, 5 homework, and a final exam. There's an extra credit quiz in the course, however, the extra credit quiz is a tough grader. Elena lectures through her lecture slides. She's very helped during her office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Very difficult class. She isn't very clear going through the lecture in class, often times speeds through the material and ends class early. She gives extra credit for quizzes, but you must attend class to get it. Material on quizzes is very different from the practice and sample questions she gives in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: - Quizzes more complex than practice tests and homework - Unclear lectures - Asks problems on Quizzes and tests that clearly aren't in the slides or on the homework. - Practice quizzes don't have solutions often times - Incredibly strict grading, unforgiving regrades
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Tests you on pre-req material (even on the final), which sucks. Gives small extra credit opportunities randomly in discussions or lectures, so if you miss that class, sorry. Only reason most go to class is for that. Puts questions that quizzes that were more complex than what was on homework/prac tests. Prac tests often don't have solutions.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Not a very hard class and he's a nice guy, despite the reviews effort = easy A basically guaranteed, class average was VERY low on exams but I studied the night before and scored the/near the highest so just do the same. Lectures are not very helpful, but you should still show up because participation will add up a LOT.

He's alright, I guess. Main thing is that he doesn't teach that well. He reads of slides on google colab and thats the lecture. Also assigns weekly homework and doesn't give an indicator whether its due on the regular day its due or even earlier.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He gives a lot of homework, the volume of assignments is tough. However, his lectures are interesting, he visualizes a lot of concepts, the slides are made professionally, and most importantly he provides real-world applications and useful justifications for "why we are learning this". Never skipped a lecture because they were very informative.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Tests are hard, but not that hard, just the way he grades makes it hard. No curve even though class test average seemed like it was 60~70%. He literally just reads off the lecture slides and still finds a way to make it confusing. Around week 7 I stopped going to lectures and just learned from youtube - ended up performing better after doing that.

This may geniuenly be the worst teacher ive ever had the pleasure of taking a class in. towards the final week of class i felt suicidal because of his last assignment. my advice take it with anyone else if he is the only option please drop!!! he makes the class much more confusing and unnecessarily complicated than it needs to be.
Bro genuenly dosnt teach just speaks outloud with a textbook in the hand
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I did it for CS010C. All he did was read off slides and wouldn't elaborate too much in depth when student's had questions. His practice midterms and finals reflected the difficulty of his exams, and his exams were fair to the content covered. The main issue is just the way he taught.
He just read through his colab stuff throughout the entire class, and most of us donot understand what he is talking about.

Prepare to read through many Colab notebooks, because that's the material covered in lecture. And Ty hardly ever elaborates more than what he says. He'll demonstrate how to use the topic of each notebook, but not the concept of it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Class is easy if you already know music. For beginners, class moves very fast and can be confusing. She switches topics fast and is redundant with her teachings, but doesn't explain topics well. Lots of worksheets are given. Attendance is mandatory for lecture and discussion. Final was a take home final and you could work on it with anyone.

Interesting material, but not an enjoyable class because of the professor, the only way this class was doable for real beginners was because of the TA. It just seemed like she was so unserious, took very long to grade and to upload resources, moved very fast but would say "you know this". Was catered more towards students who new material already.

Very soft spoken so suggest sit near the front of class. Homework is given but the instructions are really easy. Don't have to attend lectures BUT HAVE to attend discussions (for me my TA helped me a lot). A lot review of topics that we learn. Overall pretty easy for those wanting to get into music theory. Just know it's a lot in general.
Good teacher and very experienced

DO NOT TAKE PLS I BEG says beginner IT IS NOT she never answers emails 
she rambles on and on and on she talked more about electric scooters than actual music terms I learned from youtube not her. i literally have never done one of these in my 3 UCR years but this prof was SO BAD I ABSOLUTELY HAD TO also attendance is mandatory or no one would go

Professor Moore is kind but is not equal to beginners. Although it is a beginner class, she favors students who have prior music experience. Attendance is mandatory and taken every session. There is also not to much homework. Homework that is assigned is rarely turned in but you should do as it is helpful with exams.

She is a very nice person, but the teaching skills are not clear. She caters to people with experience rather than those who know nothing (supposed to be for beginners!), constantly using words and expressions only those with experience would understand. Learning schedule is not very organized. Course is 70% self study to know anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

Don't let his last name fool you, he has great English! Is very clear to understand. I wish he taught all of Molec 107B, instead of only half the quarter.

He is really helpful if you have issues understanding the subject matter. He doesn't expect you to know the basics and is easily approachable.

Great professor. Very knowledgable and effectively answers your questions in a really understandable manner.  He will  frequently pause to ask if everyone is comprehending and tries to engage the class into a discussion, so it is easier to pay attention and follow along during lecture. The textbooks is helpful. Don't procrastinate.

Ridiculously easy class; so much so that I skipped all lectures from week 3 until finals week and passed with a B. For "lectures", he only does chapter summaries which you do not need unless you did not understand a chapter. He is a very kind and passionate person but I don't recommend him at all.

Yes, I would have to say the lectures were not the best, but Professor Felix was a very great and flexible professor, especially when it came to the midterm and final. There were also a lot of reading, but I found it pretty interesting.

He's very okay if that makes sense? I learned a lot in his class, he posts slides, 3 essays and in class essay style exams, no attendance for lecture but yes for discussion. BUT he's not an interesting lecturer, altho he's nice and cares about teaching. Depends if it matters to you, but sitting in lecture taking notes it DOES! Overall solid 7/10

It is an easy class, I would recommend for gpa boost. There are 3 essays, including the midterm and final. Lectures slides are posted on canvas, it heavily related to the textbook but he posts summarize slides, just show up to discussion fs.

Professor Felix's Political Violence in Mexico class was very interesting, professor was very passionate on what he was teaching. Readings that were assigned were interesting as well, the last book was a bit rushed but I still find myself reading it on my own. Mainly essays and attendance graded, but were open note/ book.
Professor Felix, is a heavy on lectures. Can be a little boring because he does not know how to keep us engaged. However depending on you TA grading should not be hard, effort equals passing.
Good professor with class being based on 2-3 paper assignments based on class reading novels that are very manageable! Lectures are posted on canvas and are mainly quote reviews from readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: As long as you show up and participate in the discussions, you will be fine. Your grade is determined by your papers, so just make sure that while you are writing your paper, you have the rubric next to you and that you fulfill the requirements. There is no final or midterm.
Online class with prerecorded lectures, essentially no contact with the prof at all. Grade based on 3 essays and participation in discussion. Read one novel, rest of the readings were posted online

Other responses are spot on with the grading. Very easy to get full points by just asking your TA to check before you submit. HOWEVER, I really did not like his teaching style. I believe that it is the job of a professor to allow students to THINK about the issue and not just spoon feed them what YOU believe. This professor, sadly, was the latter.
His class was graded by only 3 essays and they were pretty easy to get full points on (but that might depend on your TA). You don't have to attend lectures to complete the assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The grade is entirely based on 3 essays and showing up to discussion. The readings and lectures had nothing to do with the papers. The professor came off as very rude during his lectures. Make sure to talk to your TA about your papers because they will either make or break your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--So many papers

reviews.comment: honestly an interesting and easy class. I could have gotten a much better grade but I did not go to discussion about 6 times, and that really affected my grade. He gives some extra credit opportunity but his midterm was an essay based off a book we read but he hints about the topic throughout the lectures and the final was a take home assignment.

Professor Felix emphasizes the problems going on in today's society with the U.S.-Mexico racial violence with the local communities. He talks about relevant readings, but can get a little repetitive on certain occasions. Discussion is mandatory since the TAs grade the work. Participation is recommended to help gauge the discussions. Overall caring.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The lectures were not mandatory only the discussions. You don't need to go to lectures as he doesn't test you on the slides but you should go the days before the midterm. Grade consists of midterm (in class essay) and final book review as well as two 1-2 pg analytical papers. You don't need his book but you should try to get access to first book.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Passionate lecturer, but his accent was honestly so heavy I opted to just read the textbook. Final exam was all free response but reflected the learning objectives. He tells you what equations you need to practice, so memorize those. Biggest hurdle is understanding the material tbh, crystallography is tough but self-study is possible
Honestly the easiest class you could take. If you want to boost your gpa take this class

Super passionate lecturer, but I didn't really understand what he was saying in lecture because his accent was so thick. However, his lectures had a list of questions at the end, and those questions translated to the final really well.

he literally gives us the recipe to getting perfect scores on every assignment. itd be boring but during lab he walks through every single step for the computational part of the course & tells you exactly what to write. TAs took FOREVER to grade though. his accent was tuff to understand in lecture but lectures werent even useful for assignments tbf

I felt that Dr. Fan's lectures and explanations were very helpful in clarifying the challenging concepts in X-ray crystallography. reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I had Professor Fan for BCH184 and BCH015. His online lectures for 015 were long but made the labs very understandable and easy to complete. For 184, he was fantastic, contrary to previous reviews. His explanations on crystallography (such as Miller Indices) were much more helpful than the textbook! I thoroughly enjoyed my time in class with him :)
Dr. Fan's labs were fairly straightforward because he takes time to walk through them step-by-step, and the TA was very helpful during the office hours. Memorizing the amino acids is key.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Previous comment mentioned that Dr. Fan' thick accent gets in the way of delivering a lecture. What I find difficult is not his accent but his lack of preparation. He goes backward on his points both on a GLOBAL sense (goes back to clarifying information given in previous lectures) and a LOCAL sense (backtracking what he says a few slides ago).
good luck understanding what he is saying. sit up front and attempt to read lips

It is basically impossible to understand what he is saying because his accent is so strong. Slides have almost no text so his PowerPoints are also useless. This course overall is very difficult and Fan doesnt do a good job at explaining concepts clearly. good luck
could understand lecture at least 15% of the time. I know I'm kind of dumb but he makes me feel like I literally should've just changed my major .

The class was not hard, but the labs were VERY difficult to get through. Professor Fan goes through the procedures too fast and gives unclear instructions. It's hard to get help from him outside of class. There are prelab quizzes which were hard because he never told us what they were about. He's not that bad, but I wouldn't take again.

I have no idea why anyone would give him 5 stars, Professor Fan is awful. He is difficult to understand, which is usually fine for other profs bc they make sure to provide extra help so you understand, but Prof Fan is stubborn and unwilling to change his teaching style to help. To himself, he is right and that is that. Avoid him at all costs.

He's a little hard to understand and his quizzes are relatively difficult. If you're new to biochemistry, it's going to be a little tough. However, as long as you memorize your amino acids and what not, the quizzes will be fine. The lab itself is easy since he goes step by step (granted a little quick sometimes).
tough class
easy

Dr. Gaudette was awesome! Took her Politics and Public Policy class as a breadth requirement, but very much enjoyed it. She was very nice, and it was clear that she was excited to teach. Would recommend taking her but if you don't like writing you might not like the work because of the policy memo we had to write. OVERALL THOUGH, amazing professor.

There are no mandatory lectures, but attending and taking notes is super helpful. There are quite a few assigned readings, but they're short. The main assignment is a long essay, but the grading is an easy A Overall, the class is not difficult if you come to class consistently and take notes and do the readings.

relatively easy class if you're not a fool or completely new to college, just go to lecture or do the readings if you dont. this shouldnt be a difficult class by any means and if you find it hard you might want to either switch your major or consider a career outside of college
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: prof Gaudette is amazing! i only took this course to satisfy a breadth requirement, but she was able to keep me interested in public policy with her humor and was extremely thorough w/ the content in her lectures. she is overall very kind and supportive of your learning; just attend lectures and pay attention and you'll be set!!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing teacher! She made her lectures very fun and easy to understand and even though this was just a class I needed for a breadth course, I did enjoy it and maybe one day will take another one of her classes. 😁
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Gaudette is an amazing new professor! She is passionate about public policy and her expectations are very clear and consistent. 100% would take again. Charismatic and engaging professor, with clearly organized and outlined content. Readings are usually websites or excerpts - really easy. TAKE HER COURSE!
1) Course: Literally show up and take notes and you'll get an A. It's like a teacher who says they "want you to learn, not care about the grade" but like actually good.

genuinely cannot put into words how much i LOVE prof gaudette. she's very passionate about public policy and it shines through her teaching. class is graded on a midterm, a final (you get cheat sheets on exams!), & a policy memo that you write on any topic of your choosing. attendance isn't mandatory but go to lectures! she's so funny and engaging

reviews.comment: Professor Gaudette was amazing, she makes class enjoyable and she makes government enjoyable. lecture is required but she uploads slides.
