reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Firstly, this guy is hilarious. His sense of humor made the class somewhat fun and interesting. He also is very helpful with understanding the readings and improving your writing. There are short pop quizzes so it's imperative to do the readings and come to class; with that you'll do fine in the class.

Toughest class I took, I worked so hard and got an A-. Papers are so long and require a lot of concentration and effort. He gives amazing advice and is willing to speak with you in office hours as long as you need. To some, his lectures are boring but interesting to those who like discussingdebating relevant issues on life. Again very tough grader

Go to his office hours! He is willing to help if you make the effort. Although his lectures can get boring at times,  he explains everything well.  Do well on the essays because it pretty much determines whether or not you pass.

Very good teacher funny and very caring, assigns good books for the English class and although his grading is difficult it is helpful and consistent. It may not be an easy A but it's an enjoyable class

Tough grader.  Very rare to get an A on an essay.  Each essay is 6 pages long.  Wastes a lot of class time talking about irrelevant things and making "sarcastic" comments that I didn't find too hilarious.
too much HW essay prompt will be given the day before rough draft
Horrible, so much homework. Not worth it. I regret taking his class so much.
He is really helpful, willing to talk to you about ideas for papers, helps you with drafting. He puts a lot of time in helping you. Go to office hours!

Figured he would be just another boring english prof. I was wrong. We read three novels throughout the quarter that related (some more than others) to the three types of papers we wrote: a remembered event essay, a profile, and a concept explanation essay; each of which were about 6/7 pages long.Funny guy, knows what he is talking about.

He takes role, gives a quiz(every other class session) and lectures most of the time which could get boring. extremely sarcastic when he is asked a dumb question. His lectures dont really help with the essays you write. Allows some rewrites but generally he grades chill. Read the Books!

Talks most of the time during class. Boring for some students, but interesting for others, depending on who you are. If you go to office hours, he's not going to fix your essay by writing comments. HE'LL TELL YOU WHAT YOU NEED, SO YOU'LL HAVE TO FIX IT ON YOUR OWN. It's tough, but I think that's the best way for you to learn the material.
He's very sarcastic.

Albert is an excellent professor. It is evident that he spends a lot of time writing comments on essays. Show him your essay during office hours. That will really boost your grade. My essay writing really improved after taking his class.

He grades really hard on essays! Class was boring. He doesn't seem very approachable and assigns too much reading. Don't bother turning in late papers bcuz he takes 50% off so you'll get a fail anyway.
Great teacher and very helpful when it comes to essay, his classes aren't that difficult but you have to read cuz there are quizzes! but other than that hes an awesome teacher
he is an awesome teacher.. other than his office hours, he spend some time to help his students..
He is very very helpful teacher. If you really want to learn english!!? pick him!
Nice, he understands your situations. go to classes. and do your homework. dude. so much homework... seriously. little quizes every friday based on your homework.
he's so nice and cute, i loved going to his class. he's not really that hard if you participate, and once he knows your name class seems easier. i didn't go to office hours though...
he was my favorite! he was so much fun and so nice to everyone--i loved taking his class
DO NOT PICK HIM IF YOU DONT LIKE GOING TO OFFICE HOURS.he likes to be worshiped upon. if you dont go to his office hour then your game over. very bad teacher
extremely helpful during office hours. if you seek him out, your papers will improve greatly. if you work hard, an A is definitely possible.
Very laid back, comfortable environment. Encourages discussion, but doesn't force it. Helpful and approachable

whats up anthony! he is a great teacher and a great person.  Very helpful!  If you find him bad then there must be some**** wrong with you. *corrects grammer* neways, very good teacher and laid back like what the other guys said.
He was really helpful and easy to talk to.
awesome teacher, really easy, really nice.
He acts like he does not like you, but I think that's just the way he looks. Go to his office hours and at least pretend you care about the class. I got through with a B+.

I had a very bad experience with him. He apparently had some bad feelings towards me and I picked up the impression right away. He was never smiling or encouraging when I visited him during office hours.
this class was so chilled and laid back; watched a bunch of commercials and videos; cool teacher; grades prty lenient; bottom line, i didnt read and just showed up 2 class and got an A

Most interesting english class i've ever had cause we basically talked about pop culture and commercials the whole time.  Nice guy who is a fair grader, but the group discussions we had were very boring.
great teacher, always willing to help, alot of group reading discussion which gets kind of boring after a while.

albert anthony is a really cool laid back easy teacher. gave 4 essays and 1 final and i got A's on all of them. participation is 20% of the grade so show up to class and say stuff.  how can anyone get a D they must be dumb.  watched some good films too.

I think he's an awesome teacher, discussion is fine as long as you read. He's always willing to help with essays and is really approachable. He comes across as someone that would be cool to hang out with outside of class.
I like him. He's pretty nice and he's cute too. ^_-

He's pretty un-organized, changes his syllabus too many times, no extra credit.  Not accessible during office hours and gets made if there's a lot of students wanting to access him during office hours.  Gave so much reading material that was of no or litt
No Comments
No Comments
gave too many Ds
His a very good teacher and a very good discussion teachers as well!!

He seems really nice at the begining but then he turns out kinda mean toward the end. All of my friends, including me, got a D from that class (so not fair b/c we all did our hw) dont know why he is mean to give us a D *_*
He is the worse english teacher I even had.
Don't know what he wants, critical
hard for an english professor, and wants oral presentations
Excellent teacher.  I Learned more than in any other English course.
He tends to vacillate in his lectures.  Gradingwise, he is difficult.  The most you can get on his essays are "B+'s."
Don't know what he wants
No Comments
No Comments
This class is not easy, but he knows his stuff very well. If you go to his office hours he helps you understand the material. Overall he is a good teacher.

He moves through pretty tough material very fast. Class itself was hard, and the tests were ridiculous. We had to explain and justify almost every step of the problems in sentence form for points. HARD grader!!!

He has a passion for math. If you need help then ASK otherwise good luck studying on your own.  The midterms are 80% like the practive midterms but the final will probably kill you. Good luck.  Look him up on youtube :)

He is a very guy. He helps you out in office hours. You should study everyday cuz its kin of hard. midterms are harder than tests. I like the curves. Take the homework seriously. Sit in the front cuz its kinda hard to understand from the back.
Somewhat hard to understand because of his accent. Some times hes good at explaining stuff, other times hes terrible. As far as math teachers go, hes not the worst you can do at UCR.

This is a good teacher. If you go to his office hours he helps you understand the material even more and he gives you the answer to the homework. His midterms are just like the sample midterms. His accent is a little distracting but he knows his stuff. He curves the midterms at least ten points.
excellent teacher! tough on grades. he makes you work really hard and you better take his homeworks seriously if you want to pass the tests. you will learn a lot from his course.
His exams are hard and this class is not easy. But he knows his stuff and he is very helpful. If you study regularly it's easy to do well in this class.
Really hard to follow during his lectures
He is a very sweet man. His class  is hard but if you study then you should pass. His study guides are just like his midterms.

This class is very hard and I can tell you that if you like to procrastinate like me, it won't do the job. He knows his stuff and his Curve its Great, that's how I passed the class. Don't take it unless you are serious about proofs and lots of HWKs.One thing is for sure everything I learned will be stuck in my head forever.
Horrible teacher...also the tests are insanely hard and do not match what he taught...i passed this same class later on and did not recognize anything apoorva taught us.
Apoorva Khare is the kind of person that knows what hes teaching. unfortuinately he sucks at conveying it. do not take his class. He will just fail you
tRY TO AVOID Aproova when signing up for math 8b. He is a horrible teacher and his test are ridiculously hard.

Was intimidated since the 1st day of class, lectures are fat and u need to pay attention, if u procrastinate u wont pass, i almost got a bad grade in the class but did all the homework and got a B+ on the final (which was very reasonable) and got an A-. prof can seem unforgiving on the outside but is very forgiving as long as u put in the work

When setting aside the difficulty of the class, the professor is very fair.  He does give quizzes, but he makes sure they are always relevant to the homework and lectures.  He can be a tough grader, but he makes his expectations clear, focusing on straightforward practice problems that you will see again in quizzes/exams.

Hard to keep up with during lectures; handwriting is often illegible and professor expects students to understand when he throws out random variables and formulas. Professor will expect you to memorize every single obscure formula and will often throw in curveballs in quizzes and exams. However he is very forgiving when grading.

DONT COME LATE TO CLASS! This man will put you on BLAST if you are even 30 seconds late to his class. He will also make snarky comments if he thinks you ask a dumb question during lecture. Weekly quizzes and homework are given out. Quizzes are 25%, Midterm is 30%, Final is 40% and homework is 5%. Need to be good with moments and equilibrium.
Help me.

- Lectures are understandable and well taught
- Quizzes cover lecture, and he goes over the answers after
- HW is based on participation, and he also gives the answers w/ steps before hw is due
- Final is cumulative and hard, but he gives you ample preparation.

Overall, a fair class but prepare to ask questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This course is one of the more difficult engineering courses. He is a good lecturer and he knows his stuff. He allows open notes, but the exams are long and difficult. Weekly quizzes are doable. Be prepared to bust your butt for an A though.

Besides his humour, there is much positive to say. He often derives equations with the expectation that students know which assumptions to make to properly utilize the formula. His class is very unorganized with very little preparation for the chaos that is the labs. His tests are heavily reliant on notes from the course so try your best at asking.

This is for UCSD not UCR- he's a really cool person and he makes the material he teaches relevant to whats going on in the bio world. He is a little quiet so you have to tell him to speak up sometimes. Grading however was very harsh and specific in my opinion but he curved and gave 5% EC so it made up for it.

I highly recommend Dr. Akbari, he made the class enjoyable. He doesn't just lecture the whole time, but he actually brings in some researches to help us engage in the lectures more. His exams are fair, his questions are based on understanding, not just memorization. He even curves the exams very generously. 5% extra credit just for iclickers.

He jumps around with his lecture. Very disorganized. Ex. Starts talking about transcription when we haven't talked about DNA replication. You need to have a strong biology background to follow through his lecture. Not very clear... nice guy though

Professor Akbari is a nice professor however he did not prepare us for the lab class that corresponds to this class. Some of his midterm questions were based on things he casually mentioned in class , which was also not podcasted. You will do ok on his midterm and final if you skip class but it is necessary to attend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Really good professor! Thorough, fair and clear. Assignments really help so do all of the questions! He curved our midterm but don't know if he will curve our final. Only minor thing is that slides can be hard to look over because they can be unclear. Would still take again.
He is a really good professor. I admit his test can be  tad confusing, but just study and you can get an A in the class. I would take his classes again

Dr. Akbari is a  great professor. Clickers are not mandatory for his class, but going to class is very helpful. He is a bit softspoken, but you can ask him to speak louder. His tests are quite fair; just study the notes and you can get an A

Dr Akbari has a clear passion for teaching. His lectures are inspirational as he links together class content with real world matters. He is very approachable and will go the extra mile to make sure his students understand the content. I truly enjoyed his course and highly recommend students to take his courses.

This professor is quite honestly very bad. He shows little care for his students and assigned 100+ problems for homework a week before the final exam. On top of all of this, his lectures make no sense unless you come into the lecture already understanding the topics that will be discussed.

This is one of the worst professors I have had in the ME program at UCR. His grading is confusing, his lectures are shallow compared to what he would give during quizzes(curveballs). He would constantly hound us for doing poorly in quizzes and get upset at students simply going to the restroom or arriving late to lecture. Avoid at all cost.

His class was the hardest thing I've ever had to do in my life HOWEVER I'm not gonna lie he pushed us so hard past our limit in a way that made me adapt a work ethic & a new problem solving mindset I've never had b4. His quizzes will always have curveballs & be 10x harder than the hw same for the midterm/final. He does try to maximize ur grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: worst professor I have ever had in my entire college/university life. His course is hard (like Sundar) but his teaching skills & lectures are just horrible (unlike Sundar). get ready to learn on your own and I wish your TA is good enough to lecture u instead of him. he jumps around, lacks context and keep changing notations during lectures. bad bad

Let me start off by saying that everyone who rated this professor in the month of May 2024 were the glazers dude they lying this professor is the hardest ME professor. The whole yells at you for being late is true and he will call you out in the middle of class if you're late. Avoid this professor but if you're ME youll be seeing him often.

Venky actually teaches quite well but he tends to move pretty quickly and assume everyone understands, which is understandable because he asks whether people understand something first and always encourages office hours. His homework, quizzes, and tests are all fairly similar so as long as you know how to do the homework you should be fine.
He's a good teacher who teaches a somewhat difficult subject. There is a single homework assignment per week and a weekly quiz that is graded very leniently.

Ignore all of the negative reviews. If you actually come to class, did the homework properly, went to office hours, and studied, this class is extremely straight forward. Venky has a strange sense of humor and character but not degrading to the extent these negative reviews claim. If you did the bare minimum of work, of course you'd get a low grade

Literally, the worst person I have ever met let alone a professor. I have never seen this many students withdraw from a class in my life but he warrants it. He is condescending and degrading towards students and seems to want the majority of his class to fail. He creates his own ways of solving problems and doesn't accept anything else. AVOID!!!!!

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS IF HE IS TEACHING IT. avoid at all costs. This professor truly does not care about teaching. He takes pride in failing students and brags about it. He will stop lecture to harass students if anyone shows up late. He doesn't really explain his methods for solving problems and inconsistently uses them.

You won't pass this class if this man is teaching it. He takes pride in failing students and often brags about failing 30%-60% of his classes each quarter. He states he's here for the money and not much else. He will publicly harass you if you're even 1 minute late. He creates new formulas to solve problems, and then inconsistently uses them.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He knows what he is talking about, but horrible at lecturing. Whenever students were confused and had questions, he usually told them to think like an engineer rather than help them. He often introduced something as insignificant in class, and it ended up being on the quiz. A lot of the material on quizzes was fond only in lectures than the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The class had very little structure to it, was extremely difficult for an introductory course, and prof isn't good at teaching things. He constantly preached the importance of learning things on your own time. I have no idea how his average rating is so high-- I can see how he might be well suited for an upper div course but def not an intro one.

Where do I even begin. Dr. Venkatram is by far one of the worst professors I've taken in any level of college. He derives equations in class and typically derives them in a general sense which is usually helpful but does not properly explain the assumptions one needs to make to properly apply them. His tests are a joke, adding useless information.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: While this was undoubtedly the hardest professor I've taken, the difficulty comes at the cost of true learning. His lectures and exams are not just plug and chug, requiring you to understand and apply the underlying concepts. Rise to the bar he sets and you will succeed and take the knowledge with you.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He's a good professor and cares about his students. But he's a little more on the traditional/ strict side of things. Don't come late.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Amazingly intelligent and knowledgeable. Horrible lecturer.

what can i say ? he is good because he is trying to teach students learn what he understood. this is important , because 50% of professors just explain  the ppt, and 49% of professor may give a fair handwriting about what textbook says. He is the only one teach useful knowledge .

Despite what everyone has said, he is an amazing professor. He is super hard, and although he is mean if you ask questions, he WILL answer the questions in class and clear up ANY confusion by giving several examples. You just cant be scared to ask.
His tests are very confusing.

Since it is Venkatram, you will need to work hard to get your A. His quizzes take much less effort than midterm and the hellish final. You will need to know the material very well(every bit of it) to do well on the midterm/final. and be sure you know MATLAB otherwise, you are SCREWED! Be sure to not fall behind if you want the A in the class.

This class shouldn't have been hard but Venkatram somehow made it seem to be hard. He was gracious to us at the end with the curve and dropping quizzes and replacing midterms so it all kind of balanced out. Prepare to study his notes thoroughly and you will be able to pass the class.

This class isn't hard; it is physics. You will be working on the lab assignments a lot since you are new to MATLAB.He does explain things fast, since he expects you to know it. He is just preparing you for upper divs.
He was a fair teacher and everything on his midterms/finals was fair game because of the practice exams he gave us. Study hard and do not skip a lecture or you will be lost.

This is a TOUGH class, 40%-60% fail rate. The first 2/3 of the quarter I seriously left every lecture annoyed, angry, and confused because I understood nothing that he just taught. He is a nice guy though and tests/quizzes are fair because he gives slight variations of problems we've already seen. You'll be teaching yourself the material every week

You'll probably get lost during his lectures. Not a big deal though, cause once you start working on the labs, everything will come together. Midterm was overkill, final was fair. Offered final to replace midterm if better grade. You'll spend a lot of time working on lab assignments.

Very helpfull professor. The class does make you grind out questions and he does expects you to suffer. But asking the right questions will just blow your mind away. Dont show up late cuz he will single you out for teh lulz. He KNOWS HIS STUFF.
A good teacher who cares bout his students. Has a tough going teaching personality but it willing to make sure his students knows what's going on

Dr. Venkatram is a very tough professor. But he is very considerate about the student's needs. He tries to help us learn the subject. His tests are extremely hard though, but very helpful and tolerant on labs.

This is by far the hardest professor ever !! dont slack off, dont ask stupid questions or else he won't answer it. dont come even 2 seconds late or else he will call you out. dont play on your phone or even drink water in class. great professor, he knows his stuff but he goes really fast so dont slack off

This professor was terrible! He has a thick accent and when i pleaded to him for help he just doesn't care.  Needless to say i am transferring to Davis and the retaking Dynamics there and the prof is way better.  All venkatram does is terribly fast-paced hw problems and derivations in class.

Professor Venkatram is honestly my favorite Professor. As long as you pay attention in class and attend regularly, everything is pretty simple. The final consisted of nothing but example problems he did in class. Also at the end of the year he invited everyone for pizza at the Getaway which was pretty awesome to talk to him outside of class

Mr. "High and Mighty" will SCHOOL YOU!!!! He expects you to know everything that he teaches. more than 50% of the class obtained a D grade. This guy is insane....HE LOVES MATLAB....the class can be unrelated to MATLAB and somehow he will make you use MATLAB. "You are late to my class....get out!" This guy doesn't play around.
He knows his stuff, but he  hardly cares if you know it.  Most importantly the final is worth 50% of your grade!

If you can, do not take a class with this professor. All of the material is from his lectures (which are very convoluted and sporadic). Expects you to know everything before you take the class. His projects can take an insane ammount of time to complete. All tests are scary to say the least.

Despite rumors and appearances, Venkatram is a very good professor.  If you pay attention, he's easy to follow along with.  He's hard to approach initially, but once he starts talking to you is real nice.  Just don't try coming in late or drinking in class.
No Comments

The hardest engineering professor. All material is from his own lectures. Never really understood what he did in class. The final exam was insane! First time I took a break just to stare out the window because of the massive headache I got.

This has been BY FAR the worst experience with a class/professor I've had. She does not understand the material and it is evident by how she regurgitates the textbook (poorly) to us and is unable of doing anything beyond. Her lecture notes are littered with mistakes, she's missed/cancelled many office ours and lectures. Overall very unprofessional.
She doesn't understand the material enough to teach the class. Cancelled or missed office hours. Her notes had so many mistakes.  Her lectures were useless as she copied the entire textbook.
Great Professor. Class is difficult, Exams are not all that difficult. Assigns a lot of homework

Brilliant professor. I had her for RLST129 (History of Philosophy in India) in winter 2026. She is extremely knowledgeable and the class was very engaging. She fosters participation and reflection well. Attendance is rightly mandatory; the material the course is based on is quite inaccessible otherwise. Tests aren't easy but are curved accordingly.
Lectures are mandatory and the class grading is compromised of 4 short essays and a Final essay. If you put effort in writing the essays you should have no problem getting an A.

Ana is a domineering woman. She does not want her students to engage or have discussions with her. She does not want you to have any opinion other then hers. This is not someone who will support you or help you unless she absolutely has to. She's fine for a quick class. JUST DO NOT DISAGREE WITH HER.

Prof. Ana was great! There are PowerPoints which are posted right before class so you can follow along as she reads over them. There are a lot of readings (no textbooks just pdf's) and I recommend reading them before coming to class. She stops throughout lecture to ask questions and this counts as your participation. Very thorough but not dry.
There were essays due every other week but were pretty short and easy so long as one watched the lecture videos and skimmed the readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Honestly a really good class to act as a breadth alongside a heavy course load. She is a very nice professor. There is a midterm which you have a cheatsheet and a final in which you work on the entire quarter. Good luck!

I took this class to satisfy the ENGL1C requirement. BEST decision ever! If you ever see this class and Prof.Anthea is teaching it. JUST TAKE it. She was so kind. Throughout the quarter there's a giant paper to work on(with multiple progress work). And a midterm with 1 page cheatsheet. It's way easier than a regular 1C! My TA Pannaga was amazing!

Fun professor, could tell she really cared about dance. No actual dancing involved, but you get to watch a lot of cool and entertaining videos so I recommend going to lecture. Only one paper and you work on it the entire quarter.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors at UCR so far! DEFINITELY take this class if you can as a substitute for a regular English class. You only have one paper for the whole quarter and you work on it literally all quarter so there's not too much to do come final's week. Lectures are super engaging and there's a bit of reading but definitely manageable.

I needed my ENGL1C class fulfilled so I took this course and despite it being writing heavy, it wasn't even that bad. I focused on The Greatest Showman throughout the quarter and put all of what I wrote into one big paper at the end of the quarter and submitted it. Super easy and definitely really interesting. Extremely doable!

Overall a very easy class — she tells you exactly what you need to do in order to get an A. Pop quizzes are extremely easy. She is a very nice professor who cares about her students. Important Note: The main focus of this class was the POLITICS of dance NOT THE HISTORY.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This professor is really understanding! She allowed us to be on zoom while she did live lectures. Each week there is only one easy assignment due and for the final, its just a paper. Theres also one midterm as well. You can tell she loves dance and makes the subject interesting. I would take her again!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Taken as a W course with no dance knowledge with 3 paper assignments: own movement analysis, music video analysis, dance film analysis. If you follow the grading rubric it's easy. Workshops help a lot! Professor was passionate about the topic and incorporated DWTS into lectures. One extra credit assignment worth 15 points. Would recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--EXTRA CREDIT--So many papers

reviews.comment: Easiest professor I've had here at this school. She is so clear and concise and gives so much extra credit that there's no way you can't pass the class. One midterm and one final. Midterm was literally the easiest test you can have (multiple choice, fill in the blank, matching). Class is just memorization but so easy. Take her!

Most striaghtfoward class EVER. She's was a very nice teacher.  She tells you exactly what to look for on midterms and tests.  Even on write-ups, she tells you exactly what she is looking for and how to analyze and write it and the different techniques she wants and expects.  .  I don't think there is an easier class than this .
This class was interesting and you learn alot about dance history. Study the terms she gives because they are all on the tests! Overall, enjoyable class and good professor.
easy A. didnt do anything. went to class once in a while. just study the terms she gives you in study guide and do extra credit.

The class is pretty interesting. There are opportunities for extra credit that aren't extremely hard. I would suggest going to the classes and reading the readings because it really helps with the quizzes she gives out, though they're not that hard

She is GREAT!! Super Easy! make flash cards for your midterm and final and you will do fine! i got an A. she makes you write a paper about dance, a midterm, and one final. She shows videos in her class and makes it fun to attend. great class!
She is a very interesting teacher, she showed numerous movies, and videos to help keep the class fun. Test are easy, as long as you use flash cards to study. GREAT TEACHER!

Very easy class. You get graded on attendance, 3 writing assignments (just answering questions) and a final project video. Honestly not bad at all, and Anderson is an interesting lecturer. He also talks about very interesting topics. This is a good pick for a breadth or just to take credits tbh. Gives lots of extra credit opportunities too.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is incredibly friendly. He gives fun lectures and covers a wide range of topics in insightful ways. He loves participation. He will ask for someone to answer a question after every sentence or two and he likes the people who raise their hand. Sometimes he uses academic jargon that is hard to understand at first. Most grading was done by TAs.

Such a great professor! You can tell he is interested in what he is teaching. He always goes into full detail and helps all his students. He is very respectful and is willing to make the class engaging. Just pay attention and answer questions when he asks. overall such a nice professor and an easy class!

probably the easiest course in this entire school. just show up to class, take the quiz a million times until you get what you want, and u should be able to make one 7 minute video project about two topics in 10 weeks. would lowkey be sad when only a couple people would participate in lecture because he seems passionate about his subjects.

Dr. Anderson has honestly been one coolest and most caring professors I've had at UCR, the class structure was very clearly laid out, two take-home exams, three easy worksheets, and the writing prompts in lecture. He was very passionate in what he was teaching the class. You have to put more effort into failing than passing. 10/10 recommend.
Dr. Anderson is amazing! Take his classes, all of them are great!

The professor is truly enthusiastic about his lectures which makes it interesting to always attend. Nothing was difficult as long as you do the assignments online and the tests were taken at home and only be passed if you pay attention to the lectures and read articles. It was overall a good class and something new to learn.

Professor Anderson is kind and passionate. This class provided a great perspective on workers' rights/union organizing and we had a variety of guest speakers. All the tests are take home, the worksheets are easy, and the final project is a short video comparing 2 labor movements. Make sure to attend the lecture for attendance and prompt credit.

Given the situations that came about during this qtr, I expected him to be a little more supportive & understanding. This was not the case. I didn't feel that he cared about his students. Pre-recorded lecture material was insightful however, it was hard to enjoy his class when he didn't acknowledge events or accommodate my peers who were affected.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The textbook is not required to do well in this class. The quizzes/tests were all online and you could take each quiz up to 3 times. There was only one essay we had to do and no final exam, just a group video. Overall, the class was nearly impossible to not pass. If youre looking for an easy A, take this professor!

Good professor, theres a lot of reading assignments that are very dense but if you skim them to get the basic idea + attend the lectures you'll be good. Lectures are mandatory because he makes you do little short answers for class participation, but you'll be ok if you miss a day or 2. All tests are online do them early to get a good grade.

Very easy class, attendance is not mandatory because he puts all of his slides online. Gives study guides of exactly what will be on test. A group video project and essay where you have to analyze a media product. He also gives a lot of extra credit opportunities.
Tests, Group Projects, Term Paper, and Extra Credit. Reasonable professor and T.A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: MCS001 requires you to attend every lecture. Professor Anderson doesn't post his slide online and usually covers material at a fast pace. The class requires no textbook. There are only 5 quizzes throughout the quarter without a midterm or final exam. In addition, there is a final project at the end of the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Gray did a great job making the many topics we spanned both digestible and enjoyable to learn about. He has occasional quizzes at the beginning of class, but lectures will be interesting enough that you *want* to go to class. 2 field trips and interesting labs.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Gray is nice but his exams were tough and had vague wording, he also referred to his exams as a 'game.' He does not provide study materials for exams and reads off of powerpoints. Studying requires going through 17 separate powerpoints with 30+ slides, no curve, would not recommend. Labs are interesting.

One of the most understanding and lenient professors in the ENSC department. His lectures weren't that engaging, but it's his first time doing online learning. Due dates for projects & assignments are relaxed; don't have to worry about meeting them exactly on time, but be aware that there's heavy emphasis on reading scientific research papers
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: I took him for ENSC 101 and Ecohydrology. Amazing professor, who genuinely cares for his students! No reading in either class! Only downside to ENSC 101 is is there is a bit of formula memorization, even though he says there is not. I would highly recommend Professor Gray and would take for a 3rd time if given the opportunity!
Good professor look at slides for guidance. No textbook required.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Very effective professor, posts slides and old exams online. Old exams are super helpful and so does the slides. Attendence is not mendatory but recommented. Interesting class.

Slides are posted online (exams are based on these). He also posts the old exams and keys for you to get ready for the exam. A very effective teacher, however, can spend like 15 minutes on one or two slides. He is funny and very nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Great personality, but teaches way too fast. Aji cares about his students though and has a nice curve in the end. Homework can either be easy or difficult, but most of the time, they are doable. Midterm/Final was alright; not easy nor hard. As long as you get the general gist of how to apply the formula/ understand the concept, you'll pass with a B
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: The difference between PHYS40B and 40C is night and day. Prof. wasn't bad; the fact that I have to retake it was all on me. Honestly, they should make multi-variable calculus a pre-req like at other universities; it really, really helps. Knowing seriessequence calculus is a pre-req for some reason, but you never use it.

He is very articulate. He does cool experiments in class. He will help you step by step, but he will assume you understand it if you don't ask questions. He does a lot of cool examples that help you understand principles of motion. Homework is demanding because his homework is difficult, but really helpful on the tests.
A great physics professor. He knows his material very well. Very helpful during office hours. He teaches difficult material very well to students. Very satisfied with this professor.

You have to attend lectures even though they become repetitive. Participation is important. TAs do the heavy lifting. Although you read a lot, it's not difficult. Easy course. Only issue is they grade fairly late compared to others and take forever to upload midterms and final.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
Prof. Winer is a very insightful professor who is very laid-back and professional when he speaks.  Participation is crucial for your grade in lectures and in discussions with your TA.  He is a little hard to reach out of class, but should you need anything, your TA will likely have you covered.

Also: be prepared to read and write!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The difficulty of this class depends on your TA since they grade your participation/homework. I had an amazing TA who made this a really fun and easy-going class. Lectures are long and mandatory, and so is participating in lectures, strict about leaving early or if you don't share in lectures. Participation matters a lot in this class so beware.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Winer as a person was great. He was respectful of students, made sure to remind people to put trigger warnings before reading, once stood up for a TA who had an inappropriate comment made to her, and gave good feedback. The class itself was time-consuming and had a lot of work. Tip: thrift books to save money on all the texts needed!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Good writing professor in general. Easy A if you turn in all the hw and participate actively in class. Would recommend if you are just taking it for credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: The class is fairly easy if you just read and don't hate to write. The lectures and reading become redundant after a while. This class depends on your TA and how strict their grading rubric is. Also depends if you can get past a bunch of first-years who foam their mouths at Winer.

New book every week along with a weekly journal/creative piece. I must be a glutton for punishment because I took one of Winer's classes previously and did not enjoy it. The lectures are tiresome as are the journals after you hit the five week mark. You won't learn a ton but it is nice to have the authors come into class. Participate in lecture!

He relies on his TA's to do the heavy lifting. They're great. He doesn't add any real substance during  class. A book a week is unnecessary, especially considering how little or redundant the info we get is. He introduces the writers who come in as old friends so there is a sense of nepotism. It's a very costly class since you buy every book.
Really easy as long as you do the homework!

Winer is a chill and entertaining professor. The class is not hard as long as you are a competent writer, though if you are not a fan of literary analysis, you might not find this class very fun, especially since the lectures are 3 hours. That's the only reason I would not take this class again, but if you can take that I'd greatly recommend him.

The lectures did not seem too helpful regarding the course material. The homework was formatted in an needlessly complicated way which was more tedious than a good work exercise. It was also difficult to truly digest the readings per week since there were many. Not the best but definitely not the worst.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lecture is long and kinda boring. Each week a new piece of a fiction/nonfiction/poetry piece is revealed. You have to do weekly journals, which can get tedious, especially depending on how your TA grades. Midterm and final consist of your own creative pieces. If you don't think you can handle a three hour lecture, DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS!

Loved this class!! If you love reading and writing, it's perfect. The homework (reading a lot of novels) is a bit heavy but the books are interesting and easy reads. The 3 hour lectures aren't bad at all, we had breaks, weren't doing the same things the whole time, and discussion is interesting. Prof Winer is very approachable, nice and funny.
Professor Winer is amazing. Yes the lectures are long but theyre very interesting and hes hilarious. If you love reading and writing I say take this class its an easy A.

I really enjoy Professor Winer, he is so kind, smart, and a great teacher because of how much he cares. What I enjoy about our class is how much he structures our discussion around student's participation, it makes me feel like my ideas matter and actually make me interested to learn and read the material. He is very thoughtful and gentle.
He is an amazing professor! The only downside is the three-hour lecture, but other than that it is an amazing class! All the work is graded by the TA, so get to know them! Very flexible and lenient.

Taking class because I love reading and writing. Definitely only got one of the two reasons. The books contain heavy subjects (including rape and suicide) and are just about failed relationships thus far or some form of drama. Might as well watch a soap opera TA's are great. Be warned, you have to buy books and that can get costly FAST.

Winer is a bit much, you will love it. He will go on and on about things. He is friendly and will spend time every class just talking to students. The TAs are the ones that grade and most of the learning happen in discussion. Lots of writing. Participate, talk in lectures. Get to know the TA, go to office hour. Need to create original work
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I really liked my professor, and would gladly take the course again, but the one thing that I hated was that the class was almost 3 hours long. If it wasn't so long i'd for sure take the class again. He has clicker questions, so make sure to show up for class. The TA's are very nice and comment on your work and give out great feedback. Loved it!

I had a 3 hour lecture, so it was heavy. He was very repetitive and didn't cover the books; he would get stuck on ONE SENTENCE, taking word by word, for 20 minutes. Read a book every week, and wrote on it and had to dissect each line. Papers were weekly and based on the style of the book. Quizzes for attendance each class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Winer's class is a must-take class if you love to read and write! This class is a 3 hour long lecture, which is understandably a deal breaker for many! Definitely a lot of reading! But if you love to read, write, and talk about novels in depth and society in depth as well, this could be a great class for you :) I personally loved it 100%

Lectures are 100% useless and 3 hours long, I found myself going for the clicker questions and there wouldn't even be any. I understand that he wants to teach writing through observing but he didn't seem organized or prepared half the time, it was like he was stalling. Book choices were cool! I only read 5/9 though.

A nice guy. Expects you to read a lot and quickly. Some of the books are interesting, some are awful. Have to do weekly writings and journals but it is manageable if you read. Lecture is run like a discussion, most of it is listening to students read or he goes off on random tangents that don't help writing. Could be better, could be worse.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: I hated this class from the start. He focused on menial things more than necessary. E.g.: spending an hour or more on a word's definition. A lot of his advice wasn't that great nor helpful, and overall made things WORSE. Work is easy & clear, but his advice wasn't good in terms of how to write or edit. Funny sometimes. No personality connection.

I love creative writing, but this class sucked. Long, meandering lectures. Lots of hair flipping. Made us buy books we didn't read. Made us buy HIS book in hardcover. Waded through his fan club to get to office hours. Ended class confessing how he cried in the bathroom waiting to hear from his publisher. Inspirational? No. Self-important ? Yep.
Interesting prof, interesting book choices. Obviously a good writer. Do the work and you'll be fine.
Great professor! You learn a lot about the different ways of writing and how to make your writing better. Grade consists of weekly journals and a midterm and a final. VERY EASY CLASS.

Professor Winer is brilliant and hilarious. Being introduced to new books to study as a writer is so important, and he's an excellent writer himself. He understands the mechanics of writing, and the orientation of the writer's mind. Perfect for a CRWT professor. If you are looking for a gratifying Creative Writing experience - take him.
HES REALLY FUNNY AND INTERESTING. I LOVE HOW HE MAKES THE CLASS THINK EVEN THOUGH THE CLASS COULD BE SHORTER

Winer was hands-down my favorite CRWT prof at UCR. He assigns tons of reading and provokes deep philosophical discussion, but if you do the work, he grades pretty easily. He's a dynamic teacher, supersmart, hilarious, and has read everything. Always ready to help you find a book list to help with your latest project. Took every course I could w/him

He is very philosophy oriented which really turned me off to his class and he makes you read writers that are very political and philosophical, forcing you to interact with the reading to do your homework. It got very "busy work" esque and I don't think it really contributed much to my writing. On a plus, almost everyone gets an A in this class

He is such an amazing teacher. You learn A LOT in his class! Attendance is not mandatory, but if you miss it you will also miss the book discussions which are very helpful for midterm and final! You will learn a lot and read amazing books too!

Winer is a genius. An interesting professor that you'll learn alot from. His syllabus is always intimidating, but dont judge his class based on it. he gives alot of work & reading, a book a week. but he's not a tough grader. There are lots of books you have to buy & assignments every week. you also have to participate vocally in classes
I learned a lot in this class and enjoyed it a lot. It requires a good amount of reading, but they are good books and movies!

i am probably the wrong person to vote because my girlfriend who was in it dumped me halfway through. still if you are a crwt major at ucr and you dont take this class or at least one by winer you are just cheating yourself. brilliant, witty, hip, and master literary craftsman. that about sums it up.
hes really funny and knows structure, plot and character really really well. cant ask for a much better teacher. plus he wears cool shirts.

He's a fun teacher who made the class very interesting.  I felt that I learned a lot from him.  Just be prepared to do a lot of writing, especially writing your own ghost, detective, and other original stories (which isn't exactly easy).

Todd is a cool dude. He covers material rather quickly though. If your trying to just chill and get by you will certainly perish into the utter emptiness of the universe. But if your up to the challenge Todd will definitely make you a better mathematician. He understands math is hard at times so he does set a curve although he doesn't make it known

Todds actually good. He's so giddy about math(cool). He assigns maybe too much hw. His exams are really fair. His grading scale is curved 60-69C and 70-79C+ office hours are like jam sessions. He'll help you more if you don't act like you haven't even looked at the problem. Overall, you'll learn a lot, Todd's a winner, if you can handle the hw sets
He's a great professor; however, TONS of homework. The workload was a little ridiculous at times; however, he curved generously at the end! Go to all his classes and you'll be fine!
Awesome professor!! Helps his students if you choose to go to his problem sessions and office hours!
Great class!! Very helpful!

Im still waiting on my final but am expecting either and A or A-. I think he is great at teaching, but it's really up to you to make the most of what he teaches. Don't ever miss lecture, the book is useless haha. He is also pretty funny. Grades HW on completion. But his exams are heavily based on the hw. He has high expectations of you though.

He eventually stopped assigning hw due every class, but there was still proof problems due each week. There's a review sheet for the exams and he'll "like" certain proofs. Memorize the proofs, you might even understand it. If you must take this class, you might be okay if you DO NOT procrastinate on the project and studying the proofs.
Worst math professor ever.  This guy has no curve and he throws things fast at the students.  Do not take this guy.  He will ruin your GPA and life.
I dreaded his class so much I dropped it to take it with a diff professor.  he has hw assigned every lecture so hw due 3 times a week, he docent curve, and grades unreasonably strict.  Don't take
He runs the class solely on proofs and is incredibly anal about them on tests.. He expects you to know everything word for word even if it is not covered in the class.. Avoid if possible

he assigns homework after every class which you have to turn in at your next class meeting, he makes you type up proofs with a program that I have never used before.  he goes really fast, this is a hard teacher I highly suggest you avoid him.

He made us use a program to write up our proof homework every day. I have never used or even heard of the program before and had to learn it completely on my own in 2 days. He assigns a massive amount of homework. He tries to joke around, but his jokes are... well, lame. Dropped after 2 weeks. Didn't want to deal with it.

9C is a hard hard class in general, much more dense info than 9a or 9b. His lectures are useful, but didnt like the quiz and worksheet method he uses in discussion. Midterms  wasnt too hard, but hes a harsh grader. has a scaled curve and final was 70% of the total grade. didnt pass the class, but definitely not taking his class again.

He was pretty good at teaching the concepts required, however, his tests were ridiculous. He used numbers that one needed a calculator for, but there aren't any calculators allowed. He also used obscure rules and examples that were mentioned maybe once in a lecture.  Good teacher, BAD tests. Don't expect an A.

Todd is an excellent professor.I had him for math009b last quarter and got a B+ but this quarter I have a different professor for math009C. My new professor is HORRIBLE and i really missed Todd's teaching style, so I sometimes go to Todd's lecture even though im not in his class. pretty much half my class attends Todd's lectures so we can learn :)

He's a great professor in teaching, but his grading can be a bit harsh. Average was about 40 on the midterm, and that was with some grading by nicer TAs too. He does give a ton of examples during lecture. A majority of questions on his exams do come from hw. So take good notes, do hw with effort, study discussion quizzes, and practice practice!

Hard grader, has horrible jokes, and in general a bad teacher, he had more reviews on here all saying how bad he was but looks like someone took them down, only 7 people got above a C on the midterm,  dont take his class

"If it were my choice, there would be no curve"   -Todd                   Yeah.. You have to work your butt off to get even close to a B in this class. If you want to pass, go to office hours for both the professor and the TA.
Grades way too hard. The class average for our midterm was a 40. Otherwise, he is actually a pretty good teacher and is funny at times. Take him if you want, just beware of his ridiculous grading
Pretty good teacher, very detailed in showing work. If you ask questions, he might be a bit harsh on you. Most of the work is simple since you don't need to rely on your calculator.
His lectures are kinda boring. The exams are surprisingly pretty easy and he is generous with the extra credit. His class is very passable because he doesn't want students to suffer.

The programming assignments/HW were difficult and sometimes covered things we didn't even learn. Lets you work in pairs though. Lectures were super boring. Also it took 4 weeks to grade the first midterm and he uses AI to grade the exams. BUT he is EXTREMELY GENEROUS with grading and extra credit. I was about to fail but got A+ after the curve!!

There are a lot of assignments but make sure you keep up with all of them and you are good. Try to do extra credit whenever you can cuz they help a lot. He gives fairly easy midterms and there is a huge extra credit opportunity on the final.
He has unfair grading criteria. He hardly listens to the students request. If you perform well throughout the quarter and put in your efforts, still you may end up getting C/B.

Lectures are very clear and engaging. Tests are extremely straightforward if you attend lectures and complete the homework and there is also a curve. No coding Judy pseudocode and lenient grading on tests.

He has an accent but his lectures make a lot of sense. CS141 is one of the hardest courses at UCR and he makes it so much easier than the other professors like Yan Gu. There is no coding in his course (just pseudocode) and tests are extremely straightforward, just do some basic problems from online and understand the class examples.
The lectures were mainly just slides, but the final exam had 50% extra credit opportunity that raised everyone a letter grade. Pretty much just Zybooks besides that. Overall the class was alright.

I rated him before, but i was wrong, this man is a saint. The final exam was the easiest I've ever had in any class, my had was literally moving on its own to write the answers. He also gave two questions at the end, 25% extra credit each. I got a 135/100 and my grade shot up to and A+. Was a pretty hard quarter though, don't slack on assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Magdy was VERY confusing and his lectures were really hard to understand. When we asked for a midterm study guide, he refused to give one and instead said to study everything. Any other professor > Amr (even Elena).

Just plain unhelpful. I saw that he records his lectures but he won't post them in the slack for some reason, when I asked to get a link he said he would send it later but he never did. His "review materials" for the midterm was just a 7-question little quiz. Didn't even set up the zybooks correctly, there aren't any due dates for any assignments.
Tests are pretty straightforward if you know the material. Lectures are very helpful in general.
Hard to understand professor with a heavy accent, not responsive on slack, vague test questions, but he curved the final a bit.

Relatively easy class if you just study. Glosses over slides way too fast though, so be prepared to teach yourself. Cares about little things way too much like mandatory selfies and the TAs carries the actual material breakdown. Wishes she focuses more on teaching than taking selfies.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Do not take this class. Run.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Reviews are low for i dont know what reason. As long as you keep up week to week with readings and attend discussion to get clarity on topics you're unclear about you will be fine. The majority of your grade is based off 3 exams and then discussion/lecture attendance. Just lock in.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her material was a lot of reading and memorizing. If one is able to memorize all the materials then one will be fine for the final. The tests are multiple choice and are easy if one can memorize.

Attendance is mandatory, you can miss 3 times without it affecting your grade and 2 points ec. Tests are curved, everything on tests are provided in lecture and study guide. Ratings make it seem like she is a tough professor, but honestly as long as you know the material and how to apply it you will be able to pass this class, an A is doable.

Shes a nice professor and wants us to succeed but I did not like the way she structured the class. We originally had the class earlier and ended up switching to a much later time and she made attendance mandatory by taking a selfie. She goes very fast and expects us to memorize everything that day it was taught. VERY LECTURE HEAVY.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: My favorite professor by far! Attendance is mandatory but, this is great for students because this course is lecture and reading-heavy. Attending these lectures will make exams easier! I finished this class with an A.
Professor Amy gives A LOT OR READINGS, in which you have to make sure to read since they may come in the quizzez.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Kroska is by far one of my favorite professor's at UCR. She's inclusive and kind to her students. Mid-quarter, she offered an online option for those who could not attend lecture. There were only three exams; all were an easy A as long as you took notes from the powerpoint slides, which she posted on canvas. Attend lecture, study, and you'll pass.

I was hesitant on taking her class because of the reviews. But now that I have taken Soc 142 (not Soc 4) with her and comparing her to professor Rotondi Soc 3 she is amazing. What you learn and what is in her study guide is what is on the test. No bull with her. People who complain about her class have clearly never taken a class with Rotondi.

She really is passionate about the topic I respect that, and she did curve the test since it was her first time teaching at UCR and the test was all over the place. She is understanding but the tests were difficult, I felt I knew the material but my score said otherwise. SO much material and I felt the test was nothing that was used as examples.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: It's obvious she knows the material; how she explains it is a different story. So much information to retain and she wants you to know every bit of it for the exams. The only way most people passed this class was by begging for a curve, which she had to do for every quiz/exam. You seriously have to work for this class with studying and guides. GL
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: She is not a good professor, she does not have an organized way for grading. Took the final and still have not received my grade. Mind you this class was taken on canvas and normally you should be able to look at your overall grade and somehow now the class is removed from canvas. Idk why she decided to do canvas instead of ilearn waste of time
Its a difficult class, but shes really sweet. You really, really have to work your b*tt off. Not a bad class but get ready if you take a class with her.
Lectures are hard to focus on and she gives so much information that it's hard to remember it all especially for the midterm. Would not take any class with her again.

Professor Kroska is decent at teaching. Perhaps it's because of the virtual learning format, but her lectures are draining. And by the end of listening to her lectures, barely any information is retained. Not to mention the course format, which is dependent on a student's ability to memorize hundreds of concepts and terms.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Amy is overall helpful and wants you to exceed. She has chosen the material well and has clear expectations for what needs to be learned for examinations. She is helpful when approached with questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Easy class, teacher got an attitude and was rude during office. Do not recommend.
Rude and passive aggressive

I really enjoyed the class and what was taught. Amy's a little intimidating and passive aggressive, but she does give note cards for the weekly quizzes, and posts learning objective questions at the end of each lecture, so it's easy to get a good grade.

Amy is the worst professor. She is rude and will pick on small things and make it bigger. She is very unprofessional when you talk to her about her mistakes she will make sure to get you back and will drag you down. TA should be teaching this class. quizzes are worded hard and she will get mad at you for asking the same questions. Not recommended

BPSC133- The class is pretty straight forward with lectures and quizzes taking up the most part. Love cheatsheets. Amy as a person is rude, but I love the TA and Andy they're wonderful people. She's picky and disrespectful but you for sure should pass overall.

Lecture is test heavy quizzes every Tuesday + 2 Midterms & Final. Amy is a fair professor , she gives cheat sheets for quizzes/final/midterm every Thursday making attendance mandatory. In my personal experience, she was very understanding of student's situations. Only complaint is that you don't know your grade until its posted on rweb.
not a great experience. Wish her the best but if it weren't for Tito I would've purposely break-checked a semi otw to school.

Was a difficult class but not impossible. U got cheatsheets for quizzes but only if you're present in the previous class. She's a bit condescending, but TAs are helpful. Ask questions before or ur just gonna be hit with low marks. Worst part was that she uploads grades only on banner, so you'll have no idea what ur grade is until its too late.

Difficult Professor. Shes not very helpful and very passive aggressive. I worked really hard in this class for an A, but grades weren't known until she uploaded on banner (which was probably on purpose so that students could not contest their grades or ask Qs). avoid her class, the projects and structure of the class are not great

BPSC033-Idk if this was just a bad quarter for her, but I wish I took ENTM instead. Amy was okay at times, but very passive aggressive. She gets annoyed easily which is why a lot of us leaned towards asking TA questions. The class was based mainly on month long projects. you wont have ANY idea what your grade is until after finals. take a diff prof

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. AWFUL!! TA is very nice and helpful, but Amy is rude and conceding. Anytime I asked for help, I felt as though she was mocking me. Never hated plants more in my life. The projects are awfully specific and no one understood what she wanted. Hard work and effort will not guarantee you a good grade.

This is the most exhausting class I have taken in my undergrad. grade is determined by 2 projects and a few quizzes, but those 2 projects are awful. Many of us struggled with what she wanted bc there were so critical. WE ARE NOT BOTANIST; GIVE US A BREAK. I went to OH and still had difficulty. boring lectures and mandatory atten. AVOID THIS PROF.

Professor Amy is great but there way too much quizes to do. Like there a quiz every week in class, then in the lab there's more quizzes, then there practical (2) in lab, 2 midterms and one final. She does give notecards that can be used for quizzes and midterm. It just a lot do don't take for easy A and dont take with other harder classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Lit's class is not hard, you will have to take a weekly quiz and three midterms in total. As long as you are keeping up with her lecture videos/lecture, you will do alright. She's also very kind and is very passionate about her work, all in all, great character to be around.
Shes the reason you will do well in this course
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I had her for the 2nd part (plants) of the class. Her clickers are pretty simple but don't look like her test questions, which seem like book questions. She emphasizes important concepts during lecture, so keep an ear out. Overall, just an avg professor.

Best lecturer I've had in university. Caring and highly educated on everything she talks about. Easy to ask her for help. As long as you pay attention in class and put in the effort she asks for you will excell in her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Amazing! I loved her

Definitely of the best professors I've had, very caring and wants everyone to succeed. No final, the exams reflect material covered, and many EC opportunities. She has mastered presenting which makes the lectures enjoyable and fun..... would take her again!

She has really mastered her presentation skills which helps a lot in lectures. I had her for intro to chemical and environmental engineering which was a very easy but insightful class. That class has been perfected in every way, and she cares about feedback. Great professor. Would definitely take again!

Very kind professor and is very approachable. This course has no final, but there are two midterms each worth 15% of your grade. The HW is worth 40% and it is the most important part, it can require a lot of time to complete the homework. The exams though are not focused on writing code. Lots of extra credit opportunities too.

Probably one of the best professors on school. Very good lectures, really wants to make sure that everyone understands and learns all of the topics. Exams are exclusively on the material covered and are not difficult. Very approachable with any kind of help necessary.
She's very clear and makes learning easy for students.

Dr. Rupiper was a very fair professor! She is actually one of the most considerate profs I have had. She is so kind and caring. 40% of your grade is just HW and if you do it early enough she will even check it for you. Definitely attend class as most examples she does in class will be very very similar to the ones in the test.
He's a really good professor. The subject was difficult, but it was easy to follow along with his lectures

This class is one of the hardest in the CS degree. Prof. Amey can move too fast or give too much work on accident since he has mastered the concepts. However, he always admits when he makes a mistake. His lectures aren't the best, but his genuine care for students makes him a great educator.  CS141 as a 5-week summer class was doable thanks to him!

Great professor with excellent lectures that teach you how to think about algorithm design. The homeworks were pretty challenging (around leetcode medium/hard level). The exams and quizzes were extremely fair and accommodating. Overall, one of the best and helpful CS courses at UCR.

He is a very caring professor, he understands students and is very flexible with how his class is ran, there was a take home midterm and a take home final albeit harder. Homework needs to be done ASAP, so do it early if you can. Very approachable in OH, the TA's weren't that helpful to be fair. But if you go to his office hours you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Bhangale spends a lot time going over each algorithm by working through examples, making sure to explain the motivation behind it. He was pretty clear with what he taught (sometimes it could be a little boring). His grading is pretty lenient, and there were several extra credit opportunities. He's also very approachable outside of class

Very approachable professor. The homework for 141 was very hard, apparently much harder than the other professors according to my TA, but I managed to do well. The difficult homework may've been key to my understanding as the lectures can get hard to follow. The class is not overwhelming despite 141's rep, but you must start assignments ASAP.
The grades were decided by quizzes, hw and a challenging final! Good lectures in person but are early morning ones :(
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Hard class but I managed to pass. Homework heavy and challenging final exam!
Professor Mackay is an incredible teacher. I love seeing people really know and love what they're doing. She also gives incredible feedback, and fostered a wonderful critique.

Professor Amy is so nice! She is great at giving advice appropriate to your level, and is very encouraging. Great at spotting areas of improving. She is understanding of emergencies and attendance is mandatory (duh) but she is lenient on being a little late (don't push it), so no stress! Super kind, interesting class, and felt like I got better!

One of the best professors I've ever had! She was very encouraging, and if you're not the best artist/still learning, or know next to nothing, she's very understanding, yet helpful in getting you to where you want to head to. Attendance is mandatory, but if you don't feel well/have an emergency, she's understanding and excuses attendance.

Professor Mackay deeply cares about students and engages in good conversation. You must purchase your own materials. She's clear about what you need for the class and what assignments you need to do. Helpful painting tutorials. Responds to emails quickly. Overall, very in touch and easy to speak to. Be prepared to speak about yours/others' art.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Overall, Amanda Lucia's class was pretty tedious to be in. While her grading criteria was clear her lectures were quite dry and there was a heavy reading courseload. I disliked her changing the final format last minute as well as raising the grade needed to get an A literally after the class ended when all quarter it was different in the syllabus.

reviews.comment: Study guides given in class were less than half relevant to the midterm and the final.
