He is very specific on what he wants, and is a tough grader when it comes to essays and homework. He provides a lot of handouts that might anytime overwhelms the students, but they come in handy once you start writing your papers. GO TO HIS OFFICE HOURS AND ASK FOR HELP! He reads your essay drafts, so take that as an advantage. WORK HARD!

Avoid! I took this class not wanting to miss the opportunity that I was actually able to get into a 1B class (since its hard to get in one). MISTAKE. He's too specific. He personally isn't a bad person. He's alright. But AVOID THIS SPECIFIC ENGLISH CLASS. MORE WORK THAN IT SHOULD BE IF YOU ARENT AN ENGLISH MAJOR!!

He is the hardest instructor I have had while at UCR. I would not recommend him to anyone who is taking an english class. He grades according to his own standard and if you do not write the way he likes, your grade will suffer. I received an A+ in English 1A and I barely passed with a C- in his English 1B course. He is HORRIBLE.
If you want to be stress out of every single detail, then take this class.  He is hard, unfair and unjust on his grading.

Prof. Jones can come off as one of those English-obsessed professors who's uptight but honestly, he's not that bad. His quizzes are tough, you really do need to read and LEARN from the St. Martin's Guide in order to pass them. He's a tough grader on hw but as for essays, he's fair. For an english class, work + study  you'll pass.

Worst English teacher ever! Do not take him. He will grade exceptionally hard even if you go to office hours. It takes 2 hours to get into his office, and when you do, you have to leave within 10 minutes. DO NOT TAKE HIM!

He's a tough grader but his directions are clear and he is willing to help if you ask for it. He doesn't take roll every class but he takes names down on days with activities so skip at your own risk.

Unclear. Unfair. That describes it in a nutshell. Believe what you read here he is a terrible professor and has expectations set way too high.  Incredibly unfair and awkward to deal with. GET OUT WHILE YOU CAN

Taking Eng50 in Esco. Class is hard if you do not keep up with the work. He is a stict grader but his down to earth personality makes the class enjoyable. I would NOT recommend his class to anyone that is not prepared to do the work. I plan on taking Eng100 w/ him because he is awesome, funny, energetic & enjoyable. By far my favorite teacher.

Whatever you do, STAY AWAY. He will make your life a living hell. I didn't know how stressful English could be until I took this course. He's wants everything perfect, and any little mistake will cost your grade. If you want to be an English major, I highly recommend his class. Your GPA isn't worth the risk to take his class.

He is very helpful and is willing to go out of his way to make sure your essay is really good. Yes, he is very specific and it stressed me out sometimes, but at the end of the day, it was extremely helpful. He is a very tough grader, but he will do his best to help you along the way. GO TO OFFICE HOURS! IT HELPS A LOT!

I normally love English but I hated this class. It felt like high school. When grading essays he cared more about nitty gritty technical details than actual content and writing style, which really annoyed me. He's just a stickler. If you enjoy freedom in your writing, don't take him.
great professor, learned alot! try him out BW3 people cuz he does pass people!

Very tough grader. First paper i spent hours on, didn't even it grade says i can revise for a maximum C grade. that takes place of my only revision for the course. He expects you to be a master in the English language. He is very difficult to please grammatically etc. Each paper has a minimum number of pre-reqs and will not grade the paper ifnotmet

he contradicts himself and honestly i never hard more trouble in an eng class. all i did was revise and i lived in office hours but all i got was a c+ only because someone else graded my final.hes a good teacher and all and you learn how to write very well in his class but he grades EXTREMELY hard.

Very happy teacher, shows lots of excitement but almost impossible to please! Got the highest grade in the class and just passed with a C+. Revise, revise, Revise and you still wont receive a satisfactory grade. Do not take.

English 1c was suppose to be a fun english class but this teacher made it extremely hard. He lets you re-write papers to try to get a better grade but he grades really hard the first time around. I got an A+ on my final papers and did all the re-writes and he still didn't pass me even though i was only 1 point away. ALOT of reading and analyzing
WORST ENGLISH 4 TEACHER EVER!!!!! very tedious and gives useless work that hurts ones grades, difficult grader.

TOUGH GRADER AND CLASS! However, if you work hard..you will be rewarded. Never read so much in my life. The directions to the prompt were PAINFULLY thorough. If you do your part..you'll be fine. GO TO OFFICE HOURS..VERY HELPFUL!

In the beginning of the class, course work may seem manageable but after the 2nd week, essays start to pile after one another. The quizzes are the easiest thing in the class if one follows the suggested readings. But for the essays one must have prior skills before taking the class. My papers were coming back with me with Big fat Fs....something i
Work for your grade--if you work for a B and show her you want that, you'll get it. If you want an A, and PROVE it, you'll get it. An A is VERY possible. Great Prof.

Mr. Jones is the best! I took 1A and 1B with him, and I wanted to take 1C with him but couldn't because of time conflicts with other classes. As long as you show genuine interest in improving your writing, and you attend a few office hours to talk to Mr. Jones, there is no reason as to why you should get lower than a A-. 85% is an A in his class.

Great teacher! Yeah, he is hard at the grading, but as long as you show you are interested in getting a good grade, he will help you achieve that. Go to office hours, that is where you will receive the most help. I love how he has every assignment explained in hangouts.

The Best English Teacher in the World!!! So good I took her twice. Go to office hours and she will help you a lot.  To do well on the quizzes you must read. Pay attention during class, sometimes she will drop hints for quizzes. Also, she can be a hard a grader on the essays, however, if you do well on them then you will get an A.- SHOW EFFORT!!
Mr. Jones is a wonderful teacher, you can tell that he enjoys teaching English. Go to class and make sure to do all the papers and you will find yourself in a very good position.
Mr. Jones is a great teacher. He explains the material well. He lays out every day in a schedule. If you go to class, and go to office hours, you will definitely get higher than a B.

Very good teacher. Very specific  everything laid out in schedule. If you go to office hours for your essay he gives good feedback and if you follow his comments you'll get a very good grade in essays.  If you do well in quizzes and in class essay you can skip the final altogether.  It's worth it to put in the effort to skip the final.

There was maybe 8 books we needed to read passages from. I didn't do the readings and relied on knowledge from lecture. Professor King also posts video lectures on the canvas which are useful. He tracks attendance through Pol lEverywhere. The essays are graded by your TA, I had Jeffrey Achierno, and he was lowkey wicked with grading :/
NICEST guy ever he honestly just wants you to complete the work and understands this material is not easy to learn!! He is always willing to help you.
Super straightforward grading criteria, pretty easy class to pass overall. Really chill dude.

Wow, i was in for a ride. I took this class because I thought it was "Greek and Latin World History" not WORD History. 

professor is super nice but man is this class hard. You have to download an app thats an easy grade, but the test are super painful. 

Still cant believe I got an A.
Overall, he's super nice professor and he's caring and understanding of his students. In lectures if someone does not understand something, he will explain

The most accommodating professor ever. Cut me some slack on many instances. If averages are low for the 
 (2) exams, he takes a few questions off to adjust. It is mostly just memorizing latin and greek terms along with 2 essays and also some history. One of the most fun courses I have every taken!

Professor King is one of the nicest professors at UCR. The class was all about memorization of greek and latin elements. The homework is light and only cares if you complete it. Two papers which are very easy and interesting when doing it. Discussion is mandatory.

I can't recommend Prof. King enough; he can be blunt, but he is a very thorough, caring, and entertaining guy with a dry sense of humor. Really, CLA040 is probably one of my favorite classes at UCR. The work barely feels like work - it's all stories, and that makes it fun. Homework is kept to a flexible minimum, and there are 2 easy essays.
I took him for CLA 040. Very easy and entertaining class. The quizzes are easy if you pay attention to the lecture. The essays are easy as well. Pretty easy A imo.

Are you kidding me? 3 years at UCR I have never had a good professor who's caring about their students so much as Professor King. He is an amazing Professor, he's very caring and understanding. His lectures aren't heavy, homework is easy. Do Cerego, it will help you with your quizzes. Exams aren't that difficult, just read the slides
Nice guy who wants his students to pass. Just do the Cerego flashcards and refer to the resources he provides for you.

Took him for greek in the fall and classics in the winter. Never been more engaged during lectures! He makes relatively boring topics seem super interesting. There was a lot of memorization (more in greek than in classics) but Cerego really really made it easy to practice and get terms down. I hope I get to take profesor King in the future!

Best professor I've ever had! He uses the textbook for a few things but I stopped reading during the first week and was fine. Lots of mini quizzes to do before or after the lectures but they're pretty easy and the midterm/final follow the same format at them. A lot of memorization too but overall not a stressful course to take

The class was not too bad, but it was a LOT of work. There were flashcards on Cerego to do + all of the small quizzes to be done before and after lectures. It wasn't a difficult class but I did more for this class than most others. As long as you're on top of the flashcards, though, you'll be okay. Probably won't even have to go to class.

He's very animated + pretty much gives you the answers you need in lecture/homework -- I stopped reading the books early on and got an A. You have to watch a few videos of extra lecture every week and take quizzes on them, but its open-note + you can retake. Lectures drag on a bit but he has good humor. He was an easier grader than my TA for essays
Hands down best professor I've had as of now, would've gotten an A but I slacked a little bit. A bit of reading but very interesting material!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Took him for CLA040 during the Fall and he was absolutely amazing and understanding so I took his CLA020 course in the Spring. In each class we had 2 papers to write, as well as mini quizzes. The midterms and finals were easy because its the exact same questions that were on the mini quizzes. Hes super passionate about what he teaches. Love him!

He was awesome. Had him in person. The readings are easy and complementary to the lectures. The work is easy to understand as long as you do it. He made the class interesting for me. Cerego does not let you binge study. Start the assignments right when they open. Overall, 10/10 would recommend. Not a stressful class at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class was SO easy and the professor is so nice. The class might seem daunting because of the work but it's easy. You had quizzes every week to help you learn the topics covered in class, he posts slides, discussion is mandatory, and there are only two essays, 2 quizzes, a midterm, and a final. The only thing is you have to pay $10 for Cerego.

Class itself is pretty chill, mainly just memorization/study day of test. Flash card app (Cerego) & 2 papers but short & simple. Honestly dont NEED to attend all lectures but you get extra credit (poll-everywhere participation app) & theyre helpful if you just go & listen. Hes really easy-going. Good breadth course choice fs !

Amazing professor. You will enjoy the class if you are interested in the subject and devote a good amount of time for studying. He was very passionate and loves what he teaches. He uses pollev and it counts for credit so make sure you attend lectures to get points. 2 papers, midterm, final, quizzes throughout the week and weekly hw.

I really enjoyed taking this class. Lectures were divided into smaller sections with quizzes at the end and he gives a guide for notes. He also provides study guides for the midterm and final. There are 2 papers but grades depend on TA.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Class was very easy. Consisted of lecture twice a week & homework due midnight of lecture day. Class is mostly just watching short videos of him lecturing & homework quizzes that are easy. We also had to do Cerego flashcard. assignments. One midterm @ one final that are very similar to hw quizzes. Very understanding prof, would take again 100%

Lots of reading so go slowly or you'll miss the key points but he discusses about them in lecture. Does pre-recorded lectures on the side for you to refer back to. Weekly quizzes were easy as long as you watched the pre-recorded videos. 2 papers, 1 midterm, 1 final. Grades fairly. Does breakout rooms which I think are unnecessary as no one talks.

Fall 2020. A lot of short quizzes based on the lectures so take notes. There are 2 essays based on myth subjects talked about in the readings and lectures. Start thinking about topics once you hear the prompt early on. I personally love Greek mythology so the long readings were interesting to me. The Final had a lot of SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The most well-organized class I had. Prof. King posted the lectures weekly and a google doc telling you when, and what to study for. Everything is available and ready well in advance, and gives you space to organize. However, be prepared to read and take a lot of quizzes. Though easy, it requires you to put some serious time in!

This guy is a great professor! You can tell he teaches for the right reasons, and he's super knowledgeable about the subject. Classical studies has nothing to do with my major but this class was still enjoyable and tests followed lectures strictly and clearly!! would recommend!

This class wasn't as easy as I thought it would be. To be fair I didn't do the readings. The exams were mostly free response and asked questions that were very specific to the readings. Going to lecture helps a lot.

I think Ben King's rating is way to high on this. His lectures are very boring and the class is not as easy as you'd think. Do all the homework and you'll be fine on that aspect. If you're not into mythology you're not gonna like the class. You have to buy tophat which sucks and there is a paper that you have to write which also sucks

Professor King is very kind and caring.. He warns the class that you have to constantly study all the terms from the textbook because theyre tons to learn. He mostly cares about improvement throughout the quarter. Quizzes and participation are on Tophat. Just make sure to study the terms and the class will be easy

Professor King is, by far, one of the nicest and most engaging professors I've had so far. His lectures are really interesting and he makes sure to provide you with the proper information for the midterm and final. Attendance is important because he does TopHat questions in class. Make sure to read and go to office hours for help! He's the best!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor King is amazing! Very passionate about greek myth. Readings are a must and lectures help you get a better understandings of the readings if you had a hard time with them! Two test; 1 midterm and 1 Final not cumulative and one individual presentation in your discussion. Overall easy if you do the work
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Tests are tough--Would take again

reviews.comment: Dr. King is awesome. His lectures are super helpful and great. Readings are crucial, but attending lectures can make up for them. 2 tests, 1 midterm and 1 final, each worth 25% of the grade. Also a small report. Lectures teach you about the myth and how to interpret it. This last part comes in handy on the exams. Hes really passionate and witty!

i loved professor king! pros: super detailed, fun if you're interested in greek myth cons: skipping a lecture means you have to get notes from someone else. his outlines/powerpoints online aren't detailed enough to form your own. also, be prepared to read. although he discusses the work in class, reading helps to solidify your understanding!

reviews.comment: His passion for the subject is clear and he is understandable. By far the BEST Professor I've had!! 3 homework assignments a week, lots of studying but totally great!

reviews.comment: do not take as a ge class. this man thrives on being right and doesn't like to be told otherwise. loved my TA though, they carried the class honestly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I am a student that LITERALLY came from the bottom, failing the 1st 3 quizzes, to the top( getting an A.) It is not impossible. BUT you cannot be a lazy student and therefore I dont recommend taking this for a GEN ED rec. go to his office hours because at the end of the day he has an ego complex (like most professors) show you to care (maybe ;0)

This "professor" does little more than complain for a third of his lectures and gives little to no explanation as to how to write the essay that is worth 40% of your class grade. I used the TA's notes on his class for one of them and was given the feedback that the "information was wrong". He also has his own definition for basic ideas so good luck
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Never take his class agian, ahhhhhhh.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Quizzes are difficult because he wants HIS answer. You should definitely go to class because you'll need the notes (copy down his exact words). Towards the end he started doing attendance EC because class was empty. Papers are graded tough, but if you have a good TA they'll help a lot. That being said, I loved discussion because I liked my TA.

He's the worst professor at UCR. I'm sry if you have to take this professor as breadth. He's a tough grader on papers, a D average for students, difficult quizzes, and made a lot of non-political science major students fail this course. He doesn't care about what major you are, he expected you perform like a political professional.

It's unbelievable how hard he and his TAs grade. On our term paper, nearly every student in his class received a C or below on the term paper. The TA, Paul Teten, gave us feedback documents, but there was no real feedback or explanation for how low the grades were. I am a good writer, but it is nearly impossible to score well on his papers.

Class is basically based off quizzes and 2 papers. Quizzes were mediocre and the rubric for our papers were straight forward. Encourages students to participate during lectures by forcing students to ask questions before continuing on with lecture. He doesn't post notes so I would highly recommend going to lectures..
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do not take any class with Bishin especially if it's just for a breadth course. The workload seems easy but he makes getting a good grade impossible. He thinks the TAs grade too easily, and he failed half the class's papers. There's 8 weekly quizzes based on readings (which the class average is a 60-70%) and 2 papers (class average was in the 60s).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Horrible. He is not accommodating at all and although he seems very passionate about political science he shows little passion in actually teaching. One t.a. grades one of your two papers very lightly while the other t.a. grades ridiculously. Bishin had to grade all papers and he is to harsh. I most definitely would not take this class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Overall a decent class. Do well on the first paper and you don't have to do the second unless you want the chance to get a higher grade. Clear grading criteria and not difficult. The quizzes were weekly, were online, and were about the assigned readings. He drops a couple of your lowest ones (if I remember correctly). I would take him again.

Professor Bishin is pretty chill overall with one synchronous lecture on zoom per week and the rest are lecture videos. 1 open-book quiz per week, 2 papers, no finals/midterms. Just pay close attentions to his readings, lectures, and the questions from the prompt and the quizzes to do well throughout the course as he may include trick questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Average of 1 hour and 30 minutes of recorded lectures posted weekly, instead of two days of lectures only one day worth of watching videos. Readings are not mandatory. Two papers were assigned in the entire course. Overall, easy A, nothing out of the ordinary. Ben is also a cool teacher to listen to and not at all boring. Def recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I am a disabled student. He refuses to record lectures or post slides which makes it extremely difficult for me as a student. If you are working with a disability DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS. He is very inaccessible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Bishin adapted to online teaching very well. The class had prerecorded weekly lectures and supplemental office hours every week. He genuinely cares for his students and provides a lot of flexibility in the class' programming. Weekly quizzes and a term paper compose most of the grade. He's always willing to hear you out and help. Highly recommended

One of the best professor. II taken his summer course and If you take political science you have 1 midterm, 1 final, and 1 essay. He offers extra credit on the readings so its optional if you want to get the extra points. His lectures are very straightforward and very clear. He's very passionate about teaching so students tend to pay attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: awesome professor. He is very enthusiastic about the material, which makes you want to learn it too. He gives "pop quizzes" often, but they're purely for extra credit so they'll only help you. Reading is required to pass, and he doesn't post slides online, so go to class. Honestly not a hard class, just pay attention and do your part.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Not an easy-A writing course. The material is boring, and he uses the class to promote his own book & political theory. In a sense it feels like he teaches this course so he can make book sales. Also is standoffish sometimes and one encounter with him made me never want to talk to him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Great teacher in my opinion. The class is very much oriented towards writing since its a W course. All the papers were 7-8 page minimum. Prof. is very helpful, lectures are very informative as well. If you aren't a political science major the class might be more difficult.

I took his class in Spring 2018 and at first it was interesting. I had B averages on my essays and I didn't go to class, AT ALL. Midterm was difficult, and NOT open notes or books. However, he gives a lot of extra credit opportunities. He rambles on about the same material which isn't even on the midterm. There are 3 very dense books.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors. These negative reviews aren't accurate. Bishin lectures in a way that so easy to understand. He has three papers, but as long as you read, you're good. He's super passionate about what he teaches, and his exams are open note. He assigns extra credit so often, and he has pop quizzes WHICH ARE ALSO EXTRA CREDIT. 10/10
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Assigns three VERY difficult books that are graduate level. Be prepared to write 3 eight page papers that are very dry and boring to write. The books you have to write them on are extremely hard to understand even if you are a polysci major. I would not recommend to anyone who is trying to get easy credit for English 1C.

This was the first time Bishin taught this class as a 1C class. There were 3 papers. Don't buy the text, just buy the reading books. Come to class because he gives extra credit, which could bump your grade to the next grade (HE TENDS TO GIVE OUT EC WHEN THERE AREN'T A LOT OF PEOPLE). Readings are boring

Lectures are totally different from readings. So go to lecture, he doesn't post slides. Readings are kind of dry, but if you have a good TA they should explain it to you. Exams are all multiple choice. Gives a lot of EC just for going to class! So go!

Great professor. Assigns a bit of reading but you can skim through the books to get the concepts to do fine on the tests. Tests are open book, open note and NOT CUMULATIVE. He doesn't go over readings in lecture but lecture is very informative and entertaining and important because 50% of the tests focus on what he goes over in lecture.

Honestly this class was truly an easy A!! His powerpoints and lectures are actually interesting if you attend and pay attention! Make sure you do the readings and BUY THE STUDY GUIDES! They truly help for the midterm and final! Overall good class
He is kind of boring and his lectures most of the time are off topic. So you leave not knowing anything about the material.

Professor is fun, clear, and very smart. Gives extra credit for attending lecture. *BUT* he can be arrogant at times and belittle you. i went to office hours and he laughed at my questions and humiliated me. Then he told me to go talk to the TA. Dont go to office hours and you'll be fine :)

Wow, first off, i don't think he's such a bad professor (reading these other comments) i highly advise to not get discouraged. he's not a fun professor, but he's definitely not hard to understand, he's pretty clear at explaining things. his exams are super easy(mostly definition questions) and open note??! come on!! its an easy A class.
Very easy class. Got an A+. Do all the readings and the tests are open book and open notes. His lectures can get boring though.

This professor talks TOO MUCH. he talks so much that i always end up zoning out. i don?t know how other people pay attention... i always feel like i?m going to fall asleep when i?m in class. He makes you read sooo damn much and you HAVE to read in order to past his tests. Don?t take him if you don?t have to...

so teachers are supposed to teach you about the subject matter...but i cant say that i learned anything about political science. i cant really say that i know what it is after having taken this class. lectures go no where because he talks in circles. but his tests are open book and note but its still hard to get an a

attend lectures, pay attention and write good notes because his midterms/finals were open book open notes. his readings were a pain to do. i hardly read and ended up with a B by just attending and paying attention in lecture
Prof. is boring. Makes you read his own textbook. I learned way more from my TA & TA was more helful. 3 books to read for the quarter and the lectures don't relate to them at all.
Boring and rude

Bishin's lectures don't aren't meant to supplement the reading. You have to read for this class and attend lectures if you want a good grade. His tests are half from lectures and half from the reading. He even gives you a study guide for the lecture part of this test. He is a good teacher, you just have to be willing to put the work in.

This Professor is a decent teacher if you can sort through all the politically skewed bs.  The main problem is that you have to do all the reading and his study guides are utterly useless.  He tries to trick you rather than test you.

This class was extremely difficult! Though I rarely referred to the textbook, I went to nearly all of his lectures..and they would BARELY correspond to the reading materials. His exams sometimes have trick questions and very ambiguous. The final was completely out of nowhere. Overall, if it wasn't for my AWESOME t/a (tony) I would of HATED this cla

Bishin is not a good choice, super liberal, biased in many ways,and thinks he knows everything.A lot of his so called data is biased and his test are bogus and are what he feels like throwing together last minute, he gives you lots of readings which make up maybe two questions on midterms. He likes to talk, a lot about well a whole lot of nothing.

This guys uses this class to preach liberal politics and ignore the rest of the material. Many of his statements about government are shockingly wrong. Considering about 30 out of 350 students show up to his (not early morning) class on non test days should account for is lack of teaching ability. He is the reason I changed my major from poli sci.
He is a good teacher but you need to read for his tests.
he is really hard to understand, but is willing to help and he his class is useful if you are interested. Definitly go to class and pay attention

Bishin is a cool professor. He's not as hard as people say he is. If you go to class you'll get an A. He gives extra credit and discussion is helpful. he also gives you a study guide before all the tests. go to class, do the reading, study ahead of time and you'll easily get an A, like me!

Avoid this guy- there are other professor in political science dept who are lot better than him (Johnson, Bowler, Ramakrishnan, etc). He talks about his students behind their back. (I overheard him talking to another professor about how students at his previous institutions are better that studetns here at UCR. not very clear in his lectures. Waste

Prof. Bishin is a very articulate and knowledgeable guy, he loves talking about current events and its fun to be in his class. He also likes to put things in context by showing videos (he showed us an episode of the Sopranos to illustrate voter identities). His tests are difficult though, and you need to read the book to do well on them.

A good guy. His lectures are interesting. He spends a lot of time in the beginning talking about current issues/events. Lectures and readings don't match up and he goes back and forth on lectures all the time so I recommend typing out your notes so that you can add/amend them later. One of the better poli sci classes.

Professor Bishin uses powerpoints during lecture, but they are just outlines of what he's talking about. Some things he says in class will be tested. Make sure to read, it is crucial for getting a good grade in class. There is also a 5-7 page term paper.

He's a nice guy, tries to crack some corny jokes but he's interesting. He's got some really cool things to teach. Give him your time of day. You won't regret it. Kind of arrogant in the beginning, but he's only trying to show you that he won't let you step all over him..which isn't wrong. Great political standing though! Rock on Dr. Bishin, rock on

Bishin is a nice guy really enthusiastic about the course Its hard because on the midterm he wants the identifications to be verbatim He also assigns a group research paper, which is like 35% of your grade Dont procrastinate on writing the paperLots of statistical stuff Goes too fast on the slides, doesnt post them on ilearn, but nice guy class

Prof. Biggs was genuinely one of the best professors I've ever had. So genuine and passionate about the subject he teaches, he manages to be very funny and entertaining without sacrificing any seriousness in his lectures. Class is reading and writing heavy but shouldn't be a problem if you keep up with the material and attend lecture :)

Took it over Summer and had a great time! Only the discussions led by the TAs were mandatory.  Lectures were recorded and readings posted to watch at your own pace. Gives great advice on how to approach papers and straightforward rubrics. He loves exchanging stories with us. Would definitely recommend his class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Biggs requires so much reading and writing. If you enjoy dense work by all means go ahead. He also does not respond to emails. You will also be forced to interact with other students for pointless projects.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Biggs' expertise is Vietnam history and I did an independent study with him on Vietnamese boat people. He was awesome and encouraging with good insights. He knows his stuff.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: If you don't enjoy reading, writing, and heavy research then don't take this course. The professor is nice and can be easy to work with. But is a tough grader with essays/ research papers. Otherwise the course was semi-interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: insane workload + weird prompts with unhelpful readings make it a very difficult class

Do NOT take this professor!  Not only will you not learn anything about Southeast Asian history in favor of in depth dives on plants, but the class has an immense and unnecessary workload that involves essays every week for discussion post credit.  He grades tough and has unrealistic expectations for your writing.  Avoid at all costs.

Dude is obsessed in plants and its unthinkably annoying.  He's so friendly and yet so incompetent at his job.  He assigns massive workloads for six point discussion posts.  Get ready to write an essay each week with ridiculous prompts involving his obsession with plants, and digging through readings that have nothing to do with the assigned prompt.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: One of the Greatest History 197 courses I took this summer. If I do not pass my next HIST 197 course this coming academic year I will take him again. This class is a capstone class and attendance is mandatory.

Class was overall very easy. 2 papers,1 about historical photos and the other about family history which is basically an easy A. One midterm and final online. Lectures are optional but are very interesting. Discussions are mandatory in which you are graded for attendance. There are many readings but I personally read them only during midterm/final
Unnecessary amount of work especially for a General Ed class.

In-person lectures but past recordings available. Interesting lectures and PollEV extra credit so would recommend attending. Weekly extra credit chapter quizzes until midterm and some easy extra credit assignments until final. LOTS of readings but easy class overall
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Don't take his class, there are tons of readings every week. Curriculum is unreasonable.

This class is 100% essay based. You're literally just going to write essays & read the random pdfs of books he posts, even in discussion. There's over 60+ texts of various lengths. Yes, you have to read most of it since you'll be using them to answer the prompt. Citing multiple sources is required, and he only wants you to use the pdfs or lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I enjoyed his lectures (perhaps because I was interested in the topics) and you can tell he's genuinely passionate. The essays were pretty easy to ace if you followed the rubrics closely. He gives a few opportunities for extra credit but overall the essays were very important.

Professor Biggs was an amazing professor. Class was not mandatory but it still was a super easy class to take. I would recommend taking this class. Reading is heavy but don’t have to actually read. He’s pretty clear in lecture. Passed with a C despite scoring low on midterm and final.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Excessive amounts of reading; my conservative estimate is around 700-800 pages of assorted history content alongside 4 films and an additional textbook. Teacher seemed to understand some problems students would have but was stubborn about readings and lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: the amount of reading in this ge class makes my major classes look like a joke.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: The amount of reading required for a breadth course is ridiculous. The readings are difficult to comprehend yet the professor expects 40-100 pages of reading per lecture. The professor himself is decent in his lectures however the amount of busy work is too much especially for a breadth course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Biggs was one of the most understanding professors I have ever taken. Knowing that we are in a pandemic, he gave us plenty of time to turn in essays/projects and wasn't too strict on the due date and time of the essays. If you're willing to come to class and put in the work, it's an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Biggs was super nice and made the class as easy to pass as possible. There are 2 papers, a midterm, and a final. He basically gave everyone 100% on Paper 2 because he understood that everyone was stressed. The midterm and final are a little hard but if you don't wait until the last second it will be okay.

Prof Biggs is a great lecturer and very passionate about what he teaches; however, I wish he'd cut us some slack bc this is a breadth course. He assigns about 3 readings per lecture, but some were like 30 pages long! The readings aren't always easy to read either and the mass amount of them often lead students (like myself) to put them off.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Biggs does assign a lot of reading, but the material is pertinent and he's passionate and will talk your ear off about Vietnam, his forte. His tests are blue book essay and short ID, so practice clear and to-the-point answers regarding things like environmentalism and human rights and how it relates to history. Always available to help, too.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Biggs was one of my favorite Professors on campus so far.I did not do all the readings but I had to do most of them because of our discussion sections. Overall the class was interesting and I loved how our exams were written, gave us a better chance to pass the exams. As long as you study the key terms and their significance you will pass

He's obviously very passionate, and his lectures are interesting. If only I had enough of an attention span to pay attention. His class is pretty difficult, but seriously pay attention in class, saves you lots of time in the long run. His tests are short ID's (which he'll have listed) and a paper, but they're pretty open ended.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Get ready to read a lot (I didn't read any of the readings). The way he formats his lectures is unorthodox or different; a lot of things are verbatim, instead of being more term-heavy. Overall, he's a good teacher. Just make sure to keep up with the terms. People who rated badly either don't study at all, or thought this would be an easy A. Oof

On a personal level, David Biggs is inspiring and genuine. He has a lot of love for history and he cares about his students a lot. You can tell how much work he puts into his lectures. He tells the class more as a story so those labels and definitions can get a bit disorganized and sometimes hard to articulate but other than that the class is great

Avoid at all cost. His lectures are literally useless. There are no slides for reference, literally makes you type an entire doc of what he is saying. Lectures are unorganized af. Can talk about Great Britain for one minute and all of a sudden talks about Japan. Always says he is making an argument, but never once have I heard one. Tests are dumb
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: His lectures are great. There is so many readings. It's almost impossible to retain all the material because of how much he assigns unless you're only taking this one class. He loves history and loves to get to know his students. His class is enjoyable and entertaining but catching up with the readings is really hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Assigns way too many readings. Paper had to be written only using the assigned readings (RIDICULOUS). Lectures are unorganized. DO NOT RECOMMEND TAKING HIST20 W HIM.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: His lectures are all over the place. Switches up from China to Germany then to Russia all in the same lecture. Hes very enthusiastic about history which makes it a bit better. Its an Intro class but he treats it as a W course. Take the class if you love reading about history, if not, I would not reccomend for someone not interested in history
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I basically stopped reading after the midterm bc he assigns way too much. There was also too much writing in my opinion considering it's not a W course. I got an A- though cause I did great on the final. Oh and the lectures are reaaaaaally good. I did learn a lot so that's good.

The lectures are amazing.  He outlines his lectures in the syllabus so that's helpful.  The books are awful.  You will read for hours to get a small portion of what you need to know for the papers and the tests.  He expects you to draw comparisons and make arguments, no problem... but you have to search! for the information.  It is a lot of work!

He is an amazing professor. But for an Hist 20, not 20W class... I have never written more papers in my life. The TAs had to argue with him to cut back on essays.  We still had to write so many papers. This is a BASIC history class.  I wrote more papers in this lower division class than I have in my upper divisions. Awesome teacher, too many papers

A Buddhist once said, "Wisdom begins with simplicity". I can attest to that after taking HIST 20 with Prof. Biggs TWICE (once in summer '15 and again by sitting in winter '15).  Yes, he's that great. His content stretches over a variety of perspectives, so you get a fair dosage of philosophy, environmentalism, sociology, etc... Would sit in AGAIN!

Some lectures were boring, but some were very inspiring. He sometimes showed powerful videos in class. The main book was well-written and it follows his syllabus. Other books aren't as necessary. Don't procrastinate on the essays. Midterm was difficult for the unprepared. Overall, class was a great learning experience.

Really good prof! Makes history interesting. There's 4 essays, a midterm, and a final. But he curves all the exams and the first essay. His lectures are confusing cuz he doesn't present history in chronological order, so go to office hours and hope you have a good TA. I Never read, got As on everything.
Very nice teacher. He assigned a lot of reading but I never read anything and still did well. His lectures were hard to follow and all over the place.

He is simply a great professor. He makes Vietnam and it's wars INTERESTING. If you don't want to fall asleep durring a class, pick this one. He's very helpful and grades fairly. Show up, Pay attention, take good notes and you'll surely pass. p.s. don't make any jokes about his books title because it's called "Quagmire", he doesn't watch family guy.

Good teacher.  Lots of reading, lots and lots of reading.  The readings are key to the midterm and final.  multiple choice and essay for both.  A group project was required.  Overall the class was a really good class, I learned a lot.  If you don't mind reading take this class if Vietnam history interests you.

Lectures weren't always organized and clear, but did offer great side stories to the overall picture you gain from the readings. Attendance isn't a big deal and his group work was unorganized, but he was nice and helpful (more so during office hours than email). Pretty easy and still interesting.

Nice guy, but highly disorganized and lectures have no structure whatsoever.  Emailed him several times and never gotten a thorough response either. Class was easy, but I felt like I learned nothing, and basically zoned out after the 5th week.

He is such a great teacher. Awesome awesome awesome. He understands its an intro class and he makes it fun for you to learn. Do the readings and take notes and u will be fine. Midterm and final about 30 mc and 1 essay (open note)

Honestly I studied the day before each exam and ended up with a B. Didn't come to lecture several times. Honestly not that bad of a class :). Not much of a fan of group work though. Group work was 50% of the overall grade. The focus was developing a wiki.

He's been the best teacher I've had at UCR, really into new media (I hear he may even replace the txtbook with wiki articles next time...which is awesome!). He's really into history and very laid back (he knew it was just an intro class). Very helpful if you go to him, and just a nice guy overall. I would take it again and recommend it to anyone.

I love professor Biggs! He modivated me to do so much more stuff than just sit in class, and he really likes to get to know you on a personal level. I did a study abroad with him to Vietnam, it was one of the best experiences, if you get a chance do it! Its completely worth it...

Biggs is an ok teacher. Take his class if you have interest, but his lectures are far from engaging. He knows his stuff, but he just doesn't seem to know when he is droning on and on. Makes you waste money on clickers too.
Class is not very organized but the teacher is a lot of fun to listen to. His teaching structure has changed but ultimately, his only fault reflects his poor organization methods.
there's A LOT of reading for this class and a big research paper. other than that, there's no midterm and his daily quizzes are kinda easy. fun class, cool guy, cares about his students.
wonderful professor. he has to be the most lenient and easiest professor ever.

He took a new approach for this class (so he says). There was no midterm, no final. Instead, we had daily quizzes that made you read the books. I liked this method a lot and wish other professors would follow his method. There was also one final research paper, but that wasn't too tough either. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED PROFESSOR!

ok. so all the stuff about the midterm and final exam are true. all u need to do is memorize everything on the review sheet. he assigns a lot of reading so the quizzes are sometimes hard. but his curve helps a lot.

Biggs is a cool teacher. i love his class n everything about it. he makes it not boring. n his notes are helpful for midterm n finals. the midterm and final r easy if u jus study whatever he gives n tell. i ENJOYED the class very much..highly recommended!!!

awesome teacher! he makes history class fun and enjoyable, his midterm is fairly easy, and he does curves! Final is extremely easy, multiple choice..the stuff on the final are on the study guide he gives out...if you study you'll do fine...and his curves are great! Overall, i recommend him. =)
Probably one of the worst profs I've ever had in my university life. You'd be lucky if you pass at least one quiz, and his givens are extremely unclear. Do not recommend

Big Bippin Desai is the physics department bomb-diggity. Heckin' sweet lectures about imaginary numbers. Shout out to Pierre and Jonah. One love, google 9/11 chemtrails, the government puts flouride in our water so we won't learn complex analysis properly.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: I waisted 3/4 of a year of my life in his class.  Since I need to know QM, I now have to teach myself (but at least I don't have to learn from the book he wrote).  I didn't come to grad school to joke around and waist my time - I came here to learn and to do research, so I don't appreciate being required to sit through his nonsense.

Considering that I took the AP Physics exam and scored 5's, I found his class to be extremely easy. Too bad credit for the AP exam was only awarded for the Physics 2 series. Although he is not crystal clear in his lectures, his examinations are straightforward and do not go beyond what he does in class.
His lectures are very boring. His tests and quizzes are hard. You can't see what he writes on the board.

Beware! Difficult to understand. Wrote really small on the board, even after students asked him to write larger. Even with binoculars it was futile. Homework is really difficult, and pop quizzes and tests are based on complete understanding of the material (as in, you've gotta know how to be creative and apply knowledge in ways you've never seen).

Don't take him. His lectures were utterly useless and so are his office hours. The only good thing is that the tests are exactly what he does in the class. His lecture is mandatory since he gives pop quizzes. If you want to memorize useless info, take him. If you want to truly learn physics, wait until another professor teaches.

He really sucks at teaching. You're better off studying by yourself. He speaks too quietly and speaks in the same god damn monotone for everything. Even if you managed to understand the first half of lecture, you'll be asleep by the second half. Just horrible, especially if you're new to Physics. Oh and his writing is near illegible sometimes.

And i thought high school teachers were bad, until i met this guy.  His tests/midterms are relatively easy - most are just like the homework, but he cant teach at all.  Speaks english, but likes to babble about and can be hard to understand.  He teaches right out of the text book; but the book does a better job than him.
he reads off the slides and does examples in between. his midterms are just like the homework. some clicker questions.

I say that he's "clear" because he spent 6 weeks on particle in a box, and really a dog can get that problem before that long. Other than that, he only knows Green's functions. He either knows almost nothing about Quantum or he doesn't bother to make a  lesson plan with reasonable breadth. Rude and favoritist, extremely arbitrary in grading.

Amazing professor who cares about her students and is able to connect with us as well. She does give a lot of homework, but the midterms come straight from homework. You won't regret having her as a professor!

Was a good professor for BIEN 125 and 101, but for 115 this professor has been the opposite. Repeatedly saying umm while she lectures as she didn't know the material comfortably. Quizzes every lecture, and only drops one for the entire quarter. Probably due to low attendance from previous quarters as you can just self-study slides and get above avg
She's definitely a fun professor and I really enjoyed her class for the last two quarters. Definitely would take her class again.
She's chill for a new professor. Really smart and informative

I like Dr. Helms I just hate basketball games and if you are in the "concert band" plan on becoming a pep band member for the UCRiverside Basketball team.  Plan to give up many nights and weekends that you should be studying but you can't because you are in noisy bleachers. I would enjoy a true concert band academics > than mindless sports games.
No Comments
This band has mostly non-students.  If you are a girl, you get attention.  A bit full of himself.
He caters to certain people in the class

Bill Helms is a great Prof. I really enjoyed playing in the jazz band and the music was cool. Bill really knows what he is doing has a gerat understanding of music and thoery. He even got me a scholarship I didn't ask for. Great guy and helpful teacher. Take his classes.
Bill Helms is freakin tight.
he's sooo nice.  very patient man.  loves music in all aspects.  great listener.  VERY PATIENT.  cool guy.  don't miss class, grade is baded on attendance mostly.  easy conductor to follow.
This class is a blast!  Bill makes class fun.

Bill is a great conductor.  He tells jokes during rehearsal and is very willing to help when people have trouble playing something.  I really enjoy the music we play.  It's not too hard and not too easy.  Join the concert band!  It's fun.
Mr. Helms is AWESOME!  He is so funny.  The music is fun to play.
Great class!  Inspiring.  Expects a lot but helps students out.  The BEST class!
Terrible.  Didn't teach anything.  Favored the old people in the band and not the students.  Almost kicked me out of class because I had strep throat.
best music teacher here.  Take his classes!

I literally made an account because I hated this class so much. AHS Majors: AVOID. AVOID. AVOID. She is not like any ahs professor and not in a good way. Her lectures are long-winded and irrelevant, and she cared more about forcing people to be tech-free than teaching. I was so excited for this course bc I like prehistory but she was so awful.

reviews.comment:
inconsiderate, brutal, senseless person who made me hate her and her course assigning 3 papers each 5 pages for final when students have other exams and workload. What’s the point ?????
This is inhumane and shameful !!!!DISGUSTED
Dr. Le Blanc is brilliant and fun. If you're in it for an easy A, go someplace else. She wants you to actually read, and perhaps, I don't know, LEARN SOMETHING.

Cool professor, I imagine the class to be much more fun in person, but this was not the case. I do not recommend this class to anyone who is not an art history major. Midterm and final are 15 page essays basically. If you love art history, take this class, if u want an easy elective, look elsewhere, you will burnout. Very nice professor though

The material isn't "hard" but the workload is insane during these troubling times. No breathing period and she expects so much from her students while her lectures aren't that helpful. She's nice and very knowledgeable but I feel like she chooses to make things hard for us. Can't imagine how she is for an upper division course. Yikes

I dont suggest taking this class. Shes a tough grader and assigns too many papers. She appears to have more interest in making her class rigorous rather than helping her students. For the final she gave us a week to complete 3 essays which doesnt sound bad but cmon girl we have other classes ...

attendance wasn't mandatory, except that we had to show up 3x out of the quarter for a grade. lectures were boring and the professor discussed history no one cares about. she had 6 unit essays and one journalism assignment. this class was solely writing essays. the 15-18 pg midterm and final each were nightmares. professor was nice but annoyed me

she was good at first until the midterm hit and we were expected to write 3 essays, 5 pages each, and only gave us 3 days to complete this task. her final is the same thing, she is super picky when it comes to grading. the issue with the midterm is not the time we got but the essay page number she's expecting. I am really disappointed.

I took this class as an elective and it's very tedious. The midterm and final were both 3 separate essays which I feel like is too much for such a course. This class was more work than my upper divs for my major. Also, she deletes recorded lectures after a week for no reason. We're in a pandemic bro.

I took AHS028 as an elective. I RECOMMEND not taking this class as an elective bc it is very tedious. ONLY take this class if you are majoring in this area. Tbh, not even my upper division courses so far request as much as this class. Professor & TA have two 15-18 page essays (midterm & final). They're nice but that isn't enough to pass the class

Overall a very cool and kind professor but her expectations and the TAs are very unrealistic. Were in a pandemic and arent receiving the full learning experience required for her standards. Shes a tough grader and her 15 page midterm and final were excessive and draining especially during these trying times. A great person overall though.

reviews.comment: COVID class: Really knows her stuff, and her lectures are great but she doesn't provide slides with info on them just the art and who made it. You need to really focus on what she says and write it ALL down. Deletes the recorded sessions after 2 weeks, look at them before they are gone. 25% for part. bibliography assignment, midterm, and final.
Interesting class and great lecture but assigned a 15 page midterm two days before it was due for a lower division class.

This professor is really kind and caring but as someone else has mentioned, a 15 page midterm is ridiculous, given our current predicament and other midterms during this week. She is an amazing lecturer and provides amazing feedback, but stay far away from this course if you are trying to do an elective. Not worth the stress at all..

reviews.comment: She is very educated and a fun professor HOWEVER, she is an extremely tough grader. We only got As on the midterm if it was EXCEPTIONAL. If you did everything you needed to, but it wasn't ABOVE AND BEYOND, you got a B or lower. Other than that, this class did not demand too much other than take note of every word that comes comes out of her mouth!

apart from the tough grading & hard take home final we were assigned, the class was a good experience. Shes takes time for discussion with students during lecture and relates contemporary issues really well. Not an easy A, unless ur reading and memorizing themes throughout the whole quarter. Tell her ur concerns early, she'll listen for fairness!

reviews.comment: If I hadn't taken BCH100 first I don't know how I would've known anything. I stopped going to lecture because it felt like 2 hours of him talking but not teaching. Your only hope is to get 100% on all quizzes(online) and HW, do the EC and get above average (55%) on tests. Learn/memorize HW and lecture problems, many are repeated on the test.

While he is a knowledgeable professor, he can be quite rude at times. Talking with him may result in him stating or implying that your question is stupid, even if all you really need is an answer to said question. In other words, he is blunt. This can be good or bad depending on the person, so make your choice as you go. Lackluster lectures too.

IMO he is a great professor. His content delivery is dense but clearly motivated IF you understand the big picture of the class; there is a reason for every slide presented. If you are interested in the content its easy to pay attention to him and his voice is nice. helpful in OH but come prepared, some Qs are stupid Qs he might let you know it.

I attended every lecture. He is not a good lecturer (very monotone and doesn't explain things). His polls were confusing. He makes you memorize a lot of structures. Exam covered very little of the learning objectives. He was rude to people and not helpful in office hours. I had to teach myself everything and the material is so vast and so dense.

Professor Blaha is knowledgeable about the material and cares about his students. However, he is extremely monotone and it is difficult to pay attention in lecture. The exam is fair based on the content, just make sure you understand the homework and memorize the slides. The slides contain all the information you need to teach yourself the content.

He is not that great of a lecturer and his polls are not explained well on the slides or even in person. He makes you memorize a ton of sugars and structures which I think takes away from the purpose of the course. Exam was fair, but covered little of what he told us to focus on. Final exam had many questions straight from the HW
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very knowledgeable in biochemistry, but looking at his slides sucks the energy out of you due to the sheer amount of material on ONE slide. So get ready for 60-70 pages worth of slides, as most of it is filled with tons of yappage. The final also had no chemical pathways (could change), which was disheartening since many studied those deeply.

I'm not trying to be that person but for one his lectures are the most boring lectures I've ever been to. All he does is read off the lectures and he sometimes messed up what he tries to say. I wouldn't recommend for new students or transfer students. Also his exam had nothing to do with either the learning objectives or vocabulary.
Terrible, just terrible
Lecture  style is boring and ability of teaching bad.

Dr. Blaha is very knowledgeable about biochemistry but I just had a hard time following along with his lectures. Take advantage of his TA and ask lots of questions. Final was mix of homework, quizzes and lecture material.

His lectures can be a little dull, but because I found the material interesting, it wasn't as bad, but if you're not into the it, it can get monotonous. His tests, which was the molecular lab portion, is not bad as long as you write down the commands, and remember what you did in lab. He does ask you conceptual questions in a few questions.

Not gonna lie this class was hard, especially the homework because sometimes lecture and the hw was out of sync. Exams were tough but also based on hw so it was doable if you put in genuine effort into the hw. Professor was clearly passionate and really knowledgeable about the material so it was great to listen to him during those tangents.
I actually took BCH 190 for research units. However, I have taken BCH 184 with Dr. Gregor Blaha. Material is straightforward. I don't understand why he has such crappy ratings.

His slides had too much information and it did not clearly state what you needed to know for the final. He used homework questions for the finals, so it was easy. He caused a lot of stress near the end and ghosted us a day before the finals. The other professor had to help instead, and he didn't even teach the 2nd half of the class.

Don’t fall behind because it really hinders your ability to do well in this class. Final covers everything in the class and even the homework assignments word by word so make sure to review because I didn’t and the very last assignment ended up on the final which sucked.

This man is so all over the place. He does not allow us to ask questions in class. How are we to learn If we can't ask questions? I literally raised my hand in class and he legit ignored me. He is all over the place. We legit have to learn on our own because we do not learn anything from him.

The prof taught the 2nd half of the quarter and the material was not too difficult if you ask him or the TA questions. It was the sheer amount of material that I had to learn that was the difficult part. Lectures can be a bit tedious and the homework gets difficult after week 2. PowerPoints has all the material on the test but there is a lot.

He is not clear at all. Has an annoying chicken scratch over his lecture slides that make no sense. I definitely did not learn from him at all and had to learn on my own from reading his lecture slides. Unfortunately, if you have to take the Biochem 110 series good luck because you will have to deal with him.

BCH110A is a very dense course with a lot of information. So it is understandable that the lecture slides are very long. But the good thing is the slides has all the information you need for the exam. Dr. Blaha is very knowledgable, just focus on the questions on the HW and quizzes to get an idea of what are important.

He does his best explaining the heavy concepts but sometimes what he goes over in-class isn't what is on the exams. Really monotone but has useful clicker questions occasionally. If studying lecture slides is your thing, get ready to read 100+ slides per lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: His lectures are very dry and boring. The class itself was kinda easy, however, the lab coordinator Gregor works with for this class is very rude. Gregor kept and other students an extra hour when I did not have the time to stay but he did not give us the option. He can be a bit rude if you answer wrong or ask questions if you feel lost in lab.

the class was very easy he teaches the molecular graphics part. the assignments are fair, but his final was a bit rough. he emphasized a specific topic in and we all thought he will ask about it in the final, but he didn't. he asked 4 questions about a small part which we didn't go through that much and we had only 6 questions total for his final.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: BCH 110A was not an easy class. the lectures were very dry and hard to sit through. I recommend studying hard if it's your first Biochem class, and go to his office hours.

He's from a Noble Laureates lineage. A very fine professor with a grasp on molecular biology.

reviews.comment: Overall good professor. The only bad thing is he is very mono-toned... His lectures were a bit hard to sit through because he made it a tad boring. No book, exams are learning objectives in lecture notes. However, the material is pretty straight forward and he is willing to help during office hours. Also his exam was not bad at all!

This class is insanely easy. in fact biochemistry is insanely easy itself. I could've gotten an A had this class been taught in Arabic. The material is easy to understand. the only thing that makes this class any difficult is the fact that there Is so much information. you learn 500 slides worth of information yet only get tested on about 50.

While he does have an accent I find him very easy to understand. I thought he was a good lecturer, he doesn't dwell to much on one specific thing and keeps a good pace. What I liked most is how he talked about some modern research rather than just textbook stuff. Also, he was helpful during office hours.

If you can listen to T-pain and understand him, I do no difference between the accent rapper and a German Professor. Capable of teaching disabled students to achieve higher hopes and higher reasoning abilities.

A nice person, but everytime he taught I felt I was warped into a foreign country. Me no understandith accent. ;7; Luckily his slides do not overload on info or learning objectives. Easier to self-study.

He is new at teaching, but I think he is better than Ziegler.  His slides are straight to the point and he doesn't put so many useless learning objectives.  There are areas where he can improve on, but this is a good start.

Dude. I hated when this guy would lecture. We rotated 3 profs. He was the worst. I couldn't understand ANYTHING he would say during class. Thank goodness for the podcasts though, at least there was come comprehensible stuff if you listened closely. Might as well not go to class and just listen to the podcasts. Really bad accent.

I am not an art history major and this was my first art history class. I personally think she and her TAs grade a little hard so you have to put a lot of effort into work. 1 short paper, midterm, and final.

A really good professor who is very passionate about the subject. The lectures are a lot of information you need to pick up on your own from her words and not slide, but she provide study guides that can be filled out good if you take fairly decent notes or ask her/TAs you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Davis did always have a smile and was willing to answer lots of questions during lecture. She is passionate about art. She was strict on getting up and leaving during class. She assigns weekly hw to turn in during discussion. I personally thought the class was boring but if you show up & pay a little bit of attention you can pass.

Amazing professor! Always has a smile on her face and is the kindest person. The tests are easy if you remember the paintings and do the readings. There is one paper and you have plenty of time for it. She makes art history interesting and fun because she is so passionate and really loves what she's doing. Would recommend to anyone.

Professor Davis is very passionate about what she is teaching. She has so much enthusiasm during her lectures. Beware of pop quizzes both before or in between lecture. Make sure you memorize the dates given with the paintings she shows!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Caring

reviews.comment: I took Dr. Davis in an online course in spring of 2017. She is a great teacher and is enthusiastic about art, I just hate art. There are 3 essays and 3 quizzes.

She is good professor. The course was a bit difficult for me, but I didn't always show up for her class and the lectures are really important. She goes into specific details and her thoughts about certain pieces of art. It helps to participate, she loves those students. She is not afraid to call you out. Homework is all reading and responding.
