She's really inflexible and a bit biased. She's currently writing her dissertation and it got rejected. She personally thought it was really good. I think that's why she grades REALLY hard
Kind of unorganized because we have to turn in another essay before we get our previous one back. If we got it back before we had to do another one then we can learn more.

Teacher was very interested in the subjects she was teaching.  Unfortunately, she was a bit self-absorbed and constantly pointed out her own work.  But, she was dedicated.  It was exceedingly hard to get an A.  A paper would say "Good, well-developed ideas and excellent execution.  Needs a bit more research though" and I would get a B! Unrealistic.

She works hard, I'll give her that. You'll get a very dedicated prof, but unfortunately the class is more of a sociology course than anything remotely related to English. We just did a 10 week study on immigration...

She has much to expect from you and her grading is tough, but if you are a hardworking student your effort will not go unnoticed. If you're a slacker, drop her class before the end of the second week! hahaha.

It's too bad you don't get to know who your professor is when you register for classes, so if you get her, unlucky you. Everything has to go according to her schedule and her schedule only. If you try to compromise, you'll just get a "too bad." This class has a somewhat heavy workload, so if you're not going to take this class seriously, think twice about taking it with her. She only gave us a 2 hour time frame to turn in our last paper because she had to go to europe. She cares too much about herself and her career as an expert in Literature to even give you any attention.

Its hard to get an A in her class, but it is fairly easy to get a B so long as you pull at least some effort.  She is pretty demanding, but she covers interesting subjects and I really enjoyed her class.
its very hard to get an A in a single essay since she grades accordingly to the rubric. you must write an "outstanding" essay to get an A. Overall, shes a kind teacher.
The class is easy if you do the papers. She is a really good teacher. It is just difficult to get an A on a paper because she grades so hard.
DEMANDING BUT ALSO VERY HELPFUL TEACHER. HARD TO GET AN A. PAPERS HAVE TO BE ALMOST PERFECT.

Great course. If you pay attention in class you will do good. I took The Problem of Religion course (not listed) and it was weekly quizzes, a midterm and a final (both essays) He allows you to use AI but in an appropriate academic manner, which was helpful to learn more of the content. He offers extra credit as well. No excuses easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He is super nice and caring. The class is pretty good and easy. If students participate, he'll give extra credit
Most boring classes of all time but doesn't really matter because he gives you 20 points of extra credit if you get majority attendance to lectures and the midterm and final and super easy.

There are 2 books we went over, I read them sometimes, but you'll survive even if you never read. This class was the easiest A I've ever gotten. I got 99% on the midterm and 100% on the final, even without finishing the readings and barely studying. Discussions are mandatory (weekly quizzes, most of your grade, also easy), but lecture is not.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Chang is great. His class is easy and full of extra credit opportunities. I got an amazing TA (Chris), so that made the class even better. Definitely recommend taking.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved his class. It's not hard at all if you do all the readings that he gives. He also releases the midterm and final a week before the actual exam date so you have time to review. Professor Chang is one of the best professors I've ever taken, very nice and responsive to questions.

At first, the work seemed overwhelming but if you do the readings and the questions you'll do great. Took him in Fall 2022, I would study for the midterm because for me it wasn't open notes, he gives a study guide which is exactly the same as the midterm. For the Final, he gives a study guide as well, for that it's an open note.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Such a wonderful Professor, I really recommend him to everyone.

Took him Fall 2022, stopped attending lectures by week 2 though he gives EC for mandatory attendance (I chose optional). Only graded by quizzes midterm & final no homework except for reading ahead which I did not do. Midterms and tests given beforehand (answers found in textbook) and check your responses with him during office hours. Easy A
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took his class in Fall 2022. Dr. Chang is clearly passionate and very knowledgable about what he teaches. He provided good study guides before the exams. There was some reading but very manageable. He seems like he truly cares about his students.

I had Chang for RLST 007 also and he's the best. He's very straightforward. He makes sure you learn but he doesn't enforce crazy rules or assign much work. I don't know how he does it but he's a 10/10. He's also easily the most fluid and helpful prof I've had throughout the pandemic. Take him if you can, it's worth it and it's minimal work for an A
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Paul is a great professor. You have a quiz in discussion every week, based off of last weeks readings but the answers are given to you in class. Attendance isn't mandatory, he makes you choose optional or mandatory. Choose mandatory, and you'll receive 25 pts extra credit. You answer questions in class in groups, but it's not hard

He's a fairly new professor, but he really tries his best. Attendance in lecture isn't mandatory, but all the quizzes, midterm, and final are based on them. Lecture is just the students answering his questions that he posts before lecture, and he has the students work in groups then share their answers out loud. Quizzes are during every discussion.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: He is the best! very nice and fair professor. Doesn't try to trick you. Everything is straightforward
Such a great professor to learn from if you truly want to learn about all 3 abrahamic religions. Would take again if I could.

Great class! Weekly quizzes, but the lecture from that week pretty much went over everything so the quizzes were fairly simple. Midterm and final are papers. Encouraged participation and was overall a really friendly guy. I'd love to take another class with him! He's a newer professor but he's great at what he does.
Paul is a really nice professor. Quizzes every week and papers for the midterm and final. Katie the TA is the best.
Quizzes every Friday, but everything written on the board from the readings will be on the quiz.

The best professor I've encountered at ucr (NOT the easiest). Dr. Cioffi speaks about the course content with depth and nuance, never watering down concepts too much. This is exceedingly rare among professors at ucr. If you want to actually learn and be challenged, I highly recommend Dr. Cioffi. He also welcomes questions in class & is approachable

There are some bad reviews, I understand where those may come from tho. The review before this one is definitely a person who did not have the guts to argue during the discussion time that was given to us. Prof did not delay the midterm because his feelings got hurt-- it was asked by the class. He is understanding and always helps during office hrs
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The most biased, and non-objective professor I've ever had the misfortune to experience. He's a propaganda machine for the left, consistently saying things that I later fact checked to be incorrect. He is better suited for leading a book club than teaching the young minds of America. He'll also postpone H delay midterms if his get feelings hurt.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I found that if you did the readings, ensured active listening and attended all lectures and section, you'll be successful. My biggest tip;take pictures of the slides and only take notes on what he is saying during the lecture, then write the pp notes later. The content of the course is dense,therefore,knowing all details to some extent-is-critical
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS, LOOK THE OTHER WAY. This was the first time in all my academic years failing a midterm. You need to be in class to understand, or have a group of people studying with you, you cannot study on your own for this class if you have not taken notes in lecture since he does not post lecture slides only assigned readings.

I was really excited about taking this course, the professor seemed nice and the topics were very interesting. However he assigns an insane amount of reading, expects books read in a week in addition to 4 or 5 journals or articles 15+ pages each per lecture! He does not record lecture so attendance is mandatory. lecture is dry. RUN!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Very straight forward in terms of material and grading. Must attend lectures because he doesn't record them, but he does post all the slides. He's very understanding and got rid of final paper so we only had a midterm and final. Reading is intimidating at first but I didn't read anything at all and still got good grade on essays. He's very nice too
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Not to be dramatic but this class made me want to do a face dive into hot cement because. Professor Cioffi was great, he is really sweet and knowledgable. HOWEVER, omg, his class was so hard. Even for an upperdiv class, it was impossible to pass without reading at least 100pages per week. Really dense on the material. Run while u can :)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really fun and interesting professor. The amount of reading in this class is overstated. As long as you get the main gist and reasonings behind the assigned cases and go to the discussions you won't have to read everything assigned to you. Tests are essays that really requires you to know how to analyze prompts and write with a goal and structure.

This class was so hard! But Cioffi is very approachable and nice so that helps. I went to office hours a lot and asked a lot of questions. If you have taken an economics class before this then it would probably be easier, I have never taken economics so I was pretty lost for a while. There is a ton of reading, like hundreds per week - be prepared
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Took Con Law, no textbook but might as well create his own given how many PDFs he gives for reading. Lectures are a must! I liked his style so much I took 164 and got another A+, again a ton of reading. I recommend sitting in the front so you can hear him talk. Both amazing courses. If you need help, he is very helpful during office hours.

Definately a class you must attend lecture to clarify the material. The readings are long and dense, prior economic knowledge is definately helpful.  Prof Cioffi is very knowledgeable on the topic and helpful during office hours. Only take his course if you're ready to put a considerable amount of effort!
Hardest class ever taken

It is a difficult class. You must attend class to learn. He does not post lecture notes online.  So be prepare to come in to take notes. It is a challenging course,you must read and  might be  required to do additional reading to help you comprehend the material.
The content of the class is difficult, but it is not hard to get a good grade.

Definitely take an econ course before taking this. A lot of econ terms and theories applied here. Was difficult, but LEARNED A LOT. No books needed, he provides all readings online. Exams are ALL essay questions.
By far the hardest class I have ever taken. But man I learned so much the final was ridiculous I came out of there and I thought my head was going to explode!

go to his lectures! he teaches it like law school, so it gets you in that mentality. There's a paper, midterm, and final. I had Justine as a TA and she was super helpful! Don't be afraid to ask questions. Also I put all the cases on notecards to make it easier to study. WORK HARD

DO your readings, and not only will you be able to hear him(he mumbles), but you will UNDERSTAND him. He also utilizes the socratic method, and like in law school, he'll ask for your opinion but will not give you a straight answer. Don't complain if you're planning to go to law school. Amazing class. Prepare to do work, but an A isn't impossible.

You have to attend the lecture, you have to read all the readings (100pages). You don't have to buy a book, he puts the articles online (super long). He uses big words when his lecturing, which makes it difficult to understand him

He expects students to do the reading before coming to class. and he is very serious when he said that.   EVERYTHING you do, the midterms, finals, term papers, relates back to the reading and it is IMPOSSIBLE to do well in his class without reading through hundreds of pages of material throughout the entire class.

If you are considering law school you must take this course. Dr. Cioffi can seem intimidating but prepare yourself well and put forth a substantial effort and you will do just fine.  He is more than willing to help.  One piece of advice, stay on top of your reading!  The book is your best friend.  Eat, sleep, and breathe with that book next to you!

There is no powerpoint. He just asks peoples opinions and what they think about everything....again, this is not contributing to my learning. The Midterm covers only very little of the material learned. The class is easy, but he doesnt know how to lecture...and you basically have to teach yourself everything, because he wont.

Does not offer fair exams. Though we cover a large amount of material, his midterm question only covered a small amount of this material. This means that if you're not 100% clear on that small material you are screwed.

This guy is really boring. He puts me to sleep, seriously. It's sad because the material is extremely interesting. It's also difficult to keep up with his lectures as he offers no direction and jumps all over the place. I don't know where I would be had i not taken Constitutional Law with Bordner first.

I was a bit apprehensive about taking this course, but i was glad i did.  I have rarely learned so much so easily as I did in his course.  His lectures are more valuble than the reading and he is just fascinating to be around.  He does, however, have high demands for the learning and is fairly strict.  HIGHLY RECCOMENDED

Kind of reminds of Reed Richards from Fantastic Four. Super Smart. Personable. Even has the graying sideburns. Reading is a lot but not too difficult. Lecture is interesting to those already interested in U.S. history, law, and political science.
he's great!

This class made me decide to go to law school.  The readings are interesting if you're into the law, if not... don't take this class, the in class essay tests are hard and the paper was difficult too.  But if you make it through, its worth it.
Professor Cioffi is a great professor; however, he seems unapproachable.  He is great to take if you have any interest in the law.  His lectures are interesting and informative.

took two classes with cioffi... i truly believe he is not a good teacher. better 1 on 1. he talks too softly even after many requests to SPEAK UP! constantly going off topic...gives you information in a round about manner... not very interested in making sure you understand. if asking for clarification you will probably get more confused!

This class is easy if you are interested in it.   The readings are the most important thing.  Lectures are helpful to help you understand it, but you can't get by without doing the readings.   Overall great professor.  I would definately take him again.
the reason i even contemplated law school, he actually allowed students to think rather than just regergetate the information to them
Great class, My favorite class actually....

Professor Cioffi is very nice and helpful, espescially during office hours. He is happy to help as long as you're willing to learn. In addition, yes, he does not use powerpoints or visuals, but his lectures complement the reading and are meant to supplement the material. They help you view things from all perspectives, which is crucial for the test
Professor Cioffi is horrible! He is not truly interested in helping students, nor is he interested in making the material accessible and understandable.
Hard to hear (talks softly) so sit near the front.  Midterm is 40% of grade and final is 60% which means no papers but have to go to class.  Just a so-so professor.  Not very personable.
This class is very easy if you go to lecture and do the readings, he gives a study guide before the midterm and final, if you study from if you will do fine in the class.

Awesome course. Although he's hard to hear at times, his teaching style is reflected on what should be expected upon entering a law school. That is, you read the material, enter class and discuss it. Ppl who have a hard time clearly haven't done the work and aren't ready for an upper div course.

POSC 186 was a mind numbing class, but his others are very interesting. He is actually one of the smartest and helpful teachers this school has. If you cant stay awake in his class then your a bad student, your the one at fault. Take a  look at his bio.
one of the worst professors at ucr
Talks like a boring anchorman. Can't really understand what he is saying.
Such an easy class. People who complain about him are the ones who always need colorful powerpoint lectures. Yeah, he doesnt use visuals, but this is upper division, not some intro 001 class.
No Comments
No Comments
WORST TEACHER EVER!! Horrible monotone boring lectures, impossible to stay awake.  Never take this prof. he is absolute garbage.
Cioffi knows his stuff, but he is not good at teaching it. He barely writes on the board and only speaks...he talks way too quiet for a large course, and is not helpful in office hours.

He is very clear and illustrates the problems and solutions of regulation well. Get over yourself, goto class and *gasp* actually listen and you'll do fine. No surprises on the tests / essays, if you pay attention it's easy.

Easy class and a great professor, an asset to the university. Lectures are crystal clear; tests and papers are not difficult at all. Those who post negative are sorry business majors who have never had to think or write. They should go back to high school
Don't take him...
he is teaching in his own lil world. its like he enjoys his own lecture.. and he is prolly the only one likes the coures..
Loved the material.  Hated the boring lectures.  He speaks in a monotone.
He is very knowledgeable about the subject, but he is not that lively for a class of such large number (POSC 186).
Not as bad as made out.
this class sucks......do not take this professor ever..!!!!!!!!!!

Extremely boring...All he does is lecture, I suggest you bring a tape recorder because it is very difficult to keep up with all his rambling.  The midterm and final are all essay format, so it is a pretty difficult class!
sorry teacher, really boring
Goes off on random tangents, speaks too quietly, unorganized
Great professor! She wants everyone to succeed, and is always in a great mood.

she is clear and very helpful. but she also so smart and love to teach you how to think. dont' depend on attending class alone. you must let her know ur name during office hours. try not to ask her stupid questions, she hates that. you MUST understand the material not just try to pass. ATTEND lecture. test from the notes. and do HW!!! it helps
VERY good professor.  She has a way of explaining things that make them seem clear.  Nice attitude.  Class is not that easy, but you learn a lot of useful things.
Great Class.

pretty standard class. midterm was insanely easy, final however was extremely difficult out of nowhere. lectures are a bit all over the place but he is super accessible and will help you out if you need it. you're pretty much responsible for how well you do. if you put the work in, do the homework, study outside of class, you'll be just fine
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I'm not sure what the other bad reviews are but I honestly thought the professor was pretty good. He was able to explain many of the math concepts fairly well during lectures. As long if you put deliberate effort into the class, I'm sure you'll be successful.

I took Clausen during the fall quarter for 9c, I gotta say it was probably my best experience i've had with a professor. I really think if you put in the effort and interact with the class it is incredibly easy to pass, it definitely takes some work but he's honestly a great guy and he always put in a ton of work to help people learn the material.

Insanely terrible lecturer. Great guy, I'm sure, but he is genuinely so bad at teaching the material that sometimes I think that's why he lets us use cheatsheets. What was on our homework did NOT reflect what was taught in lecture at ALL. But the tests reflected it pretty well, at least. Weekly quizzes, attendance thru a PollEV based on completion.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Don't know what the negative reviews are about, but he is very accommodating and thorough with his lectures for MATH 010A as of Spring 2025. Do the work, participate, and take advantage of the cheat sheet usable for midterm + final. Useful during office hours and ensures that all your questions are answered. He goes at a fast pace during lectures.

His lectures is him doing practice problems without explaining anything. We had 2 midterm corrections due but he didn't even grade them in time. He doesn't respond to emails. His syllabus hasn't been updated since covid, and due dates for homework and worksheets were unclear. You self teach basically. My TA was also clueless bc 0 communication.

Not that good of a lecturer especially for 10A, TA saved my grade I would've failed the class without the TA. Every midterm and final felt like it was giving questions I never saw before on the homework and the layout is different than the homework. Don't take unless you have to.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I would avoid this class if possible. Prof. Clausen is helpful during office hours and in tutoring, but his lectures were confusing and hard to understand. A big part of this is due to the way the Math005A class is structured, so I can't fault him too much for being required to teach a certain way, but it's very difficult to learn and excel.
David Clausen is not good at teaching and his tests are very difficult.

Not impossible, but a pain in the neck because his lectures are essentially just him doing practice problems with little context (rely on TAs and self-study). If you can do the homework thats good (his exams are easier/simpler than hw). If you put in an honest, consistent effort to know the material, you're sailing. Would not take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Do not take Prof Clausen. He is not a good teacher, expect to learn nothing from him. The TA was actually able to teach and explain concepts to us. In his lectures, he just solves math problems like how a student does his math homework, no explanations at all. Overall, avoid his class and if you do take it, be prepared to learn things on your own.

Please think twice about taking Professor Clausen. Yes, he is a nice professor, but that only applies to his personality. His lectures are literally just watching him solve math problems WITHOUT explaining concepts or formulas to the students. To add on, his work is extremely messy. This sucks because the final is worth 50% of the grade. AVOID HIM.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class moves pretty fast, but as long as you complete your assignments and review your notes, you'll be fine.

This Prof has an extremely messy teaching style that is hard to follow, if it was not for the TA i would have no clue what was going on in the class, the final is worth such a big portion of the overall grade which sucks. He is making attempts to improve his teaching but it feels like he expects us to already know most of the material.
He is a bit of a mess but honestly if you go to his office hours you will understand the material. His tests are multiple parts but 10 questions max. I would retake him again.

This professor can not teach to save his life.He has never taught this class before, and verbatim took 9B content and gave it to us. All of our tests, midterms, and quizzes said 9B, some crossed out 9B saying 7B.He decided he did not like our textbook, and went with a different one than we were using. I would not have passed without my TA's notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It was hard to follow lectures sometimes but if you attend office hours often it is not the worst. The subject itself is hard but if you put enough time into it is really not that bad. Finals are weighted really heavily so study hard.
Final and midterm are huge parts of your grade but nothing prepares you for it. The practice exams are completely different, his slides are useless and he is not great at explaining concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is not the worst, but he's definitely not the best. He makes mistakes on ALL of his notes and lectures. It not only confuses the student but he gets confused as well. The exams weren't horrible, but he did poorly to prepare us. If you take him, you HAVE to learn everything on your own because I don't think I learned anything from his lecture.

Professor Clausen was a good teacher. I highly recommend going to his office hours. I went to the majority of them to ask questions and it really helped. Everyone was saying that the final and midterm were hard but they weren't that bad if you actually studied. The professor is good but the class is very hard. Study daily and you will do just fine.
Good lectures, exams are super difficult and very different from practice exams. Final is 43% of your grade and midterm is 29%, going to office hours is super helpful.

Okay teacher, but very fast during lectures and mostly uses typed notes which is weird for math. Doesn't respond to emails. Many students have complained about his grading but he won't change anything, the quizzes & exams are unnecessarily difficult because he uses problems that have a lot of hard algebra rather than calculus.

Well, he's not bad, but he is very fast with his lectures. He expects you to know a lot of the material beforehand and takes a poll at the end of every lecture. He posts the slides after lectures, but exams were different compared to his reviews which wasn't fair, and not to forget he showed up late to the midterm and took the papers early.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good professor enjoying him so far. Having a clear understanding on the material. You should be fine if not go to his OH or TA

he goes very fast during lecture. the examples he gives in class often times wont be anything close to the homework. be prepared to dedicate yourself to homework, quizzes, exams, & busy work for discussion

Really nice and sweet prof. Although this class was definitely more similar to a history class so keep that in mind. All exams were online, attendance only mandatory for discussion, and post slides in advance. Lecture could be a little eh but overall prof just doing his best.

God bless professor Clark. Overall amazing teacher and very easy to talk to. He's extremely interesting to learn from and puts in a lot of effort for his students. It's refreshing to find a teacher that cares for his students like he does. His class isn't hard, just show up, pay attention and you'll get a lot from him.

Honestly love his class, he is such a great professor. There was a switch halfway through the quarter because of family issues, wishing him the best!! ALSO recommend David Madrid for discussion, he breaks the whole lecture down so well, and explains everything really well.

This professor was really passionate about his class. There is 2 midterms and a final. I would recommend TA David Madrid because he simplified the study guides to include only what was the the exams. Attendance is not mandatory for lectures but it is for discussions. He has amazing powerpoints to go back to if you miss a lecture.

One of those easy general eds, lecture attendance is not mandatory, but discussions are. As long as you study the study guide given 2-3 days before midterms + final, you'll be fine! I recommend for the songs you have to memorize (they're on the exams), to make a Spotify playlist and just memorize them.

Prof Clark is really passionate about music and very caring towards student's concerns. MUS18 is interesting if you're into history. Slides are a bit long but all exam contents are available on them. Exams are online (in class) and multiple choice. Only discussion attendance is mandatory. My TA Patrick is super cool too!

Prof Clark is really passionate about teaching and really cares about student's questions. MUS18 is interesting if you're into history and music. All exams contents are straightforward and on the slides. Lecture attendance not mandatory but discussion once per week is. Read the slides (quite long) and review vocabularies well then you're good.

This class was much harder than I expected. I am a good student and I am struggling to remember the content of the class. Tests are simple yet still hard to do. He does listening portions on his exams. If you can memorize content and remember songs then you will do well. Also, I had no discussion section but lectures in person.
what a easy A class

Easy breadth course! 2 midterms (50 Qs, 25% each), 1 final (60 Qs, 30%), and attendance (20%, pass around sign-in sheet). Lectures are kinda boring bc he just reads off slides (literal paragraphs on each slide), but exams are easy enough since all the info is on the slides (just a LOT of memorization). Clark & my TA Patrick were super nice!

Two midterms, one final, and attendance are counted towards grade. No Homework. Easy A if you study. Professor is very nice and loves to teach what he does. Definitely recommend this professor for any course. Lectures are easy to follow, discussions sections are mandatory but are helpful.
I didn't really enjoy his lectures and it felt like he began to get bored too. Lots of material and memorization are required to do well on the tests.
The material is really easy and he only grades exams and participation in discussion, but the exams aren't difficult at all. It's an easy A class.

Very kind professor and very respected. Grades came from the two midterms and the final along with the discussion points from your ta. Lots of information to memorize which would be very difficult to remember for in person. Changed class to hybrid based on how the students reacted; very very kind and caring for others.

Prof Clark is super nice & everything in his lectures reflects the exams so just show up, pay attention & you should pass. Theres no outside readings or hw. TAs are great & helpful for reviewing material. You dont have to know anything music related & still do well. All you have to do for exams is look over his slides/review the listenings.

Dr Clark is a great teacher, very kind and passionate but don't take his class thinking it will be easy. If you want a A or even a high B be prepared to study your ass off. Graded on two midterms and a final and test questions are fair and from the lecture. but basically, if you're not passionate about music I would not take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If youre looking for an easy class this is definitely the move!! Interesting content and the professor/TA were super kind!! We are only graded on two midterms and a final and they were pretty easy.

Professor Clark made this a very easy going class especially considering it had to be taken online this quarter. Only graded on a midterm and final exam which were multiple choice and involved questions from the lectures and listening exercises. Pretty easy class and you dont have to know anything about music to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: This class is fairly easy as long as you make sure to study the terms he gives you on the study guide. Before the midterms, he gives you a study guide and as long as you remember the details he went over in class and listen and memorize the audio files you should be able to get an A in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Write down whatever he writes. He's memorized these facts pretty much verbatim from the test. Places and meanings/definitions are heavily tested on exams, specific years people were born/died are not important (but the periods are important). Final is literally the midterm questions copied and pasted in addition to questions on the new material.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Music 18 with Dr. Clark was a bit hard and required a lot of memorization, but his passion for the material was really cool and his stories were entertaining! Fun fact: he was knighted in Spain
Good teacher, says what will be one the tests with no tricky questions whatsoever. Attend class and it's an easy A, also remember to listen to the Reading and Listening examples he gives out
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Clark is honestly a fantastic professor. He may seem intimidating at first, but try to get to know him. Be prepared to remember history about music in Spain. His lectures may not be the most interesting, but he tries his best to make students understand the material. Take time to memorize the listening examples. I loved taking this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I took MUS 18 during my winter quarter. Professor Walter Clark puts a lot of passion in his lectures and every lecture is vital for your midterms and final. So, attendance for both lecture and discussion is important. If you do your readings, show up to lecture and write down whatever he puts on his board and study it, it is all fair game!

Dr. Clark is an AMAZING professor. He is really Nice and Passionate about what he teaches. The midterms are fair and aren't too bad. Study a bit and you should be fine. The assigned essay was not bad at all and he is a considerable grader. Definitely no regrets taking the class. Got to learn about cool music and how it kept changing through time.

Prof Walter is an amazing lecturer. A lot of the test questions are from what he writes on the board so the textbook isn't really needed it's only really helpful for the paper that you need to write. Prof gives a study guide basically tells you what you need to know on the midterms/final. Hes quick to respond and truly loves music. one of the best
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Clark is awesome! He is a super cool professor and grades fairly. Honestly, you are guaranteed a good grade if you just show up to class and write down the key points of his lecture. The book isn't necessary but it helps a lot when it comes to studying for the essay portions of his tests.

Professor Clark is one of the nicest professors I've had. I really enjoyed the class! He is a great professor and is very inspirational. As long as you attend lectures, do what is asked and study what is in your notes you should be fine. When planning out your essays for the class it would be a good idea to reference the textbook.

I've taken 2 classes with him and i found them super chill/interesting (even though i'm a bch major). the test questions are based on what he writes on the board so i never bought the book. the class consists of 2 midterms, a paper, final and performance report. it's super easy as long as you go to class and take decent notes :)

Easiest class I have ever taken here. NO JOKE. if you go to class and write down everything he puts up on the board, and do the listening examples then you will get an A. that simple. REALLY chill guy. I'm glad I took his class.
easy peasy A class. no textbook needed. goes over everything during lecture. exams are straightforward, no tricks.

Boring-ish, but realllllly easy. Just do the listening. He's really nice, really tries to be funny, and so charming. But, again, the late class during dinner time is killer. but he's so great, it makes up for it. Don't REALLY need the book cause everything he tests you on he writes on the board.

Pretty chill professor. I took his class during the summer. Attendance is part of the grade and course consists: 1 midterm, 1 paper, and 1 final. Exams are multiple choice, listening excerpts, and short-writing answer questions. INTERESTING CLASS! (:
Clark is awesome! He is really passionate about what he teaches. The class consisted of 2 midterms, a paper, and final. It's a laid back kind of class but you do learn a lot.

consisted of 2 midterms & an essay. really straightfoward, just don't leave the music for the last minute. if you know everything on the study guide, then you're fine. since i took it over the summer, attendance was part of the grade. it was really interesting and laid back :)

Had him for summer session. class was two midterms, a paper, and a final.  the paper was on anything related to music that you wanted and the tests were easy especially with the study guides he gave.  the only 'hard' part people struggled with was the listening examples but easy if you listened to them enough beforehand :) a lot of easy memorizatio

Lectures sometimes bland but the subject matter is interesting.  Tests are multiple choice and listening examples are a big part so just take good notes, know everything on the review sheets and you should be fine.  He has a wonderful personality when he gets into it and he really does know a lot.  Also, he's a pretty good musician :)
Great teacher!!!!!!

Excellent professor! Tests consist of listening, multiple choice, and essay, but are easy! Take notes and you'll be fine. No book required. Listening examples are on ilearn...try not to listen to them all before the test and you will be fine! Great class, interesting material. More should be taught about Latin American music. I LOVED THE CLASS!

Grade is mostly just 3 major essays which are paced rather poorly with equal time for each despite 1 being half the length of 3. The lectures are mandatory, but very unhelpful for the course and cover English at a level lower than that of a HS course. The essay grading however is extremely rigorous for a general education writing course. Take at CC

He overshared a LOT! He also was doing way too much work and assigning way too much work on top on his essay structures. On Monday he announced we had to have a seven paragraph MINIMUM draft done by Wednesday on top of him assigning homework and readings. Like bruh, this is an intermediate english class.

He is clearly passionate about the subject he teaches, but his essay structures and grading policies were very strict for an intermediate english class. He also would go off topic a lot which would make him take longer to get through lessons, often going over time in class which made me late to other lectures/midterms.

I'm looking forward to using what I learned here, finally feel ready for college work. I don't know how to say this, but I think some of the negative comments are because of some of the views people have against his identity. In class and in conversation, he was considerate & listened thoughtfully. I liked his sense of humor.
Is not caring for students and not willing to help. Takes a long time to reply. Also, rude.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really caring and understanding professor that saved my butt more than a few times. Difficult but fair grader, and gives you chances to fix things.

My favorite professor thus far. He is very interesting and will help you expand your knowledge on more than what the class requires (in a good way). He always responds to emails and is very very understanding. As long as you listen and follow along with assignments you will do well.

Professor Cleaves is one of the best English professors you can have! Personally, I never felt comfortable with my writing or ever been a fan of English, but he made the course manageable. He does a really good job on explaining what he expects on writing assignments and is easy to talk to if you want additional feedback. There is a lot of reading!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Cleaves is so kind and caring. I got sick during the quarter and couldn't attend class or turn in assignments for half of the quarter and he was so patient with me and gave me extensions for the assignments so I could turn them in when I got better. Would love to retake his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: This professor's work ethic is unbecoming. I would advise getting this professor because there were a lot of biases that went on and he is clearly isn't an understanding professor. The way he grades the essays seems like you always wrong and nothing is ever correct. It's the type of professor that makes you lose passion for writing. DON'T TAKE HIM!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Cleaves is an amazing teacher! He gives amazing feedback and allows resubmissions for essays. He is hilariously straight forward. Also very understanding! I once lost a packet (draft+brainstorm questions) that I was suppose to turn in with my essay and he remembered me being in class that day and him signing it, he accepted my essay!

Dr. Cleaves is an amazing professor. His quiz questions are relatively easy as long as you read. He's extremely passionate about what he talks about and gives loads of advice. Go to his office hours if you are struggling because he is always willing to help and pick your brain.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Cleaves is a really nice professor. He really wants you to try and improve yourself, for your own good. He always allows re-submissions of papers and is available above and beyond office hours.  Always do the readings bc he will do quizzes but as long as you read you'll do fine. Engage in discussions, don't be shy to speak, he's really friendly.

Grades tough but if you're a pretty decent writer, you should at least be able to get B's on the essays. You take a quiz almost every week on reading in the SMG which, if you actually read it, are very easy. That is pretty much your only homework unless you also have an essay to do. Lectures are interesting, you can tell he's passionate about it.

Five essays total. Two of them are in-class. Had to read one novel, which was what the final was on, but he gave the prompt ahead of time so it was easy to pre-write. Not the hardest essay grader, but not the easiest. If you ask him for help and take his suggestions, you'll get a good grade. Pop quizzes nearly every time there is assigned reading.

Great professor who cares about his students. Really helpful and clear during class as well as office hours. In class final and reading quizzes. Tough grader on essays but overall he was a good professor
Super hard professor!!! He barely gives you a grade higher than B-. And he has quiz every classes. If you choose his class, I suggest you drop it as soon as possible.

Professor Cleaves is a great professor. I thoroughly enjoyed his class and have never learned so much. He is very passionate about English and other subjects which makes it very easy to become passionate about them as well. Although it is not a class that you can just get by with doing little, it was worth it because of all that I learned.

He's a cool and chill. You need to read for quizes.  Avoid taking him for summer, he won't preview your paper before submitting. He's NOT so helpful. Tough grader, his kindergarten teacher probably didn't teach him letter A when she went over the alphabets. He'd give you B and B+ for a "solid" paper. If you can take the class wz someone else, do so

Run.  Tough grader. Be ready to read to pass quizzes. You can spark notes, but that won't always help. He has a passion for teaching and can be very inspirational. He is very wise, as well as a good lecturer, but can be very harsh when grading. Put in a lot of effort into essays or you will  not pass.

Professor Cleaves is one of the best professors I have ever had. You can tell he is very passionate about his subject and he is a very gifted academic. He is very funny and his lectures are very engaging. He is the only professor I have seen who spends so much time justifying the importance of his class. I would love to have him again!

Cleaves is a great professor! He's actually the best English teacher I've ever had. He's really passionate and dynamic in the classroom. He asks a lot of questions to encourage students to participate in class. He's very helpful and he's always willing to help with essays. But you won't pass if you don't read, so you HAVE to read every night.

You should follow the schedule on his syllabus bc he tells you what to read since he gives out quizzes in the beginning of class. His quizzes are generally long and asks for lots of details so read thoroughly. He's a tough grader but is willing to help you if you need it. Only had to read the Perks of Being a Wallflower and the St. Martin's Guide.

Dr. Cleaves is not an easy professor, but it is worth taking his class. You will leave with a better level of critical thinking and reading. He is one of the best English professors I've had. He gives quizzes on all of the readings, but if you actually read what's assigned they shouldn't be hard. He gives lots of extra credit on quizzes.

he's awesome! he made me feel really confident about my writing and he gave me an A-! plus, he was really helpful during office hours. he's also down to chat about random stuff, like classic films :D his quizzes are kinda hard but he tells you the questions before hand so yeah, no biggie. best english teacher/professor i've had! take him! you must!
hes a really smart guy and full of wisdom, but he assigns alot of readings and has pop quizes.  the class is difficult but hes a really likeable guy.

Professor Cleaves is a wonderful teacher. He explained everything very well, and was very clear. Quizzes were based on the readings, and they were not too bad. Also, he explained the topic of each essay in depth and made everything easy to understand. And he was also extremely helpful during office hours. A great, kind, and caring teacher.

I am not a big fan of english and writing essays but Wallace Cleaves made it super easy to do so. He would go over the prompt and talk in depth about it. His office hours are also very helpful I honestly did not read a single book that he listed on the syllabus but still got a B in his class.

Best english professor I've ever had! His quizzes were pretty easy as long as you read most of the chapter. He had 4 papers whose topics weren't hard to write on and his final had 2 short in-class written essays. He's not a hard grader so that was also good! Highly recommend taking his class!

hes a really funny guy and has a cool voice.  He is in the english department committee and has a good heart because he always works to help students get english classes, and fights for school funds for the students.  He actually grades pretty easy as long as you have alot of support for your argument.  He can always tell who isnt reading via quiz
he was funny and cool teacher at first but then we started to write essays and then he really didnt explain it that well and he is a really hard grader
Professor Cleaves is a great English teacher and much harder than other English teachers. He demands a lot from his students. There is reading everyday, 4 papers, AND a final.

Overall, Professor Cleaves is an excellent professor. He is sincere and passionate and he motivated me to excel in his class. His grading is fair, but make sure you do all of the assigned readings for quizzes. You will learn how to write, no doubt about it.

If you hate reading (like me) then you're in for a treat! Reading is critical. Did I mention DAILY quizzes?--oh joy! Great teacher and funny too. He pressed the tech help button, they called back, his response "Im sorry my fat butt pushed the button" haha great moment. Just read and you'll be fine! Oh almost forgot he's very picky on his essays!
Best English Professor at UCR, keeps you motivated and is very enccouraging, class seems hard but is actually kind of easy at the end! LOOOVED THIS CLASS

Professor Cleaves is GREAT. He is extremely intelligent and knows his material VERY WELL. You will get the proper Education in his class. Do your reading because there is quizzes every lecture. However, they are only to boost your grade. When you need help with your essay, ASK HIM. HE WILL HELP YOU. This class is hard but not impossible.

What can I say about Professor Cleaves? He is OFFICIALLY my favorite professor since I started at UCR. No, I'm not a 1st year, either. He's very intelligent and made my writing much stronger. When he talks, you want to listen. All these idiots talking s%!# need to grow up and start taking college seriously. Won't take 1C unless it's with him.

Awesome professor!! Enjoyable to look at. Lots of work, but it's not impossible. It's college: suck it up and learn. After all, you're probably paying a mountain of money unless you get substantial financial aid, unlike me. TAKE HIM IF YOU GET A CHANCE. Great English Class. Go to class and just do your work.

PROFESSOR CLEAVES IS AN AMAZING PROFESSOR! Before his class, I not only did i hate English, I also wasn't interested in it at all. Now I seriously love going to English..and I'm a business major. Few tips...Read for weekly quizzes, talk in class even if you think you might be wrong, and GO TO CLASS!

Before I took 1C, I looked Prof. Cleaves up on this website.  I read all the reviews and decided that I would actually get an education if I took his course.  If you do all of the reading and the assignments, you will pass this course.  Sure he expects a lot out of you, but this is COLLEGE people.  Our professors should be expecting a lot!

This teacher is hardcore. Spent way to much time working on English essays and neglected other classes and still received a B-. Office hours are useless. If you expect higher then a B, your going to have to read and pass the quizzes. Grades way to difficult on everything. Also did a useless debate. Has a final, midterm, 4 essays, AND daily reading.

He is one of my fav teachers @ UCR! he knows what he's talking about,and although he does grade pretty hard he expects a lot. I got really good grades on my essay,and ended up with a B+ in the class. quizzes are helpful to boost up your grade, so read! he's really cool though & fun to talk to. YOU WILL LEARN A LOT, WHETHER YOU WANT TO OR NOT.

Prof. Wallace was very helpful.. whether it was during his office hours or when he returned an essay back. Each essay was bleeding with corrections, which was so helpful. Especially because he offered revisions for 3/4 papers. READ! READ! READ! There are 2 quizzes max per week.
he is really hard and you always have to read! Never come to a class without reading!
He grades the papers with ridiculously!He gave me a C- which is not a passing grade, so I had to take the class again...and guess who I ended up with?WALLACE CLEAVES!for the second time!!!!!AWFUL

Not a professor for the weak. his grading is difficult, no doubt,but if you have a genuine interest in getting an education, i'd recommend taking his class. Do the reading and you'll be fine, half the students failed his class when i took it cause they didn't read the texts. do the reading, write well, talk,  and  you'll be fine.

His class is semi-easy, very understanding guy..Grades hard on essays, but what else can you expect with a college composition course? Um, he's really smart..sometimes he can talk to you in a way that makes you feel stupid..he probably doesn't realize it though. Weekly quizzes are EASY, never did the reading, but somehow managed to get an A.
It seems like he only helps the students that he wants to help. Attendance is mandatory, but his lectures are okay.

He's not a very great professor.  He grades his essay unreasonably.  I hardly changed my rewrites and got practically full credit.  If you don't agree withy him he won't give you a great grade.  Avoid him, for your own sake.

His lectures may be fun, but not a great class to be in. If you have him as your professor, I highly recommend dropping his class. His office hours are not helpful, he grades the essays hard, and seems like he only really helps a student he wishes to help, not being fare to some students. Bad experience.
If you have grammar problems I dont recommend taking his class because he you wont get a better grade than "C". He likes students that talk a lot in class. A lot of readings. I hate it
great teacher! i learned more from him in 10 weeks than i did in 4 years of high school!

I highly recommend this professor! After reading the ratings he got on this site I decided to enroll in his class and I am soooo glad that I did. Such a cool guy and very interesting. A lot of reading but he allows revisions on every essay except for the final. Theres a Quiz at least once a week so do the reading but easy quiz questions.

If you take this class you will regret it ... this is not a class where you will get a good grade if you have grammar problems. Grammar problems will get you a C in the class. So if you are not a hardworker just drop the class while you can. Office hours are no help at all!

Takes attendance sometimes.. Funny somtimes.. Boring class.. All your points in the class are basically based on 4 essays and a final essay that's committee graded.. just do good on all your essays.. if you don't pass an essay, visit his office hours and he'll give you some good tips.. overall good teacher, semi hard class
A great teacher, very eccentric and very interesting. Would take this guy again.

great guy...hes really fair...if u get him yer pretty lucky...i missed about 5-6 classes and he has a rule if u miss 3 classes itz auto-fail..point being i got A's on my paper and instead of failing me he told me that he would jes giv me a C...pretty kool...
Funny funny teacher, kind of odd but and good teacher
Wallace is a fantastic teacher. Put something into the class and he'll see it. Cliched yes, but also true.

class is very easy if you are willing to put in the work and reading required. lots of reading is required though! he was extremely helpful during office hours and he really cares for his students. exactly what an english class should be.
He's a great teacher.  Lots of reading and work though.  You have to work hard on your essays to receive a good grade.  Overall, good teacher.

Don't get this professor for 4D because he tends to grade by the scale. If your paper isn't "top quality" it's very hard to get A or B on it. Fluck all my papers and C+ on my first essay because I had a chance to redo it. Not many people receive A in his class. Had to retake Eng. 4 and had a better teacher who gave me better grading on my papers.
Man Wallace was a great professor - good class, fun times.

Wallace is a great professor, he grades hard on grammar problems, the quizes each week are easy if you do the reading, and the midterm and final have a multiple/fill in the blank section and two essays, but they are made easy so you can up your grade.

omg she is literally the sweetest person in the world! very inspiring, her classes were so fun and something to look forward to. as long as you do the work you will pass, it's not hard! super easy class.
A really great professor and highly suggest to get to know her!
Amazing and inspiring professor! The seminar class was super easy and fun.
Professor Claassen Thrush is so caring and understanding. The assignments are also very straight forward and easy. 093 is a pass or fail class so as long as you do the work, you will pass.

Prof. Clarke is one of the most impactful professors I had at UCR. He's clearly very passionate about the material due to his personal connection as a Native person himself. He goes above and beyond to make the class engaging with Native foods, crafts, and events. I took this class simply for the units but left with a new perspective. TY professor!

He seemed like a cool person but he had a horrible structure of the class. He wanted people to show up even though attendance wasn't mandatory. He would change the grading criteria and the few assignments we did have lacked clarity and structure. I will say, we did learn a lot and and the topics we covered were very important

Professor doesn't care about grades because they are a "capitalist construct". He couldn't care less about your success and grades no matter how it impacts your future. He changed the grading scale at week 10 without any warning. The TA's were unnecessarily harsh about grading and even threatened to lower our scores if we asked for a regrade.

He's a decent professor; however, for a prerequisite class this was one of the hardest As I've had to work for. Doesn't have a clear grading scale on the first day of class, and changed it up on week 10. TAs grade your research paper with a strict rubric. He doesn't upload lecture notes as "incentive" to attend lecture.

Professor Clarke is awesome, one of the best professors I've taken. His lectures are really interesting and he has a great sense of humor. If you show up and do the assignments, you will pass. I wish I could take more of his classes. He is really awesome!!

Such a caring professor and I cannot recommend him enough. Sadly cut a bit short due to the strike, but he was in total support which demonstrates the type of professor he is. Extremely passionate about the subject and made the class extremely enjoyable. One of my favorite classes and favorite professors at UCR.

Professor Clarke was so inspirational and amazing to listen to. He cares so much about his students, so plz attend lectures or he gets kinda upset. This class didn't feel like a class, but rather speeches you would listen to and really take in. We had assignments here and there which weren't bad at all. No exams, just a final. Definitely take him!!

Great professor who cares about his students. Barely any homework so its a good class to take if you have a heavy workload. Online lectures and is accommodating. Had Bianca as TA, she's good. One test (final) that was an open-note 2/3 pg essay. Prof's main goal is to teach you to see race and ethnicity in your daily life. Would recommend!

Clarke is an AMAZING professor. He shows so much passion for the subject and such a willingness to understand his students. He is truly a gem among the UCR faculty. I took this class through Zoom which I think allowed for the lecture to be much more engaging through the chat. I'm grateful that I took this class and got to be his student!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Clarke is one of the best professors you can get, he is very understanding and cares about his students. Lectures are always interesting and gives you the pdfs to do the homework. Would definitely take this professor again!

Really chill class, the professor is an amazing and passionate speaker who really enjoys the material. few disc. 1 paper and a final. If you attend his lectures, which you should even though its not mandatory since the class is so chill, you will definitely get a good grade. Take him, you will learn a lot, and did I mention it's such a chill class?

I would take this class again in a heartbeat. The professor definitely had so many interesting lectures when I did attend class. There is a midterm book report but you were given notice and clear instruction almost 2 months ahead of time. If you do your work you will pass. And if you go to class the final should be a piece of cake!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Really good speaker and you can tell is really passionate about the subject. Very fun lectures that you don't need to attend but I encourage you to. A few discussions, a paper that weren't too bad. Finals also doesn't seem bad, a few essay questions about the material. If you have 2 hard classes and want a chill class, I highly recommend this.
Gerald is by far the best professor I have yet to interact with at UCR. He is caring, genuine, and provides everything a student could need to learn.

This class was pretty easy, with a few discussion posts, a film review, and a fair research paper. He gives the assignments in advance, so it allows the opportunity to work on them. He records the lectures, so you don't have to attend, but discussions are pretty important for attendance. Overall it was a pretty interesting class and an easy A.

Professor Clarke has amazing insight and wonderful stories. I genuinely enjoy showing up to class every week. He has an uncanny ability to see the content of his classes from multiple angles and it gives students something to think on . He encourages students to have their own voice, which in an academic setting is often the most difficult part .

Class is a guaranteed A. Just write your research paper in with his viewpoints (even if you don't believe them) I got 100% on it literally... LOTS of extra credit too. I got a 70 on the final and I got a 95% at the end of it all.

He's a cool guy and professor. Make sure you do all of the assignments and readings - will be important for the final. I recommend paying attention in lectures but you don't really need to take notes. He'll post lecture slides at the end of the quarter so you can study. Final exam has trick questions so details are pretty important.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: You will definitely learn new things that you thought you knew, but really didn't after taking this class. Very easy going, approachable, and is open to hear everyone's opinions on the topics he teaches. No midterm exam, one research paper, and a cummilative Final. Make sure to do the readings!

This class was the most memorable class I have taken at UCR. Prof Clark truly cares about his students and the content of this class which makes him amazing. As long as you show up to class and the field trips you are pretty much guaranteed an A in the class. Would highly recommend anyone that is interested in animals and keeping GPA high

Professor Clark is one of the best professors I have ever taken at UCR. I recommend any Biology Major (Pre-Health) to take Professor Clark's course. Professor Clark hates quizzes and exams and will base your grade mainly off of field trips. He is one of the most genuine and passionate professor's I have ever had. Highly recommend for 163.

This class went well despite having to be taught online. Yes, there is work. You have to show up, do your assignments, etc. Care and youll get an A. It was taught well and graded with students in mind (open note to avoid disadvantaging students). Format may change in person, but I think that the quality of teaching will be great no matter what.

Attendance required since whatever he writes on the board  on the exams. Material is easy to learn + tests are memorization from the notes on the board, not too much the slides. Is approachable & lectures are entertaining. Practicals in lab are a lot of memorization too. Field trips required but fun. I have more respect for nature now.

Clark is the best professor I have ever taken! The class is straightforward, anything he writes on the board is fair game for the exams. The field trips are fun and worth taking the class. Start early on the final project and definitely put in the work for the practicals. I would 100% take the class again, best class I have ever taken!

Dr. Clark is an amazing professor! Please don't let the syllabus intimidate you, it was honestly so fun; the field trips help you learn what you learn in class into the natural world. Yes, there is a lot of work, but the subject is so interesting and engaging. Dr. Clark loves teaching this class, and cares about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Clark is the best professor ever! He is very passionate about the subject & his enthusiasm makes class fun. This class was one I always looked forward in going to, and the field trips are definitely the best part. Dont let lab or the amount of work discourage you from taking this class, everything is straightforward. 11/10 would recommend

Dr. Clark is by far the best professor I have had at UCR. I looked forward to lecture and the Saturday field trips every time since they were so much fun! I learned so much from him about wildlife and to appreciate it. I tell everyone to take biol163 now. Clark is easy to understand and he helps you out in ways that make sure you learn. Funny too!

Dr. Clark was my favorite professor at UCR! The best part about this class is that he is so passionate about what he does, and so he really does care about you learning the information. All lectures are handwritten notes so you have to show up! Dont let the amount of work or schedule intimidate you! The class is super fun and straightforward.

Clark is the BEST proffesor at UCR!! He gives you so many facets to absorb knowledge: slides, written notes, vids, reviews & office hours! He offers letters of rec to ALL BIOL163 students! He definitely sets you out to succeed and broaden your mind! Beware, on his exams managing time and comprehensive answers are key. I got As in both his courses.

Must go to class because he does hand written notes. Occasionally makes mistakes in his notes. Has absolutely no clue on how to write tests. As in you can know the given material front and back and still come out with a C out the exam. FACT.

Lecture and information heavy, but he is a great storyteller. He really makes you want to get involved with the information at hand. During lectures he wont have slides or anything up other than his face, which makes it kind of hard to follow. He has amazing TAs, overall a pretty lax course.
I absolutely love Trafzer. He is a big storyteller but somehow is able to relate back to the lecture( not boring). There are 2 book precis, 2 exams and a final. He also has great TA's

Very good professor! But make sure to really pay attention to what he says during lecture because his PowerPoints are not well-detailed, more like an outline. A lot of talking of his experiences and of people he knows. Quite lengthy but you learn so much. Definitely has a passion for what he teaches. Good person and caring of others. Cool dude :)

AMAZING professor and amazing man. I recommend everyone taking at least one of his classes. It surely was a pleasure being able to be apart of his Native American History class my first quarter at UCR. He was really great, understanding, and made information easier to understand. HIGHLY recommend.

He's a great professor. Very passionate about Native American history and lectures are funny and entertaining. No final just 3 midterms which consists of two parts, a take home 3 pg paper and simple multiple choice section (20 questions). Easy and fun class. He made us give him a standing ovation so he could win a bet with his wife, it was funny

Spectacular professor, really cares about his students and uses different strategies to keep us entertained.  Even brought in native americans to tell us stories! He's extremely passionate and his lectures are like story time.  2 tests, one 7-10 page paper the TA's are helpful with. (Kevin Whalen is the good TA).  Highly recommend this class.

Professor Trafzer is a wonderful person with a great sense of humor.  He will improve your writing tremendously as he did with many students.  His grading is very reasonable as long as you follow his guidelines.
He is an awesome teacher!!! Very helpful and always open for discussion!!!
A good guy, very helpful.

the best hist prof i've ever had by far. doesnt play games and is really straight forward and real. passionate about what he teaches. he teaches oral history which is much different that mainstream written history. i love his class!

Cliff was my advisor throughout undergrad and grad school.  He is a really good egg with the metabolism of a hummingbird and an almost obsessive desire to help his students.  If you want to learn about oral history, he's your man.  If you want to go into NA history, go talk to him.  My writing improved enormously because of his red marks on my papers.  He is active with local tribes and on the NA Heritage Commission.  He publishes a bazillion books a year and is helpful when you want to publish.
He's a great professor.  Very straight forward lectures and tests.  Learned a lot from him.
Absolutely stellar professor.  If you take any Native American history classes, take them from this man.  Great sense of humor, too.
Best prof ever
Great professor, very enthusiastic about his teaching material! If you want to learn more about Native Americans take this course.
Great Prof! He's half Native American! Worth taking if you wanna learn about Native Americans!

Thinks her class is the most important class you are taking and assigns ridiculous amounts of work because of it. Outrageous attendance grading which doesn't allow for mental health breaks or colds, so clearly you must be absolute perfection. Or rich and go to the doctor for every sneeze to get a note. Does not stick to syllabus!!

She assigned a zoom presentation and I had to do it with my face being blurry because my camera was broke. I did all the work and turned in the recording with my face being a little blurry. She gave me a zero after I told her I didn't have a choice since she doesn't accept late work. I asked her about it and she wouldn't let me redo the assignment.

She is a great at teaching and helping you understand Spanish. She is also very passionate about the subject which will help you learn. However you need to work especially hard because her grading is often very harsh and sometimes too critical. If you dont miss class & or any HW assignments (there is a lot) you should be fine.

She is the best teacher I have had at UA! She really wants you to succeed in her class and she helps you as much as possible. The only thing that sucks is that she doesn't accept any late work and there is literally always homework but thats how every spanish teacher is going to be. GO TO EVERY CLASS! She rounded my grade up 2% so I'd get an A

If you have a good understanding of Spanish from Spn 1 and 2, then Spn 3 with Claudia isn't hard. But the class is not an easy A. You have to STUDY. Claudia by far has the worst reputation as the hardest Spanish teacher, but I loved her! the pele who don't like her expect an easy A and are surprised/pissed when she doesn't hand them out. if you are actually interested in learning Spanish, get Claudia! plus she's hot

I really didn't like whole point system bc it was unfair for students. Like you can only lose 20 points in order to keep an A  (25 for an -A) such sucks. reviews.comment: Really isn't as bad as everyone says. There's two midterms, one paper, and one final. Midterms weren't too hard as long as you took good notes and thoroughly went through them. I purchased all the books, but never opened one of them. Lectures provide enough information to pass the class. He did give off a rude vibe, but was overall pretty chill.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's honestly really rude. He doesn't care about his students and is very hands-off. His tests are hard and he doesn't tell you when he uploads the study guide or anything. Really depends on your TA. This class sucked.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: His lectures are amazing because he tells a story. YOU HAVE TO DO EVERY SINGLE READING and even though showing up to class isn't mandatory I suggest you do. His exams are extremely hard, so I suggest you study. Also, everyone saying he's chill, I feel like we had completely different experiences, he's extremely off-putting and rude one on one.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Hands down the chillest professor you'll ever have. He ends each lecture exactly on time, and still leaves enough time for questions throughout. Just show up, bring the laptop, and take notes. Class was easy, but effort is needed for an A.

Honestly, an easy class. Chrissanthos is like story-telling and is always entertaining. Just type your notes, don't write, as it will be hard to write down everything he says as he speaks. Both midterms were fair, short response/fill in the blank. The final was cumulative and essay-style. Just make sure you get a good TA as they grade everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Only take this class if you are good at listening and memorization. Professor Chrissanthos lectures the entire time without using any slides. Both the midterms are challenging since they are fill-in-the-blank and short-answer questions. The term paper is incredibly broad. Discussion attendance is mandatory. The final asks specific questions. Tough.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Do not buy the book. You won't need it. His lectures alone are sufficient enough. He talks slowly and in a story like fashion so it's easy to copy down everything he says. Do attend all lectures though.

He gives 2 midterms, 1 final & 1 paper (assigned on 1st day of class, can be on whatever topic of your choosing as long as its within the time frame of the material the class covers). He does not post lectures online so you need to go to lecture to know what is covered. Great instructor but you really need to put in the time in order to pass!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He's a great professor! Take your laptop to lecture, type everything he says (it's easy to do because he pauses between sentences so you can type), and do the study guides. This class is really easy if you just put in the effort. Don't be scared about the exams being free response and fill in the blank because it's a lot easier than you think.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Gives list of terms for both midterms and final. A lot of information to remember, midterms are full in the blank for a majority. If you get alice as a TA, youll get a good grade if you just show up. Attending lecture is a must.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: 2MTs, Final, 1 Paper, Discussion Mandatory. If you skip lecture you will fail. He insists you buy the two books because "you will need it for the tests." I never got the books though and did fine on the midterms. I'm waiting for my final grade atm. If you attend all lectures and use the quizlet SGs specifically made for his class, you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Seen as an easy A class but isn't really, you do have to study. There are 2 midterms , one term paper, and a comprehensive final. He posts a list of terms that you should memorize or at least be familiar with, as the exams are fill in the blank or completely free response. TA comes up with part of it and grades everything. You should go to lecture

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors. Really clear and I enjoyed going to his class.

reviews.comment: His lectures are a majority of the test(2 quizzes, midterm and final. Also one essay due at the end of semester)with some of the text book involved. You dont need to buy the sources book. Do his study guide & youll pass the class with an A. His lectures are just pictures and he tells you exactly what to write down.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Not much to add in my review. All the other reviews nailed it. Class felt more like story time. He doesn't hand out A's but it's very achievable. Show up to class, write down everything he says, which you can because he pauses after almost every sentence, and do the readings, which are interesting. Honestly one of the best professors at UCR.

reviews.comment: He is a great teacher, and his lectures are amazing. He tells them like stories instead of making you memorize dates and names. Overall good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: His lectures are captivating and reminded me why I came to college. I never even wanted to skip class, and I have no problem skipping others usually. 2 Fill in the blank/free response midterms. 1 paper. Short essays for the final. Put in the work and guaranteed A. It's worth it. Let the study guides guide your reading from his required texts.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Do all the reading and go to every class and you'll pass. If you don't do the reading you will not pass the class his tests in this course are heavily based on the readings. He's a great professor and I learned a lot.

reviews.comment: great lectures. test heavy. participation/discussion matter
