reviews.comment: Really cool person overall and had only a singular quiz all year. Our final was just on couple essay topics that we knew from doing projects on. He has fun and intriguing lectures the first day and even until the last day. Only problem I had was getting up early to go to class but that is really on me lol.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's literally one of the best if not the best professor. Great professor with a charming personality, if you pay attention in class you'll be fine. Available even outside of office hours. His class is very fun and he's very knowledgeable and knows what he's taking about, you will have a solid base for every air pollution class you will take! GOAT

had him for an honors seminar so i cant attest to how he might be in a larger more traditional class, but i really enjoyed his teaching. was generally very relaxed and willing to engage, allowed us to choose the course of the class and expanded on our interests. would def b open to taking one of his reg classes

As a freshman I think this professor was very welcoming and made me feel like I belonged in college. Although there was a couple of essays it wasn't impossible to pass. Would take his class again, kind of sad that the quarter is ending because this was my favorite professor )):

An amazing professor that really cares about what he's teaching. He asks for a lot of participation, but he doesn't put someone down for giving an incorrect answer and explains how what the person said makes sense, even if it isn't correct. I would definitely take another class with him again.
Pure awesomeness

Cocker is a great professor. He really wants his students to do well in his class. His office hours are very helpful; he usually stays for another hour after office hours. His exams can be challenging,but he grades fairly.
Great Professor to work with. One of the coolest among whole chemical and environmental engineering department.

This guy is alright except he is 5% in the Environemental lab and then suddenly walks in to annilate everything the TA has said for the last 60 minutes. Take his class but not the lab if you have a choice.
Great professor.  He really takes the time to work with students in the class and lab.  Cool guy to hang out with too.

The professor does not give clear instructions on papers, including the critical reflections and final essay, which does not help at all. There is no true structure to assignments. Also makes you buy his book, which I did not do. For an online class, it is not well structured. Don't take this class or just any of his classes.

reviews.comment: Not a good professor! Makes you pay for the book he wrote, and it does not have clear instructions. Everything is super confusing and never clear.
hes lowkey hard for an easy class... chilllll

The class consisted of Twitter & discussion posts/replies every week, 2-page assignments every other week, a midterm quiz, & final 5-page paper. My only dislike was the class being uninteresting and having to post replies on different days. Overall, was easy to pass as I think the TA graded based on completion rather than reading assignments.

reviews.comment: He seems nice/accommodating, but is also a "no excuses" type person in terms of class content. Grade hinges on final, final paper, and discussions with busy work in between.

reviews.comment: Get ready to write, a lot. reviews.comment: I took him b/c he guest lectured in another class but he wasn't as interesting in his own class. I swear he just uses his class for his student's research. If you're thinking about taking a class with this prof. please don't. It's not worth it at all. Didn't accommodate the class for his students due to the pandemic until a bunch of students mass emailed him. Didn't want to accommodate again during this social movement and barely changed his mind once students mass emailed again and all TAs helped
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I hated it. It was a waste of time but it was online. He assigns so many chapters of reading OF HIS OWN BOOK. Definitely not a professor that wants to interact w/ students. The only time I asked 1 question, he was kinda rude. I would recommend any other elective course. Best way to describe the course: what you imagine an upper div to be.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was easy but you have a lot of unnecessary busy work. Like tweet, do reflection paper (2pages), discussion ( 150 words) and reply to them. All the assignments are super easy. 1 midterm 6-7 page essay for final. Midterm was super hard with 60 questions. He said it would be easy and no tricks he lied. I got a D but still got a B+.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dont take this class if you forget easily. A LOT of assignments for an online class. Every Tuesday by 12 PM you have to tweet. Every Wednesday at noon you have to post in a discussion board w/ a reply to a question on the weeks readings. Every thursday by 12 pm you need another tweet. And you also have to post in discussion 3 other different days.

I took this class because it was an online class. I was thinking that because it was online it wouldn't be a huge time commitment, but there was much more work than expected. Basically there was an assignment due every day which is unusual for any online class I have taken before. Not a hard class just be prepared to do a lot of busy work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Super easy class. I don't know why people are saying he's hard. Basically just tweet  (1 point) and the 2 page paper (2 points) every week and you're fine. I missed all the quizzes (1 point) and most of lecture and still passed with an A+. What he talks about in lecture is all in the readings and its repetitive, and you don't even need the book
Super dope class. Highly recommended

Super easy class. Reading assignments every week with a 2 pg paper due for discussion but it's nothing tough, just an analysis. Did not really show up for lectures but the materials and topics are easy to understand and grasp if you read. Final project is either a paper or video. Random quizzes. But passed with an A easily.

Good teacher! Not the easiest class because there is a good amount of reading, but more than that a 2pg paper each week. It is also important to keep on track with tweets and coming to class to be prepared for quizzes and tests. However, readings were not hard any neither was the class if you put effort in it.
Good class. Participation from students is important and the quizzes are reflected on how well the students discuss with each other
Dr. Comeaux is an excellent teacher. Very clear and engaging when it comes to his lectures. Do the assigned readings and you should get no less than a B in his class.

He teaches they way you are suppose to, engaged and active.  Luckily it was a topic I was interested in so I wanted to participate and work in the class. One of my favorite classes and teachers at UCR. Wish he taught more here.

Dr. Comoeaux is a very passionate individual about student athletes and ways to break barriers when it comes to certain stigmas. It is a great class that will help you learn a lot! Take this class!!! Won't disappoint!!!

The first day of class I thought this was going to be my most cool teacher of the quarter, and he was. He's funny, makes you think critically, analyze and contribute to class lectures. He is well prepared and does his best to remember students names.  You can do well with out purchasing the book as the readings are easy and clear. Great class!

Great professor! Very knowledgable. Work load is pretty moderate. Reading load isn't too bad, and it is interesting. He pushes you think rather than just speak your mind. It isn't an easy A, but it isn't a hard class if you just show up and keep up on the readings. He does give pop quizzes, but it is a fun class if you are engaged and involved.

Professor Comeaux is the perfect ex of what an educator should look like. He is dedicated and committed to helping his students in anything from in class work to outside of class with letters of rec. The class is easy if you participate & do the simple yet tedious tasked asked of you. For example we had to post on twitter each week. 1 post 1%pt

Eddie C is a great teacher!!! You have to do a lot of reading and 2page papers every week... The midterm is really hard If you don't do the reading... If you do the reading and come to class, you will find it very easy-This class is very rich with knowledge!!
He was alright.
interesting class, and learned a lot
His exams are difficult but the study guides he uploads are great and help with preparing. My issue is he speaks so monotone and at .5 speed it is difficult to stay focused.
Very good professor the best to ever to do it ever.
took summer class he was detailed and understandable. clear on exams and was lenient with curve

Decent professor. Lectures contain loads of information and anything from them can be asked. Tests on lots of little details and questions can be really specific and tricky. Knowing slides is a must as well as anything written on board. Does curve, which helps. You'll be talking about ion channels and action potentials 24/7. Try not to fall behind.

Lectures and material are fine but dont be fooled. Dont try asking to round up your grade even if youre as little as .3% away from the cut off as he will say theres nothing he can do and he wont change his grading for one student. Wastes your time trying to seem reasonable by asking you to check if he can give any points back but he wont

I took him this summer. He was very considerate considering its a summer class, online, through COVID. He was soooo understanding and kind. Class was about ion channels, action potentials, resting membrane potentials, synaptic Transmission, sensory neurons and two more topics. We had 2 midterms and a cumulative final.
Basically everything you write down from notes will be in the tests. If you truly study what's on the slides (some pictures, mostly words) you will do fine on the tests.

Taking CBNS120L over the summer with him was amazing. He is a funny professor that assisted with all the labs we had. It was quite difficult to get somethings to work, and he managed to help all the lab stations. I would love to take another class with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This is a very time intensive lab that should be a 4 unit class. I would not recommend taking this class with CBNS 124 during the summer (another time intensive class to study for). Make sure to write your lab reports by what your TA is looking for - they grade your labs. Lab write-ups take a lot of time so start early. Note: Nathan is the best TA.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--SO MANY PAPERS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Best neuroscience prof. Professor Currie teaches the material really well and is very approachable if you have any questions. The exams were multiple choice and free response - fr portion is harder so make sure you really understand major concepts, how to use equations, etc. Study and memorize slides to do well in discussion quizzes and exams.

This course is basically 106 but in greater depth. Professor Currie is passionate about neuroscience and even gives supplemental material. He is a bit soft-spoken, so I recommend sitting in the front. He is fair, reasonable, and gives a nice curve. If you put in the time and effort, you will earn the grade you deserve.

Way too much information is poured at you, seemingly in random order. Lecture slides have chart after chart and graph after graph. Lecture is a must. Tons of lists and names and obscure information that you will be tested on. Rarely touch on big picture topics or deep dive into good information. Tests are hard, with 5-6 option  multiple choice.

Don't bother reading the textbook. For the exams, study anything he mentions. Record the lectures if you have to. Very nice and always clarifies anything. Great demos (loved the saw one). Very funny. Don't worry about experiments till the final. If he spends a lot of time on something (and draws it on the board) study it. Nice curve
Very good professor but the material itself is quite dense.

He is AWESOME. Really engaging lectures that make you actually want to attend.  He is really passionate about what he is teaching and loves teaching which makes for a really fun classroom experience ( using a saw to explain frequency? Genius!)

The midterm and final were harder than what was expected, and not really related to the learned material (especially for the final). As long as you do decent in hw and lab you'll get a good grade. She gave a MASSIVE curve because the final had really low grades.

Professor Cui did a decent job for her first quarter teaching in-person this course. Her slides were organized and stayed punctual with due dates/announcements. However, her exams didn't align to the assignments which may have caused the average scores to be low, but she atoned for this by curving the distribution of overall scores. She'll improve.

The material in this class hard but the lecture slides have most of the information.  The homework was a lot harder than the tests and take some time so start a head. Attendance doesnt matter but she does some easy to find polls during lectures. She gave a FAT CURVE that brought my final grade from a D- to and A. Shes really good on communication.

Funny guy. Solid class. Wasn't that hard but you do have to actually study and pay attention to do well. There are "pop quizzes" but its really just on the in class topics he teaches us that day and he only keeps the top 5 best scores.

I'm a Junior at UCR and Joseph is literally the worst prof I've taken. He gives surprise quizzes all the time and besides being very awkward, he will not show any care for students. He gets off topic a lot so be prepared to teach yourself the whole course.

It is an enjoyable class with a straightforward professor who gives good lectures. Although attendance isn't mandatory, it does help to show up as he explains things well. Get ready to use Excel for the problem sets. Midterm and final test on understanding of the concepts (almost no math), which I appreciated. Overall, great professor and class!

1 midterm, 1 final, 2 homeworks, 2 small writing assignemnts, 2 pretest quizzes
pre test quizzes have questions just like test. If you show up to class and pay attention youll be just fine. Homeworks are pretty easy just dont wait too long to start them since its on excel. Very funny guy but jokes don't always hit (tough crowd)
If you show up to lecture it shouldn't be too bad, the class consists of two homework two practice quizzes and two exam with a decent amount of extra credit.

Was nice and had good lectures, clearly enjoys the topic. He tries being funny, which is difficult when we are talking about mass starvation and poverty. Very few assignments, but also he gives extra credit that can be worth up to like 5%
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: i LOVED Prof. Cummins. Took him for a developmental econ class and he is one of my favorite professors I have taken a class with. Very friendly with students, incredibly interested in the work he is teaching about, and overall seems like a good guy. The homework is not too hard and he provided supplemental videos that helped solve it.

Professor Cummins is an amazing professor! He makes lectures interesting. He curved all tests. There was 1 homework due each work, but instructions are clear. He is very understanding of students situations. He actually wants all his students to do their best.

He's really interesting and you can tell he enjoys econ. The exams are based off of the lectures, and if you hate going to lecture he posts all the slides online! You do have to put in work but if you're an econ major you'll enjoy it. Oh, and he curves!

Never take this class! The test is real heavy, and none of the material is useful in the class ppt. THE Exams are all lots of long and short answer questions!The homework and lecture material will not help your test too much. Homework is in group, However you have to write individual form for group work !them just stick all teams' paper together

This class is easy, just pay attention. If you pay attention in class and have basic problem solving skills, his exams are a piece of cake. Don't underestimate the homeworks or the paper though. You can't just do them the night before, they take a lot of work and thought. Start on them early. But I can't exaggerate how easy the exams were.

He was pretty good. His homework is kind of open ended and you're kind of left to figure out on your own but he explains things pretty clearly and as a whole I did enjoy his Econ 193A and ECON181 class.

His Econ Development class was very enjoyable! He's very knowledgeable of the subject and does a great job of keeping you interested in the subject. If you study well enough, his tests are not too difficult, and he is a very fair grader. His homework assignments can be time consuming if you are not proficient at Microsoft Excel.

Professor Curras-Collazo is an effective lecturer. She posts video lectures, which are helpful for  clarifying difficult concepts. While the course content is dense, it is manageable if you stay on top of the readings. Her commitment to student success is evident, and with consistent effort, you can do well in the course.

This class is awesome! Implementing questions in lecture videos helped keep me on task and I found myself to actively learn the material. If you plan to take anatomy, I highly recommend taking this course. This course may seem to be harder to understand in an online format, however the lecture videos and slides were very concise and in depth.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
So Dr. Collazo is awesome. She cares about her students and responds to emails promptly.

Its an upper div neuro so its not a cake walk, but if you pace yourself its a very fair class. Her exams are a little hard but its balanced out since 40% of the grade is "free" points. If u know how to use Anki/Quizlet to make flashcards, you will do good.

I didn't think this course was any harder than any other neuro course. If you do poorly at the end then you probably didn't put in the time required for most college classes. The flexible schedule of online lectures let me self-pace myself and staying on track is pretty manageable as most lectures are only 20-30 min. Also never skip discussions!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Curras-Collazo is a wonderful professor. She's caring and available to answer questions in office hours, by email, and canvas discussion board. The material was well organized, and the online format helped learn according to my own schedule. Overall, this has been my favorite course at UCR. I highly recommend taking it with Dr. Curras-Collazo.
She is rude sometimes, and she doesn't prepare the material. Seems that she doesn't know much about neuro.

Professor Curras-Collazo is a great professor and truly cares for her students. I would highly recommend her for CBNS124 as she does her best. If anything, the material is a little difficult which should be expected for a third tier neuro upperdiv.
SHE is horrible and rude. Don't take her!

So help me god, this was my worst experience ever! She could not even write an email without typos! Exams were atrocious, she was not helpful at all, and the lectures were all asynchronous. I don't know who this professor thinks she is that she gets an exemption from doing her job, but UCR needs to fire her immediately. Trust me, avoid this monster

Professor Curras-Collazo is an effective lecturer. She posts video lectures, which are helpful for  clarifying difficult concepts. While the course content is dense and demanding, it is manageable if you stay on top of the readings. Her commitment to student success is evident, and with consistent effort, you can do well in the course.

This class was very informative but the exams were brutal. Studying the slides alone is not enough. Exams tested on material from the books and a lot of applied information. There is a lot of content tested on each exam, so be prepared for a lot of reading.

Professor Curras-Collazo is amazing! Lectures are detailed and well-organized. Exams are fair, and office hours are super helpful. Unstuck ai was a great study tool alongside the textbook. Highly recommend this class!

The online format of the course allowed me to sit down and watch lectures when it was best for me, with that being said, do not skip any of her lectures, her slides and her points in the videos are what will be on the exam. However, she does a good job of explaining everything, so just keep up with the soft deadlines and you'll be ok.

Prosser Curras-Collazo is a great mentor and professor. She cares for her students and only wants to see them succeed. The effort you put in is noticed. If you ever need mentorship in the academic world, she is one of the best professors to ask. She gives great guidance and has real-world experience, having expert knowledge in neuroscience.

Overall, she is an amazing professor! Very thorough lectures and a fare grader. Also recommend getting to know her because she is extremely nice and caring. If you have the chance to take her class, I highly recommend it!

Dr. Curras-Collazo was a great professor and provided excellent feedback on questions I would have. The slides are detailed and organized and cover the exams. The exams were also very fair. Although there is a lot of material, obtaining a good grade is possible. I found the material exciting and highly recommend it to anyone interested in neurology

Professor Curras-Collazo was an amazing professor. She taught us about her research, mainly focussing on how toxic chemicals affect us and where they can be found. Grading was simple, complete the assignments, participate in class discussion, and write a good 10-page final essay.  Great class would love to have this professor again in the future.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Curras-Collazo is one of the best faculty members UCR has. If you have a chance to get to know her she provides great advice on life and becoming a great scientist. She always looks for the best in students and shows compassion. One of the best professors UCR has to offer. I recommend taking a course with her if at all possible.

I think your success in this class depends on your learning style. The online format and the way the professor just reads off the slides were not conducive to my learning at all. There are also constant technical issues. I suggest taking other classes that teach similar material to prep for this because other profs may explain the topics better.

Dr. Curras-Collazo is available outside of class both through canvas and through email. She does a great job preparing you from exams. The lectures are recored and very detailed, the cases studies are questions often. Pay attention to the lectures and a good grade is achievable. The class is very well organized. I highly recommend this class.

I had an incredible learning experience auditing the course. The instructor's dedication, grading my work, and interactive elements transformed my experience. I wish I could officially enroll, but even auditing taught me so much. Looking forward to more neuroscience courses with them. Quizzes and interactive question were really helpful.

This class wasn't bad, the grading criteria was pretty well outlined throughout the course. If you have access to a decent wifi signal, a private space, and a modern laptop, you should be able to do everything in the course without any issue. The professor was also very caring about student's progress and accessible outside of the course as well.

Dr. Curras-Collazo does a great job of providing supplemental case studies to reinforce learned material. Her and her TA were very accessible and understood the nature of online classes. She has quizzes on the case studies so be ready to read, but if you read and pay attention to lectures, which are recorded, a good grade should be attainable.

reviews.comment: Dr. Curras-Collazo is a wonderful professor. She's caring and available to answer questions in office hours, by email, and canvas discussion board. The material was well organized, and the online format helped learn according to my own schedule. Overall, this has been my favorite course at UCR. I highly recommend taking it with Dr. Curras-Collazo.

This class is fully online which was intimidating at first but Professor Curras-Collazo is an amazing professor. She made the format of the class easy to follow and allowed us to watch lectures on our own time. The lecture embedded questions were extremely helpful for studying for exams. She is kind and was very helpful during her office hours.

I previously took CBNS 124 with her before I took this class and enjoyed both courses. She makes the information easy to understand. Exams are content heavy on all from the lecture slides and case studies gone over in discussion sections, make sure to review her past exams and midterm reviews since she often reuses questions!

CBNS129 was one of my favorite classes taken at UCR! Professor Curras-Collazo does an excellent job in explaining the human body and its various autonomic and somatic connections and is supportive in answering questions about the material. Taking well detailed notes and participating in class discussion will allow you too to succeed in her class!

Professor Curras-Collazo is a great lecturer and a kind and compassionate professor. She really wants her students to succeed and adds in case studies and guest lecturers to supplement the coursework. She is kind in answering questions about the material and very approachable during office hours. I would highly recommend taking her class!

Dr. Curras-Collazo became one of my favorite professors at UCR after attending just a few lectures. After taking her CBNS 124 course, I made sure to sign up for her CBNS 129 course the following year. She is willing to support students in their desired careers by giving top-tier advice and writing letter of recommendation to those who put in work.

She cares a lot about the education of her students is very helpful and willing to make time to meet with students. It is not the easiest, but the benefit of understanding foundational material provided in this class provides knowledge that will take you into graduate studies.
She is rude sometimes, and she doesn't prepare the material. Seems that she doesn't know much about neuro.

Dr. Curras-Collazo is a wonderful instructor. She knows the material and is able to present it in a way that we students can understand. The material is hard- there's no getting around it, but if you put in the work and reach out, you'll be fine. The people here saying she's lazy probably didn't put in enough work on their end

Professor Curras-Collazo is probably the best neuroscience professor I have had in UCR. Yes, the material can be daunting. However, she organizes the material in such way that all that is needed to excel is to watch every video and complete the homework assignments. Plus, her practice exams are conceptually identical to the midterms and final.

In the age of the pandemic, Prof. Curras-Collazo has risen to the occasion. She has set up her class to provide as much transparency and material to the students as possible. Every module was available Day 1. Every point listed in the Calendar Day 1. To do well, Students need only to reach out and take advantage of the resources she provides.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Curras-Collazo truly cares about her students and will do her best to accommodate you if you reach out to her. Her class is pretty fair and straightfoward and I would recommend taking CBNS124 with her.
Laziest professor I have ever see! Awful!

Dr. Curras-Collazos feedback was extremely helpful in developing my presentation skills. She was extremely caring, and she even took the time to meet with us individually to further discuss how we could further improve our presentations. I truly believe that my presenting has greatly benefited from having taken this class!

Professor Curras-Collazo is one of the best professors that I have had. Not only did this class instill great fundamentals of Neuroscience, but also taught me how to approach studying in other disciplines. I still apply the methods we used to study sensory pathways to further my knowledge in kinesiology for PT. Great class, highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class was terrible. There was no interaction AT ALL between student and professor. The online lecture videos had embedded questions which were helpful however you can only watch the video once which made it difficult to study for exams. The slides were word-heavy and the tests were extremely difficult.

I waited to write this review for some time. Looking back, Dr. Curras-Collazo is passionate about teaching neuroscience. She had some trouble with organization and making sure she shared the right set of slides, but her slides were straightforward. I found her OH very helpful and she really tries to be there for her students.
Subject is challenging and professor does not help with understanding the topic.

This class was discouraging, excessive at times, and the little regard/assistance we were given as students, particularly technical assistance, was concerning ever since we began this class. If you can take another professor for CBNS124, I highly suggest making that decision.

Such an amazing person to be ending my college career with. Seems people in her classes early last year did not bother reaching out to her, as she has been so caring and there to work with me. Super sweet, passionate about the material, happy to clarify/explain further in both class/office hours. Hard class in terms of material, but that's CBNS129!

I enjoyed the class a lot. We did case studies in the discussion section which provided real-life examples of the things learned in the lecture. The material is very interesting and professor Collazo made it easier to understand. She is available during office hours which I would highly recommend going to. She is very accommodating to students.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The class was online during the pandemic and professor Curras-Collazo made it very manageable. I loved the format of the class. It had pre-recorded lectures with questions in between which made it easier to understand the material. She is very helpful during office hours and the exams are similar to the practice exams she posts.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: One of my favorite classes by far. Not going to lie this class is not easy. Collazo is one of the professors that is willing to go into detail to help you understand the material. She gave us a lot of help and was willing to accommodate us during this pandemic. Don't cram for the tests because there is a lot of content to know. Would take again.

I enjoyed my time being in her class. The test were pretty hard for me, but I felt like all of the test were still fair. Everything in the lectures were on the test so I feel like good note taking could of helped me out.

I've taken CBNS124 and 129 with Dr. Curras-Collazo. Her lectures are really detailed but interesting. I still remember information from her lectures to this day. She is incredibly helpful during office hours and really cares if you understand the material. Make use of her office hours! She truly cares about her students and wants them to succeed.

Not an easy class, but CBNS 129 is tough material & you do NOT want someone who makes this (or other CBNS) easy. Does a great job in lecturing , and her knowledge is immense. Make sure you've taken the pre-req's and study plenty! Exams are a time-crunch, so make sure you know the material well & read carefully. Willing to drop Q's & gives much EC.

Professor Curras-Collazo is a great professor. She cares about her students success and it shows both during her lectures and office hours. CBNS 129 is challenging, but by taking good notes and visiting office hours, getting an A is definitely possible. During COVID-19, she took the time to listen and accommodate her students.

Professor Curras-Collazo is by far one of the most supportive, caring professors I've had who truly wants all of her students to succeed, given that you work hard to consistently keep up with the material. She does an amazing job breaking down rather complex concepts in a way that is very easy to understand. I highly recommend taking her course!

Professor Curras-Collazo's class topics are very interesting and not too difficult to understand. However, if you feel like you are not really getting something, you need to show genuine care by asking questions during class, office hours, and email. The more you ask her and the more you explain the confusion, the better your performance will be.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I took CBNS120 with Dr. Curras-Collazo & she was able to break down complicated topics in a way that is easier to understand. Her lectures were always engaging & time felt like it flew by. I enjoyed her teaching style so much I took CBNS124 with her too. She is also very helpful during office hours, so don't hesitate to reach out to her for help.

There was A LOT of material covered throughout the course, but I guarantee you its worth taking the class. Dr. Collazo REALLY cares about your understanding of the material and makes it very clear what she will test you on. There are also well chosen case studies that you will read throughout the course that really help you understand the material.

Dr. Curras Collazo is by far one of the most educated and insightful professors in the Neuroscience Department. By no means is her class easy, but it will contribute to your future success. She genuinely cares, and her class will help you grow in the field for sure. I found CBNS129 particularly fascinating.

If you put in the effort to attend office hours and show up to class as well as study the homework she gives, you should do well in her class. Prof. Curras-Collazo shows a genuine concern for how well her students understand the material and is a fantastic lecturer. She provides detailed slides in lecture and clear explanations if you ask her.

If you carefully study & understand the slides & HW, & read the case studies, youll do fine. Some topics can be challenging but Prof. Curras-Collazo is really helpful in office hours and will make sure you get it. & if OHs dont work shes helped me thru piazza. She truly cares about her students learning, wellbeing, & success. One of the best.

The professor makes the course enjoyable and wants you to succeed. Review the slides & thoroughly understand the concepts highlighted in homework assignments. Use these as checkpoints & ask the prof about what you dont get during OH. Great course to establish your understanding of neuroscience, just the right amount of detail. Great for MCAT prep.

This is the 2nd class I've taken w/ her. I love her! Many people feel that the class is unfair but I think if you take the time and put in the effort there's no reason not to get an A. The material is dense but she wants everyone to succeed and is accessible in office hours and by email. If you're hard working and love neuroscience take this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Absolutely furious with this professor and this class. I went to check what I got on the final on iLearn and she had deleted the course from iLearn before anyone could even see scores. There's no way I can calculate my grade. I have a feeling she didn't even factor the final into grades because she's angry it was an online test. Awful! AWFUL!

Dr. Curras Collazo is an overall amazing professor and is very knowledgeable of the applications of neuroscience. She is very helpful in office hours and challenges you to expand your comprehension of the material in ways that are actually relevant outside of the class. Be sure to get to know her while you have the chance! The work is worth it.

This class has great material to present but this is the worst teacher possible. If you like a professor who is late and unavailable she is the professor for you. She only cares about her historical averages and will make you show up to class during the corona virus.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Like the person said its a doable class if she give us guidance but she putting 5 heavy lecture material plus 3 lectures from guest speakers that sucks all with out a ounce of guidance on this test She had us in a panic saying no practice midterm now until 5 day before the test she finally decided to post HW keyof 14 essay question & a few sample Q
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Alright, when she gives a practice midterm with the images we're supposed to label, the tests are very doable. However, when she doesn't do that, you're stuck in a panic over knowing what images to study and memorize. There's a lot of them. If you're going to give us an obscene amount of information to learn, you need to give us the study material.

Curras-Collazo is great! She wants everyone to do well in her class. Exams are MC, fill-in, and FR but the FR questions are the same as the homework questions she gives you a week before so there is no excuse to get those wrong. This class required effort + time; memorize and watch the lectures, ask questions if confused! Would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: One of the worse professors I think I have taken. I have never written a review about a prof but here I am on a weekend after Thanksgiving. All she does is read off her slides during her videos and her office hours are awful with nothing helpful mentioned. Her tests are incredibly long which makes them hard. Memorize her slides for the tests!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is one of my fave profs at UCR. I have taken two classes with her and this one was the best. I highly recommend it for pre-med neuro majors, the concepts are so medical. The exams are lecture heavy, make sure you understand each and every slide. Her office hours are really helpful. She really cares about her students and their progress.

Lectures are heavy, especially if longer than 1 hour. Learning objectives don't match exams; however, she does an excellent job at explaining topics she's passionate about. Expects you to memorize small details for Fill in the Blank portions on exams. No curve. Quizzes and Hw are easy. Lab is fun. Office hours helpful with great insight. Study Hard
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Constantly late,  extremely disorganized, she posts her power points and then adds and removes slides for the class but doesn't update them online. Don't take her classes if you can avoid them

This was my 2nd class with Dr. Collazo, she's honestly an amazing lecturer & a great person. I would recommend CBNS 129 to all neuro students & premed students as the materials we covered in this class was both very interesting and highly relevant to things you''ll need to know for MCAT. 129  introduced essential physiological and medical concepts.

Dr. Collazo is an amazing person. Her lectures are highly informative. If you enjoy a Neuro talk, you'll love them. Her slides are straight-forward; if you study all of them, you'll do good on exams. For 129, you'll need to read for the case studies. Go to her office hours, she's a very nice and helpful professor; and honestly one of my favorites.

I've had her for a few classes and she's not the best CBNS professor, however, she guides you to study the appropriate things. If you go to her office hours she'll sometimes tell you what she expects you to know or into how much depth you need to go. Study images, focus on what she emphasizes and ignore anything she briefly mentions.

I had one conversation with this woman in her office hours, and she pretty much crushed any hopes I ever had of working in her lab or enjoying any of her classes.  I felt like a pest to her, like she wanted me gone immediately.  She also said a pretty thoughtless and rude comment about undergraduate students to me; unprofessional and dismissive.
Absolutely horrible professor. Avoid as much as possible Please don't take these other warnings and comments lightly. She does not explain concepts well and merely reads off her powerpoints.

It is not required that you go to class. But if you take the time to go over the notes and the helpful diagrams in the notes you will do well in her class. You just need to study, as you should do in any class. Anything she emphasizes, especially right before an exam, will probably be on the exam.
Absolute worst professor at UCR. Will ruin your GPA. Do not take or you will regret.
Got the second highest grade in the class and really didn't try that hard. As long as you have an ounce of intelligence you will do fine, unlike these previous commenters
Ridiculously long and dense midterm. She doesn't seem to care if her students do well or understand the material.

SHE IS HORRIBLE! Her lectures are very boring and dry, but mandatory because she does clickers and in class quizzes. Her midterm and final were ridiculous! they both consisted of mult choice, fill in the blank, free response, calculations, put into order, labeling, and matching. she only teaches what she knows, and not what we need to know. avoid!
Horrible teacher. I have no idea how she is teaching still. Very disorganized bad part is she's the only one who teaches this course.
The worst teacher at Riverside. Try not to get stuck taking her classes.

The worst teacher I have ever had at UCR. DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS. Shes extremely unorganized,unapproachable, and puts her class on the back burner. She's too preoccupied with her other activities that she puts little effort into the class, yet has very high expectations of her students. No consistency or structre and ruled by her emotions.

Margarita tries really hard, but it just feels uninspired. Her lectures are pretty dry and she's a slide reader. A good professor should really insight you with the significance of the material, she just reads it off. Her exams seem pretty straight forward though. She was pretty helpful and friendly at office hours.

wow its sad to read all previous comments of like four years ago and notice that she is still the same unorganized and confusing. Its terrible that she was the only professor to teach this course because if anyone else would have taught it, it would have definitely been a way better experience.

She's a terrible lecturer, but you can't escape her lectures because clickers count as points. I don't know how she keeps getting to teach CBNS classes when she's the worst CBNS professor I've had. She assigns homework casually but grades it so hard and doesn't even give a guideline to what she wants. Pretends to care but doesn't.
She is incredibly unorganized and condescending. Doesn't reply to emails and grades homework without a rubric!
very hard to understand the material but she is not so helpful

Dr. Curras is an awesome professor and person. I've been through her several classes and was always impressed with her genuine desire to teach and tangible interest in students' success. I also worked in her lab, and would like to say that the time that i spent there helped me to lend in one of the best medical schools in a nation. Stick with her!

She is a good teacher. She won't test you anything she didn't cover in lecture notes even if its in the book. Tests are challenging but fair.Exams are straightforward. Just study the lecture notes and you'll be fine. She really cares about how students are doing and curves exams based on how well the class did.
Good class.  Just don't work in her lab.  You know who you guys are from the class of 2006.  Just remember the drama and wrath..hahahaha

Dr. Curras-Collazo was very helpful teacher, I used to stay after class and ask her particular questions about the lecture, she would patiently explain my questions and stay late after class. Although most people felt asleep in her class, I always paid attention because a lot of questions from the exam came from the lecture. Overall, she cares abou
6 high ratings in one dy after a spate of low ratings - think she might be rating herself?
This professor clearly knows what she is talking about

It was one of the most interesting classes at UCR. The materials in this class were very interesting and influenced my career decision. I remember that her lecture was clear and easy to follow, and she was a wonderful person and the most helpful teacher I've ever met.

This was a very interesting class. I highly recommend it to any science major. Tests were MC, free response, matching, and diagram labeling. Everything on the test was from lecture material and some reading. Always go to class because there are clicker questions. Discussions were great because we studied the anatomy of an actual human brain.

The class is good and very detail oriented. The professor was very helpful in office hours. Attending lectures and doing the study guide helped a lot in doing well on the exam. Just make sure to study all the diagrams, pictures, and figures that she used in her lectures.

By far the most interesting science class I have taken at UCR. The material helped me prepare for the MCAT and I recommend it to anyone considering the medical field. The class seemed hard at first, but by attending all the lectures and doing the reading, the tests should not be hard. The curve was generous too.

Despite having taken Dr. Curras-Collazo's class a few years ago, I am still grateful for the foundation I needed which helped me better understand neuroscience as it applys to medicine.  Having a neuroscience backround definitely helped at various points in my medical training.
I really enjoyed her class.  She is very knowledgeable.  Her style of teaching is very clear.   She also cares a great deal for student learning.  I had a wonderful experience in her class.

Tests are m.c., T/F, matching, ranking, and short answer but its easy if you pay attention and pick up the clues so go to class. Do the reading including captions for everything (pictures, diagrams, graphs). There is no text book but theres a reader and she follows it pretty well, nobody should be lost in this class

She is by far the most disorganized and unreasonable professors at UCR. She is a bit neurotic in what she demands and unfair because she doesn't teach either of the courses with the attention they deserve. It is a such a waste to pay for the courses and get a professor like her. Avoid her at all costs.
Unbelievably disorganized.  Shows up to class late.  Extremely unclear lectures and unhelpful explanations.  Exams were insanely long and questions were vague.
disorganized; yelled at students for asking too many questions; tries to use all available equipment in room and wastes time figuring out how to work the screen;

Awesome guy Wore a suit to lectures

To those saying that he is a tough grader, I don't think he is anymore. Maybe he's loosened up, but when I took the class in Winter 2016, he was a very relaxed teacher with a clear grading rubric. Follow the rubric and use his advice to write a college-level essay, and you'll get an A every time.
His essay grading are extremely tough. Very hard English professor.

the class was okay. essays were tough but not unmanageable. office hours helped, but not entirely. helped those who did not do the assigned work on the day of earn back points. pretty lenient about that & not turning in essays online in time.

WORSE ENG PROFF. He is a very cool guy, but he is one of the hardest graders i know. On top of that he didn't even teach the class, we had a lot of group work. very boring professor, but easy class. Your textbook is your lifeline and her final/midterm is based solely on her lectures so make sure you take good notes

She is a really caring professor who loves what she teaches. At times, she gets into what she's saying, and doesn't look up to see if students have questions, but that's no big deal. She's really cool, and brings food to class when discussing recipes in class. Good times! :-D
I was in her discussion section. Very easy grader. Just read and write a decent essay..
I did not like her. She had good notes but were had a lot of assignments.

She is one of the most helpful TAs I have ever had! She really wants you to pass...unlike other TAs that are there just to be there. She holds great review sessions and pretty much gives you what will be on the midterms. She also LOVES to talk about her fiance so she will go off topic for sure...but its kind of fun to take a break from stats
Anne was the best! Really GREAT TA, you have to take this class with Anne she will help you out:)

She is really helpful and nice! But there's a lof grammar hw and readings.
this professor grades on everything. her grading scale is unfair.

Her teaching style is hella stuck & she is a hard a$$ grader.  Looking at the big picture, I'm HAPPY that I file an absent & went to the jr. college when she failed me...SAVE LOTS OF MONEY & LEARN A LOT MORE COMPARED TO THIS PROFESSOR!
Gave out pretty large homework assignments everyday. Grading is fair. Not an easy or hard professor.
She gives out too much homework for a college english course.
grade really hard on the essays

She is a very good teacher. She assigns homework everyday, but its easy. She is helpful in office hours. She trys to get you to write your own ideas, by not telling you exactly what do to. I became a better writer because of her. Her class was interesting and she is very nice.

I took her class for Eng 1C. Seriously the worst english prof. I've had thus far. All my other professors we're helpful during office hours telling me what should I elaborate on she never did that. She leaves too much HW. And grades hard on the essays. NOT Recommended!!!
She's very nice - Homework everyday - Easy essays but grade them pretty hard - Can't seem to afford to miss any class - Books  are necessary

Prof Tuell's alright. She's nice enough and grades pretty easily on the homework and essay, so if you just do the readings/homework (which is everyday) and a decent job on the essays, you'll probably be fine.
She is very helpful and is always trying to get the class to talk. There was homework due every  time, but they're easy points. Shes a good teacher
She very easy but alot of hw like 2 hrs worth and very tough on essay but if your a good writter u will get a good grade
Assigns a lot of work for an english class (HW every class, about a page of writing usually). Grades sort of hard on the essays, but not too bad if you can write over a 10th grade level. I liked her.

Who'd have thought american history could be so fortuitous? I can say that everything I knew about sewing before this class was surprisingly inadequate. Your GPA will thank you - believe me, I received the medal of bravery.
easy class as long as you do all the homework and essays.
She give lots of work but I learn lots too.
SHE IS SO UNHELPFUL, SHE WILL ASSIGN YOU THOUSANDS OF WORK WHICH ARE UNNESSCARY. jUST THINK ABOUT THE AMOUNT OF YOUR DAILY HOMEWORK IS EQUVILENT TO AN ESSAY.
nice teacher, gives a lot of busy work. she grades fairly.

She is a very nice teacher; however, she assigns countless of homework everyday. Chem 111(Not Listed)

Each TA is ticked off and deducts points for different things. Worst part is some have unique requirements only specific to them and not stated anywhere AND are worth TONS of points. Only way to know is asking, but how would you know to even ask for that specific thing?

instead of memorizing how he solves stuff, figure out how to solve it yourself. study every day and really get the math down. easy class but too many of us procrastinated and didn't take advantage of the retakes. so don't do that. ochem tutor, OH, and SI helped so much.

I never went to class & discussion or even properly did homework and just used his review material which 100% reflected his exams. Just no, I studied so much just to get a really bad grade wtf.

reviews.comment: Davies is honestly really amazing as a person, but his expectations for grading are completely unrealistic, there's 6 problem sets and 3 midterms BUT he no longer curves (BS), instead there's a final that replaces your grade, basically the only way to pass the class is ace every midterm of ace the final, overall, tough class with no curve.

i literally studied so hard, and i didn't even do bad on the tests, he just sucks at being a professor. i also emailed him because there was a mistake on my test, and he didn't even have the decency to check it. also the midterms are hard af where even if u get one problem wrong it docks off like 10+ points. DON'T TAKE HIM

Crazy hard tests, but really push everyone's knowledge of the material. Derivation based and exam questions for the first two exams were pulled directly from the slides.... Professor Davies has a cool accent. So, that was nice. His lectures are very boring, though. He just annotates slides, so to be honest, if you missed class -- you didn't miss much. HUGE curve

reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He does offer extra credit, but if you see anything about him curving from previous sources, do not listen. Midterms are deathly hard, be sure to UNDERSTAND what you learned

First midterm was difficult and was nothing like the previous midterms. The 2nd midterm was copy paste from the practice offered and the average was 70s/100. The final was difficult as he took questions from the optional reading with the average being a 65/100. Room for extra credit but DOES NOT CURVE and DOES NOT ROUND GRADES. 41/195 people failed
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Reading the book should not be a determining factor for passing the class, as he SHOULD have ample material in his slides but does not. Take this course with a different professor if you can.  With how much we pay in tuition, you'd think professor Nelson would annotate his slides.  Most of the material in this course you'll have to teach yourself by reading the textbook.  Exams are astronomically harder than the quizzes and practice tests.

While he is super passionate about genetics, you cannot survive without the book. Posts previous test questions, but you MUST use them as a stepping stool rather than a carry through the tests (obviously). Extremely difficult, as even the TAs stated that the first midterm was difficult, but the second wasn't as bad. Best advice is to READ THE BOOK

I don't know if genetics is just a really difficult subject or if Dr Nelson just purposefully makes it more difficult. I always felt like there was a huge jump between the lecture material and the quizzes and exams, like we were supposed to know more than what we were taught. Really hard to study for this class

homework wasn't worth any points so if you're bad at tests, good luck. offered cheat sheet for exams but cheat sheet ended up useless regardless of what you put on it because big chance you're just gonna get it wrong. nelson seems like a nice guy, his class structure just wasn't for me.

Legitimately top 3 professors I've had in CNAS. Makes the subject matter clear, gives good examples, and reviews are really helpful. Tests are difficult since they're very conceptual and will be based on situations instead of just memorizing definitions, but he gives practice tests that help a lot and does more than enough to prepare students.

Definitely one of the best professors I've ever had! Clearly cares about his students considering how many extra credit opportunities were provided. He's also really funny, and makes genetics very enjoyable. he even gave us candy before the final! :) Caring, eloquent, intelligent, adept, etc - really, what more could u want from a professor?

Nelson is a great professor and genuinely cares about his students. the class was tough but there is definitely opportunity for everyone to get above a B+ imo. First midterm focus on lectures and hw problems, second midterm copy down literally every practice exam on your cheat sheet. 3 cheat sheets for the final.

Dr. Nelson was a great professor! He graded off of 7 discussion quizzes (1 dropped) and 3 tests. The tests were very fair and reflective of the practice exams and homework. This is a difficult class and requires extra work outside of lectures, but Nelson explains practice problems well and honestly the lectures are enough to get by.

You can tell Dr. Nelson genuinely loves genetics and that passion translates into his teaching and students' success. As long as you put in the hours, come to lectures, and take advantage of his resources, you're golden! He's a great lecturer and always explains concepts in a way that's easier to digest. Other peers I've talked to felt the same :)

Theres no way you can pass this class at all if you only watch the lectures and dont read the book or teach yourself. His lectures are useless, you only need them to know the topics on the test, the test are hard

Nelson is probably the best genetics professor u can take. It's a very difficult class, but it's doable if u put in the work. 4 exams but he drops 1. Weekly quizzes in discussion (don't worry too much about them). He gives EC as well. As long as u put in the work, u will be alright. Just don't slack!!!!

Wonderful professor. Exams are very reflective of the sample exams and the textbook problems. I would recommend purchasing the solutions manual for the textbook as it does not come with solutions. 

Very forgiving class as he drops one of the exams (he counts 3 out of 4). Meaning if you did good on the first three midterms, you can skip the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Pay attention to lecture slides. For the first midterm, do all of the hw book practices. For the second midterm, do all of the practice exams and review concepts in lecture. For the last, review lecture slides and rewatch lectures you are not sure about.

Honestly a very great instructor. He knows what he is talking about and is very engaging during lectures. Be sure to read the book, study previous exams, and practice. You will do great if you are setting aside time to study. Take him for genetics, as you will learn a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Nelson is definitely one of the best teachers I have ever had! The enthusiasm he has for the class made me excited to learn. His lectures are clear and easy to follow and I appreciated how he was always willing to explain something if you didn't understand. His exams were very fair too.

His tests were hard but being online they were all open book/note. Nelson is really nice and eager to answer any questions you have. Discussion wasn't mandatory. Do the readings before lecture and do his practice exams and you're set

loved this prof! really nice and cared for his students. listened to students feedback which is especially useful now w the pandemic! understood that tech problems would arise. great teacher and his exams were decent. assigned textbook readings were optional but helpful! he was funny and you can tell he cares for his students which i value a lot!

Prof. Nelson was a great teacher and one of the best science teachers I've had. Since I took him during corona, he recorded his lectures and I was able to view them as many times I needed. His test are a little difficult but fair. He offers a generous curve and drops your lowest test and midterm grade. He also offers extra credit. Take him!
I wouldnt recommend attending his lectures, not because theyre so useless, but because they will get you so confused as well! The book is your best and only friend in this class.

Professor Nelson is unable to convey the proper lecture material in class and is confusing. He also tends to run off on tangents that are not helpful to the class. His lecture slides he posts are just pictures with little text and he doesn't explain it clearly in class at all. 3 Midterms, 7 Quizzes. Best of luck, any other professor may be better.

He doesn't know how to teach properly; go home and study the material yourself in order to pass the class. Lectures are mainly pictures and if you don't understand them, the class will become hard. Lectures become extremely confusing over time. Best of luck as he made this class more confusing than it has to be.

Professor Nelson is a great professor and genuinely cares about his class. Regardless, genetics is a tough course and requires some effort. Professor Nelson curves the class pretty nicely and makes it possible to get an A. Overall very fair.

Beware of his exams! 3 midterms since the final is not cumulative, and 7 quizzes drops the lowest. I did all the homework and went to class every day and it was not enough. Youtube was my best friend for the whole quarter. I thought he was going to be a good professor, I was wrong. good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He's really good at teaching, at the end though he started to rush. The exams are pretty fair. I recommend for the first exam doing the homework problems he gives. He gives 3 midterms instead of 2 and one final. The quizzes are fair, the exams are fair too. Just make sure to study and do any material he gives as review. It helps a bunch.

Prof. Nelson genuinely loves the subject and makes class relatable and interesting. 100% of your grade is based on quizzes and exams and the exams are pretty hard, BUT he gives an EXTREMELY generous curve. He curves in a way that only the bottom 10% on the exams receive a D/F, so as long as you're not that 1/10 you will most likely pass the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Nelson is alright, office hours no good. However, I HIGHLY recommend TA HELP!! His exams are HARD!! Read the book and do the homework, trust me it helps! Read and make really good notes because sometimes he add things on his exam only said in lecture. Overall decent professor. And do outside research if book doesn't cover enough, trust me...
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Nelson is one of the few professors who genuinely cares about teaching. He always came prepared to lecture and discussed genetics with the big picture in mind by applying it to real world scenarios or modern research which I found to be interesting. The exams and quizzes were challenging but the class is curved generously.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Class is not super hard. Average is around a B-, but you NEED to read the book. Come to class to listen to what he says, and read it in the book to solidify the information. He is a super nice guy, and cares about his students. He loves genetics. 3 midterms, 1 news report, quizzes

Dr. Hinckley is a respectable instructor, but he is a tough grader. He allows for revisions of essays and gives good feedback WHEN YOU ASK FOR HELP (go to office hours/email him!). His lectures are laidback and can be boring if you do not find the topics interesting. Go to lectures regardless, because he takes attendance and has pop quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He really is a tough grader, but for good reason! His class is a lot of work, you're going to not only read the assigned texts, but also take notes and be able to critically analyze them thoroughly. Be prepared for a lot of work, this isn't an easy class. Definitely go to his office hours! One on one feedback will help improve your work drastically
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Some of the reviews are definitely biased towards their dislike of him but he's a great professor,a pretty tough grader when it comes to writing but is willing to meet up and give advice. A tip I would say is to be ATTENTIVE and TAKE NOTES in class.He notices and will remember you and put you in his good graces and be nicer to you when grading.

Professor Hinckley can definitely be controversial at times, he's a super tough grader (the kind that doesn't believe in giving A's) but if you read the novels and try your best to communicate with him you will do. He also was very flexible with deadlines and often extended them. Beware of many pop quizzes and he suspects everything to be ai.

stem majors WATCH OUT!! his lectures are so incoherent. his opinion of a "a really REALLY good essay" is a B-.  HE IS A TOUGH GRADER and has a strong opinion on words that you cannot use or you will get docked HELLA points. if you are taking him good luck, you will need it

reviews.comment: Tough but fair. good feedback and helped improve (Coming from not a good college writer but excelled in high school). reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Hinckley can be a tough grader but also helps you improve your writing. He always shows enthusiasm for his lectures and connects them to real-life examples so that we will be able to understand. He is super easy to get in touch with if you need help.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class
