reviews.comment: working with him outside class can help your grade bc he is an extremely tough grader on essays and will only boost your score (maybe) if he sees you putting forth your best effort. hardly gives out good grades and never puts anything in the grade book so you have to ask him if you want to know your grade

Professor Hinckley was nothing but nice but his grading and feedback were never consistent. If he doesn't agree with whatever you are writing about he will just give a tough grade with no feedback and is very nitpicky. He does go off on tangents and I don't think I actually learned anything other than accommodating myself to his expectations.

he is just an ok teacher. he likes to believe because he read the books he knows every single thing about the time and era, but does not. if you do not like a teacher who goes off on tangents every five seconds, he is not the teacher for you. four essays, one presentation. overall just ok.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: SHOW UP TO CLASS! He takes participation very seriously and is actively looking to give students extra credit so long as they participate and show that they're listening. Do all the work, including the rewrites, go to office hours, and show him you want a good grade. It'll help believe me. Nice guy, just talk to him and don't judge too quickly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Advice:
-Do the assigned reading - makes the discussions easier to understand
-Take notes on discussions - shows up on pop quizzes
-Email him for help on papers He gives specific feedback even over email
-GO TO HIS OFFICE HOURS If you bring him your work he will make edits/tell you how to improve
-Put in the effort and follow all instructions
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The amount of reading is acceptable, but never expect a high grade. The professor is humor and patient. Some people might think he talks too much out of topic, but I think this makes his classes relaxing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: If you're considering taking this class because you enjoy/are good at English, don't read any of the reviews below. If you suck at English then it's not really Hinckley's fault you got bad grades, was it? He gives plenty of feedback and opportunities to fix your grade so if you fail, that's on you. As long as you read (and care), you're good!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Absolutely awful professor. I've taken a couple English courses before this so I assumed I would do fine, but boy was I wrong. Essay are graded extremely harsh, barely giving any feedback, and he requires hard copies of your essays or he won't grade them at all. He does not care about the success of his student at all.

Professor Hinckley is a really tough grader, but gives a lot of opportunities to recover your grade. It should be noted that a lot of these assignments have deadlines near the end of the quarter, but even still they are doable.  He's understanding about deadlines and literally gave the entire class until the last day of the quarter to submit work.

Although the prof. does give a lot of reading assignments and is a difficult grader he does provide positive feedback on papers and has extra office hours to help his students. Focus on what he says during lectures as they help answer quizzes he gives and builds upon specific themes for the entire quarter. Only hw are readings & work on essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: David is by far the hardest grader Ive had w/ the Eng series. Dr. TMI (as he says) goes on tangents of his personal life and trys to relate it back to the discussion. Be prepared to read poems+2 books and if he isnt backed up on grading expect weekly quizzes on reading. Eng majors would prefer this class, but watch out stem majors.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Hinckley's class was definitely challenging, but I am sure most are capable of passing as long as you put in the effort. He's an entertaining person to listen to and he gives very flexible deadlines. Some may think he's a tough grader but honestly, the reality is most English professors are sadly. Hinckley is a good choice.

toughest grader Ive ever met and I think he does this just to mess w students. He doesnt care bout his students success, all he does is give bad grades w out telling you what to improve on. He told me that my last two essays were much improved from the first one I wrote and I somehow got a WORST grade. Makes no sense and he just needs to retire
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Highly recommend not taking his class... WORST TEACHER I HAVE EVER HAD... stay away and save yourself the stress from taking his course
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: He was the worst English teacher I have ever had. He tells me in office hours my essay is good then when he grades it he gives me a D. He did this multiple times. He doesnt care about his students and he shouldnt be teaching because all he does during class is talk about how much he hates trump. Screw this guy he from 63rd

tough grader but overall hes a great guy. if you want an A youre gonna have to work for it & he notices if youre trying or not. avoid doing the bare minimum and youll do fine in the class. show him you want an A and hell see your goals and work with you. super caring guy. i recommend unless u plan to be lazy all quarter

Hes a tough grader but also very willing to help you so go to office hours. His lectures are interesting just make sure you do the reading assigned so you can participate in class. He also posts some  comments on the readings in his course materials that offer a lot of insight so read those before lecture. Interesting class overall

very difficult grader!! what sold me was you can rewrite essays but there's literally no point as it won't bump you up much (3-5 points max) has too high of expectations and was only available to help via email!! we did not have a single zoom session, you're basically on your own! the book we have to read is soo boring! STAY AWAY bruh i warned you
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: PSA:Took him online for summer, spent the entire course "trying" to figure out zoom then gave up on it! 10 quizzes, 2 major essays, a research essay, final essay, and an exam! EXTREMELY DIFFICUlT grader, super harsh on every detail, you can rewrite essays but there's literally no point since the most you'll go up is 5 points DONTyou've been warned!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He gives good feedback, but his grading is unbarebly tough. Only 2-5 people get A's. You NEED to go to his office hours! He rambles a lot and many times it is quite questionable, but when we discussed course materials (books) he had many insights. This class would be better if he were more organized (syllabus came 2 weeks in + fixed 2 more times).
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This teacher was horrible. He did not help at all when it came to education and learning. All he does is go off-topic and grades your paper harshly. He has favorites too.

please drop out of this class. He is very unclear of what he lectures. He goes off-topic all the time, he's a really hard grader when it comes to essays, and I feel like I have learned nothing in his class the whole time.

Worst class ever taken!!! Hinkley is very disorganized in class; He just lectures the entire class going off on tangents that do not pertain to the subject at hand and talks about himself and his life too much. If you go to office hours and he doesn't like you analysis in an essay he will just change your topic.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Hinckley likes to go off on tangents, he talks about things you don't want to hear about. He's very nitpicky and tough grader. If you don't think you did as bad as he graded your paper, go to his office hours and ask him to regrade it. I don't recommend him because he's not good at teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Listen, there is no easy A when it comes to English. However, Hinckley is extremely helpful to students who care about their grade. If you really want to achieve an A in his class, he will help you. He allows you to revise almost every essay (besides the final essay). Which helps you hone your writing skills and improve your essay scores!

I really enjoyed 1B with Hinckley winter quarter, he grades fairly. If you write a poor paper in three hours the day it's due, expect a poor grade. He gives good feedback, especially in his office hours. You are allowed to rewrite papers to improve your scores. Hey may be mildly disorganized and ramble a bit, but he is entertaining, fair, and kind.

This class was a complete mess. He is disorganized, unclear about his expectations, hardly ever even at his office hours, changes schedules last minute, assigns everything in the last two weeks, doesnt teach, talks about completely unrelated topics, and grades ridiculously hard with little explanation as to why he graded it that way. Save yourself

Be prepared to hear all about things that are not relevant to the course, during lecture. He is really harsh on grading and handed out about 3 more essays than all the other 1B classes which was frustrating. He is unclear about what he wants in essays so I would suggest you go to office hours. Plus you're more likely to score higher if you go.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: If you're a lazy student, dont take his class. Here's how the first week of class goes: He'll tell you "people think my class is hard but it really isnt". He'll make sure you're very comfortable. Then week 2-6 will be very slowpaced, barely any deadlines. Then week 7-finals week, there'll be so many deadlines. Oh did I mention he is a tough grader.
Really difficult to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: It's extremely difficult to get a B, let alone an A, in his class. Students are expected to work extremely hard and hand in top notch essays in order for him to give out an 80 or better. He lets his students do rewrites, which means we have even more writing assigned to us. He takes attendance but simply talks to us about his life during lecture.

Tough grader but fair/thorough in his grading. Really makes you work for the grades. He makes it extremely clear that he hardly gives A's and his essay prompts were simple enough but make sure you have proper information and citations. Lectures are boring but sometimes he gives info helpful to essays and exams.
Grades hard on essays however gives good feedback and you're guaranteed a better grade after the first paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Doesn't teach--Period. He constantly talks about his personal life and stories that have nothing to do with class. He's a harsh grader, yet  does nothing to help us improve. I have friends taking the same class with different professors and they seem to be doing a lot better. Don't take his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: I had taken 2 other college English classes and got decent grades so I thought I would do well in Hinkley's class, but no. He grades super hard and just gives out C's and D's..

Most of the class was him talking about himself, he would often dismiss us early despite not really teaching anything, he doesn't post grades online, won't do online turn-ins but lost a student's papers multiple times, and the list goes on. Nice guy though- passed me, but I get the vibe he only did that so we didn't call him out on the other things
Ddint help at all. I needed help with an essay and he just rushed it because he had to leave. Talks too much about his personal life and barely even teaches.
Definitely a tough class just because he grades super hard. He would say I did well on my papers then give me a C or B.

He is a nice teacher, but tends to talk about his personal too much, so he might actually teach about 10% of the class. He sets very high expectations, your paper might be an A in another class, but here its maybe a D . I liked that we read Dracula, as I never had before. But other than that your going to wish you had an easier teacher.

In the first lecture he told us off the bat that he's a tough grader, so it was no surprise. He was a good professor. If you needed help he would always be available.  I personally liked his class. The only downer is that he doesn't post much on iLearn.

Hinckley is a tough grader! 1st paper I write I got a D. Fortunately, he allows re-writes so that helps a lot. If you want to do good in your paper, before you turn it in make sure you take it to ARC or something to get it revised. Other than that you can be a liked student especially if you incorporate what you know from other classes to his.
Constantly goes off topic. Tough grader. Unorganized (changes schedule frequently, missed one class without sending out an email, and left our in class writing assignment in his car).

He's nice but an extremely hard grader and expects a lot out of his students. Gives out a handful of essays but they're doable if you manage your time wisely. If I knew before, I would've switched professors because I know other students who did half the work I did just because they had a different professor. If you have him, change professors.

The professor makes it super hard to get an A. Why would you allow revisions, but take the average of the two grades. Makes it impossible to get an A. Also, I went to office hours like 4 times for one essay and he said it was a good paper. I get it back and it was a B+. He doesn't even tell you what he is exactly looking for in an essay. Don't take

Cool guy who talks about politics and his life stories most of the time. However he is a hard grader and expects spectacular essays to get an an A. Go to his office hours and he will help you out. Got points for just showing up....

Hinckley is by no means an easy grader. He's a good guy and you do learn a lot from his class, but getting an A is damn near impossible Worked my ass off and pulled a B when he said 90% of the class was in the C+ to B- range. Go to office hours, do your revisions, attend all the classes, actually put in some effort and you should be solid.

Do not take his class. He is disorganized, and he goes off topic frequently. I should have passed, but he lost my papers and did not grade them, so I have to take English 4 again. He is a nice person, but he is a terrible teacher.

DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS! For the whole hour and twenty minutes of class, we probably discussed English for ten minutes, he easily gets off topic. Also, he grades hard, will not give an A or B out. He contradicts himself when it comes to grading. Look for another English teacher.

I really enjoyed his class. I went to his office hours a lot and figured out more things and got a lot more out of our class by talking to him. He's super helpful and he really wants his students to come by.
I actually really liked him.  He was unorganized and got off topic easily and took forever to give papers back, but he was a very fair grader.  Attend class and you'll do fine.

He gets off topic a lot. We had to get the St.Martins but it's better if you grab the FREE PDF version because we used once or twice in class. He has four essays. If you want a higher grade I really recommend going to his office hours and having him correct your essay. That way he'll remember you.  Go to class even if you learn nothing.
pretty easy overall. gets off topic a bit, but its not an issue considering there are only 4 writing assignments all quarter and the quizzes are passable without doing any of the reading

He gets off topic a WHOLE lot! He doesnt very much teach, all he does is rant about stuff. He seems nice at first but he grades HARD! Waste of money for the books too! we hardly used them. He isn't organized, i would suggest you not take him.

Very easy class. Kind of irritated that the St. Martin's Guide was "mandatory" but we may have used a handful of times - waste of $. On the other hand, he allows a lot of revisions & is always helpful during office hours. The papers were very easy & there are a lot of chances for extra credit.
Whatever you do, do NOT take him.He does not teach what so ever. His grading system makes no sense. He only passed 2 people out of 23 when I had him. STAY AWAY from him!
this professor sucks! he is cool at first, but does not help! Even going to office hours isnt enough! DONT GET HIM!
GREAT teacher. Yes, he does talk a lot but most of his stories are very entertaining. He is understanding and not a hard grader. One of the best professors I've had.

attendance is mandatory! avoid if you dont attend class. he takes roll often. FAVORITE teacher at ucr. he tends to talk most of the time so you just chill and listen. he teaches life lessons from whats learned in his class. he's very down to earth and very fair on grading. do your essay revisions for good grades! he is funny take him!

I have no idea how he grades what he grade. He doesn't post grades online so you have no idea what you have either. So I was suprised to find out that I received a C+ when I SHOULD have had an A before leaving for winter break. Don't take his class because you won't learn anything and it won't help your grade either.

he is horrible. he doesn't keep his word and he doesn't know how to teach. in class, he talks about what he wants and always run out of time. he delays things at the begining of the quarter and cramp everything at the end. he would say you don't need to agree with him on some stuffs but trust me, i learned it the hard way. just agree with him, if n

I thought it was supposed to be about literature, but every class would have LONG boring talks about politics, conservative this, liberal that...HORRIBLE! and he was USELESS in office hours. went to get help w/ essay, and when it came to turn it in, he was like: this is unclear...seriously?! couldn't say that in Office hours?!

Fun lecturer to be around, but doesn't explain what he wants well enough. He could give you a prompt but you'd be confused as hell unless you go to office hours prior to finishing your essays. Tends to ramble during class when the time could be used for working on stuff. In 1B, the way he grades is strange and irregular. Ok teacher.
Good teacher. Funny but a little unorganized. I thought he was easy on grading. I got pretty good grades.

funny man. bad teacher. will help analyze stores but doesnt help with writing. he has a set way of explaining stories and if you don't write up to his expectations you will fail. felt defeated from this class

Professor Hinckley has a tendency to ramble off topic in class a lot, but then again that might be a good thing since you dont do much work in class. BUT he still grades essays really really hard, but if you show up enough in office hours, he will definitely help you a lot. So don't take his class if you suck at writing, but overall he's not so bad
Not a good teacher at all-not organize, joke around too much in class. Doesn't explain clearly & above all GRADE ESSAYS REALLY HARD!

He's a funny man yet an unorganized teacher and a tough grader. At first he may sound like an easy professor by letting you rewrite your poor essays and attending his office hours for extra credit, but its not as easy as you think with his difficult standards. Beside that he does make class interesting and less boring.
awesome. halarious. never prepared but always making through the class. you have to read the book but its fun interesting. have to write some essays but good class overall
Do NOT ever take Hinkley. There IS NO WAY you will get an A, let alone a B. I would avoid him at all costs. My friend let him proof-read his essay 4 times, yet he still got a C! AVOID AT ALL COSTS!

This Professor may always sound easy when it comes to essays, but watch out, he's a very hard grader. I went to his office hours twice to correct my paper, turn in my revised draft(which he corrected 2 times) and still ended up with a C+! If your not a very good writer, avoid at all costs.
Not too hard since he lets you rewrite your essays and you are guaranteed a higher grade.

Hinkley is a good teacher, but he teaches you how to write in his style.  He does not assist you in trying to find a style that fits your writing capabilities...also, he did not have good office hours and did not answer emails promptly.  He talks a lot and tends to get off subject and gives you extensions if needed, but overall he doesn't help you

he is a cool teacher but talks too much. he is good one on one and getting straight to the point on information. the final he gave this year was take home. few in class quizzes on short clips of films or on topic.

one of the best professor's at UCR. he is very helpful and interesting guy. he required reading is also very interesting which i cant say about many other classes. if he is teaching you should definetly take his class.

Not the best teacher! always talking about his personal life (hey teach we get it you are french canadian!!) Needs  to be more organized and needs to learn how to post grades that way people can actually keep up.

Smart as hell. Nice as hell. And caring as hell. Prof. Hinkley is one of the most caring Prof I've had at UCR. His style is not conventional, but his brillance and dedication are clear. He meets students half-way and cares to help, but cares to streach us. Everyone should take him.
Wortst instructor I have ever had.  So disorganized, can't teach.  Talks too much during class about his own views.  Not helpful at all and very confusing. Class was a waste of time

Very understandable, uses many methods to get his point across, has a fun attitude, you will enjoy his class, especially if he shows The Matrix in class to provide a contemporary look at Renee Descartes’ theories.
Good prof. Picks interesting required reading. Very informative, but lectures all class, every class, so avoid if you like group work/discussion.
Disliked his class as he was not organized and very liberal.  Was helpful during office hours though.
No Comments
good prof., likes discussions, if you don't discuss or do the reading he will quiz you so don't be dumb and not do your hw!  interesting discussions.  understanding.
not recommended

Absolutely the most dedicated professor at the entire university and you will realize this even more outside of class than in. 

The amount of time he devotes to help students outside of class is immense (imo to a detriment). He has his principles and he stands by them firmly. Tough grader? Yeah 100% but fair.
He truly appreciates discourse.

He's a great guy! He does require you to actively participate in class which gain you points but never picks on someone. You have quizzes every class but they aren't worth a lot ( I miss a ton and still passed). You should def visit his office hours because he gives really good feedback and help. He's funny and loves to tell stories lol
His class is really difficult and challenging.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Helpful professor even when you're struggling as long as you go to his office hours
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Be prepared to read every night because he assigned a quiz for every lecture. He graded very harshly on grammar. If English is not your strong subject or it is not your first language, you will have a hard time. He graded on a curve but his class still gave me so much stress. Make sure to attend office hours for help and participation points.

Prof Hepler is a silly guy. I enjoyed lecture because he would bring up other topics and was funny at times. He is a tough grader but overall made my writing better.Reading is heavy and required because he gives quizzes every lecture since it is how he makes sure students read. 3 essays and two papers which are only extended and rewritten essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Hard
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Bad
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Hepler is the most straightforward professor I ever had. He is a tough grader but I believe his course changed my writing at UCR for the rest of the four years I was there. If you want to be a better writer, take his class.

Dr. Hepler is a harsh grader. He teaches things that we were never taught before about grammar, punctuation, and even verb tenses. I am glad that I took this class. If you actually want to get better at writing, take this class. He is willing to help you as much as you are willing to work. GO TO OFFICE HOURS FOR HELP ON PAPERS. Do the reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Essays are graded harshly. Small mistakes in grammar or formatting can make or break your grade. Very lenient rewrite policy allows for a good way to recover points. Feedback on essays is unhelpful unless you set up a private meeting with him.

He was definitely a hard essay grader for an intermediate composition teacher; small missing details in essays can lose you a lot of points. He gives quizzes at the beginning of each class and requires that you participate in class for points. His stories are interesting and he is a kind professor during lecture, but hard on paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Hepler was a very hard professor. I rewrote all of the essays and still ended with a B-. I learned a lot, but was it worth all of the stress? Definitely not.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: He gives quizzes before every class which is stressful at first, but you get used to it. Very particular about all grammer and spelling, you'll have to work for an A. I slacked off a bit and still passed; getting the essays started on time and using a checker(grammerly) are essential. He has very helpful feedback and interesting lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very tough grader. Class would be somewhat interesting but he made everything about his conservative views. Would not recommend because he was often rude to others.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: You can tell professor Hepler really enjoys what he does. He is really tough and can seem picky on grammar. Trust me though, his scrutiny will help you with future classes. His office hours are crucial to ensuring your success in the class. Not only are they mandatory ,but he will give really helpful advice on essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Hepler was a great professor. He made each and every class fun and interesting either with his jokes or his enthusiastic behavior. His class is pretty difficult especially since he is a tough grader, but he does curve his class which definitely helps. Overall make sure you go to office hours and get to know him outside of class.

He is a really great teacher. His lectures are amazing and always tries to make students laugh. He focuses a lot on the grammar so make sure you proof read your essay everytime. He really helps me a lot when I attended his office hours so go to his office hour! Quizes every class, but it should be easy points since he has a curve on it.

Great professor. Highly suggest. He is a strict grader, but worth it. Office hours are a part of the grade. Quizzes every class. A lot of participation points. Total grammar guy. Probably would hate how Im writing. There is a lot of reading. Grades based on actual score or a legitimate bell curve; whichever is higher.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: HE"S AMAZING. GO to his office hours and he helps you a ton lot! Although he's a grammar nazi, he's super nice even though he looks intimidating. I came in with a weak grammar background, however, once I took his class, I can say that I improved a lot. It's not THAT "strong" yet but with his motivation, he gave me the confidence to do better.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Hepler focuses a lot on grammar. There are quizzes every day, so make sure to read the assigned readings. He is hilarious and gives a lot of controversial speeches, so his lectures are never boring. He is a tough grader, but the class is graded on a curve and he lets you rewrite two papers. Overall this class was difficult but insightful!

Although he's strict, he's very motivating. I came into UCR not knowing much about grammar, and I even failed my first quarter English with another professor. However, once I took him as my English professor, I became more motivated to improve my English and grammar. Sure, there may be a lot of work, but it's worth doing to improve yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Hepler was a great professor, even though his course was extremely hard. He was extremely critical with his students' essays. If it wasn't for him, I don't think my English would have improved. Office hours were extremely helpful, so go. There are in class essays, which are rough drafts of your final essay. The workload is heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Good professor but very harsh when it comes to grading. Gammer is very important to him. Loved the process of doing essays (did rough draft and then a final paper). Go to office hours it helps but plan to get there early b/c people do attend quite often. He also takes a long time to grade and give work back. He also gives quizzes everyday so read!!

He's an okay person with cool dorky jokes and gives inspirational speeches on life. But it always seems like he's trying to make someone feel dumb. He's conservative and expresses his views so be prepared to argue with him. He's strict on his grading but can be pretty easy going for the most part. All in all, it's a challenge.

He is adorable. He has the cheesiest jokes but he entertains you in class. Along with his lectures he shared a lot about himself. He really wants his students to improve in grammar so he really tries to simplify lectures.

Professor Hepler is a great english teacher. He really cares about his students and strives to make them appreciate grammar. He motivates the class to participate in class… but he is a very tough grader. You cannot afford to procrastinate. Assignments are difficult but office hours are extremely helpful and encouraged. Quizzes are very simple.

He is very vague in what he requires, prompt wise. He expects a lot and is a tough grader. He complains about how he gives twice as many assignments than a regular 1B teacher because he can never keep up with the grading. I really disliked him. He tells you your essay is good in office hours, but get a sucky grade when he hands it back. Avoid.

Hepler is the best teacher I have ever had because he actually teaches you correct grammar. Yet, he has honestly stressed me out with his expectations on the papers we write in class. He is very passionate about arguing! But as long as you go to office hours he will definitely help you out. I recommend him if you like being challenged.

His assignments are horrible. 4 in class essays, 3 take home papers, 4~5 journals per week, quizzes every day. if you don't try to say something in every class you would lose point. I gotta have him because other sections are all closed.

He was horrible at emailing back. Made everything philisophical. Books were semienteresting. He was never clear on what he wanted done for his class but would mark you down significantly because it didn't match what he wanted. You would go to his office hours and he would say your paper looks great and then give you a low score when turned in.

By far one of the greatest prof of the bio series. Her notes are simple to follow and understandable. Just read the notes of the ch she provides, lecture slides and participate in clicker question and you should earn a decent grade.

She is absolutely amazing. If you can take her do it. Her clicker questions were all similar to what she would ask on the test. Great lecturer, almost like a crash course. Easy to understand material as well and very accommodating.

This was her first time lecturing anything Biology related but she did a great job. She's a great lecturer and provides notes before and after. Go to lecture, even though it's not mandatory there are clicker questions which are free points. I did not give a 5 is because the exams are quite tricky compared to the depth lectures delve in to.

It was her first time teaching biology and I thought she was great. She posted her notes and slides ahead of time, which was helpful as I wrote notes before class and added additional info based on lecture. Attendance isn't mandatory but I would recommend attending as the iClicker questions done in class are types of questions to appear on exams

Her first quarter teaching 5C, but damn if she isn't the best biology professor I've had at UCR. She emphasizes the core concepts and tests within those parameters. She's funny, she's great, and if you don't take Biology with her, you'll probably end up with a subpar professor. All I can say is Lucy Delaney is amazing. UCR protect her at all costs!

The way he explains the concepts is very confusing and not intuitive. I feel that the way he teaches them will not be useful to people who aren't mathematics majors. Besides the final, nothing else is graded on correctness so if you just want to pass, it's not difficult. Cool guy though.
David Weisbart's MATH 005A class was truly inspirational. He truly cared for his students and none of his lectures were confusing nor difficult. An amazing class, would take again.

Dr. Weisbart gets a lot of flak on Rate My Professors. Mostly for his lectures, which are definitely weird for a freshman class. This is why I rated him a four: he is very caring. He will spend a lot of time with his students after class if needed. Your only real test is the final, which is completely open note, and the rest are take home.

Dude is a funny and chill guy but the man can only yap, not teach. The material itself is already confusing and his explanations add even more confusion. Your TA can be clutch but sometimes they dont even know how to answer the questions. Only saving grace is an open note final worth 50% of your grade so take good notes and you'll hopefull do well.
most confusing class ever... and final is 50% of your grade. he's really nice but it's hard to fully pay attention during lectures because he'll go off topic a lot.

Cool guy, he LOVES MATH and hes literally a genius. He can't teach. There is no textbook and the homework looks very different from the lectures. He makes simple calculations look really confusing. Also the final is 50% of your grade but its open everything basically.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. clearly loves math but he cannot teach. He does not contact or respond to students or TA's so you are on your own if you need help. There's no textbook, only his rambling notes and lectures, and the final is 50% of the grade. You can use notes for tests at least so try to jot down what you can. Do NOT recommend. I passed but learned nothing.

He taught MATH009B like we were grad students. Even though his tests were open note, final exam was 50% worth of the entire grade. No curving in the class because students cheated on every exam to simply have an A. My honest self got left with a D in the class smh.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: People who are complaining about David is someone who is not academically ready. Sure, his course materials are tough. However, now I am in the higher divs, his lessons help a lot. He is hilarious and actually really caring to his students. Any concerns you have, he will stay even 40 minutes after class to hear you out. Great professor, for sure.

this man is the biggest yapper ever. each time i went to lecture i ultimately learned nothing, the homework is way better and you have to teach yourself. the final is worth 50% and he told us our midterms do not even matter. all exams are open everything so this class was a piece of cake but not good cake.

Honestly this guy does not teach very well.  He's really nice and means well but he fr does not teach.  His lectures are straight up a yap session and it's really hard to stay engaged and follow what he talks about.  The course is difficult because he doesn't teach and you're at the mercy of your TA.  Mine was a chill gym bro but also sucked.

Professor has a passion for the subject, but their teaching style can be confusing. The class is challenging, with a heavy emphasis on self-learning and a 50% final exam. Use unstuckstudy and other resources to stay on top of the material. Overall, put in the effort and you can pass this course.
I learned absolutely nothing and there was no textbook but midterms were take home and final was open everything so chatgpt carried.

He's a good person and all, just not good at teaching at all whatsoever. There's no textbook and the whole course is basically made up by him. Lectures are confusing and he goes all over the place and goes off on random tangents. I learned nothing in this class and wrote random stuff on the final and somehow got a B. This class was a waste of time.

Don't go to lectures expecting it to be like the homework. Not mandatory but definitely recommend going to lecture as he will drop important info every now and then. Homework heavy but as long as you do it you'll have 100% before the final. Prof definitely cares about his students and wants everyone to pass.

reviews.comment: Professor wastes time, gets off topic easily, and the material he goes over lecture is all over the place. Although its an easy class and easy to pass the quizzes and exams, youll be left with so many questions

reviews.comment: He will teach like you are a PhD students, so prepare for the most difficult mathematics class of your life. His course will cover 5, 9 series and 10A materials, and I am not joking. Study, and study for the class materials. If you do well on his class, you are good to cruise until 10A, because he probably briefly covered them in this 5A course.

had him for the entire math 5ABC series last semester; if you wanna actually learn smth, don't choose this guy. while he means well, chill, and is clearly passionate about his subject, lectures are pointless and confusing and he's honestly all over the place. his grading is questionable and unorganized. waste of my time, i passed but at what cost?

Awesome guy and super easy to get along with.
Accepts late assignments and will work with you if you put in the time.
Final is 50% and is difficult so don't miss lecture

very nice and passionate guy, class material is very hard and he expects you to learn the material before the lecture, very confusing way of teaching the material and not very thorough with his explainations, the class material is hard the final is not as long as you study all the practice problems he gives you + it's also open book

Great personality, but I didn't like him as my professor. 50% of your final grade is on participation (Midterms, homework, etc.), which is graded all on completion. The other 50% was the final exam, which was graded on accuracy. He was constantly changing due dates for assignments and his TAs were unsure about the material as well.

David is a genuine guy that is really passionate about his job, like it's really obvious he loves doing what he does. The only problem is that he doesn't explain all the steps and expects students to self teach themselves the lessons before entering class. He also has a really confusing way of explaining, but other than that he's a good professor!

Taken in Fall 2022. Professor was unable to be reached out through emails and anywhere else which makes this class all self taught. Final is 50% OF THE GRADE. The class is made up by him and confuses it tenfolds. He makes decisions that cant be kept especially regarding the final. He isn't able to teach which is why he had to curve the final twice.

Professor Weisbart is an easy teacher when I took his class. All you have to do is complete all the quizzes and surveys before the final. Furthermore, as long as you watch the lectures on canvas and take good notes from the discussions, it will help you pass.

reviews.comment: DO NOT SKIP. If you skip this class you will be so lost the final is 50% of your grade dont mess around go to the lectures as useless as they are and study a lot. He barely does anything in the lectures hell spend most of the time talking about other stuff that is pointless honestly just pray and hope for the best dont know how i passed. NO CURVE
overcomplicates simple math algorithms and looking at lecture notes is like reading alien language. very passionate about math but cannot teach at all.

This guy is really nice, but I really disliked this class. When I look at his notes for the homework, he just randomly makes up gibberish that spawns out of nowhere. He literally made up an entire course and expected us to do it without a textbook. It is the most complex topics ever and he explains them horribly. Worst class ever

Took this class and had him MATH 149B the quarter after. My is definitely my favorite math professor and he made learning probability so much fun. I am planning to take quantitative economics for my masters program because I enjoyed these classes so much.

The class and homework is a lot harder than the exams, but he’s very lenient with everything. A lot of proofs, but whenever he isn’t doing them its pretty easy to follow. Exams are open note, and are very similar to the practice exam, which he goes over in detail in a recorded review session. Class can be rough, but definitely manageable.

Pros: enthusiastic, caring about student learning.

Cons: teaching style was unorganzied 2hr lectures that would overcomplicate even the simpler concepts with what felt like endless proofs. Additionally, consistently getting side tracked and not covering many core concepts of the class.

Not recommended !

He's a nice guy. Never take him for a harder level class. He refused to record lectures due to ethical reasons and posted lecture slides days late. His homework and exams were of the same general concepts taught, but if you didn't 10000% understand the concept you will NOT be able to do anything. He does not curve and the midterm is half the grade.
Lectures and homework were confusing for me but I did well because TA was amazing.

Professor Weisbart was a pretty solid math teacher. He didn't always post his lecture notes on time, nor did he make all his videos. However, he was super useful for office hours. He did talk a lot about the philosophy of math but overall, he's really caring and super nice. Just study hard for the final it determines your grade for the class.

This class is hard and its taught in a very different manner. Some tips I can give is to really look at the sample midterms and finals he gives. They are very similar to the actual midterm/final. Professor Weisbart is an amazing professor. Although some material was pretty difficult, he was so helpful and offered extra online office hours and review sessions. You definitely have to put in some work, but it is all worth it in the end. He really appreciates when students try their best and show improvement. Such a great guy.

Dr. Weisbart could be a tad eccentric at times, but at the end of the day he was a great professor who was clearly passionate about what he was talking about. He was a tad fast at times, but if you can keep up and take good notes you'll pass his class.

Professor Weisbart is an okay professor. reviews.comment: WORST professor ever! David is a nice and chill person, but when it comes to teaching, he's the worst. He provides a syllabus with tons of examples (only thing I liked about his class). Study A LOT, and be prepare for a horrible ride.

David is the most chill person. Just go to his office hours because the problems he goes over in office hours helps with exams as they show up again on midterms and the final. Also go over your two midterms and quizzes as it repeatedly shows up on exams especially the final.

I had the opportunity to have Dr. Weisbart as my precalc professor. Let me just say, I did not know I was capable of learning so much about precalc in such little time. He is the most caring and compassionate teacher I have had. I strongly recommend you go to his office hours because HE IS THERE TO HELP!! Start working on syllabus problems asap!!

David wants you to do well. If youre willing to put the work in, he is willing to help. Go to ALL his office hours. If your TA is good at teaching, go to theirs too. ALWAYS learn from your mistakes on midterms and quizzes bc theyll pop up later. Get to know David, hes a great guy. Hardest math class Ive taken, but so interesting and worth it.

David is a heart-felt professor, he ensures his students get the best grade they can get. He has weekly quizzes, but they are stress free. He automatically gives you 100% just for submitting, and an extra .2 (a total of 1.2/1) if answered correctly. His way of teaching is very different from HS precal, so don't come into lecture w/ low expectations

He explains problems very carefully and happily answers questions. He teaches you how to reason rather than just have you memorize steps. Some students think that he overcomplicates things, but actually, the ideas he teaches makes calculations so much simpler. I loved his lectures and I'll really miss this class. Not easy, but worth it!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: His lectures are confusing, but because I took precalculus in high school, I was able to self-learn on my own. His syllabus is helpful because he gives examples and practice problems on there. Go to his online office hours if you need help on homework or a lesson he taught in class, he will try to clarify. Con: he spends too much time on 1 problem.

I was an A student when it came to taking math in high school but David made this class so much harder than it needed to be. Unfortunately he is the only Math005 professor which means I was stuck with him.

He is pretty nice but I just did't like how he teaches (He teaches really fast). 30% of total grades comes from your home work and worksheets. So make sure to submit all your works if you are not good at math.

The class overall was terrible. He tries to teach math in his own way, so the methods he uses are often very intricate. The homework is very annoying and the only questions that matter are the boxed ones. The tests have three sections, but the midterm is much easier than the final. There is somewhat of a curve in the end.

The way he teaches is much more valuable and easier than what you learned in high school once you take the time to understand what he is doing. Don't skip class if you struggle with math and try to go to office hours as much as possible because that's where you'll get the most help. Do the study guides because they're very similar to the exams!!!

Weisbart can make some concepts a little confusing. He is very understanding, very involved, and has a clear passion for subject. All lectures posted online but it helps to go to lecture and see how problems are worked through. Lots of hw but hes lenient with grading. If he knows you went to office hours and tried, hes lenient on final grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I took precalc with him and didn't really get why he did things the way he did at the time. Now, it's a year later and I get it. It helped me so much with my later math and physics classes. He gives you everything you need to do well, just trust him and study hard. It was the best class I've ever had. He's very kind and never makes you feel dumb.

I had Weisbart for Precal and I thought at first the class would be a self-learning nightmare with his complex lectures. But its honestly an eye-opening yet challenging course. To get a B confidently, you need to commit to the optional homework, go to T.A office hours not his, and really focus on his study guide practice exams and that's it.

Honestly, if you have a brain you can easily pass his class. His test questions are extremely simple and he provides practice problems that mirror the test. I been to class four times. First day, First and Second Midterm, and Final and I easily got an A. Gives around 3 percent in extra credit too, so super easy

He posts all lecture notes online before lecture so you can come in prepared. He teaches everything from basic principles, so you really don't have to memorize and can really understand things. Exams are like the practice problems, homework, and worksheets, and he reviews these problems as examples in lecture. Don't miss lecture. I loved his class!

His lectures are overcomplicated, full of proofs, and ties way back into the basics. Homework is nothing like the examples he goes over in lecture. Don't even bother going. Just do all of his practice problems, and you'll be ready for the midterms and finals. Don't rely on your prior knowledge of math from high school. Study hard!

I just finished his Math 5 class. I gotta agree with the two comments below. It was definitely different, but once I realized what it was all about, it was REALLY good! Come in with an open mind and you'll learn a lot. I've never learned so much in a class. Follow the advice in the syllabus and ask lots of questions. You can get an A. I did!

I will admit, David was quite the enigma. His lecture style was pretty unique, to say the least, but the dude was very caring and nice. The way he teaches math concepts can be confusing at first, but if you keep going to office hours and really try to do the practice problems, then I'd say it's very possible to get an A in the course :)
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: It's so weird that the student below is upset because "he teaches you the basic fundamentals" and that the class is "nothing like what you learned in high school." His lectures didn't help me at all because he taught the class as though the students already knew the material. Online videos and Chegg were my best friends this quarter. If you wanna do well on the exams, DO NOT study the homework. Follow the study guides he has on his website and you'll be fine.

reviews.comment: attendance is not mandatory but go! he posts his annotated slides on ilearn. has in person and online office hours. put the effort you'll pass.

All you had to do was go to lecture. Some people found his lectures overcomplicated because they are used to doing math a certain way, he teaches you the fundamentals and helps you understand what you're doing. To be honest, this class (particularly the homework and midterms) was rather difficult at times, but if you show up to lecture and go out of your way to show him that you care about this class, he'll be more than willing to help you out. Dave is an incredibly humble and really enthusiastic when it comes to teaching the course, the only downside is ... the way he teaches the course is less than desirable. Prof Dave Weisbart is a very humble, yet is a terrible, confusing, tough, intense professor. You will not understand the homework, will not understand the lectures.
