reviews.comment: Professor Eacott is an okay lecturer, nothing special though, but as long as you pay attention you'll be fine. Readings are all free, just got to go to the library. You can miss a few lectures as long as you read to make up for it. TAs will grade your stuff so have a good relationship with them. Easy class, just listen and take good notes.

His lectures are rapid and detailed but his slides give little to no info. You have to write fast. He's sort of funny and not boring. The readings for discussion have no correlation to the lectures. Be ready for writing essays and short answer paragraphs for testing. You have to go to lectures because he doesn't post any information online.
I've taken his class before, and would again. He's a great lecturer, a very spicy meatball (handsome), and hilarious.

Great lecturer, definitely would not mind coming to class again just to hear him speak. Lectures were very focused and direct while also being interesting. He lectures very actively and engages the audience well. His tests were basic comprehension of the subjects covered, so prepare well with that knowledge. It's a lot, but not hard to get.

Probably the best professor I had so far. Very informative on the subject and really knows what he is doing. Even if you aren't a history major, you'll most likely enjoy the class. You don't really need the textbook but it is wise to at least look at it so you can cite from it. I would highly recommend taking this class.

I loved this class. The professor is clear in his lectures and the readings correlate to the class discussion. The content is very interesting. You must go to class and do the readings to pass this class.

Eacott is a great professor. He's very interesting and always enlivens the mood and makes the class and content very interesting. His midterm was a little obscure. My advice is that attend lecture, and study for everything for the midterm and you will do fine. Also read all of the required readings they will help you ace the midterm and final.
He was definitely different in that he teaches the class based on how commodities tie everything together. It was interesting, a little difficult but one of my favorite classes.

Go to lecture and participate in discussion. That'll save you in this class. Take good notes and read the Marks book right before midterm/final. This class really isn't as hard as reviewers are making it seem. But there's 2 papers and weekly readings that range from 20 to 80 pgs. Just do your readings and study. The papers are graded fairly easily.
You HAVE to attend every lecture! Take really good notes. Do not slack off in this class. If you do your readings and study enough this class is fairly easy.
not easy  but passable

Challenging. Attend discussion (worth 20% grade) and pay attention. Do all of the readings. Put in the time for the papers. Take very good notes in lecture. Great professor, lectures well, helpful during office hours. Befriend your TA because they grade your exams and papers.
If you want an easy A, then this is NOT the class. No multiple choice, two essays that require lots of reading, and two tests that are free response (more essays). Do not take PLEASE

Not an easy class. You need to put in the work. However, this is college and you should not be surprised by this. He is an amazing professor; lectures extremely well. Really knows his stuff. He will do whatever he can to help you succeed. Great, great guy.

He is a great lecturer. He talked with clarity and in a way that made the material easy to understand. The readings correlated with his lectures most of the time. Attendance isn't mandatory, but slides or study guides aren't given out prior to the exam, so I'd recommend attending all lectures. Overall, great professor.

Awesome class! He makes history really interesting and his lectures always go really smoothly. Extremely nice guy and always willing to help after class or in office hours. Make sure to do the readings! And on top of all that, he's pretty attractive. Definitely take a class from him

Did a fair job at making World History interesting, focused on commodities rather than events/names. I felt like the readings didn't correlate too well with the course but we were forced to reference them in the final anyway. Also probably the best looking professor I've had!
He's alright I guess
Great structure ! Assignments and lectures were engaging. Not to mention he is good to look @ !

You must attend lectures because he doesnt give out a study guide and his powerpoints just have the main terms you need to know for the midterm/final. Theres two easy papers due. His lectures are interesting though as he shows a lot of pictures and plays songs that relate to the subject.

My only quarrel was with the fact that he was very wishy-washy in the way he graded the written assignments. He would mark you off for something on the first paper, and dock you points for not doing it in the second. What was more irritating was that most of his criticisms were stylistic. Maybe it's just because he studied in England...

Really should not have taught an upper level class. Readings felt random and class gave no coherent picture of the topic of study. Regretting taking this class. Grading was spotty and the homework assignments came perilously close to pointless. I took this course a William and Mary and, honestly, thus far, it has been sub-par to every other class.

A very easy class, as I put little effort in and earned an A. He is very likable as he is clear and articulate and has one of the easiest, interesting and fun structure of class. Very helpful and understanding, he is extremely good looking to top it off. You also get to see one of the greatest unknown movies ever for extra credit. Definite win.
Loved this class; the movies, art images, and music made this course a non-typical class!!! HIGHLY RECOMMENDED.

I really enjoyed this class and I earned an A. It was not an easy class but it is upper division so you cannot possibly expect it to be like His20! IF you do "cherrish" (as the poster below me so eloquently wrote) your GPA, maybe you should give an A effort and youll receive a commensurate grade- rather than searching for an easy ride. Great class!
Its funny how professors that get bad ratings come on here and try to give themselves high marks, Just check out the previous 2 below, sounds like he wrote it. STAY AWAY if you cherrish your G P A
man i worked so hard only to get a low grade. He is cocky and arrogant and likes to hear himself speak. AVOID and take another class with a better professor

STAY AWAY, GRADES HARD AND IS PROUD THAT STUDENTS DO NOT GET A's IN HIS CLASS. likes to hear himself speak and expects you to know a map he cant even draw to scale. There is hard and there is this guy BEWARE!

Professor Bruner is an experienced musical scholar with an abundance of talents and knowledge. I'm always in awe by the professor's knowledge. Besides being a professor, Edward Bruner is also a songwriter, a conductor, and an awesone classical singer!

He is so inspiring about music. He has a great voice too! I have been with him for 3 years and improved a lot. He expects you to improve over the quarter, so practice! He is very approachable. I have asked him for homework help with other subjects and is helpful. He is also a great person to talk to and gets along well with students.
This guy is awesome and loves music. I think some of the bad ratings here are from kids being babied in high school choirs, dont mean to offend anyway. I love this guy.

Dr. Bruner is the best choral conductor I have ever encountered.  He is clear, consistent and doesn't take any crap from the whiny third grade sopranos who want to sit in class and text the boyfriends instead of singing.  How about warming yourself up? Dr. Bruner is amazing, I highly recommend and will continue to study with him while at UCR.

he never warms us up and often starts the sopranos singing on high Fs...Not cool. He also runs through the music very fast without stopping to fix the parts that aren't working, he simply bulldozes through the pieces just to get to the end of them. Also has the tendency to go off on a tangent very very often.

Alright, see that rating 2 below this one, with the yellow smiley face of me saying Mr. Bruner's calm and collective? Well, I change my mind. I've taken his class for over a full year, it's a very SMALL class, and I found out he still doesn't know my name. He spelled it wrong on the program!

Dreadful. Doesn't warm students up because "professionals don't need to do group warm-ups", then insults us by repeatedly calling us amateurs. Then during the concert he sticks his 40-year-old friends in the chorus to drown us out when they never rehearsed with us before. I and many others quit after taking his class.

Class is easy. Mr. Bruner cares about what he wants the choir to sound like and is one of those calm, collective people. However, his spur-of-the-moment stuff is a bit weird. He tries these "surprises" during the concerts that really end up looking incredibly stupid. But fun experience.

Mr. Bruner teaches Choral Society. This is a very easy A; however, he does not make learning music fun. He does not care about the students learning music. This is a great class for those who just want to get an easy A to help there GPA go up. Audition is required, although it is very easy to get in

Definitely take 110 with him!! He explains things well and doesn't overcomplicate them. The exams weren't too difficult and were open note, but you do gotta study to do well because some of the concepts are tricky. He lets you know what you need to study for each exam. Also offers a generous amount of extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a great professor. Very accessible in and outside of class. No homework, graded on two midterms, one final, and section points. Flexible. Opportunities for 3 extra credits based on writing a one page on topic and having it be peer reviewed. If I had done the extra credits I have no doubt I would have gotten an A+ but I had much going on.

Highly recommend taking this professor if you have the chance. His way of explaining information was very clear and made learning difficult topics easy and interesting. Lectures contain a lot of information but the explanation and his dedication to teaching makes it easy to understand.

I had a great time in this class. This specific topic of psych was very information heavy but Prof helped us to understand the concepts. Additionally, he provided helpful study guides for each exam. He gave ample opportunities to make up points from the exam through extra credit. I ended up learning a lot because the lectures were engaging.

I wish all professors were as amazing as him! The material isn't the easiest, but with Prof. Zagha's clear and thorough teaching style..he makes hard concepts much easier to digest. I found him to be not only highly intellectual, but he was also very caring, funny and humble. Will never forget this class or the instructor!

I can't believe the negative reviews, he's a fantastic professor! He is truly passionate about the subject, he's very interactive with his students and I have yet to have a class with so much student participation. He gives a study guide and provides his own notes on his lectures. Highly recommend!

Professor Zagha was a good instructor. Psyc 110 is a hard course and both he and the TA's helped students as much as possible. He showed a passion for the subject and I overall enjoyed his lectures. They were a bit heavy but it's a Brain and Behavior course which is expected. I'd personally take Professor Zagha again!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Exams are difficult and he isn't willing to help students study effectively for it. He didn't give in for a study guide until the final and everyone scored higher because we knew exactly what to study. He does spill so much information during lecture so write everything down. Without the study guide I would have not passed. I wish he cared more

He gives no homework or quizzes. Your grade is ONLY 3 exams + 15 pt discussion. His lectures very specific and and his slides and lectures don't help much unless you rewatch lectures over and over and over. He's not forgiving have to make up much for any reason, medical, family, or anything. He only curves 5-6 points or not at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Zaghas class was pretty hard given the complex content revolving around physiological psych. The only things graded are two midterms, the discussion, and the final. The tests were pretty hard & much of it isnt clearly found in his lectures. You REALLY have to work in this class if you want a decent grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Good guy - good class. Not wound up about the title of being a professor, people respect him naturally. Course material is hard, but prof and TAs make it very easy if you work hard. I wouldn't recommend taking it with other heavy courses, it requires a lot of studying and genuinely understanding the concepts.

He is really knowledgeable about the subject. The class is difficult itself, but he does talk a lot so it is confusing to take away major concepts. He doesn't look at the chat for questions or clarifications in his lecture, which makes it more difficult to retain information. He should care more about students concerns in the course as well.

Dr. Zagha is one of my favorite profs at UCR. Clear explanations, simple PowerPoints (be sure to look at PowerPoint notes), and very considerate of students and their situations. He was very excited about teaching each lecture, especially neurotransmitters. PSYC 110 is basically an intro to Neuroscience course with some clinical applications.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: He's a great professor, but the class itself is challenging. You have to really pay attention to lectures and study a lot to do well on tests, but the material is interesting. He talks a lot during lectures, and there isn't much on his slides, so you need good notes. Overall good professor, though!
Great professor who really knows the material. Highly recommend taking his class. Not uncommon for him to let everyone out early.

People complain about him not giving enough time, but the time limit has been the same for every professor who has taught this class. I've been able to finish every time with 20 minutes to spare. He goes into detail a lot but he ALWAYS repeats the main idea of what he wants you to know. You will need to work for an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He isnt great. His tests are super hard and he only gives you 50 min to take a 40 question test. Not enough time to read and comprehend. His curves are a joke despite the limitation of time on the test. His lecture slides are no help either when he talks about it in so much detail and cant note it down much. Also, he wont answer questions
Very sympathetic towards student issues. He also does a very good job at helping students utilize all the information they've learned from previous classes to better explain new concepts.
The best professor in the land!!

Hes definitely the best professor Ive ever had. Hes clearly brilliant, but very approachable. He actually inspires you to think and learn, and pushes you to be better. His classes are amazing and I would encourage everyone to take him.

Talk about an amazing guy. He's a neuroscientist with a medical degree, but he's easily the least threatening professor I've ever met. He gives so much encouragement. Plus, he doesn't give exams in his seminars! Which makes the learning all the better 'cause there's no exam pressure. Definitely take a seminar with him, the man is incredible

Professor did not post grades on Canvas so had to email him what I got. Class felt unorganized. Presentation order was moved around halfway through the quarter and expectations are not clear in this class. He graded my attendance incorrectly and when I emailed him, he proceeds to criticize my presentation even tho its a different grade category
overall a decent prof, his lectures are boring and hard to follow but if you study the slides you should be ok. exams aren't always super easy but are fair,

Don't get scared by the bad reviews. Come into class with a good mindset and be prepared to pay attention and actively take notes. Exams were very chill if you memorized his slides. He drops hints on exam content and gives some answers during lectures so go to class. 5% EC opportunity. I recommend asking questions in class and going to office hours

I was scared due to the reviews, but I really liked him! He's actually a nice professor & answered emails in a timely manner. There wasn't any assignments outside the quizzes & exams. If you find it hard to understand people with heavy accents then I recommend to take someone else, I was able to understand him, but not many can.

really wasn't a hard class, didn't attend lecture a single time and only studied 1-2 hours the night before every exam and passed with a b-, exams focused heavy on practice questions from study guides/discussion slides. also gave us 5% ec assignment
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Korzus was so caring even when ppl were cheating. You do have to study since the topic itself isn't as easy. Study the TB but if you don't have time, discussion slides cover majority of what's on the tests and TAs will emphasize what to study. A few practice Qs that he posts w/ answers are on the exams. EC: 5% boost on your overall grade.

This class was one of the worst I've ever taken at UCR. The professor was so sweet but the overall experience was horrible he was so unorganized and in structured is hard to get a hold of very very test heavy. I once asked if there would be a study guide for the final he went on a rant about a completely different topic take over summer or at a cc

He honestly seems like a caring person who is passionate but lacks organization and structure which is reflected through exam grades. To psych majors who aren't pre med, this class will be challenging. There is a lot of information to remember in comparison to other psych upper divisions and takes up A LOT of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He cares about his students & wants them to succeed BUT the structure is awful. The lectures are hard to follow, chaotic, & unclear in what's going to be on tests & doesn't provide a useful study guide. He will ramble & waste time that should be dedicated to content. I would avoid taking his course if possible, no positives outweigh the negatives.

I really enjoyed Professor Korzus' class! This content is not easy and cannot be crammed for sure, but if you put the effort you'll ace it. There are 3 exams non-cumulative and 30 q's (1 hour). The best way to study was to attend lectures and then read the textbook on what was mentioned. Also, his office hours! There is also EC offered! Good luck:)

Professor Korzus was the worst teacher I have had in all my years of taking education. His lectures are boring, and he will have an hour and twenty minutes to discuss important things, but somehow, he will ramble about nothing. You will have no idea what is important to remember or any clue as to what to study. If you have him, godspeed.

Professor Korzus is one of the best at UCR!I have taken his 126 class as well as 117.I wish he taught more classes so I could take them!He takes the time to get to know his students and helps his students when they are struggling.Hegoesaboveandbeyond.Althoughhemaynotseemlikeit,heis chill,patient,andalwayswillingtoanswerquestionsorprovideextrahelp.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's not the worst professor, but he definitely isn't the best. He has a pretty heavy accent and uses a lot of complex vocabulary for a class that only has psychology 001 as a prerequisite. It's a lot of self-study and very test/quiz heavy. There are a few EC options that really up your grades so most don't fail the class.

Lectures and slides can be all over the place, but just focusing on the slides should be enough to do well on the exams so you don't *have* to read the textbook. Definitely go over the study guides he provides and attend office hours for any clarification. Bumped scores for the first exam, offered extra credit, and dropped the lowest exam score.

I took this course in winter, and I don't get the low ratings. But there's a possibility he changed his teaching style because while some of his lectures are confusing, he's ready to clarify and encourages his students to call him out if something's confusing. He drops your lowest score and gave extra credit, and finally, he wasn't rude at all??
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Nothing good or bad that stood out about this professor. He was particularly boring and monotonous, reading the supplementary textbook will get you farther than attending lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Extremely rude but if you can bare that, you will do great in the class! 117's grade is based on a really big presentation you have so make sure you put 110% into that.

Took both his lecture over summer and his seminar afterward. Really enjoyed his lecture style, coming from a neuro background. If you are a psych student, you probably won't enjoy this class as much, as he might gloss over some background concepts. He also puts a heavy emphasis on engagement in class. His accent can be hard to understand though.
Very rude professor, not easily approachable. Asked for help and his rude responses led me to no longer even want his assistance. I'll figure things out.

This professor has a serious language barrier and belittles his students for his own confidence issue. His grading basis is not clear. He will switch it up all the time and lie that he never said things. I’d avoid him at all costs he’s very disrespectful and does not truly care to help students.
Class: PSYC117 (wasn’t choice)

Lectures were messy. Exam questions were all short-answer and graded unfairly. It doesn't matter whether or not you clearly understand a concept. If you fail to include a key phrase (which is not made known to you in advance), you will not do well. Exam scores are not reflective of whether or not you understand the material. You're set up to fail.

PSYC110 is a really hard class that intros complex hard topics that must be learned for a psyc student to proceed. I don't doubt Korzus' expertise, I imagine I would gain more from his class if I had a previous understanding of topics. The language barrier mixed with the introduction of complex & abstract topics just don't mix well.

You will survive in this class, but he makes you work for it in a ridiculous way. He is the classical STEM professor that wants to go above and beyond to make you work for it. Mid 2 was much better from mid 1 but he is changing our format for final to standards which don't show sympathy for whats going on. Avoid but if u need the class, GOOD LUCK!

Dr. Korzus is a nice person but had flaws. He is willing to work with us however, I highly dislike his ego. He is very rude and inconsiderate (wanted us to show our face in the face cam which is fine but the way he said it, it basically said if you don't, you will be penalized). What happens if it doesn't work our cameras? Feel like he blames us...
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Nightmare. 2 midterms, 1 final, all mc, some quizzes/assignments in disc. Seems straightforward, is not. Pretends to be understanding and "accommodate" but does nothing to help. the avg for exam 1 was an F and he responded with useless lectures and treating less fortunate students as if they should fend for themselves. He's rude and inconsiderate.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE! He is rude and so condescending to students. He is very privileged, doesn't care that you don't have access to stable wifi, he basically says that its your problem not his and doesn't understand that just because things load quickly on his computer it is not the case for everyone.

DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR FOR ONLINE CLASSES! He has no regard for students concerns. Refuses to make reasonable accommodations. The class average for our midterm was an F, and the professor placed all of the blame on the students for failing. Stated that just because we are in a pandemic doesn't mean we are not able to learn the material as well.

To summarize: 1. Hard exams; despite open notes, TRICK QUESTIONS. 2. Little to none communication 3. NO Study guides; review sessions, but irrelevant 4. Curved first midterm, but only because class average: F. 5. Hard to understand. 6. Blames students for bad grades 7. Nice person, but difficult professor. Overall: I will NEVER take him again.

Professor Korzus was a great instructor. He gave study guides that were very close to what would be on the exam. He never gave trick questions. He truly cared about the success of his students. I would highly recommend taking him for 110. It is impossible to fail his class. Just read the book and study his study guides ad you will pass. Easy class
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This class doesn't appear intimidating because the midterm+final are MC, discussion quizzes/paper easy and straightforward. The thing that got us was the grading. The syllabus said the class was going to be curved, but it wasn't. Everyone got their flat percentage. You can't afford to mess up ANYTHING! I scored low on the midterm and paid the price

4 Quizzes&2 assignments: very easy if your TA was as cool as mine. Midterm&final: Prof's slides are titles and subtitles of paragraphs in the book. So, I recommend you study the supplemental reading, then use slides as an outline for review. That's how I aced the final. I studied slides for the midterm and FAILED it. Go to lecture anyway, trust me.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: This is a hard class. There is a midterm, final, and two short papers. Content for the midterm and final come directly from his slides, so I would memorize them. The reading just gives you a better understanding of what is already on the slides. He does curve the final course grade, which is literally the only reason I passed with credit.

He stays on each lectures slides for 15-20mins and talks about random stuff. His grading scale is worst.  If you are A student , you will barely get B if you put same effort.  1 midterm with nonsense essay questions and 1 final . no room for bosting grade if you mess up once.
Do not take him. enough said, do not trust me ???  Go take him and make sure give your feedback here lol. Goodluck

This class was very scattered. The teacher isn't very much of help and he doesn't explain concepts very well. Instead he starts ranting off about facts and ideas that are not going to be helpful for the test. The midterm is easy, you just need to know what they want you to study in great detail. The final will catch you off guard. No curve.

I took him over the summer and fell in love with learning and memory. His accent is really easy to understand, his tests weren't tricky at all, he told us what exactly to focus on and really meant it because he asked us about it in different ways. He was so helpful in his review sessions. This class is a must for all neuro majors

Pros: Easy final (and by easy I mean, just memorize his slides - the book isn't much help IF it's MC) CONS: Terrible lecturer, super unclear, will stay on the same slide for 10-15 minutes, his midterm is short answer and essay questions and you'd never really guess what they want to see. READ for the midterm, memorize slides for the final. NO CURVE

Extremely nice person, visit him in office hours if you'd like.  Textbook-heavy class!  Sometimes you can't understand him in class because he doesn't explain a concept well.  Read textbook 10 days before midterm, highlight what you want to read when you come back to book.  Re-read highlighted stuff.  Read his lecture slides.  Textbook is amazing

Easy first midterm, but everything gets pretty hard and detail oriented after that. He disappeared during second half of the course, and the substitute said he made sure that everything he taught would be on the test. Things he didn't teach were on the final. ): Anyhow, make sure to understand the case studies.
Very friendly and funny professor. Class is doable if you can memorize all the information, and there's a lot. Do not slack off for the final, it will ruin your grade lol.

Such a funny professor! He wants you to be your personal best and doesn't force you to compete with fellow students. Also, to the person that is resentful of his leaving in the last week of the quarter, get over it. People have issues in their lives and families that sometimes mandate serious attention. It's not like he felt good about doing it.

This class was straight up BS! perfect scores in lab, 98% on both midterms and above average score on the final and ended up with a B-!!!! Professor went "missing" for the last four weeks of lecture and was kept himself strictly out of contact. Every in the class was lost with the material and there was no communication with professor what so ever.

I loved this class! Professor Korzus has such a rosy disposition. The class seemed daunting at first, make sure you know your cbns 106 material, but all in all, this class was pretty fun and not too hard. pay attention in class; it'll pay off on the essay portion of the tests. if you pay attention, you'll ace it for sure!

This Prof. is cool. Class is very easy, i mean... I studied ONLY the practice tests and the sheep brain thing, and i have an A so far. I'm sure I'd have an A+ if i study the book, but i didn't bother buying it! To put it in perspective; I'm currently taking BCH, Anatomy, Pop. Genetics, and this class. This class is by FAR the least of my worries.

Seriously he is the best neuroscience professor by far. Puts Curras-Collazo, Hatton, and Hickmott all to shame. Wonderful class, and as long as you focus what he says will be on the test and read here and there, there should be no problem getting a great grade

Dr. Korzus was really helpful. He actually returned my call one day to help me out in the class and give me a heads up on the next test. He's always honest when he tells you what to study. There's a lot of work you have to put into the class. But it definately pays off in the end and you learn how to improve skills you already have.

This was a very good intro class. He was a new prof so sometimes it was shaky, but he managed to keep it fun and entertaining with great examples. Make sure to read the book and you’ll get a good grade.

Dr. Korzus's class rocked!  Very easy class, very interesting and fun!  The whole class is basically about the hippocampus.  Each week there is 1 group presentation and 1 lecture, so class attendence is mandatory (u can only miss 2).  There's a weekly discussion, but there r only 3 mandatory attendence dates.  Study what Dr. K says, n u get an A!
No Comments

Amazing professor. You need to work hard in his class but he is extremely helpful. The tests are multiple choice and he gives As to 25% of the class. Read the book, go over his lecture notes and you should be able to get a very good grade. Try to get talk to him, he will always listen

very clear and makes math seems very funny. sometimes joke and have very interesting math facts. likes a quiet but engaged class. very easy to talk to and helps students. one midterm(30%) and one final(50%). homework(10%) and quizzes (10%)

Amazing professor. He's extra prepared for class and his examples really help to understand concepts. He makes sure to cover the midterm and final in class. He really set the bar for other professors. If you can, get him for math.
Great Teacher. really helpful. If you can try to get him for as many math classes as possible.

He puts up alot of slides and expects you to really grasp the information by memorizing a ton of details. I failed the exam even though i spent more than the 6 hours required for the exam. Not easy, tedious and time consuming.
The class consisted of one midterm, one final and two visual practicals. There is ALOT of information and everything is fair game. Never used textbook in this class.
easy class, very clear professor..

Very nice and approachable; does cover a TON of material, all of which is fair game for the exams.  Truly wants to see you succeed, but will not just let you slide on by.  Likely to retire soon--this will be a huge loss to the department!
Teacher very helpful. Easy. Interesting.
One of few who is very approachable and understanding.
No Comments

He uses lots of figures from scientific literature for his lectures. It could come to be a little unorganized & hard to keep up with. He is very nice and always willing to help. His part of the course is the more difficult, but his lecture summaries make it more clear. Test questions aren't too bad.
Fun class!
nice guy
The best teacher in the world
No Comments

The class had probably about 40 people in it the first day, down to about 7 in the following weeks. Weird assignments, boring lectures (it's all just him talking about infrastructure, does not encourage people to speak) and he is not very approachable/helpful. Not hard, but pretty useless.
Interesting content, I disliked that we had to make Twitter accounts, Tumblr accounts, and YouTube accounts, though, just for this class.

She is by far my favorite professor. I look forward to going to her class every day. Learning is actually FUN with her, unlike most other professors. TAKE HER!

shes really nice, always smiling, passionate about russian. she wants us to succeed. easy grader, but fair too. quiz each week, but not too hard as long as you know the material. one midterm its not too bad. she is pretty easy overall
she is so easy and fun. she keeps you engaged in the class and makes you participate, which really helps you learn. i love her.

Not surprising she has a high rating on this site. One class session with her and youll love her. Its nice to go to class and see such a happy, engaged professor. Youll love her accent, too. Its hard not to. Attendance is mandatory, don't miss class. Participation is required, too. 2 presentations. 1 paper. Even if youre not into Russia, take her.

Took soviet cinema, i thought it was going to be boring but i LOVED the class and the movies are AWESOME! i am now a very big fan of russian movies, oh and she is the nicest and sweetest prof ive ever had at ucr, very helpful too, shes not easy and shes not hard, your expected to do your work but shes very fun about it! TAKE HER CLASSES!
Very chill teacher,showed interesting movies. Definitely take her if you have the chance. Easiest and most awesome teacher ever here at Riverside.

Kind, understanding, very sweet.  Not extraordinarily hard but not extraordinarily easy either.  Expects work to be done well and on time.  Pretty much a fantastic professor whose classes were some of the most enjoyable I ever took.
She is friendly and easy.  Maybe it is just hte Russian language, but she is teaching all of the exceptions right away which can be confusing.  BUT THUMBS UP!!!

Prof Yudina is the nicest professor on campus. She is super easya nd very funny. If you get anything less than an A in this class, you should really consider probably Riverside Community Collge...or just working...she grades based on attendance, some participation, and 2 EASY exams with pretty pictures on them. Take this prof! help ur GPA.
What a sweetheart! I wish I could have continued with her classes.
She's the sweetest instructor in the school.  Super lenient, but still challenges you.
she's really nice and super awesome.

dope a$$ teacher, 1 of the coolest not only cuz of easy A but seriously knows her shizzle. go 2 class its fun, movies are boring during the 1st weeks but pick up pace n have really good movies l8r on. grade based on review papers of movies (easy only 1 pg) no midterms, writing style can be flexible
My second or third favorite teacher at UCR, and I have been here almost 4 years.  Such a nice person, gives easy A.  Very enjoyable class.
this professor is AWESOME.
great professor, fun class, and easy A

My favorite teacher I encountered at Riverside.  She is wonderful.  I learned so much from this class and every bit of it was interesting.  The only downside is the particular class has a lot of reading, but it's all worthwhile.  Very interesting class and an excellent professor!
great energy, great teacher, fun, cool, informative, love her!!!
just a fantastic teacher, she made me seriously consider russian film

There is a lot of reading. The book is like 2 inches thick! This was a pretty cool class! We had a field trip to look at Russian icons! This is more of a Russian history class. If you're into history, you'll like it.

Kristen was a great TA. Had her last fall. She was very understanding and helpful during covid. Speed-replies to emails. Seems to genuinely care about students. This class is hard as heck, but she'll break things down into memes before letting you fail. She also cracked me up and was a relatable mood a lot of the time tbh

Bruh this TA saved my grade lol this class is INTENSE (do not take it as a crunched summer course people!!) + shes probably the only reason I passed. EXplains things in plain straightforward words, also points you toward what to study + what to focus on more (so. much. content.) so at exams you dont feel as doomed as lecture would make you feel
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I'd never tried philosophy before but she made it easy to follow, and kept the drier stuff interesting. Is accommodating about participation, you can turn in written thoughts if you're anxious or don't like to talk in class. If you go to the office hour, she helps a ton and is also way more casual and down to earth. Nice person, easy grader, fun TA

MGT 200 is an excellent class. She is a genuinely talented educator. The asynchronous lectures were clear and actually helpful, which made the in-class time feel meaningful instead of repetitive. Participation matters in this class, and she does a great job making it feel worth it. I learned a lot and appreciated how intentional everything was.
I enjoyed her class and it's a lot of interactive work so if you have a good group it's fun. This sounds weird but I feel like she's very try-hard when she doesn't need to be. Just the vibe I get

Actually had this professor for one of the AGSM classes, Organizational Behavior. AMAZING professor. She's incredibly thorough and she's one of the very few professors in the graduate program that help you want to strive for greatness. 

The one 1.0 review is probably a bitter student who didn't attend classes and got a bad grade.
terrible professor. she is unprofessional in lectures and kept on saying stupid stuff that doesn't matter. avoid at all cost

reviews.comment: Prof Wong responds to emails very promptly, posted interesting lectures (although the embedded quizzes were a little frustrating) and was easy to talk to. Her grading was clear, feedback was pretty decent (if you asked, she would give more detailed feedback), and her class was overall very engaging. Don't take this if you don't plan to participate.

Great, passionate professor you can absolutely learn a lot from. Class is easy but lots of busy work, if you have a super busy quarter i dont recommend. unrelated: but i get the feeling she really dislikes me and i am not sure why (i try in her class), so make a good impression and show up lol. u can def learn alot.
Great Professor for MBA Students

Elaine was an awesome professor to have. You will not regret taking her course. Attendance is necessary but she makes herself available. This was an MBA course so expect to do allot of coursework. Overall a great professor.
It was a cool class, pretty easy too not really much to say about that... I did find her really attractive for some reason when I would talk to her, it was kind of weird but yeah haha

Best teacher I've had at UCR, the content of the course is extremely applicable in life and is beneficial. Must read cases and book plus lecture slides. Pay attention to examples given in  class. 2 exams and a group paper.

75% of your grade is based on exams. Most of the people cheated on every exam so he did not curve, as compared to other classes who had 15%+ grade curve. None of the material he gave us reflected what we were tested on (explains the cheating) and majority failed the class. Trust, take it next quarter if this is your only option

75 percent of your grade is tests (2x 15% MT + 1x 45% final), which over 1/4th of the class is using ChatGPT on because his test problems are ridiculously hard (homework and practice midterms don't help). Please trust me, wait a quarter if you have to, but don't take this class or you will fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A 1/4 of the class cheated on mt2 raising the avg to 80%(mt 1 was 47%). This disturbs the curve and is unfair. Everyone changes their answers while lining up to turn in their tests. His practice tests have vague work and is hard to track so it took me a while to learn. Also boring lectures.
ya im sorry who thought 75 percent of your grade being exams was a good idea?
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Can't lecture, practice exams will not prepare you for the actual exam, and cheating is rampant so averages will always be significantly inflated. His solutions to the sample midterms and final are also either super vague or completely different to the methods most students would use to solve the problems, so they only confuse you more.

Dude has to be aware half of his class is cheating with test averages at 50% and 1/4th of the class being all at 100%. If you don't actively use chatgpt during his exams you WILL do poorly, or more likely fail his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Most difficult physics professor I've taken. Doesn't do demonstrations, lectures are boring (reads off slides) but there are participation polls for accuracy making them essentially mandatory. Midterms and exams were extremely difficult and not like practice materials he gave. Mass cheating on his midterms, so the averages were really high :(

Ellison is not a bad instructor. It's just that he doesn't post his lectures online and makes everyone come to class and do polls. Most of your grade is on the final and he adjusts the grading scale 5% by the end of the quarter. As along as you take good notes and do the HW, you should be good.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst class I've taken here. Cheating is rampant and inflates the averages, making it nearly impossible to compete without cheating. It's frustrating to put in weeks of studying only to get outperformed by the entire back half of the lecture hall using ChatGPT. Ellison and the TAs make no effort to regulate exams. Lectures were useless.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Wouldn't recommend.

lectures are very boring and slow as he reads off his slides. does pollev in class for credit. midterms aren't that hard, but the final was challenging. he gives sample exams which are similar to the actual exam but the question asks to solve for something different so know your formulas. don't cheat yourself on the hw, understand the concepts

He teaches the class content well and has good studying resources, but he is clueless. On exams, people cheat, raising the class average to a point that does not seem typical of a physics class. This makes it unfair to those who scored below average but would likely have a score reflective of an average if no cheating was done.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: midterms are easy if you use the practice he gives you. final exam was a lot more difficult than the midterms so that brought me down to a B+. just go to lecture (he goes at a good pace and is super friendly to answer any questions and explain more in depth) and do his practice exams. overall one of the best physics professors i've had.

There is a curve. Two midterms 15% 1 final 45%. If you study you can do good I did bad the first midterm and did good on the second and decent on the final. I would have had a C but the curve made me have a C+. He doesn't record lectures which kind of sucks. Does pollev in lecture so attendance is mandatory.  Overall:7/10

No recorded lectures. Cheat sheet for exams. Formulas provided. Practice midterms helpful.
Grading:
- HW 10% 
- PollEv 5% 
- Discussion 10% (attendance) 
- MT1 15%
- MT2 15%
- Final 45%
MT1 avg: 71.7% 
MT2 avg: 64.3% 
Final avg: 67.6%

90% is an A. 85% A-. 80% B, etc. Curved and brought boundaries down by 5% at the end; 85 is an A, 80 A-, etc.

Nice guy. Lectures were pretty boring and his voice lulls you to sleep, but he has polls so be aware of that. Everything was very well organized. Tests were very fair, plus he allowed a cheat sheet. Grades were posted really fast. Had a great discussion TA which helped a lot. Best physics prof I had at UCR by a landslide, but the bar is pretty low

Lectures were very dry. He mainly just reads off slides and class normally ended early. He definitely does try to explain concepts if you have questions, but overall, not very engaging. Also wished he did demos to better explain concepts but unfortunately he didn't do any.
Overall nothing too special. Tests were really easy as long as you go over the practice exams. Classes were usually cut short 10 minutes on average.
He only reads off slides and I find myself using his lecture as a means for dozing off, but if you actually do the hw and understand how to use the formulas you'll do okay
Hard to understand, his explanations are overly complicated, he skips steps, exams are nothing like the HW, and a majority of the student get a C+ in both classes that I was in.

Not a terrible professor but he just read off his slides, the class regardless of the professor will be hard. He was nice and the class averages tend to be around 50% at least for my class so he fixed the grading around that. Not a class one must avoidable and the sample midterms did help. All tests were multiple choice.

Professor Ellison does not curve your grade no matter how close you are so forget about asking. Exams were all MC which was cool, but avgs were still low. The curve was alright. You have to attend class bc of the polls you have to do as they count for ur grade. Overall, you might have luck with another professor, ik I've had better.

Attendance is mandatory since you do Poll for grade. His curve is decent so if you score the mean or slightly above you will get yourself a B-. Issue is if you are after the A.. His lectures are useless and you gotta self teach with the book, I was less than a HALF A POINT away from an A, he didnt give it to me

Professor Ellison is an okay lecturer but his exams are often not fair assessments of knowledge due to them being made up of a few multiple choice questions opposed to FRQs with partial credit. To add, he doesnt nearly curve the class or tests as much as he should given his grading scale. Overall, wouldnt take him again and wouldnt recommend.

Great, caring prof! Explained phys concepts well, but really helps to read textbook before class. Homework may initially seem challenging but is much easier once you've covered all topics in that chapter. Exams were fair and reflected homework/sample exams. Sometimes confusing answers to questions but he tries hard to help students.

He curves down. I had a 92% as my raw score on iLearn and ended up with a B+ in the class. He did not even consider changing my grade. I would not take this class with Ellison unless you are positive you can get a 95% or better as your raw score before the curve.
He is a nice man! He graded down which sucked. Not gonna lie, I didn't learn anything from him. I had to learn on my own by reading the textbook. My lab TA was amazing!!
He curved our midterm and final grades down if too many students got 100%. 90 was a B, 80 was a C, and the midterms and finals were only 10 questions. So if you miss 1 you drop to a B.

Good physics prof, does make concepts clear and even works through example problems during lecture. Sometimes isn't the best at answering questions; but he certainly takes care to try to answer all questions. Gives samples for exams for practice, and they usually reflect the exam. Very caring & understanding, especially during covid.

ONE OF THE BEST PROF'S!! Some of my friends took this class before me & said it was a little hard, so I was kinda worried but he was AMAZING! He tough well online & his lectures were everything. All his slides were so helpful and never felt like it was too much info. Physics can be kinda confusing, but he made everything so easy to understand!

I 100% recommend him! He breaks down concepts so that they are easy to digest, and is very helpful if you have any questions. He is understanding, especially during this pandemic, as he changed his grading scale. More professors could take notes from him on how to effectively teach while maintaining standards and empathy during a global crisis.

THE BEST physics professor. He was so understanding and helpful during this transition to online learning for Spring quarter. He even changed the weight of the final so more students could do better in the class. His exams are similar to HW problems and study guide problems. He grades very fair, but it is physics so you need to put in the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: His teaching is pretty monotone, but a fair grader. The midterm was 4 free response questions and the final was 6 free response questions. The midterm was fair, but the final was way harder. I got 9 points above average on the midterm and the final literally dropped my grade. But the curve is 75-100 A. Pretty easy.

If you take this class over summer, then there are no clicker quizzes.  He recommends reading the physics book before lectures which actually really helps.  If you dont stay on top of things, the final will be hard.  If you try your best on homework and read the book, it is really easy to get a high A.  P.s. the lab final was only 15 questions easy

He gives both a sample midterm and a sample final letting the students know what kind of problems to expect on the actual tests.  The midterm was alright, but the final was more challenging.  To put into perspective, I got a 100 on the midterm and a 87 on the final. However, 75-100 % is the grade range for an A making a hard final very understandab

Midterm was very straight forward. They were straight out of the examples from the textbooks. I didn't use any lecture slides or notes at all and still got a high score on the midterm because of the examples. The final was a little harder than the midterm though. But the average is usually 50 or 60, so there's always a curve.

Ellison is fairly good professor. He has a few clicker questions scattered throughout lectures ...one day he'll have one and maybe five other lectures won't have any ...bt they're pretty easy if you have the slightest idea of what is going on. MasterAnything is entirely horrible, so it no doubt will apply to you when you do HW on Mastering Physics.

He's a pretty good professor, compared to soome of the other physics teachers here.  The midterm was alright, 4 free response questions.  The final was hell though..dropped my grade.  But, he does have an interesting British accent, and does interesting demos in class.  Take him, I think he's worth your time.

I wouldn't call him a bad teacher, because he's definitely not incompetent or malevolent, but his lectures are very dry and he's so soft-spoken that I had to strain to hear him in class.  But the textbook he chose for the class...god, I don't think the people who wrote that mess could have made the material any less clear if they tried.

He was very dry and boring. Probably one of the most unpassionate teachers at UCR. Midterm was simple, final was very hard. Do as best as possible on the midterm, homeworks, and lab because the final is HARD and will most likely bring your grade down. BUT as with any physics class he is generous with the grading and curves. So I guess take him.

he's really not that "easy" because the curve is usually crazy in ANY physics class you take. Not much different than any other physics professors. Even the one with bad ratings. Physics is physics. Practice midterms he gives are kinda similar to the actual exams but don't expect to pass the midterm just by studying that alone.
great teacher!!! he knows how to teach!!!

Ellison is a good teacher. He explains things well. He gives plenty of examples. He is easy to understand. For my class the midterm was easy but the final was very hard. The exams are very similar to the practice exams.
good teacher, gave good practice midterms similar to the real midterm. final was not as easy. NO clicker quizes!! :)
This guy mumbles a lot. You need to come to class having read the text book with a good understanding or don't go to class at all. HW is kind of hard but the tests are easier.
Great professor. If you do the homework and understand it you will do well.
Lecture was great even though it was at 8 am.  And your grade should reflect whether you like the subj or not.
Does a good job teaching. Native English speaker. Pretty easy.

his accent is difficult to understand. while he makes a good effort to teach, I get lost in his boring lectures. Unless you are interested in physics (and think you can stay awake), don't take ellison.

This is how physics professors should be. Not scaring off students from science but helping them do well. My favorite physics professor. I really appreciated all his review sessions. And I'd say I learnt the material very well.
Very generous curve. Cheat sheet on exams too.
cool teacher very cooperative, really helps you about grades. study homework, and practice problems, it should be no problem getting good grades.

Sometimes I wonder if this guy is a hobbit. But he's a coo foo. He has a cool accent. His class is fair. I got an A in class. Back in highschool he was a homie. I like this guy, I'm gonna hit him up tomorrow so we can chill. Good guy!
i got an a... what else can i say?
this english guy screws up demo a lot
Really good, a bit boring, but eh its physics 40a, just do the homework early and you will be fine.  He does have big    ^^^^^ ears .                     C ' D
Good teacher.  Very clear in lecture, and nice personality.  Fair testing that is on the easier side.  A more serious teacher/not a lot of humor, which was neither a benefit nor a disadvantage.

class is very dry, mostly derivations and equations that come from the physics gods out of somewhere? STUDY THE HOMEWORK!!!!!!!!!!!! that is what midterm and final is based on. BTW, he grades MEAN curve. 4  A's,3 B's, 8 C's, 6 D's and an F
he had big ears and an english accent

Very dull and jokes suck so much I wanted to kill myself when I went to class, but despite my total incompetence in physics I still managed to pass so hes a fair teacher, but I didnt learn anything what so ever.
a page of notes! all you need
No Comments

This is a tough class, but not unfair. Exams are challenging with no partial credit, so you must understand the material. She's organized, provides a formula sheet, and focuses on reasoning rather than memorization. Homework took me 6+ hours a week, so it's a real time commitment. Not an easy class, but a solid one if you put in the work.

This course is very hard. If you go to restroom and come back, you wont know anything laters. And the rest of the course will be bored. It is very very hard to focus on and have to watch the video of the class. Exam is hard, if you have a bad grade, you will take this course again.

Professor Goodman is definitely difficult. However, her explanations and expectations are clear. She knows the material well and her presentations are well made. Homework is graded very generously and seems to be intended mostly for practice. Tests are difficult and there is not partial credit, but she does provide a formula sheet and curve grades.

Prof Goodman put in a lot effort to the class compared to other professors, her ppt is organized and contains a lot of useful information. She also provides a formula sheet for the exams so the tests are focus on understanding the materials not memorizing. Great class overall!

Although her class is really difficult and homework-heavy, I would say as long as you follow, you will learn a lot from her if you want to do anything analytics-related in the future. She teaches every reasoning behind the formula so it is very easy to remember. Her exams are hard but as long as you listen to her lecture then you should be fine!

If you don't know quantative/statistics before, you're going to have a disastrous semester. A simple basic knowledge was the same as advanced mathematics problems in ppts she showed. Goodman doesn't want students to bring any electronic devices in her class, but feel ridiculous that she doesn't have enough copies for each class.

reviews.comment: She will teach you a basic question in a complicated way. The midterm and final exam will cover a wide range of complex questions. If there are other professors, I recommend not to choose her.

Prof. Goodman is passionate about what she is teaching and is very good at articulating the material in an understandable way. Her class is fairly difficult, however, it is because of the subject, not her. I feel she set me up to do well in other classes too. I think she is fair in how she grades and would take another class she is instructing.

Goodman's way of teaching is backwards &all over the place. Once you think you have got the grasp of something, she throws a curve ball. It almost seems as though she is teaching herself the content for the first time as well. To add on, she has a very nasty attitude. When wanting clarification she almost makes it seem like your question is invalid
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Lectures were a bit drawn out. Midterm and final were a pain in the ass too. A lot of questions had a "none of the above" option which constantly made me question the answer I got. The tests have a HUGE curve, so as long as you learn some of the basics you should pass.
This professor assumes you know the basics of stats and gets upset for asking any simple question.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Unfortunately had a very bad experience in this course. I have taken statistics before and it was not as over complicated as she made it. reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This class isn't easy, but she does a good job making sure you understand the material. Start the homework at least a day before, because sometimes it can take a couple hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Very odd grading system; every assignment/exam were fail/pass. If you did all required assignments/midterms/final then you'd get a guaranteed B in the class. If you wanted an A you had to do "Extra Labor" which was honestly very easy. Exams are extremely easy, just don't write anything that is straight up wrong, also gives prompts before hand.
Amazing professor. Would take a class with her every quarter if I could.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Work is graded on completion. Doing all the mandatory work gets you a guaranteed 85% so if you want a higher grade you need to do some extra work, but it's also graded on completion and it's really easy. Some of the extra work options were making a playlist for one of the stories or showing up to office hours. I really liked showing to class!

I totally recommend taking this class for breath course. Professor Stapes is very chill and informative with her lectures. After each of the first 3 units you'll write a short reflection about the stories, tons of extra credit. Hardest part is after the fourth unit you'll either write a 5-7 page creative writing or a collaborative creative project.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Stapely is an extremely knowledgeable and passionate professor who cares about her students while making the most out of her lectures. She provides great feedback on essays and allows students the flexibility to break out of the standard essay format making for a more enjoyable writing experience. Overall, I would recommend her!

reviews.comment: Professor Stapely provided all the books required for the course which was helpful. The syllabus was very straightforward and so was the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Extremely caring and clear on grading. Guides you through the work but won't do it for you. Breaks down assignments and recognizes effort. Grades fairly. Took capstone course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: A very accessible professor but honestly way too many essays. Easily 1 essay every week after week 5. No final exam which is a plus. Seems to be a very understanding grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment:
Expect LOTS of political bias in her class. Also, she spends a lot of the class talking about current issues (like, first 20 minutes of class). The slides are somewhat interesting through a history perspective but I wish that her content would stay more true to them. 

Homework isn't as bad as people have previously said, but expect to read a lot.

Overall amazing professor and well versed in ethnic studies, workload was weekly readings and group projects that mostly involved answering 2 questions in depth with groupmates each week. The professor does drone on a little and can be a little hard to understand sometimes but she really does want students to learn and is genuinely caring.

Professor Hue is an amazing, passionate professor who genuinely cares for her students. Her course does have a lot of readings; however, you can easily finish the readings without overwhelming yourself by reading one a day! There are no “exams” just “open-book assignments” where she prompts you to answer concepts from the class using the readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Recommend her class! Textbook reading was easy and group discussion involved. It was a fun lecture
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I liked my class with her so much in the Winter quarter I am taking two more classes with her this Spring quarter. I know of other students that took more classes with her also. She is one of the most caring and understanding professors. She is not a harsh grader in the slightest, yes she has weekly discussions but 3 OPEN-NOTE tests/assignments.

Cares about her students & gives students chances to make up work There are a good amount of assignments but not too much. Worst part about the class is group work, every week you work on an assignment with your group. Sucks because some people don't do their part Use google doc to track that. A few papers. attending zoom lectures, videos, articles

Class was far better than I expected; it was very laid back w few deadlines per week. HW per week were to submit a question & 2 responses + answer a couple questions w your group. Gave a lot of EC, accepted late work + no exams/papers(just a group project). Lectures were very interesting & she's very understanding & kind despite negative comments

Dr. Hue is an amazing instructor. All the negative reviews here are whiny complaints about the workloadbut anyone who is invested in learning, who isnt expecting an easy A, should appreciate insightful, generative readings. She presents genuine research because she actually treats students as adults who want to learn, not to be handed a diploma.

I don't know why I chose to retake this class with this professor. The workload has been ridiculous and this has been the most unreasonably demanding at UCR so far. The assignments have been too much to handle and I can't even keep up with other classes because of this one. I'm so stressed out and unhealthy, and it's all because of this professor.

reviews.comment: This professor is no joke in terms of workload. Grad students warned me about her but I still chose to take the class. I should have listened. Regret, sorrow, pain, tears, so many tears. Excessive and tedious work. What's troubling is the performance of kindness she exhibits while in class. Sadistic? Very passive-aggressive, almost scary.

reviews.comment: Upon taking this class I traveled to a sea and stood at the edge contemplating my life. I wondered why this class was so tediously demanding and considered if I should drop out. There are 2 kinds of people. Those who use dishwashers and those who use it as a dish rack. This professor is the former. Mama told me never trust those who use dishwashers

reviews.comment: This professor is assignment-heavy. I heard she actually reduced the amount of work for this quarter because of the pandemic but the workload is still heavy. reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Where do I even beginnnnn? Terrible teaching style and exhausting amount of work (this is an understatement). Eichler is such a slay he made chemistry understandable to me for once and was very passionate about his teaching. He offers retakes on the midterm also and offers extra credit opportunities!!

2. Make sure you answer each Canvas quiz correctly. It's easy but you only have 1 attempt usually
