But she seemed to have  good grasp and I ended up loving the lectures. She teaches in a way that makes difficult material accessible. Lots of examples to help explain concepts. Recommend taking
This was Prof Hanes last time teaching at UCR and she will be missed. Best instructor I've ever had

Very enthusiastic and inspired me to major in psychology. Her tests are hard, but if you study and especially pay attention in class, you'll do well, but she'll throw curveballs in the exam. Not hard to earn a B.

This class was OK. What I disliked the most was the fact that you were given no points for participation, even though we did many activities in lecture and section. And the exams were tough. Pros: The lectures were very interesting, and the instructor provided "lecture breaks" where we wrote our own quiz questions. That actually helped me learn.
I loved that I learned something new every lecture. The exams were tricky, but Esther offered extra credit. Overall, I would definitely take a class with her!

Her exams were tricky! You must know the book AND the lectures to actually do ok on exams (like a C). The lectures did not always overlap with the book, either. Frustrating at times, but the lectures were really interesting, and worth attending.

She definitely wants you to pass this class with a B or higher.  She is very eager for feedback and takes plenty of acts to help students learning and grades.  Gives points for unfair questions, shows funny videos, and is super friends.  Overall awesome class! If you gotta take psych, you better get Esther!
great teacher, he's so nice.

Dr. Eulgem is very kind. The classes he teaches are difficult but that is to be expected. He makes learning difficult material fun and understandable. He loves to answer questions and will ask the class questions to help make connections and to increase engagement. I recommend this professor for any upper-division courses that he offers.

Enjoyable class and he does his best in explaining the material. Going to office hours helps if you are not 100% on some topics and he is really approachable. His tests were tricky and difficult, you have to study, but some of them were from (or similar to) his assignments and study guides. I recommend this professor

love him as a professor, he really cares about his students. however, this class was not easy, you need to put in a considerable amount of work. weekly homework and a midterm and a final. though this class was hard, i enjoyed it a lot. TA is extremely helpful as well, try to go to both OH if you can

Dr. Eulgem is a good professor, but fair warning youre going to have to put in a lot of work. Last quarter, I spent the most time studying for his class out of all my upper-division classes and ended up with a B. The material isnt terribly difficult but you really need to know your stuff to answer his style of test questions correctly.

Dr. Eulgem is a great professor at UCR for Plant Biochemistry/Pharmacology. Prior exposure to biochemistry course is highly recommended but the highlight of the class is in the pharmacology section and they relate to biochemistry. Do not be scared of the class just because it says " Biochemistry" Office hours are extremely helpful for the class!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He is a great lecturer. He really cares about his students and always available to help. Two midterms and one final. He also provides study guid which is very helpful. Going to the office hours is a big help for this course.

Dr. Eulgem is by far one of the best professors I've ever had. He's a great professor and is super passionate about what he teaches. He's very friendly and really wants his students to succeed. He provides study guides, which if taken seriously can guarantee an A in the class.

Professor Eulgem is one of the best in our campuse. He is a great lecturer and makes the lectures interesting for students. Two midterms and one final. His handouts are very helpful for the exams. He is very approachable and his office hours helps a lot. He really cares about his students. I wish he teachs other courses I could take.

Great Professor! It's always nice when they show passion for their field and the class is very interesting! There is a lot of review from BCHM 100 for first midterm and the second is pharmacology. Follow the handouts and answer the questions because some of them pop up on the midterms! Final is cumulative.

Dr. Eulgem is my favorite professor on campus. He is very passionate about what he teaches and even if you don't care about plants, his class is very informative for prepharmacy students. He is a GREAT lecturer because he doesn't just read off the slides and makes class interesting with stories. His handouts also help a TON!
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Would take again

reviews.comment: By far my favorite professor at UCR. If you see him listed down on course schedule/catalog take his class. He is a very passionate individual and made pharmacology so interesting. I don't recommend skipping his class because he gives very good detailed lectures so you definitely want to be there to hear the extra information, and tests are fair.

Amazing professor. Very passionate about the subject, and is extremely helpful. Definitely would take his class again. Covers material that will help pre-meds, pre-pharm, and future grad students. Would highly recommend this class. Grades very fairly, must work for the A though.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: No curve sadly. Amazing lecturer but if you skip class you won't pass. He gives handouts in class so you'll need to definitely be in class to get them. The material accumulates fast so make sure you read and study daily. This is a no easy A class but a B is duable with effort in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: I recommend taking this class if you are interested in pharmacology or are pre-med. The class is interesting because it ties secondary plant metabolites (plant chemicals) into modern day pharmacology. The professor is extremely fair, and his study guides do a great job at reflecting the material that is on the tests. Take this class.

Great class. If you are at all interested in the subject, you should take it. Nothing extremely hard core though so dont be scared if plant biochemistry is not your thing. Its a very comprehensive and fair class.

Class is great. First midterm is pretty hard so dont slack off for the first one and youll be fine. Office hours are extremely helpful. Attendance is important as he hands out a weekly handout that is very helpful. Basically a study sheet.

Dr. Eulgem is organized & passionate about teaching. He gives out handouts that summarize his lectures & have concept questions. If you understand those questions, you'll get an A. This is an upper division course, so it requires a little bit of work. Two midterms (25 pts each) & a final (50 pts) multiple choice & short answer.  My favorite class!

One of the best biochem electives. It provided a great insight in plant biochem and pharmacology. He is a great lecturer and is extremely helpful in office hours. Attend lectures bc he tells you whats important from each slide.  Do all the questions from the handouts that he passes out during discussion. Also his exams are fair. Highly recommended.

I'm interested in biomedical research, so I wasn't sure how much I was going to like this class before taking it. That said, I have thoroughly enjoyed Dr. Eulgem's class, and it has been an excellent addition to my knowledge of biochemistry obtained at UCR. If you are slightly curious about taking this class, I recommend it! So far I have an A :)

This class is the perfect intro to pharmacology! It also reinforces topics from organic chemistry and biochemistry. Lecture slides are plenty but the professor emphasizes exactly what you need to know and what he wants. GO TO OFFICE HOURS. Super helpful!!! One last thing, he is super nice but DON'T underestimate studying for the midterms!

I really enjoyed learning about Plant Biochemistry and introduction to Pharmacology. The way the class was structured was fairly straightforward: lectures are enhanced by the texts the professor references (depending on your learning style). If you didn't understand a concept, Prof Eulgem was really helpful in Office Hours (Highly Recommended).
Such a nice and patient professor.  Always happy to help you. Motivates students a lot!!!!!!

A Professor who really cares about what he's teaching. His accent is not only easy to understand, its very relaxing. I never really enjoyed my science classes, but the way he teaches, you can tell he cares about each of his students, and I wish I could have him for every class. Not necessarily and an easy A, but very achievable with some effort

A great professor who is genuinely interested in the success of his students. Dr. Eulgem understood his students were generally pre-med, pre-pharm, etc. and showed great interest in presenting lecture material that is still helpful and relevant to myself today!

One of the best professors at UCR, has a clear understanding of the material and field he is actively involved in. The class is beyond a simply "plant biology" class, it's a challenging, but rewarding undergrad class that rivals some graduate level courses. Expect actual research grade experiments that are practical and a great experience.
Great professor who is very enthusiastic about his teaching. Loved the class and the information was very useful.

Very interesting course and an amazing professor. Dr. Eulgems enthusiasm for plant biochemistry and in particular plant defense made lectures extremely interesting. Truly cares about teaching the material rather than testing and handing out grades. Very helpful and easy to talk to during office hours as well. Highly recommend taking his course!!
One of the best teachers at UCR! Teaches with clarity and works to make sure you understand the material. He's very approachable so do attend office hours!

Amazing lecturer and person. Not only can he explain material really well, but encourages students to attend office hours and is very approachable. Now as a pharmacy intern, a lot of this material was applicable in a clinical and research setting!

My favorite class and professor at UCR! Dr. Eulgem was obviously very enthusiastic about the material that was taught. This made the class very interesting and motivated me to do well. He was very approachable and very helpful when it came to answering questions. I have audited BCH183, which he taught clearly and didn't just read slides. RECOMMEND!

Don't really know why everyone is hating on him, quizzes were relatively easy as well as his exams. Just study the homework and quizzes and you should be good. Sometimes his teaching wasn't clear, but he will happily help you understand if you just ask during class or even during his office hours. He also has a dry sense of humor which I enjoyed.
I went to all lectures and office hours and I thought he did a great job! Email response could use some work but I liked his teaching style
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He was hired 2 weeks before classes began at UCSD and is genuinely one of the worst teachers I have ever had. He cant seem to teach the material in an engaging way and is very confusing. Almost half our class failed the course because of his teaching skills.

Made this class content much more complicated than it is. Getting an A is not hard with him, but learning is. His assignments are really hard, quizzes super easy, and exams easy/average. He graded the last 3 assignments out of completion/effort which was nice but it was because they couldn't grade them on time. Wouldn't take him again personally
He is a easy teacher, but bad at teaching and really bad at keeping up with grading and responding to students. I am still waiting on a homework turned in 2 months ago to be graded...

I can understand why some people may think this professor isn't great. In my opinion he makes math a lot easier to understand by keeping it real with everyone, he needs to improve in administrative tasks but I'll cut him some slack as its his first quarter teaching, the grading scale is extremely lenient and frankly the class is quite trivial.

This professor is terrible. He was an emergency hire at UCSD and he does not seem to care at all about the course content. There have been multiple occasions when he was corrected by students during class due to his lack of knowledge. I started watching the other lectures because I couldn't take it anymore. DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS.

All the hw was written and took 4 weeks for it to get graded(perfect for the quarter system). The midterms were just unnecessarily annoying and it feels like lecture didn't explain a thing that showed up on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: not a really hard class so far but he's not good at teaching. Constantly switches between teaching formats which makes things hard to follow, and his lectures fall behind homework by a solid amount. I typically turn to online textbooks/resources to help me understand content that isn't covered despite being half or our homework

Best TA i've had! I never usually go to office hours but he makes students feel comfortable enough to speak up. Very helpful during office hours, will go step by step to make sure you understand whats going on. He cares for students ! Very appreciative to have had him as my TA , whole class enjoyed him!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Super cute.
Easy course.  Not really helpful.

Ethan is awsome. He was one of the professors I was actually looking forward to take a class with. He is well knowledgable although young, and keeps the class interested in the material. You get a page of cheat sheet back and front for each test. Buying the book is not mandatory for any of his classes, which saves you tons of money.
Learned a lot. cool guy
Good Professor.  He is no ****!  You get what you put in the course.  As long as you study his slides and understand them then you will most likely do well.
professor namvar is excellent. I learned more in this course than I have ever learned in any of my undergrad courses. I got an A. And he's super cute!
He tries hard to explain the material.

Prof. Namvar was great in this class. I learned so much about real estate and I felt pretty confident after the course. It's true, just pay attention and you will learn what you need. It's obvious he takes care of the good students. I disciplined my self to not fall behind and got an A :)

I took Bus 136 and 137 with him in the spring quarter. I love ethan because he was extremely helpful and gave me great advice about my career which other professors could not give me. I got an A in both classes but it wasn't completely easy.
I took Bus 136 and 137 with him in the spring quarter. I love ethan because he was extremely helpful and gave me great advice about my career which other professors could not give me.

this guy is great. he's young but smart. one of the few biz profs that's no BS. he kept the students honest, what you put in, you got out. grading was very fair, a ton of As were given. i got an A just by reading the notes a few times and doing the practice problems. the material is not easy, but i got what i needed out of the lecture, go to class!

Very easy class. Got an A and didn't open the book once. Go to office hours and my number one recommendation is to buy a financial calculator!! it will make your life SO MUCH easier! He lets you have a cheat-sheet for each test. Do the problems in the lecture slides and the hw problems to study.
He is pretty nice and easy compared to other professors who teach finance. Study the lecture slides, review the hw, and go to office hours and you could probably pull of an A.

this professor is very understanding and cares about his students alot. he makes lecture interesting and is very clear in what he explains. the textbook definitely helped out alot b/c it explained in more detail of concepts and gave you formulas. getting the text is recommended for this class...very cool teacher tho!

i went into this class thinking that it was going to be really hard but it turned out to be ok.  his notes aren't very helpful just go through the book yourself and do some examples. DEFINITELY get this text book. the TEXT BOOK IS VERY HELPFUL!! if i didn't have the text i think i would've failed the class! overall not a bad class
he is good

namvar is very easily the best professor at the business school. he really cares about the students and does what he can to help you in every way. no required book, notes are free, exams are straight from the notes. p.s. don't take prof khoury's class, you won't learn anything from him.
Lectures are review of the slides he has posted on ilearn. 3 exams, which if you read the book and went over the notes you will do ok. He does curve so it does help. Overall good professor.
very cool and you learn a lot. he teaches you real world application. smart guy and funny!
just pay attention and take notes. i got an A

He just lectures off slides that are from the textbook. He shouldn't be a professor. Exams are multiple choice but class average is a low C. You won't learn from him, best thing is to learn by yourself.
You have to be really paying attention to understand what he is trying to say. Pay attention, and you'll learn more. Other than that, he'll try to help you out if he can
lectures were soo boring. he can't teach but if you study it wont be that bad
No Comments

Extremely nice and approachable. Is very lengthy when he talks, but you can tell he is doing it just to make sure you understand it well. A lot of homework, but it really helps. Make sure to do them. Read the book or watch videos but make sure to stay on top of all the lessons. Definitely do the test your knowledge questions at the end of each ch.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Caring

reviews.comment: He is a very difficult professor. Go to class and put in the best effort and go to his office hours if you need help. Study the material before class and make sure you understand the material before lecture to follow along. Uses analogies to understand and gives clickers. Try your best go to office hours, go SI sessions, put in the effort.

Had him for the first half of bio 5A, second half with martins-green. I have to say he's the more clear one of the two, and I enjoyed his section more. He's super helpful and really knows his bio. Honestly, if you took AP biology, this class is basically just review.

Monotone but funny.  Final was nothing like the Midterms. It was 100 questions and felt like hell. Do not study last min. unless you plan on failing. CPR's are pretty easy if you go to TA office hours and ask for help. I got a B bc I did not really prepare that well for the Final.

Dr. Nothnagel is a good professor who helps students who come to him with questions. He has a likeable attitude and he definitely isn't mean or intimidating. He liked bringing up his power points from lecture in office hours, so if office hours aren't your thing, then his power points are a good resource.
Homework/exam questions are super long but provide a lot of background info that help answer the question. Good professor overall. Gives clicker questions. Very helpful outside of lecture.

Good lecturer. Need to attend class and take notes, the exams are based solely on lectures. Don't need book. He is a great professor to get to know for opportunities and letters of rec. He really cares and is interested in all his students. Great to take advantage of if you are a top student.

Absolutely terrible professor. Teaching style is useless. Very monotone and just reads off his paper. Test material is not reflective of what he goes over in class. To top it off, he is extremely rude and unapproachable. AVOID AT ALL COSTS.
I love his voice! He tries to explain things clearly. Great professor but midterm and final are HARD!!!

Professor Nothnagel is super friendly and brings an exciting tone to biology. He tires to rally the students to be excited by the subject and he tries to liven the lesson with examples we can relate to.
He reminds me of the grandpa from Up. He is a great professor; just his tests are a pain in the butt. Make sure you study. AP Bio was easier than this class, I'll tell you that.

He is an amazing professor who really cares about his students. He attends almost all of the labs and even introduces himself to each student and memorizes everyone's names. He really goes out of his way to help students learn. He is always available through ilearn or office hours. Great professor. I highly recommend taking any class he teaches.

Nothnagel actually cares about your progress in his class. I hated plant bio in the beginning, but his lectures actually made things seem relevant. His tests are not easy, but they're definitely doable if you look over the slides. Textbook not needed, but clickers are. Overall, one of the best professors at UCR I've had so far.

He really cares about his students. Always available for office hours and puts all of his notes on the chalkboard. Wants you to do well but won't just give out good grades - he makes you earn them. Also, he makes you think about the material instead of purely memorizing it.

I don't really understand why people are complaining about him. They probably didn't even try, or they tried minimally. Nothnagel is one of the best professors I have had. He's a really nice guy, and I'm so happy that I was able to have him as my 5a teacher. He taught me so much, and he's always available to help. Great, dorky personality too!

This professor made Biology a nightmare for me.  I went to his office hours, and he was useless.  I was passing biology until the final.  The final was very hard and there was a 100 questions on that final.  Do not take this professor.  He will ruin your GPA.
His class is the worst. Unnecessarily difficult in order to weed out students from the pre-med track. Very discouraging. Tests are ridiculously hard. Very stubborn.
the best celular biology teacher i have ever had., dont miss the oppotunity to take his couse if you really want to learn biology

He is a very straightforward teacher; he puts his notes on the board, gives examples, and is enthusiastic. Material is thoroughly covered. I would advise studying if you don't have a very good memory. This is by NO means a class meant to weed out students from the pre-med track. This is just an involved class that requires interest! I enjoyed it.

I took his research class this year. It was not hard, but took me a lot of time for waiting. His lab is old. You need to learn how to use an very old balance. If you want to learn something new, you'd better to find an 'new' lab.

Nothnagel is the perfect introductory professor. He explains everything in such a way that the material seems interesting and easy to follow. His HW and tests are straight forward and fair. If you get the chance take his course over anyone else.
Nothnagel's really cool. He really cares for you and your grade. His lectures are interesting to listen to and his midterm is REALLY straightforward.

Be careful, he is a very hard teacher. His class is designed to weed students out of pre-med track, so just know an A is hard to come by. Wasn't helpful in his office hours, made exams very hard, and just expected too much out of an intro bio class. I got an A- but had to WORK.....If you want an A, I recommend taking someone else

He is honestly one of the best but hardest biology teacher. However, he is able to make the class exciting and all you really need is his notes. He truly cares about his students and is a joy to have as a teacher. I miss getting a solid A by 4 points but it is possible. You will learn in his class. So i recommend taking him.

The best prof I have had here at Riverside so far. Do not take martin's green if you can help it. :P He might be hard but at least you will learn something in the class and his teacher style is superior to the other bio prof's.

Doctor Nothnagel truly cares about the students' progress in the class. You don't really need the textbook. Just look at his class notes and homework. He makes biology extremely interesting. I am definitely going to miss his class.
awesome nerdy and understanding
He's a pretty good professor. You really don't need the textbook. Exam quations come from hw and self quiz from textbook. If you study you will do good.

I have had Dr. Nothnagel for two classes, and I thought he was great both times.  He is seriously adorable and works so hard for his students.  His tests are difficult, but fair.  He won't ever trick you, but don't underestimate them!

Once when bell rang and people began to leave when he was not finished he tripped out and demanded everyone to sit back down and chased down this guy who didnt ROFL.  This is the only thing I remembered from his class.

he is a very good professor, he is very clear in what he is teaching. he explains the material really well. his midterms were similar to the homework and was a fair game, it came the lecture notes and the homework.

Not sure what the people below me are talking about....this guy was difficult. His test questions were so obscure. He's not extremely hard but he sure isn't as easy as these two people are making it to be...

don't really need to read the book because class notes should be enough for hw and tests. great at helping and office hours. midterm questions are god awfully long and unfair in a way because we only have 60 minutes. other than that pretty good professor.

He's excellent. The person below me is true. His tests are based on the notes and HW's but they might be long.. no curve though. As long as u 're willing to dedicate your time for Bio 5A and know the materials u'll probably get at least B or eventually A. He also works very hard for us. He wants his students to succeed. He's funny-looking btw.
he is so cute. and really helps the whole class stay on top of things. he explains very well. tests are based of the chap questions on back of each chapter and pop quizes. very easy tests.
his tests are really hard.  he has a squeaky voice.
A great teacher. Was very helpful. Some of his exam questions were hard, but most weren't that bad. Also his lectures are very helpful. Just attend lecture and you can get a good grade.
I love this man!  His tests are hard, so don't underestimate them, but he is a kick ass teacher.

He is a very caring prof. Very comforting attitude. His hw is a little tougher than Martin-Greens, but his overall teaching style is A LOT better. Make sure your notes are organized and you should be ok

He is a really good professor. He is very easy to understand and he is quite helpful when you have questions. I recomend that anyone whose interested in this class, take it because you can pass if you take notes.

he is pretty hard but is really good at teaching the material. If you keep up with his teachings you will be fine! he has hard tests though! but he really cares about the students and if they are learning! loved him!

This professor is very nice and explain the material very clearly. His Homeworks are very helpful. His midterm is very similiar to his HW, self-quiz and the majority of the material comes from his lecture notes.

he's a really good professor.  his lectures are great and his teaching style is awesome.  he's just a really hard teacher tho.  but if you try and read the book and go to lecture, you'll be fine.  oh yea his online hw is super hard but study those for the tests!
HARD AS HELL! i dont know why he's getting all these happy face comments for. 90% of the class in the winter quarter got Cs and Ds!
hard, but very informative and helpful.
Can be a boring when giving lectures, do not recomend taking him for an early morning class.  TA Mitch is excellent.
hate this class. hard to pass. if possible, try to avoid taking his class. same w/ martins-green

He's a hard, but great professor, so study hard. Grading scale is pretty fair.  We had homework in the class, which helped a lot.  Midterms/Finals were somewhat hard, but they weren't horrible.  He writes on the board a lot, which helped.  Great professor overall.

Nothnagel is the most cool teacher that I ever had.His class is very hard but he is very helpfull during office hour. He give very hard test but useful notes in lectures. If you study very hard then you will pass with a C's or B's grade but not likely an A's. (Charming guy!Very Sexxy!)

His lectures were all on the board, which made it easy to understand.  For my class, the midterms questions were pretty much taken off of the hw.  Midterm was decent.  I highly recommend this professor!
he's boring and his exams are EXTREMELY difficult! needless to say, i didn't pass his class.

Great professor, very clear and helpful.  People complaining about the CSI/Survivor questions don't know how to take tests -- most of the page of reading could be skipped, CSI question could be solved by elimination.
He is a great professor and mentor. I was lucky to be his student (not the grade), but his way of life and how he go about thing make him a great mann
He's a nice guy, but the types of questions that he asks on the tests are very long and time consuming.

he has these crazy csi/survivor questions that are a page or 2 long and with barely any time to read them, let alone answer them. he's a nice guy but a very tough teacher with no curving at all. every quarter at least 60% fail and he doesn't care.

I found the class hard. The test question was a page and a half- completely rediculous. While we were trying to read it, our hour for a midterm was slowly fading away! It seems like he and his co-lecturer take pride in their increasing failure rates.
hard class, great teacher

This teacher wants to help you understand.  He's definitely the best teacher I've had at UCR.  Even with the enormous size of the class, he is still very approachable.  The class is hard, but he makes it interesting.
"Find something to get excited about," the famous opening words of this remarkable professor.  You are in good hands- simply trust his challenges.
he knows his stuff.  don't bs him.  attendance matters in the class too.

About 60% fails each quarter. His tests kick your butt, and there's no curving. Given all that, this guy wants you to succeed, and he makes himself available. Wierd class, you want to hate him 'cause it's so hard, but you can't, because he's so nice.
Although the material wasn't super interesting, Prof. Evans made it enjoyable and stress-free. The class was easy-going, and I learned more than I expected to. She is a great professor

reviews.comment: Professor Evans is knowledgeable within her field. The class consisted only of 2 short papers one in class midterm and a final 15 page research paper. Not a harsh grader either. The 15 page might sound like a lot but professor Evans is more than happy to answer any questions about it and gives more than enough time to do it. Discussion is mandatory

Just downright awesome.
As long as you do the reading and participate in class, you'll be fine. He's also pretty insightful and engaging, so just pay attention and take notes.

We stopped using the textbook 3 weeks into the quarter and nothing was graded until the end of finals week so we had to just live with the grade we were surprised with at the end. If you don't participate at lease twice a week it will tank your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The discussions were valuable for understanding the readings and the professor always made the classes fun by going on tangents about what the class is discussing and being a relatable person. That being said, you do need to be a good writer to earn a good grade, and a fast one for essay 1 because you only have 2 class periods to write it.

Really great professor—super accessible. Attendance was mandatory, but it was very clear that he cared for each and every one of his students. He consistently encouraged us to participate in each class and pushed us to stay engaged.

Dr. Evans is very welcoming of every student's ideas and is a great teacher overall. If he does criticize them, he does so in a way that is not discouraging and connects it to the overall conversation. It made it very easy to participate every class. Though his class is objectively difficult, his feedback and class discussions are very helpful.

reviews.comment: Prof. Taylor is a really, really nice and understanding. In some cases he could be considered a hard graded, but as long as you follow the guidelines and rubric you should be fine. Moreover, take advantage of his office hours, it will really help you out and get you that A.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I had him for ENGL1A in the Fall of 2024 and for ENGL004 during my freshman year. Honestly one of the best English professors at UCR. He is a very understanding person and grants a ton of extensions (with valid reasoning), even though he isn't a fast grader, he gives everyone a fair chance and helps you improve when needed. Great professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Good professor. Managed to get a B in his class. Wish he wasn't so tough in his grading for essays

I would honestly recommend doing the readings and reaching out to your TA. My TA was a big reason I did good on the midterms!

reviews.comment: Professor Fischer is an extremely wise individual who will teach you a lot philosophy. This class was a favorite of mine. The class only has three exams - two midterms and one final. There's one book required for the class which was a really good read! Overall an amazing class and an amazing professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Just read read read, if you go into lecture already done with the assign readings, lecture should not be too heavy. He has jokes sometimes, and there really is no lecture slides, he just talks a lot. Test should not be hard if you understand each main idea of a chapter. I would encourage to really study his study guides.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I wouldn't miss out on Professor Fischer. He's a Distinguished Professor of Philosophy at UCR and it's an honor to take his courses. You will do well in his class if you are passionate, have a strong background in philosophy, and can write good philosophy papers. I highly recommend his Metaphysics course; he is a leading figure in this area.

He is an OK professor. He does answer any questions you might have in class or through email which I appreciate because there are some professors who don't even bother responding to your email. His voice gets a bit boring in the long wrong.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very clear & fair professor, no surprises. He does repeat a lot of ideas, but if you jot down notes of what he repeats you'll notice that its the answers to the short answer exams, you just have to expand on it using book/lecture material. Hes got a monotone voice, but his humor will definitely get you to enjoy most lectures with some laughs!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Fischer is a good professor. This is my second time having him as a professor. I had him for PHIL001 and the format was exactly the same apart from not having quizzes. Two midterms (20pts each), Attendance (20pts) and Final (40 pts). Exams are short answer questions. As long as you do the readings and take notes, it should be easy B.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Fischer is a very nice professor. He's very monotone and the seminar tends to drag, but the topics we read about were very interesting. He's kind and approachable, so don't be afraid to ask him if you get stuck. Only one paper due at the end, don't procrastinate.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I loved taking Dr. Fischer's class. His lectures are very dense and it can get a little boring, but as long as you do the readings and go to discussion it'll be fine. His midterms and final were a bit tricky because they're all free response. You really need to understand the material and expand upon it with your own objections and/or agreements.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: YOU WILL FALL ASLEEP IN LECTURE. Unless you get a good T.A., you probably will have a tough time in this class. He goes off on tangents a lot and is very monotoned. He doesn't use slides either so it's quite boring. Grading consists of 2 midterms, a final, and weekly quizzes in discussion. All of the test are essay questions.

Only went to lecture once and got an easy A. The T.A.s will literally review everything on the midterms and final in discussion, so you never have to study for more than two days before the exam. The tests are free response but they give you 5 prompts and you only have to answer 3 of them plus an EC question on the tests. Also discussion quizzes.

John Fischer is a very well-spoken professor who teaches very difficult topics, my only complaint is that his tone is very monotone and his tests are long and somewhat difficult so be prepared to come to class, pay attention, and participate.
Fischer, while passionate about philosophy, rambles. However, if you go to discussion and actually read the assignments, you really don't even have to listen to him.

Great teacher! His voice is a little monotone and he tends to repeat himself a fair amount, which makes the lectures a little boring, though you're almost sure to pick up on the material if you're doing the reading (a MUST, by the way). He's super friendly, he grades fairly, he's transparent about his exams. I'd love to take another class from him!
I loved this class! Very interesting.He's a great Professor in Philosophy. He was clear and concise in his lectures. I would definitely take another class taught by him.

Good professor. As long as you do the reading and really think about the material you should do well. My friends who took the class said they thought he was boring, and I can understand that. But I had section with him and he is a really good guy and very helpful too.

This class is not easy unless you pay attention to the lectures. Everything he says are basically the answers for the midterms & final. So if you really want to get an A, go to every lecture and pay close attention to what he says & takes notes.
At first it was boring & monotone but towards the end you notice his humor, he's really funny, I enjoyed this class and lowkey kinda miss it!

Obviously, this class is not even remotely easy (you should know this coming). Material is difficult to analyze and comprehend, and exams are PURELY essay-based regarding book content (he wrote the book). I would say lecture is mandatory, considering. GO TO CLASS, TAKE NOTES, AND READ THE BOOK. You can pass, just try. It's GE, right?

material was difficult to understand even though i read through all the material at least twice. exams are purely essay based and depend on your ability to interpret the "meanings", and arguments behind the various topics addressed in the class.

he doesn't care he put resp. on his TAs.  TAs are not helpful. He is unorganized.  His lec. notes don't have title and are bad hand writing.  The TAs were not helpful to answer the questions and hehimself does,t care to listen.  At last some TAs curved and some didn't.  If you don't have to don't take this class. It lowers your grades and takes tim

Yeah, the class material challenging, and you have to be able to write, read and think to do well in the class. Not a thrilling lecturer, but the guy knows his stuff. It really does make you think. This is what you went to college for. Don't be a wimp.
This class is way hard. TAs are very bad, too. If you get nice TA, then you will pass. Do not think about getting A from this class.

Never take it, unless you have really smart friends to get answer from them. He is boring, not easy at all, you have to write well for every tests, and TA s are  hard grader, they grade hard for this class.
This class is horrible with him. I attended this class everyday. Some TAs grade very hardly. Not helpful. Not clear. Not easy.

He does not write down his lecture clearly.  The lecture notes we have to write it ourselves or you wont understand what he is trying to say. It is a very boring class.  Midterms and finals are jus essay. It is so hard to stay focus when he lecture.   He is not helpful unless you pay attention which is very hard.

His class is so boring, monotone voice. And his midterm is based on the writing skill, how well you explain basic concept. If you are good at writing, you can finish midterm study in 30 minutes. But if you are not good at writing, then you will get****ty grade even though you got the concept. If you want to get an A, then you have to study forever
boring but isn't too hard of a prof. =) very nice.  the way he talks/looks reminds me of dr. phil
Just take good notes. He gives EVERYONE B's. For an A, you might have to kiss a little a**.
pretty easy. great discussions. fun class. =D
Good Teacher, Good Class.  There's a lot of bad Phil. teachers at UCR, but Fischer isn't one of them.  Take him if you can.  He even wrote me a letter of rec.  Great Guy.

Ok after a disasterous showing in phil 7 I thought about quitting philosophy.  Dr. Fischer brought the study of ethics down to a very personal level for me.  I will always remember his character.  Great teacher and interesting class
Classes are easy breezy.  Be opinionated and willing to back it up and you can get great grades.
Dr. Fischer is an excellent philosophy professor!! If you can take a class with him, DO SO!!
This guy is funny in his own way. He's a cool guy, but he repeats himself too much. I wasn't too interested in this stuff before the class, and I'm not really that interested afterwards either.

This guy has been teaching the same course since 1980.  That's longer than I've been alive.  He knows the material very well, and he seems really laid back and relaxed.  I like his class, it's also very interesting lecture material.
This man is a very gentle genius who is sexy in his middle aged kind of way. Very funny too!
he's great! thought he was boring at first, but turned out to be very humorous in a lowkey kind of way. his story about meeting his wife is definitely the funniest!
a little stale and monotone but obviously knows philosophy.  interesting to talk to, open to hearing everyone's opinion.  ask him about his veganism.
Very good philosophy teacher
Great professor that gives really good advice and tips on real life things like jobs. Final project is an interview. Grades okay not too harsh.

Extremely tough grader. Got an 80 and it was a C+ according to his own grading scale. Extremely vague with what he wanted out of assignments and graded them hard. If you take him go to office hours and ask what he wants because he wont post it. Felt lost throughout the entire class.

Uses lecture materials that are not even his own, and has recycled it for years; lecture slides are full of information. Good luck taking notes fast enough. Assigns a large marketing plan as a final project instead of a grade, but is very vague about what he expects.

He never seemed very knowledgeable about the material he was covering. He recycles the same lectures from different classes and goes way off topic. No one would show up for lectures. I don't care about my grade as much as taking something away from the class. He doesn't read the papers, he puts them through a program to grade. Tests are from a bank

Lectures cover the book and his own take on what he thinks we should learn. His lectures are fun and engaging by making jokes, using videos from shows, and understanding his students to get teach a concept. He has to include boring info slides/videos from at times, but followed by a funny video to lighten the mood and transition to next the topic.
He give you a low grade on essay without telling you reason, even you ask for a feedback. Only word he said is "not deep advise"
Best teacher in UCR in my opinion. Do yourself a favor and take his classes. You'll actually understand how to get a job.
He is extremely helpful, and genuinely cares about his students. He makes class interesting, and he gives you the materials to pass, you just have to be willing to do the work.

Professor Fialho aims to provide a class that teaches you useful information - he accomplishes this most of the time. Classes are primarily watching videos with brief interludes of lecture. Assignments are mostly writing based, save for one math assignment. All exams are online. Show up, do the work, and you'll be okay. Just monitor your grades.

Professor First is by far one of my favorite professors at UCR! She is very organized and the lectures were interesting. The workload is fair and her exams are not difficult. She would accommodate if needed and was always available. I enjoyed her class very much! I recommend taking her :)
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She is awesome. Her lectures are organized and easy to follow. She explains concepts well and provide examples so that we understand it more. There are 3 short assignments and she drops the lowest score on one. Also, 2 exams and they were relatively easy as long as you understand information in lecture. I would definitely take her again
Great professor, she provides clear recorded lectures that are engaging. I hope to take another class with her before I graduate, shes been my favorite professor at UCR so far.
Had the opportunity to study happiness though coursework with professor Firat. So grateful and lucky to have had her as a professor. If you have the chance take her. She is wonderful!

Professor Firat was pretty easy and the lectures were powerpoints. I took her winter20 which consisted of pop quizzes, a midterm, and an online final (bc of the rona). Overall the readings weren't too long and the material was easy to understand.

Professor Firat is great, she is clear in her lectures and is very fair on exams. Pop Quizzes are frequent, but its literally just on the lecture of that day, so as long as you pay attention, you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr Firat is amazing! Show up to class because she gives pop quizzes, but they're always based on what you just learned and she goes over them before you take the quiz. Very friendly, tests were not very hard as long as you studied the notes. Makes lectures very interesting. I loved attending her class

She is quite professional. Her exams are from her lecture slides and quite fair; she explains everything and allows for class discussions. No essays were necessary in this class, and the pop quizzes are really just to measure attendance. I strongly recommend her.

Dr. Firat is great. She uses mostly powerpoints and gives pop quizzes, but she is thorough and always available to help. She also gives great study guides and practice exams that helped out big-time throughout the quarter. She's a solid professor and I highly recommend taking her for Soc 4. TIP, use the old edition of the book. Much cheaper!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: CBNS116 is dense, but Professor Fiacco is clear about that from the start. He genuinely wants students to understand the material and provides everything you need to succeed. This class is not an "easy A", but it is fair. If you're ready to work and want to actually learn, you'll grow a lot here. A tough class doesn't mean the professor is bad.

Dr. Fiacco is an excellent professor, who clearly cares about the success of his students. I took him for 106 & 116 and his class is structured perfectly - he literally gives you all the resources to succeed, but it's up to you to use them. Go to lecture, don't be afraid to ask questions, and study well as neuroscience is an intricate subject.

I took this class because everyone said he was amazing but this class was so bad. I'm not sure if it was him or the material but it was a lot harder than expected. He did preface it is the 4th hardest class at UCR but still so bad. Grade is based on 3 exams, and 3 quizzes, no mcq all frq. Better be ready to study for hours on end. Horrible class.

Honestly a great professor! He's really kind and gives clear, thorough lectures. Also, he does well to encourage and answer lots of questions during lectures. Attendance wasn't mandatory, but it'll be difficult to do well without attending. Most of the grade is made up by the midterm and final. Hard class, but he makes it more than manageable!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ignore the other reviews about how amazing this professor is. His slides have little to no information on them and he expects to teach yourself the content by reading a chapter of the textbook for each lecture. His exams are not fair, but instead are built to trick you on every question. If you want to at least pass you gotta teach yourself!!!!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a great professor! He's really approachable and always answers questions in class and OH. His midterm and final were very fair - he gives you all the resources to succeed,  is not easy, it's complex subject matter so you need to study on your own time in detail along with going to lecture and asking Dr. Fiacco questions!

he's an awesome professor. always willing to help and answer questions in class and OH. his exams were very fair, attending lecture and reviewing midterm thoroughly on your own time is a must! he gives a practice exam for the first exam that prepares you more than enough, and final sample questions. the book is very helpful in the first 1/2!

Professor Todd was an overall nice professor, you can tell he is a genuine good person but his lectures are tedious and makes you fall asleep. Your grade is based on the practicum (10%), midterm (45%), and final (45%), and the midterm and final had a lot of trick questions like " A, B, C, D, A&C, A&D, or all of the above".
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Great professor. Great lectures, streamlines information you need to know, gives lots of practice exam problems. His exams are very straight forward with few trick questions. 

The material of the course is easier in the first half and much harder in the second half. He only taught the first half for this quarter, so the experience may vary.

Dr. Fiacco was an amazing prof to have for the first half of 106 (another prof taught 2nd half). Lectures were pre-recorded and he had office hours that were super helpful in clearing up confusion; he really takes the time to answer thoroughly and help students understand tough material. Wish he had been teaching the full course, great professor.

Class was asynchronous so you get to watch the lectures whenever you want, don't fall behind tho. 94% of your grade is midterm and finals, 6% is discussion. Tests are super tricky, you need to understand the material well enough to answer tricky mc questions. Lectures are interesting, bland if you're not interested in the material. Curve @ the end.

Wished I listened to the other student who cautioned about taking this class. The class was solely based only 1 midterm and 1 final. No homework or extra practice that could count as points and expand on what you learned. The lectures were the definition of dull and pointless b/c it crammed too much verbal info. The testing time he gives is a joke.

Honestly, it's 2 midterms with one on first-half + anatomy and second on second half + new anatomy. The lecture was literally wtv I can't even with that one image and a word, so get prepared to fill it up with text on Notability or something. Took the 'final' thought I failed it but I ended up missing only one question like bruh.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I enjoyed the asynchronous format. I found lectures very interesting and informative. A couple of lectures were a little confusing but OH cleared that up immediately. Hes very caring for his students and wants them to succeed. Read the book, watch lectures, go to OH, do the study guide questions, and youll probably get an A.

I really enjoyed this class and the asynchronous format. It's scary grades are made up of only a midterm and a final, but if you watch all of the lectures, read the outlines, and go to office hours, not bad! Didn't need to read the textbook much unless I had questions, but usually just going to OH cleared it up. Draw things out when studying!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Despite all of the good ratings from previous quarters, I wouldn't take him now online. He made the midterm and final 50-50 of our final grade. The exam questions are really tricky, and you won't have time to look through notes. His lecture slides are boring, and you're basically just staring at his notes until you memorize it. D to C- is 60%.

The professor seems to know a lot about the material and is able to explain it in an understandable way. The downside of this class is that your grade is made up by tests only. Yes it is open note but don't rely on them helping you much since there is a huge time crunch and his questions are ultra tricky. Goodluck with this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Lect was asynchronous but midterm was taken during class time not proctored. Midterm was 70 min 55 MC q. Final was 90 min 63 MC q can't backtrack. The whole class is 50% midterm and 50% final. You won't have time to look at your notes during exam. This class is pure memorization. The average for midterm was 71%! Disc is completely diff material.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: In this class we watch lecture vides at out own time. It is not engaging at all. I hate it. The videos are extremely bland no color its just white. The exams are extremely tricky. I did really bad on my midterm. The types of midterm questions are those: none of the above, all all of the above, a and b, c and a type of question. I hate it here!!!

That 2018 comment saying this class is an easy A um no! They're playing you lol. I this class is tough but doable. The professor will give u a lot of information but its very interesting. He has lecture notes READ THOES!! know them and you'll be fine. Its going to take a lot of studying but his office hr are so helpful and the TA is awesome!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Students saying that the exam questions come straight from his notes. NOT TRUE AT ALL! His final was really hard

CBNS 106 had a new revision: half of the course was taught by Dr. Cho, the other half was taught by Dr. Fiacco. Fiacco was excellent-explains things well, really cares about his students. His final was 50 questions +2 EC (all multiple choice), but very tricky. Curve is typically 10%. 45% midterm, 10% lab practicum, 45% final.

Loved this guy! Such an awesome professor. Exam was very fair to his notes and lectures. He scans the book chapters you need, but if you memorize his notes you should be good to go. Not the easiest class but it's by no means freakishly hard. Go to class. Office hours are a GREAT way to review and clarify. Cares about his students!

He is an amazing prof. If you're a neuronerd and want to really learn I highly recommend him. Three exams that are non-cumulative (no final); they were not easy but fair to his lecture notes. He prepares you well in class so you shouldn't skip. Go to his office hours every week he clarifies all the material really well. One of my faves at UCR.

You dont need to go to lecture as you are given his self made notes which is where the test comes from. Simply study those at home and youre good. Me and my friends got almost a 100% in his class from using this method. This class is an easy A.
Awesome professor. Great guy, super informative. Great lectures. Great office hours. All around 10/10 guy and professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: probably one of the better choices for CBNS 106, took it during winter and withdrew, took it again during fall with Fiacco and did a lot better cause of the way he explained things. 1 midterm on first half of the course and final on 2nd half. His lecture notes werent super informative as others said, lectures contained a majority of material tested

One of my top professors. His lectures are long and jam packed with information  - this class is not easy - but he is one of the best teachers when it comes to providing you with the information you need. Gives amazing lecture outlines and office hours are top notch. The book is secondary to his excellent notes. Studied hard and got the A.

Great professor. Class requires a lot of attention. Would not suggest taking it with other hard classes. Go to office hours. He's always willing to re-explain hard concepts. Don't procrastinate. Exams are free response; and he always includes a couple extra credit questions. Best class I've taken in my 4 years in college. And he cute so... bonus :)
Fiacco is a 1010 professor. Eager to answer questions and repeats anything you ask. Tests are difficult but not tricky. Study hard and don't procrastinate. you will do well.

He's very nice and friendly! 30% midterm. 10% practicum. 60% final. His tests are challenging, but he is a straightforward forward professor cos he posts pdfs that include everything you really need to know. Study those! Study those!! STUDY THOSE!!! Go to office hours, even if u don't have questions it's nice review to specific points on lecture!

Tough class, no curve, everyone bombed the 2nd midterm, avg. was  55.93%... he was nice enough to make the 2nd midterm not weigh as much as he intended but yeah, this class requires tons of memorization, tests are all free response/T or F, no MC, blank out during test and youre screwed

Dr. Fiacco was an excellent professor! He is very clear, organized, and nice! He posts lectures and practice midterms and sample questions for the final. His tests are tricky, but if you know the material you should be fine! Must be willing to do the work in this class.

Never read textbook. Only studied everything on lectures. One midterm, One final and a practical. Questions are very tricky. Final included two essay questions and you chose one question to write about.

Fantastic professor. Enjoyed every single lecture and I attended every single office hour. As stated, the tests are not easy, you really have to know your stuff because a lot of the answers could be right. The subject was extremely fascinating. Overall, awesome professor (in my top 3) but you have to do the work and focus on the notes.

Ignore the comments below. This prof was pretty bad. You have to buy a reader which he claim will help you on the midterm. It was nothing like the midterm. He makes the midterm extremely tricky. where you can lim between A,B maybe C and choice D is both A,B and E is all the above. You have to know your material to do well in this class. Bad prof.

The class itself was very interesting.  I enjoyed most of the materials throughout the quarter.  Dr. Fiacco received a makeover in the middle of the quarter(trimmed his hair and shaved his beard) that came as a surprise to most students in class.  His new sharper looks definitely made a lot more students want to focus more on his lecture.

He was an interesting and engaging professor. I don't really like neuro, but he made it pretty easy. Don't buy the book or the reader, its really unnecessary since he provides you with very detailed lecture notes alongside the power points. I studied a few days before the final and midterm and ended up with an A- in the class with a 75.6%.
The only thing to focus on are his lectures and attend office hours! His midterm is hard so be prapared.

He is clear and concise. He is very big on students participating in class. Go to his office hours he is very helpful. He covers the material productively. He is one of the better CBNS professors. His tests are not tricky. He sets you up for success because his notes are so good. His lectures are my favorite. He loves teaching this stuff.
I never attended his lectures. I don't even have a book. I survived with an A. Grades are curved. Self-studiers, you will be fine with his notes only.
Kind and helpful professor but lectures were somewhat boring. Midterm and final were much easier than I expected.

He makes everything as clear as possible. His tests are not that bad. Make use of his office hours. He likes it when students ask questions. He is very organized and sets you up for success. He is excited about the material. Take this class, this professor is awesome. He is also very fair with grading.

This class was pretty easy in the sense that he's pretty organized with his print-out lecture notes and letting you know the things that are going to be on the exam. He made it seem like the multiple choice questions were extremely challenging, but when you take the test, it's really not bad at all. I'd say his pretty fair overall, take him.

"you should read each chapter about three to four times" who has time for that!?! his lectures are basic but it's pretty hard to understand him and the point he's trying to get across.  the material is pretty interesting but he makes it a lot a LOT more complicated than it actually is.  slight curve to the class, midterms and final were okay.

Hands down the worst professor I ever had. We did not have any test, but he did assign weekly pop quizzes that were mostly based on the readings or movies he had us watch in class. He hardly would spend time on lectures, but when he did he would mumble a lot so it seemed like he didn't know what he was talking about.
This teacher is a waste of time and money. Please listen to the comments below, no wonder he's not a full time professor.

He is the worst professor I have ever taken! He gives stupid pop quizzes that are random. He doesn't know how to have a conversation, his class is boring and he waist time. He gives extra credit which is the only thing good with him. I wouldn't be surprised if hes not back at UCR next semester. No final or midterm which was good!

Everyone was lost at the beginning because he didn't know what he was doing. He's not a good professor because all he does is shuffle around the front of the room and read his notes. He mumbles A LOT, so sit close. The class had 4 quizzes, 4 assignments, discussion, and a final. It was nearly impossible to not get an A or B. Offers extra credit too

Really enjoyed this class with Professor Field on Civil War, Race, and Reconstruction; it made me realize how little I knew about the period. Classes were a mix of powerpoint lectures and discussion of readings homework (usually 40-60 pgs between each class meeting).  Assessments were online reading responses, the midterm test, & 2 long essays.

Professor Field is the most difficult professor I have ever had. She is very dry on her lectures and requieres the students to attend writting workshops. This is a history class, not an english one. She reads word for word from her notes. Her grading is unfair and her midterm impossible. She is a new professor so avoid her!
SOOO boring and i learned most everything in the 8th grade not a good choice for people who like history

Professor Field is the best professor I have had thus far at UCR. She's incredibly knowledgeable and passionate, and is more than willing to answer questions and help students. The lectures are sometimes dry, but generally the points are well made, and class readings supplement them nicely. A must take professor.

She has 2 types of class days: 1) she reads word for word from her lecture slides (In my opinion, that's not teaching, it's reading...something I can do on my own.) I leave her class feeling just the same as when i entered. She taught me nothing, the readings did. And 2) days where we 'talk' about assigned readings which are far more helpful.

I've taken Professor Field for HISA113/115/116. She is SO unbelievably knowledgeable, willing to help, and keeps you captivated in lecture. The reading is very interesting and helpful. Take her for Slavery and the Old South; she'll teach you everything they WON'T teach you in high school. Great professor, fair grader, and HIGHLY reccomended.

Field is a great young professor who is EXTREMELY knowledgeable in her field. She has creds from Harvard and NYU so following her lead will likely do one well for furthering their education. The readings are fairly heavy (around 40 pages between class meetings), but are also very informative. She grades very fairly.
Great professor! one of the best at UCR. she is extremely helpful and her grading is very straight forward. easy class just do readings and show up to lecture.

Professor Field is too much for words. She's extraordinarily smart and compassionate, and she will push you to your limits! I would one million percent reccomend her, and am planning on taking my seminar with her Winter 2011. Take her and you won't regret it! She changed my life, and I'm sure she'll change yours too.
Great professor. Very lenient on grading. Drops a lot of things in every category which is cool. Great guy and pretty clear grading criteria.

Kind of confused by all of the bad reviews, great professor, chill overall. Tests and assessments are super straightforward, as long as you do the practice and hw, there shouldn't be any surprises. Great overall vibe, very understanding too.

Professor Flegal is so passionate and it shows! The class was pretty easy at first, but it definitely got harder gradually. For each tests he gives, he provides a practice version. If you understand the practice, you'll do just fine. There were never any curve-balls on any of the tests and the lab was really easy.

Flegal praised his curve all throughout the spring 2021 quarter even though he didnt curve anything towards the end. The more evidencethe class has mastered the materialmore generous the curve will be.-HIS syllabus. Class did improve with the avg midterm being 54% while the final was 78%, but he didnt stand by his words (coward move).

Stat100A with Flegal is not a hard course, however, I am writing this because of his blatant lies to our Spring 2021 class. Dr. Flegal had said on recording that there would be no extra credit for iEval's as he is curving the course. As he put grades in, he actually ignored the curve, and when we tried to reach out to him, ignored us as well.

He broke down the material well, and was enthusiastic about his work. Extremely intelligent TA.

AMAZING!  I failed Soc 5 twice (with Swanson & Kposowa) before I had him for summer school.  He really breaks the material down and makes it easy to understand.  I'd definitely take another class with him and I highly recommend him to those who have struggled with Soc 5 before.
this dude is a trip. easily one of the best instructors ive had. great passion for the subject. definetly recommend.
A little harsh when it comes to grading. However, gives you propers tools to carry out what needs to be done. Great at explaining very difficult concepts. Makes dull classes as exciting as possible.

While the students teach.

Dr. Wilson is a wonderful French professor!  She has a very laid back personality and is extremely approachable.  She is always full of energy and spunk, which makes her class enjoyable.   She is always willing to help students out and do whatever it takes to help them understand something.

Dr. Wilson is hilarious. Once you get to know her, you will really enjoy her class. She is easy-going and makes me feel like I can make mistakes. Recommend
So so helpful and kind!  I learned so much in this class even though I didn't love the quizzes.:)
awesome, kind teacher. Great TA for my french film course. thanks!
awesome teacher! I don't understand some of the other comments here.

Very knowledgable! Definitely a class that you will LEARN something in! She's not too stingy with her As but you must go to office hours and actually work on the papers to get an A! SHE'S MY FAV TEACHER EVER. SUPER SMART AND NICE.

notes are essential to get a good grade.

Shes okay not the worst but she does not explain her instructions well, Every assignment is very confusing as her dirctionson are very unclear Also she yapps ALOT so if you get her just know that classes feel like 5 years because she talks a lot and very slow. tough grader on the essays but will actually help you if it you need overall id stay away

Her essay prompts were confusing, she's a tough grader, you had to go to office hours to get an A (MAYBE), and she assigned an insane amount of homework. AVOID at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Please do not take any classes with this professor. Her tone is rude, her essay prompts are confusing and have no room for creativity, and she assigns way too much work than she is able to handle. I am not afraid of doing a lot of work but she overwhelmed me with homework and readings that did not fit the structure of a summer course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Friedrich is a very passionate in English and tries to rub that passion onto her students. Many of the students I have seen complain in her class simply do not put the work in for their grade. She is tough but fair; ask questions and think deeply about the prompts and you will do great. Be prepared for a lot of work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Has an obnoxious teaching tone, complex essay prompts, and an unorganized Canvas.
Will not specify on anything or make any slight reminders and will always defer you to the syllabus. Also requires much more activities than just a the papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Obnoxious teaching tone throughout every lecture, makes kids not want to participate. Assignments are graded after you forget they exist. Definitely a textbook teacher who talks a lot and says nothing. Essay prompts are vague and most assignments feel like busywork. You can tell who had her online vs in-person. Boring class for my English haters.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She makes you work for your grade. You don't have to go to office hours, but approach her in class with your questions and concerns (she keeps this in mind with your participation score). Go to class, if you dont you wont understand how to do the complex prompts. With her feedback and going to the UCR writing center for peer reviews, you'll do good
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: My best advice for taking Dr. Friedrich is go to office hours. Her office hours are extremely helpful and she will give you direct advice. She expects you to think outside the box and make interesting and unique commentary in your essays, but if you struggle with this at all go to office hours. Also she's not super picky about grammar and structure

Surprisingly, I loved this class. It is clear professor Freidrich has a passion for teaching and she is by far the most accessible professor I have had at this university. Content is relevant so it is easy to stay engaged, but she really makes you think outside of the box to earn your grade. Grades based on complexity so papers are tough.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I was hesitant to take this class with professor Friedrich because of previous ratings, but she was amazing! She is so helpful and easy to access outside class time. She provides good feedback for what she expects on papers. The class is super interactive and I loved all the topics and readings we did. I recommend!

Professor Friedrich is the best professor for ENGL1B. She is so understanding and caring, willing to help you at any time. Through the course we wrote 4 different essays. They were difficult to write but she helps you along the way and is understanding if you need more time to write the essays.
Unorganized teaching style and passive aggressive tone made it very difficult to understand the complex essay prompts.
Super helpful and flexible with grading. Gives good feedback on essays and thoughtful insights on the importance of this class and what it teaches!

Professor Friedrich does not explain the essay prompts well at all. She makes things VERY confusing and hard to understand. Compared to the other professors teaching English at UCR, she is definitely one of the hardest so if you have the chance to take the course with another professor I highly advise you do so.

I took this professor during my Fall 2019, I was scared for the portfolio as I saw other comments. To be honest, if youre willing to keep all classwork material in a separate folder youre absolutely fine. Her essay feedback is amazing! I passed thinking I was going to fail this course. You got this!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Friedrich was an awesome professor out of my english classes in UCR. She really was passionate and cared if you really did put out your thoughts in your essay. There were a good amount of readings to do but it was doable and it also supported the essays we were doing for the unit.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: She is an amazing professor, tough grader but offers a lot of office hours. If you go to her office hours she will help you write an outline for you essay if you are having trouble with it. Do the readings, and don't slack off. Also, she doesn't give you busy work so you won't have to worry about dumb assignments.

She is accessible outside of class, but she is a very tough grader. If you are looking to just take the class and don't really enjoy English, this class won't be fun. She also gives little to no direction in her prompts as well as expects you to know exactly what she wants.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Professor Friedrich cares about your thoughts and putting together an essay with original thoughts. Although the prompts are vague, she will help you with composing an essay that meets the requirements. Also, she is very accessible outside of class and is there to address any concerns you may have. STAY ORGANIZED!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: at first i thought she was a harsh grader, but she actually cares about how you put your thoughts together in an essay. of course it's not an easy class if you don't enjoy english, but if you work for a passing grade you'll pass. stay organized, she won't really tell you what to put in the end portfolio because she expects you to be responsible
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: She is very weird and focuses on zombies. I really disliked the topic of the class and the professor at first, but if you do all the readings you will truly enjoy the class.
