Waltz's class is super exciting... only if you enjoy listening to the many interpretations of how to sound out vowel sounds. It's the lamest class I have every taken. Too bad it's a requirement! Go to class regularly and try to stay awake...
her accent is not that bad.....the class is extremely boring...I guarantee u will fall asleep.......
Get over the accent thing.

Damn, her class is as exciting as watching paint dry off the wall. It was an easy class,  but so dumb. I'm a physics major with a minor in chem, and I took this out of the blue, but no more ling for me.

HARD TO UNDERSTAND BECAUSE OF HER ACCENT. VERY UNCLEAR. WHAT WAS ON THE STUDY GUIDES IS NOT ON HER TEST. NOT ORGANIZED IN PUTTING UP YOUR GRADES. MAKES YOU FEEL STUPID IF YOU ASK A QUESTION. I DIDN'T LEARN MUCH. BUT YOU DO GET CREDIT FOR DOING THE HOMEWORK EVEN IF IT IS WRONG.
Prof. Waltz is a great teacher. I would love to take more of her classes, because she is enthusiastic, kind, smart, and funny. The class is very interesting!

Ling 20 is so straight forward and Prof. Waltz outlines everything that will be on the exams in the study guides, and homework counts as credit if you do it. She is resourceful and knows what she is lecturing about and her accent is not even bad. Geez, whiners.
Wow Prof. Waltz is really an amazing person she cares about the students and lends a helping hand when you need it. She has to be one of my favorite Prof. during my 1st year of college.

I have no idea what you past people are talking about because Dr. Waltz is one of the best professors at UCR.  Not only is she incredibly helpful, she is one of the nicest and sweetest people you'll ever meet.  She really cares about her students.  I am more than happy to have taken her classes for the last four quarters.
Great professor. Great Classes (Ling 20, 21, 111, 121, 141). Good projects. Interesting papers. I learned a lot in her classes. She goes slow enough to understand the concepts.
Sometimes late but not always... great teacher and person!!
the weekly assignments are pretty easy if you pay attention but the midterm and finals are pretty hard. she has a harsh accent so pay attention.
Her tests are kind of hard and study guides aren't the greatest, I thought the test were over-graded, you weren't given points for something right but lost points for something wrong.

Class is much harder than she says, there is nothing you need to know after the first mid term EXCEPT sentence trees, because 60% of the final is on those. She shows up to class late everytime, never there during her office hours, and her english is not very good becuase of her accent. Do not take!

Always late, she walks in late to class all the time, at least 20 minutes. She came in 35 minutes late to the Mid-term. She teaches different terms that what the book says. Never in her office during her 'office hours'.

THIS CLASS IS DUMB. YOU WILL NEVER USE ANY OF IT AND SHE SWEARS ITS THE BIBLE. NO CURVE. SHES LATE ALL THE TIME AND IF YOU NEED TO GO OVER SOMETHING SHE WONT BE IN HER OFFICE DURING OFFICE HOURS AND IF YOU MAKE AN APPOINTMENT SHE WILL BE THERE 30 MINS LATE.

Interesting, laid back type of course. Homework is about the amt u get in elementary school. Not much material covered which makes studying a breeze. Go to class, pay a little attn then nothin to do outside of class. Go for it! Anything less then it wouldnt be considered a class.
always late to class! I would be embarrased to be a prof and constantly get to class 15-20 min late and unprepared.
Readings are confusing, but lectures are clear. You really have to study for the tests.

teaches terms that are different in the book.  1/2 hour late for final exam with minimal excuse.  things on study guide not on exam.  does not put homework online.  tests on subjects only minimally discussed in class.
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments

Productive classes, relevant homework, good lectures that make sense.  She makes the dense material in the linguistics classes and concepts easy and very well-presented.  Her (upper division) classes have a small, friendly, accessible feel.
Extremely inaccessible at office hours.  Watch out for mis-grading.
Good teaching style, cares about his students.

The lectures are very important and information dense. Goes off on tangents a bit but they are interesting and relevant to chemistry beyond 002A. The tests (2 midterms + final) were moderately difficult and not easy to prepare for besides the final. The final was the first 2 midterms almost exactly + chapter 6 and 7 problems. Very engaging.

I did above average on both midterms and final. Read the book and do practice problems! Also, do your homework and study! The class is not an easy A but with hard work you can get A. There were no practice exams so you had to go to class. He is very generous when it comes to grading!!! The homework had a 2% penalty which was unfair.

Harman wasn't bad. For midterms review homework and textbook for conceptual questions. Go over your midterms in office hours as he repeats some questions on the final. Quizzes in discussion were easy and lowest 2 were dropped. He was a solid lecture who made Chemistry interesting (I hated 1B material) and made me want to go to class. Overall solid.

I think this is Harman's first time teaching Chem1C. His lectures are really confusing and sometimes he confuses himself trying to explain the stuff we are supposed to learn(which makes me worry a lot). He also doesn't really explain how he gets his answers which is frustrating because he avoids explaining even after you ask. He's funny sometimes:/
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lots of work for homework. Homework is done online with the textbook. Textbook and Smartwork are like $75
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: The homework can be very difficult, but not as the exams. He only tests on what is being covered in lecture. First midterm was not as bad, but everyone does worse on the second one, and the final is even harder. Don't worry too much about the grade, the curve is pretty fat.

The homework can be hard sometimes, but his lectures are helpful. The first midterm is easy, but the second midterm is a lot harder. Study the midterms and you can do well on the final and in the class overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures--Would take again

reviews.comment: The homework is a little hard but really helps with learning the topics. I hadn't taken a chem class since sophomore year in high school so I was worried about how it would be but he was able to teach it well. As long as you read the textbook, do the homework, and some practice questions you should be able to do pretty well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Harman is amazing. His homework is always harder than his midterms/final, which makes it so relieving. I took this class with my last chem class being Chem Honors from High school Sophomore year and found it very easy. Participation does matter because of clickers. The online textbook is a bit expensive but helps a ton.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Good professor. A little boring. Don't always rely on him. Homework helps and so does textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This class was really easy. Professor Harman was very clear from the start what he expected, and the exams aren't too hard. Study the homework, pay attention in lecture, and you should honestly be fine.
He is a great teacher. There are two midterms and a final. He's pretty clear and I really enjoyed his class. Homework was pretty hard. Take him if you want to really understand the material.

Professor Harman was amazing, he actually made me enjoy learning about chemistry.  He is an average grader and prepares you well for the midterms and final.  Very clear and easy to understand- makes chemistry about as enjoyable as it can get.
Harman is a great teacher. He gives a huge curve! Best thing to do is read the book thoroughly and keep up with the lectures.

Professor Harman's chem 001A class is not difficult. There are clicker questions, so attendance is highly recommended. He has 2 midterms and one final, which is nice. He uses Sapling Learning, so there is no need for the Alex book. The Sapling homework can get quite hard, but there are online examples for you to look at. Hes a pretty good teacher!

Dr. Harman's new but he really knows the material but his handwriting on the board is sometimes illegible but is open for fixing the mistakes.  He's understanding and assigned office hours are quite flexible so you won't usually in a hurry to leave.  Online hw is a pain, but he'll help! He is strict but make sure you do questions from the book!
Never went to MATH009b class and ended with an A+. This guy is the absolute legend. I wish he was teaching 9c this quarter.
GOAT super easy

I had him for Math 009b, and I think he's a good professor! He's lenient with extensions, grading, and curves, so much so that I got a C- on the midterm, but got an A- on the final and ended with an A. Homework was reasonable, the practice exams are very similar to the real ones, and he is understanding as a person overall.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: His explanations are thorough and he understands how confusing the topics can be. Practices Exams were given and similar in difficulty to the real ones. Attend lectures and understand what he's explaining. He posted his notes outside of class and videos for the practice exams. Just review his notes and he gives an outline of what's to be expected.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's alright, I took Math009B w him and he was really good. Webworks due twice a week, a midterm/final. He's rlly good at responding to emails and he's very lenient when it comes to grading/late HW. One of the nicest teachers at UCR. I personally struggled hella in the class but he made things so much easier imo.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: this professor was difficult to hear + pay attention to ( especially at 8 in the morning ) as he does not use a mic, and does not speak for minutes at a time while writing out his work. he often focuses more on definitions in math, rather than the actual implementation + examples.

Math 9C Winter 2024:
Honestly if you go to every lecture you will pass with an A. Quizzes, midterm and final were similar to what he went over in lecture. The only low I had was it was quite difficult to listen to him sometimes as he is a quiet dude. Overall very helpful if you actually seek help.
Part 2. I took Professor Hong again for Kor 002. She is very nice and flexible. However, the midterm and final are no joke. You have to study!

Part 1:
I almost done with Korean 001. She is an amazing language professor. Even though Korean is a difficult language to learn. Professor Hong is very fun, and she makes Korean fun to learn.
When I look back at my four years here, she will probably be the first professor I remember. What a great experience. Very easy class.
She is an amazing professor. This is my 3rd quarter with her; her classes are very easy and she makes learning korean very easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Okay just wanna preface that I am not a native speaker.  After taking the class for 4 quarters, I didn't learn Korean at all because it was during COVID and online so yardy know I finessed it.  It was a lil tough for me I'm ngl.  She was really nice and all but when it came to verbal tests, she locked in and really drilled people when they're wrong
underrated professor at UCR, she is amazing

Probably the most caring professor I have ever had. She is amazing and I am so glad I was able to learn Korean from this instructor. Just pay attention because she says a lot during lecture that is crucial for Korean speaking.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I love Professor Hong! She's very sweet and understanding. She understands how busy students are with exams and homework and as long as you communicate with her and try your best, she'll try her best to make sure you do well in the class. She is patient in class when students are struggling. Exams are not difficult as long as you stay caught up.
As someone that didn't know any Korean before taking the KOR1-3 series, Professor Hong is a great professor and the class is organized and structured well

I found her explanations to be confusing and difficult to understand at times but the textbook really helps explains things better. Only graded on 3 homework assignments and 1 test per chapter. We also had a short presentation on 1 part of Korean culture. Easy class if you take notes and read the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: tbh when i first saw her, i thought she was just another scary ajumma so i was prepared to hate the class. but after the first day of class, almost every student in my heritage learners class luv'd her. she's accommodating of students' circumstances, is accessible, interactive, and motivates all students. i wish every professor was like her.

I personally did not have a good experience with her. The way she manages the class is VERY messy. She did not emphasize that we only had to do certain pages of hw, she doesn't update her syllabus regularly, she made me present my culture project on the wrong day even though I tried to tell her. However, the work is easy. Just keep up w/ everything

Professor is probably the kindest professor at UCR. She comes of strong at first and can seem strict but she really isn't. I absolutely adore her and she always checks to make sure everyone is on the same page. Class was super easy for me because I am fluent but even if you're not, she helps you if needed.

Very easy class. Weekly vocab quizzes & homework from the workbook (don't need the textbook but workbook is mandatory), PPT, video project, midterm, final If you don't feel like going to class, you can email her some BS excuse and she'll excuse you. She's understanding and lets you take a quiz days after its original date. EZ A even tho i got a B+

I took the class as a heritage learner, so she was much, much harder on us than her regular 1-4 series. Even if you don't speak Korean, she helps you learn how to improve. I went home after the quarter ended, and my parents were able to hear a difference in me. I wish I learned sooner, but sooner is better than never.

If you have an interest in Korean language/culture you'll enjoy the class. She's very caring but she can be a little intense, because she really wants you to learn the language and pass the class. I'm a non-heritage learner and currently in the 5th level so don't be too afraid of taking the class if you have no experience in the language

She is a very nice professor. Extremely understanding. The textbook is not necessary, but the workbook is. She can go off on some random tangents sometimes, but the class is always really good. I would recommend taking her class 100%
really really enjoyed her class pretty easy and learned quite a bit

SHE IS MY FAVORITE PROF. AT UCR! She is so helpful and such an easy grader. You don't have to buy the textbook but you have to get the workbook. Easy GPA booster. Video presentations each quarter are really fun and she gives food at the end of each quarter!

Prof. Hong is one of the best teachers at UCR, I agree with another post. She's really good at teaching her native language, and she makes her class very interactive. She really wants all to learn her language and does what she can to get us to that point. HIGHLY recommend.
she is cool, nice, and the best.  really fun in her class
one of the best teachers are UCR. she is extremely nice and very helpful. very fun class. its easy but you still learn a lot. SHE's GREAT!!!
Really nice, really understanding, and generally a fun class.  Sometimes I think she's too nice and students end up taking advantage of that.

Be careful when taking her Korean classes because I think she doesn't take into account enough that some people in the class actually don't know Korean (the majority of her students are Korean with at least some knowledge of the language).  But otherwise, she's really easy and really nice. Loved her.
Cool teacher.

Upper level Korean (3+) is going to be a little hard if you don't know Korean because Prof. H. goes a little fast, but if you know some, this is going to be a breeze.  If not, you may have to study harder, but again, if she knows you're trying, she will take that into account for your grade. She gives lotsa HW, but they're so easy it's a joke.

i love love love prof. hong. she may come off as stern but seriously, she is the nicest professor at the institution. if she sees that youre making the effort to learn, its going to show in your grade. just make sure you are respectful and nice to her because she really deserves it.

I had professor Hong for Korean 1, and Korean 4 when she moved me up. She is a great teacher, extremely concerned with students learning. I was struggling in 4 because of the sudden level change, but she stuck with me and paid particular attention to make

She is the nicest, most understanding teacher. She cares about her students a lot,... and she makes it her goa/priorityl to have her students appreciate their korean culture.She is easy as hell, and the sweetest woman. I will miss taking her classes. EASY A as long as you know some korean.
Taking her for summer school and so far she's been very helpful and informative.  The class isn't hard as long as you know some korean and do all her assignments ( which isn't that hard ).

One of the most hardest working professors in UCR.  She really tries to reach out and help you get something out of taking her class.  You learn many cultural things when she goes off on a tangent.  All you have to do is show up and do the homeworks.  Easy A ~ A- if you know Korean well enough.
Really care about her students...if you try at all she will be nice to you and it will show in ur grade
She's pretty easy and helpful.  Only thing bad about her is that she takes attendance every once in awhile.  If you don't mind showing up to class everyday, it's a good GPA booster.

I took Dr. Judelson's graduate course. He is a very interesting and wise professor, and also very approachable. He prepares his course materials with great care and always ensures that everyone can keep up with his explanations. I highly recommend him.
This is the best class I've had at UCR.   He is fantastic.  Course isnt easy, he makes you use your brain, its not just memorization.  Changed my perception of what science is, its cool.

Professor Judelson is the best professor in UCR, no one of. He is really patient and helpful and loves his experiments. I feel so lucky to take all his great lectures and get interested in Molecular Biology. Thank you.

Dr. Judelson was the best professor I've ever had! Loved him and his class. Going to office hours really helped. You don't need specific questions, you can just ask to review a specific method you're having trouble on. The class is HARD but doable. You really need to enjoy it to do well. The curve is really great though.
AWESOME PROF

Really interesting class and lectures were great.  Exams were hard, but curved.  Prof was helpful in office hours, one of the best UCR profs (but not the easiest).  Work hard on  problem sets, they were not graded, but help you learn.

Thought I hated molecular biology until this class.  But this course was fantastic!  Not just memorizing trivial facts, it focused on concepts and methods with real-world relevance.   Exams were hard but fair.  Prof was clear, helpful, and cared about students.

Tough exams.  Not like other classes where you could just memorize whats on slides, instead exams focused on general concepts and applying methods.  Do the weekly problem sets, they show what prof thinks is important.  Prof told jokes in class, hah hah.  Overall good class.
Inspiring class.  Loved the bovine genomics topic.  Moo!

Good class.  Was well organized, the slides were clear, and the assignments were helpful.  Professor did a good job.  There was just one test, which was a little scary, but the prof gave a list of 10 questions in advance, 3 were on the final.
Great class, great prof
Very nice professor and extremely helpful...
I learned a lot from the class.  I wasn't bored at all, maybe because there was little overlap with classes that I have taken before.  Most of the work is a final exam and a class presentation.

This class wasn't hard. The final exam was difficult but he gives you 12 long essay questions a week before the exam, and he only asks 3-4 of them on the exam. The class can be pretty boring though and overlaps a lot with CMDB201 and undergrad Bioinformatics. The project is the exact same as the CMDB201 project. I can't say I learned anything.
Awesome class.  Prof did a great job.
loved the class. prof stresses problem solving approach to topic not just memorization.  really really interesting, made me like science again.  not easy but worth it.  prof is a sweetie.
Awesome class. Not easy at all, can't just memorize, but prof really pushes your brain up to the higher level.  Really glad I took class.

Howard is very clear in his speech and looks a little like a cute little koala. His first midterm in his class was ridiculously hard. Avg was 43 out of 100. Highest grade I've heard of so far was a 78. Mostly free response Q's.
took class last year.  liked it a lot.  Prof lectures very interesting, he does good job.  Better than most profs at UCR.
Really good.  Learned a lot.  Professor does a good job.
Very good class.  Teach more classes Dr. Judelson, you are great!
Good instructor, lectures and handouts very organized and up to date.  I recommend that you take the class, it helped me a lot in my research.

I took the class last quarter.  It was a good class, and really helped me in my current classes.  He's a very good prof.  Expects a lot from students, but is fair in grading.  Works hard to give a good and entertaining lecture, and helps me think of future career options that I never considered in science.
A pretty tough class, sort of like biochemistry.  Exams are pretty tough, too.  Prof's lectures are very good and the prof is very helpful in office hours.  Overall, I'm glad that I took the class.
He was an excellent professor and very helpful. The class was not very difficult, and expectations were very clearly stated and grading was very fair and reasonable.
He worked us hard, but I loved the class.  One of the best profs at UCR.

The course was great, lectures very interesting.   Teacher pushed us hard to learn, and sometimes I struggled, but it was worth it in the end.  Means on exams were low, but the course was curved pretty high (I think that the average was a B).
he is great!

I took his class last year.  It was one of my favorites at UCR; he really worked hard to teach the material and make it interesting.  I ended up with a B, but it wasn't his fault.   I only wish that I had studied harder, to get a better grade.

Dr. Judelson is an amazing professor. He makes molecular biology challenging yet engaging. His course was one of my favorite courses at UCR because he is well organized and engaging to his students. I learned a lot in his class and enjoyed his approach of teaching molecular biology!

One of my favorite classes!  Not that easy, but lectures interesting and the professor was cool even though some of his jokes were not that funny.  Prof makes you understand why biology is important and relevant to the real world--and might help you get a good job.  I'm much more interested in science now after having taken this class.

Very clear lectures, and very helpful in office hours.  This professor really expects you to learn the concepts--memorization is not enough!  But I guess that it is the concepts that are most important in the real world, so that is OK.  He really tried to make the class relevant to the real world, with examples of applications, etc.
Tough class but good professor

BUS20 is a lot to learn, but Professor Paik was very helpful the entire time both from lectures, to homework, to exams. Mid-term and exam were curved, and he is very understanding that the course is difficult but he's teaching style makes it better. Would 100% take this professor again.

He is a great professor! Really comprehensive lectures and the homework relates directly to what he speaks about. The final was hard since I didn't study much but as long as you understand the homework fully, you'll be fine. Doing the case studies isn't required but really helps, so if you're struggling take a shot at those and go to office hours.

He is very helpful if you are willing to reach out to him outside of class. This is a hard class, so seek support and help when you are lost. Going to his office hours helps a lot! Study as a group. Homework is heavy and loaded. The finals were online, and the exams were exactly what you learn in class. He is always there to support you.

Professor Paik is a very kind and caring instructor. The only downside is that his exams can be somewhat difficult, and his lectures are long and can feel boring at times. If you attend every lecture, study consistently, and ask questions during office hours, you should be able to pass.

Prepare to self study. Prof. Paik is not good. His slides looks like it was prepared last minute. The slides were unclear and disorganized making it hard to read. He uses PollEV for engagement, however he does not know how to engage the class to understand the content. He's chill outside of class though and happy to help during office hours

Professor Paik is so chill, took the 8am which wasn't his choice, but do attend for credit and material. All three exams are multiple choice and T/F. HWs are group assignments and the workshop project is beneficial (and not stressful) so have fun with it. Prof is understanding and patient, don't be afraid to reach out if you're having trouble!

One of the kindest professors I've had here at UCR! Homework assignments are very straightforward, two midterms, one final, one course project due at the end of the quarter but he gives you feedback throughout the quarter! He wants to see all his students to succeed and I'd say he makes the class pretty engaging and worth-going! 10/10

I'm not a business student so I found the class rather difficult, but Professor Paik was honestly what helped me and so many students. One of the best professors here on campus. He's super approachable and is a professor who truly cares for his students. The class itself might be difficult regardless who teaches it. ASK QUESTIONS AND STUDY!!!
Such a nice guy! Truly cares for his students and is very understanding.

I'm not a business major and this class is my first BUS class so I was struggling. The professor was very caring and understanding. BUS 20 is a curse class but I'm glad Prof. Paik was sub in as the new instructor, bless him!

Dr. Paik was brought in last minute to replace the previous professor for BUS20, and he did a great job considering the circumstances. He is very kind and caring of his students, and did his best to make the class a good experience.

Besides for being a great teacher, Prof Paik is one of the nicest people. He's super understanding and cares for his students' success. Attendance isn't mandatory but the class itself is pretty hard, so it's best to attend lectures. The Prof explains everything very simply and makes it easier to understand. Overall very good professor.

Amazing professor. He was assigned to teach accounting for the first time because of a professor switch but he tried his best. He was lenient and gave us the best available resources that he could. But Bus020 is hard overall. If you do not go to class, you will have to self-study a lot so make sure to understand the content.

Great professor. UCR is terrible but Hoyul is the goat. UCR cancelled classes and this professor has been getting screwed over for the past quarter this year, but he still pulls through and tries to give us the best resources as possible. I believe this is his first time teaching accounting for this class, but it was very good.
Had him for BUS 020 and this man is actually the best. Give him a raise! We love you HP!

He is pretty cool professor but the class is very hard if you do not go to class. You have to self study if you do not go to class and make sure you understand the content for each week so you can do well.

Professor Paik is one of the nicest professors you will encounter. His lectures are a little boring, but it is obvious that he cares for your success. If you attend lectures, and especially attend the review sessions for the midterms and final, then you will do just fine. I highly recommend this class, as the professor is great, and class is useful

This professor is the nicest professor you can encounter! He's really understanding and lenient when it comes to his class. His lectures are a little boring but he genuinely cares about you and will do his best to make sure no one fails ( unless you cheat, please don't cheat this class is so easy to pass ). Deffo a class I'd take again if I could

Great Lectures and super flexible. This is an in person class but he will post lectures and workshop videos. Your grade will reflect your effort but its not difficult to pass. In addition super communicative!! You can even ask clarifying questions on exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He's a very nice, understanding professor. It is definitely lecture heavy but he gives out a study guide and formulas for all of the math equations during the tests. He cares about his students a lot. Although he's not a very exciting professor during lectures he's very understanding in a lot of ways  :-)

Great Professor. You must attend class, since it is quite a lot of material. Very helpful material. You will become more financially literate. Highly recommend this class as it will you real world skills. I wish every high school taught this class. There was fairly easy homework and group project. You must study for midterms and final. Good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: A very understanding and open person, an excellent class to introduce you to the basics of personal finance.

Easier compared to other professors, given that the curve is very generous, but you still have to put the work in. Make sure you do all the problem sets and practice exams before the midterms and finals! His lecturing style wasn't really working for me because he talked so fast, but luckily, there are old TA lecture notes on Canvas that got me by
He's BRITISH

Hooley is a very strange case of a professor because his lectures, are decent, there is a surplus of information and resources available, and you're allowed cheat sheets. However he's incredibly coarse and condescending as a human being. Mention him to a grad student on his floor and there's a huge chance you will get an emphatic response.

His exams are graded pretty brutally, but you are allowed a cheat sheet. His practice problems just don't match up; I would use the textbook problems instead. The lectures are fine, but not enough for his exams, so put in the work. 2 midterms, 1 final, 5-point quizzes almost every week. I never missed a lecture and managed a C.

The exams are graded brutally, and they rarely match up with the practice problems he provides. Lectures are good, but not enough for his exams. I would stick to the textbook practice problems for sure. 2 midterms, 1 final, short quizzes almost every week, and you are allowed cheat sheets!

Ochem in and of itself is a really tough class regardless of who you have. Make sure you attend all lectures and be ready to do a lot of work outside of class to pass. The lectures are informative but not enough. Good thing is, anything on the problem sets and practices will be what you see on the tests. And you also get cheat sheets.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: the way he grades exams makes me wanna pull my hair out, super strict. lec is well-paced but content-heavy. optional hw and supplemental vids, but def recommend doing bc exams are similar to hw probs. hooley's exams were def an experience...
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Best professor you could take for ochem. HW and practice exams prepare you for the real exam. Allows cheat sheet on exams. The class is curved. Take him, he makes it really easy to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: VERY BALD!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The curve definitely saved me. I'm not very good with chemistry and I found his lecture to be a little lacking in information. I found myself just sitting in lecture drawing structures without fully understanding why I'm drawing it. I will say that his practice exams are pretty similar to the actual exam and the cheat sheet could help.
Very difficult but very fair.  Curve saved me
Very good prof!  He gave us lots of resources and review sessions.  He also has a huge curve which is helpful in a class as difficult as ochem.  We also get cheatsheets which are so helpful.

DENSE and fast lecture, lots of detail about things you dont need, so listen to what he's saying and not just what he's writing. lecture style did not work for me but a lot of people liked him. tests are long, kinda. hard, but lots of places to pick up easy points. curve SAVED me 
final was hard, avg 45%. do problem sets!!!! and practice exams

Great Curve but be ready to self teach everything. His lectures were as if we already knew the material. The majority of the courses I had to self teach through YouTube. His practice exams are certainly helpful for the midterms, although midterms were a lot more in-depth. Not much partial credit on problems either.

You can't go wrong with Hooley. Grading is very fair and based on how much effort you put in. Lectures were often confusing and overcomplicated but this was made up for with the sheer abundance of resources. I treated it like a self-study course and had a lot of fun with it. My advice: learn everything and don't rely on the cheat sheets

Hooley is an amazing professor, if you want to learn ochem comprehensively and retain it long term he is the best choice for you. His lectures are clear but very dense, his exams are extremely fair while challenging, if you study throughout the quarter you will do great. 100% recommend. Very helpful and provides a lot of study materials. Huge curve
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Hooley gives in depth lectures that are confusing at first. But once you read them again, they become understandable. Exams are pretty difficult, but if you just study for a good amount of time, you should be able to get the average or higher. Final is very difficult, but he gives a very generous curve.

Prof Hooley is fast-paced but fair. Though lectures can be dense, his practice exams are super helpful. Dedicate time to study, use resources like Unstuck study, and you'll do well. Ochem is tough, but Hooley makes it manageable.
BALD!!!!!!

Hooley has high expectations for his students. His tests test your ability to apply what you've learned rather than restate info. He gives out problem sets, mock tests, and videos to review and prepare for his exams alongside great SI leaders and office hours to ask questions. He is a bit intimidating but passionate for O-Chem.

His lectures are very informative and offer all the information to succeed on his exams. Many people claim he is rude, but in my experience, he never came across that way; in fact, he was often quite funny. Although his class is challenging, it is fair, and all of his course materials and problem sets closely resemble the midterms and finals.
gang is chill fr but bro be a lil cranky sumtimes. tests are free asl tho so u mad chillin. ez A+ gangy. he a dawg fr.

Cool lectures interesting and you can learn a lot from them. The exams are the same style and type of questions as the problem sets and mock exams except that the actual has slightly trickier questions to see if you grasped the material. The MT cheat sheets are a scam, my tip is to understand everythin and only use sheets incase u forget something.
hes immensely rude buts his class is really easy. I'd take him again
his tests are easy but hes mean sometimes. yeah not much else to say

curve was insane, needed like a 25% to pass. gave so much practice, just do them over & over & youll be set. some of the practice (especially on NMR) is kinda useless for exams though & when theres so many problems, you gotta pick n choose whats most important. go to office hours, go to SI (amazing), go to all his reviews (even on weekends)

This is a very doable class if you are ready to put in the work. The professor provides almost unlimited amounts of practice problems and even two practice midterms before each midterm. Reading through lecture notes and completing all practice material will almost guarantee a good grade as the class is also graded on a percentile basis.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: two midterms one final, my quarter's avg was ~45% and an A was 75%. very tough exams but do the problem sets and mock exams until you understand everything, they are great resources, very similar. lectures were useful for me but not necessary since self study is so efficient. hooley is british and funny, SI leaders were amazing.
Do the problem sets and mock midterms until you feel like your eyes are going to pop out of your sockets. It is a very doable class if you are willing to put in the work. Goated professor IMO.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: ez class, just do problem sets and read the ta notes. dont fall behind
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ochem is a culture shock for sure. Hooley is a great prof but if you fall behind at any point, it will be near impossible to catch up. If your gen chem profs (esp 1A) were bad, do yourself a favor and study resonance before you start 8A. Hooley also lectures super quickly, 50 min straight, very dense info. Be prepared to dedicate time to his class.
BRO DOESN'T KNOW ANYTHING! MAN DOESN'T CARE IF PEOPLE HAVE DIFFERING ANSWERS FROM HIM. IF ITS NOT HIS WAY ITS WRONG. IF HOOLEY SAYS 1+1=3 THEN SO BE IT!

By far one of the best profs I've ever had. As someone who isn't as gifted or overtly intelligent, he made the class very doable. He incentivized hard workers above all else and made the class BEYOND fair. His curve was huge and really made it easy for many to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very doable. Lectures are confusing and you need to put in a lot of time aside to study but you get the grade you put in.
this man needs to pack it up and go back to australia

Hooley is a good professor and is passionate about what he does. Fast-paced lec so it takes a bit to get used to. There's no reason to fail since he gives all the material necessary to practice for exams & mock midterms are nearly identical to the exams. Has some sassy man syndrome in his Q&A sessions sometimes but overall great professor for 8A.

If you're a note taker, his class is gonna be hard bc he writes ALOT on the board and it's disorganized. It's better to just focus on what he's saying and listening to it. He's the only professor who gives cheat sheets for the exams and he gives LOTS of practice with the problem sets and mock exams. Overall not bad for ochem.

Ochem is hard but Hooley made it do-able and his exams are definitely fair! He allows cheat sheets and his practice exams and problems basically preface the exams. The material is hard, he may be fast and sassy at times but taking time to study and utilizing SI materials is very helpful. His grade distribution is also relatively fair.

Best ochem prof for 8A right now. I read the old reviews too but casselman filled up so i bit the bullet. Turns out he is an amazing prof. Lectures are heavy, but he gives lots of notes, problem sets and prac exams that are exactly the same as the MT. SI leaders help hugely. Very passionate and caring prof-not a free A but very doable with effort

Hooley is a good lecturer, but I found his problem sets and 5 mock exams to be extremely valuable to prepare for his tests. I genuinely believe getting a raw 90+ on his tests is very doable, just keep practicing his problem sets, and review Natalie's (his SI) notes she uploads for extra help. Not easy, but very fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Hooley gives everything you need to do well in his class. 9 long problems sets and mock exams that are very similar to the actual exams. Lectures are a bit confusing. Go to si to get extra help. Memorization gets you a C, thinking gets you the A. It's all about practice and pattern recognition.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Honestly Hooley is my favorite chemistry professor in UCR so far. He lays out his material without beating around the bush, and his problem sets and mock exams prepare you well for the exams. In my opinion, he never really came off cocky to me, just very passionate about what he does. Very approachable and very enjoyable professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Hooley lectures fast, and lectures are dense. He posts few notes so attend class. Has optional HW assignments but definitely do them, they are very helpful. Gives practice exams exactly like the real exams. Two midterms one final: quite difficult, but curve is huge. SI leaders are amazing, and an A is very doable if work is put in

This class is passable with a good grade, however it requires a lot of effort outside of class studying. The hw he gives us prepares us for the exam and is curve is huge. So if you fail its your fault. Also make sure to go to Natalies Si session as I found it wayy more helpful for topics i didn't learn in class.

I forgot to rate Hooley for 8B a quarter ago but I had him for 2 quarters and can say without a doubt, based on what I've heard, he is the best 8A and 8B professor. His curve is massive (25% is passing), his exams cover exactly what is in lecture and his mock exams are the same format as the real deal. He allow cheat sheets and he's approachable

I came here to change my rating because after taking an even tougher professor for OChem, I realize how easy Hooley actually made it for us to pass. He allows cheatsheets and has such a low curve. There are 5 or 6 modules that don't really do much to help your grade. Most of the grade is based on the exams.

He's overall a really great guy. Make sure to do the problem sets and the practice exams that he gives out because they are very similar to the test. Even if you feel like you know the material, always review. His tests are hard but the mechanisms are very repetitive. Go to office hourse and SI!

Dr. Hooley's class is rigorous but fair. He posts resources on Canvas, such as mock exams, problem sets and topic summaries that are very helpful in understanding and doing well in class. His TA also posts notes on Canvas. His exams were fair and similar to his mock exams. I would recommend going to SI sessions to help understand the content.

Allows 2 sheets of paper for cheatsheet each midterm, and 4 total sheets for the final. Has grade redemption if your final exam score is higher than your grade by 2 steps (eg. You have C and you get B- (C -> C+ -> B-). Low averages but has a generous curve. Uploads weekly notes and holds review sessions. If you put in the effort, you will get an A.

Approachable, FAIR, & understanding. Curve this quarter:~25% C-, 75 A. Exams are IDENTICAL to the practice exams. Gives plenty of optional practice problem sets. Uploads weekly notes. If you understand the notes youre set. Grades & releases exams in a FEW HOURS, along with curve & averages info. Lower averages = higher curve.

He is very knowledgeable about the subject. He came across as condescending and unapproachable in my opinion. His in class modules are not graded fairly and do not add anything but discouragement. He does not teach naming conventions because it annoys other professors that students don't know it in B making life hard if you take someone else.

People like to downplay Hooley but he's a great professor. I wasn't one of the sweats who went to all his office hours etc., just an average student who appreciates his class. The concepts in the class are difficult, but the manner in which he allows us to learn through his resources and his generous test curves make it feel much easier than it is.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The entire grade is made up of 2 midterms and a final exam, but he generously curves and gives you everything needed to do well. Study practice exams, self-study outside of lecture a bit and you should be golden. The TAs I had graded harsh so don't be surprised if you have to dispute a test score. Pay attention, study for tests, all there is to it.

Midterms were hard but fair. Good TAs. Graded exams the day of. His practice exams are nearly identical to his actual exams so u know what to expect. If u need extra practice theres the problem sets which are hard but if u can do them youll do good on the exams. 95% of ur grade is from exams. Gave a generous curve. If u actually try, youll get an A

Pretty good professor. Tough class, good lecturer, material isn't that hard but not easy. Review lecture notes and do practice midterms/final to get an A, DO NOT WASTE YOUR TIME WITH THE PROBLEM SETS! They are difficult for no reason and never show up on exams. Everything on exams he has taught. Midterms each 100 pts, final 200, modules 25.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Extremely respectful and nice when you approach him during office hours, not condescending at all (unlike Casselman). He has hard material, but the tests are very straightforward and he tests us on what he TAUGHT specifically in class, nothing more. Lectures are recorded so make sure you take detailed notes.
