lectures not mandatory but it sort of is. useless slides, no words on them. memorize the book. lecture is eh. lets be real, this is supposed to be an easy class. the topics are basic.

Lecture slides only set up the basic information- MUST GO TO CLASS FOR COMPLETE NOTES. Test was difficult, but most topics had been covered in class which is boring so its hard to stay focused :/ To best prepare for tests: go to class, actively listen, take really good notes, and be able to understand and APPLY the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Hard exams. Not enough time to finish. His section Ruined my grade
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Attendance not mandatory. Dont waste your time going because you learn nothing in class. Easy topic, hard professor. Seems to take peoples grades as a joke. Be careful with your GPA.
Not really a good professor. I had to teach myself everything and if I hadnt memorized the whole book I would have failed the final because his slides covered maybe 1% of the final exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Not a good professor. lecture is useless and his slides have no correlation with his final exam.

prof Hs lectures were 5/10, the book for this course is good, easy to read and understand but a lot of information to sort through. final had questions that weren't in his slides. slides are practically empty, no valuable info in them. clear speaker, not monotone, but for what use? seems like going to lecture was a waste. finals 45%

Very hard professor. Doing well in the class but I studied for over 80 hours this past week just for this one final an I barely got a B- on the final. I went in thinking Im going to ace it. Time was a huge issue. Guessed halfway when I was running out of time and got lucky.
Id give a 0 rating if I could. This should be an easy A class. The material is not hard unless you are stupid. Prof. Hongdians final was one of the hardest Ive ever taken. Not enough time.
Basically gotta teach yourself everything and hope you dont get screwed over for the final.

Not a good lecturer. My grades high so far due to the first half of the class being taught by a different professor. His slides are nearly empty. All pictures. You have to go through the book by yourself and add your own notes. Why do clicker problems, essentially making lecture mandatory when you get nothing out of it? Went to all lectures. Waste

This professor acted like we chose to have this coronavirus pandemic and its around UCR to target his family. Unfair online final. Not enough time. Has no respect for his students mental health and he teaches a neuroscience class.

As I write this I just want to say that the first half of this class (which was with a different professor) was a different story than the second half with Yang. Yang's lecture slides are not applicable to the exam to a large extent, and there's too much in the book to remember for the final. He gives EC but it's not a lot. Be really attentive.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Honestly, 106 should be a piece of cake for all neuro majors. It is super basic. But, Yang did have the harder portion of the class to teach (somatosensation). It was completely doable if you went to class. He emphasized the really important things that showed up on the exam and he answers all questions clearly. If you're a good student, easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: So the class itself was very challenging and his lectures did not do much to help clear a lot of the confusion.

Test on avg was about 57-62% and I was good enough to stay above it from a 78-86-91. But you have to be willing to put the work in, alot of students did bad because they didnt take the class seriously and ended up not showing up to class. Alot of questions on the test he says in lecture so show up or take careful notes because he records lectures

Tests were lecture heavy so be ready to read and review material over and over but it'll help. I averaged like 60s on both midterms and final but curve helped me to a B-. He cares a lot and noting what he says in lecture helps cause that'll be on test. No hw just debates for disc but real easy.

Dense for breadth. Curved grades, multiple choice midterms/final questions designed to confuse you (a la "I literally just made this question up"), seems overwhelming but stick heavily to a class discord study guide and it's a B or a C. If you can put up with someone calling multiple choice questions a "celebration of learning," go right on ahead.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 2 midterms and a final, must complete at least half of the polleverywhere's, and in your discussion, you have to debate twice in front of the class. the average was really low on his exams and he ended up curving which shows how badly we did. you MUST study, all the info comes from lectures which he goes through quickly and hardly adds text

Don't take this class if you're looking for an easy course. Midterms are hard, the average was 62%. Lectures are heavy and there's a lot of material to study. Final replaces lowest midterm grade. I really struggled in the class but did well in the end because of the curve!

Amazing Professor. Funny + passionate. Lectures are fun but attendance graded by PollEverywhere. Tests are hard  (average was 66%) worth 75% of grade. Tests not open note so you must study. Most material covered in lectures but good to skim textbook too. Some stuff not covered. You have to really try in this class. The curve saved everyone tho.

Very passionate at teaching the course and exams are all all multiple choice based on lecture !  Drops your lowest midterm grade at the end of the quarter and offers only 1 extra credit being a 1 page long single space essay reflection on a discussion debate topic that counts toward participation only. Polls everywhere counts for attendance!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor was funny/great, but get ready to pay attention most of the grade are the exams (75%) and they are closed note. Most of the exam material is covered in lectures, but make sure to do the readings! As long as you show up to class and review the slides, this class will be manageable. If you fall behind though, it will for sure be hard.

This class is a completely different experience depending on your interest in the material. If it's your major and you're interested in this stuff, them his class will be really easy, and you might already know half the material. If you take this as a breadth course, be prepared for some very information heavy lectures. Not too science heavy tho
Homyak is very passionate about his work, he is easy to understand an overall a great professor. However, his lectures pace is extremely quick!

Overall an amazing professor! Goes over the material quickly so you'll need to keep up, but only grades off two open note midterms and a final. Participation matters for Poll Everywhere participation points. Truly passionate about what he studies and is an inspirational teacher. Super caring and kind.

His teaching is so interesting. I attended all his lectures and a lot of the class did too. He has 2 Midterm( open note) along with a final. If you pay attention in class and participate in the poll questions (that he doesn't grade if you get wrong) you have all the info you need for succeeding. Printing out slides is the best way to get notes!

Prof. Homyak is amazing! He really cares about his students & is very understanding of their needs. Gives a lot of extra credit opportunities & makes a study guide. His tests are very straightforward & its really hard to fail since he tells you exactly what will be on it. Honestly I would take this class just because he's so fun & kind! 12/10

very disorganized and bad lecturer. i never went to lecture. but she copy and pasted questions from the practice exam onto the midterm and final exam. we're allowed a cheat sheet so the class wasn't that stressful. easy A imo due to all of that. (coming from not a business/accounting major)

The class material itself is not too difficult but she's is very unprofessional at times, said she was available all the time but responds late, didn't even post the grades for the final, only the grade for the whole course. Has a heavy accent, which is ok but she speaks softly which makes it very hard to understand. Sometimes does pollev.

The lectures are very disorganized and difficult to understand. Her voice feels like listening to nails scratching a chalkboard. The homework will age you 7 years and destroy your will to live. You're also forced to pay $90 for a crappy website to do said homework and a textbook. The tests are awful and if you don't have a good TA you are done for.
Curriculum super difficult to understand and have to drop a lot of money for textbook. Disorganized and not that helpful lectures. Grades things super late, but bearable.

Super disorganized, slides are messy annotations are messy. lectures were so empty she had to add attendance as part of the grade. She also has an incredibly horrible accent, and her tone sounds like she's trying to sing opera when lecturing. The first day we had lecture was on April Fools and I heard her speak and I thought she was pranking us.

I've had harsh professors, but she beats everyone. I thought this class would help me however, she does not teach very well during lecture. She is not organized at all. The amount of times she has delayed projects due to her lack of efficiency is horrible. She gave the class a midterm on material she has not introduced. 100% DO NOT RECOMMEND!
Very bad at being a professor. Rambles on about different things and is incredibly hard to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took her for 165b and 165c. She's super chill, tests are open book, note, and "computer." She takes attendance in the form of a discussion activity randomly so you do have to go to class.

I took the Bus 020 in winter quarter, This professor use other professor's syllabus. And the class time of the Discussion and grading guide was wrong. And i send her email about that. She never improve that. And the form of the exam in the syllabus were wrong. I was so unlucky to choose this professor.

Kind individual but rather lazy. Poor lectures. Class expectations and grading percentage system not explicitly listed. Does not address emails well. Highly recommend waiting, if possible, for a different professor if she is your only option. Felt like I have learned nothing from this quarter.

I have never made an RMP post about any professor in my entire college career, but man she is something else. She regurgitates 80-90 slides of info in a day which is essentially a chapter a day. I felt like I was taking a summer course during a regular school quarter. Group projects were easy, and exams were sort of related to content.

By far the greatest accounting professor at UCR. The prof is caring, thoughtful, and flexible. She works with students to help them pass and compensates for ANY and all difficulties. I had her for 165 A, B, and C and she was the same for all of them. Same class setup, hw style, and attitude in all.

Honestly her lectures were a mess but her exams were identical to her study guides with a few random questions here and there. Be prepared to teach yourself! Easy A if you put in the effort. Other than that she is a very nice and caring professor.

Prof. Vagelis is a nice person overall and the course is not hard if you have some relevant background. It's not the most interesting class, true, but not something that is too bad either. Wasn't hard to get a good grade.
unhelpful professor and does not repond to students questions properly. Avoid taking his class for CS242.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I choose to take this class as part of the computer networks requirement for CSBA majors and tbh its not that bad. The material is pretty interesting but Vagelis is definitely not the greatest at explaining. Also make sure you have someone in your group that has experience with java/python. Huge curve at the end though which is always nice to see.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: For this class, don't be too dependent on the lectures. Make sure you take modestly detailed notes on the Zybooks material. He's not the most memorable prof, and he's not the worst either. He does give a nice curve though. Everyone loses a lot of points on the quizzes, and in the end, he curved my final class grade from an A- to an A+.

Not good at all. His assignments he makes them up on his own and they are extremely difficult. I am a student who stays on top of everything and this class was pretty hard. We use zybooks as well which isn't too bad. His lectures are pretty helpful but the material is hard so you have to work for it harder than a usual class. wouldn't take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Really interesting class, covers a lot of important material in information retrieval. There are pop quizzes but you basically get free marks. There is a very interesting and straightforward group project. Really fun to do!

Heavy accent, class is curved by a lot. He makes his own coding assignments that are pretty time consuming. You can study off of assignments and lecture slides imo. His tests aren't memorization heavy, but you should understand how you implement things in the assignments to do well on the tests. Tests your understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Class is extremely straightforward. Make sure to do well on projects, which are also super straightforward. Lecture is boring, but the material is all there and readily online. He comprehensively covers everything you need to know, just not in a very exciting way. There are mini quizzes basically once a week that you get 50% on for just showing up.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Take his class. He tells you what he expects and you'll get the A if you do it. He has pop quizzes at the end of class about that class but you'll get over half the credit for writing your name on the page.

Letter grade is based on what quartile you are, pretty spooky. Heavy accent but I understand that professors are here for research, not to teach us freshmen level physics. Lectures are whatever doesn't get me out of bed every morning. The tests are free since you get every formula needed and just have to plug things in. Get your A and lets move on.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Best physics professor ever. Exams are a majority poll ev questions.

she was honestly so sweet and caring, if you make an effort that you care and stayed behind after class to ask her to explain a concept she would draw out a whole problem until you understood it and it helped me a lot as a visual learner. poll ev was similar if not identical on what's on the exams! ignore the practice exam lowkey

Professor in nice but had a very STRONG accent, so it was INCREDIBLY hard to learn anything from class. The best this is to watch YouTube videos to self teach. She does poll ev's in class so lecturers are mandatory. Exams are very similar to poll ev questions, and not very similar to practice exams. Only one midterm and one final, lots of homework

it seems as if she puts very minimal effort in her job. I could not understand lecture because her accent is so strong. Her slides were very hard to study independently. She takes prof beyermanns old finals as "practice final exams" when her final was not similar at all. She doesn't even make the effort to make her own practice exams.

Professor is not very engaging and class is pretty monotonous, making it hard to learn. Midterm was pretty easy but Final was a huge step up in difficulty, containing problems we weren't taught. Practice midterm/final is nothing like real exam so be prepared to do a lot of self studying. Clicker questions used in class so attendance is mandatory.

Would not recommend. The lectures aren't very engaging and same with the labs. Often found myself, as well as others, confused after meeting with her and quickly had to find other sources to catch up i.e textbook, online videos, collaboration.

It's best to just learn from the book and teach yourself because her lectures are very unhelpful. Offers a lot of extra credit and she structures her grading so work is not too reliant on test grades. The final was extremely difficult compared to the first midterm so be aware. Poll everywhere questions are used on exams so study them.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Took CHN020B. Class is very difficult if you don't put in the effort/ not good at Chinese. She is very straight-forward and test/ assignments are graded harshly, but she's just trying to teach the class right. She is sweet & funny, but a little crazy. There is HW + quizzes every other day and 3 big lesson tests and memorized speaking performances.

She's a really sweet professor and really enjoys doing her job, but she is a really strict grader in a sense where she wants you to actually improve your skills in Chinese. It's a really time-consuming class so put in effort to earn results, but she genuinely seems to want the best for you. Tests are worth a lot, but she makes them pretty clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Liu is the sweetest. The class is really hard but in the end she is just trying to do her best to teach us the material. She always has a smile on her face and quick to greet you. Her grading is more lenient compared to before and she is willing to adapt. This class is definitely hard though. If you want an easy lang, take something else.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Take a different language. Professor Hsu was great for 20A but Liu is a tough teacher. She grades like you are majoring in Chinese, and expects you to know stuff that most other teachers wouldn't require. Homework is graded toughly, speaking performances are graded ok, and exams are again graded toughly. Just take Spanish or French online.

This class is way too time consuming for a breadth course. Even though we meet four times a week, we're still expected to put in at least two extra hours daily. The workload is a lot, assignments daily The professor grades harshl. If you're looking for a manageable class, avoid this one unless you're ready to dedicate your life to it.

Time consuming, basically work every single day. Unclear instructions and tells us work literally a day before they are due, giving us no time or preparations. About 3 speaking performances and one final oral presentation + final written exam. Two quiz for each lesson (pinyin+english and character). if not native speaker dont recommend.

Took CHN020B. Class is very difficult if you don't put in the effort/ your chinese isn't that good. She's very straight-forward and can be scary with all the assignments and tests, but she's just trying to teach. Homework and quizzes every other day with 3 big lesson tests and memorized speaking performances + lots of writing. she's sweet and funny

demanding, high-maintenance class. she is a very hard grader and is very inflexible. there is no room for mistakes if you want an A, which is absurd because this is a breadth class for almost everybody.

Was disappointed with Hsuan Ying Liu due to her teaching style. The professor treated us like children, criticized harshly, and discouraged questions, making learning difficult. Tests had no clarifications, and the strict environment stifled discussion. Overall, the approach hindered our understanding and enjoyment of the subject.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Grades extremely harshly, singles students out, tells students to ask questions but never actually answers during tests, assumes that students know everything, gets mad at students who write notes during her class even though she is the one who told everyone to get a notebook for her class. Overall, one of the most stressful classes I have taken.

had this prof for CHN020B. Cares a lot about her students. Homework and quizzes every other day and there are 3 exams and 1 final. Hard class but if you put in the work, it's doable. Mandatory attendance. Be prepared to spend a lot of time on this class every single day.

Great professor and is very caring about her students. There are a lot of speaking performances and the course is very past pace so be prepared to study a lot and you have to know your Chinese or else you will fall behind.

Best Chinese professor! She is so kind and caring and I can tell she genuinely wants students to learn chinese as much as possible. She also explains grammar, pronounciation, and chinese history very concisely.

Can't wait to take her again for CHN003 :)
the best teacher ive ever had, her office hours were very helpful. the most caring teacher ive met in my life

Made learning Chinese fun. Each class period was not boring. Respected how much she wanted to teach Chinese and answered everyone's questions about Chinese and cultural questions even if it wasn't the topic of the day. Curiosity was always welcomed and answered by her.

Very good professor, especially for those that are non-native. I personally had a great time in this class and Shu Laoshi was very helpful and gave good insight. She is a fair grader and cares a lot about her students passing with a good grade. If you are struggling, don't be afraid to seek out her help, she is very willing to help.

Definitely a hard teacher but very caring and respectful. She is very clear with her expectations and her class is well organized. Fast grader and gives constructive feedback, she is definitely the type of teacher you grow a relationship with. You definitely have to put in a lot of work in this class but she is by far my favorite professor at UCR!

I did not have a good experience with this professor over the summer. She's such a harsh grader, nit-picky, and does not offer any extra-credit opportunities to at least help make up for her harsh grades. I don't know what she's like in the regular quarters but I would definitely avoid taking her over the summer,

Harsh and tough grader. Made an accelerated 5 week summer course even tougher by leaving no room whatsoever for any mistakes. Deducts points for the smallest things. Laughs at mispronunciations. No opportunity to make up late work either, whether through extra credit or late submission for partial points. Avoid!

2 exams consist of fill in,t/f,translation. cumulative final. pinyin/character quizzes. choice of oral exam or oral presentation. hw is not bad. study guide given. study tip-go over slides. speaking hw is you recording ? and say answer and upload it. final is cumulative. took chin4 in summer and it went by fast. Overall, it was doable. :)
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: beginning of the class is challenging because of the pinyin you learn. exams consist of pinyin, a story she says in Chinese and decide whether statements are t/f in English, fill in blank, and translation. pinyin/character quizzes but can drop lowest score. explains material well, i took Chinese before at mt sac. recommend chinese IF YOU KNOW IT
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor was an extremely engaging and caring language teacher. She always sought out the best for her students and challenged us all the time. Lots of vocab, grammar structures, etc. Chinese is a hard language, especially for non-natives or if you have NO background (Chinese school). I had no background but definitely do-able if you PUT IN WORK.

The only reason this class isn't easy, is because it's Chinese.  Professor Hsu is a great teacher that gives constant feedback on your tones and pronunciation, which is imperative to learning a new language. There is homework and/or a quiz on most days, both short, but it forces you to really practice. Buy the books! She uses them for CHN002 also.
Very engaging teacher. She takes the effort to learn everyone's English and Mandarin name which is great as it feels that there is a personal level to learning Mandarin.

Professor Hsu is a GREAT professor. She encourages her students to work hard not just for a great grade but for the gift of learning. She has a great sense of humor when her students struggle with speaking. Overall, she establishes a warm, strong, and cooperative classroom environment. During OH, she is helpful and attends to each student equally.

Since I have been learning Chinese for the past year and a half, this very beginning Chinese course came easy for me. She has a sense of humor, but she expects you to practice speaking out of class, either at the ARC or with her during office hours. You can get by with making copies of the hw pages at the library, but it's best if you have the book
She's so funny! She is really nice and very approachable. She is willing to help you with Chinese and wants students to be better at it. She cracks a lot of jokes during class and with her students.
Best teacher ever! She is super nice and really helpful! Once you get used to the class, you will see its not that hard. She is really funny and I am so glad I took this class!

if you have the chance to take this professor, dont think twice, and just enroll. you'll thank me later. this woman is amazing! she makes learning chinese so much fun and has a real genuine interest to help her students. one time i came to ask her for help and she stayed an extra hour pass her office hours to help me! enough said!
she is so nice! she has a great sense of humor and always willing to help. she's the BEST professor i've ever had at ucr! she really tries to connect with her students.

She's a great professor and always willing to answer questions, but she gives a quiz, a test, or has homework due EVERY single day of class. You really have to be on top of your studies and ALWAYS read your syllabus the night before. Vocabulary quizzes are given the first day of the new lesson, so you have to memorize it on your own before class.

This was an easy class really. She likes to call on people to participate other than that just study for quizzes, do homework, pay attention and if you understand the concept and everything you should be fine. She's helpfully so go talk to her if you need help.

His in-person lectures can get boring, I recommend watching the video recordings instead; however, all you need is the slides. His curve for our class was around 9.5% and the extra credit was extremely generous: 5% from optional quizzes, 5% from presentation. Overall a good professor with simple slides.

Test are mostly memorization but a good portion does check for mechanism understanding or differences between two similar things. The extra credit offered is extremely generous and the group presentation project was not too bad. Lectures are prerecorded and class time serves as office hours. I'd recommend, he truly cares about students doing well!
Overall pretty solid professor. Tests were difficult and you have to know literally everything from the slides. Extra credit is very generous

He made this course asynchronous, so it was up to you to stay on track. Overall, easy class and the tests are based fully on the slides. Averages in the mid 80's so don't expect a curve. Really basic microbio stuff. Quality of the lab portion is dependent on TA; some are difficult graders and others are easy graders.
Group project thats really hard and midterm based off of random things no clear structure. hardest class I've taken
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Highly recommend, lots of studying and memorization. If you really study the slides you can get an A. I would study 3 days before the midterm. One group project thats a big part of your grade, so people actually work on. LOTS of Extra credit

He is straightforward and exams are fair. Anything on the slides will be on the exam. Lots of process memorization but it really isn't as bad since his slides are very simple. Average was 70-80%. Lots of extra credit as well and one group project

Although the class was pretty dense on the material, he was pretty clear on what he expects you to know and what is going to be on the test. He's very approachable during office hours, if you go to them. All the materials are on the slides, but he does occasionally specify important topics during lectures. Don't buy the textbook, it's a waste.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I think its important to attend lectures because you start to get an idea of what he really expects you to know, pay attention to the objectives. He's very approachable during office hours and clears up anything you have questions on. Exams can vary in difficulty but if you keep up with the material and do the homeworks you'll be ok.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Hsiao was very clear on what he expected and fair on the grading. Going into this class I was worried about a professor with no reviews, and I am so glad I stayed because it became one of my favorite classes. Not only is the topic interesting but Dr. Hsiao is quite engaging. Definitely go to office hours he is super helpful and friendly!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He goes very fast in lecture and its hard to keep up. Midterm was 38 multiple choice questions in 50 mins and it was not easy at all. I would not recommend this class.

Really great professor. Knows what she's teaching and incorporates all sorts of activities to make learning easy and fun. There is a short quiz nearly every class, but it's mostly to monitor your development in the course and ensure you are keeping up. Enjoys teaching and does an excellent job at it.

Shih Lao Shi is very nice and fair if you put effort in her class. Study the study guides that she provides and do the homework and you will be good. She is very passionate for the subject and will provide help if you need it. There are quizzes for a majority of the classes to check your progress and tests for every two chapters.

Shih laoshi is a great professor, actually one of my favorites. I took her for both Chi 1 and 2, although I didn't get to finish the first quarter due to illness. She has a great personality and cared about our progress as students greatly. Learning Chinese is not easy, but she makes it doable. Expect a quiz everyday and plenty of HW.

This is the third class I have taken with Professor Hsu.  She is very underrated.  If you actually invest time in the class, do all the readings, and attend, obtaining an A is very easy.  Also if you talk to her, she is very approachable, and will provide clarity to any questions you might have.

I took Asian Art History and wow - I dropped the class after 2 weeks. Ginger is very dull and lacks personality. Has very high and sometimes ridiculous expectations for the class. The book required for this class is $200 alone, too. DO NOT TAKE ANY OF HER CLASSES - YOU WILL REGRET IT BIG TIME

OMG! most horrible teacher i have ever had. she speaks chinese/japanese/korean half the time and doesnt even explain what shes saying! her accent is horrible and the material is soooo boring!not to mention her tests are hard! DO NOT, i repeat, DO NOT take this class! its horrible!

To get an A: lots of reading and well-written papers. Understand the material in order to be able to discuss in class. She is very enthusiastic and knowledgable. I just read what was required, nothing more and participated. The class itself was interesting but the dull moments were when we OVER-analyzed paintings

Didn't have any idea what we were supposed to be learning, enthusiastic, but completely unorganized.  No feedback on work. However, very knowledgeable about the subject, she wrote one of the textbooks.  Wouldn't recommend

You can get an A, like me, but you'll have to spend a big part of your life pouring through the readings on reserve.  I knew nothing whatsoever about the subject beforehand and I never liked it either. The readings got me to like the subject and understand it, but  all the reviews here are pretty spot on.
Want to kill your GPA? Take this class.
semi-good.

DO NOT KNOW HOW TO TEACH!!! She talks so fast that we do not have time to write down the notes; she uses foreign words without explaining what the hell they are; she pronounce non-sense (by the way, if she says "long shak" in lecture, she means "loan shark.") She makes us to go to a museum for an essay, but she gives the WRONG address!!

very hard teacher.  Her grading is awful too.  her class grading consists of two 40% each for tests which is a midterm and a finam.  The last 20% consist of attendance so if you failed just one of her class, you are in trouble.  Tests are very hard too.  Class is very boring, students are always sleeping in her class.  Would not recommend at all.

Brent Hughes is really nice and cares about his students! reviews.comment: He can be funny sometimes or really rude. It depends on his mood and I think that gets in the way of his teaching too much. Essays were ok but his prompts can be confusing and unclear. His organization doesn't seem like the best and he jumps from topic to topic during class. So its easy to get lost if u don't pay attention(go to class or its worse)
I really enjoyed his class. Probably one of the best professors I've ever had. The prompts for his essays are very interesting and he isn't a hard grader. Just do the readings and attend class.

Not gonna lie I should have gone to more lectures later on, but otherwise the professor, or "Instructor", as he had us call him, was really nice. We read a book called the Fifth season and used St. Martin's guide as far as I can remember. First few essays were a breeze but make sure you give 100% on the last one. He also had a take home final.

This professor truly shows dedication for teaching through his lectures. He always ensures all students in his class understand the material he goes over, and he engages them with humorous anecdotes. I would HIGHLY recommend participating in his courses, I personally took Music of Scotland, but I am sure any of his classes are worth enrolling in

Mr. Whitelaw makes sure that you learn how to play the Bagpipes correctly. I am amazed by how much I have learned and accomplished as a bagpipe player since he has been my teacher! I would recommend this class to anyone that loves music and wants a challenge for learning a new instrument. The class was a great stress reliever from bio classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Class was awesome! I learned how to play the great Highland Bagpipes. I have never played the instrument before. During my two years of taking the class, till I graduated, I was able to: play on campus, join the UCR Bagpipe Band, play at my graduation, and was personally hired to perform! Mr. Whitelaw is a great teacher and wants you to succeed.

Professor Whitelaw is probably the best professor that I've had at UCR! He is kind, understanding and more than happy to help a student out when they need it. He is a really interesting lecturer and makes the class enjoyable by relating the content to various life stories! SENIORS, you have a chance to, please take this class! It's one to remember!

I took this class thinking it would be an EASY A, and it was LOL I do agree with the person saying that the class is tedious, however, it really is not that bad. If you want an easy A take either MUS 20 or MUS 21, he will do his best to help you get an A

I mistakenly took MUS021 instead of MUS020. This class was extremely tedious and you had to read and write notes for different musical pieces. The two midterms consisted of over 100 notes that you had to write. This class was very stressful, but somehow ended up with an A. For an easy class, take MUS020! Not MUS021!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I am glad I ended up taking this class. Professor Whitelaw is wonderful teacher full of enthusiasm to teach. This class is a super Easy A, it is literally impossible to fail this class, unless if you dont show up. He gives you the answers to his test, all you have to do is come to class.

Honestly, something had to have changed since the last class. I took this class because he had such great reviews, but I regret taking this it. He didnt teach but expected us to know everything and he made the class way more difficult than it needed to be.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Loved taking this class. Learned a lot and had a lot of fun in this class. Definitely would recommend taking this class if you want to have fun and get an easy A. I feel like this is how all college courses should be, but I loved coming class everyday feeling like I am going to learn something new and still have a good time.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Would take again

reviews.comment: He is just nice enough.

Was this class often boring? Sure. Was the professor continiously off topic? Sure. But this class is also super easy. You show up to class, and you'll pretty much get an A. He gives all answers to midterms and finals. Is there singing and dancing? Sadly for me, yes, but its honestly worth it for how easy it is.

HE IS THE GREATEST! He is so funny and does the best accents. He is very passionate about the subject. We have two midterms and a final, which are very VERY easy! We have a term paper, which is basically a creative writing class. Super easy but very fun. TAKE THIS CLASS!
BEST PROFESSOR, HONESTLY. IT IS MY 4TH YEAR AND I AM SAD I DIDN'T KNOW ABOUT HIM EARLIER.  The 1st week seems hard but promise you if you stick through it, it will be worth it. Super awesome prof!
This professor does not give too much homework. We just listen to him to talk and he gives the general idea of what is on the midterm, sometimes with the answers to the test.

Great professor that teaches well with relevant information AND tests are easy. It's so important to attend ALL lectures because he takes attendance. You must take notes. He writes all his notes on the board. There isn't too much but all the notes he writes down, those are the midterms and finals. Super easy class overall.

Professor Whitelaw is a little unique in personality and his style of teaching. He's very passionate about his subject and has a lot of good stories that go along with what he's teaching. Attend class regularly, I feel that's the only way to get a good grade. Office hours are really helpful too if you don't know how to read the music notes.
Very informative, highly passionate instructor. Humorous with storytelling and really sets up the students to succeed in the class.

He sometimes jumps around from story to story, but he takes this into account when reviewing for tests. He truly wants students to do well and will help them out in any way he can. He also expects excellence from his students and I think excellence is becoming a lost art, so thankful for a professor who demands it.
Really cool guy. Extremely helpful and interested in students doing well. Exams were very straightforward.

Every “A” I received was earned and every assignment required critical analysis and thinking. He not only presented us with up to date information, he also created a stimulating learning environment by incorporating live music, relevant videos, and extra credit opportunities into his class. If you want to learn something fresh take a course w/him.

By the end of the quarter my knowledge, understanding, and appreciation of Scottish music increased tremendously. Professor Whitelaw successfully taught us the significance, relevance, and intricacies of Scottish music within the short 12 week quarter. Real cool guy too. If you want to learn something new and fresh, take a course with him.

This class is awesome. Attendance isn't technically mandatory, but if you want to learn the instrument you should probably show up every day. Ian is such a cool guy too, full of awesome stories and jokes and he's a great instructor. If you're practicing and showing up you'll be fine. It's a really fun class.

He really emphasizes "active learning" and requires students to work with one another to learn material. Real horrible lectures, he draws a lot of figures which makes the content confusing. There is a lack of powerpoints. If you don't have a good Biology and Chemistry background, study your ass off!
Very interesting and cares deeply about our future.

I didn't really enjoy he's class. He spends a lot of time drawing diagrams and if the class doesn't do good he'll lecture you about it  (instead of lecturing biology). Yeah, he'll help you if you go to office hours, only the people who go get good grades. He takes the fact that they know him into account. Study with MCAT books. Do it.

Very approachable in office hours. I highly, HIGHLY recommend going. He loves working with students who attend office hours he are actually helpful. His tests are difficult though. Lots of troll questions which include something along the lines of: is it I, II, or III, I and III, or II and III, or none. Best biology lecturer I've had so far though.

BIOL 107A is notoriously difficult, but Dr. Hyman is very skilled at breaking down the concepts. He gives you the notes, powerpoints, and clicker questions after every lecture, along with practice problems. This doesn't mean you can skip out on class, though! Go to class, study hard, and if you have questions, ask him, he's very approachable.

Do not take Hyman/Maduro for 107A. He expects way too much from his students and his exams are beyond hard. I have never taken a class worse than this. Avoid at all cost unless you want to ruin your GPA.

107a is probably the hardest upper div I've taken at UCR, its equivalent to taking BCH 110c, dont take this class unless absolutely necessary, made the mistake of taking this class and had no idea what i was in for. Hyman is super helpful  and cares alot.

He is the one of the nicest professors. He really cares about students and is willing to spend alot of his extra time to talk to you and help you get good grades. His tests are very difficult seeing as how midterm avg were 13/26. He CARES ABOUT EACH INDVIDUAL STUDENTS SO GO TALK TO HIM HE'S NOT SCARY

He's not that bad, great great great lecturer can make anyone understand bio, which is amazing esp if u plan on going to med school!! quizzes=5% midterm 1=20%, midterm 2=30% and final is 45% and gives 5% extra credit!! go to office hours and SI

Hyman by far is the worst biology professor, his first midterm was moderately difficult, I went to all his office hours and I went to the SI meetings, he gets mad if you don't ask him very detailed questions. His second midterm was beyond difficult, the material he had us study was useless, and I image the final will be the same as the second test.

Probably one of the worst teachers I've ever had in my college career.  He did a dual-lecture series with Dr. Haimo, and it was terrible.  Pedagogy is all off the charts, tests overly hard (meant to trick), TAs mocked those who were trying and violated university privacy rules.  Don't take him.  Oh and I've taken many biology classes before too.
I wouldn't say hes the greatest teacher!?? not worth it

Not that great. Sure he's clear and a great lecturer, but be prepared before asking him questions, he can be mean but its only because he wants you to understand every bit he teaches. I worked hard and got a C-, with above average quiz scores in discussion and ok on midterms. OH help.5A isnt bad, just work hard.

I had taken AP Biology and scored a 5 on the exam, so that helped a lot, but it's not the reason I rated him high. He's very clear and engaging in his lectures, and his tests are fair and make a lot of sense. If you pay attention and took good notes, and read the book for some clarification, you should be able to ace this class.
Favors students who go to his office hours. Get good seats, because he uses the chalkboard a lot! And anything that isn't in his lectures won't be on exams
Amazing professor! He really wants his students to learn. His tests were hard but office hours are really helpful. Really organized and the class was very interesting.

One of the best teachers I have ever had.  Listen to everything he says in class, as a lot of what he says is very important.  Utilizes the blackboard most of the time, taking his time to be sure students understand concepts and explains things in detail.  Very approachable, and as the person below me said, he is very well liked. Two Thumbs up.

Dr. Hyman is a hell of a good teacher.  His attendance is very high.  I stayed behind for the next BIOL5A lecture and that professor had barely any students.  At the end of the last lecture this quarter, everybody gave him an ovation.  He tries very very hard.  He uses the blackboard and chalk most of the time.  Not a boring power point teacher!

He is a good professor, but the only way you would be able to do well is if you have passed the AP BIO exam in high school or studied 6-8 hours per day. These are the only two options to get an A in his class. You might boost an A- to an A if you ask the right questions during office hours. He writes the midterms based on his lectures.

THE BEST PROFESSOR I HAVE EVER HAD!Very well organized,perfect lectures,extremely knowledgeable,he loves what he teaches.If you are dedicated to learning the material and are willing to make an effort instead of expecting an easy "C",you will enjoy this class.VERY ENLIGHTENING!He REALLY WANTS YOU TO LEARN YOUR STUFF,so if he seems stern,thats why!!
Extremely dedicated to his students, helpful and always goes out of his way to help you undertand. Tests are fair, but if you go to lecture w/o reading you can still get an A. Excellent!
Explains material very clearly, but really mean during office hours.
One of the best bio professors at UCR!!!! hard yet teaches extremely well! take him if you get a chance!!

he is the greatest professor u'll ever have regardless of some pple say. he really knows how to teach the students. go to class, read the material and don't procratinate! if u don't do those stuff seriously what are u complaining about? be sure to know every little details in bio. don't just read it and think u get it. go to the OH it helps u alot!

Mean teacher in office hours.  Bio is bio and therefore the tests are hard.  With any teacher, one needs to study very hard with the Bio series.  5A isn't bad though.  Not generous with the curve at all.
Not worth it!

Great professor! His lectures are very clear and interesting. Office hours are really helpful, just don't ask him to do lectures over again. You have to ask him specific questions, or he'll hella call you out in front of everyone.

BEST PROFESSOR I EVER HAD, however also the most DIFFICULT. He knows his stuff, but you have to do your part in reviewing the lecture notes every night, go to office hours, and integrate the material, dont memorize, but UNDERSTAND, and practice everything, dont sit on ur butt!
One of the best teachers at UCR, I was lucky to get him
DEFINITELY ONE OF THE BEST FACULTIES IN UCR.  Great Professor! The reason a lot of people think it's hard is because the class require understanding and applying concept..not just memorizing.
Best professor I've ever had. Period. Very clear, and super helpful. He is a distinguished professor, after all.
No Comments
You have to study hard for his class but he is a master at explaining the concepts.  Go to office hours and you’ll be fine.  He is one of the best professors I’ve ever had.
No Comments

Extremely organized, well presented lectures...simply keep up with reading and with class, and you will do well.  This is not my major, but I wish my engineering classes were this clear and well organized!

good teacher, good lecturer. he actually cares about students, and will try his hardest to help you. i accidentally pissed him off, but got an A nonetheless. i enjoyed the material alot, but most people have trouble with it... so be careful of your grades.

Great teacher. He writes everything that you need to know on the blackboard, and really trys to spell out the hard stuff. Midterms were hard, but you could still get a good grade if you know ur stuff. The final was impossible. Take him if you want to learn but arn't too worried about GPA.
very clear. I like his teaching style. Likes students who go to office hours with questions. Presents material in a clear and orginized way that makes note taking and understanding a lot easier.

Took his class 2 yrs ago and repeat for better grade. I wanted to took with him the second time because he was the best Bio5A teacher I've had. Present the material in a very organize and understanable manner. Helpful and show concern for student. No wonder he is awarded Campus Teaching Award.
He is a good teacher, but I'm sorry to say that an intro Bio course does NOT weed out future physicians like previously stated.

Best professor I have had here at UCR. Even though the tests are a bit difficult, he is super nice and very thorough during lectures.  I studied my ass off and finally ended up with an A-! You must be willing to put forth time and effort.  This class separates the doctors from the medial technicians

Key to getting an A: Read material ahead of lecture, KNOW and UNDERSTAND concepts(memorization will at best get you a C, if you're lucky), go over lecture slides online.  Tests aren't simple no-brainer definitions; you MUST carefully think over instead of just read through notes; VERY in-depth class
No Comments
No Comments

I thought he taught well but the tests were very confusing. I studied very hard for this course but still managed to get an F. Also he is very rude during office hours just make sure you don't ask any "stupid" questions
avoid taking this professor as much as you can....tests are very hard and cant explain material clearly...almost half of my Bio class failed in the winter quarter...DO NOT TAKE HIM!><

All you guys are crazy.  This little dude is wack!  His tests were so hard!  I studied all day, every day till like 4 am and i still managed to get a D in his class.  He and Cardullo sucked.  I suggest you take some other teacher.
I don't know what you guys are talking about. I thought he was a crappy teacher. I took him Fall '03. His tests were impossible and you could study all day and night and still fail the class.
Awesome prof... loved his class.. and loved asking questions.. he hasnt taught this class since fall 02 so if you can catch him i strongly suggest taking it!
he is nice, but his tests were really hard. an A is still obtainable if study a week b4 the test.
his tests were hard, but an A was still possible to obtain. i studied so hard and ended up with a B finally.
Awsome teacher.  The course is a tad difficult but he definitly clears stuff up.  Visits labs too.  Very approchable.
His lectures were good but his tests were VERY hard!  Not very good with communicating with students either.
This guy has attitude when you ask him too many questions, but his lectures are GREAT and hes a GOOD instructor, too bad the tests are hard!
He is a good teacher, but he does give students bad attitude when students do bad on his tests.    and tests are definitely HARD.  recomment not to take him
His tests are VERY DIFFICULT! Just studying the book and the notes will not give you a passing grade.
great teacher! he hated me, but he was still a reallyreally good lecturer. hard tests and hard curve, but hey, you learn biology damn thoroughly from him

Dr. Hyman is a wonderful teacher!  He is incredibly helpful and always makes sure that people understand.  His lectures are great, he goes into detail and he draws simple picture on the board that break everything down.  But tests are really hard!
he's grrrreeeatttt!!  even though i fail the tests and quizzes, i still like biology because of his teachings. =D
Dr. Hyman is a great teacher, he explains the information in great detail, is easy to approach, and is always available in office hours.
He is awesome teacher. He will explain you and give examples how to write an essay. Good lectures.

Ian was my favorite English series teacher. His prompts are very fun and not boring, as they have to do with pop culture. He is a comic book fan, and by being in this class, I've been made a fan as well. He grades fairly, but gives a lot of helpful insight before essays. Take him!

Awesome teacher with a vast knowledge with comic books! Very approachable, and fun prompts! Not an "easy" A, but if you put in the work and if your English is decent, you will do great. In love with the book we had to read this quarter. Take him during the summer session! Its fun and its fast, especially if you love pop culture.

Ian is extremely helpful, chill and relaxed. He chooses interesting prompts rather than boring academically centered ones although the phrasing could be a bit vague. He leaves a lot of time for improving essays. Grades fairly and easy to talk to. Prompts are centered on comic books and modern culture so it's  not for all people.

I liked that he is a nice professor but grades harshly. He goes give helpful feedback during his office hours and recommends going to the learning center. If your not good with English you will certainly struggle.

He is a nice graduate student to approach, but he grades harshly. He does give good feedback during his office hours and he recommends students to go to the learning center. If your not good at English then you will struggle with this class. He wants his students to be on time everytime. He only allows one revision which sucks.

He is a nice professor, but he grades harshly. If your not good really good with English you will struggle.However, he does recommend going to the ilearn center and he does give some good feedback on what you need to improve on.

Ian Ross is a great instructor. There are about 4 essays and you can get an A on all four if you follow the book and what he says. He allows a lot of freedom for essays compared to other instructors I have had. He is always willing to help. He also allows you to redo essays. Fun and enthusiastic guy. Definitely take him.
super hard! avoid this teacher at all costs!
DROP WHILE YOU CAN

Ian Ross is one of the most insightful TA's out there.  He is very intelligent and he wants to pass that on to his students.  This class is not a gimme, so it is imperative to keep up with readings and assignments.  He explains things in ways to relate to students and I appreciate him for that.  Overall, you'll learn a lot from this man.

While it's clear that the professor is very knowledgeable on the subject, a three hour lecture, no matter the class, is too long. A lot of the material is very abstract and hard to understand if you are not already an expert in film, and she is not very approachable when you try to ask any questions. It's as if she's offended that you didn't get it

Despite being a 3 hour long film class, we did not watch any films and all the material we were graded on(1-3 question quizzes) were solely based on long readings or obscure details in the movie that you would have struggled to catch unless this was your second or third viewing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She has shown triggering content in class without any prior warning. Her lectures are full of fragment sentences because she never properly finishes the points that she makes when she speaks. She is unapproachable and will make you feel dumb and unsafe to ask questions in class. She talks a lot but has almost nothing of substance exit her mouth.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Not only I personally didn't like this class, but I never heard someone saying like this class. The chosen film themselves were interesting, but other than that this class is sucks. The pop quiz as an attendance was crazy. Also, what she talks about in lectures is too specific and subjective POV of her. At least this class is not an introduction.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Obviously very educated on Japanese culture and provided good movies for the course I took (Intro to JPN Film). Her 2hr 50min lectures make me fall asleep everytime and talks the entire time, and it can be pretty hard to follow what she is trying to teach. She gives short breaks and will sometimes give two quizzes during the lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: You're expected to watch the films outside of class, and 90% of the weekly 3hr lecture is her talking string along jargon-filled sentences. Also, many weekly quizzes are "gotcha" questions that don't make you think critically. Discussion is easy enough as are the tests, but the lecture is dreadful. I highly recommend avoiding this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Highly recommend taking this class with her. She is caring and respectful. Class needs to be more structured but overall this class is an easy Upper Div.

Professor Tasha is such an amazing professor. This class is fairly easy and the TA's were super amazing. Even though this class was not structured correctly. The professor did not have clear instructions on some assignments but still easy to complete. Offered EC opportunities to those who wanted a higher grade. Lectures give codes for attendance.

Tasha is extremely disorganized and does NOT supply students with any concrete/direct lecturing, and instead has students spend hours searching the deepest parts of the internet for academic papers that don't exist or are behind paywalls. This entire class will have you going around in circles with no support or actual education from Tasha.

Professor Iglesias is very disorganized. She does allow for late assignments and regrades. There are a lot of papers throughout the course. It's basically a bunch of papers that are repetitive to be honest. I was confused as to what we were supposed to do during class. There are way too many group projects that aren't relevant to the course.

It's clear that prof. Iglesias cares about teaching, but she is very disorganized with how her class operates. She also assigns alot of group work projects and does not take the time to carefully explain directions/expectations for assignments. Do not take her class unless you want to not know what's going on most of the time. Just plain awful.

I'll just say the work load isn't bad, if you're working in a group. On the other hand, be ready to be extremely confused all the time and to ask questions to the TA or your peers.The general set up of the course and explanations/instructions of assignments are very, very messy and everyone in the class is constantly confused on what to do lol

She doesn't have clear grading criteria and the work you get is constantly all over the place TAs seem to clear up most of what she doesnt clarify and even then there are holes in what ur doing it's not harshly graded mostly busy work  I haven't seen is impressionable. I say overall the class structure is extremely disorganized wouldn't take again

I love Professor Iglesias. She is very caring and respectful. We learned about DEI Initiatives in higher education. There are two group projects but there was an option to work individually. All the assignments in this class are easy and help you reach your goal of finishing the final project (a PowerPoint).
Such an amazing professor and has very engaging lecture. There can be a lot of participation with in class group work. However, there is barely heavy assignments and is an easy class to earn an A
Don't buy the text book in his class. Lecture notes are helpful. Be prepared for tricky exams question. He's a generous grader however.
He rarely fail anyone. Big curve, but hard exams.
One of the best professors at UCR.  Made communications very understandable and clear.  As long as you go to class and pay attention to his lecture, his tests are very easy to Ace.
Excellent all-around professor...made a confusing subject very clear, and was always helpful and accomodating to the students.

She is horrible! More than half the class failed her midterm! She says she only gives easy problems on the tests but she gives SUPER DIFFICULT problems! I'm taking her class and I do super well on the quizzes and homework, but I flat out fail her tests. I study day & night, only to fail! NEVER TAKE HER CLASS! Okay, have a nice rest of the day! :)
Going to the lecture is useless, only one midterm and one final. Final is insanely hard!
Such a great teacher! You should most def. take her class!! two midterms and they were fairly easy! just go to class and you should be fine! (:

She gave good explanations of theory, lots of examples, practice exams that show what you need to know, and always told people to come to office hours if they need help. If you do poorly it's a lack of effort on your part, because she does everything she can to help. She gave the practice final less than a week before final, I wonder if she forgot?
Great professor. Really helps and loves to help students. She has no problems answering questions and will do anything to help. Highly recommended.

Ignatova never tells what you need to know. She only gives examples. Thick accent that is hard to understand. Makes a lot of mistakes when she writes on the board. I will say that all of the things that she posts online are helpful though. But you basically have to learn from what she posts.

Took this professor for BIEN 120. He is okay during lab. communication about exam content was unclear. The first midterm included a very challenging question that accounted 40% of  exam grade. He is exactly the professor he told us he doesn't want to be, someone who lies about what's gonna be on exams. Gave me trust issues
Noshadi is a very enthusiastic professor. His class is pretty easy to follow but it is mostly memorization. The midterms are not hard, but be prepared to know small details from each slide

Noshadi is such a sweet professor. He cares about his students and learns their names. The class is composed of 2 midterms, a final, and some group quizzes (open note). He makes the class a comfortable environment and is good at teaching the material. My favorite professor I have had so far!
worst prof at ucr. very unorganized, posts paper rubric the day the paper is due. gave final review a day before final. doesn't care about students, makes life miserable for a breadth dance course.

I took Dance 12,(rate-my-professor didn't have another class option for this professor). Analyzing articles weekly, group projects, one final 5-8 page paper on a topic you develop within your group and no final exam. Easy, busy work type of class but easy A if you attend class and discussion. Would take again, great teacher and TA.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Johnson was very kind and was welcoming to all. Had to choose one of three (conventional, research, or creative) as our quarter project. Offered extra credit questions on midterm and final. Since it was online, the midterm and final were open note and provided great feedback. Enjoys listening to students' thoughts on lectures in class.

Spring2021. Great lecturer and explainer of things. Class structure needs work. We had to do vlogs and those were pretty stupid even though they were fairly easy to do. Not a difficult subject but he makes you work for the grade.
This class made me think about organizational life in a new way. Cool guy but being online sucked.
This prof deserves tenure ASAP. LOVED his class and always looked forward to his lectures!
The lack of explanation on the group project and papers blew my mind. You would think they would be addressed further in lectures especially when they are over 30% of your overall grade. Good luck.

THERE ONLY FOUR quizzes DURING THE QUARTER, NO MIDTERM AND FINAL. THE LAST QUIZ WAS GIVEN FOR FREE POINTS AS 100. THERE IS ONE TERM PAPER AND ONE GROUP PRESENTATION. THE ADDITIONAL READING FOR EACH PERSON ON DISCUSSION SECTION WILL ONLY HOLD TWO ARTICLES for 10 WEEKS, YOU WILL BE SELECTED BY TA'S WHEN IS YOUR TIME FOR carrying THE CLASS.
Great Professor. New to the university and has a strong passion to teach about group cooperation and the logistics behind it. Really did an amazing job in his first quarter.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Professor Ingram is incredible. I enjoyed the lectures and how he kept students engaged. There is a group project towards the end that you want to choose the right people for as you aren't going to be graded on much. Quizzes weren't difficult, but they make up 40% of your grade so make sure you pay attention in his lectures.

This class is not difficult per se, but it is hard to get a good grade because he grades on so few things. I can see he has a passion for the job, but it really shouldn't be this hard to get a good grade. It's also kinda ironic that he is teaching psychology and OB but isn't very accommodating to students and their "stressors" and mental health.

amazing professor, very passionate and great lecturer overall. The class isn't difficult, as long as you go to lecture and pay attention, you should be able to do well on the quizzes. Pick a good group of people for your group project and you'll be fine. Hes amazing, if you can take him, do it!
BUS 107 winter quarter 2024 asynch. Loved him. So good. Did 4 vlogs (100pts each), term paper, and group presentation. Still working on the last 2 things but I loved him.
So pleased with this course - particularly as I have heard foundational courses in the business school are awful.  Ingram was passionate and deeply concerned about student comprehension of lectures.
Inspiring, insightful, intelligent. I really enjoyed this course.
very difficult to get an A but easy enough to pass
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: oh gosh this class is supposed to be easy but good luck trying to get an A. easy enough to pass but if you want anything above a B+ you're gonna work like a dog. the weightage of his quizzes is 40% for 3 small exams, and if you get more than 1 question wrong it's an automatic B. averages on these quizzes were Ds and Cs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class's average quiz score is consistently 66%, but the professor curved it to 75%. Despite this adjustment, your 40% contribution to the class suggests little impact. The lectures are excellent, but the quiz questions diverge from the lecture content, posing a challenge for students.

Prof Ingram has been my favorite professor out of all of my upper-division courses; his lectures are very engaging and he is passionate about what he does. While he is definitely a tough grader I still enjoyed this course a lot. There are frequent quizzes which can be hard to do well on so make sure to study the readings and participate for an A.
This class is based on teamwork. If your teammates give you an F then that is you grade. Very unfair class

(WINT 2022). No textbook was required. Dr. Ingram had interesting lectures with real-life examples. We had to read weekly research articles for TA's discussions, with mandatory attendance and participation. Every other week, we had a quick and simple quiz. Instead of a midterm and final, we had Case Competition Presentations and a term paper.

Professor Ingram was a totally fair professor. As long as you actually put effort into the course, you should have no problem with 107. Make sure to utilize all the resources available, especially for the CCP. Very engaging!
Ingram has very had quizzes but everything else is a cake walk; he however was not very understanding of people during covid and was a bit "Strict" on missing assignments etc.

First impressions reveal that Prof Ingram is very passionate about the subject. The lectures were very engaging. The quizzes are straightforward, granted you reviewed the lecture slides. There is one group project in the second half. The only assignment I dreaded was the final paper which is about 10 pages in length. My TA was also great.

Professor Ingram's lectures are very engaging and his attitude helps you stay awake during them. The only thing I was intimidated by was the paper, but it didn't end up being so bad. The prompt is vagueish which is good. Overall, liked having him as a professor, he wants his students to succeed, and he tries helping us out as much as he can.

He's so knowledgeable on the class topic and example. very enjoying to having his lecture and the teaching method that he gave out.

I've taken BUS 107 ,finished BUS156,and planning to take BUS 145 in summer. 
Hope he will be teaching in the summer.
Grade based on 5 self reflection, 4 quizzes and one group project. It's not hard, just take time.

I've taken 107 and 156 with prof ingram and he's amazing!! The work isn't hard if you just pay attention and participate tbh and he's super understanding. He does a decent amount of interactive activities and there's a decent amount of participation. Overall the classes weren't too hard and he's an amazing prof !
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Loved this prof. Well done UCR

Vlogs are aftermath; however, if you really try hard enough, you will end up with an 85 to 90. The professor does an amazing job in terms of explaining the material. The TA is the problem; they don't know what they are doing the entire semester.

Took this class online and the professor was very strict on grading and was not flexible or lenient about your grade. All he did was give the lectures but everything was graded by the TA. There was a group project and 10 page paper due at the end of the quarter and an extra credit assignment for 1 point.

I enjoyed this Organizational Behavior class and learned a lot about OB behavior and I am very thankful for passionate professors like Ingram! HE gave a lot of amazing creativity growth and advice during this summer with replacing quizzes for Vlogs. I would've loved to have the final project to be a LIVE presentation than a recorded video.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: One of the best at UCR! Professor Ingram is clearly passionate about his work, and it is evident he wants to see students succeed. His lectures are interesting and thought provoking, and he designs his courses around theory and practice. If personal and professional growth is your aim, do not miss out on this guy!

Prof Ingram is a great teacher and respected. The material is difficult and his quizzes are challenging as they are based on what he explains during lecture. Take good notes and you should be fine. There is a group project and there is also a 2500 word paper due at the end of the course. Overall, not an easy class, but it was fairly interesting.

Passionate & insightful professor. Lectures are engaging & interactive due to frequent participation & seeing theories in action. Dr. Ingram clearly defines his expectations & his lectures are clear & easy to follow. He is a nice person who genuinely wants his students to succeed. I had a very positive learning experience! Definitely recommend!

One of the best professors UCR has to offer. His quizzes are only tough if you dont attend the lectures. The Case Competition was a nice way to see theory comento life. Without a doubt, Ingram deserved the Golden Apple!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I took his BUS 145 class. We did a team project and I found the grading criteria to be vague and too subjective. The pop quizzes were also difficult; most of the time the average ended up being a C. Otherwise, Prof. Ingram seems like an okay guy. Avoid Professor Ingram if you desire an easy A.

Professor Ingram is one of the few Professors at UCR that actually care about their students and their learning outcomes. His quizzes are not as difficult as people are saying, perhaps they did not attend lectures.

The case competition project grading criteria is flawed. Ingram gives too much power to your group members. Make sure you take the class with people you know. I did my part (the main idea + multiple slides) and we even placed first in our section which should be an A+. But I only received a 90% on this project bc of their ratings.

The class is an overall great experience. Quizzes are really hard, depending on the ta you get. Overall, the class is manageable and worth taking. You can really see that he loves his job and tries to make the class entertaining.
The quizzes in this class are way too difficult because they are worded in such a weird way. Would rather take Raj for BUS 107.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Ingram is my favorite business professor at UCR. We participated in activities, group projects, and lectures to better retain information rather than just trying to temporarily remember it. This class can help you become a better team player; which I think everyone needs. We applied more than just learning the theory. This class is top notch.

Took this class thinking it was going to be a different professor and that it would be extremely easy. That said, having Professor Ingram was a great surprise. He is a great teacher that gets students involved in class activities and fosters interactive learning. Just do the readings and you'll be fine, he wants everyone to get a good grade.

60% of the class is based on exams but he does grade the exams on a curve and takes out questions that the majority of class missed. I liked that the professor had activities for some classes. The teacher was also very vague about the criteria he expected in his class even though I went to office hours. Lots of work for leadership development

Professor Ingram is so cool! UCR finally got a good teacher that's versatile. I'm not a great test taker, so the exams are what got me. But the class is super fun and you definitely learn a lot. There's truly only a few assignments and it's pretty much average on work load. I wish I could take him for another course!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This professor is AMAZING. The midterm was a little harder than we all expected and he was so kind enough to take questions out, that majority missed. He truly cares about his students and what he teaches. I have never met someone so passionate. He is an amazing lecturer and ensures that everyone understands. No busy work and he brings his dog!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I originally took 156 because people said it would be an easy A. However, after a few weeks with Prof. Ingram, I figured that I had to work for that A. Nonetheless, he is a great professor. Great lecturers and great readings, if you stay on top of your assignments and studies, getting a good grade isnt a problem. Definitely learned a lot too! :)

This class was way more work than it was supposed to be. Unfortunately I got the professor that teaches this class a lot harder. I took this class because I thought it would be relatively easy and would improve my leadership qualities but it seems as if we are doing a lot of work and studying and not learning.

Great professor!! His class his awesome, there's no homework, just keep up with the readings, which are reasonable length. Very valuable inter-/intra-personal course. Would take again, look forward to lecture, stay openminded, and keep track of when the quizzes are! you may think you did well but actually did poorly--know the material.

Excellent professor. 5 pop quizzes (he does hint when they are), group project, paper, and attend discussions. Clear grading rubric and easy class to pass. The quizzes are easy as long as you review lecture notes. No need to buy textbook. I would definitely take again.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: No extra credit. 1 midterm and if you score higher on the final it replaces your midterm grade. The midterm is doable but the main weight is on the short answer questions which are hard graphs about policies. Multiple choice are easy if you read the lecture slides. There is also homework and 1 group project for which you have to present in class.

I don't recommend this profs at all. Trust me, in her econ 105b, you have to learn by self, it is a little difficult to understand what she says, sometimes she confused the content, only one quiz in discussion class. one midterm, one final, no extract credit. It is a tough class.

In the beginning she was slightly different then other but one the we got settled it was beautiful teaching experience I got everything very easy  she very friendly and knows exactly what student's need and have his gifted knowledge to be passed up to others and she does it beautifully like filling up a glass of water in student minds Arvind SSCM

Difficult to understand, both because of her accent and how she teaches the class. She often has to answer questions because of her confusing explanations. If you want to pass, it is essential to read the textbook because her lectures are not worth going. Just hope you get a good TA because they are probably better at explaining concepts.

She was not a very effective professor, at least not for me. Most all of my understanding was from the book, the homework or the TA (who was pretty good, I must say - he should have taught the class). It isn't her accent, it's her way of teaching. She does curve it, and you'll pass if you try, but it might not be the grade you like.

Serious accent. Has to answer a lot of questions in class because of how unclear she is. The assignments will save you, she is owned by Pearson! Read the book and just show up and you'll pass. I like this stuff but it can be really boring to most.
