reviews.comment: He is one of the best professors I took for English. He teaches you about interesting concepts of society and how it functions. Definitely go to his office hours and take his advice on essay help. Don't skip the class it counts towards your grade, plus easier points by participating in class. I would take him again he is the best for English :)

Winter is not the easiest grader. He'll catch you on little things, and knows when you've pulled an all-nighter on an essay. Make sure you do the reading and at least try to go to office hours. He tells you when there will be quizzes on the reading and allows for revisions. Most importantly, DO NOT SKIP CLASS YOU WILL LOSE POINTS!!

reviews.comment: Not the most entertaining but was cool. Three papers throughout the class. Grades a little difficult. Homework was only reading and you read one interesting book through out the class. Would take again.

reviews.comment: Uninteresting instructor, no personality. At least two PowerPoint presentations per class period. Will not give you full points on worksheets. Gives B's to everyone as a benchmark. Very unreliable, will say you can include something on an essay one day and then say you can't when you ask him the next. Unorganized. Does not provide good feedback.

Professor Winter was an overall great professor. His grading criteria was clear and the papers weren't that difficult as long as you showed effort. Grades lenient and gives good feedback. You do have to read one novel but it was actually enjoyable once you dive into it. Would surely take again.
lacking in compassion and will make you feel inferior if you go to office hours no kindness in his heart

reviews.comment: He is very unreasonable and does not respond to emails.  I could can take a strict teacher, but there is a line where it is too much when I cannot even get an email back.

Ppl that say he is unreasonable are being babies that expect engineering to be easy. He is a very fair professor and his expectations should be the standard for bcoe. Yes his exams are hard, but he teaches well and they're not impossible. He needs to have strict guidelines for a reason… but students love to complain. This class needs to be hard.
Slides are extremely disorganized, doesn't post the answers to the hw, doesn't give enough practice. Gives pop quizzes every lecture which everyone fails. Very strict and attendence mandatory.

reviews.comment: Fantastic at explaining complex topics in an engaging and comprehensive way. Hw is short (and helpful) and exams are wholly reflective of class material. Taking 115 with him made me feel like i chose the right field, and I've loved his grad courses and TEs even more. His dry sense of humor has given him a rep for being stern, but he's very kind.

I really did learn a lot as far as biomechanics from his class last year. He is an awesome lecturer and really motivated to ensure that every student comprehends. He definitely can keep your focus while lecturing.

This class was one of the hardest classes not only in the Bioengineering Dept. but at UCR ive ever taken. Make sure to go to lectures even if attendance is not mandatory. The slides are very vague, and its important to go to lectures to memorize and write down what he says. Do not procrasinate on the project.

reviews.comment: This guy is a knowledgeable prof, but his grading is rough, average on mt was a 54, avg on the final was a 50. Know the lecture slides, score high on the first mid term bc the final is hard. FRQ's are majority of the time covered in the TA's slides. Project is hefty so don't wait till the last second to see it. Good luck!

Dr. Liao is passionate about the subject he teaches. Exams cover anything from the slides and the research papers. Beware, while attendance isn't mandatory, things he says in lectures that aren't on the slides do pop up in exams. Despite the exam difficulty, he is very knowledgeable, and I learnt interesting bioengineering applications from lecture

Dr. Liao is a great teacher. Had his lab and his biochemistry class. Passionate teacher, also has very interesting research lab. Lab class correlates with his research (on a much smaller scale). Lab was fun, much preferred it to bioinstrumentation lab.

Doesn't give full time on finals and midterm, very nice professor tho, and good at teaching, but really hard grader, and here grading scale makes no sense, it's a tough class with a lot of memorization, and the final is not easy or fair because of the lack of time.

Fire. Lectures were easy to follow, homework was identical to lecture material, exams were identical to provided practice problems. Each homework assignment had extra credit opportunities to code the algorithms we were working with.

She's straightforward and forgiving. Posts lectures notes online, good amount of extra credit opportunities, the examples from the study guide for midterms are similar to the actual test. The final was harder, but the study guide is also provided. Overall, she's nice considering there's already a curve coming into the class.

She had a ridiculously long final, many students did not even have a chance to finish it, worth 40% of your grade. Curved our grades but if you already have a decent grade in the class.. only expect to move up a couple of points. Also lectures were confusing and the homework problems were almost nothing like the examples she did in lecture!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Weekly HW or project, lowest HW and project is dropped,  there is one midterm and one final. Practice tests are EXTREMELY helpful to prepare for midterm and final. Lectures can seem a little slow paced, she recorded every single lecture.
Good lecture, helpful notes, and moderate tests and quizzes, it is fortunate and pleasured to have her as my math professor

Don't worry about the concepts in the lectures, the example problems she does explain things pretty well, the accent takes a while to get used to though. All the notes she does on class gets posted, clearest notes I've ever seen. Lots of WebWork homework, but frankly you learn the most from them. Practice exams are on point. Final counts for a lot.
Concepts are explained well, usually with examples. Practice exams are close to the real ones. Homework is not heavy and very straightforward.

Great professor! Straightforward exams. Gives practice midterm/final. Lectures were easy to understand, despite the accent. Homework was not time-consuming at all. Gives the formula for all HW problems in class, so all you have to do is find the formula, plug in the numbers and that's it. Very good teacher for the class!

Professor Smith is though but only if you don't try hard. If you have the mindset that it will be easy it won't! You really need to work hard. He will push you to try your best. But overall, he is funny, caring, and will work with you; all you have to do is ask. Hope this helps!

Made his outside performance MANDATORY for class. Students had to find transportation and pay. Very disconnected. Will :) in your face, pretend everythings ok, constantly talking about right/wrong in hypothetical situations during lecture just to be dismissive of questions/challenges/concerns from students. Choreo is cute but hes v PRETENTIOUS man
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: If you want to take dance 005 for an easy A, just DO NOT take this pro's class. midterm is hard, final is hard, clarify is weak.He would record your movement when you doing your dance  phase assignment.You need to write lots of essay by using SINGLE SPACE!ALSO!GRADE HARD! NEVER REPLY EMAIL! wtf!!!

I took him for bus 152, not bus 112. I didn't get the option. It is a super easy class as long as you do the work; lectures are simple. Be prepared to present 3-4 projects with your group within the quarter. No exam has some homework to do, but overall a good, easy class to take.
He is a very fun professor.

Good professor, but the assignment directions were sometimes unclear. Overall pretty easy and interesting class, just beware for the pop quizzes, had a couple of assignments which you are able to do it groups, and a group project about pricing strategy.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Never take her class, I mean it when I say this.

Dr. Morrision is a great, however it is difficult to say that her teaching is good since she primarily reads off of slides. At some point in the quarter it became difficult to keep up with all the material because each powerpoint is about 50 slides or more, and EVERYTHING is fair game. It is important to do well on the midterms if you want an A.

There is a pop quiz that could be any lecture which was pretty difficult. Final was made difficult and 140 questions because the averages were high due to cheating. Someone even got caught cheating during the final but he was allowed to take the same final again. 94 is an A btw.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: 2 midterms, 1 final, 1 POPQUIZ. Juliet Morrison is a nice person but her lecturing can get dull; she only reads off slides. People raise their hand to ask questions and she never calls on them to ask, just keeps reading the slides, that's mainly all she does is read the slides. The pop quiz was not too bad, I would probably not take her again.

Dr. Morrison is hands down one of the best professors I've had at UCR. Attendance is "mandatory" due to PollEvs, but they are relatively easy. Lectures are engaging and exams are straightforward. She even provides extra credit opportunities. Dr. Morrison is extremely approachable after/ outside of class, and just wants the best for her students.

Her lectures were fun to listen too. Her exams are very fair and based on her slides. 1st midterm had 20 t/f questions while the 2nd midterm had half of t/f questions. Final was cumulative sadly. Provided 20 extra credit from polls & discussion assignments. Content wise it was interesting if you like how the immune system so it wasn't too bad.

I took both MCBL123 and MCBL129. I loved the classes. Prof. Morrison's is super organized, instructions are easy to follow. Her slides, polls, and exams are all well-aligned. She's very patient and approachable, you can always ask questions. She makes learning about viruses fun and inspiring. Highly recommend if you're interested in virology!

Took in W2024. She structures course clearly & teaches w/ enthusiasm. Exams were very fair & reflect exactly what she covers in lecture. Go to class/office hours & review notes thoroughly to succeed. She's so supportive, approachable, and truly wants ALL her students to learn and succeed. Most rewarding course I've had & can't recommend it enough!

BIOL123 W2024. INCREDIBLY knowledgeable & passionate. Made complex virology topics clear w/ humor, videos, & real-world examples. She has a love for teaching & genuinely cares about our understanding. Taught valuable study techniques I'll use beyond undergrad. The BEST esp for pre-health ppl. Study lectures well and go to office hours to succeed!

Dr. Morrison is one of the best upper-division professors I've had at UCR. She goes above and beyond to make her lectures engaging, fun, and most importantly, all-encompassing with all the details we need to know about certain topics. Her exams are very fair and reflective of this as well. I would take this class again in a heartbeat-it's amazing!

i loved professor morrison! you can tell she's so passionate about what she teaches and the material of the course is not difficult if you study. group project was required in discussion but her exams are not hard and she gives extra credit on exams as well. overall, she's accessible and makes things easy to understand

One of my favorite classes at UCR. Extremely interesting and straightforward since it goes hand in hand with MCBL121. Dr. Morrison is very approachable and knowledgeable, so don't be afraid to ask for help during her office hours. She helped me solidify concepts and relate them back to the physical labs which I really enjoyed!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I've taken many upperdivs at UCR and I think Dr. Morrisons class was one of the most engaging and exciting classes. She approaches the material very clearly and concisely and the topic itself is very interesting. Her class is fair and if you pay attention and go to office hours I think you will certainly get an A. She tests what is on her lecture.

BIOL 5A + taught half the quarter. Condescending, didn't know her material, + couldn't answer questions without referring to her slides. Notes and sample exams came from different professors. Memorize figures and small details to succeed in the class. 4 midterms; retake for m1 and curved m4 10pts bc everyone failed those. Need a 93.5% for an A.
Mcbl 129 was the best class Ive ever taken at UCR! It is so interesting and engaging, shes pretty knowledgeable, class isnt easy but its not impossible

Only the final and midterm matter but if the class does bad enough on the midterm shell average out ur scores to replace the midterm. She is willing to help you if you show up to office hours well in advance. Tests are similar to the practice versions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: midterm was 30% and final was 45% so the exams are 75% of your grade. doesn't matter if you get 100% on homework and attendance if you do bad on the exams. get ready to teach yourself the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Normally I'm not one to go on RateMyProfessor but if you are seeing this, don't take her. Her quizzes are balanced terribly, causing your scores to go down entire letter grades if you get a single question wrong. The way she worries about people cheating borders on insanity, and her lectures are about as useful as reading her notes.

There is a lack of online and technology savviness, especially handling the Lockdown Browser (This tool doesn't solve the fundamental issue). Please do not take this professor for her teaching abilities. A professor's teaching ability does not completely correspond to their personality. Required online polls for attendance during lecture.

just go to lecture regularly if u want a solid grade; its also stats so.. the final being airdropped only happened this quarter cuz ppl weren't going to class so idk if itll be a regular thing. i like the lectures and she a nice professor

Jun Li is a horrible professor. Lectures were no different than the online slides, with attendance waning due to her lack of ability to stray from her presentation. I basically taught the entire class content to myself using the textbook. She also gatekeeps practice exams to people who don't come to class (airdropped the practice final) DO NOT TAKE

bruh basically 70% of ur grade is dependent on about one midterm + one final, and then quizzes r graded interestingly. but once you take ur final it's a blind box and you don't get no feedback or anything. no curve. idk why I'm even learning this. class made me statistically calculate if i want to do this anymore.

this class was pretty content-heavy, the grading scale was 10% hw, 20% quizzes, 30% midterm, and 40% final. hw was assigned weekly, quizzes were during disc. quizzes + tests were straightforward if you follow lecture examples from notes or practice exams which are all posted. downside is no curve but you can bring a formula sheet to the exams.

Make sure to do the homework and show your work on all the labs. FRQs on quizzes are also based off of work. Make sure to show all work to get full credit and maximize points. She was available via email and office hours so take advantage of that when you need help. You need to be proactive to get a good grade.

Jun Li was a good professor. Her lectures were kind of boring, but she was always available in office hours and via email if I ever needed help. Her grading criteria was clear. Just do the homework and review the key concepts of the slides and you will do well in the class.

I'm gonna be honest, Jun Li isn't a very good professor. 

Her lectures are honestly pretty useless because
a) she treats lectures like speedrunning sessions
b) she doesn't show her work or explain concepts in detail
c) she has bad handwriting

She also tends to blame students for failing midterms/finals instead of asking for feedback

She's inconsiderate of students and will always talk over you. No curve for this class so just keep that in mind. Weekly quizzes labs & hw, 2 midterms, 1 final. Not enough time for quizzes and exams. Reads from her lecture slides, so attending lecture isn't helpful. You'll probably still pass the class, but most likely not with the grade you'd want

Class wasn't too bad. Do the hw and reviewed the slides so you're good. Labs were annoying-10% of grade. She reads off her lectures slides, so I would never attend. Recommend reviewing the examples from slides cause similar questions on midterms. Also, review quizzes! Unclear FRQ directions so show ALL WORK - BE EXTRA! Not hard to pass. Got an A.

Professor is very direct in lectures by reading off of slides without providing any extra information. The amount and difficulty of questions given during her exams are not appropriate for the time allotted, which is 50 minutes. She doesn't provide any practice exams for midterms or finals and simply asks students to do better if they scored low.

Professor Li is the worst. No consideration for her students and just reads off the lecture slides. Quizzes and tests are heavy and must be taken timed. Due to quizzes being really heavy, the time she gives to complete them is not enough. Don't take her; take another stats professor.

One of the best professors at UCR. He made learning really fun and interactive. Although attendance wasn't mandatory. Going to class made a huge difference in test scores. As long as you do the work and go to class, you will do fine.

Possibly the best class I have taken at UCR, he is not strict about attendance and clearly states what is expected to be on the weekly (short & easy) quizzes. There is no midterm or final, however there is a short project that can be done in a day. He knows how to keep students interested during lectures and offers a lot of extra credit opportunity

If taking soc, take Huft! His grading policy was amazing and he offered lots of extra credit. I stopped going to lectures around week 2, barely took notes, and was still able to do really good in this class. Make sure to go to discussion and do well on the online quizzes since they take up most of your grade. No exams, only an easy final project!

Professor Huft is great! Lots of good insight on sociology and our world. He is funny and respectful. He cares about your feedback and takes time to make the class better as the quarter goes on. There was one project that acted as our final in a sense and one online quiz each week.

Prof Huft is an amazing person and couldn't help not leaving a review. He's passionate about the subject and is easy to follow. Very caring of his students' personal lives and tried making this class lenient for all to succeed. There is extra credit and its easy to contact him in and out of class. Overall, a knowledgeable instructor.
Probably one of the best sociology professors here. Lectures are enjoyable, and he clearly cares about the concepts and his students. Very knowledgeable about the subject.

Lectures were enjoyable. Weekly quizzes and one online presentation, plus a lot of extra credit opportunities. I really enjoyed this class overall. Especially because he's a very engaging lecturer and also really funny

Professor Justin was a very engaging sociology teacher. I enjoyed the class a lot despite being a large class. Tasks were straightforward and he is willing to give extra credits to boost our grades so I like him. Overall an easy intro class. If you have any chance to take his class, do it! TAs grades all the tasks. Some were harder than others.

One of the most passionate instructors I've had at UCR so far, made attending his lectures every time something I looked forward to. He actively incorporates student feedback (and sociology studies) into his teaching. 1 video presentation on a topic of choice and weekly quizzes (timed, open-note) with no midterm/final, at least for W24.
One of the best professors I've had at UCR. He made me excited to learn new concepts. All assignments were straightforward and easy.

Professor Huft has been one the best professors I've taken at UCR. He's a funny guy and explains material in a way that is very easy to understand. Workload is extremely manageable, its easy to forget about this class lol. There are no exams, just one simple hw quiz on canvas every week, and one video project due towards the end of the quarter.

Good professor and great content. Although she asks you to buy 5 textbooks and convinces you the class will read all of them. Turns out that in lectures you don't even go into depth on the content in the textbooks and she covers it through slides in class. You could buy no textbooks for this class and you would be good as long as you go to lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Asynchronous. None of her lectures are her own. Posts a 300 page reading and expects us to read that and other readings. Midterm/Final are so nit picky. Would rather write an essay as a final for her. Midterm was graded incorrectly for 5-6 questions, took it back and she had to go regrade one by one. Don't even know what she looks like LOL. Easy.

Asynchronous class it wasn't too bad. Justen is not a good TA. Class grade is never available and the instructions for everything are vague. Lecture videos are terribly made and hard to follow. The midterm was a 35 question test but had nothing to do with class material. Would not take this prof again.

Although this was a seminar class, it felt more like a lecture class to me. You do do a lot of outside work for your group project. Readings were pointless to me. Only needed to do it for the midterm. After that, you don't need to do them. Gives good feedback. Encourages us to do our best. Brought her dog to class sometimes. Fair grader. Take her!

Don't understand why this professor has bad reviews. Class was easy and straightforward. I'd take her again if I could. Yes, all tests are essay questions, but it's not that bad and it is not hard to pass if you go to lecture. Offers extra credit on some test and gives you extra credit if you attend every lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I had her for the 5 week summer session. Doesnt pressure you to speak up in class so if youre shy like me, shes a good choice. 5 reading annotations in which you can choose which day to do them as long as you complete 5. Outside group project (not bad). Doesnt use power point slides but rather lectures. Take home final and midterm. EASY!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I recommend taking this class. She is a great professor who provokes interesting discussion which makes you think about the deeper meanings of certain actions. Her requirements are clear as well as what is expected of you to succeed. Her grading is generous and she provides comments on where you can improve. She motivates success.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She is very knowledgeable about the things she lectures about. I would take her seminar again, she does not pressure students to speak and is very understanding if something comes up where you needed to miss class. I enjoyed this class overall and I believe she helped me become a better researcher! Sometimes what she is saying is unclear.

I feel like I've learned so much about dystopia, fertility, gender roles, ecocriticism, and feminism. The reading load was doable--four novels in ten weeks--and I enjoyed the group activities and the opportunities to discuss current issues in class. Also it was really cool to gain insight on various controversial topics that are relevant today.
She makes you buy 10 books in which you will only read 1 chapter in each book and then never touch it. She ruined my gpa with her harsh grading. Avoid her.

I have went through all ten weeks of this class and I still have no idea what she talks about in lecture and on the tests. There are three midterms (cumulative} and the first isn't a lot of points, the second is more,and the third is more. The midterms are confusing. There are two essays and one is a final. The readings are confusing too. Dont take

I took this class last Spring quarter, and I recommend avoiding her. She goes off on tangents every lecture, and SOMETIMES talks about world politics. She made us buy 2 very expensive books, and we only used one. I've never fallen asleep in lecture until I took her class. I never want to take a class with her again.
Horrible professor. Talks about literally whatever she wants to talk about including the most random examples about shopping that don't explain anything.
She assigns a lot of readings but if you do all of the work, you should be fine. She gives a lot of extra credit opportunities which help your grade.
The least punctual professor I've taken at UCR. I still don't know my grade because she submitted them to the Registrar late. If you attend section you will do well.

AVOID THIS CLASS AT ALL COSTS. Her midterm and final are ridiculously hard. You have to do two essays and a literature review each week. She goes through her slides super fast in lecture. Make sure you do your reading or you're screwed, but seriously try to avoid taking her class.

I am in her honors section, and I can assure you that she is a bit confusing. She rambles on and you really have to know your theory to understand what she says. She is unclear on her assignments and such, but she replies back my email. Can't really say if I would recomm. her or not. Maybe for political science majors only. 3/5

Prof. Allison is an amazing professor. Yes, she is a feminist--get over it. She uses a feminist lens with her analysis of IPE and Env't Politics. Best class ever--show up and do the readings. It's worth it.
AVOID THIS CLASS AT ALL COST! seriously!
Terrible Professor. She goes through her slides faster than a cheetah and she rambles on and on for the entire class.

She's a really nice woman when you really get to know her. She isn't as mean as everyone says she is. When I went to her office hours, she really helped me out, even when I slept though her class. Her TAs do some work, but it's a class of 300+ people, how else are you going to control the class?

Not a very good professor, rushes through the slides on her lectures and goes on tangents. If you really pay attention though she does tend to sum up the reading. Once in a while she'll give extra credit in lecture. I got an A because I read the text, which is what the exams are based on. The extra reading is pointless. The TAs assign the papers.
worst teacher i've ever had in all my schooling career. goes through lectures like if there's no tomorrow. her tests are really tricky. she has her TAs do all the dirty work. class is a mess.

Awful prof. She makes the exams tricky. The average was 55% for the first midterm. She goes through the slides fast. She is a feminist. She is hard to approach. She bags on other peoples majors. She is awful.

Bad Prof. She goes through the slides at a really fast rate. She is hard to approach and if you do she tries to make you feel stupid. She bags on everyones majors unless your poly sci. Oh and she is a hard core feminist. Almost all her lectures are tied around how women are mistreated by men. So if you want this take her. if not.. run.
unless its your major dont take her class. tests are hard doest repsond to questions and she is a feminist
BORING CLASS, goes through slides too quickly.  Rarely attended lecture, always went to discussion. if you read, you'll do fine, but I would not recommend her as a teacher.

She goes through her slides very quick but it is all in the book. From the slides it is mainly the theorist you would want to write down because all the other stuff are in the book. Her test are hard.

She is a terrible teacher! She flew through the slides so you could barely write 2 words down. On top of that she didn't put her slides on ilearn even though you could barely write them down during lecture. The class is so boring and it made me feel like i should change my major(polisci). Then i took a better polisci class(not hers) and loved it.

Lectures: all over the place. Not really with a sense of direction. Class: boring for many, yet case studies are not so bad. Grading: hard - must analyze info, not only reiterate. Mostly essays, no multiple choice at all. Extra credit is offered. Professor: nice, but too into her own life.

Way too into herself. She has this whole, I'm a hippie thing going on. She was extremely bias to her honored students and directed her lectures towards them. Making it pointless for the rest of us to even go to lecture. Don't take her if you don't have to. Try to get a great TA if you do, they help a lot by teaching the stuff she forgets too.

She's terribly boring. She starts class with a 5 minute meditation to lull the class into silence so she can talk straight for an hour and a half. Other professors I've had were more Socratic. The environmental policy topic is cutting edge! Have some discussion in the class and the students won't be so bored.

This prof. does not really care about her students understanding of the subject... she rushes through the notes because she expects you to have read the book. Avoid taking her, well unless u like to read and learn by yourself..

Her lectures are all over the place, but I found them interesting and more informative than boring slides. You need to analyze the information and she makes you do that. Go to class, read the book, talk to her in office hours. She's REALLY great in office hours and a really great professor overall, just different from the norm.

The most self-absorbed egotistical woman. DO NOT take her. 2 papers, 2 midterms & final. Does not follow syllabus, rushes through lecs. can't copy down PPT slides. Doesnt let you take whole 1.5 hours to take exams. Doesnt care about students. I'm a poli sci major and hated her class! Shows up late to lec. LAZY has TA do all of the work AVOID if pos

Professor Allison was very informed on the subject, but her lectures were all over  the place and almost never covered the readings (which didn't realy matter because we weren't tested on them anyway). If you are really interested in the subject, it is best to learn it on your own. Fairly easy class, but not really informative.
Professor Allison is a great teacher.  Her lectures are kind of all over the place, but her case studies were interesting.  The final was pretty easy.  I would definately take her again.
Horrible. I didnt learn anything. Basically gave us the books, made us do essays that have nothing to do with lecture.  Quizzes are from the textbooks. ALL 10 of em.

Sort of all over the place.  Hers was the first college political science course I took and it really put me off the subject.  Her lectures and somewhat unnecessary and I didn't attend half of them.  Still received an 'A' though.
all she did was talk about herself, but it was pretty easy.

Really really awesome professor!!! She cares about her students and really takes time to explain things if you don't understand. She expects a lot, but only because she knows that you can do better than what you usually present.
bad, bad, bad...show up, she takes attendance. i never take notes because there really is nothing of substance to write down.  easy or not, this class is the worst.
word

One Word to describe this woman. TERRIBLE! i thought i would give her a chance and not listen to all the bad reviews from my friends, but all the "rumors" were true.  Run and keep running AWAY from this psycho.
At 8am, I wish she could be a bit more interesting and funny....but a good teacher overall

Her notes were a little unorganized, but she was very helpful in office hours. My class was a summer school class and I missed a week and still managed an A plus. For me it was hard to tie in her lecture to the essays but if you read you can do an ok job.

she was by far the worst political science teacher i have had at ucr. completely worthless. her work was pointless and did not teach me anything. if you are going to take political science classes at ucr take anything by neiman or siler. they make you work
No Comments

Lectures are loaded with interesting information, but it's hard to take it in because you're not sure how its relevant to the topic at hand, and to the overall structure of the course. Make sure you participate because she takes down names!

She is not the most class organized but if you go see her in her office she takes the time to go over anything that you want to go over. Class is only one part of school. People tend to make it the only place they utilize their professors.
No Comments
No Comments

Pretty easy as long as you write her papers and show up for class.  Make sure she NOTICES you.  I had her for International Environmental Politics.  I think as long as you speak up in class and seem like you're interested, you'll do well.
Prof. Allison was one of my favorite professors at UCR!  She really cares about the issues and inspires students to think.  Of course her class is challenging, she wants you to learn something.

I have to disagree with the negative comments - I think she is an extremely engaging professor who is interested in class participation rather than just lecturing and having everybody take notes.  It is very important to attend class regularly or else you fall behind.  She is late a lot, though.
Very nice person and very involved. Sometimes she is little disorganized however as long as you do your work you should do fine.
She is a horrible teacher, her lectures have nothing to do with what the class should be about.  I had two classes with her and they were horrible!
Not very helpful, doesn't teach much worth learning.  Occasionally just plain incorrect.  Take someone else.

Always late, uses her students as free dog walkers.  Vague, unhelpful.  Injects feminism into EVERYTHING we talk about.  we get the point.. you're a feminist.  I don't know if she  realizes that our class is on the International Political Economy or what

The worst teacher I have ever seen! Very helpfuless, always late for the class making every one in class waiting for her, takes her kid or dog to class every time. Anyway, I can not believe the university has such a professor!

You can tell how passionate he is about the subject material. His lectures are funny and engaging, the projects are creative, and the quizzes/exams are easy as long as you go to class (which you should, because he checks attendance). You can't ask for an easier, more enjoyable class to fulfill those breadth requirements.

Professor Kane shows passion for what he is teaching, makes lecture fun and interactive. There is one midterm, one final, an extra credit opportunity, and an essay. Quizzes every discussion! (very easy quizzes that the TA go over in discussion before you actually takeit

GEO 6 was changed b/c admin complained that it was too easy! 100 MCQ midterm & final, no cheat sheet! Extra credit Eaton Project (find a sci-fi story in the library's special collections) and write a summary. Weekly quizzes during discussion section, lowest grade dropped. Lots of info and quizzes/exams test on the smallest details so go to lecture.

All you need to do is listen in lecture and discussion, take really good notes, and you can come out with a great grade. I didn't study and still came out with a B. The lectures are pretty interesting and easy to follow. There are weekly quizzes, but the TAs basically give you the answers during discussion, you can drop your lowest score too.

LISTEN IN LECTURE and you'll do well; take intricate notes & study them. 1 midterm (60 mc) and final (100 mc, short faq). Really interesting and fun class! Topics are generally easy to understand. Looked forward to lecture every week. TA's are awesome and Kane is really kind. Highly recommend for science credit (coming from a non-science person)

He is the most amazing professor even at UCR, it is quite easy so attend weekly discussions to do 9 quiz, storytime essays in which you can write your own sci-fi story based on 12 narrative pathways and there are mid and final exams which are not that hard to pass so overall it is great. I really love it when he talks about Warhammer 40k and Alien.

Such a good lecturer, very interesting to listen too, makes going to lectures fun even though they are not mandatory. Only mandatory thing is the weekly quizzes during discussion, but they're very easy if u listen at all during lectures.

Professor Kane posts all the slides, so there's no problem studying for the exams. He allows a letter-page worth of notes for both of the exams. Discussion is mandatory and there is a weekly quiz, but the quizzes are easy. There is a simple project due at the end of the quarter. Easy coursework and you will most likely get an A.

Favorite professor at UCR! The class is simple, fun, and VERY interesting! He is so passionate about the subject (he created the curriculum!) and is an AMAZING lecturer. It is hard to not pay attention in class, and I was genuinely sad on the last day of class. Only weekly open note quizzes in discussion, a midterm, a final, and very short paper!

Amazing class, and rlly interesting lectures. The topics were so unique and you can tell he rlly loves sci-fi. Super fun, and we had a midterm and a final, both with a cheat sheet. Exams can be a little tricky in the way he words questions, but nothing too difficult. Also weekly quizzes in discussion, but they're open-note.

Professor was very passionate about the course material and actually made learning it enjoyable. I am by no means a STEM student but I did very well in this class and understood a lot of it. Only downside is weekly quizzes in discussion sections, but they're open note and he lets you have a cheat sheet for the midterm and final.

A great class, I actually added the teacher on rate my professor. It is a fun introductory astronomy class with a lot of fun sci-fi connection made throughout. I definitely recommend it. I loved the lectures. The class was pretty easy, it graded on a weekly quiz that is multi choice as well as a midterm and a final that is also multiple choice

considering the fact that this class is called planets in science fiction, it was really missing the science fiction portion. interesting material but very easy to get lost in class and there's hardly any text on his slides to refer to. maybe the class just wasn't for me, it was a very cool topic, but it just felt like info was getting dumped on me

Hes very enthusiastic about this class which makes lectures more fun. Each discussion includes a quiz so PAY ATTENTION during lecture. Exams are kind of lengthy, be sure to study. Overall, he was a great professor that taught the material thoroughly and simply. Provides lots of sci-fi films to watch to understand references/ connections to sci-fi.

I have never had a teacher that felt more genuinely caring for their students than Kameron Sanzo. Every piece of feedback she gave always felt so thoughtful. She displayed so much kindness and respect for her students. I wrote about my social anxiety once, and she responded back with an incredibly kind and beautiful personal message. Love her!
Professor Sanzo has been my favorite English teacher I've had in college. She's awesome, a great grader and taught me how to be a better writer.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Sanzo gives wonderful feedback on essays and strives you to do better. She really wants her students to be great writers and I agree my writing has substantially improved after taking this class.

Professor Sanzo is by far the best English professor and best professor in general I've had during my first year at UCR. She is genuinely excited about what she teaches which makes the class more enjoyable. Participate during discussions because that is when she becomes passionate and responds to your insights. Also, she responds to emails quickly

I really loved having Professor Sanzo as a teacher. She is a fair grader and accessible outside of office hours. She offers clear grading criteria and is always willing to help. Best English teacher at UCR, I would recommend taking her gain
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Kameron Sanzo is one of the best English teachers out there. She is accessible through Office Hours and Email. She will respond to any of your emails. You get to skip 3 classes, no questions asked. There is assigned readings and usually there are pop quizzes, so you should read the assigned readings. No surprises if you have read.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Inspirational--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Kameron was a really good professor. Expect daily quizzes after every reading assignment, but they were pretty simple and straight forward. The class was essay heavy, but she is a lenient and fair grader. Attend her office hours for extra help.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Very interesting class. She does lecture podcasts. So it is more like a story than a lecture. You have to write your thoughts and you can do this in anyway for the assignment like tiktok or essay. Then you have discussion which was easy. I lucked out and had a great TA. 5 project parts. Did it in ArcGIS Story Map. Very easy just put in effort.

One of the easiest classes i've taken at UCR. Her instructions are very vague bur the TA explains them, and they grade very leniently. Projects are simple just don't wait till the last minute and you'll be fine.
Too much work. Each week you have to complete a lecture reaction, and a research project every two weeks. Grade is completely based on your TA. Unclear grading criteria. Would not take again.

Just okay. A bit vague on assignment criteria, and sometimes weirdly pretentious? But class overall is not too difficult. Just research projects that require a lot of writing for an intro class, imo. She does offer some extra credit and drops some lowest scores. Not a good choice if you're looking for an easy breadth.

The assignments aren't too bad but her rubric and grading scale is kinda confusing. You're gonna be accustomed to hearing mini lectures on the 20th century and stories of her great grandmother. But overall, the class isn't terrible but the assignments can seem tedious and overwhelming during midterm season & finals week. She does give E.C. tho.
A nice professor

Terrible prof, genuinely has no idea what she's doing. If you want to have a project every other week with the most vague instructions possible, take this class. If you want to have unhelpful TAs with strict grading, take this class.

The worst research class and requirement class I've taken. I'd like to express my history as freely as hers, but you get the LOC, and that's it. If you can keep up with no answers or help, this would be for you, but it was a terrible experience on my end, even if I pass. More time was put into this class than my upper divisions; think on that.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't do it. You think it's history; it's just her rambling about her own. I prefer learning over hearing someone's romanticized war story. Both the lecturer and the TA are unhelpful, and the TA has an ego. Hope she learns instead of stressing more students out with unclear projects. I think they are graded on how they feel that day, honestly.

Fall 2025. I just want to say, the point of asking for help isn't there. While I can't say much for the professor's podcast lectures, her rubric and syllabus fail. She had students survey what the class needed improvement on, to change nothing at all. You're better off taking HIST15 or 10. Essays are better than these "research projects."
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: projects make no sense and lecture podcasts do not help nor does discussion. workload outside of projects not heavy but class can most def be run better

I don't have any complaints about Prof. Levy. She has her 2 weekly podcasts that you write on and it's not difficult. However, every two weeks there is a research project. Very unclear rubric and grading seems subjective. Rubric also changes every time so you can't get better and learn as you go.

The professor is very passionate about history and her lectures are like podcasts. But the majority of your grade is based off multiple research projects, which have an extremely unclear rubric.The TAs grade harshly and the average was a C for these projects. Definitely a time consuming class,

Pretty easy class. The entire class is just a research report about any topic world history related in the 20th that you write over the course of the quarter. These reports are separated by decades and one is due each week (summer). They also build on one another so your final report assignment is really easy. Pick a topic and ask prof if confused.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Love Levy! she really lets you do your own thing for assignments and her lectures are like podcast. Really easy class.

Very surprised I got such a high grade in this class after feeling so stressed out by it. I probably got it from extra credit and the final paper. The content of the class is interesting, but there is a Storymaps paper assignment EVERY WEEK. The instructions on the weekly assignments are very vague, and the professor sets harsh grading rules for TA

Easy online course. One short asynchronous lecture per week. Extra credit quizzes once a week. Lecture response (150-200 words) assignment given once a week. One longer assignment per week as well but never super difficult, just time consuming. Story maps is where all assignments are done - takes a little to get used to but nothing too crazy.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This was genuinely one of the best professor I have ever had! She is so kind and caring and amazing. Every week there's typically a medium sized project/ assignment due along with lecture comments. You need to put a little effort into the class, but overall very doable. I've had Levy twice and she is an amazing professor!

This class really depends on your TA. There were weekly podcast reactions which were easy. Every two weeks there was a project which was a little annoying and time consuming but that is it for this class.

I liked my experience in this class. It was creative that we get to choose our own history projects at all times. The instructor used podcasts as lecture materials which was quite fun and unique. Overall it was flexible. But I think we do have to put work to get good score! You get 9% of extra credit. My TA Hailee was so amazing, kind and helpful!

Very sweet professor. Lectures were short podcasts. Passionate about her knowledge in history and introduced us to stories of her own family history. Homework did get a little confusing and tedious at times but was never difficult. She was straightforward with deadlines. TAs were very helpful. Asynchronous no textbook no test. You will not regret

AMAZING CLASS. Don't overthink the assignments/fall behind. Just pick a topic, find 3 sources, and WRITE about it and you'll pass. Instructions are vague on purpose so don't overwork yourself. Just do something! Expect to spend 3-4 hours for each of 5 assignments. Lecture reactions just make picture notes. TAs are hilarious!! 9 zooms that are easy
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: definitely one of the easier history classes for GE especially if you can get the summer course. there are reading but it is graphic novels and she offers extra credit. assignments could be tedious and do take more effort, but as long as you follow the prompt you're guaranteed a passing grade.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: The class is fun, but be prepared to read and write. The rubric's were often confusing, but the professor responds fairly quick if you ask a question. The TA's will be the best place to alleviate any confusion, since Levy doesn't appear to grade the larger assignments. Missed an assignment worth 10% and still ended with an A+ thanks to extra credit
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: pretty easy class. even though we didnt go over the lecture in the discussion it wasnt a bad class. It was a bit boring but easy.

I took her for Hist 020. Free A, it's online. She makes history very entertaining. I just wish she went through some more events during the century. Besides some random facts, I feel like I didn't learn much outside of my final project topic. Fun class, though.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Julliette Levy is very passionate about the Long Twentieth Century. Her class is straightforward and gives a lot of extra credit, which helps. I would however avoid TA Christella Maldonado if she is a TA for your course. She graded very harsh and does not care about giving students failing grades on assignments. One of the worst TA's I have had.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Levy will probably be a good option if you don't like history. If you want to challenge yourself with new material and perspectives, it may be better to look somewhere else. It might've been my TA but I found the class to be stupidly easy. I didn't really feel like I learned much at the end tbh. On the bright side, she was accessible.
Professor Levy slays. I loved this class so much. Yes, there's a lot of reading and 3 essays and 1 final paper but they are really easy to write to. I would 100% take one of her classes again.

Levy is an awesome professor. Even though you have to read and write a lot, there's so many extra credit opportunities so it's honestly not hard to get an A, but you have to work for it. The class was entirely online with the only attendance being taken is on discussion, and there's no lectures (you listen to podcasts instead).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor, understanding and would take another class with. 10/10
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Levy is genuinely a great teacher and tries to make you view history in a completely different light. Some of the reviews here are outdated in regards to how papers are graded (previously 0,50, or 100%), as when I was taking it, each paper was graded out of a 5 column/row rubric.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor, weekly lectures are pre-recorded podcasts that you can listen to at any time. The weekly homework is just writing a commentary on the podcasts. Lots of EC, so can definitely bring up your grade a lot. Flexible with deadlines. Overall passionate professor who finds joy in her work and is a pleasure to learn from.

Professor is super kind and very understanding. Genuinely cares about students. Willing to adjust anything for students benefit and is super accessible! Lectures were done thru podcasts and are very engaging and interesting. Assignments are also interesting and extra credit as well as buffers in due dates make things so much better.

Pros: Lectures are pre-recorded podcasts (not long/interesting/enjoyable). Hw is basically replying/commenting about them. Discussionreview/attendance. EC assignmentseasy. Cons: Research papers (2-3 total) can have vague instructions (4pg/not too bad). Graphic novel readings assigned sometimes (tip:save time-look up summaries). Finalpaper

There are lecture comments every week along with EC quizzes, an essay every two weeks, and discussion is mandatory. The lectures were structured as podcasts which were nice, but the essays were a killer. You have to do a lot of research, but thankfully there is a week grace period so you can turn it in late and still get credit. The prof. was nice.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Levy is a great professor and gives very informative and engaging lectures. She does a great job of explaining how historical topics tie into today's events. However, her class is a lot of work. A lot of research papers and readings and it can be tough to keep up if you have a full course load.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --So many papers

reviews.comment: Levy is a relaxed professor. Her lectures are podcasts that you can listen to on your own time. The projects are time-consuming, but nothing difficult. There are readings assigned every week, but I did not read them and was completely fine.
Very good class. Being a workshop class I expected it to be bland but Professor Levy really made it interesting with a zombie theme for researching history. Weekly assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Never had a lazier professor, absolutely can feel how little she cares. Her grading is terrible either a 0,50, or 100% no in between cause that would require more effort to grade. She does recycled podcasts from last quarters. Got a 0% on the final cause it was "offtopic" she literally read my rough draft and green-lit it.

Professor Levy is a super chill professor who was very considerate of different learning styles as well as the current situation with covid. The lectures are relatively short podcasts and you don't have to take notes. There are a few larger assignments but if you have a good TA then they aren't graded too harshly. Definitely recommend.

I absolutely loved taking Professor Levy's class. She's very inspirational and her weekly podcasts are so enjoyable to listen to. The workload isn't too stressful but gets your brain thinking for assignments. I love how History 20 became a class more about the quality of knowledge rather than the quantity of assignments. How every class should be.

Professor Levy has officially made history way more interesting to learn. In her podcasts she makes sure to provide a well-rounded view of history in a way that allows you to draw connections - this makes the course work much easier. Just make sure to stay on top of the assignments and everything will go smoothly.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Took this class online and unfortunately did not learn much. There are no notes and about 30 minutes worth of podcasts a week that just brush over topics. The final project which was an essay was graded so you could only receive a 0%, 50%, or 100%. If you missed a little part of the prompt you would get a 50% which dropped my grade from an A to B-

I would not recommend this professor because the way the grading system is set up, if you miss 1 assignment, its worth so many points that you can't even get an A. Otherwise it would be an easy A. Things were graded as 100% 50% 0%. Getting 50 on one big assignment takes a solid 5% off your grade, getting a 0 takes off 10% FROM YOUR FINAL GRADE.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: a great professor, she's really understanding and her class is as interesting as it gets for an intro history course. if you have the chance to take her course, I recommend it.

Professor Levy was really amazing this quarter. Her class really easy, we only had to attend discussions, weekly assignments, and listen to her podcast and leave comments. Her podcasts were actually really interesting to listen to!

World History class. Grade is a few research assignments, weekly responses to the notes, and the final paper. She's a nice grader. Ton of EC, your grade goes up a full letter if you do all of it. Lectures are podcasts you listen to on your own time. Discussion is the only thing you have to show up to, assigned reading is graphic novels.

I took her online Hist99W class and its basically weekly small essays that increase in length and research time. Lectures were asynchronous and discussion was synchronous with the TA. Very understanding and accommodating to students, especially because of the pandemic. Lots of extra credit opportunities and is just over all a really nice professor
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT--So many papers

reviews.comment: Tons and tons of useless assignments

Professor Levy was able to teach history and make it relevant enough to engage college students who might have been that interested beforehand. She makes the content of the course as well as the assignments applicable to us individually. She is very accommodating to our needs and understands how to engage us in the class. Her podcasts are great too
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: There is no textbook, lecture, or final. She has 10 podcast app 20 mins each that you can listen to any time in the week. There are 2 real assignments due a week, Podcast comments and weekly decade assignment. She offers a full letter grade of extra credit 10%. Really easy class to get an A in that only requires maybe an hour of work a week.

Her online class was very enjoyable due to the structure of the class. It was organized into decades which made it easy to focus on what to write about. Extra credit was easy and helps a lot. On Piazza, she does have snarky replies but other than that the TAs are very helpful and you dont interact with Levy much unless you choose to.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: For a humanities course, I would say this class is a lot more difficult than I thought. She expects so much from you and assigns 3 FULL chapters in the textbook for you to read (weekly), which is insane. Gives weekly quizzes and some questions are pretty tricky. Her lecture videos are super short and useless. Don't recommend this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Took her online class, and it was the second one I've taken. A lot of reading is to be done an lots of "mini essays" as well. I felt the readings were a bit excessive at times but nonetheless an okay class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: weekly quizzes, podcast comments, and decade assignment(mini essays) due. She gives you freedom to choose what you want to write about for your decade assignments. The podcasts were short & enjoyable and made the online class more personal. Do the extra credit assignments, they help out A LOT. You won't regret taking this class.

This class is the most straightforward class ever. Most of the assignments literally just require you to follow directions and you'll get an A. Prof. Levy is incredible, she realizes online classes are different and changes the class as we go to tend student requests/needs. Always available and super interesting podcasts! Just follow directions!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Levy is awesome! She really cares about her students and will do whatever it takes to see them succeed. I took her class online so it was different than a normal class, but through her podcast lectures I feel as though I learned as much, if not more, than I would have in person. I highly recommend taking her class!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Gives good feedback--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Definitely more work than a regular class. Weekly decade assignments due every Sunday by 11pm. These took the most time but as long as you follow the rubric, youll get 100% on each one. Weekly quizzes with 3 attempts each & weekly podcast comments. Discussion was just the TA talking about the upcoming decade assignment & small group discussions
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: At first, I was nervous about taking this course but in the end, I enjoyed taking this class. She gives great feedback and also allows you to improve your grade by providing extra credit opportunities. Her TA's are awesome as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: At first I was skeptical about taking an online class because they can be confusing. However, I was wrong this class turned out to be pretty easy and only took minimal time away from core classes. The final is a typed paper about 2-3 pages. Overall, Professor Levy is a great professor and made history interesting. Great Breadth class for CNAS
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I really liked this professor, she used her grandmother information and life to explain the history of the 20th century. YOU NEED TO DO THE WORK ONLY TO PASS BUT TO GET AN A YOU NEED TO WORK FOR IT. She offer lots of EXTRA CREDIT.

Class is super easy. Do your work, try on essays, get an A. Work load is not that bad for a class only 3 weeks long.  Lazy people will say the class is difficult but if you answer the prompts for the essay and have all the requirements you'll get an A.

she makes you work for your grade. there is a lot of reading but I found a way around it. there are weekly quizzes and essay (short/long) assignments. if you really try, you will get an A. participation is a MUST. she also gives you tons of chances for extra credit. Carolyn is also one of the nicest TA's, she cares so much. overall, fun and easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--SO MANY PAPERS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Levy's podcasts can be a bit boring but overall, Hist020 consists of a quiz, podcast review, and a paper due every Sunday so it's very consistent so you know what to expect. It wasn't a difficult class, she did give clear grading criteria so there aren't many surprises. Extra Credit is offered throughout the course.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: You will have to write a lot for this class. Be prepared for peer reviews, DZ missions (they take a long time), and lecture comments in addition to attending discussion sections weekly and WAC workshops. On days with both discussion section is a good two hours.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Just because this is an online class doesn't mean it's easy. She assigns so much reading, it's ridiculous. She will assign at LEAST 3 full chapters to read each week, quiz you on them, and expect you to do a writing assignment on something that was remotely related to the textbook reading. Her lectures are SUPER short and not helpful at all either.

I took this class because I wouldn't have to take 1C and it's required by my major, but I think this would be easier than 1C. The entire theme of the class was about zombies and it made the class interesting and fun. The essays are different and innovative. If you can take this class I would recommend it. However this is my major so I am bias a bit

I came out of the class unclear of if I had actually learned anything. The class makes it seem like you will learn research skills, and writing skills equal to a historian's. All I learned was that Chicago citing style is a pain.  Her essay prompts are confusing, and when answering questions, either leaves one word answers, or a cryptic paragraph.

Opportunity for a full letter grade bump. She was kind, and an easy grader, and the TA's were very helpful. There was a lot of participation required, and 3 assignments a week, which as overwhelming at first. But once I got into the rhythm of the class, it really was quite easy. Project at the end was enjoyable and unique, and not that hard.

Professor Levy is amazing. There was a lot of writing, but there are writing workshops. She took a unique spin to teaching researching skills and it made it fun and interesting. The final project for the class was fun to work on and she or the T.A.'s were always available to give feedback or answer questions. She really wants students to do well.

She was a good professor, but was very vague with her description of assignments. Especially the final project, she said you can use whatever topic you want, but then when it came down to it she regulated what topic we could write about. She rambles on and on, at first it was interesting but over the quarter it became annoying.

AWESOME TEACHER!!! she demands a TON of work, she has at least 2 things due each week. but her and her TAs are very helpful, always ready to respond via email or twitter/Facebook (that's right). If you have to take a W class, take her's.

This class demands a lot of work. You have a writing assignment that is due every week, weekly quizzes on the readings. If you put in the effort and do the work this class is doable. Really enjoyed this class.

This class is a lot of work (and more than I thought was necessary) but not difficult.  As long as you understand what she expects of you and do it, you'll do well.  A lot of work but the nice thing is that there are a lot of opportunities to earn points to sort of buffer the points you didn't earn by missing some assignments.

She is my least favorite teacher. Not only did she make History99W my hardest class ever she was very unorganized. She is rude to students and very annoying. Quizes are random and based on attendance. BEWARE!!!! Less than half of my class was going to lecture by the end.

I did not attend class regularly and still got a decent grade. She podcast her lectures. Asks you to read a lot of articles but honestly you can get by without reading them. Midterm is only 4 questions what you must only pick 2 from. She gives you these questions beforehand. Final is an option, I did a video and received an A. Take her class!

Great professor! Just do the work and you'll do well. Interesting lectures that can be a little hard to follow but is always willing to answer questions. Encourages students to interpret readings and primary sources from their own perspectives. A lot of online work required. Passionate instructor, puts in a lot of time making sure students get it

The class is not an easy one. She is a very hard grader and the midterm and final have nothing to do with the lectures. She gives you an option on what you want to do for the final but all three options are the same as she grades hard. Part of your grade is participating in the online discussions.

I you really want to avoid getting a bad grade, don't take her!!! She is a really hard grader and expects a lot from you! Her lectures are really boring and she talks really fast! The midterms have nothing to do with the lectures!

Prof. Levy was great, she does talk a little fast at times, but all of her notes are posted online and doesn't seem to mind people asking questions during lectures.  She can be critical with grading, but all of her notes on essays and exams make perfect sense.

She talks way too fast, which makes her mumbles sometimes.Her midterm is extremely hard even though she gives out midterm questions one week before the test. You have to read textbook at least 3 times if you want to get good grade in her class. If ur not interested in history, dont ever take her, i kinda regret that i took her class.
Class was interesting but she talked to fast. Midterms were given before hand but were very hard graders. Class was fun but really hard graders.

you must make sure you read the text book since her midterm and final are all based on the reading and a few detils she includes in lecture. make sure you take notes and read, read, read!!!!shes very helpful, but can speak fast at times.you'll be fine if you read, but put a lot of  detail when writing the final and midterm.

you must make sure you read the text book since her midterm and final are all based on the reading and a few detils she includes in lecture. make sure you take notes and read, read, read!!!!shes very helpful, but can speak fast at times.you'll be fine if you read, but put a lot of  detail when writing the final and midterm.she expects a lot of you,
great teacher...one of the best we have here @ UCR. If u have the opportunity to take her, do it, you will not regret it.....
No Comments

she's the greatest..almost convinced me to change my history interest from the american revolutionary war to latin american studies...she's really smart and even more helpful.  Her essays could be a little easier but other than that she's awesome.
LECTURES ARE EASY TO FOLLOW AND HER SARCASM MAKES THEM INTERESTING. IF YOU MEET UP WITH HER DURING HER OFFICE HOURS AND HAVE A CHAT, YOU CAN QUICKLY BECOME HER FAVORITE
Did not like her at all.

The lady is awesome! I loved her style of teaching and all her sarcasm! Take her if you can! Be prepared to read a lot ... oh and she's a lil' tough on the grading of essays ... she demands a lot! Nonetheless, great professor! More like her are needed!

hard grader, and demanding on her essays. The class is really interesting tho, and I think she does a really good job of explaining things. But be prepare to read a lot, because she has crazy reading assignments.

i really liked her at first but then she mocked what billie ellish said at the grammys about ICE. She goes off topic a lot in lecture and talks about political things. She grades so hard and you are only graded by the essays basically. There is a few assignments but they do nothing to your grade if you do good in them.

reviews.comment: Thought provoking discussions and interesting course material. Thoroughly enjoyed this call.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Leen is a great professor and id reccomend her! reasonable deadlines and avaiable to help as needed. decently easy class
Leen is the goat. Just write the essays she gives you and stick to the prompt!!!

This professor was a very bubbly fun teacher. She gives 3 essays and 1 essay for your final. There are quizzes and 4 responses throughout the quarter. She does grade kind of hard but if you pay attention and go to class you should have no issue.

Heavy on pro-Palestine perspectives to balance U.S.-dominant pro-Israel narrative. Politically heavy, but if you're not sensitive to politics, it's an easy course. Grading is straightforward, clear rubric, and she provides helpful feedback. She's also easy to contact. The structured essay format she provides is very useful. Book & reading required.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Was very political during lectures, making it unbearable to sit through especially for an english class. I did not enjoy going to class to listen to political talk

Professor Kawas was amazing! The course was decently difficult but she always allowed you to reach out with any questions and she helped us draft our essays and expand on themes. There is a lot of reading but that's with any english course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Your lab experiece is completely dependant on your TA. Lab reports are auto-graded which can screw you over if your data is incorrect or if you didnt write down all the needed information. There is a balance  at the end of the course based off of how strict/lenient your TA graded so all is not lost.

Quizzes are difficult and super specific, especially hard with only 10min. Lab report grading criteria is so unnecessarily brutal. reviews.comment: The grading weights are atrocious. A- on the midterm, A- on the Final, A- on the Paper, full discussion points, ended up getting screwed by a single homework assignment that I forgot to do. I could have done it in class the day it was due and decided not to (honesty). Ended up being worth 4.5% of the grade! Brought my grade down to a B. Unfair IMO!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: MCS 1 is supposed to be an easy introduction class and she makes it challenging. This class should be an easy A but it is not, if you need a good professor for MCS 1 which is an intro do not take her. Also hard to understand lectures
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I am a science major and it is my fourth year in college so I've had my fair share of breadth courses. Some of her readings can be challenging to understand and her lecture slides provide little help. Even if you put time into studying, it does not indicate how you'll do on the exam. The essay is graded too harshly as well as discussion activities

She's passionate but has a strong personality. Didn't let anyone sit in the back during lectures, if no one answered her question she would go around and pick on people.  Topics were interesting, teaching style not so much.

Attendance is mandatory because she gives two pop quizzes during the term. She was pretty helpful and flexible; very willing to accommodate students. Helpful during office hours. TAs were TOP NOTCH as well. Tests were insanely easy. Subject is actually terribly interesting. I thought I'd be bored to death but now I might declare a minor. Take it!

Her teaching method is horrible. She has a thick british and indian accent and it's hard to understand what she is saying. She often rambles and diverts from her lesson plan. If werent for her TA, I would fail. Very opinionated, will say that you're wrong and crush you. who does that.. She isn't clear on what she wants on her assignments. DONT TAKE

I'll get straight to the point. I'm a 3rd year CNAS Neuro major with a 3.5 gpa. I took this as an "easy" breadth course, and it was NOT easy.. i do not recommend it. I got 96%'s on both the final and the midterm papers and ended up with a B in the class. Hope this helps.

I do not understand why people give a lot of negative feedback. She is an amazing  professor. She is very helpful if you go and visit her to office hours. The readings that she assigns are pretty interesting, and you mine as well do them since you are required to write papers. She is not difficult,  do the readings, and do your work. Easy A.

She was absent a lot. The TA did most of the teaching. When she would lecture she would ramble. It was difficult to understand her at times. She says "isn't it" a lot.  She is very opinionated so the information she expects on papers should only be her viewpoints and arguments of the articles she has you read.

Worst professor I've ever had. She consistently asks for class participation and recently started taking role. She goes into the audience and asks random people and puts the microphone in their face while demanding an answer or quick on the spot example. Consistently shows up 20 minutes late to her own class. The TA's really do all the work in here

Worst professor ever. She's often late to her own class and has her TA's teach the class. The TA's are as bad as her-- they are no help and have no interest in helping you pass the course.  The essays and readings are ridiculous.

i seriously do not even know why this person is a college teacher. she seems to treat us like high schooler and talk to to us in class. Even if you go to her office hours it does not even help. It honestly all just depends on the TA. They do all the grading anyway.

horrible. very difficult to understand her. 3 papers, 1 midterm 1 final and doesn't post slides, we hardly watch movies like we should in any MCS class. She yells at us in lecture because not enough people come, and she does pop quizzes because no one goes.. this is a breath class.. and i hate it, she told us to raise our hands if we want to leave
She's annoying and very opinionated. She cuts you off whenever she doesn't agree with you. Turns everyone in the class against men in society.

Taken 2 classes with her. Mostly complains about how students don't do the reading and don't pay attention in class. Only values her own opinion and will waste time arguing with students about things in class. Hard to understand sometimes. But mostly multiple choice tests and some short essays for grading, which is not too bad.

Khan is an extremely interesting and intelligent professor. I learned a lot of interesting material in her MCS 001 class that really changes your perspective on a lot of things. I look forward to taking more classes with her in the future.

Not a difficult class at all, really enjoyed it. Kish really cares about the topic so it made it more interesting, but you don't really need to be in class to get a good grade. It was made super clear what you need to know/do to get a good grade so very simple class in that sense.

Strap in because this professor is more inexperienced than a newborn horse. The lectures were long winded if entertaining sometimes, you won't need the textbook if he actually remembers to post his slides. The course content is interesting and engaging, as long as you keep track of dates.

Rambles on about stuff not on the tests, but he's clearly passionate about the subject. Super easy to contact, and I recommend attending his office hours for extra clarification. Attendance not mandatory, but the tests are only on the readings and terms discussed in lecture, so going to those is really helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very easy class as long as you go to lecture. Prof is nice and will help if needed.

There are weekly hw assignments that are due on the midterm and final. I barely attended lectures and still passed with an A. The tests and quizzes are just memorizing Greek terms and talking about Greek stories like Medusa. The times I did attend lectures they were kind of boring but he really cares about the topic.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Little hw, ez tests, lecture not mandatory. Seems knowledgeable HOWEVER if you actually like the subject you will not get anything out of the messy, unorganized lectures. Very disappointed as I wanted to learn the material from a professor and not just read a book

One of the most chill professors I've ever had for an upper-division course.
