His tests consist of two phases: an individual portion (85%) and a group portion (15%). You can always guarantee a higher test score if you do the second phase, plus you can work with other people and look up answers.

There are also really interesting papers he assigns!

BIOL 108 lowkey goated when allele frequencies are the vibe frfr. In all seriousness great class! Well organized, accessible, and interesting. Class involves weekly quizzes, weekly article readings, three exams (non-cumulative), and pollEVs.

Dr. Samuk was great! He does an excellent job teaching and explaining the concepts. However this class is not easy. 3 exams , 5 quizzes and discussion attendance and participation. If you put in a good amount of work in an A is possible!  Class was interesting:)

He's a good professor. I enjoyed his lectures and he had a couple of poll ev questions during each lecture to make sure you were understanding the material (and attendance). All the test material you need to know is on the slides and articles you have to read for discussion. Tests are a bit confusing though, with somewhat low averages.

Prof Samuk is rlly nice and can tell he cares about his students. Lectures were pretty interesting. Exams had several Qs that were unclear/overcomplicated/he messed up and no correct answer, and he didn't rlly understand/give extra points back for most of those. Tried to help students by giving some extra credit from ievals at the end.
he's kinda dry but his grading is chill.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I just finished taking CBNS 101 with Alex as the discussion TA. Personally think he did a great job, well versed in both the lecture material and lab material and was able to answer all questions I had. Allowed me to come to multiple different sections of lab and was overall very helpful. Class is difficult by nature, study hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: i know cbns101 is supposed to be hard but i feel like i wasted my time every day by going to this man's class (it was required). he held us to very high standards despite teaching awfully. INSANE test questions and only 19 people in the class but he knew nobody's names. he's only a phd candidate and i would not take a class of his again.

Genuinely the Lebron of TA's. Failed the final but was still able to get an A- in the class because of how helpful he is and his willingness to help on lab reports and in lab. Always very approachable and had a clear and concise answer for every question and it was evident he cared for students and their understanding of the material. Stan Max.

actual goat. tanked the final but still ended with a B because bro helped me with the labs throughout the quarter and I was able to go home and do the rest of the calculations correctly which translated to the quiz grades which he prepares you for + gives actual useful feedback. lebron of ta's.

Max is an all-around great TA. He indulges your jokes, but he also makes sure you're on track and gives good help and advice if you ask. If you're confused, he helps you step-by-step during office hours. He gives you back your graded work during the next lab period, but he puts in grades on Canvas before then.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I'm awful at chem,having max as a ta was probably the only reason I am going to pass with a C or over.When the labs were confusing, he explained to us where where went wrong and gives us the steps to get back on track, if you have any questions,he'll answer them,if you need help, he'll help you.I truly think its a miracle I ended up in his section

Good instructor in short. Designed our labs + assignments + in-class exercise carefully with lots of real data and made it fun. You will def need to work hard understanding the problems and coding. But its really worth it(grade-wise and knowledge-wise). Generous with correction points. Gives prep questions for exams. His lecture are 5-min vids tho.

Assignments are far more difficult than what is covered in his barely informative videos. Does not care about the students at all. Replied to 0 emails when sent about clarifications about assignments. Assignments are worded extremely weird. Tough on grading. Will mark points down for codes/comments on code even if it is good enough for full credit

He doesn't care about the class at all. For the lecture, he just put students into breakout rooms and askes them to watch videos that he posts on youtube. However, you still have to attend the class since he makes participation points. The deadline for the homework is weird, and there is no reminder for the deadline. Lost 50% grades for being late.
Good T.A.
He's very considerate and always accessible for office hours. He doesn't power trip as well unlike other professors, which is good
He's alright, talks a lot.
Amazing Professor
Great Professor
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Other ratings seemed pretty harsh, but he was not bad at all. I thought he taught the course well especially since this was his first time teaching it. He used Brisk syllabus for the class so expect a 60% or higher on labs, exams, and class to pass. But he was very leninent on the exams. Which I didn't take for granted. Overall he was very helpful.

He is an extremely friendly guy and easily approachable but the way the class is designed made it extremely time consuming. During lectures he would just talk for 10 minutes and expect us to do the in class exercises never really teaching. The labs are extremely difficult and take an average of 10-15 hours a week. Exams are fair however.

3 extra credit opportunities are offered, but have absurdly strict expectations that eliminate any project of easy to med complexity. It's effectively a COAS scenario; even if you have that much time, it's not worth putting in a ridiculous amount of work for the measly 15 points they offer (out of 1000 for the class). Otherwise a decent professor.

LOTS of homework so be ready. Allan is a great guy who loves his students; his lectures can be off-topic and messy, but that only adds to his charm. Final isn't too bad if you do all the review and run your understanding through Allan + the TAs (your TAs will be very important since you spend most of your time and effort on labs). Hard but doable!

Absolute worst professor at UCR. Terrible at responding to emails, incredibly boring lectures that are simply just too long and unclear, and extremely disorganized lesson plans. I would stay away from his course. Sure, it's not that hard, but I'd rather take a harder course than get him as a professor again.
Go to lecture and actually read the textbook and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Allan Knight is the GOAT. Love this man and his teaching.
W mans, he has street cred in the school. Every CS student says he's the goat. Would take him again

Super cool guy. Even boring concepts can be entertaining when he's teaching. The quizzes are on stuff you cover in lecture, and the final is super similar to the practice exam. The programming assignments and labs can be challenging, but they are definitely doable.

Took this class in Spring quarter 2023. There are definitely a lot of things to remember in the class, but he allowed us to have a cheat sheet which really helped during finals. Lectures were not boring and he emphasizes important information. Work load was not bad, but labs were a bit confusing, however TAs were really helpful and patient.

I have never taken economics, so I have no prior knowledge to economics. He would talk as if everyone has taken microeconomics and understood it well. His tests were based off of his power points but I had trouble understanding most of it. Luckily I went to the TAs office hours every week and she was able to clarify some of the material.

very difficult to reach. He had two TAs, one was out of the country during the first mid term, then the OTHER one was gone during the second mid term. No significant curves, average of mid term was 65. Would not recommend unless you have to take it.

For students who never had Econ background, the materials can be a bit difficult. Since this class is more interesting than other econ courses such as macro or micro, it is more fun to learn. While the materials can be a bit confusing at times, Professor Keith tries his best to explain them clearly. I would recommend students to record his lectures

Go to his lecture! That's all I can say. He rarely uses textbooks. He is very old fashion so make sure on the exam you mention every concept he talked about. You can't really bs your way through on the exam it 100% based on class materials

He is a really cool professor who got stuck with a boring topic to teach. His lectures are boring but he tries to make it not so painful. The exams are easy and straight from his lectures. There was a decent curve at the end.
Beware of this class if you have no prior economic knowledge. Class is incredibly dull and professor teaches as if everyone understands microeconomics before-hand.
Hoplessly dull class.  Professor is a nice and very helpful man, however, who gives generous curves.

Knapp is good at explaining concepts. People don't come to class, that's why they don't do well. He tries to explain things in a way that we can understand and he doesn't expect anyone to already know something about economics. It is an economics based class so be prepared for graphs! Easy class.

This course is very complex, but Knapp does a good job of navigating you thru it.  Most of the information he lectures on is not on the test, nor is the material covered in the book. He is moderately clear, but he has trouble explaining big concepts, and relating the big picture.

Course difficulty was difficult but not out of left field. Some topics are much harder than others, but only if you try to implement things from scratch. Lectures involve very helpful in-class coding exercises but are not technically mandatory. Klefstad also had a lot of helpful tips and stories on career development.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: If you're willing to put enough effort into learning something new and interesting about programming, you should definitely take Klefstad. His classes are hard, homework assignments are huge, but lectures are amazing + grading is explicit and fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: As a person I really like him and he's hilarious, but as a professor he is incredibly scatter-brained and disorganized. After hw 6 all the homeworks are quite difficult because the instructions are terrible and he does not prepare you well. You'll be scrambling to get them done and most likely will be lost because the TAs aren't helpful

The biggest blocker to your class will be his disorganization and him blatantly not caring about the class. Be ready for last minute changes to assignments and projects. He's is not responsive at all to emails, nor piazza, and will berate you in OH for asking stupid questions. This class is completely carried by the TA's.

Let me be clear, the class is easy but the professor makes it pretty hard. The things that were graded were Lecture attendance, Lab attendance, Lecture quizzes, Discussion quizzes, Homework quizzes, Homework and a Final exam. He does not respond to emails and not considerate of student circumstance. Office hours is the only form of communication.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Klefstad is the must take CS professor at UC Irvine. HE is the only professor that understands professional requirements and prepares you for interviews. I would not have made my first 7 figures without this class.

Maybe because this is a new class. It was not structured until half way through the quarter. It was designed for students to practice coding interviews. In the end, the interview part just gets dropped and becoming a leetcode class. Most of the class time are just quizzes on memorized algorithms and watching cat videos.
Worst experience with this guy, do not take him

Klef's 31 is not that hard. He made some adjustments on the course material, and I think these are actually necessary. You need to learn things by yourself sometimes, but since the materials are not so hard, it should be easy. You can easily get an A as long as you follow the class. You may not learn much in lectures, but you'll enjoy his jokes.

In his lectures he tells jokes and makes funny side commentary... However, he doesn't lecture on things that you actually need to know to do the homework. Instead, you spend a majority of your time googling how to do things. This class also requires a ton of time to do the assignments. Weekly homeworks, quizzes, and labs take about 20hrs/week

Doctor Klefstad is brilliant and very knowledgeable in system design. However this class is very poorly organized and extremely time consuming. Homeworks and quizes every week along with labs demand your time and attention to do well. Was taught in C for the first time this quarter and the learning curve can be daunting. Be prepared to spend time.

He dismissed questions in class, and even at times refused to cover new materials. Students are expected to grade each other's quizzes, and assignments are extremely vague and unnecessarily challenging. Avoid if at all possible, he was an extremely subpar instructor.

Way hard. Start early as possible so you don't die during the quarter. Use codewiki, yolinux, and lecture notes for example code and understanding concepts. This class can get exponentially harder or easier at any point depending on his capriciousness. Good luck.

GPA booster. Classes cannot be much easier than this one. If you take the quizzes and complete the lab assignments you will get an A. You don't even have to score high on the quizzes. If you average a D on them you still manage an A or B. If you do show up to class he is funny but boring and very helpful with understanding material.

No midterm, no final, what more could you ask for? There are quizzes though (hard quizzes!). The labs are also confusing and you sort of have to figure them out yourself sometimes. Lecture was never boring, though. He goes off topic quite a bit.

hated the class and him. if you want your quarter to be hell. you will have to spend every hour of every friday and saturday working on hw if you even want to scrape by in the class. hes the only one that teaches it so this is a warning to all.

Worst professor ever! He has a click of students that are his "followers" and the rest of his students hate him. If you are a student that already knows everything then he is for you. If you need to learn or be taught anything you are screwed. All of his knowledge is off google, he doesn't know anything. His assignments and quiz specs are  unclear.

Funny guy and lively lecturer. Knowledgeable in CS, tells a lot of funny stories about his life. Not the most prepared professor I've had. You'll eventually get tired of the briefness of his assignment specs, but it's not that big of a deal. You will probably enjoy your quarter spent in his class.
HILARIOUS. I had this class at 8 am in the morning and was able to stay awake the entire time...did not bore me.  Unclear about assignments but the guy is awesome.
Easiest Class Ever!!!! Labs were about 60% of your grade wich were very easy. No Midterm or Final. Just easy weekly quizes. Very funny and very cool teacher. Easy A+ class.
HE IS REALLY FUNNY AND NICE. HE GETS DISTRACTED EASILY
BEST professor hands down. Makes the class interesting, isn't boring, relatable to students.  He makes me stay awake during 8am lectures...LOVE HIM
Really good teacher, made a hard class a lot easier than it could have been.  talked randomly about non CS related things, but he was efficient with the time he spent teaching, so it ended up ok

What a refreshing professor! Has a good sense of humor but can ramble at times. Ask him a question to get him back on track. If you honestly attempt to learn, dig deeper, and pay attention to the course material, you should get an A grade.

First impression of this guy was he should be doing stand up comedy lol.  Then he become a professor. let us watch south park and youtube videos periodically during the course =).  All in All study for his weeky quizes, and just show up to disc. = easy A. Good prof. good slides. good easy course.  Make sure you pick a good TA.  (muhamid or w.e A+)

Dr. Klefstad is extremely knowledgeable and if you take the class seriously and put effort into understanding the material it's cake. However if you don't dig deeper you'll quickly realize you didn't ask questions when you should have and you'll end up dropping the class.
He's the best professor on campus! Haha! He did it all! But I'm the computer nerd so I was just there to chit chat all day haha!

Nice. Funny. Down to earth professor. Easy lecture, not mandatory but enjoyable. Easy class. Quizzes, no final or midterm, and two big projects. Do your BEST on the projects&LABS and youll pass Everything averages. LABS & PROJECTS R MORE POINTS THAN THE QUIZZES. I GOT A 58% average on quizzes, and a 100 on each project 100 LABS and an 82% overall.
I only had this guy for an intro class, hope to have him again. I just need to say this guy is so weird and enthusiastic. He loves to ramble, haha.

I'm not quite sure how you could ever hate this guy, he's hilarious. Always so excited, like a little kid or something. Really easy class although the labs can be frustrating, but if you go to Klefstad for help he'll basically do it for you. Answer questions in class and he'll love you.

This teacher is good, clear, and genuinely cares about his students. the student who complained about him talking about his personal life didn't realize that the teacher did that to reward kids who attended. he also said that graduate students where the ones who told him that UCR was second rate. you get out of this class exactly what you put in.

Good prof, really likes to teach, he exploded in class once but it was reasonable.He apologized. Not a bad teacher, just wants students to go to class. Easy class to get a B in if you go to class. No need to buy a book. Overall good, rewards good students that go to class. Very interesting guy. Would take again=)

Terrible professor! Tries to impart his personal views on his class. Quizzes covered mostly personal questions about his life and his wife. I did not learn anything from his class. Told the class that UCR is a second rate school. He should go back to Irvine, which he says is the best.

The most lively professor that I've had so far.  He's a very interesting and well-qualified professor (knows his stuff), however, sometimes he rushes his lectures, making it difficult to grasp certain concepts, so you have to ask a lot of questions, either in class or in office hours.  This class is not a piece of cake, it requires A LOT of work

Great professor, approachable and wants to help you learn to material. He really knows his stuff. However, in lecture he can go on for half the class time talking about his life stories. New at UCR but already making a name for himself in the CS dept. Sometimes condescending ("You're not thinking!") but nice guy overall.

All you need to do is show up to lectures/discussions for attendance and write 3 papers + a final paper. No homework other than reading (you can just skim the readings for quotes for your essays) Lectures are slow but it is what it is. Go to office hours to improve your essays. Pretty light class

Professor Kotz was pretty decent. She seemed extremely scatter brained, but overall excited to teach. We only had weekly postings (that stopped after week 4 because she stopped posting), and two essays. Overall, solid professor. Interesting class.
The only reason to go to class it because of attendance. There were 4 papers and one was a group paper. Show up and do the essays and you'll get a A.
Gave the guidelines for a ten page essay the day before it was due.

Dr. Kohli is AMAZING. 10/10 recommend. This class really makes you think about whether policies are for the best or if they are the status quo. Definitely a better future educator after this class. Go the her office hours! She is awesome.

GRAD CLASS
Lecture slides had a lot of information but she didn't share them, powered through them, assuming students got all of the same things out of the readings. 3-5 reading/week. 1 group presentation. Kohli is very knowledgeable. Encourages discussion among peers. Not many assignments, partnered paper for master students, indv. for PhD's.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed taking professor Kohli, I wish she was teaching more classes this quater. But her grading criteria is very clear, and although group projects and assignments are graded through the TA she still manages to learn names and class, forming relationships. Amazing professor!

Professor Kohli is a wonderful professor who truly cares for her students. She does a lot of discussions and provides a safe space for her students. She brings in real life examples and education leaders to talk to her students. There is one group project and weekly reflections that are only 2 pages long for weekly article readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: He was good at discussing a dense topic, and all his lecture material was thorough. Quizzes were online and open note, so you can't really mess those up. The exams were in person, and make sure you pay attention to what he says about the graphs in his lectures, as that makes up most of the short answers on exams.

Professor Kono is funny and straight forward. Participate and pay attention to his lectures and you will do fine in his class. The test is a bit difficult, but he gives you all the resources you need so just enjoy his class and pay attention. He makes himself available for those who need clarification and help. this Professor cares about students.

Pay attention in class and you will do great! All of the expectations are very clear. Kono's lectures are content heavy and he speaks slowly, so patience is key. But he is very knowledgeable and the class content is interesting.

Prof Kono is one of the best profs I've had at this university. Lectures are super engaging + relevant as involved current/recent events too. Exam-heavy as 20% of the grade was quizzes and 80% was exams. But if you go to lecture and try to understand, you will be fine. He also cares about his students passing and curves/drops the lowest quiz.
Mr. Kono is an easy professor hes very lenient on class hw and the lectures and very to the point. Tells funny jokes and is very encouraging. Would take him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I took this class for the Winter session and he was amazing. I wasn't sure I was going to like this class but I ended up learning a lot. He helped us in everything and if we ever had any questions he was always there for us. He's truly a great teacher! I recommend him highly.

Prof. Kono makes government easy to understand. He lectures straight off the book, he simplifies the reading clearly. Homework is self explanatory and the instructions posted for it is always clear. All in all good teacher, he doesn't bore you to death, entertaining yet gets the point across for each section.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: POSC 005W: I am a few years late writing this review. This shows that I remembered him even after a few years from taking him. Danny is passionate. When it comes to writing, he makes you the best. Not an easy A, but he will give an A for effort. Very understandable. Not sure if you need a textbook (I never use them).

One of, if not the best teacher I had at UCR. You have to read and participate, but it's interesting and fun. Danny is very respectful to other peoples' views. His lectures are fun and he's got a sense of humor. The syllabus is laid out clearly and he is a fair grader. I thoroughly enjoyed his class and teaching style. Thanks Danny!
Professor Kono is very passionate about his subject and makes the very dry material interesting. He is personable and engaging and makes a sincere effort to connect with his students.
I wouldn't say this is an EASY class, but it was definitely straight forward. Professor was hilarious and made the class enjoyable. Favorite polysci class by far.
Danny Kono is the homie.

AWESOME!!! I had him as a TA and I have no DOUBT he will make for an outstanding professor! He is passionate, he puts things in prospectice successfully, and is a fair grader. I attended his office hours often, and constantly spoke up in class. He makes himself available, so get the help and ask questions! Till go a long way!
Amazing TA! Great person!
Makes political science less dry and boring
Really fun, kept class interesting. Good explanations.

He is an amazing TAProfessor. He made class easy to pay attention and interesting. He is very accommodating to students and easily approachable. He likes participation but with his personality he makes it easy for you to chime in and have a class discussion. One of my favorite classes I have took at UCR even if the subject was very bland.

Kono is the way to go. I have literally never enjoyed a class where I had to work for an A. Professors tend to have their fair share of arrogance. Not Kono, he's worked hard and managed to still be down to earth. Take his class at all costs. He's funny, contemporary, and a breath of fresh air.
I normally don't rate professors, but he is hands down my favorite teacher at UCR. :)
Very approachable . Helps the students out !easy to talk to

Danny is a really nice guy, but his discussions are usually 20% on topic and 80%  tangents after tangents, entertaining tangents but usually off topic. I didn't find discussion helpful, but I went because of attendance. Office hours are more helpful, so do take advantage of that if you have his class.
Great TA!

Love him! He is the greatest. Wonderful TA and person. I really look up to him - he helped me so much when he was my TA, he's amazing. Not an "easy A" necessarily, but super willing to help you in any way he can. If you put in the effort and do your part, he will do his. Amazing TA. Amazing person. Definitely one of my faves. Hands down.

Amazing TA. Amazing person. Danny is wonderful. He helped me so much. I'm so glad to know him. He's absolutely wonderful and I've known him for a little over 2 years now & still talk to himhang with him. He is amazing!

Danny has such an approachable manner that at times can throw off the average person but overall, if you show him that you have an eagerness to learn, he'll do what he can to help you be successful in the class. Basically how up to classes and participate. I recommend to have this guy period, he is an AMAZING T.A! One of the best without question.

Danny was a great TA! He makes himself very approachable so it's easy to attend office hours and ask questions. He cares about your grade so if you're not happy with what you are given on a paper or exam he is open to discussing it with you. He is also funny and good looking which makes actually going to discussion a lot more enjoyable.
He was a great T.A.. I enjoyed his humor very much. His style is different yet I really appreciated his approach to help us understand the text.

Danny was such a GREAT discussion teacher!! If it wasn't for him I would have probably dropped the class or just stopped even going! He always came up with personal or life examples to relate what we were discussing to. He was my favorite part of this class! I hope to have him again as a TA! If you have him consider yourself lucky!!! :) :)

Danny was a great TA who actually taught us the material in plain english. I would highly recommend him to anyone if he is available for whatever political science class they are taking. I chose him specifically because of the reviews he had on here and they were right on. He's a pretty "dope" guy.
Danny was an awesome T.A. He was very informative and down to earth. He was easy to talk to and a fair grader. I Couldn't of asked for a better T.A my first quarter at UCR.

Danny is such a great T.A. He is very intelligent, easy going,a pretty easy grader and is freaking hilarious. He makes going to discussion section very enjoyable. I am going to miss having him as a T.A. Also he's quite the looker so thats not bad :]  "Ducks fly together!" He may actually be the best T.A I've ever had!
Danny is the best TA I have ever had. Hes very intelligent and funny! He teaches in a way that even the most complex ideology is easy to understand. He makes section enjoyable.

Danny is an amazing TA and you would be so lucky to get him and to get to know him. He is so intelligent, insightful, knowledgable, and so funny! I can't explain how much I am going to miss being his student. He made the course so much more interesting and he really helps you to better comprehend the fairly difficult readings. He's the best!

Danny makes complicated materials presented in lecture or the readings really easy to understand. He really understands the complexities of political theory and he explains it in a clear, concise, yet comprehensive manner that actually makes sense. He's really approachable and an awesome person, you'd be lucky to get him!!

Danny is so intelligent and funny! He is my favorite TA at UCR! He is very accessible with office hours; I highly recommend going to talk to him. He has been known to be a tough grader but I received an A on the essays and the exams. He is simply the best! Do the work and you will succeed! That goes for college in general.

Professor Neville is an exceptional teacher. You can tell he actually wants to be in that lecture hall. The lectures, though long, he manages to make very engaging. Even at 9:30 in the morning, his demeanor is energetic and warm. 10/10 would recommend. I would want to take another class with him
Professor is way too hot—like, distractingly hot. Also, UCR is not good enough for him , he's so smart he deserves much more

Professor Neville was clearly passionate about what he was teaching. He did get a little boring from time to time. Attendance was just signing in. Only 5 things in grade book; attendance, paper1, paper2, midterm, and final. Memorize those slide ID's, that saved me! Don't need to do the additional readings, will never be brought up. GO TO LECTURE!

If you skip you won't pass. Too much info. Just memorize the slides, and keep in mind the terms for buildings. Memorize the ones he repeats in lectures, might be on midterm and final. Study ahead. 2 papers, are not that difficult, TAs are good, so pay attention to what they want on papers. Look for a study buddy if you feel you need extra help.

You don't need to read the readings that are assigned but definitely memorize the slide IDs he shows early on in the quarter because they seem like something you can put off but the grading for them is specific so all that info cannot be memorized the night before. The class overall is interesting and he seems to be a rather cheerful professor.

I personally really liked this professor but students are only graded on midterm, final, and paper There wore many ID's to memorize (80ish for final and midterm), I think overall grades would have sky rocketed if students were quized each week on IDs and readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the worst professors I've ever had in my life. I've made an account to tell you how terrible this professor is. An absolute pathetic waste of time. A sorry excuse to be called a "professor." I promise you; you do NOT want to take this class, no matter what. Trust me, this class will stress you out to the core. Don't TAKE IT

I don't know who taught him how to teach but I give him the lowest score possible. Mumbling the lecture and then expecting you to be a genius who will remember every word that comes out of his mouth, every date, and read a ton of material like you don't have a life. But when you ask him a question related to the subject his answer is I DON'T KNOW.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Neville was great! Took this class for elective credits so I'm in no way an Art History major. Class consisted of 1 midterm, 1 paper, and 1 final. I wish he had weekly quizzes on the ID Slides because I thought that would have helped. Also, READ the material. He's really helpful in office hours.

I would not recommend taking this professor or class if it is not your major. This class was super hard because of the tests, no study guides and there is too much to study for that is not on the test. Goodluck.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This is one of the hardest classes I have ever taken and it was an elective for me. I regret taking it because you need to know 90+ images for the midterm and final, only to be tested on 10 of them. He assigns way too many readings as if this was the only class I was taking the whole quarter. Do not take him, this class is ridiculous.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Hes amazing!! honestly really good and he even inspired me (and convinced me lol) to make art history one of my majors and hes kind and intelligent and it was actually the best class i had this past quarter
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: The only downside of the lectures is that in order to hear everything clearly you must sit in the front because he doesn't use a microphone and can sometimes mumble. But overall great professor. Lots of memorization but overall interesting subjects.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I'm a transfer student and out of all the Art History professors that I have had, he has to be my favorite. His lectures are interesting and straight to the point. He honestly cares for his students and encourages people to ask him questions. He has a lot of patience and is just a really likable guy. There is a lot of memorization and readings!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: His lectures are very long and not the most intriguing. The midterm was very difficult, you need to start studying AT LEAST two weeks in advanced.

Prof. Neville is a very well traveled and is obviously dedicated to his subject. The class is straightforward: 1 midterm, 1 paper, 1 final with weekly readings to keep up with. Do NOT skip the readings there is always a question on the midterm and final regarding one reading, he doesn't say which it will be. He is not an extremely strict grader.

This class is basically all memorization. You're expected to memorize artist, title, year, and location for 90+ paintings but are only tested on about 10 each midterm. The TA's are helpful. No book needed. He's passionate about the subject so lectures are interesting and overall the class is not too bad if you study. He's also easy on the eyes

This class was probably the hardest class I have taken at UCR. His exams are ridiculously difficult. Be prepared to memorize 90+ paintings' name, date, location painted, and artist for each exam. It's a midterm, final, and a paper. You also have to visit the California Photography Museum. Don't take this class if you are not an Art History major.
The class is way too hard. The tests are vigorous and memorizing is unnecessary. Would be much better to memorize only an artist instead of four categories. Tests should be multiple choice.

Be ready to be bombarded with a lot of information. Skip the study sessions because you and your classmates can spend the entire hour asking the wrong questions. If you have a question go to his office hours. Many test questions come from the assigned readings.

Kind of annoying, and he does this thing when he walks on stage where he like, clicks his heels, and it's very distracting. Overall a good prof, but he could have been better. Interesting class, but a little pretentious sometimes.

Great speaker, clear and able to answer questions. Positive attitude. You do have to memorize 70 images but flash cards will help. Essay question based on overall understanding and one short essay answer from the readings. The readings will help with understanding other essay questions too

This class can be really easy if you are really good at memorization. 70+ pictures per test to memorize but he will only test you on 10 of them (author, name,city, year). Very fair exams i could say and the essays are not that bad either. One of the best speakers i have ever had so far at this school.

Dr. Neville is an amazing guy. The course is difficult, probably because I'm a Freshman and this is upper division. Readings are a lot and you have to go to class in order to do well on the tests. You have to memorize all the images to do well on the tests as well. He's really helpful if you're in need of help. He's really good looking too. :)

Amazing professor. Attending lecture is actually fun, maybe not so much discussion, but just know all the paintings and that's pretty much it. Set aside a good hour to two to memorize for the midterm and final though. You do NOT need the book, all required readings are online. I never used the book and still got an A- in the class.

His class is quite rigorous, lots of slides/readings/note taking. His exams are very thorough covering all materials shown/spoken in class. Very helpful professor. You do have to earn the A in his class, because its not easy as it seems.
simply the best!
really good class! guy knows what he is talking about. lot of slides to remember for tests, but managable. easy on the eyes as well. great class especially if an ahs major.

Prof. Neville has high expectations so if you're a slacker you won't like him. There are a lot of slides to learn and fairly complex readings that he does test on. He's an awesome teacher who is more than willing to go the extra mile for serious students who want to learn.

Prof. Neville is great. He really makes you interested in what you are learning and he grade really fairly. He all around enjoys teaching. He makes jokes with the students and helps whenever you need it. Highly recommended but you have to be interested or your gonna hate it.

Neville's lectures are not clear. He reads you the "lectures" from pointless essays he brings in class. The tone of his voice is boring, he covers the material boring. No study guide and nothing is covered in textbook. If you want to pass, go fetch by researching a~z all on your own. Tons of memorizing to do. Bad grader.

Tests can be difficult, and there are a lot more slides to memorize than in the average art history class. everything is really manageable though, and you have to be really stupid and miss a lot of lectures to get a bad grade.  I would take him again.

neville is one of the better art history professors in the department.  he's really chill and down to earth on a 1 to 1 level, which comes as a surprise because he has somewhat formal mannerisms and speech in lecture.  the class is really interesting, and the grading is fair.  highly recommended.
He is a really awesome professor and makes lecture really interesting. And he even tells gook jokes. He also has a really nice voice like professional voiceovers.
Great teacher who knows what he is teaching and actually enjoys it...

He's horrible..first when you ask a question he looks at you like youre crazy and will completely avoid a direct answer. Secondly he straight up just throws the information at you and expects you to know every detail behind any image. Thirdly, you have a written exercise to do, yet, none of the paired images are covered in class. 4 no study guides

Professor Neville is awesome!  He really knows his stuff.  He grades fairly (always gives you the benefit of the doubt).  His tests are also somewhat easy compared to other Art History classes, just make sure you do all of the reading because there are always questions on the reading.
Very nice person, he tests and grades very fairly. Be prepared to do the assigned reading.
Good class, nice professor.

I scored 37/40 on midterm and 43/58 on final I got full credit on attendance and I got a B-, he takes his class way too seriously maybe because he's the dean of the SOB or whatever but I truly did not study for more than an hour for both tests combined, the material is easy although his ABC scale is trash, in any other class I would have had an A

Study after every lecture guarantees you an A. Attendance is mandatory, lectures recorded. No hw. Grade depends on 2 noncumulative exams + 1page Google writeup which takes a few minutes. Professor encourages participation/questions and respects everyone's opinions. People are just mad because they don't study/go to lecture and they end up failing.

Never miss exam day. I had COVID the day of the exam and had to take the makeup midterm. But instead of a multiple choice test, I got a short answer question test. I got the worst score in the class. I thought this was completely unfair since your entire grade is based on 2 exams. I had no control of getting COVID and this professor does not care.

The biggest issue I had with this class was that our grades were based off one group project. This meant that if you ended up joining a group with subpar classmates you were essentially screwed. Originally, he planned to have 3 exams but changed it to due to COVID so my review might not be valid in the future. Material was interesting though.

I'm personally not interested in consumer research, but this class was overall extremely helpful. Having to read research papers helped improved my writing and understanding of how to read research papers. He is very approachable, easy to understand, and makes his lectures fun. The presentations were easily graded and participation really matters.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I took him for an honors seminar I had for Irrational Consumption. You need to participate in class. The class also has a lot of reading research papers, discussion, and presentations. Even though the class had a lot of work, I didn't mind because the subjects we went over were really interesting. He is very kind and cares about his students.

He is funny and sarcastic. He engages the class and uses examples students are interested in to teach the material. He is thorough and respected. If you're a bad tester, then you're doomed. No group projects. He values participation and goes over tests so you learn what you did wrong which is very helpful in learning. I liked this prof.

I took Prof. Kramer's class for about 2 weeks. I dropped it because spots opened up for a core major class and Marketing wasn't my major. However, the two weeks spent in this class I was mesmerized. Very fascinating stuff, it's almost like a magician showing how a magic was done. I would definitely love to attend his lectures if I was allowed to.

Professor Kramer is an excellent professor with deep knowledge and experience of what he teaches. His lectures include several examples related to things we see happening today in marketing which is something I really liked. I didnt like that the only way to make points in this class is on the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Would take again

reviews.comment: Hands down the best business professor I have had at UCR. His lectures are very clear and the material is well explained. He gives a review session prior the exams and they extremely useful. As long as you understand the material, you are fine. Exams were MC and each question was a 1% of your grade. Make sure you understand concepts!!! No Homework.

The material is easy to understand but your whole grade is based off of 2 test each 30% and the final is 40% he doesn't cure the class and to get an A you can only miss 5 points and the class is out of 100pts !!!

Stu is super charismatic, intelligent, and cares a lot about his students. Also, he wrote the land before time. His anecdotes and advice about the industry are worth a lot. I can’t wait to take more classes with him!

We had amazing guests during our class meetings... that was the only positive of this class. Stu Krieger is a very accomplished man but he lacks compassion. Our ta graded all our previous assignments but at the end Krieger decided to grade our final paper. Went from having an A all quarter to going down to a C, such bs!

Prof. Krieger seems to care, but he basically repeats his comments over and over until your write your screenplay the way he wants you to write it. Which is how he would write it, for kids...It was an very annoying experience being micro managed every week. If you don't have a mind of your own, you'll love his class.

Fantastic professor. strict on writing deadlines but gives excellent suggestions during workshops. Gentle hand guiding the stumbling writer. He has a lot of professional experience and he passes on his knowledge willingly.
He's very nice and is very accessible.
Rudi is a great TA and made this class a lot better since the instructor was horrible. He offers great feedback and was always available when I needed help.

Rudi was a really good grad student for this English class. He is really into sci fi and zombies, which made the class even more interesting and engaging. Tough papers because he expects a lot out of the papers. But if you go to office hours, he is very helpful and gives great feedback. Really great and nice guy overall. Would take a class again.

Super awesome guy, loves English and is there to help, go to his office hours it will make a major difference. Almost impossible to get an A unless you're Shakespeare. You wont fail but forget about that A. He loves sci fi so keep that in mind. If you try you will learn alot from him.
Overall not too difficult class ,was not a fan of his no device policy

Great professor for Public Policy. Some might've found his zero tolerance for electronics policy annoying but super helpful cause all you can do is listen to lecture. Is a very clear, straightfoward guy in lecture and exams. Lots of reading but wasn't bad. TAs were great, overall would totally take again. 2 exams + final.

I thoroughly enjoyed this class. Prof. Schwabe has been one of the best professors so far. He is passionate about the topic, and I appreciated the phone restrictions and the zero-tolerance cheating policies he had in place. If you did the work (attend lectures & take notes) the exams were easy. I would gladly take this class again.

3 midterms and 1 final will drop your lowest midterm, quizzes during discussion sections. Lecture heavy, has pollev for attendance and expects you to take notes. The exams weren't hard, a lot of the questions were common sense and the cumulative final was just the same questions as the exams. He was strict about phone usage during class.

I really loved this professor and class! (I am very passionate about policy though).The professor is highly respected among policy experts and students.He definitely shows that he generally cares about his students and being fair. My only criticism is that he is too strict on phone use during lectures. All tests are MC and you can drop 1/3 midterms

This isn't the worst class but I wouldn't take it again. 3 midterms(20%), final (30%), and participation. He's super strict about attendance, cheating, and phone usage. Lectures were interesting and fun in the beginning but got more boring as the quarter went on. Don't recommend if you're not interested in public policy.

He is an awesome professor, although this class can be quite difficult due to the economic graph concepts. There are 6 short quizzes, 3 problem-set assignments, and 1 final exam. Also, he is really quite strict on phone usage unless you ask him, but overall, he is funny, interactive with the students, and willing to help them succeed in the course

Amazing professor! It was a graduate course and he was super helpful. The course was on climate change- science, economics and policy and truly speaking I understood clearly the economics part of it after taking his class. He is always caring, and the class is not boring at all. Had real fun and I wish I could take his course again.
Love his econ joke of the week. Everything was crystal clear. Kept classroom to a professional level. Good professor.

Prof. Schwabe will come off as a very stern and strict professor (which he is), but he is fair, and knowledgeable.  He uses terms that one may go more in depth in a traditional macro/micro class, so that might be a bit confusing, but overall the class is reasonable, and his grading is fair.  If you're reading this Dr. Schwabe, you're awesome!
He is really willing to help and a great professor!
He is a very good professor and he wants the students to understand what he's teaching.  There is homework once a week.  If you really study the material and ask questions then you should do fine.

I really like this class. He's always trying to review the materials we have learned, It will make you much easier to understand. All you need to do is go over the print-outs and homeworks. His discussion class is a little annoying cause you need to turn in the summary every class. He's good-looking, funny and friendly.
Easy class since it's only 2 units. Assigns some homework but not too bad. The only thing you really need to do is the 10 min presentation. Very nice teacher.

This was my second time taking this professor and she continued to be amazing! She doesn't put much information on her slides at all so showing up and listening to lectures are very important. Her lectures are like showing up to hear your grandma tell a story through the course content and its really relaxing.
Very straight forward class, just go to lecture and discussion and take notes. TA is there to help you so ask questions if confused

pretty easy class, she talks really low during lectures so sit in the front! attendance isn't mandatory, TA was really nice. lots of reading, i honestly wouldn't take this class again tho bc i just couldn't learn from the way she teaches but that's okay! she is really nice tho and midterm was just a written essay
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Kugel is a sweet and caring professor, that I look forward to taking again next quarter. She works closely with the TA and has interesting lectures. The midterm and final are like AP tests in high school, but only the writing portions. Though lecture attendance isn't mandatory ( go since they are really interesting), discussion is.

This was one of my favorite courses at UCR. Dr. Kugel is very passionate and engaging with the material. Grade is based upon a midterm, final, discussion attendance, and two 4-page essays. You can get away with not going to lecture, but you have to do the reading; same goes vice-versa.

Class was made up of 3 one pagers a midterm and a final, both of which had two essays. Professor is very invested in the subject and makes the content easy to understand. Prof yaps for 2 hour class with slides that have almost no information, so get ready to listen. Online readings can be long and boring. As an essay grader she can be opinionated.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Kugel is a nice and caring prof. Class consisted of 2 papers 1 midterm 1 final. It was relatively easy, everything important is talked about in the discussions or class readings. The readings are very important to the class as all the work and exams come from it. Not too many either. Easy grading and lenient. Attended close to 0 lectures but got B.

Dr. Kugel is one of the few instructors that allowed me to excel the way that is comfortable for me and at the same time encouraged me to go beyond my comfort zone in writing discipline. I would recommend her classes.

Great class, you learn a lot. If you go to class (or watch the recordings) then you'll be fine. All you have to do is skim the readings and you'll get an A. Teacher is available and is very interested in the topic. Would recommend!

As a mentally and psychiatrically disabled student, I found the immense levels of support and flexibility highly helpful. She is by far one of the most accessible and carrying professors I have ever had. As long as you reach out to her she will do her absolute best to help you.

Absolutely loved this class! Exams are straightforward but VERY lecture heavy. If you skip class make sure to get caught up on what you missed. Her lectures are not visual, at all. She literally just talks freely w/out a powerpoint or any sort of visual and although this wasn't a problem for me, it might be for some. Passionate lecturer though!

Professor Kugel was a very enthusiastic professor. You cannot miss her lectures or else you will fail the midterm and final, since that's what its basically based on. Its a lot of notes, so i would recommend a laptop if you can't write fast.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: If you want to pass, she is very lecture heavy. Sometimes it can get a bit hard to memorize the information and your eyes will glaze over (trust me, I've gone there). You can tell she is very genuine when teaching the course. The TA was a tough grader but if you need to clarify any topics you missed they're glad to help. The readings are helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very informative, sometimes she talks about trivial details and interesting. Never was bored because I was interested in Native American History. Readings are interesting and must be done. Some of the readings are dense but my TA really went through the material well. Attendance required. Recommend her. PS Don't pack up early, she will lash out lol

She is a great professor who is willing to help you and clarify any questions. She is very approachable and friendly. You will be reading about an article or two per week, but they are not very long. She gives many examples that make it easy to remember the information. The papers are short. She values the understanding of important not memorizing.

Professor Kugel does give long lectures, and unless you go to the lectures you won't know what she's talking about. If you need clarification on something just ask, and the TA they are both very enthusiastic to help you! It's a college course and they teach it that way. Overall I loved it, and the Native American perspective on our nation's history

She rambles a lot and gives out a lot of info. Im surprised i got a B+ but the TA's graded pretty tough. I personally wouldnt ask her for help because theres the TA's but ive spoken to her and she seems nice. GO TO LECTURE TAKE NOTES

Lectures don't involve any visuals. She just puts up words and talks as if you should know what she is lecturing about. Does a terrible job of preparing students for exams. No study guides or hints of what's going to be on the exams. Very tough grader. Tends to go off-topic during lectures. Very hard to follow her lectures. Do not take her...ever!

She enjoys her job. Lecture is hard to discern important parts. Often, she will just talk about something and waste like 20 minutes since it won't appear on the test or be only kind of relevant. The TAs grade even more harshly than an English class. Not an easy class, don't take unless you are good at writing papers. 2 papers + midterm + final.

Prof. Kugel seems nice but when I approached her, she was of little help. I asked her to look at a rough draft of my paper and she refused. Unhelpful. When I went to her office hours she was very distracted/rude and asked her grad student to get her coffee which reflects her personality: demanding. The class was an easy A, but I learned little.
She is the sweetest teacher! She is understanding and fairly easy as long as you participate!

Kugel had an interesting personality, but if you don't pay attention there's no way that you'll pass since none of the lectures are posted online. Other than that I wasn't interested at first, but now I think the class was worth taking.
She is a wonderful professor!! Native Pride!!
Great Teacher!!!!!

Professor Kugel is a nice lady but much too unorganized in her lectures. simply writes little key concepts on board and lectures the whole period with no power points or any kind of visuals. Definitely not an easy class!
Just awful, don't bother with this lady.

Kugel is a great instructor, who always gave positive feedback and encouraged good discussion. I do agree that the class might have been a bit unorganized for the midterm, but that's why you come to class and take good notes. She even tells you specifically what terms were important so you can only blame yourself if you screwed up. Recommended!
Excellent teacher. She really makes students interested in the content. Her tests/papers are pretty straightforward: if you take good notes and attend lecture, you will get an A.

Oh geez. People who complain about her obviously didn't STUDY for the midterm. She told us exactly which article the essay question would come from. So stop complaining, get off your butt, and do the work. She is an excellent professor, very clear with what she expects. I would reccomend Professor Kugel to anyone! Take her, and you won't regret it.

Prof Kugel is a very interesting teacher. She clearly loves what she teaches and while it may be a little challenging to follow her lectures (due to her wandering off topic) as long as you take down what notes you can, you will do fine. She grades VERY easily on papers and exams.

useles teacher, her midterm is based on little lectures and one article. Her lectures arent too bad a little unorganized. She seems easy at first then when you take your midterm and every1 does bad she doesnt realize that if all do bad it is her fault. DO NOT TAKE HER IF YOU WANT AN A

I'm in her History 35 class and I'm not enjoying it at all. There is no textbook so everything is based of her lectures, which are unorganized and all over the place. I feel like she expects us to know about Natives already even though most of us don't. I DO NOT recommend this class to anyone.

Professor Kugel is very passionate about Native Americans therefore she knows alot. She makes it easy to learn & her class consits of two 5pg papers as well as the midterm and the final. She is helpful, but can be a hard grader with her papers.

Monte is one of the history dept.'s greatest assets.  She is even keeled, warm, and knows how to facilitate discussion.  I took both her senior seminar and grad seminar in Native American History.  If you are worried about class discussion and critical reading, take her classes and learn how to do it in a constructive environment.  She is very giving of her time and genuinely wants students to find their academic niche.  Plus, she rocks.

Monte is the greatest. I had her for a graduate materials course. The format made a usually excruciating discussion class interesting and bearable.  She's also very helpful and offers tips to grad students on how to write your C.V,submit articles to journals, etc.

Her lectures were very informative however, it seemed to me that not all the material that was on the essay q. midterm/final were talked about in as much depth as she expected you to answer on these tests. The good side is she was willing to help out students nad she is easy to work with for sp. cir

Kugel is an amazing instructor, I basically aced everything in her course, but not because her course was easy, but more because she illustrates everything so well and is a an amazing lecturer in opinion.

she's a really nice teacher that genuinely cares about her students. the midterm and final were based on lectures. final wasn't cumulative. had to do 2 easy papers. not tested on the text. pretty easy class. take it if you want an A.
She mostly teaches Native American history and she is part Native American herself.  She cares about her students and is approachable.
Easy A if you do the work.

Dr. K Math10 course was easier than I expected. I am horrible at math and I was able to pass his class. I highly recommend keeping up with the lectures and doing all the homework. Homework is essential since it is based on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Summer: It was really fast paced. Still, I was able to keep up and do very well in this class. Math is my worst subject, but Dr. K knows how to break down the lessons so that even I could be good at math haha. You MUST pay attention though. If you space out, you won't pass. Grading criteria/expectations are crystal clear. 100% would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Students are able to learn from the lecture. As long as you pay attention in class and do all homework its an easy A to get.
Very good teacher willing to help you if you need it.
Dr. K really attempts to help his students understand while also being personable.  His lectures can be somewhat funny at times and that keeps the interest in the class.

Shilong Kuang's stats class was incredibly easy but he made attendance required which is ridiculous considering college students shouldn't be babied or spoon fed. Also, he tended to go over concepts a million times and spent whole (required) lectures reviewing. Just finish and review the homework and you'll get an A.

I took Professor Kuang's Stats class at Saddleback and loved it! This material is not easy, but once you get used to his teaching style, you'll be okay. Study a lot, and an A is definitely possible. This exams were clear and came from examples from the notes. He is very supportive, and wants you to enjoy the class. Inspired me to minor in stats!

Dr. K was hard to understand at first but after the first couple weeks he relaxed and so did the class. He's very helpful and made a big effort to make sure I understood everything. He's patient and fair with grading. No extra credit and attendance was not mandatory. Took MATH 10 at Saddleback from him and got a B in class. I would recommend him.

He's really not a bad professor. If you are familiar with math terms already, his accent won't get in the way. He tries his best to explain the lesson, and cares about his students learning and His quizzes/midterms are straightforward. He was really nice, since he tried to control people's rude behavior.

I first thought he was hard because there was so much material, but then he turned out easy. You get used to the accent. Exam questions are nigh straight from the notes and quizzes. Final was difficult but if you learn the concepts instead of just memorizing examples, you should be fine. Drops lowest quiz. Big curve. I passed the class with an A+.

Not a bad teacher. He really does care about his students learning, but during the end he got annoyed at students' inappropriate behavior. He is a little unclear because of his accent, but it's nothing unbearable. The exams are based on the quizzes. I passed with an A+, so it was an easy A to say the least.

At the beginning of the year he was pretty fun, but after a couple of weeks he began to show his bad side. He was very harsh to students and made the final unfair compared to the examples in class and the homework. If you are not great in math DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR!
He is a very helpful and good professor, however  he randomly turned mean. The final was absurdly hard and i expect everyone to have failed.

He is one the best math teachers. He absolutely cares for every student in the class. He's pretty funny sometimes. His accent might get in the way, but he is good at re-explaining. He knows what he is talking about. All his quizzes and exams are problems from the homework and notes. So you got to go to class.

He was hard to understand and there were several problems that he actually made harder - you're trying to follow what he's saying and you suddenly realize that what he's talking about is very simmple and he's muddling the explanation

Best TA ever! If you need help, go to his office hours. before you leave, he will make sure you understand it, usually by making you explain it to another student or do it on the board (dont be afraid of that because it truly will help)

I enjoyed attending class even though it was at 8AM every day. I learned a lot, and if I didn't understand something, he was always available through email or at office hours and cleared everything up. I recommend taking his class.

He will answer any questions on and off class whenver you can find him. He cares for the entire class and will push you if you fall behind. (rarely found in ucr these days) Attend his class! His class is very amusing and you'll love mathmatics
one of the best ta in UCR. need help??? find him.

He knows what he is talking about, but who knows if you will.  His English is very poor, its almost impossible to understand him.  Plus he tends to have a hard time understanding any questions the students ask.  Okay professor, but if math is difficult for you I would go with someone you can understand.
He is very straightforward in what he wants you to know for the exam.  There are almost no surprises when it's time for the quizzes and tests. Taking organized, clear, and detailed notes is a must.
He is extremely clear in his lectures and, as someone mentioned, you need to go to class everyday. Also, he is always extremely helpful.
mr kuang is a very helpful ta and he is very clear with his lectures.  his midterms and quizzes are exactly like his lectures so i strongly suggest you go to class everyday.
Don't know which math 22 professor to take? Take his class he is the nice and helpful TA I ever seen.

This guy is better than the professors that teach the course. This Man is like a God. He can teach you anything in math and you will understand it and ace the tests because of his help. He will help you on the quizzes b4 he hands them out.

If there was a calendar for TA's, he would be Mr. June... beach season. (aside from the front cover) he knows his**** and he's very helpful. Try to stump him with questions. You'll be wasting your time, cuz it seems like he wrote the text book. yes, hes a genius. and hes funny.

He did a pretty good job with the class, especially since it was in summer school. He was organized, punctual and very leniant. Im sure as he gains experience, he'll get alot better. Make sure you come to class because most of his quiz and test question are directly out of lecture!!.
i love his voice. mr shilong is the most awesomest ta ever.

Phenomenal Professor! Very farsighted and kind! He will not create easy tests, that's for sure! However his lectures are very intertwined with the real world, so it is compelling to participate in the course!
Professor Kurzfeld was one of my favorite professors at Bates. His lectures were always interesting and it felt like he always found a way to engage the students. Would recommend!

I do not understand the other comments about Prof. Kurzfeld. His Law and Econ class is my favorite class at Bates and he always has some really interesting insights about the topics. His passion is evident.

Without a doubt the worst professor I've ever had. One day he'll give one definition for a term and the next day he'll give you another. Then it's up to you to guess which one he'll give you credit for on the test. Lectures are dry and uninteresting. Grading criteria was never made clear, and seemed to change depending on how he was feeling. Avoid.

Hands down the worst class I've taken in my college career. Kurzfeld is perfectly nice and easy to get along with, but his lectures are unbelievably dull and full of contradictions. He's quite proud of the difficulty of his tests which are only difficult because his grading criteria are extremely unclear. Save yourself and don't take his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Kurzfeld is without a doubt the worst I have had in my time in the department at Bates. His class is extremely boring and does not bring a persona that makes you want to learn. The material is very dry and difficult to conceptualize, since most of it does not make sense to apply to the real world. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He's honestly an awful professor. His lectures are useless & don't teach you anything about economics. You will only be able to pass his class if you've had other professors who have already taught you what he's trying to teach. He gives far too much work for a college professor & makes me feel like I'm in middle school. Unpredictable grading too.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Prof. Kurzfeld is very clear in explaining the material.  The homework assignments are directly related to the exam questions so be sure to understand HOW to do the homework and you will do good on the exams.  If you need any help at all Prof. Kurzfeld is more than willing to help you during office hours.  A very good experience. Take his class

I was always afraid to take Immunology as many told me that it was one of the hardest classes on campus. Professor Spurgin was an amazing teacher, who made the course so enjoyable as well as easy to manage. There were worksheets to do every week based on the Lecture Slides. The Midterm and Final Exam were all from the Slides as well! TAKE HIM!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I took his immunology class over the summer during covid19 online format. There was a lot of info in his lectures. keep up with notes. allowed test to be open notes due to online format. However his in -class format is just as fair since he said his average for in-person exams were around 80% and ours it was 90%. Questions straight from notes
Dr. Kurt Spurgin is an amazing Professor, he teaches good and he also makes sure that you understand each chapter in the book. Be prepared to study ahead and you'll be fine.

Great teacher. Very clear and concise. I had actually taken this class and failed with another teacher, re took it with Dr. KURT and passed with an almost an A (89%) pay attention and do the homework you'll be fine. He's great. Highly recommend him.

An amazing professor with great and straightforward powerpoints. Everything on his midterms he covers thoroughly in class. There is nothing on the test that is going to be a surprise and nothing is supposed to be tricky. Study and you will get the grade you work for. He really cares about the students' understanding. He is very knowledgable. TAKE!!

Pro's - Super accessible with great office hours and email responsiveness. Good tone of voice and doesn't put you to bed in class. Tells good stories and keeps it fun. Con's - Power points can be a little unclear, way too many lists and ambiguous concepts that cross over to other long lists. Needs to make ppoints more concise to prevent info vomit
He was a good professor and gave a study guide before the midterm. His lectures had all the information necessary and sometimes told stories that related to the lectures.

Dr. Spurgin made the lectures interesting for those of us that are pre-med by providing case studies to make systems neuroscience more relatable. His clinical insight is also valuable. The tests were 40 multiple choice, 2-4 free response, fair and straight from the slides. Lecture style is easy to understand.

I would cross University without looking both ways in the hopes I would be hit by a car and wouldn't have to go to class. Save your mental health. He accuses many students of academic misconduct on programming assignments. Long process. He doesn't answer emails. Lots of homework. SAVE YOURSELF!!!

He does not explain things well. Most of the time what is explained in class doesn't feel related to what we are currently talking about. The only time lecture is helpful is when he goes over exactly whats on the lab/programming assignments. He does not care about his students, you must get over 70% on 5 quizzes or else you fail the class.
I AM ON MY KNEES WHEN I SAY AVOID HIM PLEASE SAVE YOURSELF. HE DOES NOT CARE ABOUT YOU. I REPEAT. HE GENUIENLY DOES NOT AND WILL NEVER CARE ABOUT YOU.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: AVOID AT ALL COST!!! Even if you have to take this class at CC! He will accuse students so many students of "cheating". The worst part is he won't tell you until the end of the quarter, so the whole time you "think" you passed until you get hit with the email of accusation. The worst part he doesn't answer emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE KRIS MILLER. HE WILL ACUSE YOU OF CHEATING. I know countless students that have been falsely accused of plagiarism, some of them fought against him. He NEVER answers emails. BUT, if are falsely accused, and you fight the allegation, YOU WONT WIN, it takes at least two quarters if not more... avoid him.

Does not care about his students. If you slip up and miss an assignment or something he will not care at all. I had a misunderstanding about one assignment that is worth 5% of my grade, and while I was able to submit every other assignment with him knowing I just had this one misunderstanding, he still gave me 0/100. He just does not care at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He has a glorious shiny bald head

I think Miller is a good professor. CS061 sucks more because of the class rather than because of him. I think he is effective at teaching and I don't have any gripes with him. Class is hard and homework is plentiful but I think is manageable with effort. My only thing is Miller may talk weakly and unorganized which may detract from the lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: There are 5 quizzes and you have to get at least 70% on all of them to pass the class. You're allowed one retake each. Pay attention in lectures because sometimes he'll say exactly what will be on the tests. Plus he's great at explaining things. Awesome professor, really cares about his students
Professor never answer any emails once the quarter is over. Ignored all my emails.

Kris Miller is an alright professor he wasn't the worst to me but I personally was bored in class. Grading is pretty light as long as you put effort into the homework you'll be fine. Quizzes mostly easy except for conceptual type of problems in which you know it or you don't. No midterm and the final exam was almost exactly like the practice final.

Not a bad class with him to be honest, but don't expect CS61 to be easy. Put in the work, keep up with the reading. He's helpful during office hours. He might go fast paced at times, but it's your responsibility to keep up. There is a learning curve that comes with this class, and it might take a few weeks to adjust to it. Very solid class.
In any case,

Attendance not mandatory, but lots of class activities for extra credit. He's very clear on what will be on the final, and you might see copy-pastes of practice final problems on the test. Programming assignments get harder with time. 5 quizzes, lowest dropped. His lectures aren't super exciting, but he tries his best to help if you reach out.

Kris Miller is a good professor. He shows examples in lecture, so make sure you go to lecture to learn the concepts. This class is difficult than CS010A, but it is easy to pass if you do good on your 5 quizzes and turn in assignments early. No midterm or final.
Terrible Professor
Honestly, the class itself is pretty hard and professor is no help. LIke he doesn't curve the grade and don't be gracious when it comes to the grade.

He flat out just assigns you projects and homework inorder to figure it out yourself. He makes it seem as if going to lecture is gonna help you understand what he is saying. Unless you were able to take CS010A recently he does not make it easy for those who never took that class. Better off figuring it out on your own or getting help. He is lazy
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Most of the learning will be from Zybooks, and the lectures will only be for review of what you read. Lectures become a little monotonous after a while. There's no midterm or final, just 5 quizzes throughout the quarter and 2 during finals week. He keeps the highest 5 quizzes. Just turn in assignments on time and it's an easy A.

He is not very accessible outside of his office hours. During lectures, he primarily goes over examples rather than teaching the concepts directly. His quizzes come in multiple versions, with some being more difficult than others. He has very little patience for those who don't understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment:
Simply the worst  professor and class ever. 
His grading policy is pretty funny and no curve at all.
Don't expect anything from him

Overall a very good professor. He answers questions and shows examples in lectures, so the class is an easy A if you finish assignments on time. We had no final or midterms, just 5 quizzes throughout the quarter and take-home programs. As long as you do the readings and finish labs legitimately, the quizzes and programs should be easy.

Kris is a solid professor overall. The class can be tough, but the lectures are worth attending and office hours are super helpful. Utilize resources like unstuck ai alongside the textbook to ace the course.
Just too many homeworks. And no curve for the exam
This professor sucks. Too many homeworks and no curve for the exam. Does not care about the students at all. dont ever choose to take his classes

Just get ready to do a LOT of reading in Zybooks, which costs $78 to purchase. His lectures are good as he goes slowly and emphasizes many important things you must master to do well in PAs, quizzes, and assignments. The only main issues are reading and the frustrating PAs you must complete, as these are time-consuming and annoying.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: too many homeworks.

You cannot cheat in this class; if you do, you will fail. The final exam/four quizzes are all proctored in person.
