The first half of the quarter is manageable, but it gets more difficult when you reach the topic "Vectors". Do not wait until the last minute to complete programming assignments. Ask questions, attend lectures, and be prepared to read.

The class is quite difficult, however, Kris explains a lot of the material very well. If you struggle with CS, I would highly recommend going to the lectures and office hours. The lectures are not mandatory but help with doing well on the quizzes. The class material is quite a bit and a step up from CS10A.

Ngl, I had to retake the class and def. harder than 10A, but I was able to understand more of the materials than before. The prof. is overall nice and cares about his students, but the lectures aren't always helpful and can get boring. His way of teaching slightly improved but still isn't the best. I find myself mostly self-learning using zybooks.

Get ready to have your eyes stuck to your screen. He's a great guy, little rough around the edges but not bad overall. Interesting person with strong insight on C++. Hella homework and TAs aren't really the best. Only annoying thing is 65% or higher on final. PA is worth more than quizzes so focus on getting PAs right.

Took CS10B as Fall 2023 first year (came in with AP CSA which used Java). Watched vids on youtube on c++, really similar to java. Lectures are helpful and sometimes he says certain topics will be on quiz. Mostly self learning through zybooks ($77) online textbook. Good prof. quite easy class for me but there are certain topics that are hard to get.

Prof. Miller is a very warm guy and he comes off as respectful and caring. Grades are very test-heavy but they'll be pretty easy if you understand the material. Important to note that you actually read about, learn, and practice concepts in zyBooks (online textbook) and lectures are used exclusively to answer questions and do in-class exercises.

Had him for summer session 2023. If you are passionate about learning c++ and willing to put in the work this class will be easy. Be warned, if you do not get at least 65% on the final your grade gets capped at a D+. The final exam is heavily based on pointers, linked lists, and recursion so make sure you understand those well.

Miller was one of the better CS professors I had at ucr so far. In order to pass his class, you should go to all lectures and his office hours as he is super helpful in those. I got a 93 on the final with the curve, yet the average was like 63. Make sure u understand pointers and recursion. Make sure to get above a 65 on the final or you auto fail

I personally did not like Kris' way of teaching. Made us sign up for lots of unnecessary things. He would also make you feel stupid for asking questions at times, which irked me a lot. Confusing lectures. Didnt prepare us well for finals. In class participation was kind of stressful. Look for another 10B prof if you can.

Definitely a lot harder than 10A, be ready to self-study a lot because his lectures aren't very helpful. Not the best at explaining things and can be a bit confusing. Labs are okay, but programs are every week and are very hard with the final based heavily on them. His rule is > 65% on the final is an automatic fail regardless of class grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Course difficulty is about what you would expect, it is a bit more than cs010A, Challenge activities take up a significant amount of time, though they are worth very little points overall. Attend lectures so you don't miss In class activities, I recommend using visual studio over visual studio code if you already understand linux command line.

Lectures are very hard to follow and usually don't make any sense with the material you're learning about. But if you approach him outside of class for help, he is very helpful. The labs and programs get very hard towards the end, and the TAs aren't super helpful. A lot of independent work but if you enjoy coding, this class is very interesting.
People exagerate the final, pay attention and take notes and the final wont be too bad
lectures weren't too helpful and were often boring. I learned more by going to his office hours(which were very helpful) and self learning
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: A great all-around lecturer. His assignments can seem lengthy, but they are fair and worthwhile. The midterm and final were good culminations of what was covered throughout lectures and labs. The only downside is that he condemns skipping lectures, even in the first lecture where much of the class is moderately experienced.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: tired and hard to learn , spent almost full time on following his lectures, luckily my major is not cs.

If youre passionate about the material, the class is very easy. Programs and Labs can get frustrating, although hints and tips are given in lectures. Hes very adamant in making content significant; hes very focused on aiding students in real world object-oriented design. Very quality prof, would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Miller was a caring for his students and was always willing to answer any questions, but he explains the concepts well. He tries to incorporate fun activities for his class making the class bearable. As long as you read the text book and do the activities and labs you will pass the class as well as the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: The "Dad" figure of CS at UCR. He's passionate about the subject and seeing his students pass. He is the perfect professor for intro CS. In terms of difficulty, you will sweat a little (CS014). Material is not hard but volume of work is a lot.
His course is very friendly to newbies. I have studied Python with him and I would like to study C++ with him in the next quarter.

hands down one of the hardest classes to take as a freshman. if you don't know c++ well, then PLEASE start with cs010 do NOT jump right into this class unless you're ready to put all your time and energy into it. Lab's and tests are difficult. All I can say is good luck, hope you dont have too many mental breakdowns
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The lectures are a pretty important part of the class as he goes further in depth in them and expands on the topics you read about. Keeping this in mind, it is also imperative that the online textbook is read and the programming assignments and labs are done on your own as if you work with others often times you don't learn the lessons you need to.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dude is straightforward, hell repeat important concepts in lecture and tell you to focus on them for the exam. Also, there are lots of programming assignments that can be a pain but ultimately help you grow. If youre really struggling, go to office hours. TAs/Kris will help a lot.

I loved Dr. Miller as a person, however as a professor, he lacked in many areas. The final is heavily weighted, however capping a grade at a C- because someone does not get higher than a 70% on the final is absolute anarchy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I DO NOT RECOMMEND THIS PROFESSOR! Kris is a nice guy, but he barely teaches anything and expects us to teach ourselves. I went to the ARC a lot, yet, prior to the final I had a B- and then after the final my grade dropped to a D because he puts so much weight on the final. Good Luck is all I can say. Paid $65 for the HW to not pass a class.

Kris Miller is a good professor who does a good job of expecting his students to read the material and the lecture is to build on what you should have already learned. Good at explaining concepts in class, and those concepts are often the free-response questions on exams. Like any CS class, the Final is heavily weighted. So study the material well
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I had cs12 with Miller and the class itself is pretty challenging and comes with a lot of work (a program assignment pretty much every week along with reading and labs), but I thought Miller did a great job of explaining the material and preparing you for the assignments and tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Horrible teacher does not care about his students and class is extremely hard

Miller is the most straightforward CS lecturer at UCR, since that is his actual main job - he does no research. His classes are fairly easy as long as you put in effort to understand the content, as a lot of it is cumulative knowledge. Those who do not follow tend to have a hard time catching up.

CS14 is a tough class regardless of professors as the subject tends to be very dense. However, Miller is the best choice at the moment for students who are taking CS14 in my personal opinion as I have heard/know more students who failed with the other professor. Be prepared to put in countless hours into studying/programming

Professor Miller was a great professor back in CS010. Over the quarters, he seemed to have lost motivation to teach. At times he can be extremely thorough with his lectures. He speaks extremely fast and does not attempt to simplify his explanations. His programs are relatively hard, but it teaches you how to think it terms of a computer scientist.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Took the class for CS012, and he's really good at explaining certain algorithms/data structures, so as long as you pay attention, take notes, and PRACTICE CODING, then you'll be fine in this class. Take note that you have to pass the final with at least a C, otherwise, you'll fail the class. I didn't get an A, but I passed; that's all that matters.

The class is designed to weed people out so the class is tough. But, Miller is very thorough and will answer any questions you have during class. There is a lot of homework so the class will take up a lot of time. Just study for the final because if you get below a C- on the final you are capped at a C- in the class and can't move on to CS 14.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Professor Miller is a great professor. I mean he is one of the greatest at UCR. He is really engaging and his use of words aren't confusing. He's is straight the point, very practical. IDEALLY you want him for all your CS class (I had him for CS 10, 12, and 14) and I genuinely enjoyed every class.

Great and lenient CS professor. He is clear during the lectures. During the hard parts of the lecture, he can explain the parts in detail. The final is a pass or fail thing. So if you fail the final (73%) yet you have a high-A in the class, you still fail the class. If you pass the final, yet you have 73% in the class, you fail too.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great professor. Was able to clearly explain all of the material despite it being in an online class. He encourages you to ask any questions and cares alot about his students succeeding. If you are looking to take the online version of this class make sure Miller is teaching it. Class is fairly difficult but just work hard and go to office hours

This class is extremely easy if you just keep up with the material. Miller is an excellent professor. Only advice I could give is to make sure that the work you submit isn't someone else's, he will find out!

Okay first off, about a third of the class failed the midterm and probably dropped out. The midterm wasn't hard at all. I guess it true, CS isn't for everyone. Okay, Miller is an amazing teacher. Office hours are remarkable useful and boy were the labs and assignment are incredibly fun. Let just say that I had a "lit af" experience. ;) Thumbs up!!!

Boy this was one tough class, but I learned a lot about c++.  Professor Kris Miller is an excellent teacher that honestly wants you to understand the materials and wants you to ask questions no matter how minor they are.  Overall, be prepared for a heavy workload with tons of programming homework, labs, activities, etc. Study hard for his class!

Very tough class for those with no prior programming experience. Be prepared to put a lot of time on the programming assignments. Kris is a very good lecturer and is passionate for his job. He is open to question and will clarify things that are confusing. This is a weeder class for CS and getting anything below a 70% will cap your grade at a C-.

Really helpful teacher. As an exchange student I went through a lot of problems enrolling in classes and getting cs account. He was the only professor at UCR that helped me and supported me even when I was not fully enrolled and did not even have an account to use at labs.

He gives in class exercises that take your name down for credit on some days. Skip at your own risk. He's a really helpful and nice professor unlike the others in the CS department. Lectures are really helpful and sometimes essential to assignments.
I got 2 lectures late because of the international  process , and he was very helpful guiding me. I could do well the class.
Fun and easy class but beware...this man is as smug as they come.  I'm talkin' smug emissions through the roof.

eZ claSS cUz of Gre@T pr0F3ssor!!! Assignments are tough sumtimes, but thatz cuz comput0r science classes are generally difficult. His enthusiasm, attention to detail, and clarity make his lectures great and enjoyable. For any incoming students, attend your lectures and you'll end up with an A, unlike someone who got a B+. PSHHHHHHHH

Starts off great, but he becomes less caring and less clear. He seems to enjoy the subject but he doesn't seem to enjoy teaching it. Even if the entire class does not understand an assignment (the last one), he will not clarify. Also if you get an A- or a B- in the class he will still give you a C- if you fail the final, which a lot of people did.
The Hardest class I ever took. All the assignments are tough, very demanding, and took all my time for this class only. Make sure you are really good at C++ before taking this class.

HARD CLASS!! had to take this class for my major and let's js say i am considered technologically stupid and had NO programming exp before this class. it's like they expect you alrdy know the basics. the assignments take up SO MUCH time it's a pain. i would probably suggest to take cs10 at a cc if only this one is required for your major

Professor Miller was pretty nice and easy. I only felt challenged in this class at the last assignment. He wasn't strict with assignments but also didn't give so much direction sometimes. Curved final generously. I felt like his lessons were good but slow cuz he repeated things a lot sometimes. Our class had 7 As, 8 Bs, 8 Cs, and 4 Ds. Got an A+

This is probably one of the easiest classes you will take as a computer science major. I took CS 10 in 2011. I slacked a lot as a incoming freshman and I started to focus after averaging a low C around week 6. Ended up getting a B on the final and an A on the final. Just keep up with the work and you will do well. I regret not getting the A.

CS10 is hard. We had one programming assignment due each week, and each of them take hours, literally hours (only a small part of the class can finish without any help from TA). Other than that, Kris is pretty helpful, clear and nice. But I wouldn't take CS10 unless I like computer stuffs and good at it.

He took a difficult subject and made it clear and understandable! CS 10 is difficult for some but if you leave time for your assignments and read his notes that he posts online the class won't be difficult. He is just a great professor!! Study the quizzes and his notes and you will do great!

CS isn't easy, but this guy did a great job teaching the course. Tests are tricky. You will spend a lot of time on the assignments. Go to TA office hours! This class requires 20+ hours a week to master everything. Overall very rewarding, and after the class I was able to pick up BioPerl super fast.

VERY DIFFICULT CLASS. The professors cannot help you with the assignments (but will drop hints with large room for error) and everything goes by so fast that you master nothing. the labs are a pain, and they end up  not helping you. then the assignments, they will eat up your life, they are beyond difficult and require many more hours than needed.

CS itself is a tough subject,especially if you don't have prior experience but if you're willing to put in the effort,you'll do fine. I got an A in the class and didn't have CS knowledge beforehand.Miller does the best he can and the TAs are very helpful as well.A lot of work but it's necessary to do well in a class like this.

Definitely a great professor. Nothing to worry about if you spend a decent amount of time every week on the assignments and reading. I previously had no experience with any C++ or programming and it was a pretty easy class. Going on his online forum to ask questions is really helpful.

He is a pretty good professor. He does the best he can. The material itself can get pretty difficult sometimes. You have to practice and read on your own. He is lenient and he tries to help as much as possible. No curve in class or final.

I never took a computer science class before, but I thought cs10 was tons of fun to watch your codes succeed! Hard work guarantees an A:  you have to start hw early, and go to office hours a lot to get full hw points. There is a final exam minimum to pass the class, but it is very simple if you attend every class.

Mr. Miller is awesome! The very best teacher I have ever had in this school. I came into this class not knowing anything about c++ and his lectures were very helpful. C++ is not an easy class. I passed with a B but I worked real hard for this class. Be prepared to study!

Class is extremely difficult, it would not be considered a beginners intro course to C++. they should take it down a few notches. MAny people go in as a beginner not knowing anyhting about C++ and they expect you to know a basic amount. I went to every lecture and attended office hours and still failed. have to get at least 70% on final to pass

This class is way too difficult for beginners. Theye should dome it down a bit, i went in not knowing anything about C++, and they pretend like you know the basics already for it. The quizzes/tests/final are really tricky and you must score a 70% or higher in order to pass the class..seriously many people failed, they should make this class easier

This class is wayy too difficult for beginners, i took this class winter 2011, and it is extremely difficult. The class pretends you already know the basics and everything. Must score a 70% or higher in order to pass the class. This is a fail class, they should dome it down a lot more so it seems like its more for beginners. quizzes+tests are hard

The poster below me basically took the words right out of my mouth. It's not that Miller isn't a great teacher, it's just that the class is way too difficult. Miller will do anything to help his students and he's truly a great prof. However, the class is way too hard for beginners! Plus, there's no curve, so most people end up failing it.

UCR's curriculum for cs is too difficult. I went to class everyday, office hrs every week and still didnt pass the class, you definitely need prior experience to do well in this class, you simply cant pass the class by reading the book and attending lectures. Programming assignments will take your life away. The final was based off of the stuff we learned the last day in class. And you had to pass it with a 70 or higher which is stupid for beginners.  this class is not fair at all stay away !

Going to lectures definitely helps.  Labs, codelab hw, and programming assignments are fair, as far as the difficulty level goes.  Just watch out for the weekly quiz/exams.  Together they make up 40% of your grade! So if you can keep up with those quizzes and get above a 70% on the final it's easy to pass the class.

definitely one of the best cs teacher i've ever had. He is very helpful during office hours and grades fairly. He makes this class very interesting, even for the beginners. I would definitely take him again for CS class.

I took Kris two years back.  He's truly an amazing instructor. Everyone who gave him a bad review either cheated (got an F) or didn't do the work. It is a lot of work, but you must do work to understand and be good at the material. I wouldn't recommend this class if you're not genuinely interested in the material. Easy and fair if you are, though.
Extremely helpful, always willing to give time out to help you understand, you have to go to do the assignments to understand but if you do them its an automatic A

I took this class as a Bio major and I got an A, but this was the most useless class ever. He sucks at teaching he expects you to know everything he says and his assingments are so dumb i dont know how he comes up with them. he doesnt answer emails and on the discussion boards hes just rude he doesnt help at all. he ignored all my emails. DONT TAKE

Miller isn't hard if you go to lectures and PAY ATTENTION. Make sure to get a head start on Programming Assignments cause they are time consuming sometimes (AND DON'T COLLABORATE! TRUST ME). Review your quizzes once he grades them, cause he likes to reuse questions, ESPECIALLY on the final. Class is kinda pointless if you're not a CS or CE major...
Miller was really helpful in this class. As long as you go to lectures and pay attention, you should be fine

If its ur 1st time learning C++, GO TO ALL LECTURES! It mite b hard at 1st but i thought the class wasnt too bad. Programming Assignments(pretty much like homework) can b VERY time consuming.. but i thot the quizzes, midterms, and final wasnt too hard. labs can get a little frustrating. MAKE SURE U ALWAYS ASK 4 HELP IF UR STUCK.

Took this class as a Biology major. This class requires a lot of work, it's more busy work than anything. Teacher expects you to understand everything after explaining. Don't take this class if you are not a CS major. This is a warning.
he doesn't make grading personal So he can makes it hard for everyone just to see who can keep up

I really liked this teacher.  I had never taken a computer programming class before, but his class got me so interested in the subject that I'm now declaring it as my major.  Very clear, not too difficult (just the right amount of challenge).  I actually thought the class got easier in the second half.

Great Teacher! Beginning was easy as pie. Later on it becomes a bit difficult. In class quiz, lab quiz, programming assignment (basicly hw), 1 midterm and 1 final. Midterm has a bit of concept in the beginning then  solving algorithms (like what's n + 1 if n = 5). Extra credit on the  midterm but not on the final. Final = same format as midterm.

If you have taken computer programming before, then this should be an easy class. If not I highly advise you study or get some extra help. this is a hard class for new comers. He thinks that everyone already knows what he is talking about.

I don't know what some of these people see in him by saying he is easy, it is quite the opposite unless you have prior knowledge of the material. More than half the class drops or fails his class after the first midterm. His quizzes, midterm, and final are extremely tricky, try multiple choice A through G. He designs his tests in favor of CS majors

Very understandable and clear.  Has quizzes every week and he drops the lowest quiz score.  Be sure to get help when you need it or else you will begin to get lost on the material that follows the midterm.  Overall, great class and i learned a lot of the basics of C++.

Kris is a cool teacher.  His tests are straight forward with very little trickery ie Linard type vocab questions.  He eases up a bit on the quiz a day vibe of CS10 and really explains things in a down to earth simple manner.  Overall he's a good teacher and a cool guy, can't wait for 14!

wow people, if you find the cs10/12/14 series too hard then switch to some humanities major. Sure your grade rapidly drops trying to slack off but its more than doable to get an A with effort. Kris is pretty easy too.

Ok heres the bottom line,CS-12 is nothing like CS-10 so if you thought that CS-10 was fun and you enjoyed CS don’t take this class,This class is very difficult and requires an immense amount of time,Although I got an A in the class, it was because i had to consistently think CS Kris is a very good teacher and actually understands CS not like Linard

Teaches class in a very understandable manner. Very structured, organized and easy to follow. Even if you know almost nothing about computers u will be crapping C++ with no problem after this course. great teacher to start your comp sci series
A pretty good teacher.  Him and Brian Linard are like the main undergrad CS lecturers.  He is easier and seems more willing to give someone an A so take him if you want a slighter smoother time.

Easiest upper-division biology requirement ever! He assigns alot of work, but it's not hard and if you do it, you won't have to study for the midterm. I went to class, went to lab, did the HW, didn't study for the tests,  and got an A. He is very good at teaching. WARNING: No Curve whatsoever!

Extremely helpful teacher. Made sure you learned the material even though it's really hard to get into programming. Gave a lot of homework but that made you learn the material well. If you want to learn CS from the basics this is the class!

He is very clear in explaining the basic concepts of programming. Even though I had experience in programming prior to taking this class, I believe that he explained them in a way that newcomers to programming would be able to grasp as long as they try. One thing to note is that I hardly used the textbook for this class.

To be honest this guy is extremely hard...I heard how he is helpful and understanding, forget that non-sense...He has takin Linard's Approach, WAY TOO MANY ASSIGNEMNTS (Code Lab, Weekly Assignments, Quizes, Lab Practicles, Weekly Lab Assignments, Quizzes, Midterms, Final) Yeah and he gave us a Quiz two days before the final...Insane amount of work!

Programming is inherently boring.  A lecture on syntax is the most boring thing I can imagine.  This is no exception.  There are way to many assignments thought.  You have to do lab assignments, lab practicals, lab exams, code lab, in class assignments, exams, and quizzes.

Great teacher, very straightforward. He really breaks it down to an understandable level and makes sure everyone is learning. The curve for my class was pretty high (B average), which is rare for a CS class and it's not because the class was easy, but because he taught it so well.
BORING BORING BORING!!
sucks at explaining things and hes a very boring person.
BORING!!! his lectures are the most boring things ever. He always puts a lot of people to sleep because he doesnt make the class interesting.
very good professor, very clear explainations and seemed to care about students fully understanding material a great deal.
Miller is a great personal. He is more concerned that students learn, rather than deadlines. I wish he taugh CS 12.
I have only one word for him: boaring, boaring and boaring. He should have been single the rest of this life. His shiny balt head freaks me out. Does not trust anyone at all.
No Comments

VERY BORING! And too easy. I hope I don't have 2 take another class with him. I wasn't challenged by the class, and it was my first class in C++. VERY BORNG! Too repetative. An entire week of lecture was condensed into less than a minute of note reading from a friend. I like programming, but his class just sucked! Sorry for being an ass, but I hated this professor's class.

Excellent undergrad T.A. The programs are very challenging but he makes everything clear and is always there for any help. If you attend all lectures there is no reason why you should be getting less than a B. Wish he was in CS12
AWESOME TEACHER, LOOK FORWARD TO TAKING HIS CLASS.
No Comments

It's true, this guy is the best teacher I've had. I only wish he'd teach CS 12. His class is awesome, just show up to every lecture and pay attention because he tells you EXACTLY how to do everything. I never once opened the book.

i thought his assignment problems were hard, however they are doable as long as you understand the material and put time and effort into it.(which i didn't do) he's a really nice guy. but there is no curve.
great guy. best undergrad course teacher to get. makes for an easy A but is still challenging enough to be fun.
He is the coolest teacher. He makes a huge effort to teach, and sees to it that you understand the material. Best teacher to get.

Very helpful, especially for people without any programming experience.  If you know your stuff, you don't even need to go to lecture.  Quizzes are fairly easy and class is based around simple homework and labs.
Nice guy. He is very clear and helpful.

go to class. look at slides. get out. this class is sooo boring, but i wouldn't blame him. constructing a fun cs is impossible. he does try to make it more fun by having group interactions. other then that, he's very lineant and its hard to anger him. either that or he hides it REALLY well.
Cool teacher, will go out of his way to help you out.

The class is pretty easy but he's really boring.  He lectures from slides so falling asleep is unavoidable.  But the upside is that the tests/ are just like the practice ones from previous quarters so it's easy
teaches from slides....put me to sleep and deterred me from going to class!

Hes a great teacher who knows that he has to teach you the material and will do what it takes to get you to learn it.  Read the book, skim the notes, and go to class.  A lot of people dont go to class and complain later about the grade they deserved.
good teacher

forget what everyone else says.  ALL YOU HAVE TO DO IS READ THE BOOK. i only went to class for quizess and in-class exercises. go to lab, and do the hw and assignments early to get extra credit. DON'T GET LINARD!

Easy class (although I had some background in programming). Quizzes are easy, he gives lots of examples so that you understand the concept. Some classes pointless (style of coding? come on!), others are funny (the juggling sticks are like cin and cout
It's not boring.  I think this guy is great.  He teaches well and he tries extremely hard so that everyone can grasp the material.
not a bad guy, but not the best teacher.  he's actually quite friendly and approachable, but if you're the type to sleep during class, then bring a pillow because it's unavoidable.

This guy is about business, he explains the material well, but you have a program to write each week. his grading scale also is terrible, though at the end of the course things usually work out. Dont cheat because he WILL catch you, trust me i know.
his grading scale sux so bad. hw, assignment, and quiz every week. too much work for such a little points. you have no choice but to take him cuz you really dont' want to take Linard's class.

He is by far the worst teacher I ever had. He shouldn't be teaching but instead have one of the students read of the slides because it is essentially how his class is taught. If you don't come to class just read the book, both are the same.
nice guy. almost seems like he's scared of his students.

BORNING....His class is a sleeping pill...But veryt easy and nice since he lets u run away when a quiz is over...Cant lecture only read off slides so learn to learn by your self...Grading scale sucks but class is easy if you know what you are doing.......
No Comments
If you like being fed information directly from slides, this class could work for you.  Expect to teach yourself everything you need to know.

Could not figure out how to use the mic so he decided to shout the lectures for the term. We had surprise quizzes in class and many students received 1/10 or 2/10 scores. Grading system is pretty fair; there was curve for the class grade that helped everyone's grades and accounted for low averages on quizzes/tests.
exams were killer

Took him for Materials in the summer, his lecture wasn't helpful and his office hours weren't either. Second time taking this teacher not by choice and he was still as rude and unhelpful as ever. The test are the Homework so if you the HW you'll be fine.

Rude and disrespectful, lectures are basically useless, but you have to go because he hits you with pop quizzes that aren't in sync with what your learning in class. The midterms are the homework problems, so if you do the homework this class will be easy.
Teacher wasn't really friendly in answering student's questions, he has the condescending tone towards you. Wouldn't recommend.

In this class, Kumar was a very helpful teacher. He explained all the CONFUSING equations and formulation clearly. His homework problems prepares you for the exam, so do them. Make sure to study very well on the last part (Nodal Analysis) because it is not in the textbook explicitly. Aced midterms and finals after thorough studying. Not impossible.

He is quite helpful if you want to learn, though a bit dry and dull sometimes especially for the time of class(5-6:30). His way of making sure people are understanding is asking "Right or not?" So just keep that in mind. Overall class wasn't too difficult. If you can do the homework, you can do the exam/quizzes.

Pretty easy professor. Quizzes are just based of the homework. Midterms are easy if you have done the homework and gone to class the averages were very high. Everyone failed the final because he told us it would cover post midterm material but it was actually pre midterm material so just beware!

A pretty easy class, although there are readings due EVERY lecture with a quiz to go with them. A bit frustrating at times because you don't even get credit for taking the quiz, if you don't know the answer you get a 0. If you are not one who regularly takes class, don't take this professor! Quizzes are worth 25% of the grade.

This class was very easy. If you do all the readings (there is a lot!) and pay attention in lecture, you should get an A. Professor Kwan is very passionate about dance. This class is only the STUDY of dance (history, culture, movement, etc. So don't expect to actually do any dancing. Overall, I liked her class and enjoyed it.

gives reading before every lecture mandatory attendance because gives quizzes at the beginning of each lecture mandatory disc because its30% of your grade I personally wasnt too happy with her class thought it would be much easier then it was Reading is pretty long if your not interested in dance dont take this class,but shes a good teacher
i liked her. very good professor. if you go to her lecture hours she'll be willing to help. no midterms and the final was extremely easy if you study.

online reading.no textbook. quizzes at the beginning of ea. class on online reading. no midterms. lectures are interesting but boring. you do have to do a small performance, you'll see what i mean the first week of class. final was easy as long as you semi pay attention to lectures, read, and go over lecture slides.

Great professor; He gives very good lectures which are highly detailed and you don't have to take any additional notes because everything is transcribed from the recording on a pdf file; Class is interesting and similar to Bio 5C Relatively easy upper div class; the tests are open note due to the COVID pandemic and the lectures are asynchronous

this class isnt hard, the material isnt hard. the test is weird and that is what threw me off. I would def rather take ochem or biochem over this class. for me it was hard with annoying information. eventhough people say it is an easy class it requires logic and understanding. If you are not ecologically logical dont take this class.

Makes lecture very interesting. There were two midterms and one final (multiple choice). There are homework assignments due every discussion section. Test material is straight forward. Textbook is not really needed, but it helps with note taking because his slides are usually very simple.

Skip class? Sure, just read the textbook and you'll be fine. Anything from his slides is mostly on the textbook. Easiest A+ in biology I've ever gotten. I never went to lectures. Really nice guy, never went to office hours either though. The subject matter is generally pretty dry for ecology, imo.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Anderson was a good professor for this course. Not hard to get an A at all. Tests are mainly his slides (make sure you know what his slides are saying, they are mostly pictures). In general, not a hard upper div bio class. I would recommend taking the class.
It was an easy class. Make sure you understand the pictures from the slides and you should be fine. I got an average score on my midterm and final and still ended up with an A.
This professor made me love ecology, his class is super easy IF YOU PAY ATTENTION DURING LECTURE. Also, focus on the graph that he provide in the class and you be fine.

to be honest This class sucks. i took it going for the good grade boost, but realized this class was not worth it. I reccommend taking ANY other class dont get me wrong alot of the questions on the test were easy, but the averages were so high (85% range) that if you mess up on a vague question (ALOT) that was worded weirdly youre done!

This Professor is one of a kind. His jokes makes you want to not learn classes and his midterms are very straightforward and easy but then somehow the final becomes hard. The questions on the final were very poorly made and he did not even know how to do a few of the questions when asked. Would not recommend if you want to learn science.
Just a good guy overall. His lectures are extremely clear, but hard to stay awake because he has such a soothing voice. Tests were pretty fair, I just wish he taught the 2nd half of BIO005C.

Andersons class is very fair. As long as you go to lecture and pay attention you should do well. Pay great attention to his graphs and examples in his lecture slides, they may pop up on the midterm and final. ;) Other than that, nice guy. He really does care about your progress. So bring your questions to him and ask away! :)

To be honest Ecology is a pretty dry subject, but fret not! Anderson is one of the chillest professors on campus. Brightens topic with beautiful language and tries his best to make it entertaining! His tests are fairly easy if you pay attention in lecture and understand the graphs! Get front row seats to check out the most beautiful baby on campus.

Exams were tricky. Walked into the final with a B but got an A in the end because he of the extra credit final questions. He also curves the class. Don't know how I got an A, but ill take it. p.s ecology is very boring
me likey
cool guy. possible friend. I got an A

The Kurt E Anderson is a great professor. Mucho entertainment. 10/10 would I take him again? yes i would. yup. Take the class of ecology for a fun time and a great learning experience. BIOL 116 is the best. Also he has cats. who knew?
he cool.

Professor Anderson is definitely worth taking! I had him for both Biol116 and Bio5C. i loved bio116 with him, he gave weekly homework so you never fall behind and don't need to cram as much for the exams. Very engaging lectures and useful and fun slides! Subject itself is slightly boring but he tries his best.

I was stressed from the start because Anderson is unclear about how he grades his homework, which is 30% of the grade. I did above average on the 1st exam, average on the 2nd, and got 100% on the final, due to his extra credit. Honestly, don't even stress for this class. If you did the work and were slightly above average, you'll get an A.

Spent a few years in Dr. Anderson's research lab. Would not B as succesful, if I did not. If U R looking for a P.I. that is hands-off & lets you spread  your wings to soar but guides so you don't burn your wings on the sun, send him your resume and an email. Accepting, non-judgemental, supportive, awesome. Math/Ecology/Computer/Microbiology

Anderson has been the best professor I've had at UCR, till date. His lectures are phenomenal and if you just read the book and focus on the material, I promise you, you'll do well. I got screwed over by Reznick for the second half, and still I missed Anderson every lecture. He will make Ecology very interesting for you, take his class. :)

Nice and funny dude kept me attentive in class. Tests based on lecturers  and makes it clear what he is asking of you. Does some recapping through out his lectures to show how everything connects. Powerpoints used are general outlines of what he is going over in class. Tests are fair and straight forward(nothing tricky given).

Hes a great prof. pretty easy, show up and try a little, like study the night before or 2 nights maybe for final and midterms and you'll get an A. gave extra credit on final, and average on the final was a 90, no curve, did not need one. hates cheaters, but you definitely wouldn't in this class anyway.

Anderson is awesome, really fair, and easy, take this as a GPA boost, for upper div, seriously, just have a brain and don't cheat and youll get an A. Went to class 4 times, he was always awesome, I was just busy, gives extra points on the final, really nice, really understanding, hates cheaters and will call you out. MUST TAKE

Not that easy! I've taken easier classes. Midterm 2 was a tough one for me, but overall great class. He's funny too! Midterm questions come off lecture notes. Final was generous with extra credit questions. Does not repeat midterm questions. Fair!

very easy class, very clear, completely a gap booster as long as you have a brain, studied very little overall and was very fair. Tests are easy, record lectures and you'll sleep through them, but overall pretty good class

He is really funny if you pay attention! He is very clear, very easy, & very fair. He actually makes ecology interesting! two midterms and a final with homework everyweek but the homeworks really help with the midterms. Just be careful you understand graphs

Dr. Anderson lectures at an appropriate pace and is engaging to his listeners. He doesn't overload his slides with details, and the homework/exam questions aren't unnecessarily complicated. Overall the class is very easy for a biology course. The textbook is helpful but he will cover all its main points in lecture, so it isn't absolutely necessary.

Hands down the easiest pper div class... Don't need a book, just memorize ALL OF HIS GRAPHS in slides and questions given during the discussion.... All MC exams and are straightforward.. also gave extra credit at the end   20 points!!
Definitely not the easiest upper division bio class I've taken.  I had to put in a lot of effort to get by.  Barely escaped with an A+.
Easiest upper division bio class I've taken.

Dr. Anderson is an ok professor. His midterms are seriously not tricky. They are right off the powerpoints. I guarantee you an A if you go over his slides over and over. No textbook req. KNOW ALL GRAPHS. I was able to pull an A on both midterms. The final to me was a bit trickier than the past 2 midterms. he gave us 25 xtra credit pts on the final

Dr. Anderson is awesome.  Extremely nice and he's pretty funny.  He looks like a young guy who's like 34 years old.  Sometimes it feels like he's reading off the slides, but I still like his humor.  His lecture slides are very good for studying, so study them a lot.  He does not have trick questions at all.  25% MT1, 25% MT2, 30% Final, 20% Dis
he's an okay teacher. this class is not that difficult if you put the effort into it. grading was fair; he gave extra credit to boost up your midterm and discussion grade!!

he's an okay teacher. this class is not that difficult if you put the effort into it. grading was fair; he gave extra credit to boost up your midterm and discussion grade!! as for attending lectures, don't bother. just go over the lecture notes and skim the book.

I dont know what the hype is about this guy....hes an okay professor, thats it. He doesnt make his own notes he just takes the premade lecture from the textbook website and reads them verbatim in class....you could just stay home and read the textbook. His grading is unfair....only people who can get extra credit are the ones who did really bad.

He is very nice and although I did not do the best on the tests, I studied hard for the final and with the help of a curve had a Bt! I did read some of the chapters though despite the fact most of the information is from the slides.
Really cool teacher. His tests are based on the slides. Really fun guy, always jokes around.

i was really scared to take the class, always hated biology, but he made it really fun and i'm actually sad the class is over. the tests aren't bad, most of them come from the slides, but the book is a good review. he's always around to answer questions, and he's a pretty funny &personable guy. definitely worth taking, i wish i had him again
i wish he taught all classes in all disciplines.

I love this professor! He has a very approachable and fun personality, though the subject he is teaching is quite blah. Makes his lectures very easy and understandable. The midterms are easy if you just study the slides that he gives out. I would recommend this professor for everyone! If I could I would take another of his classes. He is awesome =)

Professor McMillen inspired to be a better person! I usually skip most of my classes, but I would never miss one of his, because I knew it would always be a fun one. :) While a tough grader, I would recommend his class to anyone.
My favorite T.A. I have had at UCR so far. Gives good feedback, is funny, and lectures very interestingly. Also, he dresses very nice.

Kyle is a wonderful professor, he expects a lot out of you, but he wants to see everyone succeed. His papers are tough, and he grades the first one tougher than the final. If you have him for this class remember to read all the articles, and highlight quotes because you may use them for the papers. All in all, I'm glad I had his class!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: While she seems intimidating at times, it is clear that she takes her job seriously and cares for the success of her students. This class was us reading a book a week, giving a presentation on one book, and writing two essays. Every class felt more like a book club than a class and I enjoyed that. She isn't for everyone but I would recommend her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I did not receive any graded assignments or meaningful feedback during the term, which made it difficult to understand expectations or track my performance. She later said she took points off from laughter. Interactions were dismissive and critical rather than supportive. Overall, the course was unproductive for my learning.

I did not care for Prof Lalami's class at all. I found her to be quite rude and belittling. Even though the subject she taught is one I love, her classes were often the bane of my day. She's a fine grader, and knows her stuff. You will learn, but be cut off.  scolded some times. embarrassed. She's a bit inconsiderate. will not be taking again.

She knows what she is talking about and cares, but she is such a tough grader. I worked super hard for the Entirety of the quarter, and she gave me a B minus on my final paper. Ive never received anything below an A on a paper, and the way she graded papers and participation was strict. My final grade lowered my GPA which was a bummer.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: My experiemce with Laila was excellent throughout the entire course. She was always following my progress close enough as to encourage me to be constant and continue with the tough work I needed to finish in order to be succesfull not only in the completion of the course but in taking my english up to the next level. Excellent teaching skills.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Would take again

reviews.comment: You will learn a lot from Laila if you attend class and pay attention. Leads a great workshop and is super knowledgeable in the subject.  Great professor overall.
Great professor! She's a little tough but also supportive at the same time.

SHe is very rude and will yell at you. She does not allow students to give their opinion clearly, and she will cut you off mid sentence. Please save yourself the trouble from being offended and don't waste your time do not take her.
Great teacher, I learned a lot in her class!

Professor Lalami is AMAZING. Her passion for the subject was conveyed in each class. She assigned a lot of reading (a book a week), but they were all very interesting. She knows what she's talking about and will push you to think critically. Lots of analyzing; really great class. She was tough, but at least you learned. TAKE HER!

My three years of JPN I would try my best to get her class. yes tough and strict but she is amazing! She does gives out fair amount of hws and essays to do.  If you like a strict prf that knows what they doing, take her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Sagawa Senei is a very stern and strict professor. If you want to get a good grade, you need to prepare for class, want to learn and really have your crap together. If you're not serious about learning Japanese, she is not the professor for you. She does have a caring side, though, and does not want students to fail. Very good prof. But scary.

Honestly it's almost impossible to succeed in 101A if your only Japanese experience is the JPN1-6 series at UCR. Pulled all nighters, went to office hours, studied for hours before exams. Hard work will not get you the A. You have to be N3 level to have a fighting chance. Better to wait a year and self study than to take this right after JPN6.

Average difficulty, she make things difficult just because she's in the mood. Give me only 50% class participation point(even though I came to every class, answered every in class question). Plenty of quizzes, exams aren't too hard, but she loves to make trick questions that even herself would fall for it. Very unprofessional.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: this course costed me years off my life. she's available during office hours but that sometimes leaves you with more questions. other students are stuck up. worst class ive ever taken. learned a lot tho ig.

This class has convinced myself and several other students that our Japanese language skills are absolutely awful. Every mistake is recorded and counted, even on the homework! Most students feel stressed and nervous for the smallest assignments. Few As and lots of stress. Terrible learning environment for mental health.

Sagawa Sensei is a highly intelligent and admirable woman and I have nothing but respect for her as a professional. That said she in no way creates a safe learning environment for students to make mistakes and learn from them. She has made condescending and snide remarks towards students who may not know the answer to question she deems simple.

Sagawa-sensei is one of my favorite professors at UCR!  I have taken her for Japanese 1-3 so far and have enjoyed all of them greatly. She is highly intelligent, funny, and accommodating. She is a very fair grader - you get what you earn. If you pay attention, actively participate, and study, you'll do well.  I would highly recommend her!

Sagawa sensei is overall great. Yes, she can be a bit mean and drill you sometimes but thats usually only if you dont know your material or arent paying attention. daily hw and lots of quizzes, strict grader but very doable. dont take her if youre lazy and want an easy A tho def gotta put in the work and study your material if you want an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Sagawa Sensei is amazing. I love her teaching style and I really think shes unfairly criticized. Shes doing her very best to instill good work ethic so we really truly learn the language. I think people misunderstand her because theyre not very aware of how Japanese usually are and thats ok. That said shes surprisingly open and helpful

I won't deny that she's excellent at teaching jpn. Her lectures are worth it. HOWEVER she grades really strict. It's entirely possible to do homework and get a 0. Her tests and quizzes are difficult. Participation matters but only for correct answers in class. Difficult to get ahold of over email. If you're not passionate, don't take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Teaches like you're in a Japanese classroom. You should be prepared for cold calling, practice your pronunciation of phrases before class to be confident when you have to speak. She's a bit strict but is a fair grader. Will keep you on your toes. Memorization is key to this class, master it.
This class was so hard, she does not take any small mistakes and too many tests and quizzes. If u are predicting a good grade, skip her class.

YO This lady applies every Japanese school system into ours. I get that she is trying to teach us the culture but sometimes shes so extra and such a tough grader on the test. she doesnt even accept small mistakes. So my recommendation is to go for other options.

Sagawa sensei is one of the most respected professors at UCR. I love her. She's a great  professor who really cares about her students. Her teaching is easy to follow and she expects a lot out of you. However, her exams are fair since she helps you by drilling in all of the things you need to know for the tests. I had her for JPN1-6 & JPN101 series

As long as you pay attention in class, it's not a difficult class to pass. She tries to get everyone to understand, but if you don't, just go to her office and she'll help clarify whatever it is you're having trouble with. Very down to earth.
Sagawa-sensei is an excellent teacher, far superior to the professors of Japanese in this department.  Her explanations are clear, and if you ask for help, you'll get it.

She is a very difficult teacher, but inspired me to do better and try harder. Unlike her opposite Hain Sensei, she is not a complete (fill in the blank). She is a good teacher as long as you put in the effort. Once my phone rang in class and she yelled at me, it was pretty funny. Anyway stay far away from JPN if you're a business student.

If your major doesn't require you to have a high GPA, take Sagawa-sensee.  But if you're a science major trying to get into pre-health, be warned!  I would say that 80% of students receive a B or lower in here, 10% get B+, and the other 10% get A-.  Requires tons of work, but GREAT teacher for sure!  She teaches JPN really well.

Incredible teacher! Everybody gets called on to participate ~2x per day.  Bio major, took JPN to get away from boring biology. Hard to get an A, but A- is VERY do-able imo.  Class requires lots of work to take home everyday.  Class took more work than BIOL 161A (Anatomy class that all BIOL majors are scared of).  Gorgeous prof too!

Sagawa Sensei is amazing as a teacher. I have taken classes with all three of the teachers, and by far Sagawa Sensei is the best. She's funny and clear, and spends a day or more on each section of the book, depending on it's difficulty. She grades a little bit harder than the rest, but it's easy because she teaches better. She is very attractive !
Very helpful and very thorough. She does call on you often to make sure you know the material and the daily homework and occasional quizzes really does help you better learn the language.
At first she was really intimidating and it seemed like the class would be hard, but it was actually fairly easy. If you do the homework and attend class you'll do fine in the class.

Sagawa-sensei is very terse with her students but still very helpful. she can be a little intimidating but it's only because she expects a lot out of her students. all in all, she is a great teacher and her english is very clear. she is stricter than sato-sensei but i think you learn the concepts better in her class. =)

She is nice and speaks very clear English. She is a little on the hard side, but she is extremely helpful. Pay attention because you will get called on everyday. She can be quite difficult because she expects more of you (even more if you are taking an upper level class with her). Just study all the terms and review the concepts.

Expects a lot from students. It helps to read the material and get familiar with the vocab before attending lectures. Be prepared to speak in class (read and answer questions in japanese). She's a fair grader, so work hard and you'll get your A.

Has a bad reputation for being difficult, but she makes sure you understand everything whereas Hain-sensei is big on self-reliance (not saying it's bad though). Sagawa-sensei is also fiercely funny and intelligent and it's easy to grow a rapport with her. I recommend her out of all the Japanese senseis, though I've never taken Sato.

Sagawa gets a bad rep for being overly strict but I think that's all baloney. I'd say her class is just right for college students. Not only does she have a great sense of humor, but she's terrific during office hours. Basically you get what you put into the class and as long as you keep up with your work, you'll be fine. Highly recommended. ^^

Sagawa sensei is a good professor, but I think that her rules get in the way of learning, and if you fall behind, it will be very hard to catch up.  I think she is more sutable for advanced students, I learned much more in Sato's course.  Exams range from easy to bloody difficult, so be warned.  Does not curve or use a modified scale.
Very difficult, but extremely knowledgable in linguistics. Good luck if you get her.

she perfectly knows what she is teaching, and even tough she gives lots of homework, she help us improve our language skills. she is a real nice teacher and if you get into this class, YOu will know that you are not gonna regreat!! If you truly want to learn, take this class !!^^

She definitely knows what she's doing. You can tell she's experienced. She isn't an easy grader, either. If you want to ace her class, you'll have to work hard to avoid making stupid mistakes on your tests. She's stern in class and  wonderful during office hours.

Sato was MUCH easier but Sagawa teaches MUCH more effectively.  I got a B- but I feel like a learned a great deal of Japanese this quarter. If you want an A... take Sato or Hain.  But you will probably learn the most in Sagawa's class.

Sagawa sensei is very nice & teaches in a manner I can understand. She writes things on the board and is very clear. Like most language classes there is daily hw assignments, but good feedback is provided. She gives exam reviews for tests but the FINAL killed me - dropped my grade from an A to a C!

Sagawa sensei is strict, but not without reason. Drills until you understand. Very clear about the schedule, everyday we discussed the current of upcoming week/test/hw. Must be on time or you could miss a 3 minute quiz (learned the hard way).
The structure of the class isn't the same as Sato but she's nevertheless still a good teacher. It's just that I wish her notes would be more clear. But overall still a very effective teacher.
Awesome teacher, very helpful. I had a great time in her class, just turn your cell phone off in class.
Don't let your phone ring, or you'll be marked absent!  Very stern.

This was a hard class, but mainly due to the nature that it was accelerated. She was clear and answered any questions students might have. She could be a little stern at times, but never overstepped the bounds of common courtesy or politeness.
Difficult. I heard the other professor was MUCH easier.

I've taken most of the Japanese language professors, and I like Ms. Sagawa the best.  She teaches the material in a way I really understand and she understands the importance of smiling!  She really cares about kanji stroke order though.
She just really awesome.

Drills, drills, drills.  Sets a solid foundation for getting to the upper division classes by *hammering* the material into your skull.  Watch out for the occasional  special homework  bloodbaths in the classroom (I hope you can raise your hand fast).

He does not give lectures at all. All he does is to let you watch some videos and talks about himself. He never touches the readings or asks any questions based on the readings. The quiz questions are not helpful and strange. The only way for you to learn the readings is in the discussion sections where the TA clarifies some readings.

By far the worst professor I have ever experienced. Every lecture is 3-4 YouTube videos (really shows his lesson planning), asks students to discuss more than he lectures, talks about himself a TON, grades heavily on pop quizzes, and forces Chicago format on undergrads but does not go over samples or how he will grade it. I have learned very little
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He completely read off his slides which weren't helpful at all. He is a very harsh grader and lectures were boring. He spent time talking about random things too.

Professor Lake's attendance quizzes are very important. They help pull up your grade if you don't do well on the three essays. The Final essay is rough, he didn't really explain what he wanted towards both the Students and the TA's. TA's are in charge of grading so if the Professor unfairly grades your work, ask your TA to regrade. Do not take.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This prof told the entire class that he deducts 5% of a student's grade for every hour an assignment is late and that if a student wants an extension, they need to provide documentation like a police report or letter from a therapist on campus. Three essays. Switched with a different professor who was going to be teaching the course.
He is really harsh grader and his rubrics demand  a lot

Professor Lake is not bad at all he for sure isn't the best. He cares about what he teaches, which I really enjoyed as a Political Science major. Attendance is REALLY important. he has a quiz every day for lecture at random times, if you answer you get your attendance GO TO LECTURES PLS! No exams or quizzes, which I loved 3 essays, 1 final project
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall he isn't a horrible professor, he's very passionate about his topics. If you are truly interested in the class it will be enjoyable. There are only 4 real assignments, 3 essays and one final essay. There is a lot of readings and he is still new to the school so his communication with TAs can be a bit wonky.

He is a bit strict on the rubric for the short essays and maybe the final project. There are three short essays and a final you have to prepare for. Attendance Quizzes were dreadful for some because of the 5 minute gap where you can answer before it closes. It feels like he leaves the TAs' in the dark with the information and grading for the essays
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He was honestly not terrible; his lectures weren't too dull, which helped me pay a bit more attention. He would randomly assign a word of the day quiz, which, if you're on time and in class, shouldn't be an issue for you. If you're a commuter, I wouldn't take this class, though, since he doesn't really excuse late attendance.
Will close attendance in 5 minute and sets it at random times so you HAVE to show up. Easy class No midterm or Final. 3 easy short essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I needed his class bc I switched majors and he approved me to join late (he could've denied), refused to excuse attendance even though I wasn't even enrolled in the class at the time, and I had to send back and forth emails for 2 days just to advocate for myself. He said bc I joined late, I can't get an A. Graded my essay unfairly with no feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Really good professor, interesting class if you're into music and the ORIGIN of hip-hop, very little homework but insightful, has many extra credit opportunities, no midterm, final is a group project, and very manageable to do
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Easy class, but at times lectures feel boring because he just reads off slides. Sometimes he doesn't use a mic either, so you can't even hear him. The course is interesting, but he sounds so uninterested that it's hard to be engaged. Also, he disrespected Queen BoA calling her a group?!?! #APOLOGIZETOBOA
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's super chill actually just go to his class cause he cares about participation but yeah he super sweet

Super chill professor, only one small weekly assignment, no tests, and 1 midterm relating to the final and the final, which was an easy group presentation. Lectures were interesting and covered many topics and influences of music.

He was a good professor. Just make sure to complete weekly assignments. The weekly assignments provide specific reading for the short summaries. He also only grades a group project for the final and one midterm, which is a short topic proposal.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Only one quick assignment a week. No tests. Final was a group project based on anything of your choosing as long as it had something to do with music. Lectures were intriguing and covered many different aspects of music.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: hes tough, but because there's often a lack of participation. he asks for complete participation, and in a class we're paying for, i dont think that's too much to ask

This professor has long lectures about mainly abstract artist which can be boring. I do like abstract art but he talks about it every lecture. Homework wise it is very stressful with a large work load. For example you can spend a good time on an art piece but he would say this would be better if you up scaled it to the size of the room.

Professor single-handedly made me want to drop out of college. EVERY art critique there were always students who never got a chance to showcase their work (3 hour class btw..) and would have to stay late after class. Professor favors AI content and makes it very clear. He reduced the art I spent hours on to a piece "we don't have time for."

Did not do much teaching, but that's on par with what this class is since it's mostly guest speakers. Required papers weekly on each artist and was very strict with attendance, but the TA who actually did the grading was very lenient.
So much work in so little time, and criticizes when we aren't as creative as he wants.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Homework assignments and midterms are online but don't let that fool you because the final is in person and if you do bad on that, expect a C. I knew a lot of people that got B's. Lectures are beyond boring. He reads the slides word for word and has an endless number of slides. You're better off teaching the class yourself. The final was difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Friendly prof, HW w/2 attempts, midterms online. Reopened missed HW. A fundamental understanding of the processes that underlie darwinian evolution is about 80% of Li's 5C. Be warned, the final was significantly harder than the midterms, w/ some material that was not thoroughly covered in class. Test/quiz questions are occasionally confusing.

You must read textbook! You cannot get by just by reviewing his slides bc they are 40-50 slides long per lecture and some of the content on tests weren't included in them. Midterm 1 was alright, but Midterm 2 and final were a lot harder. The quizzes and curve at the end saved me. His lectures suck bc he reads the slides word for word.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I attended all lectures for this professor, and he did not lie when he said that you must read the textbook in order to get the full grasp on content for midterms. However, the final was in person and not online, and was lecture/slideshow heavy, not so much the textbook. You can do good in class if you do well on the quizzes, read, & study slides.
lectures were not helpful. final was insanely difficult and nothing like the class. midterms were both online so as long as you do well on those and get full credit on all quizzes you should be fine.

lectures were mostly useless if you did not read the textbook. midterms were conducted online, however the final was in person. the final contained almost no material from the lectures nor the textbook. it was filled with a ton of terms and case studies never touched upon during class or the textbook. overall horrible experience. good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Genuinely I have no idea where he gets his test questions from but I swear none of the stuff we learn is on the exams. Final was absolutely atrocious
GPA killer for a lot of people. Tests did not correlate to lectures at all. Had to curve a lot at the end which is the only reason I ended with a decent grade.

Long and boring lectures that are unrelated to any of the exams, very rude whenever people ask questions in class, and very slow to respond to emails. If you have this professor for Bio5c please drop and take it another time with a different professor, I wish there was someone that could've told me this before

If I could rate this man a 0, I would. Avoid!! PLEASE! His exam qs are pulled off random sites (quizlet) and have lil correlation to his lectures. His lectures are monotone and copied... He changed his exam style for our 2nd midterm so he can "determine the A students". He somehow made his exams harder then ochem exams... Overall an unfair class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is was a horrible class. He just reads off his slides that are minimum 40 slides per lecture, so it's really boring. First midterm wasn't too bad but second and final were hard. He even made the second midterm harder on purpose b/c lots of people did well on the first one??? This class was literally harder than my ochem class this quarter.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: whatever you do DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS AND I MEAN DONT EVEN IF YOU HAVE TO WAIT ANOTHER QUARTER. His exams are unrelated to the slides and the textbook so you are doomed.
Avoid him at any cost. Cannot put into words how bad his class is

Lectures are so boring because he just reads off the slides and doesn't explain anything. No matter how much you study, you won't do well because the midterm questions have nothing to do with what he teaches in lecture. Reading the textbook didn't help either. He also doesn't curve and is very rude when answering questions in class.

OVER 40 SLIDES PER LECTURE! he basically glosses over them, does not describe anything in further detail than whatever he regurgitated from the textbook word for word onto his slides. honestly sometimes felt like it was his first time seeing the content too. did not learn a thing besides the fact he is a lazy and rude professor

I cannot imagine a worse professor. Very rude, boring lectures, midterm/final have nothing to do w/ lecture content, refuses to curve. cant do well no matter how much you study/understand concepts-go to quizlet & practice those questions cause that's what he likely copy-pasted onto your exam. Avoid at all costs if you want to save your gpa

Boring and extremely condescending. Does not give practice exams (claims quizzes are practice). Exam questions are either nonsense or stolen. Anytime anyone asks a question he is very rude and says to refer to the syllabus, which never helps. Lectures are just reading off the slides or talking about his very very important research

Professor Larry Li is most likely the worst Biology 005C Professor on this campus. His lectures, while understandable, have zero correlation to the midterm exams. He is unreachable via email and is extremely rude to students who ask questions in class. He doesn't post midterm key after an exam and you have no ability to check what you got wrong.

very boring lectures, just reads off of the slides and very condescending when you ask questions. His test questions are just pulled from quizlets online. Chose harder questions for the second midterm just because we did "good" on the first midterm (the average was in the low 70s).

He reads off slides so do not have to come to monotone lecture. Never skip a quiz because he does not let you make it up. Was on track to get an A and did not get it because of one missed online quiz that everyone gets a 100% on and quizzes count a lot. Test questions stolen from the internet (can find in quizlet)

Two things about this professor. One, the professor reads off his slides in a very monotone voice. Two, his slides  (which is a summary of the textbook) and the textbook did not help prepare for his midterms. Professor deliberately made our 2nd midterm difficult since supposedly he believed our 1st midterm was "too easy."

BORING! His lectures are useless, better off reading the book and even then the midterms and final are not easy. Questions are obviously just pulled off the internet without any correlation to class material. No matter how much you study dont expect a good grade bc exams are not fair. Your grade will be saved by lots of quizzes and lab points.

Incredibly bland lecturer, only reads off of prepared slides that are summaries of  text assigned. Although grade scale is forgiving and will be brought up by lab and assigned online quizzes impact it, actually grasping material is much harder. Tests were not a good reflection of lectures or text. Professor is prompt in responding to emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: So boring as a lecturer, but u have to pay attention bc he adds a lot of stuff not on the slides. When he does use the slides, he straight up reads off of them. Quiz and midterm questions are way too complicated and a lot are on material he doesn't go over He's a nice guy though, responds to emails fast and fixes problems. Just not a good lecturer.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Condecending when asked questions, reads of slides only, don't take this Professor.

Lectures are sooo long (50+ slides without fail). I didn't go to class at all - he reads straight off his slides but I also ended up with a B+ so I would probably suggest going. He gives practice questions if you go to class but doesn't post them online so there's some motivation for going. Overall, he was an ok professor - not great, not terrible.

His lecture slides are stupidly long, which actually means you should go to the lecture, as you probably won't have the motivation to go through the 50+ slides at home. If you effectively learn by reading the textbook, then this is definitely the professor for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dude's nice and his test questions are easy. The only bad thing is his lecturing. I swear he gets his slides straight from the book. It's a struggle to even stay awake in class. If you're good at self-studying or can watch paint dry then I suggest taking his class.

Boring lectures. Has WAY too many slides per lecture and doesn't get to like 1/4th of them. Tests are poorly worded/phrased and has many typos on it. Nice guy, but it can be difficult to understand him at times (thick accent). Avoid if possible.
His notes included too much information and he was hard to understand sometimes in class. Test questions were overall easy, but some written poorly

Does the 112 series. I don't want to be mean, but after taking 112B with professor Clark, there was a massive difference in my personal engagement with the course material. Her lectures were difficult to understand at times and the workload was A LOT of reading and reflecting on textbooks. She's kind but definitely made the course feel like a drag.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: If you are not required to, do not take this class. The professor never responds to emails, is easily short-tempered with people in class, and the two-hour lectures are difficult to sit through.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This was an enjoyable class. The lectures are not mandatory but HIGHLY recommended since she doesn't post her slides. The tests rely on all of the lecture slides so thats why you have to attend class. The tests are not bad but if you study you'll be fine and the test would be easy. You only have to analyze music in this class.

Very easy class. Just attend lectures and do the assignments and you'll be fine. Quizzes are short and done in discussion and are directly from what was on the lecture slides. Slides aren't posted online, so you must attend lectures and take notes. Two assignments per week, one major project, quizzes, a midterm, and a final.

If you don't love music, don't take it! Quizzes make up a large part of the grade for this class, but the prof goes over her slides really quick during lectures and does not post slides online, making it necessary to take notes in class to do well on quizzes. Additionally, she likes to cancel office hours, so be prepared to receive no help at all!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The workload for her music history courses is unnecessarily heavy. Her teaching style needs to be updated. Her two-hour lectures get very boring most of the time, and her assignments require more time than they should. She will deduct points from your assignments if you don't meet her high-level expectations. She never replied to my emails.
