Professor McKee was very hard to understand. He would go too fast in lecture and not use up all of lecture time. Those extra minutes could be taken to slow down with the material. When I went to office hours he said "it should be in the notes" "it should be in the book". If you're a BIEN major then you're stuck with him. Good luck. READ THE BOOK!!!

Prof. McKee is a great professor that has a very straightforward class. There are homework assignments that actually enhance my ability to learn the material taught in lecture. I looked forward to his classes every week.

Lectures are pointless, yet mandatory or he won't post the notes (despite posting his notes weeks after the lecture). Misdirects students in their preparations for exams. Lecture slides are terribly organized. First time teaching the course but overall is not equipped with the skills or knowledge to teach this course.

Creeped me out by taking my phone off my desk and scrolling through it to see "what I was doing while she was lecturing." OK I get it I shouldn't have had my phone out. But that's my phone, my private messages. She fully read my very personal exchange with my girlfriend and like gave me a look. Super not OK.

Professor is monotonous. Class attendance is not mandatory although extra credit is given every once in awhile. Midterms/finals questions will be on the study guide, so study the study guide! Not much effort is required to pass this class.
She is monotone and boring. But the class is easy and there are study guides for the midterm and final. The tests are easy if you go over the study guide. Easy class just extremely boring.

She's a really nice person. The class was an easy A. Not much effort needed. Just study the lecture notes and study guides and you'll do fine. Make sure to go to lectures though cause she gives extra credit once in a while.

She is very nice. pretty easy class. She gives study guides for the midterms and the final. Just study those and do all the work in discussion. make an effort to go to class because she provided extra credit for attending class. Should get no less than a "B" in the class.

Very nice professor though her lectures can be fairly boring at times because it's all power point. As long as you study the study guides she gives you for the midterm and final it's hard to fail the class.

it would be advisable to show up for lecture on video days because she will usually take role on those days. Discussion is mandatory but the TA's are helpful.  finals are easy due to the study guide she gives and goes over. all you need for the final is to study the study guide.

I loved taking this professor and learning about slavery and the deep south. She is very flexible with her assignment due dates and always communicates with the class about how they are doing in the class. There is a decent amount of reading which is doable if you aren't taking more than 4 classes. Overall I would recommend this professor.

Do not take this class/her. This class was reading based and her lectures were recaps. Provides no clear grading criteria/a grading scale on the syllabus. As a history major this class was the bane of my existence, I wish I could go back in time and drop it. She is a funny person though I just didn't like how she 'taught' this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took a research seminar with Professor McPherson and I learned a lot. I learned how to take my research and writing to the next level. it was not easy and I had to put in the time and effort, but she was available in class, office hours and on zoom - which was great because I was in another class during her office hours. Hard work, but worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor McPherson's class was relatively straight forward mainly being graded off two essay exams and a three-part "project", but her grading is rather unclear. Despite answering all the prompt's questions and providing evidence she will knock your grade for mundane items. Feedback and direction on expectations for writing are the bare minimum.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class is definitely an easy A. The only reason I got a B- was because she's so incredibly boring. It's hard to stay engaged during lecture and she's also quiet and mumbles quite often. In class quiz and presentations every week, only to peers.

She is the best professor who has great experience in Japanese culture and literature, and there will be a lot of assignment, like weekly quizzes in class every Tuesday, weekly discussion doc post, and weekly group presentations. There is 1 essay assignment, also mid & final, but she allows open notes and reading along key terms to help you do well

Professor Mcknight is one of the kindest professors I have ever had. She is very knowledgeable and for the essays, if there is something you feel passionate about you can ask her and switch the topic to research and write about things that you like. I felt that she picked good readings that were relevant and interesting and I really enjoyed class!

Was surprised at the beginning of this year that she wasn't on here. McKnight is super chill, be conscious during class and you'll be fine, struggle with Japanese names like me and it might suck. Still easy. Readings are interesting enough to keep you awake. I emailed her about a film she mentioned in class and she replied with other recs. Nice!

Professor McKnight is very caring and knowledgeable. However she picked more eccentric pieces of literature and film to discuss. Some pieces should have come with a trigger warning. Course title may be misleading. Good person, however if you are hoping on studying mainstream Japanese literature then take curriculum at your own risk.

This class is really straightforward. Most of the class grade comes from papers, which you can get a lot of help on from the Professor or your TA, who might not grade it too hard if they are lenient. The textbook isn't really necessary and the lectures are sometimes boring but the class is essays and quizzes are really straightforward.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--SO MANY PAPERS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Bell is an incredible lecturer - very passionate and interesting. She is also very fair and gives very clear instructions for the papers. No midterms or final. Just easy quizzes based from the lecture and three papers. Work on the papers early to get feedback and you'll do great.

Professor Bell is just an average professor. She knows what she wants to talk about regarding Chinese History which is a good thing. However, she does not give lecture notes, only lecture outline so you need to take your own notes. So if you miss class, you are going to miss quite a lot. Make sure you read! Her feedbacks on paper are pretty bad too
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: The quizzes are very easy if you do the readings she posts online and attend class. The essays are graded by TAs however, and my TA (Steve) did not like my writing at all. There is no midterm or final exam so that's nice!
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--SO MANY PAPERS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Professor Bell is such a quality professor--I had her for history 20w, 182, as well as 197. I got an A in all of them.  It is really hard to find professors who balance teaching with actually caring for the students--but she is definitely available to all her students, just take the time to go to office hours and know the material. I

To be honest, if you know history and need to fulfill English 1C, take this class. It is the easiest class I have ever taken to get rid of a dumb requirement. I barely did any research and got an easy A. She basically gives you all the answers and tells you exactly what to do on the papers. Do that and you got atleast a guaranteed B.

Very interesting lectures,and the quizzes are basically from the main points in lecture and occasionally include questions from readings. Yeah there's a lot of readings and tbh I didn't do a lot of them which is why I got a C, BUT I still learned in this class and if I had given my full effort I know I would've done well. Also a lot of papers to do
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Bell cares very much about her students. She is an amazing professor! There are a lot of readings but most of the time the readings are meant to reinforce what she has on her lectures. She plays music in her class and overall her class is amazing.

There's a lot of reading each week for this class. You have to keep up with it or else you'll be lost when you do your essay. Her tests are really easy, straight from the lecture material.  Make sure you get a good TA cuz they basically grade everything. Santos is a really easy grader. Office hours are really helpful with essays :)

Easiest class ever. I went to class maybe 10 times. (It was a MWF class, 10 weeks) and easily got an A. Everyone should take this class, unless you're bad at timed writing, I heard a lot of complaints about that.
EASY! Print the lecture slides online and you'll pass. Covers two breathe requirements (History and English 1C). You have EASY essays. Stay up to date with the class you'll pass with flying colors.

OMG, EVERY PROFESSOR at UCR should learn teaching skills from professor Bell. 1. She challenges you just enough to make you work for your grade. 2. Everything is clear and straight to point (essay prompts) 3. The class is just taught and organized beautifully. Everything is clear and interesting. I recommend anyone to take this class with her.

Straightforward prompts; do your reading and GO TO LECTURE! She's clear and GREAT at lectures. Syllabus is clear cut. Gotta love these classes that tell you what you need to do. Do it and you will get an A. Bad at writing? TALK TO YOUR TA AND MEET WITH THEM! THEY GRADE YOUR PAPERS! Easy multiple choice exams! Take this class with Bell! :)

As long as you keep up with the reading and her detailed lectures, and attend your discussion section, you will get an A. Do the work, it's that simple. I had Bourbois as my T.A. and she pushed our section to actively engage ourselves. The material is interesting and easy to understand, and the final was easy for me! Good luck!

Great Lecturer. Very straightforward, follows the syllabus, gives good guidelines on essays. The only thing that can keep you from an A is the TAs who grades the essays. Best go to their office hours to find out what they really want on the essays
Very straight forward class. MC is fairly simple if you understand the main concepts. The essays require more effort, but overall Bell is always available for help.

Professor Bell was an amazing professor for Hist 20W. Her lectures were very clear and she's very organized, which really makes a difference. I also had a very nice TA: Jeno! He was very helpful as well.

Bell is nice enough, understandable prompts, for both the essays and the exams. However, Jennifer has got to be the hardest, most obnoxious grader ever.It makes absolutely no sense that all of a sudden a person's writing ability depletes so much in one class when it is top notch in other English or essay-heavy classes. The TA can make or break you.

Thorough syllabus, good essay prompts. The lectures are okay, but when it comes to mixing the Writing and History parts of the class, she did it terribly. Instead of more essays, the writing is mainly from mini essays in tests. They can KILL you if youre bad at timed essays. Even if you do well w/ the material, the mini essays can ruin you. AVOID!!

She has a thorough syllabus and the essays she asks for have pretty detailed prompts but when it comes to the midterm and finals, your grade can decline like crazy. If you're someone that isn't great with timed essays, DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS! Final includes 50 multiple choice and 5 mini-essays. I'm an English major and I regret taking this class.

A very caring instructor, very helpful if you use her office hours. This course covers a lot of material that is very difficult. Essays are very hard. Expect to spend a minimum of 6 hours per week, plus 100% attendance. If you can't, don't take the class, since your grade will be quite low! You can not rely on the exam prompts to pass.

She's great, she lectures clearly and even puts on some music before and after class! Midterm, final, and 2 papers make most of your grade. Just study those tedious terms! Also, choose a nice TA, because they grade your work!

This class was incredibly easy. It was a joke. I never attended lecture, but I got an A. All the key terms are given to you before the midterm and the final. Also, the multiple choice questions can be answered from intuition. You are not required to cite any sources other than the textbook when you write your papers.

She is very enthusiastic about teaching history, although her enthusiasm wasn't enough to motivate me to come to class. She reads off of the power points that she posts up on iLearn. I had Jennifer Weed as my TA, and she was more helpful than Professor Bell. But Jennifer is a hard grader.

She has been pretty consistent year after year it seems like. 2 papers, midterm and final. Does post lectures online. You only use the book for the paper and it's only a certain section of the book. Otherwise just know the key terms she posts up and you are good to go for the midterm and final.

Also had her for Hist 20.  Both were pretty easy classes but for 182 her lectures aren't as detailed so you might want to show up to class.  She's a bit boring but is nice and very lenient with her grading.

This class could not have been much easier. At the same time though, you learn a LOT. Professor Bell is very passionate about history, so she makes you passionate about it too. 2 papers, a midterm, a final, and all lectures are posted online. Wonderful professor.

Really specific teacher I would say. 2 papers, 1 mid term, and 1 final, if you study for it you can get an A. The papers are really specific, you have to ask her what she wants and if you do not consult her about it you are definitely going to get a C. If it important to go to class although they are somewhat boring as her voice is so monotonous.
She was so easy, honestly one of the best classes at ucr. I actually thought the class was interesting. It was 2 papers one midterm and a final, which was really easy. take her

Both exams are basically vocab-tests. Study powerpoint slides and you're set; focus on the terms at the end. Textbook is only useful for reference while writing the papers. One of the easiest courses I've ever taken. I attended lecture about 5 times and received an A. STUDY THE TERMS!!!!

This professor is a nightmare. If you attend class and study you can do ok on the tests, but she is neurotically specific on how she wants her papers.  If you have a style, voice, or way of writing that every other professor has liked, that is not a garuntee she will.  She likes her own specific style and grades on that more than content.

not TOO easy for honors bc you DO HAVE TO STUDY FOR THE FR's for the exams. can't BS them and expect to do well for the test. since THE PROFESSOR is UR TA!!!! she's a very nice lady and is knowledgeable. very helpful as well. Although she does read off of her slides, it is only bc she has too much on there. however THEY ARE VERY HANDY FOR HER TESTS

Pretty cool class; A's on exams are easy if you attend lectures; reading the textbook isn't crucial; slides during lecture tend to have way too much stuff written on them, so learn to consolidate your notes; Bell is enthusiastic about the subject, so learning is less stressful; the 2 papers aren't bad at all; overall, solid teacher, cool course.

Lectures are posted online ahead of time. Class is 2 papers, a map quiz, a midterm and a final. The papers are easy because you only need to read one chapter of about 30 pages. The book is the only source you need to write the essays. I never went to lecture, didnt keep up with the reading, and I got an A. very easy class.

This class was relatively easy as long as you attend lecutre and participate in discussion.  Lecture was great because Bell posted the notes ahead of time so you could follow along and add details without feeling overwhelmed with the writing.  I had Anne and she is not as horrible as everyone makes her seem. She doesn't take crap so don't be lazy!

Bell is a pretty straight forward teacher, even though her lectures are kinda boring. You do not need to read the textbook, I probably read no more than 2 chapters and I passed the class with a B-. There were 2 papers that I didn't read the text for. I got a 96% on the first one and an 88% on the second one. One of her TAs was mental though -_-

Professor Bell was a good teacher. I learned from her...but her TA's do all of the grading. Whatever you do do not get Anne as your TA. She is the hardest one beings that she has been professor Bell's TA for 7 years!!! Marks your down for every little mistake you make. Thank god I am done with History. I was surprised I got a C+.
Professor Bell is awesome. Her class is super easy. Her lectures are interesting. She is also really nice. I higly recommend her.
class was easy, but i did take ap euro in high school.  if you took any history class in high school and was attentive, this class was easy
DO the reading, LISTEN to the lectures --AND-- ask questions.  f you don't care, she won't bother to care about you.  It's a 2-way street, folks.

Easy class if you get the right TA, section is worth 35% and TA's get a lot of input on your grade, and some will be tough.  Passed easily without reading the book, but it is useful in writing the paper.  Tests are straight off of her lecture notes, no need to study until the time of tests.

I hated this class. toughest class i had that qtr. the lectures are interesting but kinda boring sometimes, but the music in the begining is cool. depending on the ta u get.. it can be hard. the essay are soo stupid and hard. the tests are ok but its straight from the lectures. the reading is extremely long, tedious and boring, fall bhind n ur dead
This Teacher was horrible and when i first took her class i didn't realize what she was looking for in the id's.  She wasn't really clear and i wouldn't ever take her again.
This was a great class because it was interesting and I passed!!! But yea, she's really helpful and makes you want to come to class.

I've never been so interested in History before! She is such an awesome teacher. She really loves what she teachers, so she makes it so much more interesting to learn. Don't really both with the books, besides for the papers. Her tests are straight out of the lectures. Make sure you take the time to understand her lectures, they're good.

this was a really easy class.  The midterm and final are all from slides she posts on ilearn.  Got an A without trying very hard.. Her lectures are clear and I stayed awake for more then half of them. Great Teacher, Discussions are easy as well, free points pretty much.

The fact that discussion is worth 50% of the whole grade is really stupid and ridiculous. every assignment in discussion counts. even tho the exams are easy, everything on test can be found in the lecture notes. overall, this class is alright.

Pretty easy class. Exams are straight from the notes, so you don't even need to read.  Just avoid TA Leleua Loupe, she's tough.  I did very well on the exams, but discussion is worth 50% of your grade, which is why i got an A- in the class.

If you go to class, absorb what she says during her lectures. If not, just go online and read through the ppt's. She didn't give us much to prepare for exams, but her ppt's are all you need. The online exam forums online help too. Discussion is 50% of the grade, so make sure you do all assignments.
Don't take this class because its not an easy A, but she's a good teacher though.

she is an ok professor, and donr really have to read the book but lectures notes are improtant. Try t attend all the lectures, that would at least save u for an B. Discussion is hard because it is 50% out of the total grade. Participation counts "a lot" so try to partipate every time
Some of her lectures are boring some of them are interesting. She really gives you what you need to study for the midterms and finals because her review sheets are 70 percent similar to the exams.
She likes China a lot but it's a good class and a good overview of 20th century world history. Reading is secondary to the lecutures (or at least the outlines).
She's fyne!!!
She's an ok teacher, u really don't need to go to lecture as long as you print out her notes out online.

Super nice prof overall! Weekly quizzes with half the points as attendance and questions reappear on exams. Midterm and final are 20 multiple choice and 5 SRQs. She provides a study guide and allows a cheat sheet. There is a project with assigned groups, but grading isn't too strict. 5 page statistical analysis but lots of guidance from her n TA

Professor Merolla is a fantastic professor! She is really understanding and sweet. There is quite a bit of reading, and you do have to answer questions based on the readings. However, the readings are informative and enjoyable! Do not procrastinate! Or u will fall behind on the assignments assigned on TopHat. Do the work!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: You will have to do a group project ( Usually a negative). There seemed to be a considerable amount more reading in her class than other POSC classes I have taken, most of which I found to be a slog. Open book/notes tests (DURING COVID/ONLINE). She is overall a "better than average professor" and a very understanding/compassionate person.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor is solid about the content. She wants to encourage collaborative group work and does assign group work. She does post slides and gives good study guides. The assignments are all doable and she offers opportunities for assignments redo's and extra credit. It is hard to get an A though. She makes it easy to get B-/B's but harder to get A's

PBPL100A: Probably the easiest upper div in public policy, pay somewhat attention in lecture and study for the midterm/final and its a free A. 

PBPL100B: Harder concepts than 100A but still not too bad. 

PBPL132: Please actually never take this class, it is so boring and the problem sets are way longer/harder than his 100 series problem sets.

PBPL 100A; this professor is amazing. He cares about his students and is accessible and helpful outside of class. The material was challenging for me because it was my first time using RStudio. He took time to explain things multiple times and always did his best to help me understand. 1 midterm, 1 final, 5 homework assignments, don't miss class

Amazing professor! Super knowledgeable and passionate about water issues. You'll learn a lot not just from lectures, but also from class discussions and assignments. Very inspirational and always willing to help outside of class. I walked away with a understanding of water problems and real-world solutions. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: My only complaint is that the rubrics provided for writing assignments aren't very clear, but he is very accessible if you have any questions. If you want to get an A, then you can't miss assignments, and need to put in work to fully understand the material. It is very policy oriented, and you need to read, write, and learn accordingly.
very hard professor. not worth taking this class, avoid! tough grader as well. i would avoid always.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is a kind and inspirational professor of discusses the water issue and the economics of water resources and management, his assignments are 4 problem sets and there are mid-term and final exams also there are polls everywhere quiz which we had to do in every class related to reading which some of the reading material are very long so be careful.

The class consists of 1 quiz every week, 1 midterm, and 1 final. All multiple choice. There are also problem sets which I DREADED every week. They take hours to finish. The class is not hard at all it just takes a lot of time and is super boring. Lectures felt days long. However, the Professor is approachable and willing to work with you.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Unfortunately this woman is absolutely bonkers. Interesting class but poor quality person as a professor made it unbearable.

It is clear they care about student success, going as far as individual student test corrections due to the TA grading incorrectly. The midterms and homework count for a significant portion of your grade, but consist entirely of concepts discussed during class. Office hours are very open to questions if they arise.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I just finished ME134 with this instructor. New professor but always asking for feedback and shows she cares her students are learning. Lectures have been engaging throughout remote and in-person instruction, while also being accommodating by offering recordings (with good quality as well). Homework is manageable yet informative. Would recommend.

Extremely helpful to answer questions in class and in office hours; really wants the students to learn and will help you get there. She's the type of Professor to try and understand why you asked the question in order to see what knowledge was missed. Class was fair with clear solutions posted to study from.

Enthusiastic but lied about making his own slides/exams. Slides copy pasted from book - don't bother reading book. 50% / exam (not cumulative). 4% EC for doing HW in discussion. Gave 10% EC for answering questions from nobel prize lectures on final. Lied about a 20% curve (no curve). Professor says everything is important for exam (not true).
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor was definitely enthusiastic about the topics, but the overall class was not great. Miscommunication all around regarding different things like the test, regrades, and curve. The tests contained weird questions from the textbook, so make sure to do the practice questions from it. It is possible to excel, but be sure to put time in.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Disorganized class structure, frequent miscommunication between Dr. Chen, students, & TAs, and lazy instruction. Lied that he created the slides and exams when he copy pastes from the book. Ignored rampant cheating. TAs didn't share resources across sections. TA beef. Soft-spoken even when mic-ed. Told us to "study everything". Graded on 2 exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very unorganized class, TAs hid information from each other's sections, exams were regraded but new scores thrown out, professor was not present during finals. Otherwise I would expect these issues to iron out in future classes. Dense lectures but prof is caring and shows genuine interest in teaching. Exams 3/4 MCQ 1/4 FRQ, gives lots of EC.

This class was messy. His 1st time teaching CBNS101 and it shows. TAs had beef, didn't address ppl cheating which created an unfair playing field. Dense lectures, slides copy-pasted from txtbk w/ blocks of wordy text. Says to "know everything." Exams use publisher q's he doesn't review beforehand. Cheat sheet barely helps. No structure/real support
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors I had in a while. Attendance isn't mandatory but he explains the slides pretty well so should go. He's also very charismatic, great attitude and super helpful. Honestly wish all professors were like him! Dont be shy to ask for help, he always answers with a smile and with great attitude. Class is hard, but manageable.

Prof is energetic, kind, and a pretty good lecturer. He's very easy to reach out to and respectful when giving help. The lectures are tough for sure and very dense, and Dr. Chen's exam questions can often be pretty tough. But he's fair and gives you a pretty good heads up on what kind of material will be tested. Would take again.

Dr. Chen is an excellent professor, very nice, respectable, and always willing to help! However, be warned the material for this class is HARD. Especially if you have no previous molecular bio knowledge or lab experience, be prepared for a challenge. The midterm is fairly difficult, final I thought was easy (was online).

Very passionate professor but he is not good at teaching. Points out important things in lecture which is the only reason I went. Midterm and final were very difficult and test questions/wording are confusing. Homework is not similar to tests. Not a horrible professor but avoid if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: You can tell he is very passionate about molecular biology, but his lectures were difficult to understand because his lecturing skills are weak. The TA was barely helpful and his final was REALLY HARD. He does give a cheat sheet but it's basically pointless. He gives out homework and problem sets, which honestly were nothing like the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: It shows Prof Chen truly loves his field and understands subject material. He welcomes questions in class and does not mind rephrasing explanations if they are not clear, he's so nice! He always highlights things to pay attention to for the midterm/final. Disc worksheets are similar to test short answer questions. He allows cheat sheets for tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Clear expectations. He makes it a habit to mention what will be on the exams and what he considers particularly important to know for a future career as a research or medical professional. Although the subject matter can be somewhat dull, he makes the lectures engaging and relevant. You can tell that he is very passionate about teaching.

Dr. Chen is a great professor, he is very knowledgeable & was able to answer any question asked during lecture. He also tells you what he will put on the midterm and final which helps a lot, it shows he cares and wants you to do well! Although the lecture material can get boring sometimes, he is very enthusiastic about the topic which is admirable.

Professor Robbins was a great professor. Her lectures clarified all the material, and she was also helpful during office hours. Your grade is based on the research proposal, midterm, final, and lab assignments. She also gave an extra credit opportunity and gave midterm corrections. Overall, she was a great professor and I would recommend her.

She is a really great professor and explains the material clearly so that everyone can understand it. There was a midterm and a final, multiple choice questions, they weren't difficult nor easy. The research proposal was very challenging, you should start working on it early. Don't leave assignments for last minute. Overall she was a good professor

I do not understand why she has low reviews. She was very caring and patient. She tried her best for everyone to understand the material. The midterm and final were not easy or hard, they were challenging but doable. If you had questions, she wouldn't make you feel dumb.

Your grade is basically entirely up to your TA. Please try on your discussion assignments and start on your research proposal early or else you'll be stressed writing a 10-page paper with lots of sources. She allows corrections on midterm, but honestly the class is easy up until the exams and paper-- Nothing else counts for much in the grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Your grade is based on 2 exams and one research proposal. It was okay but the exams were based on scenarios and although her lectures did help it's important to ask lots of questions and go to every discussion section because even when you miss one you'll be behind. Overall, shes ok to take, pay attention during lecture!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Your grade largely depends on your TA. You have 1 research proposal to write and your TA grades. I would recommend going to lectures because she elaborates more during lecture. Her definitions are convoluted and contradicting so that is the one con about her. There is no homework/anything tedious. She is a bit insensitive, but she's not bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's an okay professor, but she does have an attitude if you ask her too many questions. Can be kind of rude if you bring up something she already mentioned which is annoying because that's what professors are for.

She literally never responds to emails and doesn't seem to understand that students are struggling outside of class. She's more willing to talk about the sort of inconvenience a student that needs help may bring than actually help that student succeed in her course. She doesn't care at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: worst professor I've ever had at UCR

Professor Robbins was an amazing instructor for this rigorous class. She was extremely knowledgeable in the subject of research methods and would eagerly answer any questions students had during lecture. Grades were based on a midterm, final, research proposal and lab assignments. She truly cares and gives plenty of opportunities to ask for help.

This class was super lecture-heavy. She would *sometimes* post slides but with a ton of blanks so you have to go to class. She uses a dense book for test questions. Grades from a midterm, labwork, a research proposal, and a final. Overall very difficult and it seemed like she just wants to challenge students/doesn't care much about assisting
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This professor is very strict about sticking to the syllabus: no extra credits, and no grade negotiation at all!!! Paper and exam weighted 75% of the class, so unless you can ace those exams and paper, or else it would be hard to get an A. The professor would also often forget to post ppt slide up on ilearn.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class was for sure a lot of work. If you aren't confident in your writing, you will need to work hard. Make sure you go to her office hours because one-on-ones with her are really helpful, especially with how much material is taught. Overall you need to work hard for the grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great professor. Very clear and thorough but doesn't overload with difficult and useless information. She is very sweet and wants everyone to do well. Midterm wasn't bad. Based mainly off of lecture slides, only a bit on the book. Haven't taken final yet. But would definitely take her class again.

Mr. Rahman is engaging as a lecturer. He is always friendly and approachable, and I can easily ask him questions during and after his lecture. He is also enthusiastic about the topics. He also considers his students workloads and makes the coursework less stressful by moving the deadlines for assignments if they overlap with exams.
Don't miss out easy points on the labs or assignments! VERY fair grader : )
Trust me, he is a teacher who truly cares. He motivates you to bring out your best, that you did not even know existed. Improved my overall performance in a way that truly surprised me...

Amazing professor who truly cares about his students. One of the best professors Ive ever had at UCR. He is super nice and caring and tries his best to make sure every student does well and understands the material. If you show up to class, youre pretty much guaranteed an A. 100% recommend taking him for CS006 and any other classes he offers.

I honestly don't know where to start Professor Rahman. He is the kindest and most caring professor that I've had at UCR. He really cares about his students and goes out of his way to ask exactly what is confusing. He teaches in a manner that is clear and his powerpoints are easy to follow. I would recommend him to everyone who wants to learn CS!

Very kind professor that cares about his students' futures and success. He was always helpful when it came to any questions anyone had. Do not worry about your grade in this class. If you show up to lecture, do the labs, and do fairly well on the quiz and try your best on the final project, he will take care of you.

I have to really say hes probably my fav professor this quarter! Yeah we had a weird final project that paired us up with randos but to be fair, the class is extremely easy. Thats probably the easiest final ive ever had. Although off topic, the book was interesting and inspirational. Overall this professor means well and wants you to pass! :D

He is a great professor, actually cares about his students and wants them to succeed more than just getting a grade. He wants his students to be better off before he came to them. Labs all build off each other so if you do the first one wrong the rest will also follow. Quizzes are easy and straight from slides. Very nice person in general.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: A very kind guy, but has many fundamental flaws as a professor. Assigns biweekly labs with zero in class instruction. Put students into a group for a project and facilitated no class time to meet with group members. The subject of the presentation had nothing to do with computer science. I took a CS class in high school and learned nothing new
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: he is a great professor I definitely recommend!!!

I know professor Rahman, was a very caring, understanding professor. He was still learning as a educator, and I believe he did the best of his ability to try and teach the class. He is a good grader, and cares about his students. 10/10 would recommend.

I had a bad experience with this class, I felt he didn't understand the students and where they were coming from. He has a strong accent so you have to pay attention. The quizzes are easy (straight from the slides) and he doesn't "teach," he just reads of old slides. attendance does matter in his class. he doesn't stick to syllabus well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class itself is easy. 5 quizzes (1 drop quiz), 5 labs, 1 group presentation. Quizzes are pretty easy since they're straight from the powerpoint/ lectures. He doesn't teach you how to do the labs in class. The final presentation pairs you up with 9 strangers to present on a completely irrelevant book from the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: The class is pretty straight forward, 5 quizzes (drops the lowest quiz grade), 5 labs, and 1 group presentation (5 minutes). The quiz questions are straight from the lecture slides and they're multiple choice. The TAs create the labs and the prof does not teach you how to do them in class, so your best bet is going to TA office hours for labs.

My most favorite Professor at UCR! I attended every class because the professor was interesting, funny, and engaging and his energy and passion was always there so I was very motivated to come to every lecture. The material was presented in an interesting way because it related back to our lives and the current news. Super nice and approachable.
Great professor who explained the concepts in detail. Went over real life examples which made the concepts much more easier to understand. Definitely would take the class with him again!

Professor is really caring, he pushes you to get good grades for class, he is hilarious, an easy A if you study , be careful to choose your parnter. Assignments a bit hard to understand but doable. Would definitely take him again.

He doesn't teach very well; basically gets his information from geeksforgeeks or other websites. He has a heavy accent, which may make it difficult to understand what he says. But, overall, he's a funny guy, and he really cares for his students. The lecture is really easy, but the assignment is really hard. Pick your partner wisely.
She is a great professor and she made participating seem easy for introverts!!
Took this course for winter '26. I really enjoyed her class. She lectures on real-world scenarios. As long as you show up, participate, and pay attention during lecture you will pass the class.
Very enthusiastic and not a hard course but definitely go to class as attendance matters. She's very caring and she's a baddie! BADDIE BADDIE O CLOCK. I recommend the class
Love love love her! The class was great and even at 8, she was always enthusiastic and engaging. Super recommend taking her.

Amazing and caring professor I enjoyed taking her class! She was very helpful and made sure I understood the material and always had an answer to my question. Projects were not that bad either, just do your work and ask for help as she loves to make sure you succeed. She's pretty  and helpful, Thank you for a great quarter Professor!

She's a great professor, she's engaging and cares about her students. She makes sure we understand the material and it does consists of 3 quizzes and a lot of group work/projects and small reading reflections for HW. Always enthusiastic. Attendance also matters. She's a ice and baddie approachable professor
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Truong is knowledgeable and works hard to make the class engaging for students. The grade is based on a lot of things. The two most important are the quizzes and group project. The quizzes are pretty hard if you don't read the articles close enough but she does hint at which ones to focus on. Overall one of the better electives.

Professor Truong is really caring of students. She is also very passionate about what she teaches and always tries to get everyone engaged. It was a really fun class mainly because the things we learned about, we can see it and apply it in personal life. There's a lot of group assignments but she gives you time in class to do some of it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She is a caring professor and today was our last day and I am going to miss this class. She was very engaging and truly cared about her students. I recommend anyone to take this class, but there is a lot of group work and a group presentation!
Great professor! I wasn't super excited about the course but it is probably my favorite class at UCR. Grade is made up of group project, quizzes, reflections, two assignments, and participation.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: One my favorite professors! Really passionate and enthusiastic about what she teaches.

Barley passed this class do to his picky grading that made no sense and mark me wrong on the smallest mistakes.He has mini quizzes everyday which is very annoying. The class is easy but his grading criteria made me almost fail don't take this professor. Not a beginer friendly class I'v studied hirigana and katakana before and still barley survived.

Sensei Miura was a great language teacher. To people who already don't speak another language besides English, you might find his class a little challenging. Since I already knew how to speak Korean and English fluently this class was fairly easy. He gives a lot of homework almost every single day, and make sure you read the textbook.

Miura sensei makes the class environment really chill. Compared to other Japanese classes I've been in, I did not really feel stressed taking this class. He was really fun and let us watch Japanese videos during tadoku to practice listening. He's soft spoken and understanding and overall a cool guy. We had a group project and a book report!

Study the assigned textbook readings, take notes of his lecture slides and study those, review the assigned homework. Class seems easy at first but will get more difficult starting Lesson 2 or 3, so don't slack. Practice is important. Prof is a cool guy. Grading seems fair, but you will have to put effort into class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: This is an easy class. You just need to study a little. However, Professor Muira messes up a lot by assigning the wrong homework, forgetting what he lectured on the day before, etc.

Great teacher that will take his time to help you out if you need it. Lots and lots of quizzes that he will tell you about. Pretty easy to get into A-B grade range for work but he makes you work for that A+ by nitpicking everything once your work gets into that range. I'd easily take a class with him again.

He is a tough grader that likes to give out pop quizzes almost everyday. The material is easy, but he makes you work for it. Sensei is a great teacher and I had fun in his class. I would take him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Prof. Miura's class is very structured. It begins with a quiz, then he lectures using PowerPoint, then in between he has us participate using our textbooks and with our classmates in activities. Grading is clear but he is a strict grader when it comes to spelling and grammar errors. His oral exam was the hardest, use textbook to study for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Miura sensei is an amazing professor!! He made learning Japanese a lot of fun, and his exams are very fair. I would take him again in a heartbeat if I had the chance

Miura-sensei is extremely nice, helpful, and funny. You will have homework every day, attendance counts, and there a lot of mini-quizzes (but he will let you know before). It is Japanese, so you will have to put in the effort to learn the material and get an A. Sensei is such a lovely teacher though, so you'll definitely enjoy the class.
If you don't go to lectures, you're going to struggle in this class. She doesn't give any study guides and I had a TA who graded super harshly. Her exams are pretty hard if you don't study ahead.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class is hard. Lectures are optional but you'll miss a lot of information if you don't go since the slides are just outlines. There is a lot of reading. Exams are all cumulative. The research paper is difficult but TAs give a lot of feedback. Professor Michalska is very nice though. She is passionate and responsive to student feedback.

One of the best professors at UCR! Her class was tough lectures were optional, grades came from discussions, tests, and one paper but it was so rewarding. Show up, work hard, and you'll learn not just about the subject, but also about yourself and others. Truly inspiring!

Dr. Michalska is patient with in-class questions, but not as accommodating w/ office hours. She scares you on exams but they're not bad- you DO need to read assigned articles, its on the tests; MC and SAQ. Recommend making your own study guides since she has none. Her slides are a bit all over the place so attend lecture and you'll do fine.

Professor Michalska is clearly passionate which makes her a great teacher. Lecture is very important you cannot do well without them because her slides give little to no information and lectures are not recorded. Though they are not mandatory she makes the class impossible without them. The material is easy if you study and pay attention.

Dr. Michalska is a great professor! Her lectures are very informative and clear, & her TA Jordan is amazing & a very easy grader as well! There are 3 tests & one 5 pg paper. She offers EC as well. She doesn't always upload her lecture slides so it's best to attend lectures. As long as you try, you'll definitely get an A+. She's very caring as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Only take this class if you truly can study alone with the material given or genuinely want to learn Socioemotional and personality development. study ahead of time and consistently stay on top of your work because her instructions are the worst. She personally did not address many issues in the class and handed it off to the TA's. there's more

She was really inconsiderate & terrible w/ responding to emails. Makes excuse of inbox exploding when other profs goes through the same thing & responds reasonably. TA Eleanor Collier is a harsh grader, introduced us writing assignment at the very last min, comes to class late, & never responds to emails. Proceed class w/ caution or avoid if u can.

Takes a very long time to respond to email. Isn't considerate of the different circumstances the students might be going through during covid. Gives extra credit to students who went to lecture but doesn't take into fact that some students may have unstable internet and situations at home. Unfair to those that are in harder circumstances.

This professor is great! She seems to really care and is passionate about what she teaches. My only complaint is that the material she teaches is all things I have learned in other classes. This isn't a bad thing if you want an easy A! I got 100% on the midterms and finals and I did not go to class often.

She really cares. Her lecture slides are brief outlines so you have to go to class to learn the material enough for the tests. She typically has one or two articles to read then it gets tied into lecture or her TAs do it during discussion. Overall a great professor and she's super accessible if you need help. You'll have one essay 3-5 pages not bad

Professor is nice but make sure you have a better TA because this class have discussion worth 30% and if you miss 1 -2 classes then too bad you will get F in your participation points. Drop this class if you think your TA is horrible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: every lecture, you have to read new articles. The material for this course is really important. Cant miss class otherwise you miss a ton of information.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She was very caring towards all of the students. She honestly wants us all to learn something. She likes to make students talk, especially if they do not know the answer. Its not to be mean but by making them talk it out she believes that it helps them learn. She is a very sweet lady and is very passionate about her area of study. I loved her class

Dr. Michalska / Psyc161: She actually cares about us doing well and learning so she formats the tests to be cumulative but they aren't hard at all if you pay attention in class. I finished my final in 30 min and still got an A (and I'm not a genius or anything). Go to lectures to have chance of earning extra credit. Very respectable professor.

Very nice, professor. The syllabus is clear about what is expected, and he is open to any questions. The lecture meets once a week to discuss readings and your internship experience. Class discussions and participation are a must. I would feel bad for him when no one would talk, so please talk. He does struggle with tech problems but nothing bad.

Very Nice and is very passionate about the material. He is also very flexible about meeting during office hours. The class is HARD though. He expects you to understand it right off the bat even though the readings are dry and impossible to understand. He also doesn't give clear instructions on the assignments and has you guessing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: VERY knowledgeable! He is very patient and passionate about theory. He isn't very organized and this caused me a lot of stress throughout the semester. We had a paper worth (30%?) and he hardly gave us instructions on it. You kind of have to guess what he wants. HUGE ISSUE throughout the semester. He is very accessible tho so no excuses!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nice guy! Pre-recorded lectures when I took him. Assignment due every week so you have to keep up with the readings/lectures. You NEED to get the main points of the material. Weekly "discussion" classes that are optional but recommended to go to since he basically goes over the rubrics for the assignments. I had an awesome TA too.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I really liked taking class with Dr. Medearis. He posted asynchronous lectures and held optional discussions using PollEverywhere for participation options. There was weekly take home quizzes and 3 essays. He was super accessible outside of class in office hours and is obviously passionate about democratic theory. He made it obvious that he cares!

The class is okay rn. Three 3 page papers, 4-5 quizzes (take home). Gotta watch the lectures and do the readings, or else the theories won't make sense. No final, no midterms, and he can be easily reached at office hours. I find the smaller assignments a bit tough since they're due every week, but the grading is generous enough. Hope thaishelps
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. M was organized, intelligent, and kind; and I looked forward to every lecture. Professor M did something rare, and actually made me think. Not every class forces a student to think about the way things are, however this class did. Additionally, Professor M cared about our class. Not to mention that his lecturers were very easy to follow.

Solid professor, kept the lecture interesting and informative. I could pay attention without falling asleep. the textbooks he used weren't too expensive, and they're a decent read. His papers were fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Professor Medearis is a great professor. He enjoys speaking with his students so go to office hours or speak with him before class. He is super approachable. He is also the Chair of the DEPT. so if you want to go to postbac school, make sure he knows you! Speak up! Ask questions, and see your TA at office hours since they do the grading!

Professor Medearis is passionate about teaching and encourages his students to really attend lecture and complete readings in order to understand his lectures. Reading and attending lectures are VERY important to pass the class! His papers have easy prompts, but require thinking and sources from the books used in class to make your thesis clear.
His lectures aren't really useful and he is very vague about exams. Hardest class I've ever taken.
doesn't post lectures and doesn't allow google docs. Hard class, lots of reading, hard grading

Medearis is a bit pretentious, you mainly see that when students ask him in regards to gradingexams. He was not very clear on how exams were going to be like, especially the first one. He would often not answer straight, and give off answers. Also grading took a while. We did not receive our first exam grade until  week 8,.

Medearis is awesome! By far, my top professor in the department. He is very helpful when you approach him during office hours.  Also, he likes getting class input on themes and scenarios. If you read before class, you'll find it more enjoyable. 3 papers, fairly graded (3pg, 5pg, 7pg).  He grades the final so make sure to brush up on readings.

Professor Medearis really encourages everyone to participate during lectures. You'll get more out of the class if you speak your piece on the subjects we discuss. Two papers, one midterm. You get quizzes if you don't read or engage in the discussion section. It's easy if you do the readings and you're interested in philosophy or moral issues.

Vey nice guy but a little pretentious. He assigns three 5 page papers and goes quite fast in his lectures. If you read the book you'll understand the final and the midterm! Pretty easy class but alot of writing.

This isn't the easiest class, but it's a definite must for any political science major. You'll go over Kant, Rawles, Hegel, and Marx, so basically the big wigs of modern western politics. His lecturing isn't the most exciting, but he makes these translated authors understandable. He's way more helpful 1 on 1 so go to office hours!

Mr. Medearis knows his stuff but not very clear on what he expects you to learn.  He's very knowledgeable but not a good teacher. The midterm results were given back 1 day before final, not the grader's fault, likes to micro-manage. Not worth buying Stiglitz & Posner. Not sure how I got B? Take home mid, class mid, & final.
He is a very nice, helpful prof.  He is extremely smart and knows his stuff, so sometimes he lectures above the student's heads.  However, he is always willing to help.  Highly suggest.
Interesting class. Easy assignments for easy credit.

Great professor. Very detailed and explicit. He doesn't post notes or uses slides, but his talking is enough. It's a thought-provoking class, however, I didn't finish all the books and I still managed to get an A- in the class. Take very good lecture notes and go to lecture, because if you miss one, you can easily get lost.

the best lecturer in the Posc department. But he is  extremely meticulous, which means, if you miss one class, you are going to feel lost. Only take him if you are willing to work hard and earn your grade.hes a great lecturer but the material is so dense that you really need to put in the effort. which is code for his class is a pain in the a
Good professor..really knows the material and provokes thought. His "incentives" and Capt. Morgan poses are amusing lol. This course seemed easier than his POSC 5 class.
Not bad, not great.  Dull lecturer--insists on wasting your time with "filler lectures".  Material, however, is fairly interesting and diverse in content.  Exams are moderately difficult.

Medearis isn't too bad. He does sometimes lecture you to sleep but he does know the material. A lot of people didn't come to lecture and they prolly are the ones that were in trouble on the tests.His midterm and final required you to know the material(I didn't read much just went to lecture and I got a B).His second paper topic was tough(on Burke)

Poor in class presence. Does little to keep students interested in material. Too much reading for breath requirment class. Hard, vague exams that do not follow any method or maddness. Does not work well or instruct TA's in the least.

seems to be knowledable, too bad he doesn't know how to apply his knowledge to lectures. very vague lectures and uses same notes for weeks. monotone voice will put you to sleep. hard exams, need to read a lot! expects a lot from tests even though he doesn't help understand the material better. avoid this class at all costs!

Clear, helpful, kind, and interested.  Wants students to learn.  Goes out of his way to encourage.  Classes are boring.  Material can be overwhelming, but he explains in a way that it is understandable.  Attend lecture and go to office hours.  Highly recommend this professor.
so borring. fell asleep every class
Very nice guy...  He actually brought krispy kreme donuts & candy for the class!  Will take his time to explain the subject to you no matter how long it takes.

This Professor was truly intelligent, really interesting and motivating. I highly recommend his class even if you are not a Poli. Sci major because you will come out a bit smarter and interested in the material.  Really great professor!

Although the requried reading material can be quite difficult, he always repeats the main points over and over.  The writing prompts for the essay and final can be quite difficult though, and the questions on the midterms can be pretty confusing.

Very good professor. He really knows his material. Very helpful and makes things clear for his students. Class was boring. Thank god Im not a Poli. Sci Major but for the time being, it was a very easy and interesting class. A lot of essays but way easy prompts. I got an A

BORING lectures!!!! Goes over the same stuff over and over. No need to read the books and still pass the test with an A. Easy midterms, paper and take home final if your really good at b.s. I recommend him cuz the class is super easy, and get Gary Goodman as ur t.a.
awesome.  actually brought dounuts to office hours.  sharp guy and nice.
Very nice guy, great lecturer.
go to his lectures and TAKE NOTES!!!  clarify the topics w/ ur TA is also important.  if u do all that...his tests will come easy
Incredibly intelligent. Papers were graded unfairly (by TA's). They don't give much guidance and you get docked points if you fail to mention something that they think is important.
Really intelligent. Knows his material, and expects students to do the same. Im not sure how I will end up in this class (grade-wise) but I still did learn alot.

Smart guy really knows his stuff can pass the class without even reading the 6 books that he assigns just take VERY detailed notes. His tests come straight out of lecture, paper topics are kind of diffucult. Then again that depends how your TA grades.
Great teacher, creates an excellent forum for discussion within the actual lecture hall.  A total recommendation.  Very fun to talk to out of class as well.
Very difficult teacher, but a great professor, really knows his material very well.  Also is very willing to talk to you one-on-one if you need help.
Boring lecture.  I always fell asleep.  Lots of reading, but the tests aren't THAT hard.  Essay midterms/final.
Nice guy.
Good professor. Involves the student in the lecture, which makes the learning environment more fun.
No MT or final.  Just two essays.  He's a hard grader so prepare to write a really good paper.  He gives krispy kreme during class for participation.  He's pretty nice.

Hard Tests and essay topics, but he's really nice and he tries to get students involved during lecture, so if you actually pay attention, it's not boring.  He even gives out candy sometimes.  (Never blew up about cell phones in my class)
