She is an entertaining professor. Lectures are mandatory and attendance is taken with clickers. Class consists of 4 tests which are based on the terms of a study guide she provides. Just study the terms and you will be fine. Textbook is heavily used. Extra credit is awarded by the amount of clicker questions you get correct during lecture.

The low rating's ironic because the professor actually isn't that bad. It's true there isn't a curve, but the grading is proportioned evenly. She gives extra credit via clickers and is very funny. A huge recommend if trying to take a pretty easy psych class.

This class is really interesting. Professor Murray is pretty funny sometimes too, so lectures aren't that bad.Lectures are mandatory because of clickers. Gives out extra credit, and there are 4 midterms(no final) nothing cumulative. Not curved though, but the class is pretty easy
One of the most interesting classes I have ever taken. Prof Murray is very funny and enthusiastic. Tests were not hard, she gives us a study guide.

Dr. Murray has been teaching at UCR for quite some time, and is an advocate for persons of color.  I find many of the reviewers previous to me to be biased against her.  She is a very charismatic professor, with a clear understanding of the material.  She encourages students to collaborate on studying for her exams.

Horrible teacher. Has unnecessary racial undertones in a lot of what she says. Repeats her prepositional phrases and the last three words of every sentence. Occasionally describes psychological conditions without any sense of gravity of seriousness. Only good thing was that the class was super-easy, plenty of extra credit, should be semi-easy.

I did not enjoy this class one bit. She makes you bring psychology scantrons to every single lecture instead of a clicker. Her lectures were unclear and I didn't buy a book. I ended with a B-, because I wasn't able to follow her lectures nor her tests.
The Murray hate is amusing. Extra credit is handed out like candy, there's no HW, and the exams are straight forward. An easy A if you want it.

She's a funny nice lady. attendance is mandatory because she has daily clicker questions and some extra credit clicker questions. There no homework besides studying. Ask your TA for help, they know whats on the exam! study the study guide and you will get an A

She's a nice lady, but needs to cut the racial slurs out of her lectures. Very easy A. Just go to class and get your clicker points and attendance, go to discussion and get those points, and do the study guides. You'll get an A no problem. Everything on the study guide is on the test. Utilize your TA cause they know what's up.

What people say about her is not true... she is a super easy A if you know all the key terms on her study guide, you'll obtain a good grade. She also gives extra credit. Overall, I only did the study guide and got an easy A. Oh yeah attendance is mandatory because of clicker questions which are super easy as well.

Dr. Murray is an interesting teacher. She has been teaching at UCR for a long time, and is very passionate about her work. She is very conceited and lazy about helping students. Prefers students to kiss up to her. Test are very tricky. Sometimes she will give you a grade you dont deserve. If you fight it, she will change it. Pay attention in class!

Attend lecture and pay attention to what she says more than what's on her lecture slides. She tends to go off her stories more than material. Whatever is on the study guide KNOW all those terms and ask you TA, they will be more than helpful. She is funny during lecture sometimes though, overall I had an alright experience with her though.

Dr. Murray's class will change your entire mindset depending on how you interpret her lectures. Her lectures are interesting and funny, and her tests are EASY, just take notes and skim readings and you'll be fine. Only problem is that she is not very available to help you outside of class (i.e., office hours/email).

Prof Murray, is a clear teacher but very unhelpful, and made me feel uncomfortable in her class as a white girl. She was very pro-black which is fine but always insulted all the white children as often as she could. When I approached her for help  she ignored me (emails) or said my questions were stupid ( when asking for help on a paper)

To be honest, Professor Murray has her ups and downs. In lecture she can be funny and you do learn in her class but there is no curve and class is mandatory. she's definately not approachable. She once stated she likes making people feel uncomfortable. But yeah, just pay attention in class and take notes. You should be fine.
She is an awesome teacher!!!! Never a dull moment with her!! On the edge of your seat!

She is that bad of a teacher that everyone says she is. You really have to try in this class to get a good grade since she does not curve. Her lectures are mandatory, but they are quite interesting. Her tests are simple if you listen carefully and really understand the terms that she gives you on the study guide.

Professor Murray provided us with all the materials we needed to be successful. With hard work and a lot of studying, a good grade is attainable. Her course is designed to push you to work harder than usual, and think outside of the box. She is a wonderful Professor and anyone who says otherwise just needs to apply themselves.

most incompetent professor i have ever come across. any positive rating on this page is most definitely written by murray herself, as she's made very clear in lecture that she thinks that highly of herself.

People on here that say she's awful are probably people who don't really try. Sooo..this is an upper division course..so yes you will have work. BUT she includes stories that help you remember. Do your work and engage in the material and you'll do great! She's a great professor!!!

By far the worst professor I've ever had. She is horrible at making exams. Many questions on exams are very debatable. Does not curve at all. Which basically means.. your screwed. Flips slides without giving time for students to write down notes. Must buy scantrons cause she doesn't believe in clickers. So basically, avoid her cause she sucks

Very unclear professor. has racial undertones in her lecture. and sounds like she doesn't know hot to teach. attendance is mandatory. Tests are tricky. First test, the average was a D. very unprofessional. pass on this professor
I think this Prof is the best!!!!!!!!!!!!! All the test are based on her notes!!! :)

Dr. Murray ISSSS awesome!!!! :D um. the class was pretty easy. 3 midterms, she's CRYSTAL clear on what she wants. 2 essays too... not bad. i LOVE social psyc and she's really animated and enthusiasmatic and funny. i love her :)

AMAZING teacher.  If you actually engage yourself in the material, it's really easy, social psych is after all mostly common sense.  She's really understanding about circumstances beyond your control.  She's very very fair in everything and as long as you pay attention and read and focus, you'll do well.  You get out of the class what you put in.

Ok I don't know why some of these people are posting the negative comments about her but I got an A in her class and I put forth very minimal effort. The only people who are complaining about her are the ones who didn't go to class, and got the grade they deserved. She offers plenty of extra credit, so there is no way to not get a good grade.
i'm going to be straight up honest. every comment before mine is true. DO NOT TAKE HER. i won't even bother elaborating, because everyone already said everything. trust them.

THE WORST TEACHER I'VE EVER HAD. She is immature, mean, inconsiderate and disrespectful against other races. She has low self esteem so she reflects it upon her teachings in class. CLICKERS are a MUST and don't ever get caught using two. I don't think she taught me anything at all in this class. It is a waste of time and money. DO NOT TAKE HER CLAS

This is a class I would say is an easy B, but a hard A. It's not hard per say, but her tests are really long (50 mc questions in 50 minutes). At least 5 of the questions on the test would be on stuff she never taught, but everything else is on the study guide. She takes attendance and does extra credit clicker questions, so go to class.

Murray is the worst teacher I have ever had. Professor Murray is awful. It seems like she only became a teacher to hear herself talk all day long. This class was so biased it was ridiculous. Horrible!!!

She is not a good teacher. Her class started out focused on how the indiviual has an effect on society, then the class transformed to how only African-American individuals had an effect on society. That is not what the class is suppose to be about. Her notes were bad and her test had questions about things you didn't learn in lecture.

Horrible teacher. She speaks way to fast and it's hard to keep up with her. She pretty much regurgitates the words in the book. 4 midterms, worth 25% each...good luck..(every 2 weeks). She also goes over pointless stuff and rushes through lecture when she should be worrying about the important subjects.
Yeah this teacher pretty much sucked. She has a friggin test basically every other day. And every test is unnecessarily long. Avoid this teacher please.

I had her for Psych 2 and Psych 140. I think she's a great professor. I really enjoyed her stories which really helped me to understand the material better (especially during exams). She's a fair grader and reasonable. Exams are pretty straight forward if you do the studying. Overall, she's a great teacher.

the class was fun, but the tests were hard.  she does give out a study guide which goes over ALL of the terms that is on the exams.  there are 2 9-12 page APA papers due for the class.  overall, the course was interesting but she lags.  doesnt like to let students out early.  study from the study guide and u'll be coo.
She's biased, she never starts on time, she goes too fast, she's damanding, and she sucks.

Worst Professor ever!! I learned absolutely nothing in this class, complete waste of time, not to mention how **** she is herself! would bash on anyone that was not black. I had zero intrest in this class and we didnt even have leactures, all of the classes were made up of spreakers who manly preched instead of taught. I didnt buy any of the books and wrote the paper the night before it was due and got an A. Easy class but I dont think i learned anything. LOL. In conclusion the Speakers were the worst part.

I hated this class. She was disorganized with everything, lectures and tests. She lectured a couple of times only; she had speakers. When she spoke, it was always putting down everybody other race that wasn't african american. I found this class extremely bias. Dr.Murray is dedicated to what she does. Classes r intereting & will force you to look at many issues that u have yet to be exposed to. Easy Class. Lecture was not boring.
She is an awesome professor. She makes the class interesting and presents the material in a clear and understandable way.
she's cool.  her class isn't too hard if you read the notes enough and listen up in lecture.

lectures are soso fun! never dozed off during her lecture. she was extremely clear on what she was saying and all her tests were easy. Most of the problems are from your textbooks and partially from lecture.
I think she was a funny teacher... very expressive and animated, kept me awake the entire lecture. Her TAs are AWESOME! Interesting class too :D

The class itself is pretty pointless, because she posts the notes on ilearn, but she gives you hints on what is going to be on the test. Marie as a T.A. is sooo helpful! She is the best. Take the class, its an easy B, but if you read the book you can get an A. I got an A in the class..no sweat
I liked her class, and loved the TA's I think they were helpful and went WAY out of their way to help us.
Her notes are clear and easy to understand. Felt lyk u actually learned something. general speakin a pretty good class to take.

Professor ranks high on the wacko scale, her hair is interesting, she had a seating chart for a class of 600, and she likes to express that she's god's creation. TA's are super obnoxious. Attending class is unnecessary, but make sure you carefully read the book.

when you go to lectures you should take good notes because she bases some of the tests on that.  if you take her study guides off ilearn and you fill it in, you'll do fine.  i got by filling in study guides and not having to read the chapter.

Madam Murray was very adamate about her stance on issues. She could be a little negative when it comes to making you feel stupid, but she helped me whenever I went to ask her for help. Others haven't had that opportunity. Gotta think on her terms to pass the class at times.

I found her to be a good teacher in Psyc 167.  She was nice to talk to and helpful outside of lecture, also.  I went to see her to ask for help on a paper and she didn't have any problem with taking her time to help me or the other students.

I do not recommend her. She is very disorganized, unclear, and biased. Her test questions are ambiguous and sometimes there is no way we can find the answers in her notes. sometimes her notes don't even make sense!

i love this class!! it's entertaining and fun! you could never fall asleep in here! plus, she knows her stuff like the back of her hand. very easy going and funny. cracks jokes allll the time..and they're funny too!..

i did take her psych 2 class and must admit i didnt like her teaching style..but social psych is a different story. she was very familiar with the area and taught it great. very entertaining.
Made a cheating chart for 600 students which was RIDICULOUS. Boring, not entertaing, uses boring powerpoint
made a seating chart for the entire lecture hall.  4 exams, all multiple choice w/ 75 questions.  uses slideshows.  a so-so professor.
Super chill professor for 40a, he explains everything very clearly and gives lots of examples. Pay attention and do the homework (without ai) and you'll be fine for the midterm and final.

Prof is chill but has trouble engaging students, the course is test heavy with midterm + final = 60% of your grade, as long as you understand whats going on in the lecture and do some reading/self studying you'll do ok, but wtv you do don't fall behind as the class is concept heavy and requires practice and understanding of said concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You'll get by if you actually digest information presented in lectures. Reddy has an insanely monotonous voice, but you can tell he's passionate about what he teaches. The final is tough though, you REALLY need to be able to apply concepts into real problems that aren't just pasted from class. Final was multiple choice too, which doesn't help.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Definitely a good professor, but the material itself brings the grade down. The average score in the class was around a 72% for my class after the final, so there was a heavy curve. Homework is nothing like the final, but it had a really easy midterm. As long as you do the homework,participation, and do well on the lab, you'll pass the class easily
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very little homework, and tests are easy

Great professor, he teaches what you need to know. Remember not to mix up rating of professor and difficulty of the course, the intro course is hard theres no argument. Physics doesn't click with most people especially moving variables around in kinematic equations. Great note, he makes the average score of the class a B-, which was around a 70%.

Professor was decent at teaching. Make sure to PARTICIPATE (go to lectures/poll evs, go to DISCUSSIONS (graded)), it can make or break your grade (if i had gone id have at least a B) (oh and do your hw its free 100%). Final is like AP Phyics C, very difficult (avg 10/22, 35%) midterm is easy (25%, 61% but ez). ~10% curve. Emails back pretty fast.

Alright Proff Reddy is a chill guy, but he's not the greatest at teaching. His midterm wasnt hard I just didn't study, but bro that final exam was crazy hard ngl. He gave us a practice exam and let me tell you it was nothing like the final, coughing baby vs tsar bomb. Study a lot in this class, teach yourself, and actually do the homework, it helps

Barely scraped an A+ after getting perfect scores on the midterm and LSA. Did not get perfect score on the final but was well above third quartile (so probably top 15%). Grade is heavily dependent on midterm, final, and LSA. Mess up one of them, you are ok. Mess up two, you will get A- or lower. A- was anything below 86% for final course grade btw.
The final was way too hard.

Midterm problems are exactly like on the HW; final problems will be decently harder. Practice final is, indeed, good practice. Stay on top of HW, though he does give extensions to the class as a whole, probably best not to rely on them. Lectures can be boring and if you can do the homework well enough then you can sleep through them, minus PollEV

Overall a good professor. He will extend deadlines if there are tech issues and spends extra time on the material to make sure more people understand it, but he will cram material at the end of the quarter as a result. The first half of the quarter and the midterms are easy, but the final exam and the remaining material ramps up in difficulty.
does not teach in lecture, most of class is easy until the final with which he will force the average grade down by 20%

Lectures are boring. The midterm was easy enough but the final was extremely difficult. It's the equivalent of teaching you F=ma and then asking you to solve world hunger with it. If you keep up with everything and know the concepts solidly you are guaranteed to pass. Instead of relying on his lectures/material, check out AP Physics stuff to learn.
20% of the material he goes over in lecture is in the Midterm and Final. The other 80% is from Homework and books. Bad class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor assumes you know a lot of Physics concepts already, and acts a little pretentious. Lectures are boring and not engaging. Get ready to read your textbook and do a lot of practice problems on there.

I wanted to post a recent review of this professor, since all the other posts are from 2022 and earlier. His lectures are kinda mediocre, and the labs were pretty hard (for me at least). My advice: utilize knowledge from AP Physics if you took that in high school; it will make this course easier and more of a review (there's hardly any calculus).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Reddy is an alright teacher. His demos are cool but his lectures don't help much. Make sure to read before class and do your homework problems and everything should be alright. Might have to teach yourself a bit thought.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Honestly don't know if lectures helped that much, prof always assigned textbook-reading & did examples in class so assume that u should know concepts already, he used PollEv for participation/attendance, and practice exams were conceptually like midterm & final, but both midterm & final were def more complex. Practice w/hw problems & u will be fine

Professor Reddy is honestly a pretty nice person and professor. However, he talks in an extremely pretentious manner and I think it offends some of the students. That said, his class isn't that difficult. The curve is almost 10 percent, if you show up to class, lab and do the homwork you will at least get a C.

Reddy was a fine professor. He taught kinematics so it was a bit more example heavy that some might prefer, but he makes all the material known ahead of time. Sample Midterm and Finals are your friends, but have a well-rounded knowledge of most kinematic experiences to pass. FAT CURVE.

Extremely rude and always disrespects the class by saying things like "I'm sure you learned this in Elementary School" and it will be a concept learned sometime within middle school/high school and/or a difficult concept. Very confusing class and wouldn't recommend.

Pay attention during lecture and make sure you understand the homework. If you miss any questions on the homework, don't just ignore that concept or you will fail. This especially applies to pullys and rotational inertia.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Reddy was a cool person but not a good professor. He made no sense in lecture and finished the problems so quick no one knew what he did. Midterm was extremely easy compared to the final. All practice problems he gave for final weren't helpful. Lecture is mandatory for clicker qs. I suggest tutoring & outside sources to learn material. hes useless

great lecture professor. makes things easy to understand. Easy midterm, super super hard final. The midterm was very straight forward but the practice final questions don't relate to the actual final, nor are they similar in difficulty.

Super easy professor. If you've never taken Physics before you might struggle, but essentially just use the equations he provides on the tests & plug the values in. Concepts in the class are pretty much explained by equations & class material is fairly light in comparison to other classes.

Reddy isn't too bad. His tests are purely conceptual. His lectures are online so I only went to understand how he did practice problems and for the clicker questions. I didn't take physics in high school so I had to read to understand concepts because Reddy assumed we already knew them. Understand the problems in lecture and you should be fine.

Reddy seemed to be alright at first, but he had a hard time getting his point across in lecture. He tends to ramble. I don't have any interest in Physics nor did I have an easy time understanding it so I didn't do well. I read every chapter before class but it wasn't enough. The only time I got to understand the material was during discussion.

Lectures are really boring, but thankfully if you miss one he posts all of them online. There are a ton of resources that help you try and pass the class, it's up to you to use them. Prior knowledge to Physics is generally useful, as the material is a lot harder without it. He was fine overall, the only knock is that he's boring.
First midterm was super easy.  Final was easy too if you understood the concepts. Teaches with an emphasis on concepts rather than the math. Fun demonstrations.

Previous knowledge of physics (especially AP Physics--C, not B) helps a ton for this course. People generally struggle without prior physics knowledge. Midterm was relatively straightforward, however the final was much more difficult. I would have failed if I didn't take physics in high school.

Took AP Physics in High School, was already pretty good at physics and didn't have any trouble in class. If you're new, however, you WILL struggle if you don't try. Mistakes my friends made were not going to Prof/TA office hours. Study lecture notes he posts online, THEN look in book if needed. Discuss questions are good practice for midterm/final

The class is pretty boring, but that doesn't mean his lectures aren't helpful. His lessons are very clear, and he provides examples to help supplement the lessons. Don't even skip discussion or lecture if you want an A in the class. He always sets curves based on how the students do on the tests. Overall, you learn a lot if you pay attention.

A hard class in general, a lot of self learning in this class due to the fact that most stuff gone over in lecture is repetitive from the lecture. You are better off reading the book throughly. Very picky when it comes to grading exams. Very confusing lectures that are mandatory through the use of clicker questions. Overall a difficult class.

Get ready to answer quickly. His clicker questions last 30 to 45 seconds, and you have the whole class (roughly 300 students) racing to buzz in an answer. Also, his midterms are very few questions (ours was 5 questions), so make sure you are very precise in your calculations, because this midterm can make or break you.

His lectures are boring. Doesn't really teach, but just goes over the material in the textbook during lecture. The homework varies in difficulty... The course is mostly independent, and it is difficult.

Provided excess extra credit for Carnap problems and offered a get-out-of-jail-free card for a draconian grading policy when it became clear that it was affecting peoples' ability to pass the class. If you know what you're doing you can skip a few lectures, but please go to EVERY LECTURE in the first 3 weeks. TA sections are basically mandatory.
I liked the class, Professor Nelson offers a lot of extra credit and seems to really care about his students. Every thing taught is pretty intuitive and the concepts build on each other.

He was an amazing and sweet professor! There is no textbook, but he does have readings during the lectures. There are weekly practice sets plus quizzes during discussion. He provides practice midterms/final which are the same format as the actual assessment, and it leaves you in a good position for the midterm/final. He provides good feedback!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He was generous with providing extra credit assignments and providing personal feedback practice exam answers. He also posts readings on canvas instead of making you buy an expensive book you'll only use for 1 quarter, though after the first midterm the readings will suddenly take on a much more complex language. Other than that, the class is good.

Prof. Nelson is a great professor. He explains the material really well; however, it is important to note that for this class you have to practice on your own as it is like a math class. It becomes way easier when you pay attention in lectures and do the weekly homework. There are also sample midterms that he provides his students which are helpful

The class isn't so bad if you pay attention and give time. However, this is not what many were expecting including me and was actually a math/CS course. He sometimes goes on tangents during his lectures as well, leaving people lost and making me feel like self studying and the TA/discussion section are more valuable. Seems like a nice guy though.

Do not take this as a breadth course if you're looking for an "easy" class. This is not logical thinking as in how people think and act -- it is a math class. This is basically coding for english and its a great course if you're in engineering and like to cry.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: This class was tough and took a good amount of work. Completing the homework made the midterms and final doable. I think professor should teach less abstractly and more hands-on to improve student understanding, especially since exams were similar to homework concepts. I often relied on TA's OH to grasp concepts and complete homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I think students would have a much easier time understanding lectures if Professor Nelson created some slides with visual representations of the examples he discusses in the lectures. Right now, he seems to be using the textbook as his lecture material, meaning students are subjected to a wall of text every lecture, which is not very digestable.

Going to lectures helped me better understand the materials. Pop quizzes during lectures. 1 midterm 1 final, in-class, on paper. Weekly assignments. Textbook was written and provided by Prof. Nelson, no need to read word-by-word. Difficulty depends. Prof. Nelson was passionate when lecturing and approachable outside of class. Shoutout to TA Bhavya!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: At first, I hated the class because it is introducing a new concept that takes a couple of weeks to get used to. After about 3-4 weeks and by the time the first midterm comes around, it's really easy to understand and get a good grade. He gives a pop quiz a week that almost everyone just gets full credit for and there's a bunch of extra credit.

Do not take Logic (008) unless you absolutely have to. I cannot stress enough how miserable and infuriating this class is. Professor Nelson is abysmal at explaining concepts and processes in ways that make sense to people other than himself. If you are even the slightest bit concerned at the difficulty of this course, let this be your warning.

Not sure if I just got lucky because of my really good TA but this class was very easy! Lots of extra credit opportunity so even though the material was hard I still got really good scores on the midterms and final!

Prof. Nelson explains this course as learning a new language, and I agree. At first, the course is difficult because he is trying to teach the mechanics behind logic. It takes some getting used to, but the course is not hard at all if you put in some effort to understand what is being taught. Good attitude and tries to answer questions best he can.

He's sooooo sweet and caring! He genuinely cares about students' progress and would adjust his teaching pacing to accommodate your needs. The material might seem a bit hard at first but you'll get used to it. There are weekly homework but they're quite easy, and there are lots of extra credits. Would recommend!
Not very accessible outside of class & not good at explaining. Complicates things more than he needs to. Wish I picked another professor

I took Logic in Fall 2019 and it was not bad. If you don't get the material in the first few weeks, you're screwed. But it's all straight forward if you understand it. It's tough at first but it gets easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This class was a bit challenging, I'm not going to lie. It does start to get challenging after the first midterm, so make sure you don't fall behind! There are two midterms and a final. He has an online version of the book that you need to read in order to pass. There's also weekly homework. Make sure to go to your TA if you are struggling.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Nelson's courses are great. It's like if weed were a professor.

Nelson never held lectures except to review before midterm & final. Cool if you dont enjoy lectures. Mandatory wordy online readings and weekly homework on a website that was clunky. Mostly rely on TA's but they're pretty chill. More or less a math course w/ letters instead of numbers. Interesting but wouldnt take again. Fine if you enjoy reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Supposed to be a lecture class but everything was online through a website. Confusing text, hard material to learn on your own. Office hours on Google Hangouts. Ridiculous.

His classes are based entirely on the Logic Spaces website. This would be fine but every time there is a problem with the website, he takes a long time to fix it and does very little to allow us to catch up. Pretty much if the website goes down it's your fault. I missed a homework deadline because of the faulty website. This isn't education.

For CS majors looking to take this class, I would highly recommend it. Nelson will be there if you need it. His homework is very helpful. PHIL8 is the best pre-req. for this class. You learn how to do derivations from PHIL8 in a couple of weeks which are tough. Nelson does over-complicate the material in lecture but overall is a good professor.

I'm not sure how he is for other classes, but he was a great professor for Logic. I guess since Logic is so clear cut we didn't have to deal with subjectivity. Over-complicated the material but doing examples made it easy. Very helpful and intelligent. Midterms and final arent tough if you study and go to office hours. Lectures are a bit boring tho

I couldn't wait for the class to end after the first 3 weeks. His lectures always went in circles and it was very easy to get lost. He never really got to the point or directly answered anyone's questions.  The grading by the TAs, especially the papers, was extremely subjective and I didn't get great feedback.

He's funny & he tries to explain as best as he can. Even when things are confusing, you can ask him personally and he'll explain to you much more clearly. The midterm was badly worded but my TA helped us out on that, so I guess that was one downfall. Overall interesting class. Didn't read much and I got an A, then again, I love philosophy.

I dont know why people dont like him or this class! I loved it he is a but confusing but if you attend class,discussion AND do your reading you'll be ok. I imagine people didnt like this class because of personal religious beliefs. If you cant listen to an opposing side and  get hurt over some arguments against god dont take the class!!
He is a very good professor. He gets nervous though and get  a bit tongue tied. He is super cute.

He does drone on sometimes and every slide is a block of text, but I think the material was interesting so it was easier for me to pay attention and WANTED to understand. I'm sure it's helpful to do the readings but I only did the first few and did still did great on the midterm! If you're interested in the class, by all means, take it! :)

I thought this class would be fun since I'm an evil person myself, but naw. Michael Nelson does try to explain things but I feel he over explains to the point that he confuses people. Also it doesn't help how his voice hits these high teenage boy pitches that really makes me cringe. I advise people to avoid this class if at all possible

HORRIBLE professor! He disregarded anyone who would try to rebut his argument towards the existence of God. I hated the sound of his voice. I'm sorry, but I really hated this class. I would not recommend this professor to any of my friends. I should have listened to people when they told me not to take his class.
this class blows! a bunch of online reading. makes you get a clicker that you only use once or twice.

I thought this class would be fun, and it might have been if Nelson wasn't so boring. He has this prepubescent voice and he over-explains everything. He is a very easy teacher, but he will make you fall asleep.

Nelson is helpful and interesting and genuinely cares about his students. Evil is an extremely interesting class, and paying attention to him in class and taking to him after helps a lot more than simply reading the texts. Only criticism is that TAs are hit and miss for this class.
a LOUSY professor...overall, philosophy is not a fun & easy class

I really hated this class.  He gave unnecessary assignments and quizzes.  I guess because I am used to doing one major assignments rather than mini assignments throughout the quarter because I am already a senior.  Philosophy classes in general are overall really ridiculous...

As this was my third discovery seminar, I have to say Philosophy disc seminars are the best suited. Nelson's time travel does not disappoint, from watching Harry Potter and Donnie Darko, to reading some interesting short stories and even a philosophy paper. The student is able to enjoy such a fun topic without any pressure. Easy and fun 1 unit.

Go to the discussions and the lecture. But what helps the most is to know which philosopher thinks what about divinity. If you get the general idea of who thinks what, you shouldn't have any problems with the class.

Second course with Nelson, and he fares much better in a smaller setting than in a large lecture hall. He knows the topic well and is adept at finding appropriate and 'fun' contemporary examples to tie in to discussions. Grades rather easily as well.
He overcomplicates the material and his slides are difficult to understand, but the workload is a piece of cake.

Previous comments are not truly representative of the class. The content is quite intresting and there is no premium on reading. I personally did not read at all and recieved an 'A-" He seemingly lacks self confidence but is knowledgable and likes the topics. Easy class to sleep in though especially at the UV. Not too much hw, quizzes or tests.

Professor Nelson really cares about the success of his students. I was really scared about taking his class because of all the former comments that I have read. Yes, it was difficult to stay awake because he is very repetitive and the seats at the UV were SO comfortable, but Prof Nelson really taught me a lot about phil. He was my favorite prof!
he says "um" a ridiculous amount. he's not clear at all in what he says and he gives multiple quizzes in lecture and section. the TAs can't do much to help either.
posts slides online but gives lots of quizes
He complicated the material.  I spent more time correcting his grammar and spelling errors on his slides.

I hate to be so blunt but he is a HORRIBLE Prof. He's a nice guy and appears to know his stuff but he CANNOT, CANNOT teach at ALL. His lectures are longwinded, incoherent, and BORING. The only time I didnt sleep was when Nick was guest lecturing for a week. Avoid this guy at ALL COSTS unless you want to die a slow, painful grade-death by sleeping.
double negatives, triple negatives, quadruple negatives. complicates the material instead of helping students understand.

This class should be avoided at all costs.  He does not know what he talks about most of the time and will waste a lot of class time going back on his own muttered statements.  Extremely inexperienced.

cannot teach whatsoever. he won't understand what you mean if it's not in his own words. not helpful at all and is very confusing. he seems inexperienced in teaching, always seems very unsure of what to do.

This guy's probably a good student of philosophy, but isn't a really good teacher of it.  He apparently has an firm grasp on the concepts he lectures on, but his intuitive knowledge of the materials get lost in the translation of intuition and lecture.

In person lectures but records them so you can watch them later, gives a small amount of hw, and the practice tests/study guides he gives for exams are very similar to tests. If you do those you will be fine, I also recommend doing the practice mcq's in the book, they were also similar to the midterm and final's mcqs.
free class, practice midterm/final questions are super similar to the tests, very little hw given, records lectures, has redemption midterm assignments allowing you to earn back points

Chill professor, always posted his lectures online so u don't rlly have to pu to lecture. Midterms were fair and would give us a "points back" assignment where u could get up to 70% of the points that u missed on the test back. Couple of HW assignments that u would always get full points on if u simply completed it.

W professors. 2 midterms both 20MC and 2FRQs, gives redemption assignment for missed points. Condenses content to most important topics. HW was answered on all lectures, quizzes depend on TA generally easy if you pay attention in lecture. Records lectures.

Do not take Dr. Neary, his class is graded by midterm 1, midterm 2, and the final. His exams are 9 questions long so you don't have room for any partial credit. The homework is not graded for points. If you have an option between him and Switzer, take Switzer because at least you have a good curve while Neary does not curve at all.

reviews.comment:
good lectuerer, I tanked the first midterm but lowest gets replaced with the final. second midterm went much better, make sure to do the homework, 1/3 of the exam is hw problems 
not too bad if you put in some effort, the final was MUCH more conceptual than expected but not bad. no heavy curve, good amount of extra credit on final and for ieval
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This was a good course! It seems that Professor Neary took inspiration from Casselman's lecture style to design a better course, although you are only graded on tests so keeping up with the material closely is necessary
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: After what I've been hearing about how rough his first time teaching this class what, I was scared to take it. But! He's actually an amazing lecturer, he's reformed his tests and what material he teaches. Midterms were also broken down to the % and each of them were fair. He did allow your final to replace a midterm score as well!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr Neary had clear expectations and was a fair grader. He worked examples out in class which was helpful. His exams were fair with some problems coming from the homework.

reviews.comment: what the hell is even this class? do not take with neary you will 100% fail he dosent curve at all and the class average is 30%
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: After looking at all the negative reviews, I can strongly say that Dr. Neary has changed and is overall a very good professor. He is generous with his grading scheme, and his lectures are very clear. He always puts a hw question on his exams, so do the hw even if it isn't mandatory. He gives reasonable partial credit.

Professor Neary was an outstanding instructor. His lectures were clear and well organized. The exams were very fair and reflected exactly what was taught in class. Clear grading scale, curved if average is low.
super generous with partial credit on exams. if you study, you can succeed. do all of the homework bc he pulls questions from it to put on the tests.

I took this class after reading all the bad reviews. Dr. Neary has greatly improved from the past. Grading criteria has been changed, with 90% being an A. Midterm 1 was hard, Midterm 2 was easy. Final was okay, he curves IF averages are low. 30% of the exams come directly from the homework. Final replaces the lowest midterm which was helpful

Dr. Neary had a rough first year and all these reviews do not reflect how he is now he was honestly not to bad. Compared to all the other ochem professors Ive taken. He was in the middle his exams are honestly super fair. The first exam is yes brutal but he gives you the chance to replace with final. Good job Dr.Neary would take again.

Dr. Neary taught half of my undergraduate advanced organic chemistry course. If all of the reviews on this page were true about him being inconsistent, then he has definitely improved. Dr. Neary was always accessible by email. He is both easy and interesting to talk to. He was even nice enough to stay past office hours with me. Great lectures too
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I had Dr Neary in his first quarter of teaching, and he struggled with providing the class with proper grading criteria. He changed the syllabus multiple times throughout the quarter. study the lecture notes and reference the textbook. Self studying is vital in passing this class. Attend TA OH and SI, they were more helpful than prof OHs.

I had Dr Neary in his first quarter of teaching, and he struggled with providing the class with proper grading criteria. He changed the syllabus multiple times throughout the quarter. However as long as you studied the lecture notes and referenced the te

All of the people saying he sucks didn't open the book once. If tests are verbatim to the notes, isn't that be good? Neary is easy to talk too and actually goes through his notes when talking to you. Take the class, he knows what he's doing. For the people who are reading this deciding between him and someone else, it shouldn't even be a decision.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He doesn't care about the students. He set an A- to a 94%, went on "vacation" after each exam, decided to change the entire syllabus/grading criteria THE DAY OF THE DROP DEADLINE because of his unrealistic grading scale. Then proceeded to come out with a half baked final with questions about HIS research NOT EVEN INCLUDED IN THE TEXTBOOK! EVIL RUN!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: New prof so subject to change: added a midterm halfway through quarter, never reported final exam scores or final curve. Dense lectures and homework, and did not give us practice exams. An A- was a 94% (!!!) and he said he would "adjust" but never told us if he did. Difficult exams not similar to homework. Take Switzer until Neary figures it out.

I had him for ochem008C the last of the series. This guy was absolutely bad... he is a good guy. And I trust he may get better someday. But lecture is boring. Lecture doesn't help hw. Hw didn't help first midterm. He had to rearrange whole syllabus because he was not prepared for how poorly his hard and test would be recieved...

Take someone else!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He doesn't make the exams anything like the homework/HIS OWN LECTURES and the grading scale was insane. He changed it twice due to low scores (I know several people who scored less than a 10/100 on the first midterm). You will need to do a LOT of learning on your own to do well on his exams... Go to SI because his TA's are your only hope!!

Professor Neary is not bad. The first midterm was very difficult but he made the second midterm and final extremely easy. For reference, I got a 50% on the first midterm and still aced the class. Dr. Neary is a talented lecturer and does go over everything needed for exams. I am only docking points because the class was not organized.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Taking this class genuinely took a piece of my soul. This class would be manageable if it was the only one you're taking in the quarter. We had to memorize around 60-page-long mechanisms and reagents for the final. Neary expects you to have PhD level knowledge. The grading scale is pathetic, with a 94 being an A, never been done before at UCR.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Compared to other Ochem classes, I had to put in the most work for this class. Neary added his own research and inorganic chapters to the syllabus. These extra chapters make it so there is a lot more covered in exams, while he also incporerated material from other Ochem classes into his exams. Tbh tho his lectures did go over everything on exams.

Neary doesn't know how to teach or how to set a fair grading scale. 94% being the beginning of an A in an Ochem class with little to no curve and very hard tests is just not fair. If anyone is telling you that he's good, they're literally just trolling. Never take whatever Neary is teaching for your mental health's and GPA's sake.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Absolute worse class I've ever taken. I heard that Switzer and Neary were teaching 8c and so I thought it would be safe to take Neary ... and I was wrong about that. This is worse than Casselman and Larsen. I suggest you to take another professor and if he's the only professor teaching it, then take it next quarter with another professor.

AVOID! Exam 1 avg were so low(~40%) that he changed the syllabus. He's making us learn polymers(his research) & it's not on the textbook & the other class isn't learning it. He went on vacation before finals and he doesn't care. The TA is better at teaching and carried us. Take another prof unless you want to lower your gpa. I got As in 8a and 8b.
His exams are so unfair, his teaching is awful reading off of pre written notes. Wish I never took him!

reviews.comment: Worst ochem professor ever. Makes Larsen, casselmen, Ana, Hooley, and kho look like angles.

reviews.comment: This was the worst professor I have had during the entire organic chemistry series. Despite there being over 30+ mechanisms he only tested us on 3-4 which made up our entire exam grade. He is also not very helpful at answering questions and simply tells you to know/memorize all the material. His notes were anything but helpful..

I've never felt bullied by a professor, I loved and enjoyed Ochem. This guy's first quarter teaching EVER. I blame him for how he structured the class and didn't prepare us enough or tell us what to expect. I never had a professor who wanted us to know 110% content point blank. Almost 50+ full mechanisms we needed to KNOW by the end of the quarter.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This dude gave his students hell, included chapters that were never taught by the other profs, made the final exam like 11 pages. Even thou I got an A, that was the hardest class of my career, but chem8c shouldve been easier than chem8b. ONLY take him if that was ur grandmas bed wish before she died, other than that, he not worth the work

even after doing well, i would never take dr. neary's class ever. if you are planning to take this course with him, be extremely careful. he tells u what to know, but he basically says u need to know everything. he assumes u know everything on the test, even stuff from previous classes within the series. take a diff professor if u have a choice
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I honestly didn't like his teaching style. His lectures were just way too dense with little in class practice. He did change his lectures a bit after the low MT 1 average, but I still found his lectures overwhelming. The class is passable, you just need to practice and put in the work. Overall, the most difficult time I had in the Ochem series.

As a lecturer, Neary was honestly pretty detailed with his lectures and the things he talked about were helpful. However, his hand-written notes were extremely vague and he would often skip steps on mechanisms, leaving a lot of it up to interpretations. Tests were somewhat fair, but, be careful of the reagents because most of them were weird forms.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Hard grading scale. Harder exams. Rude. Made his TAs do all the work while he went on vacation.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: had to choose between neary and switzer. based on how notorious switzer is, i thought this was the safer choice. how wrong i was. this guy scoffed at one of his students during a midterm for asking a question. students were crying while taking the first exam. avoid at all costs

Neary gives great lectures. Adjusted the syllabus after the first midterm since the majority of the class can't study or are lazy. Everyone whines about no cheat sheet, but his exams are by far the easiest exams in the organic chemistry series. All the mechanisms and reagents are pretty much the same in CHEM008C, so it's not too difficult to learn.

reviews.comment: Do not take this class with this professor. A= 94% without a curve. Post midterm one(avg 42%), made a new grading scale. A new test was added week 9, and still, there is a low chance of a curve. the tests do not reflect the HWs and mid2 has a practice midterm. speeds through lectures, have to learn independently to understand the material.

This man literally has no regard for his class. Bro went on vacation during finals week did not make a practice final and left the class clueless on finals day. Really strict grading scale. Basically no curve as 94% minimum for an A. Really low midterm averages because his tests were completely different from what we do in hw.

AVOID AT ALL COSTS! doesnt know how to teach, no regard to students, changes syllabus more than halfway through quarter, doesnt teach everything through notes, leaves before the quarter is finished, makes the TA work harder than him, doesnt give practice problems for final.

This professor doesn't seem to care about his students and has his TA do most of the work. His exams are super hard and cover stuff other ochem professors don't even touch. In week 9, he changed the syllabus and added an extra exam at the end of the quarter. He even went on vacation during finals week, which feels really unprofessional.

reviews.comment: Man does not know how to make a modules tab on Canvas to post all his notes and HW. 94% being an A is crazy when midterm 1 and 2 averages are 40% and 60%.

Bro had a 42% average first exam. Grading scale was standard, no set curve. If you get class average there's no way to tell if you pass or fail because he doesn't announce curve until after final. Very stressful. Basically with his grading scale, the class average was less than an F- Not sure if ill pass the class.

Neary does not know how to teach at all. He looks like he reads from a script and expects students to learn independently without guidance and refuses to make material or provide material for the students to use. He does not expect his students to succeed and even neglects his students. He made no practice material and did not reply to emails.

reviews.comment:
Sounds like he's reading from a script instead of lecturing. Homework and exams are nothing like lectures. I think he expects us to learn through the homework, but doesn't even explain the answers to the homework.  
Neary, I hope you either learn how to teach, or figure out if teaching isn't for you, because your'e killing GPA's in the process

reviews.comment: exams nothing like lectures/homework and has no curve. not a bad professor, his first time teaching ever so still finding out his style. helpful if he sees you trying but can be intimidating

reviews.comment: decent lecturer but his tests relate nothing from his notes to what is tested. also teaches through homework instead of just teaching the mechanisms in class
decent prof but changes grading scheme mid quarter and tests are incredibly unfair

exams aren't that bad. if you study you'll get an A. mans doesn't respond to his emails at all and is rude AF. went to his office hours a couple times and he was extremely rude. doesn't rlly care abt his students. steer clear.
bro needs to make his tests harder
amazing prof with very insightful lectures. big curve and fair exams. test matches the content in lecture and to the homework
very good professor, wish there was an ochem 8d with neary. bro was a good prof with bad students honestly. he deserved alot better imo
The devil if he was tall and had a baby face
mans tests are so free idk why everyone thinks its so hard like bro just get better

The professor is overrated. I've had him two times. He's okay at best. No midterm or final, just quizzes. It makes the class enticing; however, one missed attendance/ one bad quiz grade, and you'll be down half a letter grade, SO BEWARE. Doesn't accommodate emergencies/ changed the syllabus both times I took him, really annoying. Not bad, not good.

reviews.comment: Lots of cold calling to review readings. Prepare to answer questions about the reading and provide your own perspective of it. Key is to use your own words rather than reading off the articles.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Super easy, very involved and interesting

Lectures are great , always looked forward going to this class. There are a lot of readings yet they were very interesting so it wasn't too bad. I didn't have midterm or final yet there are quizzes every week on the readings so come prepared.

Hands down, most interesting and great professor I have had thus far. He is a real dude and treats students like adults rather than most who treat students as kids. There is lots of reading that may be difficult but he does a great job at explaining them. No midterm or final, but quizzes on reading once a week and a paper. Best teacher at UCR fr.

Ben is the best professor I've had at UCR. The readings for his course(s) are all from political science journals, so they're harder than your average undergrad courses, but they're far more interesting than most of what's assigned in other classes. He's super well read and challenges you, but isn't judgmental when you don't know something.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Newman is the best professor Ive had at UCR. Hes really knowledgeable about a variety of things: my notes were equal parts from the actual course material and from the interesting, funny, but informative tangents he would go on. Great dude.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: great professor, easy tests, and the final was optional

Super sweet professor and amazing lecturer! I enjoyed her class and honestly she's one of the best 5b professors. As long as you pay attention in class, you'll be fine. Her tests aren't hard at all and the final was optional.

Prof. Nguyen is really sweet but she's not a great professor. lectures move really fast, and there is a LOT of info;  150 word reflection after each lecture which is really pointless, would rather have practice questions instead. some test questions are really confusing as she said there are multiple right answers and you have to pick the best one.

Super sweet professor. Had a family emergency that I feel negatively effected my learning, not her fault but it feels like she left her students high and dry. So many tests! Study! No need to go to lectures (recorded) but there are lecture reflections every class. Tries to make class fun. Some test questions feel unfair and have multiple answers.

She's super sweet and her lectures are pretty easy to follow and set up in a way that's easy to understand and take notes. Just make sure to keep note of questions you have because things aren't always super clear. Her exams are pretty similar to the notes and the only other homework is a daily reflection. And her outfits are always amazing.

Dr. Catherine is an amazing professor. The class consists of four 25 mcq exams, reflections after every lecture (doing 20/24 will ensure full credit), and a project (was very fun did mine about 1D) She drops your lowest test score or project and gives you 2 ec opportunities. She has been the best prof I have taken my freshman year!
It was so much pleasure to be her student. Very kind, patient, funny, and knowledgable. She makes Econ fun and interesting. Take her and she'll blow your mind away!
She's literally the best professor. She explains everything clearly and really cares about her students. She's also nice and cool. Pretty sure most guys in the class fall in love with her in the end.

Hien is an amazing professor and person. She truly cares about her students' success and is always willing to help. She always comes to class with a big smile and encourages us to do well. I wish I could have her for all Econ classes.

Professor Nguyen has it all. She's super nice to everybody. She knows her stuff very well and explains everything in a clear way. Great sense of humor to keep us awake during the long summer lectures. Her tests are straightforward. Study discussion problems and quizzes, you should be fine. Plus, she's smokin' hot. You're in for a treat, guys.

Probably the best professor I've ever had.  Extremely clear teacher, no BS assignments (the ones he does assign are relevant and helpful), and teaches practical, real-world material.  The class is not super easy, but if you make an effort you can do well.  You WILL learn things.  Not one of those classes you forget 90% of the day after the final.

Josh doesn't babysit and treats students like adults.  His teaching style is unique and modern.  His examples stick with you.  His final is mega hard and he explicitly lets you know that beforehand.  Taking Josh's class will change the way you think about economics.  He's also fairly easy on the eyes.
Definitely one of the best econ professor I've taken so far. Very clear and knows what he is doing. I learned more in his class than in the required upper div classes.

Josh is a great teacher. His style is probably the best that I have had throughout all my undergraduate econ classes. It essentially eliminates the need for a book. I learned more in this class than I have in the two-three pre-req classes needed for this course! Great teacher.

Still taking this class right now, but Josh is one of the better teachers I've had here at UCR! His teaching style is great. He teaches very effectively and is a slightly tough grader, but it helps in the long run!

Josh is one of the best instructors that I have had here.The HW is super hared, but as long as you attend the lectures and attempt the HW, you'll be ok. Attending the lectures is extremely important because he goes over problems similar but easier than the HW and gives real world examples.
One of the few great instructors.  Very few have the pleasure of taking Professor Ng's class

Josh is by far my favorite instructor in UCR. He is clear, knowledgeable, and truly wants to see his students succeed. The exams are reasonable. If you actually do the assignments and understands them, then the exams should be fair. He also has the most interesting teaching style I seen at UCR, and it is highly effective. Enjoy!
Have only had him for about a week but he is very clear and shows he cares about his students.  I actually like Econ because of this professor
Had him for vietnamese and was super fun but attendance does matter

I came into this class a little worried because of the negative reviews, but I think he is one of the best professors I've had so far. He knows how to engage with his students and make jokes and light up the atmosphere (says really unhinged things LOL). One thing I would say is that there is a lot of readings, but he gives a lot of extra credit!

Class recommended for ppl who like to write essays and read. Quizzes can be very tedious in the questions so reading the assigned stories is  a MUST. Participation does matter. Extra credit is given that help boost quizzes. Overall really funny and easy but the quizzes, again, the questions are TEDIOUS and easy to mess up.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I had him for 3 of my Viet language courses and he is my favorite professor I've ever had at UCR! He is very funny and always made class enjoyable. Very engaging with his students and you can tell he is super passionate about what he teaches. He genuinely cares for his students. I enjoyed his classes would take more courses with him if I could!
