reviews.comment: rn it's week six i like my grade... the students complaining about the spring 2020 quarter are being unfair. sounds like freshmen �� of course it is going to be hard it's a bio class we got open book(enough said lol), extra credit, partial credit, and she initially offered retakes pffft I recommend taking her class

shes having trouble adjusting to the online format i think, which is totally understandable. but she told us before our last midterm that wed have a five question leeway, making the exam out of 150. but we did better than shed expected so a week after the exam, she told us it was out of 175 and shut off all of our ability to contact her.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This professor will find anything and any reason to be against the student. She will promise a set of rules for her exam but then go back on her word. We were promised resources for the exam but ended up not getting such resources. The first exam everyone ranged between 20%-40%, one student got 100% and she states that its the student's fault.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: In the middle of a pandemic where students have to live at home, take care of family, don't have the same resources, etc. she decided to go on about how easy we have it because its open book and then mocked us by saying that we still only got the average of previous years. Worst professor I have ever had if she's teaching this course DONT TAKE IT.

Had 10 clicker questions and told us that those were our practice for the midterm then gave us the hardest midterm possible. Then when students complained about the test she told the ENTIRE class to "study better" She wrote her own reviews on here, if you look you can def find them LOL. Horrible professor, if she's teaching the class dont take it.

Prof Ponisio is the most condescending and irresponsible professor I have ever had. Does not respond to students messages. She acts like she cares but dont be fooled because SHE DOES NOT!!! Exams are full of mistakes. Makes promises to the class that she does not keep. Overall terrible experience. AVOID AT ALL COSTS!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: During pandemic. Honestly, just listen to the bad reviews. They give an accurate description of what the professor is like and her teaching style. Exams hard, lectures mediocre, help nonexistent, condescending, avoids responsibilities, unprofessional, and basically just a bad educator. Take Bio5C with a real educator cause she aint it.

I understand that both parties are adjusting to obstacles created by the pandemic. I feel that she is putting more effort into "preventing cheating" than helping her students succeed. The biggest problem for me is her "accommodating" and reassuring students with but end up taking back everything she said to maintain a historical average.

I took her last quarter and she gave us all the resources to succeed! She's a nice professor that has her bad moments however, she's human just like everyone else. Instructors and students are BOTH affected by the pandemic. Although I don't necessarily agree with how she went about everything, she still gives ec, more time + leniency on exams.

Prof. Ponisio was an amazing professor. I have never written a review but I thought I should give her some justice for the students being ungrateful. Not only did she provided her notes online, she also provided a video of that lecture. The midterms and final were easy if you reread the notes over and over again. Extra credit was also given.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She's horrible. Please don't take her. She'd rather drag DOWN a class average than empathize for her students during a pandemic. She's also a liar. She told us we were allowed to miss 5 questions but instead took back her word on that to drag down the average cause it was too high. I hope she sees this and changes the way she manages classes.

Ask for help, expect to be called stupid. When called out for her mistakes, she threatened to have our midterm 1 still count (btw everyone failed mt.1), even though she said midterm 2 would replace it. Her teaching style is saying one thing then doing another. Expect hard tests, lack of empathy, no help, big/toxic ego, and gpa ruin.

I see a lot of people putting her down as a "tough grader." That is misleading. Tough grader implies a degree of coherency and competency that she clearly does not possess. She is uncaring, without sympathy, and all together baffling. Her actual content is mediocre at best and her tests are relatively easy but her demeanor is quite off-putting.
Instead of focusing on dragging her class average down to be deemed "acceptable" she should focus on teaching the material well.

The most ridiculous professor I have encountered in my two years at UCR. I'm currently taking this class during quarantine and she has not offered her students even a crumb of empathy or accountability. She has gone back on almost every policy change she has made for her class, making it impossible to keep track of progress. Should be fired.

She acts likes she so much better than everyone else. She lied about how the midterm and test will be graded and gets upset when everyone calls her out about going back on her word. I understand everyone is having a hard time adjusting to online classes, however other professors don't have the students Turning on them. Would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Ponisio is probably not cut out to be a professor. Took the class during quarantine. She advertised grading provisions, went back on them, and when student's expressed their concerns, she insulted us and refused to answer emails. It's times like this that really show how compassionate an educator is and she simply isn't.

Horrible professor She seems cool at first then you take her midterms and she literally does what she can to make sure the average is low. I got an A when she originally told us our test was out of 30. She assumed her class wasn't going to receive a C average I guess, but when scores came out she lowered everyone's grade by 15% to maintain a C avg.

Take this class if you want a careless professor or, in other words, if you want to fail. She is inconsiderate of her students. She tells us one thing and does otherwise. She is also unreliable. She NEVER responds to students emails. She sets up her students to fail and leaves us to figure it out for ourselves. Do better Prof. Ponisio.

This professor really cares about being right even though a lot of students are suffering. Does not take anything into consideration. Take her if you want to ruin your GPA. The midterms are timed and no backtracking. Tried asking for help and got "You need to study better". Blamed a BIO5A person for no backtracking feature even tho we in BIO5C.

AVOID AT ALL COST. 2 midterms online, no backtracking feature and timed. First midterm , only allowed 30 minutes to answer 15 (math problems involved). Second midterm given 1hr, told it was out of /150, anything over this was extra credit then she changed it to /170, due to one question being dropped. Blames students for not studying well enough.

She is the worst biology professor I have had out of the whole bio5 series. She uses old lectures that aren't exactly the same as new ones. Slides have almost no information, so they are not helpful when studying. She does not explain calculations well or give good examples. She thinks she is special because she went to Stanford, but no one cares.

Dr. Ponisio is very accommodating and is always quick to answer any questions you may have. Her tests are pretty standard. She uploads and records all of her lectures, but her slides are mostly pictures without much explanation. She's a very lecture heavy instructor- go to class for extra credit clickers!!

Prof was very passionate about what she was teaching. There is quite of bit of math/graphs to interpret but very straightforward questions on her midterm. Just studied the slides. Her questions could be a little awkwardly worded. Average for her midterm was about a C
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Honestly, between she and the second professor, Leonard Nunney, Nunney is better. She was unclear and made mistakes in lectures, but she did not make an announcement to correct it. She is passionate about her subjects and she is improving, but her lectures did not make the class easier. Also, going through her slides helps, but did not help much.

Very passionate in her teachings. She provides an amazing amount of resources to help students (ie. practice questions, midterm reviews, lecture videos online, etc). There is no hw or quizzes so you have more than enough time to study. Her exams are very fair and not as difficult as other Biology professors. Amazing professor, amazing course.
There's nothing more to say. Don't take Ponisio unless you want your gpa to suffer. Lectures were a mess, notes were unhelpful, tests were overly difficult.
aviod her, she doesnt curve and makes the subject harder

Not respect students. Take weeks to reply email. Not absolute grading scale throughout the course. Final was a disaster, questions from nowhere, do it just like gambling even though I study so hard for it. She ruined my life, ruined my GPA
HORRIBLE PROFESSOR !! DO NOT TAKE HER SAVE YOUR GRADE biol 5c is not a hard subject to understand but she makes it more hard then needs too

5C suppose to be the easiest Super weird and tricky exams Multiple choice ques. with mark all that apply. Exams don't reflect class material Messy, unprepared lecture Slides have nothing except pictures First time got a B even though full participation, hw points, 100 on 1 midterm with 2nd prof, 75 on her midterm, horrible final No curve

DO NOT TAKE AT ALL COSTS!!! The material for this Bio 5C is generally pretty simple but she makes her questions so pretentious. Literally paragraphs of questions. Also many of her questions are "mark all that apply" and if you dont mark the right bubbles you get the whole question wrong :)!!! Save yourself and dont take Ponisio she's the worst!!!
Totally unfit for a teacher. I would be ashamed to take money for such incompetence

Terrible. Was apathetic toward students. Lectures were terrible: read slides and spoke slowly and incoherently. Gave poor explanations for concepts. Exams contained material not covered, contained many errors, and were totally ambiguous. Exams covered pointless garbage rather than major topics. Seemed like he wrote them the night before.

this prof is difficult just because he couldnt care less about his students and how they do. his lectures dont teach you anything and he assigns a lot of book work on which he never covers in lecture. his tests are more or less unfair and designed to make you fail... oh and just cause he says something wont be on the test, dont believe him lol

He made this course much more difficult than it needed to be. Exams are very difficult, even with extensive study, and he does not give much partial credit. As a teacher, he is seems disinterested in the class and is unhelpful.

he expect you to spend as much time as u would in a programing class for math(he tells u to do every problem in the book and doesnt teach u the way).....I simply dont have that much time for a math course

Well, I am going to take an approach that isn't so bad.  For CS111, Professor Przymusinki was alright.  He is very clear about what he expects you to do.  I was expecting it to be a lot harder.  Maybe all the recommended work may seem like a lot, but if you know how to do all of them, the class will not be that difficult.

NEVER EVER EVER TAKE HIM!!! He cant lecture to save his life and he goes out his way to create tests designed to fail half the class.  Like on a final question he asked to name ALL 10 attributes of Extreme Programming, WTF like someone actually memorized that crap.

Oh. My. God. I REALLY wanted to take this class, but all he did was lay back reclined and read from powerpoint slides with the LIGHTS OFF. When the class average on his test was 50-60% (for 30+ people) he spent over an hour going over how lazy and (heavily implied) stupid we were. He tested on things that were WRONG in the book too. God, he's awful

WOW Worst CS professor at UCR! Avoid at all costs. Sure you might feel tempted to take Software Engineering because it sounds interesting but he makes it very unpleasureable, you dont even get to really engineer any software! His lectures are retarded, he just reads off the book's slides and his tests are ridiculous with irrelevant anal questions.

I had Prof. Przymusinski years ago in the mid 1990s.  He was by far the most intelligent man I ever knew.  He makes you work your butt off - but it's worth it.  You can really learn from this guy - if you put the effort into it.

avoid at all costs, he will give you an F just so you will go in and argue with him, i failed 2 classes at ucr and both of them were cs181, in his cs152 class he gave me an F then i went in and argued he changed it to a B+. F to a B+ wtf is up with that

Worst professor ever.  Wastes time during lectures babbling about nothing.  Postpones midterm at its scheduled start.  Grades like a madman.  Failed DOZENS of people and eventually was FORCED to change their grades (some from F to A+ or A!!).  AVOID!!!!

Rambles through  his lectures, and makes unprofessional comments constantly. He does have the best interest for all of his students to learn the material, and gives many extra credit opportunities, but I would not take his class again.  Good guy, just needs work on lecturing.

This was a very tough class. There is a ton of reading - most of it is pretty interesting, though. It is difficult to retain the information needed for the quizzes/tests. He does provide a study guide outline for each quiz/test, but there is a lot of information covered and they can be hard to fill out sometimes.

Took his course through NAU Online. Pro's: Prof. Pschaida is passionate about what he teaches and is very knowledgeable in the field.   Cons: He assigns alot of weekly reading and the material required for quizzes is almost impossible to retain but he does provide a study guide outline which is helpful.   If you participate he is a fair grader.

took 2 online classes with Pschaida, 1 over summer and 1 over fall semester.  During the fall it wasn't so bad, except you have to spend 30 minutes trying to figure out what you're suppose to do and where to submit an assignment.  DO NOT TAKE DURING SUMMER!  doesn't change course load, springs random assignments, and his study  guides are useless
Helps clarify big ideas in the course, and tries to get everyone to talk and talk to each other and participate in Sections.  Review Sessions are really helpful.  Sometimes kind of funny.

Dr. Purcell was an amazing professor as she's very enthusiastic about Entomology! I'm not very good at science or things relating to biology so it was slightly difficult. She gives a huge curve which is a plus. There are 2 worksheets due a week, several participation quizzes a week, a midterm, and a final; tests can be done in groups.

Dr. Purcell was a fantastic professor who was always responsive and knew a lot about the class. She was so caring and worked to make class fun and engaging. We even went on nature walks, and she would dedicate class time to answer student questions in detail. She is so passionate about her work and very reasonable grader. Must take!!

Dr. Purcell is super nice and caring. If you show up during office hours, she is really helpful and tries to explain things. She drops the lowest quiz and homework grade. Decent amount of homework and quizzes but they are fairly easy. I really recommend taking her class.

I highly recommend. The material is difficult but it's a great class taught by one of the best and most respected professors on campus. If you're pre-med, you need to take this class. Study hard, make flash cards, go to office hours etc., and you will be fine. She gives a lot of bonus points on quizzes and exams so keep up with the material.

Dr Talbot is very approachable and interactive during class. She made the class so medically and research oriented. It made it harder but much more enjoyable and beneficial if you're apremed student. Be prepared though for reading tons of info but I promise the A+ doable. You have to study notes and understand readings in the book to guarantee an A
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: It was a lot of work. But if you're pre-med you should take her. Be prepared and don't get behind on the material. Record lectures and review right after class. Go to office hours.

I do not know why my comment got deleted. Anyways, some things that you'll be tested on are hard: some MC are A,B, or all of the above type questions. FOLDING tended to be some of the challenging things (for me at least. Thus, I recommend you go to lecture! Go to office hours! Read book too I guess. If you just read off ppt, youll get a C- like me!

MT 1 aver on the 50's curve to 70's MT 2 70's Her test are very hard, not because of the topic is hard but because is so much material to cover and she test you on the little details. At the end of each lecture she gives practice problems they are a bit difficult but go to office hours and she will help you get the answer. she will use.

A LOTTTTTT of information. For M1, the average was 54% so she curved it 20% to make the average 74%. For M2, the average was 70 or something like that so she curved it 2%. So, unless everyone bombs the tests, she does not curve/ averages are high alrdy. She does give some extra credit, but it's really hard to get an A in this class. STUDY EARLY!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The class is very dense with info. You could probably stretch the material from the first half into a quarter long class easily. That being said I didn't like how many typos and errors there were in her powerpoint notes. But it is doable. I never went to lectures either.

Class has a TON of information. You have to study from day 1 if you want to get an A. Her exams are MC and written. Not too tricky though. Discussion also has quizzes every week based on what was taught in the same discussion. Basically a 30 minute lecture in discussion followed by a quiz. She does give extra credit opportunities though. Study hard

Very organized, very clear. No curve but she offers extra credit and adds points to exams. Go to class and pay attention and you'll be fine. Quizzes in discussion every week (except for exam week but including week 1) so you need to stay on top of it. Incredibly demanding but doable. Easy to study for since it's so interesting.

Talbot is an amazing professor. She truly cares about her students and her knowledge of the subject makes an impossible class doable. She holds you to a VERY high standard, but gives tons of extra credit too. Go to lecture! Book sucks so don't bother. You will get what you put in for this class. In the end, very rewarding and totally worth it.

Dr. Talbot one of the best professors I've had at this university, and that's good because this course is one of the hardest at the university. The tests are very straight forward, attendance is not mandatory (in class quizzes are technically extra credit, but I promise you won't do well unless you attend), you basically get the grade you deserve.

This is a very difficult class with lots of information and there's no curve. The lectures are really interesting though and the teacher is a great lecturer. You must go to class and take notes, but the book isn't really necessary. Exams are difficult but straight forward; no tricks. John Ta is a great TA.

Dr. Talbot is amazing!  This class was very interesting and very informative.  However, if you want an A, you're going to have to work for it.  But with much effort, it is not hard to get an A in the class. I would recommend this class to all undergraduates who are interested in health professions! Remember, you get the grade you work for!

This teacher is amazing! All these other people probably did not put any effort into the class!  She trys her hardest to help everyone and for everyone to succeed!  She offers plenty of extra credit and her tests are very straight forward!  I had an amazing experience in this class!  I would recommend it to anyone!

She gives tons of extra credit, and I believe that's because without extra credit, 80% of the class would be failing miserably and the other 20% would be getting C's.  Nonetheless, I find her to be one of the nice professors on campus, which makes her highly approachable.  Biggest negative: some questions on the exams were not covered in lecture.

Talbot is the kindest professor alive. I wish she taught other classes, I would definately take another course with her. However, BEWARE... this course is not easy whatsoever. The lowest Upper Division grade I had was an A- before taking her course. Needless to say, that's no longer the case.

This class is tough, and there is no way around that fact... you are learning human development here!  There is a lot of information presented in a short amount of time, but the professor does her very best.  She pauses after every slide to take questinos and is very interactive.  She is, without at doubt, one of the best lecturers at UCR.

The teacher was very good.  But her tests where very hard.  The TAs did what they could to get everyone through it, but its just way too much material in a short amount of time.  And no curve.  Take the teacher, not the course. (Human Embryology)

Extremely difficult class. This should really be a semester course... way too much information. Not only do you have to memorize you have to truly understand the concepts as well. The T.A's are really mean
good professor.  hard class.

There is a lot of information that is given during lecture, and the tests are very difficult. But, Dr. Talbot worries a lot about whether or not the students understand the material and tries very hard to help students pass her class. It has been one of the most helpful classes I have ever taken.
embryology is hard.  the professor is hard.  the TAs are knowledgable but do not not enough.  her test is harder than the mcats.  oh, and there's no curve. =(
Not an easy prof.  Not very helpful

His class was just unclear. He often has a lot of typos on his exams and he doesn't really teach. He only reads off the PowerPoint slides word for word. WHAT A WASTE OF TUITION. If you are eager to learn finance you will by doing the problems and FIGURING IT OUT ON YOUR OWN! No idea how he is able to teach finance. UCR Step up your game!

Although I am able to manage to get an A from this class, this is all because I have put a lot of hard work. Like how other students have commented, this professor only reads his PowerPoint word for word during his lecture. He gives limited practice problems (1-2 included in his PowerPoint) but will ask you to do upper-level questions in his exam.
THIS GUY LITERALLY IS UNPROFESSIONAL! SO MANY TYPOS ON THE FINAL! THIS PROFESSOR HAD SO MANY DAYS TO LOOK IT OVER. HARD COURSE.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You can get a good grade if you put in the work. He basically isn't really there for the students. He just reads off the slides. Not a great professor and his exams are difficult. Take this class if you have to but overall he doesn't connect with students.
The answer he gave to the students has a lot of mistakes, even some miscalculation. I don't think he has the ability to teach finance.
He doesn't really teach besides reading off the slides. I wish he did more in the class. He also doesn't grade anything which causes delays in grading. 4 exams and he drops the lowest.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: he doesnt explain anything. The hw is also difficult.

Prof Qadri is a mediocre teacher at best. He just reads word for word off his slides during lecture which is info pulled from the book. He takes attendance before every class. His grading for homework wasnt clear at all but his exams were straightforward because he provides a study guide and also gives a formula sheet on the day of the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Zhu is awesome! I had no trouble understanding his accent. Homework was from the book and was due every week. Midterm was easy with problems very similar to the homework. Final was tougher, but go to office hours and do your homework and you'll be fine. People applauded after the last lecture, that's how good this course was.

He was the only professor for 120A, so there was no voice. The class itself was mostly easy up until the final. The final was 1/2 things you would know, 1/2 things that you might know if you chanced upon the right material in the textbook and decided to study it or made sure you understood 100% of the course. Study early for the final.

He's not only a great teacher, but a great engineer as well. He's make the class enjoyable and interesting. The only concern that I have is that sometimes his accent makes it difficult to follow if you don't really have a clear idea of what's going on.
Easy class

Cool dude, cool class. He grades pretty fairly, the cutoffs are manageable. He makes difficult text easy to understand and makes what he expects in a paper very clear. If you ask for feedback he will be more than happy to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Christopher Queen is a really nice guy. Probably the nicest professors at this school. He also gives really good feedback if you request. 100% recommend.
Professor Queen made this class so fun and interesting! He gives excellent feedback and his office hours are really helpful as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Christopher Queen is probably the best English professor I've ever had!!!!! He truly cares about his students, gives good feedback and always made his lectures super interesting! He made the class about the supernatural and ghosts which was super interesting. He made us read interesting stories and overall it was an amazing class. I loved it!!!
He gives good feedback when you attend his office hours. He actually helped me improve my writing A LOT.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Quintela is an amazing professor. She makes you open your eyes to a lot of injustices that people of color face in many aspects. She has taught me so much and I feel honored to have taken one of her classes as an undergraduate. She has plenty of knowledge to share and you walk out of there with an entirely new perspective of the world.

Quintela is a wonderful professor. Definitely show up to class; notes are taken in class but not posted online. Professor Q likes to give pop quizzes based on reading. Don't procrastinate on assigned portfolios. And definitely study for her tests in advance.

Her lectures are clear and helpful but if you do all the reading it is essentially the exact same material down to the wording. I went to every lecture and really liked my TA, so overall this class was a great experience. She takes attendance randomly a few times during the year.
Lecture attendance is necessary since she gives random clicker quizzes.  However, this class is super easy because she also lets you drop 3/8 quizzes and 1/3 tests.

This course is pretty interesting. I really like how Professor Quintela drops one exam out of the three. This means that if you did well on the first two, then you wouldn't have to take the final exam. You have to read though, she asks questions on the exams from the text. Overall, this class is not very hard. The readings are pretty interesting.

This was one of the few classes I actually enjoyed at UCR. There's quite a bit of reading assigned weekly, but it's doable. As long as you read before the exams and attend lecture it's very easy to get an A in the course. Two exams account for a huge majority of your grade, the rest being short papers (1-1.5 pages) you turn in weekly on readings.

Professor Pyke is by far the best professor I've ever had. She is extremely knowledgable and passionate in what she teaches.  A lot of reading, and essay format midterms and final.  Readings and lectures are interesting, if you attend lecture, which is once a week, you'll get an A! definitely recommend taking one her classes, great professor!

I love Pyke! Lectures are 3 hours because they are once a week, but she makes them so interesting. She randomly takes attendance in lecture sometimes. Slides are posted online once the midterm is near. Lots of readings, but they are interesting for the most part. She pulls questions from the study guide for the tests.

I love Pyke! I've had her twice before! Lectures are 3 hours because they are once a week, but she makes them so interesting. Slides are posted online once the midterm is near. Lots of readings, but they are interesting for the most part. She pulls questions from the study guide for the tests.
2 take home midterms based on the  readings and lectures. The last one is an exam. All non cumulative. As long as you do the readings and go to lecture should solid.

Her class is very heavy on the readings and her lectures. She has two tests and a final and you finish in week 10. The tests are all essay style. She's very helpful and knowledgeable about what she teaches.
2 midterms and a final. Good professor.
Straight-forward. Lots of reading but interesting class.

Karen Pyke is GREAT; she is easy to understand. And there are no textbooks except, for a small book you must read. I bought mine at Amazon for $5. Attendance is mandatory and there is quite a bit of reading. There are 2 midterms and a final, but they are easy! And there are weekly papers due based on the readings but there are no grades for it.
Lots of reading but not hard or really long. No textbook is used in her class.

Out of my three SOC classes this quarter, this is my only interesting one.  Be warned though, this teacher is a staunch feminist at least in her theoretical perspectives about Sociology.  However, after some students ask her personal questions, you realize that she is actually pretty down to Earth and nice and not a crazy feminist activist.
Best SOC professor on campus!! Had her for SOC 142, 136, and 129. Passionate, knowledgeable, understandable. Ended up enjoying any material she taught. She gives you the reality of it.

Professor Pyke is awesome! Had her for 3 classes got two As & a B without even reading. Go to lecture, take notes!! Midterms are straight from lecture notes. Two midterms and in class final. Shes very clear, straightforward on the material, and organized.She is very knowledgeable and intelligent with the material. Loved all the material she taught!
I really enjoyed having Professor Pyke.  She is very organized which makes the class a whole lot easier.  I would love to take her again.
She talks a lot, her tests are confusing. But she gives you a list on "possible essay questions" and two of them appear on the tests.. Easy class.

she likes to talk. she doesnt put her notes or slides up online bc she doesnt want anyone to "steal her ideas." 2 midterms, no final, an interview and 2 pages papers due every dis. overall not a bad class, there were moments that i wouldve rather spent my time doing something else and she would tend to put me to sleep.

BEST professor at UCR. She is helpful, nice understandable and gets her students. 3 midterms no final. all the readings are online. study guide is exactly like the midterm. gives surprise pop quizzes but give you the answers to them anyway. interesting and helpful. i would recommend her to anyone!

She is an amazing professor! She is very enthusiastic and knows her stuff. Her lectures are crystal clear and extremely enjoyable. Attend lecture religiously and you will get an A. Material extremely easy. I would take any course taught by Pyke!

So far, the best Soc. Professor I've had at UCR. Esp. with Asian Americans, this woman knows her stuff! Started posting study guides up this quarter and as long as you do the readings (know the main points-even through skimming) and or going to office hours, you're good to go. Very interesting class. Learned a LOT.

So far, the best Soc. Professor I've had. Esp. with Asian Americans, this woman knows her stuff! Started posting study guides up this quarter and as long as you do the readings (know the main points-even through skimming) and or going to office hours, you're good to go. No textbook, just online readings. Very interesting class; learned a LOT.

She is ok. Curves at the end. Doesnt post the notes online so that is one thing that really sucks about her classes. Way TOO MUCH reading and a lot of requirements for the class. I would not take her ever again.

Thought this course would be rather boring but she made it so interesting. I love her sense of humor. She really respects students and cares about them. Can't believe the other comments on this site. Think they must be the angry, lazy jerks I hated in class. If you try, you will do well. If you don't like to learn, don't take this class.
Learned a lot! Loved her.
easy easy easy! just go to lecture and discussion and take good notes. you dont even need to buy the book!
Enthusiastic, knowledgeable, and personable.

Overall a pretty good professor who knows her material. Attendance is important since she does not post notes online. 1 midterm and 1 final worth about 80% of your grade. The rest of your grade is based on discussion which is mandatory but fairly easy since all we did were talk within small groups about the reading. 1-2 pg paper due every week.

very interesting course. if your're lazy, unorganized, and don't like to think critically time to time, this is not the course for you. but if you have no prob. doing those three things, you'll be fine!

Probably the worst Sociology Professor at UCR.  Merely uses her students to further her research for her book, lectures are extremely boring, and her tests only reflect the reading which she does not review.  Avoid this professor at all costs.

worst profe ever!!!!there is no point of attent her class because you are going to fail no matter what!! dont' take her class!! her test was very VERY hard and i didn't get anything !!!!!! i never had D in my life until i took her class!!!
Awesome professor...probably one of the best, but her class requires ALOTS and ALots of reading.
Extremely easy class, however the lecture was very boreing and unorganized.  Discussion was 20% of your grade but a waste of time.

Her lectures are pretty boring, I never used the textbook she assigned but I read all the e-reserve readings and i got an A-, just make sure to do everything in the section bc it counts for 20% of ur grade, and jus pay good attention in the lectures and it wont be too hard.

Wonderful prof, learned a lot. Gives a huge opportunity to keep high average in class by appointing 20% for discussion. However the midterms are very reading specific. She gives many great opportunity to work with her research to shine up your resume.

Don't read the book. Just read the summaries at the end of each chapter. Make sure you get good lecture notes from someone if you don't attend. The class is out of only 100 points and the A was a 93. She offered generous extra credit opportunities on one of the midterms and the final. (10 pts for each test). Easy A.

As a professor she may be rude, anal, uncooperative with her T.A.'s , but really...she is not bad as a person. This class is WAY TOO easy. If  you know that everything in the U.S. is ****, classist, or ****, then exams should be common sense to you. Skim through the book, listen at lectures, go to discussion...you should get an easy A!
there's no point in studying... you're going to fail either way because her questions are way too random and ambiguous. AVOID HER!
OMG!! SHE IS BOMBBBBB!!! I did nothing honestly....and got A-....all the papers you turn in are graded by your classmates....Easy going teacher funny jokes around very very interesting lecture!!

I have no complains. May one: she doesn't put up any slides/notes, just reads of her notes. The readings aren't bad, and the discussion sections are interesting. Exams are somewhat challenging, but manageable. 1 midterm(40%), 1 final(40), disc(20), curves at the end

This is an introduction to Sociology, but she does not take the time to make sure we really understand the material. Her lecures are so BORING. She should set her lecture notes on a power point so more students would stay awake in her class. She also makes a big deal about small concerns, such as people sitting on the back of the classroom.

i absolutely dislike this class passionately. she is unbelievably RUDE and anal. i hated going to her class. the things she requested from the class was nonsense..her exams are horrible so if u fail one ur screwed since the class is out of 100 DO NOT TAKE HER. her lectures and discussions are very unorganized TAs have no idea wat is going on either
She SUCKS!!! The class is very confusing and she is NO HELP.  DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS
she is very moody and erratic.  pretends she knows about asians but doesn't have a clue.

She is very hard. She tries to deliberately trick you on exams. She "claims" that she is NOT one of those professors who expect you to know little details from the readings but she does. She asks trick questions on her exams. She only curves the class a measely 4 points. She is the only soc prof that is actually hard. Stay away. I know I will......

She barely gives any points for the class.  For the whole quarter, the point toal was 100.  It makes it very difficult for students to make up for one bad test.  You only have 3 things that go into your final grade: Midterm, Discussion, and FInal.  That's it.  She also seemed really disinterested in her students and not eager to help.  Avoid her!

Class seems fun and interesting.  Just wait till the midterm and final. Memorize everything you read to ensure yourself an A.  Reading is overwhelming and impossible to remember it all.  Final was really hard.  It's like she opened the book, put her finger on a sentence, and made a question out of it.  I wouldn't take her again.

No Comments
Great professor. caring, concerned and passionate about her work!
No Comments
she roxorz. but the material sick overlaps with the psychology of women course. her feminism shines through greatly.

her class is very boring. she goes on about feminism practically and seems to hate the male gender. go to discussions to turn in hw, but its pointless cuz TA can't effect ur grade. overall boring, but easy class. dont go to class juss disc. and pulled a B

her class is boring. almost fell asleep everytime i went to that class. overall very easy. take home midterms and just pay attention in class. the only fun thing about her class is the panels. very interesting.
easy class. just tedious work. take home mid-term and final, will be based on lectures and articles. try and go to class. some of the things are interesting.
I had her my freshman year and did great.  Really good professor.
No Comments

Professor Quezada is a students professor.  Easy going, but really reads papers, sometimes twice.  I appreciate that he would give us several short breaks for this long class.  Weekly short papers, and a final.  I really enjoyed the film selection, it has opened up my mind to different typesforeign films.

This class was really enjoyable, because he is animated in lecture. It makes lecture really entertaining. Professor Quezada was easily accessible and you could tell he really cares for the students.  Although he is a really nice man, he is really direct when making comments on papers. Some people are put off by that.

I am taking him right now for 1914-45. He is super easy going and lectures conversationally so it is really tolerable, especially for a 4 hour class. A little unorganized but it seems to be controlled chaos. Really just an overall smart person, and is very welcoming. Would take again.

very easy going professor. quick on his feet, and bright IMO. my only thing with him is that he is very unorganized, and rambles.  really takes away from the class when he goes off topic.  you can tell he hasn't been teaching long.  helpful, e-mails back quick, and gives extra credit.  hard grader, but fair.

This prof is the man,young &smart!He let lots of people crash the course which is unheard of@UCR.The best part about him is his hilarious pop culture references.He called the U.S. foreign policy the Sharkisha of countries,&once showed a doc of the Alamo and said if someone had recorded that battle on video tape they'd be yelling WORLDSTAR!TAKE HIM!

Professor Quezada was very helpful.  I felt bad because about half our students are International Students,  so he kept having to repeat himself because their English was not perfect.  Other than that being a little annoying, he was hilarious, very kind, and knowledgeable.  Admits when he doesn't know something which is rare.  Would recommend!

Professor Q is super funny!  He made my transition to American college fun!  Word for cat in Chinese Maow and he says like Mao Zedong?  LoL. Whole class laugh.  Also stays after to help with students who don't understand.  Answers emails fast and is young and fun and cool.  I like him for ISE History He's A-ok.

I am Chinese student now at University of Washington, but took ISE History Class at UCR over summer.  He is very funny and shows lots of videos.  Sometimes not clear but I don't speak English good.  He is very nice and helps and ate lunch with us.  He makes us laugh a lot.  Makes fun of all countries including China.  Wrote FREE TIBET on the board.

I feel bad because he came in about halfway through the quarter to replace Dr. Simmons.  We didn't have much time with him but he pretty much just followed the same thing Simmons was doing.  I think he's a graduate student but he's very easy going and funny.  Comes off arrogant at times, but you can tell he wants everyone to do well
young. really laid back. seems like he wants everyone to do well. rambles off a lot but it makes class more interesting.

Cool guy, really young and easy to relate to.  Easy to talk to and understanding and makes a lot of pop culture references.  Somewhat liberal but its more sarcastic comments so its tolerable.  All multiple choice tests and 1 paper, and a curve.  Just a general G.E. class that you have to take and attend.

Overall the best math teacher I've had in my life. His lectures are incredibly clear (not mandatory attendance), he's incredibly friendly, and his expectations are quite clear. He's very approachable for questions as well. The practice tests and quizzes adequately prepare you for the midterms and final.

Shane is the goat. He's probably the best professor or TA you can have for math. He explains concepts super clearly and his office hours are SO helpful. if you go to office hours regularly and study, it's an easy A.

Even though he is a new math lecturer at ucr, he does a very good job of explaining topics like antiderivatives up to things like trig sub. There was 2 midterms and a final and it was really similar to problems he did in lecture and the practice midterm. He is so approachable and understanding and I really appreciate how nice he is.

Shane is such a chill and great lecturer. One of the best lecturers i had in my two quarters here. He made integrals and trig sub so easy to understand. Two midterms, both 60 pts. Final is 100 pts. Very reflective of the material and he does a great job ensuring that. Hw was due at the end of the quarter. Overall, was a great experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Shane was genuinely the best math teacher I have ever had, and the best professor i've had in college so far. If you're able to take him for math, DO IT PLEASE. He genuinely knows how to teach it and tells you how to exactly prepare for it.

This professor is genuinely the best math professor I've ever had. He explains concepts in a way that's simple and efficient. He made sure that everyone had access to the help they needed. His midterms/ finals were very similar to the practice exams he posted for us to study. His lectures and office hours were super helpful and easy to understand.

this is the prof you want. one of the best professors in the entire uni. There r 2 midterms & a final, lowest midterm gets replaces by final if u do better on final. His midterms are SO EASY because his practice midterms REFLECT THE EXAM SO WELL! Overall an easy class and office hours are helpful! He also lectures really well for you to understand!

He is an incredible professor. His lectures were so clear and the way that he presented the material made it much easier to understand an already tough subject. Quite possibly the best lecturer in the UCR math department. His exams are closely linked to his homework and in-class examples so going to lecture is really helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Rankin is a great professor.  He made sure to make his expectations clear and would test us on those expectations. His lectures were filled with important information and never felt muddled.  He made the subjects more digestible without sacrificing details.  Overall, an effective professor who made the subject itself enjoyable.

Long, text-heavy slideshows are analogous to the course textbook. For tests, you have to remember basically everything from the slides. Intense study before tests needed. For project, get feedback during office hours or you will face intense critique during your presentation. Project requires a lot of self-teaching. Nice guy, but a tough class.
go to lecture for extra credit, curves a lot

Avoid this course if possible. The professor is a strict grader, provides 400+ page slide for one midterm exams, and gives lengthy written tests. Lectures are boring, attendance is monitored, and the materials are poorly organized, making studying difficult. He expects students to go through overwhelming content, making exams tough to prepare for.
Exams are not graded strictly. Got lot to learn. There is an image about professor that he is very strict but in fact he is not. Cloud computing was one of the top 2 courses I attended at UCR.
Beware of time-consuming homework. Other than that the class is exciting and easy to follow.

Copying slides.
Out-off-date and far away from parctice knowledge.
Useless exams.

TAs are fine.
Expects research based projects in a short time frame. After reading all the other reviews on here, I wonder how I made the poor decision of taking his class. Too many red flags.

Professor seeks to torture students rather than creating a learning experience. Boring class with not many take aways. Course load is very high. It would be better if this course was offered by someone else since cloud computing is omnipresent.

Seeing the reviews here, I understand why people had not had a good experience - networking isn't always interesting. As someone who had a different - and positive - experience (and currently in networks industry), I enjoyed his class and network topics. The topics are abstract but he always is willing to explain concepts if you just ask him.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Literally all the material (labs, lecture slides, content, hw questions) is taken from other sources. He adds nothing to the course. Boring, and uninspired professor. The book is 2x more interesting to read and 10x more informative. Difficulty is average, leaning easy.

He liked to take many slides from many sources that make it hard to get his point. Also, He marked your class participation. Unfortunately there is no alternative lecturer teaching this class in different quarter. It is better to stay away.

Presents other people's papers in class behind the podium without moving a millimeter, but expects you to give a revolutionary presentation. Says the only reason we have exams is because otherwise no one would show up to class. Can 100% confirm that. But if he knows that, then he should fix the problem(his teaching style) not torture his students..

He is the physical manifestation of boring. Lab is a programming assignment every week. Midterms are hard because he takes a random slide from class (300+ slides per test) and makes you remember what was on that slide. It's usually a diagram. Actual questions are the hard ones that are taken from the internet, he does not make his own questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Stay alway from KK's courses, lots of lectures and slides. Hard to get the point, usually two mid term and a final. Assignments are also difficult because you must learn many other things by yourself.

I had her for my freshman honors seminar class (HNPG016, wasn't an option), and I thoroughly enjoyed it. Dr. Radi is such a nice and caring professor. She loves to teach, and my class was very interesting. I learned a lot.
Amazing professor! She's very passionate and wants you to succeed. Go to the lectures, take notes and memorize and you will be fine! Exams are all free response but incredibly fair. Highly recommend!

Best professor at UCR. Kind, caring, and approachable. Extremely entertaining lectures, she made me excited to learn. Exams are hard but very fair. Will need to know every lecture slide. Lots of templates to memorize, but it makes the learning easier. Lots of opportunities to get help. Quizzes every week. Don't cram, the content is very dense!

Amazing professor, records her lectures and understands if you can not attend. Very clear and cares about her students, I really enjoyed how she connected concepts in class to real life (I now hate the keto diet)

really good professor who is passionate about biochemistry. lecture and material are very dense so be prepared, but she prepares you well by assigning homework with unlimited attempts, and templates for the pathways. there are quizzes in the discussion but the TAs go over what will be on them. exams are always fair and frq.
One word. GOAT!

Absolute best prof I've ever had in my time at UCR. Made me regret not being a biochem major. She is fair, great lecturer, genuinely wants you to succeed, and has the best TA's on her team as well. Lecture slide heavy when it comes to the exams.

She is a teaching professor, so her section is very engaging. She's fun, clear, and is very transparent with what she wants you to know. Just understand the stoichiometry really well. 2 midterms and 1 cumulative final. We also had an amazing TA (shoutout Melia), so the discussion quizzes were fair! Homework was multiple attempts

3 exams; 2 midterms (both non-cumulative) and 1 cumulative final. Quiz every week. Dr. Sarah Radi is an incredible professor. I had her for BCH100 and she hyped up her BCH120 course so I tried it out. This course was so interesting and having her as a professor kept me engaged the entire course. She is so fun and truly loves what she teaches!

I took her bch100 class in the fall, and I'm currently taking bch120 with her too because I really like how she teaches material. Yea the material itself is dense but thats what comes with an upper division course. Her exams are all free response but the questions are fair, and all the material you need is in the lecture slides.
really good professor. there was a lot of material but if you study and understand concepts you should pass with a decent grade

Clear syllabus/expectations. Her quizzes are exactly what the TA's go over, her exams are a bit harder than the quizzes. Exams are structured around remembering and understanding content. She creates templates for pathways to help facilitate that memorization. Was one of those classes where u were rewarded for the time put in!

Great professor overall, funny and really generous regarding curves. 

LOTS OF PATHWAYS AND TEMPLATES TO MEMORIZE THOUGH, AHHHH

Dr. Radi's course was a fun one! She is an amazing professor and her love for the material shows when she teaches. Exam wise she is very VERY fair. I've never read a question and thought to myself, "when did she teach this?". She's a great person inside and out the classroom and is a perfect example of what a fantastic professor looks like!

1st mid term: 26% (avg 67%) 2nd mid term: 62.6% (avg 68%). Final 58%(avg 56%). Passed with C+.
Since our final average is kinda low, she curved the grades by a lot. 97% of the class passed. I bombed the 1st mid term with 26% by ended up passing the class. Just make sure to study and you will pass easily.

Wow!! One of the first core science classes I thoroughly enjoyed!! Despite its difficulty, and dense material, Lectures are explained very well. She brings great energy and prepares students for her exams very well. There wasn't one exam where I walked out and thought the test was not fair. By far my favorite professor!!
fantastic professor she is attentive and if you go to her lectures you'll be more than fine
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I was able to get 96 and 100 percent on the first midterms just by studying the learning objectives. On the final, I just could not bring myself to study the reproduction unit and I left that entire section blank on the final. Periods are caused by god punishing women for being witches for all I care, but I still got a 93% on the final somehow.
If you dont take her rethink your life. Almost 50% of the class got an A. If you thought Natalie Holt's class was easy you haven't seen anything yet.

Dr.Radi wants students to succeed. Her slides are very helpful and reflective of the exams she creates. She has weekly quizzes, but they were exactly from the lecture notes and the TA assisted with a review before the quiz. She works through all the cycles with us to help us memorize them. Would take her class again!

Material is DENSE however her exams are all free response but straight to the point.  She is not trying to trick you with the material. Best way I found to study was flash cards with main focuses being material on lectures that are a darker color and focusing on the learning objectives. Averages tend to be pretty high for good reason.
All exams free response. Information is very dense. She is a good person but difficult exams, personally. Lectures in relation to each other could have been more organized to better connect them all.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Radi was very interested in the material, which made the class more interesting overall. Its a hard class but she would tell us specific structures we needed to know/memorize and pathways we needed to compare or memorize. It was a little rushed towards the end, packing some very dense material before the final, but no other issues here (:
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr Radi is a great instructor, lectures were very informative and if you understand what was on it will you should be able to answer question for Learning Objectives. There were complains about midterm grading but grading still was fair. BCH120 is an UpperDiv so it is expected to be difficult.

Her lectures are very dense with at least 10 learning objectives for each lecture. No study guide, only study guide are the LOs which most won't be on the midterms/final. How she grades her tests isn't clear and she doesn't make it clear. All tests are free response so be prepared to be looking at your screen for hours on end. Avoid this class!!!

The material is interesting, but she can't present: she doesn't make her own slides and lectures as if it's her first time looking at them. She also "teaches" like a student, highlighting and annotating text-heavy slides as if preparing for an exam - miraculously somehow not narrowing down any of the content. She made this class unbearable.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Radi is enthusiastic and easy to understand, her online lectures are very interesting. However, she is not clear on what to know or memorize even when we specifically ask her. This class is very hard and she packs a ton of material into each lecture. Get ready to memorize a lot of information and chemical structures/pathways.

She only talks in French during lecture but her teaching style is good. Very kind and easy to reach. She makes participating easy, so just do it. She makes clear what will be on the exams so if you study and review the worksheets you'll be fine

She is very nice and helpful, the class is not as hard as you may think since English and French share similarities, making it easier to learn. There are weekly Cengage assignments, evaluations every Thursday, in-class group practice, and a final oral exam. So if you want a different foreign language experience besides Spanish, then please take her

She makes French so fun! She is so understanding of any circumstances that may come in your way. Her lectures were so fun and engaging. I was told French was going to be very difficult, but I was able to learn so much from her. She always offers help and is very encouraging to her students. The homework is very helpful as well. Do ahead of time!

Professor Ramos is one of the best professors I've had at UCR! She has such a passion for teaching and truly cares about connecting with her students. She made learning French easy and fun, and I will be taking more classes with her.

Prof. Ramos is amazing! She cares for her students and will reach out to you to make sure you understand the material. The course does proceed pretty fast, but it's definitely doable if you do the homework and watch the lectures.

Had Ramos for 2 quarters of online classes & she makes it easy to work at your own pace but also easy to reach out to her w/ ?'s. She obviously cares about making sure students have help learning the language by assigning helpful HW & taking extra time during oral assignments to make sure you're doing okay. Super grateful for her!

While we never got a syllabus, she was the most caring teacher. She arranged to have a note-taker because the Disability Center was not helpful at the time. She did things and went above and beyond what any teacher needed to do. She worked with me a lot because she is working with me to become fluent in French, and was so kind and caring to all.

She is incredibly receptive and sensitive to students' struggles w/ a new language and learning styles. She is thorough and engaging. She uses relevant and current cultural examples and words that students would be interested in using in every day life. She is enthusiastic and thorough in making sure her students want to learn. Take her if you can.
She is a great professor. Everything you need for the exam is on her study guides. She cares for her students.
She's an amazing professor! She is funny, connects well with students, and makes the classroom environment comfortable for students to speak up in.

Seriously happy I got her again! Her tests are a good overview of what we learned in class and she gives out study guides as well so there are no surprises! She's really clear and is a great person to ask for help for. Worth taking.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Jennifer is such a great prof, I would recommend her to anyone.  She manages to make the learning fun, and is very concerned about your progress. She is accessible outside of class and willing to find ways to work with you if you need help. She does use the textbook and the homework, but that is because it is helpful. Her tests are a good too.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Jennifer is a wonderful professor and person altogether. She truly cares about her students and getting them excited about the class. She has a relaxed structure and helps with class discussion as much as possible. Would take her again in a heartbeat!

Her teaching is so lax, that you won't really learn as much as you can. If you really want to learn french, I'd advice to only take french 1 with her. As it gets harder, she doesn't really enforce much and you don't learn a lot, making french 3 or 4 harder.

Jennifer is an AMAZING french teacher. I took her for french 2 and she barely spoke any english, but when she would try to explain what the word or phase she said in french she would give use clues for use to figure it out without translating it in english. and that is what i love about her. I wish she taught all 3 class, SHE IS SO GREAT!!!

Hands down one of the best french professors ive had.  Don't take her if you're one of those people who don't like to be called on in class, she makes it a priority to call on everyone at least once during each meeting to help you work on your pronunciation skills. Responds to emails very quickly, and will help you if you're having a hard time.

She is such a good teacher. I had taken a break from french for a few months but she made it really easy to get back into the swing of things. Also she is very approachable and ready to help you. Go to office hours and just talk to her, it will really improve your french
Jennifer is a very excellent teacher. She is very engaging and likes to discuss all things French. If I could I would marry her since she is so hot.

Great teacher, very helpful and loves to see her students succeed! She is always willing to help you in class and during her office hours. She is very funny and is extremely smart. OH AND SHE IS TOTALLY ONE OF THE HOTTEST WOMEN EVER!

She is super helpful, since she will grade your writing assignment during office hours or after class before you turn them in. Her tests are based on her lectures. She is a great lecturer, makes class fun and attendance is mandatory. Someone said she looks like Kate Beckinsale,but Kate doesn't even compare. She is the definition of perfection :}

First of all let me say the films were great. Unfortunately the instructor doesn't know much about film  or theory so the discussion was at a very low level. Also, wants to be liked so if you act like you like her it's easy to get a high grade.

She puts you down indirectly:( She spent the final day of class not reviewing for the final, but asking how everyone feels about her and her class.  I wish she would have talked more about the concepts and rules.
she is such a great instructor for languages. she makes you feel comfortable enough to speak in class, which you will do on a daily basis. 2 words: ma bimbo.
A fantastic teacher. She is very enthusiastic and easy to learn from. I would recommend her to anyone who wants to take French. She is probably my favorite teacher at UCR.
What a beautiful woman. Fantastic Class. Would change my major just to see her everyday.
A very fun class, a very cool teacher. Enough said
great professor. You use the text book alot. Her test are not hard just go to class everyday and review your notes. I took all of my french classes with her.
No Comments
She is very nice and helpful. She is also very humorous. If you problems with the material see her during her OH.

She's really cool. :) Like, down-to-earth. She's like 30 so she's young. pretty. fun. The class focused on a novel and a bit of grammar. I like French a lot but I lost interest in the class for some reason. but doesn't help that it was my last class of the day =/ Just do the work, though, and you'll be fine. 2 oral exams. 2-3 written exams.
She really cares about the students learning and she is extremely helpful in everything she does. just go to class and you'll get an A

I've had her for three classes. She's super easy. Homework is done online and due every two weeks or so. You can probably do it all in 2-3 hours. She is awesome. But sometimes, she is too awesome. I don't remember a thing that I learned because she is so lax about everything. I wish she would be more challenging.
Great teacher, I recommend her to anyone looking for a foreign languge.
Great, enthusiastic teacher. She is clear and tries her best to help the student understand the materials. You won't regret it.
Very young, energetic, outgoing and beautiful young woman.  Amazing teacher and just seems like a cool person.  You feel like being friends.  Hope she is doing well where ever she is.

She was our substitute teacher since our real teacher got sick. Anyway, she is very easy and understandable teacher. She also an easy grading teacher. Best of all, she is hot, and she looks like Kate Beckinsale, not the Beckinsale with the long hair but the short hair from Underworld movie.
This professor is the bomb.. I can say that there's more to life than psychology. This was soooo much better than MGT 144!

Jennifer is a very nice teacher. She is always helpful and nice and cares that we do well. She is a little self-conscious at times, but otherwise she is totally cool and after all she is only like 10 minutes older than the people that she is teaching.
She is such a great French teacher.  She is really clear and nice.

Jennifer Ramos is an awesome french teacher.  she is very helpful when you do not understand something.  She really cares about students.  My friend says she looks like Neve Campbell.  Does she?  A little bit.
You couldn't possibly get a better teacher than Prof. Ramos, not only is she an awesome teacher, she's also a great person. A semester/quarter with her and you'll have the tools to go far in life.

I got an A in her French 1 class.  Not only that she gave me her FUTON BED FOR FREE! A fairly new one too.  Also, shes so incredibly beautiful and easy going.  She has that sweet look to her.  Amazing smile.  Too bad shes not at UCR anymore.  Oh and she has great hair.
she is a very nice teacher... and whenever you need help, she's there to help you. i highly recommended her!
most beautiful english teacher i've ever had... =)
She's awesome. Loved her class.

Very nice professor with rich of knowledge and experience for both industry and acadimia. You cannot imagin how prof Ren can make thing easier and very clear in his class. Not hard to get an A, but you need attend class first.

reviews.comment: CS/EE120A is generally an easy class for most students. Seems to be one of the easiest upper division classes you can take for an easy A. Lectures are basically a repetition of CS61. We were allowed cheat sheets for our midterm and final. The only painful part of this class were the labs.

Professor is solid. Class is dense with 3 sections: entomology, anatomy/physiology, and plants. It's a weeder, but everything is in the slides. Study them repeatedly. Exams are 30 MCQ, non-cumulative. Lab is boring but easy and barely boosts your grade. Open-note quizzes help cushion overall performance.

Nothing wrong with his teaching, the class itself required a lot of memorization. However from what I've heard other professors made the class way easier. 3 midterms, no final, 6 open-book/notes quizzes.
save yourself

He is very rude and hard to communicate with. He is not lenient at all, and the class is difficult. Also the lab and the lecture have basically nothing to do with each other. He yelled at multiple students throughout the quarter and wasn't friendly. There is so much material, his exams are on specific examples that he barely mentions in class.

reviews.comment: He was pretty rude the whole time, and my friends and I did not want to go to him for questions because of that. His class is three midterms, no final, but he told me that I am not allowed to know what I got wrong for the last midterm, which I think is unfair. Tests all based on lectures; if you know the lecture material, you'll get an A.

Knowledgable professor and pretty funny too. Lectures were pretty interesting and discussion was't bad. Some questions on the test are kind of tricky but if you study, you can get a A or B. A lot of people who complain are those who study the day before or don't go to class and expect to do well.

Omg, worst Gen Ed I've ever taken. I barely got a B+ and I studied more for this class than my upper divs. AVOID this teacher. His tests are super nit picky, and makes you second guess everything by putting trick questions, and I went to 90% of lectures. The other ent teacher is the easiest A ever, get him if you rly want to take this class.

Though Attendance isnt mandatory, treat it like it is because all valuable information (which will be on the exams) are given then. He can be funny at times but when its a long lecture it can be very boring. He is very responsive to emails which is a plus. Overall he isn't a bad professor, its the structuring of the class/curriculum thats bad. 6/10

reviews.comment:
For an INTRO course I took as a 1st year, oh my god.
Redak is funny but really wants you to know A LOT. ATTEND CLASS and take DETAILED notes/use the readings since the slides alone aren't good for studying. Expect to study everyday when an exams coming up and memorize tons of traits and orders. the final isn't cumulative.. but don't risk ur sanity.

my GOODNESS this class was DIFFFFFICCUULLLT. Gotta memorzie every fact possible and feauture about bugs. average for this class was pretty low btw. you have to FIGHT hard to get an A in this class. Even though attendace isnt mandatory, show up or your cooked :)

oh my god...

DONT take this class if u just want an easy A lol

He's really funny and his stories/commentary make the information easier to memorize. Genuinely a good experience showing up to his lectures.  It's a lot of information but he has minimized it as much as possible. The class will be difficult if you're not good at memorizing a lot of information or just aren't that interested in bugs. Study!

Etnm 10 is one the hardest that I've taken at UCR. This class required me to memorize many insects and their characteristics which are not what I'm good at. If you plan to take this class, I recommend that you should have a photographic memory our a deep interest in insects. Your life will be suffered without these abilities.

reviews.comment: If you want to spend a lot of time studying this class is perfect for you.  This class is characterized only by memorizing random insects.  The start is knowing their build and different parts of different insects.  The next is all the different insects around us, appreciate the first unit.  Go to class, he gives extra credit once.  Good luck :)

Biol5B is a lot of content and Dr Redak made it clear and understandable. There were weekly quizzes that are open note and textbook that were useful when studying for the exams. The class consists of three midterms each 30 questions that were similar to the quizzes.

Struggled in this class but not because of Redak, 5B is just a lot of info. Come prepared to memorize and know every detail of lecture. Tests are difficult and averages are low but he doesnt curve which kinda sucks. Be ready for lots and lots of slides and no curves but otherwise pretty straightforward, tests are lecture content pretty closely.

Really funny and super sarcastic. Online quizzes every week, three 40-question MC tests (really straightforward), a project where you have to find bugs, and discussions are mandatory. Go to the lecture and write everything he says bc the slides don't give you a lot of info. Use FLASHCARDS, that's what I did and it worked, but get ready to study.

I took this class to fulfill my biological science requirement. There is one online quiz per week and three 40-question multiple-choice exams. If you take notes in class, you will be fine. The discussion sections consist of a worksheet for attendance. I would highly recommend this course if you want easy bio credit.

Hes a good professor, reads off the slides but talks about note worthy info off the slides. Doesnt care about your grade if you dont care about his class. A lot of memorizing but its doable. No homework but in person midterm and final and also mini quizzes throughout the week. Gave us no lecture days at one point due to the thanksgiving weekend :)

Redrik is funny and interesting to listen to but this was the hardest class I've ever taken. You need to memorize about 5-9 pages of content for each exam, the first exam is bug autonomy and the last two exams are bugs orders and you need to know EVERYTHING for about 50 bugs for each exam. There's like 10 open-note online quizzes. AVOID THIS CLASS

HORRIBLE!! Attendance and note taking is very important to pass the class. Provides the lecture slides, but attendance is required in order to memorize everything and pass the tests. Discussion class is very far from campus, so be prepared to walk.! Overall okay class, funny professor, but too much memorization involved. :)

Taught plant section of bio 5B. Hard quizzes. You really have to think about plants in a different way which I hated and found boring but I'd say read the book and attend OH if you can. Lab sort of synthesized plant concepts but for most students this wasn't there thing... Curve was small. I think the average before curve was C...
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He's very nice, but his class is difficult. A lot of memorization and there's no curve. There are 3 midterms (15% each) , no final. Weekly quizzes (35% total) and lab (20%). It's a difficult course, I suggest taking it with an easier professor, if any.

I didn't enjoy this class and had to end up taking this class pass/fail. Thankfully I passed. If you are bad at memorization, DO NOT take it. The class is based entirely on memorization of the insect name and characteristics. Three midterms and no final. Make sure to study for the midterms or you won't pass. There are also quizzes every week.

If you're thinking about taking ENTM010 with Dr. Redak for a breadth requirement I would NOT recommend. Your grade is all tests and quizzes, and his midterms are really difficult and specific. He is also short over email and doesn't accommodate students well.

3 midterms no final for us at least. Lectures were pre-recorded and posted on YouTube. Everything in lecture is in the midterms that are multiple choice. Study and get easy A! Only pain thing are the random lab assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He's a decent professor and his lectures weren't too boring. Took it spring quarter 2020 online. Class is very lecture heavy and requires lots of studying time. reviews.comment: Great professor, loves her work and getting to know the class. Took her in fall of 24, and still think about the class.

Not one mean bone by Prof Ellen! She is the absolute sweetest! Provides work, internship, E.C, community service opportunities for her students. This was my first time taking a SEHE class and professor reese absolutely loved teaching it. She is very kind and open to listening to everyone's opinions. It is a lot of readings and discussions but honestly easy to take this online course on the side of other classes. Just do the readings and you will be fine. 3 quizzes and couple assignments.

"Hey, queen! Girl, you have done it again, constantly raising the bar for all of us and doing it FLAWLESSLY!!!

Ok but fr, Dr. Reese is one of the better soc professors at UCR because she is always accessible & is committed to students' understanding of course material

Two 5 page papers and 2 mid-terms, but reading is essential, but the readings are short/interesting. No textbook which saves you $$. She comes across as shy/reserved, but she is nice/helpful!

I don't know how everyone saying she is easy. Hard professor, not helpful at all, and a hard grader. Had to rely on the TA instead of her. Went to her office hours and she gave me obscure answers. Worst professor at UCR.

OMG PROFESSOR REEESE IS REALLY EASY!!! ONE OF THE FEW CLASSES THAT I GOT AN A IN!!!! HER TESTS ARE REALLY EASY, THEY COME RIGHT FROM THE STUDY GUIDE... GOOD OVERALL!

I can see that she likes students, so I can also see that she wants her students to learn. She teaches really good as long as you keep up with her lecture, so that means you need to attend every one of her lectures because it is really useful for midterms and a final. Get at least "B" work on all works, then you could pass with a "B" or an "A."

This course was super boring but she's an easy grader. For the most part, her tests are straight from the study guide and she goes over it giving you the answers. She was a really easy grader for the papers.
She loves to get students into discussion.  She shows a lot of film clips.  She loves to hear students opinions.  The readings were all interesting.  I really enjoyed this class.

she was a great professor.  she tried to get students engaged in discussions and had small debates.  she wanted students to get involved with the protests (for or against) that were going on at the time.  the class was interesting but not too difficult.    i would reccomend this class
The class was easy because she posted her slides on iLearn and her tests were multiple choice, pulled directly from the study guide.

This class was similar to WMST 001. They even used the same book. Teacher + Lectures were interesting, it was just a litle hard to follow because it was a morning class at the UV. So it was very easy to fall asleep.
Lectures are torture, but she posts notes online and her tests are just memorizing stats trends and terms.  Attempts to stiumlate discussion are pitiful and lame.  Easy but boring class.
Very interesting -- doesn't just lecture, asks for student comments, even in a big lecture hall. Brings in lots of interesting anecdotal evidence and statistics.

She seems pretty easy, but then she also seems like a feminist and that annoys me, as a woman myself. Plus she says 'right' after every sentence like she's giving us the facts, right? Gah! So annoying!
Easy teacher, lectures can be a bit boring but she spells out the material so clear you'd have to be an idiot not to understand. Showed films in class, overall good professor and interesting class.

she's a great prof.  she does need to challenge the students more but she has good intentions.
