Really hip guy. He keeps you entertained, but he does like to pick on people once in while. He is very helpful and encourages office hours, he goes out of his way to help. He's the best English teacher i've had yet. Just do the assigned reading and you'll be fine.
No Comments

DO NOT take this class, unless you want a C. DO NOT think just because other people thought he was cool you should take this class. BIG MISTAKE! He grades what he thinks the answer is, there is not room for your own thoughts, he will tell you they are wrong. I STRONGLY RECOMMEND TO JUST STAY AWAY!!!!
one hipster teacher, had much fun in his class :thumbup:
He was an awesome teacher.. I highly recommend him
He has a great sense of humor! A lot of reading, and quizzes on the readings, not a lot of essay's. Attendance is important. I really enjoyed the class!
He is very funny and he speak French & Japanese as well as English.  Pretty cool teacher.

Prof. Sovero was 100/10; her lectures were very clear, focused, and didn't spend time on stuff that wouldn't appear on exams. HW is a good chunk of your grade and can get overwhelming if you procrastinate, but stay on top of it, and you'll be fine. Exams were straightforward and were similar to the homework and example problems in the lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor and person outside class. Does pollevs for attendance and extra credit. Course in general has light workload; 2 assignments every week which both take at MOST 2 hours. Keep in mind course is hard/weird to "self-teach" so it helps to pay attention in lecture. Gives 1 midterm and a cumulative final, all with formula sheets.

She is an amazing professor. She's knowledgeable and passionate about the subjects she teaches, and her lectures are organized and thorough. The pollev participation grade is annoying, but you can't win them all.

Her tests are open-note, just no Gen-AI, and that's very reasonable. I would highly reccommend taking her. [ECON 158 & ECON 006]

Sovero was a great professor who came prepared and would make sure that lectures weren't filled with useless information. Everything in that econ101 class was on the test but it wasn't "hard" to say. She knew what she was talking about and would own up to her mistakes, making sure everyone had a fair shot at a good grade in this class.

Prof. Sovero was an amazing professor in nearly all aspects. She had very clear examples when she teaches, the practice quizzes were helpful and looked similar to exams. Her midterm and final were very predictable and doable. She is quick in responding in emails and does a fantastic job in explaining the confusing concepts and is very caring.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She is caring and an outgoing professor, however she seems to be very unorganized. Seems to cancel class once every week or so (last second too). Exams are all free response and memory based (terrible for learning). Id avoid this class if you could, unecessary amounts of work for an upper div elective. Mid-professor gets a mid rating.

The class is completely in-person, and all assignments, tests, and presentations are done in class, so you need to make it to the majority of the lectures because she also takes attendance. She's a good lecturer, but her Exams are all T/Fs with questions that can be confusing; tests are also very memory-based. Overall, the class was a 3.25 imo.

You learn nothing useful in the class. She gives mcq exams which have no study guides so good luck. It is not easy. Awful class. She goes back on her word with her expectations and grade requirement. Dont take until necessary.

When a professor has a 2.6 average rating you better believe it. 

You can forget about learning anything useful regarding SCM because if you're not taking a memory-based exam you're doing a tedious group project with very little guidance or structure behind it. Oh, and she's always contradicting herself and confusing everyone with what she expects

The class itself wasnt hard but she graded soooo hard during the presentations, any little thing and she would take points off. Was very annoying but her homework and quizzes were simple and easy enough. Her final came with a studyguide and we studied over 8 different topics when it was purely math based... again annoying.

There are 3 group presentations. Doing the presentation isn't bad, it was pretty easy to complete. What i would say is her grading is hard and strict, she would mark off points for the wildest reasons and sometimes it wouldn't be as clarified. Exams were just tedious as there wouldn't really be a study guide to go off on.

BUS129. 3 presentations (only 1 minute of speech but you need to memorize it, no notes) 3 exams 50 questions T/F and if you get an A before the final, you can skip it. She gives quizzes for the chapters that are easy to study for the exams. If i had to choose her or Jasso, I would choose her. She's alright
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Everything was accessible online via canvas - lectures/exams/quizzes. Midterms were easy (t/f). No hw. Quizzes on canvas (multiple choice & attempts). CON: Final was HARD, cumulative but all math based, free response & wayy more complex than examples given in lectures, worth 35%. Nobody got a perfect score. Took all 3 hrs for 20 questions.
The only thing I found hard was her exam. Everything else was easy but that exam? bruh. I had no clue how to do that exam and barely passed the class. Avoid if necessary.

She's very outgoing and gives off sorority girl vibes. exams didn't reflect the assignments. If they did they were complicated. I gave her an extra point because she was able to accommodate my personal situation. Attendance matters as she gives bonus points at the end of the quarter if you attended regularly. She does curve though.

She was by far the best professor I've had. Super organized and her lectures always had me engaged. Her class is easy to understand in terms of its structure and she is super reasonable. Sohail explains exactly what will be on the exams (and sometimes even word for word). Very accessible and always willing to help. Would recommend her to anyone!

One of the worst professors I've ever had. Very unorganized and homework directions are unclear. Everything is half thought out, he reads off slides for the entire 3 hour lecture. Not only that there's a final group project which is "supposed" to help you for the edtpa, but we're literally already doing the edtpa??? He purposely drags on lecture.

The textbook is absolutely required if you want to pass exams. His lectures don't seem very organized or relevant to the exams. And he wasn't very good at communication, which is crucial for an online course (during the COVID-19 pandemic).

Exams were based on the required textbook. His lectures were unorganized, hard to pay attention to, and hard to keep up with. Sure, he seemed knowledgable about the topic and somewhat passionate, but the way he conducted the course didn't allow students to learn or feel that same passion.

Disorganized and failed to teach the material in a clear, understandable way. Lecture slides didn't follow a logical path of information and filled with overwhelming amount (paragraphs upon paragraphs) of information. Exams based on textbook, not lectures. This class had potential to be interesting, but Solis failed to ignite the flame.
Professor Solis was a great professor. He recorded his lectures and posted them on TopHat so that students can access them and do assignments anytime during the quarter.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: He's such a kind and accommodating soul. He really cares about his students and is really passionate about what he is teaching.
Dr. Park is a very kind and attentive lecturer. She makes sure everyone understands the material and shows that she cares about her students and what she is teaching.

Her lectures consist of the material being presented from the book so it's not a valuable use of time for class considering students who commute. Attendance was not being taken in person, rather it was taken from the activities through Canvas. Her exams are pretty easy as long as you take notes and study the material.
Assignments are fairly easy. Instruction needs to be improved, possibly online synchronous in the future? Consists of 2 exams, a research proposal, & few assignments plus quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Park was very understanding and kind. I took her class online and I found it very easy. There was an in-class assignment due every week which the professor helped with. There was also a midterm and final. We had quizzes and small assignments due each week for the discussion. All the assignments and exams were easy. I highly recommend her.

Professor Park was always willing to answer questions and asked for student input multiple times for feedback on the structure of the class and how she was lecturing. She even brought in multiple guest lecturers that she felt had a better expertise level on certain subjects. I thought she was super sweet and was extremely accessible by email!

This class was really boring. The professor has an accent and she didn't know how to explain the material very well. The exam should be pretty straightforward except for the fact that she struggles with grammar (it was a challenge to try to decipher what exactly she was asking in the exam questions). I would not take a class with her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: exams were extremely easy, not meant to trick you at all, and straight from the lecture slides. bad thing: last minute she decided the TAs didn't grade the presentations hard enough and had them regrade them, lowering a lot of grades. also never gave attendance extra credit like she said she would. but did include an extra credit quiz.
Inspiring, exceptional professor. Very passionate about her field. Maybe one day she will get a Nobel and I'll say I took her class!

I'm giving her a low rating as I believe her dishonesty overshadows how nice she is and how easy her class is. An A-was 95% we were not notified until after grades were out. The presentation grades were lowerd at the very last minute, Even though she herself did not watch our presentations, she determined that the tas who did were wrong
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Ignore the haters

There are 2 pop quizzes +1 pop extra credit quiz There is also extra credit polls for showing up. The people complaining dont show up to class and missed all of this. The class is so easy even if you dont study the amount of extra credit given is insane. No midterm or quiz question cant be found STRAIGHT from the slides read that and youre good!

She is an awesome professor - do not listen to the comments that tell you otherwise. She is encouraging and very approachable. She made content very engaging to learn, and brings excitement into the lecture hall, which was really nice to stimulate our brains and pay attention!

Sonali is one of the best professors at UCR. Made the class fun and engaging she really wants you to understand the material. 3 quizzes, 1 is Extra credit they are from her lecture. 2 midterms and a final. The exams are not to trick you she is straightforward with her questions. Review her slides and attend lecture. You will do great !

Her class was very fun and her exams were straightforward. I found the content interesting as well. Exams and quizzes are based off lectures, I dont understand why people complain about pop quizzes, if you dont fall behind on material you have nothing to worry about.

She is a great teacher.Bad reviews are there because students are lazy and cheated in her class and got mad she found ways to prevent cheating.Her tests are not tricky at all! You do need to study, but its not hard and she makes sure you understand.she cares so much for her students.Don't be afraid to ask her questions. offers a lot of extra credit

My experience with her class has been great. Lectures are easy to understand and the materials are simple and too in deep. She will tell you what to focus on. Exam questions are straightforward. She genuinely cares about her students. She is also very understanding if you reach out to her regarding make up for assignments.

I've never seen 20 year olds whine and complain so much about participation in class. Just go class. Do the polls. 3 quizzes, 1 is literally extra credit. They're so easy too, I'm convinced the low reviews are people who have never taken a college course before. Lectures are kind of boring but the tests are straightforward. She's also chill.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: one of the more enjoyable upper divs i've taken, she is caring and considerate and her exams are extremely fair as long as you put in the work and come to class which is very little to ask for.

Tests are easy because they are very fair to the lectures, they are simple multiple choice that are all memorization. However, you will always go to lecture feeling stressed at the possibility of there being a pop quiz, and the lecture slides have a lot of random pictures that relate to nothing, wish there were more words on the slides
Very good professor don't listen to them
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Chaturvedi is very passionate about her class. Her exams aren't easy but reflect exactly what she teaches in class and are fair. She is a little strict in class but not without good reason. Teaches well IF you attend lecture. Don't miss lecture and then complain. office hours are very helpful. try to learn and you will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Inspirational--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Def ignore bad reviews, this is a great class to take with this professor. She's not trying to trick you as long as you keep up with material/ just pay attention during lecture and quizzes are not bad. From what I hear she's not too personable but I never had to talk one on one so that shouldn't be an issue for the avg student.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Ignore the bad reviews, this class is super easy! Slides could use more visual descriptions as they can be picture heavy, but mostly easy to understand. Polls are EC. There are 2 pop quizzes worth 20pts + optional pop quiz for EC, but the quizzes are EXTREMELY SIMPLE as long as you stay on top of the material. Exams are easy, just study the slides

She is a great professor, easiest upper div class I've taken, Her exams are super easy. There are pop quizzes but she has an extra credit one at the end to help recuperate loss points. She's  a little annoying when it comes to online assessments but that doesn't make someone a bad professor.  great professor i am glad i took this class
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Ignore anyone complaining, this class is so easy. Everything youre tested on is straight from her powerpoints, there are 2 pop quizzes which are a free 20 points each and theres an additional quiz for extra credit. The accent can make a few sentences hard to catch, but as long as you understand the material on the slides youre perfectly fine! :)

bad professor overall, would not recommend taking her, rude to her students, creates a horrible learning environment, will not stop talking and moving people during exams for no reason which makes it difficult to focus while taking exams
Good professor

reviews.comment: Has pop quizzes which should tell you everything you need to know.
She is amazing, I would take her course again! Highly recommended!

She is one of the most fair professors, her lectures are very interesting, I learned a lot this quarter from her. On top of that she is very fair, she doesn't allow people cheat on the tests. There are few students who cheated on her test and she did make sure that the students know that they can't do that. I would love to have her as a professor!

Her tests/quizzes are not too difficult, but she's immensely pretentious. She takes pride in pop-quizzes always putting students on edge instead of giving breathing room to study on their own time. She also offered extra credit for students to snitch on others for cheating which is not cool. As students we look should look out for each other.

SAVE YOURSELF AND DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR!!! She gave pop quizzes in class when no one was ready that was worth a lot of points. My mental health suffered from her.

reviews.comment: Took her spring of 2024 for comparative virology. The material seemed very intimidating but she made it easy and her tests are not meant to trick you at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class was more stats focused than I expected for a research methods course. Seemed like half the class was struggling to understand the assignments and the other half thought it was easy. Chandler was very patient and always willing to help students one on one or in smaller groups if they needed further explanations.
discussion section with her are really easy.

Best class I've taken at UCR! Chandler was very caring and understanding, always encouraged students to ask questions and her slides were detailed and kept students engaged. As long as you attend class, the mini exams are pretty easy + the 3 hour lecture always felt shorter becayse the info was so interesting
Chandler is an amazing teacher! She was helpful, patient, and knowledgeable
Helpful for a basic biology class. Tests are not had as long as you study. Gave many extra credit opportunities.

This class has changed from previous reviews. Three midterms, and they each focus on one third of the course. No cumulative exam. Labs were easy and had no tests, only worksheets. He also said he would round lab grades if one lab was significantly lower, so if you get a bad TA just talk to him. Go to lecture, take notes, study. You'll pass, easy.

This class was by far the most traumatizing (3rd year). I barely passed and that was because of my participation in lab (i scored around D on tests). If you have a job or a life outside of school don't take this class because it requires a lot of hours of study. Also he gave us a quiz during the lab about something he had not gone over in lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Final alone is worth 30% not open note, and all based on memorization and its cumulative. Midterm 1 = 15% of grade and midterm 2= 15% of grade. None open note all based on memorization. Would not take again. Lecture heavy, memorize everything for a good grade. Small details on bacteria, animals, and plants. Weekly quiz in lab, all memorization.

WAY too demanding for an intro bio breadth course. The sheer amount of material you have to memorize for the exams is ridiculous, our final exam quizlet was OVER 700 TERMS. He doesn't provide a study guide, but instead says to pay attention to the highlighted terms - then half of the exam isn't even on highlighted information! Take another course.

Too much info to memorize for an intro bio breadth course. Attended all lectures and still struggled. Professor refuses curves on exams despite low class averages. As of winter 2023 he doesn't provide study guides and doesn't allow open notes for exams. 2 midterms and the final was cumulative (worth 30% of grade). Take different course if you can.

SUPER lecture heavy, no notes during exams though so you have to memorize like 10-15 vocabulary words per lecture and 2 midterms (that each cover ~7 lectures) + Final exam, if you need it for credit don't even try, find something less demanding for ur sake.

3 exams, weekly quizzes, lab also has weekly quizzes. Lecture heavy, very dense information. Professor goes through long, information loaded slides way too quickly for anyone to take notes in lecture(even typing). No curves, no open note exams, has asynchronous lectures. Attendance not mandatory, but recommended.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very lecture heavy expect about 60 slides per lecture. 2 midterms all based on memorization and they were not open note and no study guide provided. He always throws in the most random questions. One cumulative final so you need to study every slide. Labs were long and had a memorization quiz in each lab. A presentation in lab for week 10.

Lecture not mandatory (recorded and posted) 3 hour discussion mandatory but always finish 1-2 hours early. Weekly quiz, 2 Midterms and 1 Cumulative Final-NONE of the exams were open note, refuses to provide study guides and NO CURVES. Class test average is a C- and he doesn't care. Doesn't understand this is a GE and most of us aren't bio majors

I actually took Biology of Human Problems. This was my best professor out of all years at UCR. He is an amazing, understanding, accommodating, and compassionate professor. This professor can easily be approached and is the one you definitely want to befriend! He is awesome. He builds soft skills and kept the class interesting.

Solid professor. The tests are pretty fair on the material being examined but the final was a bit clunky and lengthy for me to care enough to do well on. The class had no curve but really there shouldn't be one as it was all online with relatively easy questions. It's the labs you have to look out for since some of those TAs grades harshly.

There are weekly quizzes for both the class and the lab, with 2 midterms and one cumulative final. We were allowed to use notes on all of his tests & quizzes. There are also lab worksheets. The class is fairly simple, though beware, as he does not round grades up. Lectures were never really mandatory, bc he posts the slides on iLearn.
the class is fairly easy but the midterms and finals are heavily weighted :/
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Clicker questions are in every lecture. Lectures are too long. 60 slides each. All slides are online which is great help. Holds review sessions lecture before exam. Posts clicker question answers. Only negative thing is that it is very lecture heavy so write notes ahead before class because he goes through them quickly in class. Weekly lab quizzes.

Really enjoyed the way he lectured. Class is pretty straight forward and so is he in what he expects. Says lecture attendance isn't mandatory, but you have clicker questions every lecture. Overall, I really enjoyed the way he taught and his lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Not much to say other than his class is very straightforward. The professor himself is also very straightforward. Just do your best in the class and you will do fine.
Explains very clearly, very helpful office hours, and willing to sit down and help. Nice guy overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The lectures were all online. Decent at most. Speeches were graded inconsistent and feedback was not helpful from TAs.

The professor only appeared for one day in September, so it's a class that's taught by a TA. The lectures are actually online, taught by the professor through videos. But the assignments overall were easy. TA in my class was sweet and understanding, so I never had any issues. A really fun and not-so-difficult class for my TFDP people :)!

Awesome person. Very enthusiastic; you can tell she has a passion for what she does in her video lectures. Patient and caring, gives good feedback/advice/help during office hours. 

If you take Intro to Public Speaking, know that it's done online via video lectures and recorded submissions. Not the professor's fault, but it is unfortunate.

Professor was decent, although it was an asynchronous class so we never had much interactions. In terms of the TA's, Kori was terrible! subjective grading, no clear grading criteria for the speeches, it's whatever she felt you deserved on the speeches she gave you. very inconsistent grading. and your grade is based 4 (3-4 minute) speeches.

Honestly one of my favorite classes I've ever taken. She is a great professor who is so organized, enthusiastic and good lecture videos. Your grade consists of lecture video quizzes , discussion participation and speeches. It's a fun class and easy if you do the work! Definitely recommend

This is a chill course that is also a very helpful one. There are mini online asynchronous lectures to do during the week, and one in-person discussion. My TA was very kind and gave lots of extra credit opportunities. Environment is very friendly and welcoming.

Note that she counts a 93% as A- not A! Class is heavily weighted on 4 speeches. Grades harshly but does not give advice on how to improve, seems like graders are looking for things to nitpick. Quizzes throughout lecture videos but can't rewatch section before taking quiz. Lecture videos are more about types of speeches rather than giving tips

Your grade is mostly weighed heavily on your 4 recorded speeches. The class is pretty easy. The only HW involved with the course is the microtutorials on canvas, the speeches themselves, & peer reviews. As long as you do all the work & attend weekly discussion in person, you should get an A. Also, some TAs gave EC if you participated in discussion.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Took this class and barely saw the professor throughout the whole quarter. Pretty much ran by the TA. Only saw the professor once besides the online lecture videos. Seemed really kind and understanding, though, wish I got to work with her more. Class was easy, though, TA was nice lol.

One of my favorite classes. Lectures are asynchronous, but Professor Speer is extremely engaging and her lecture videos are an easy and enjoyable watch. The prompts for the speeches you are to give throughout the course are diverse in both content and style, so there are many opportunities to learn something new.
Amazing professor, one of my favs at ucr.

Professor Speer is an excellent instructor with succinct and powerful lectures. I learned a lot from this public speaking class and highly recommend it in its current format. Course is online, so all speeches are done in video form. Section attendance is required but that's only once a week. Easy workload, fun speeches, great instruction!

Prof. Speer is a great professor. This course was asynchronous but the recorded lectures were very informative. It is not difficult to succeed in this course as long as you pay attention during lectures. There are no quizzes and tests just speech’s. Discussion sections are mandatory and are beneficial when it comes to writing speeches.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Even though the class was online this quarter, I loved Prof. Speer as a teacher. Her lectures, though pre-recorded, were really engaging and lively. This was the only class I really took time to write good notes for because everything she discussed was incredibly helpful. She was also really funny and it was clear she practiced what she preached.
her online course was good! She was super accessible through email and gives great feedback on speeches. I recommend her!

Professor Speer was great. She answers emails very fast and is always happy to help. All her lectures were asynchronous this year, but were short and entertaining to watch. The class is easy if you just try your best to follow the directions and watch the lectures. The discussion class feels a bit pointless, but easy enough.

Although I can honestly say I disliked UCR, credit where it's due; I had an amazing time in Dr. Speer's Public Speaking Class. Dr. Speer knows what she teaches and you will learn a lot. As a Business Admin Major, this class taught me more than any of my major classes combined. If you can only get 1 thing out of UCR, take this class with Dr. Speer.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Speer is great! However, her lectures aren't online so you need to make sure to go to class. If you have a lot of anxiety about speaking, don't take this class because you give three speeches that are a large part of your grade. If you think you'll be okay with speaking in front of your discussion, go for it! Super great class and not hard.

Not my favorite professor, but not the worst; def she's on the better side of that spectrum but this class was a public speaking class so I wish she didn't use the textbook so much. You'll be fine if you take this class, grading is done by the TA.

Professor Speer is a great person who genuinely cares about theatre and her students- doesn't really like Shakespeare, which is ironic seeing as she teaches a mandatory "Shakespeare in Performance" class for first years. Easy to talk to her, easy enough class and a warm welcome into the theatre department.

GREAT PROFESSOR. Easy class that consists of 3 presentations, midterm, and final. Gives a lot of great feedback and tips to actually help you do better and improve yourself. She is passionate and easy to understand. Do the work and perform well, youre expected to receive at least a B. TAs were awesome too.

Professor Speer is a wonderful professor. I absolutely loved this class and her. She's funny, makes the lectures relevant, is thorough and will go over the materials before the exams. First exam is MC test on the first 18 or so chapters of the textbook, second is a speech analysis essay, and last is the persuasive speech. Fun class, loved it!
Awesome. taking this class with this professor is a must

prof speer knows how to make the material not boring, but a majority of the class is taking notes and watching clips based on shakespeare adaptations for an hour and a half quiz on othello in the first few weeks; midterm is othello, textbook, and lecture; final is making an adaptation on a scene from othello
Professor Speer is funny and makes nervous speakers more comfortable with public speaking. She makes communication concepts more interesting by using politics and pop culture examples.

Professor Spear was a wonderful professor for public speaking. Her lectures were really engaging. The speeches we had to give were super easy. 2-minute speeches on whatever topic fit the criteria. No final exam but a very easy multiple-choice midterm.

She is a fine professor, but the class was boring. I wish she made the class interesting. The "textbooks" we used were not actual textbooks. We read the play Othello, and How to Read Shakespeare. The midterm was based on those two readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This class was mainly on 3 speeches, midterm, participation and self evaluation paper. I felt that the speeches were graded too harsh. I considered to myself this was an introduction class to public speaking so nobody can be perfect. The midterm was not bad as long as you studied from her notes and the textbook.

Speer is still a relatively new professor, but her long lectures were fascinating. I developed my delivery skills tremendously. Unfortunately, your overall grade in this class relies on which TA you have. My TA graded extremely harsh despite all the effort I exerted. Do not underestimate the written exam. Overall, Speer was a passionate instructor.
She helped me become so much more confident in public speaking! Tests are easy and as long as you put in effort, you'll get an A
It was great to take a class with Professor Speer. She is absolutely hilarious and though her class is in the evening, she makes you want to go to class because her lectures are that enjoyable.

She is an amazing professor, probably my favorite so far. She is very energetic, kind, and genuinely cares about her students success. I never skipped a lecture because they were so great and she taught the class with so much passion. Her tests aren't hard as long as you keep up with the reading, which isn't much, and go to lecture.

I love professor speer's excitement and passion for teaching, it definitely makes the class worth going to. She doesn't post notes so you basically have to go. Her assignments are very do-able, her TA's are all very understanding too. They get that most people are nervous when speaking in public. The textbook is also very interesting

With no prior experience or comfort speaking in large groups. I took the intro class and the advanced class. I have learned A LOT throughout the course. Though my speaking abilities are still average, I can easily say that Dr. Speer educates the fundamentals in a clear and organized manner. I would highly recommend this class and this professor!
Great professor! She's funny and makes coming to class fun. I expected to hate the class because I don't like public speaking but she made it one of my favorites.
She was a great professor! The only thing that makes this class difficult is if you have a fear of public speaking. But she tries her hardest to make it easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Extremely welcoming and friendly; Doesn't add unnecessary stress

She was a really energetic and entertaining professor. The class was designed to help us get over fears, become better speakers (in different settings), analyze what makes a speech good, and make improvement in each assignment. The book we needed was also funny, informative, and easy to ready, and it's one Ill be keeping with me. Easy class overall

While its an interesting class, the tests are pretty hard (avgs are in the 60s and 70s) and unsure about potential cutoffs aside from the syllabus.  Class is overall very dense material wise and difficult to do well if you are taking many other classes at the same time.  Manage your time well, and live and breathe plant anatomy if you want to get A

reviews.comment: Plant anatomy was terrible. Slides present wayyyy too much information for any student to remember. Expect students to regurgitate weeks of information on exams to most minute detail. Overall, extremely difficult class if you're taking with other time-consuming courses. Exams and lab practical make up ~75% of total grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Springer is great, she truly wants each student to do well. She presents material very clearly, but there is a lot of it. You have to study for this class in advance to make sure to have stuff down. Tests consist of identifying slides, multiple choice, matching, and short answer. The lab practical is more difficult than the ones in Biol104.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: really nice prof. she teaches really clearly and wants you to understand the material. you don't need any book. exams are based on notes, which are really straightforward. go to office hours if you need help or just to hang out. she wants you to pass!

***BEST, BEST, BEST****Professor Springer is THE BEST professor at UCR. She is so understanding, so patience,and so helpful. I couldnt make it to her regular office hours, and she would make time for me. Material is not easy, you must go to class. Go to her office hours. As long As you try, you will guarantee to pass the class.

Must come to class (and NOT LATE because she will call you out).  You take a lot of notes on her power point slides.  She's very strict and likes to act like your mother instead of a teacher sometimes.  Overall, she is fair and organized.

One of the finer UCR's Bio teacher. Her lecture is very organized and very good at explaining concepts. Homeworks are hard but they do a very good job at preparing for tests. Tests are a little too in depth but she ease up on it at the end.

Dr. Springer is a great professor who cares for her students.  Class consists of two midterms, final and one quiz every week.  Lecture and readings are a must to pass class.  If you liked biochem 100, you'll like her class.

He's a pretty good professor, very enthusiastic about the course material and clearly outlines what you have to do to pass his class. The class was asynchronous so there weren't that many in-class meetings, but the discussions held during were decent. He's fairly accessible outside of class and responds to emails quickly.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He is a pretty decent professor. His lectures were easy to understand and his little discussion homework assignment were easy. His tests have free response. YOU MUST ATEND HIS CLASS TO GET THE NOTES. He doesn't post them online and he doesn't let you take pictures of the, either. The book isn't necessary. Easy professor and an easy class.

There are 2 exams and together they worth 70% of the grade. They consist of multiple choice questions and free response. He doesn't curve grades. Lectures are mandatory because he doesn't post his slides. You can't take pictures of them either. Lectures are really boring. He doesn't sound passionate about his work.

Although he does tell you to buy a textbook, you won't need it IF you attend his class. Won't post slides online, so better bring  your laptop to class or write really fast. Lectures can be boring, but are very interesting. Discussion is worth 30% of your grade (or 40%, I don't remember) so better go to them. I took an intro class.

I respect him a lot because he shows real passion for his class. He also travels to Maya areas and shows pictures. Lectures can be boring, but usually they are interesting and notes are necessary because they help with the study guide and tests. Quizzes almost every week, but pretty easy. Just go to class and study and you'll get an a/b grade

Easy going, straightforward about what he wants and what will be required of you. Overwhelming amount of material to read each  week,  carve out plenty of time for these, in order to participate in in-class and REQUIRED online forum discussion.

Good professor and nice guy. Syllabus is clear and concise. Two papers and a final and hes clear about what he wants. There is a lot of reading and a discussion post every week. You can still get by without doing all the readings as long as you go to lecture. You still have to do some readings for the essays. I would take him again.
You really need to read the textbooks and there was a lot of it.

He assigns a lot of article readings and questions that goes with it, and it's part of your hw grade. These readings are crucial for your essays because he requires you to incorporate those ideas into your writing. He grades pretty fair. Attendance is mandatory and is part of your grade also. Overall helpful and informative professor.
Straight forward. Actually has experience in field.
Great teacher with fun activities and easy to understand. He taught section and knew the material better than the professor.

Makes you write two page paper every week to turn into discussion. I didn't really understand him when he was lecturing, i think he gives out a lot of work. He's not that bad of a TA...but i've had better.

Bio 119 is a tough class any way you put it. I had Springer for the second half and he explained concepts very well in class which helped confusing topics make sense. His exam and quizzes are fair and definitely doable if you put the effort in and do the practice problems. I did much better on his part of the class. Small curve (C+ to B- for me)

Prof Springer teaches the second half of Systematics. This half is similar to basic Statistics. He posts his slides online, but without attending lecture for his explanations you could easily get confused. He presents things at a nice slow pace, step by step. It can be a little dry but is very clear and helpful. He's a nice guy.
Very passionate in what he teaches. Such a inspirational character, very helpful if you have questions. I would definitely look forward to another class with him.

Dr. Springer basically reads off his powerpoint slides during his lectures, so lectures can sometimes get boring. MAKE SURE to do his practice problem sets and practice midterms, because they are very identical to the actual midterm questions. STUDY for the practicals, they can really boost your grade if you do well.

Springer is a great professor! The class is obviously difficult since it is anatomy. Just make sure you STUDY! I cannot stress this enough. The practicals are hard and go by fast. Midterms are challenging but fair as long as you put in time to study. I studied the lectures for 1 hour after the lecture were given and ended up getting a B+ good luck!

Nicest prof!! He really cares, but you have to put muuuch time into this class, your entire life into it since it is extremely time consuming. The midterms are hard, for me the practicals were easy except the last one, you have to practice with many cats since they all look different.

Professor Springer is very helpful and clear. Of course anatomy in itself is a difficult class but he makes it easy. He holds a lot of study sessions before the midterms and finals which helps a lot!!
best prof i ever had

he's straightforward and really nice. office hours is really helpful and it gets packed during exam week. lecture notes are great and the only time i ever used the book was once for lab. study early for practicals cuz those are actually harder than his exams believe it or not.
really nice and helpful. straightforward exams with questions that come from his notes, but his lectures are really boring.
Great professor. Slides are very clear and never had to look in the text. Exams are straightforward. As long as you studied the material you'll do good.
good professor. slides have a lot information and the class requires lots of memorization. Tests were difficult but read/memorize slides. lots of studying required!

Difficult class, requires lots of memorization. In the beginning, Springer mainly reads off slides, but attend class and pay attention! Material ties-in to later lectures. Study slides and lecture notes; not much emphasis on book. Tests MC with some short answers. Study early on for practicals; they require lots of memorization.
Great Professor, but class is difficult.  Exams are multilple choice. Read the book but concentrate on the lecture and slides. I got an A- but the avg. was C+ to B-.

This class requires A LOT of memorization! Prof. Springer is one of the best professors at UCR. He is an excellent lecturer and his notes are very dense. Didn't use book that much, just as a reference. Multiple choice exams are tough but if you know the material you will be fine! Nice curve too.

He really knows the material and explains it well.  Class involves A LOT of memorization, but it didnt seem too bad.  the practicals were kinda difficult, but do-able.  Didnt need the textbook too much for his class.  Most of the tests were the lectures and lab/discussion.  Overall, a good professor.
Great lecturer, knows his stuff. Study hard though cuz the tests are hard!
Really funny peer mentor, helps give us tips on basic college survival skills. His one-on-ones were fun and helpful. Nice guy.
This guy is too funny. Keeps us entertained by telling jokes and making fun of himself. Sorta rambles at times, and goes off on tangents, but he's great.
As a peer mentor Spencer is great! He is so nice and he is really helpful! So funny!

I took him for the lab course bch 102 so maybe he was a little different from a purely lecture course.  His final was the easiest I have taken at UCR and was exactly like the practice.  Reports can be epic and long (lab 3-6) so don't fall behind.  TA's for his portion were awesome btw. Average for final was in the 80s I believe.

Awesome professor. Very UNDER-rated. He is approachable and helpful, so long as you show initiative. He expects you to understand and know his Learning Objectives; his exam questions are verbatim from the LOs, which is very fair. Toss the book and stick with the notes. Stay on top of the learning objectives and you're set.

his lecture notes are simple, but exams are challenging since he really wants you to memorize bits and pieces of different cycles. not only memorize what happens, but also the stuctures, enzymes, reactions, everything in great detail! he's really rude during office hours and don't even bother emailing him. curve was super generous in the end.

Spindler didn't spoil the class and spoon feed them. You actually had to THINK about these things.  Not only that, but he gave all the questions he'd ask BEFORE hand. I mean how hard is that?  Me my friend answered those all in one night.  If it  hadn't been for this guy, our avgs would have been super inflated. Made my A that much more satisfying.

This guy sucked.  His slides are packed with info, and he just mumbles through them, with no emphasis on anything.  I did not learn one meaningful thing from this guy.  thank God he only taught half the class.  What is he doing teaching?
Intimidating during office hours unless you know the material WELL
this dude is crazy, he expects you to know eeeevveerrryyy ssiiiinngggllleee deeettaaaailll on the subject matter. glad his stuff was only 25% of the final. eitherwise, i would have failed.
No Comments
No Comments
Don't know why people are complaining. He gives you the exam questions!! Answer them, and study review each set at the end of each week. If you leave them to the end, your screwed.

This class is pretty straight forward ..but requires a lot of memorization.His lecture notes is note very clear and his test is not so fair also.he just randomly picked 5 questions among more than 150 questions from study questions!It will be a great class if u have a large capacity of memory!

Compared to Dr. Larsen, a very bad boring professor. Exams were biased and you have to know figures. Not very helpful in office hours and doesnt seem passionate about his material. Bad professor, should be kicked out. Class average on midterm was very low.
[pp
He refuses to answer emails and is really rude in person.
grades hard, notes unclear, agree wit what person below me has said 100%
Class average was very low.  Notes not always clear,several errors in notes.  Wanted much more detail than he let on.  Arrogant **** if you see him during office hours.

very good professor. gives you study questions which the finals are verbatim from. expects alot of detail, but gives you everything you need to know for the tests. adds alot of funny bch history stories (b/c he's THAT old...) that help make the subject material interesting. great prof!
No Comments

He is not a good teacher. He follows some standard slides with so many details and not much insight. He does not care about students really learning something and it seems he only teaches the class because he has to!!!
Seems like he wants to hurry through this or he has somewhere to go but he'll stop and give an explanation if you ask.  He gave a sweet curve when I took it.
No Comments
Doesn't care about his students.  Has the attitude that teaching a class gets in the way of real work.  He really has no time for students, so don't count on him helping you out.
Very kind professor and accessible. Literally uses questions from the practice midterms/final on the actual exams. Gives extra credit.

This class is difficult, but there is a generous curve, and it's possible to still do well in the class. I recommend studying ahead of time since the majority of your grade is exams. The professor is great and wants all of his students to do well, the content itself is just difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: please do not be fooled by the first midterm holy moly the material gets harder. i mean it is my fault for like studying last minute and hes a great prof for sure but the midterms and final exam is like graded pretty harshly
He is amazing at carefully explaining everything and very responsive to the class!

Professor Su is a great guy. Tests are hard because the material is hard. Does examples in class and wants to answer our questions and help us. One of the best professors Ive had at ucr. Curve is generous.
Good and funny guy. Could've done a better job at explaining and clarifying concepts. Exams were nothing like homework.

He's a really nice professor and offers quite a bit of extra credit. Tests were a bit difficult but if you get the average or above you will be fine. The final wasn't too bad. Practice exams are similar to the actual exams. I think he also used the clicker questions sometimes as exam questions.

I LOVE this guy. Great lectures where he explains things in an easy to understand manner and will take the time to make sure you understand the underlying concepts at hand and how they integrate with the course. However his test are much harder than the rest of the course. Highest average was a 60% but the curves are generous.

Honestly this class was a bit difficult for me not because of the professor but because of the foreign TAs.  Now it's not bad that they are foreign and I think that's great honestly-- its just... the accents are hard to understand.  Prof Su is great and nice.  Content is difficult and if you get a bad TA then you will have to work much harder.
Great Professor! Beware of caveats in his midterms/exams. DO PRACTICE MIDTERMS AND FINAL!

Professor Su gave amazing lectures. He explained a lot of difficult material well enough so that the students can understand what he is talking about. His homework and exams are difficult, but if you practice and keep up with the material, then you should be fine. Also, he gives out poll everywhere's for credit.

He is a very nice guy and good at explaining things, but he micromanages the students hard with polls everywhere and the homework. Some people may thrive on having the professor manage them but I found that it would often waste my time with busywork and required attendance when I could have self studied certain topics more efficiently.
Took his class during COVID. Online exams were hard but once it went back to in person the exams were straightforward and fine.

Really friendly prof, offers generous extra credit, and is relatable and easy to talk to. His tests were HARD and I personally struggled to understand things the way he explained them. LOTS of homework but if you do it all you'll be preped for tests. I didn't pass because I had personal circumstances but he went out of his way to help me catch up.

Chem1B I think is the hardest in the series I think, but he did a good job explaining concepts in lectures and poll questions were worth credit but sometimes a little odd. Lot of HW but it was good practice, practice ALOT. Practice exams were similarish. EZ quizzes, final was a pain cause how much recall it took, threw my A cause of dumb questions

Not a bad prof, but bad run class. Tons of hw, even on midterm/ finals weeks, exams are impossible and averages are 50's and 60's bc he doesn't test what he covers. Opened practice questions for the first time and it was like reading a new language. Submitting final grades without even inputting final scores.

Professor Su is a pretty good professor, he offers a lot of extra credit and even replaces your lowest midterm grade with the grade you got on the final. However, the midterms and final were pretty difficult with the average for my class being around a 50-60%, so make sure that you study and read. He also submitted scores without telling us.

Su was a pretty decent professor at the start of the quarter. His lectures were pretty concise and covered most of what would be on the tests. The midterms and final were a bit difficult, but they did reflect the class material well. He gives a lot of extra credit. The only thing is he didn't share or upload final grades to the students.

he does not lecture well, it is rather dull and dry but he does explain stuff clearly and repeats stuff. our final ended up being redemptive and that saved my grade. im very appreciative since it gave me a chance to show that i did learn the material in the end! theres also two extra credit opps! either help ppl w chem or make a tiktok!

The tests are difficult and there are clicker questions during class, and if you happen to miss the class for whatever reason no matter how justified, you can't make up these points. The professor also submitted the final grade to the university without telling the students their scores on the final exam. Overall would never take again.
He is a nice person. He is generous on extra credit and he gives curve for the course at the end of the quarter.

this professor's lecture is useless, our class average for the midterm and final were around 50 percent, those midterms are hard and has completely different questions than what we learned. I studied all night before the midterms, but it didn't help me at all.

I did amazing on his midterms and final, which would've put me at an easy A, but since I missed 2 HW assignments I got way worse than that. My fault? Yes. But 2 HW assignments shouldn't put me from Med school GPA to borderline failing. You think I'm joking... I wish I was. Apparently HW matters more than actual intelligence. DO YOUR HW

Professor Su is one of a kind honestly, came into college failed Chem 1B, so this is my 2nd time retaking it. He really wants you guys to learn, really wants you guys to pass. He's not the stuck up type to just give super hard tests, super practical. Study the practice exams and you're honestly good. No curve balls, but curves generously!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Amazing professor. Totally should take and lots of fun as well

A wonderful professor and person. This is my first rmp review and his class prompted it. Super great at explaining the concepts and is a really funny and genuinely nice guy. I felt like he wanted us to succeed.

Great professor. He's new but he surely made a great impression for his first year teaching. Poll Everywhere questions every day so participation matters but the questions are straightforward. 2 midterms and he drops one which is really nice. They're exactly like the midterm but they're only easy if you actually study. Overall great prof and person

TIm Su, or Master Su, is young & passionate about teaching. His style of teaching is very easy to follow- he goes over concepts, and provides basic example problems in class to solve. He's straightforward. His practice midterms exactly like the real ones, so study hard and there is ample extra credit w/ his TikTok challenge, and participation!
he let us make tiktoks for extra credit, if you did ap chem in high school, it is VERY easy, do the homework and youll pass, 2 midterms and 1 final concepts: thermochem, bond energies
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: For my class, she only took attendance on one of the days (Wed). The teacher is super sweet and kind, really passionate about the topic. Paying attention to the lecture helps because she tells you what will be on the tests sometimes. Lecture notes and textbook life-savers. Lots of memorization for the tests and hella readin on the lecture slides.

Took this class as an elective, and got a C-. Everything went well except for the final, you had to fill in the blanks with bunch of nuisance and detailed information. I tried to talk to the professor but never got an email back. Beware of the final

HNPG018 005: Global Communication.

Prof. Su is a good lecturer who has knowledge and passion for what she teaches. The essays and reading reports were manageable, and the final was just a group presentation. Pretty interesting and thought-provoking class if you're into global politics, even if Prof. Su can be a bit dry sometimes.

Bruh the readings are so long and some are not even tested on. She is pretty monotone but she does point out some key things that will BE ON THE MIDTERM and FINAL. Just attend class and take notes. She provided one 5 minute break each lecture which was nice.

This class was relatively easy. Professor Su is pretty chill and super easy to talk to or email if there is ever a problem. You only need to show up to class for participation points, which are mainly just mini group assignments that take about 10 minutes. Study the study guide for tests and you'll be good to go.

For me, this class was extremely easy. Do the work (study study guides and lecture notes with the book in hand for exams -CTRLF for the free ebook should be your best friend) and you will be fine. Lectures only need to be attended so you can get participation. While paying attention helps, studying the textbook and slides make lecture unessential.

Very friendly and really knowledgeable on the course topics! Just show up, take notes, do the participation assignments (usually something brief in almost every lecture), and study for the exams. The class isn't too difficult. She has an accent, but you can still understand her just fine.

The grade is made up of a midterm, final, participation, and discussion. The midterm was not difficult (just study what is on the study guide). Going to lecture is not mandatory because she posts the lecture slides but there are unannounced in class assignments, which count as attendance. The material is very dry but it is worth the easy A.

Took her Intro to Media class.  She's tone deaf on certain cultural issues, and it became apparent that her political stance is somewhat right-leaning.  She of course is entitled to her political views, but it began to show that she was tone deaf on certain issues related to race and society.  I got an A but have a hard time recommending her class.

I've taken 2 of her courses already and plan on taking more. She's a really nice professor who is willing to hear out your concerns and she even offers extra credit opportunities if you need it. Overall, a very effective professor.

Very confusing from time to time. Sometimes you feel that she does not have any idea what she is talking about. I think it's simply a language barrier, as she does have an accent. Would recommend reading the book, as the midterm and final are mostly based on defining terms. On the other, she is a very nice and is an easy grader. Don't skip class!

Professor Su received her PhD in Communications, yet she is one of the worst lecturers I have ever had. The material is really interesting but the set up of the class is incredibly poor. On the bright side though, participation and attendance were worth 50% of the overall grade.
Hard to understand with her accent. Lots of readings, but open book tests are easy if you go over the readings. Go to class because she gives points for attendance on random days.

She's so nice although shes hard to understand, her class is easy, notes on ilearn. Not very detailed study guides but you can make your own based on key terms. A+ totally achievable.. She has a big curve!

She's a nice professor and the class is easy. For the midterm and final,you need to memorize a lot of terms, but these are not really hard. As long as you attend the class and prepare for the exams, you'll get better grade. We chose from either doing group presentation or writing a paper as final projects.

Shes a really nice professor, but when it came down to finding out anything grade related, good luck you might as well have waited until its posted on Growl. Her midterm and final are pretty hard so of course no one does that great and its heavily curved. Group project is easy and fun so an "A" isn't hard on that. attendance is pretty mandatory.
She is REALLY nice. I screwed one of the tests and still got an A-. The group project helped a lot.

My 3rd time having Su. She's extremely kind, something you dont want to take too much advantage of. Her class is pretty easy so long as you keep up with the readings. She has a generous curve but thats because the class never takes her tests too seriously. lol But yes, an A+ can be achieved with mild effort.
Professor Su is very sweet and understanding of students' needs. Overall, she is a great professor. I will definitely take another class with her.
For someone whose last name is Spaise she sure doesn't give us any.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Even though she can be a little harsh on grammar in your essays, but she gives good feedback for your next one. Shes really helpful and willing to help her students whenever they need, so go to her office hours. Her grammar excercises are also helpful, it helps me improve my writing a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I loved Dr. Spaise! She's such a sweetheart; she genuinely wants to help her students pass the class and improve their writing. English 1PA comes w weekly tutorials so you have to meet up with the TA once a week which at first seemed annoying, but it's actually very helpful. You have to buy the St. Martins Guide and another grammar book too

Dr. Spaise is a great professor who actually takes the time to teach her students grammar. Most students do not have a solid foundation in grammar so I think the amount of homework she gave was good because it definitely helped. Make sure you proofread your essays and avoid grammar mistakes because that will be the difference between an A- and an A
If you pay attention in class she will basically do all the work for you. I learned a lot regarding grammar and punctuation and she tells you exactly what she wants regarding papers. Very sweet lady.

Although she gives a lot of writing assignments and grammar homework, she's pretty cool. As long as your essays are clear and have no grammar errors, passing this class will not be that difficult. She only gives us a lot of homework because she wants us to practice our writing more so that we can be better at it. Overall, she is a fair grader.

She is a nice woman. However, her class had a lot of unnecessary homework assignments such as grammar practice. She was very particular about using the new MLA format and grades essays for grammar rather than content. The group project is a good way to boost your grade though.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Her class was absolutely AWFUL. She gives too many unnecessary assignments that do not help with writing AT ALL. Super anal about work cited and grammar. Worst professor I have ever had. I was really disappointed. It felt like I was in high school because of the commas in sentence practices she made us do.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Her curriculum is grammar based because many college students do not know English grammar. The group project is on the same topic as the paper, so it is not too difficult to research and prepare for.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Focused too much on grammar and not enough on our ability to write well-planned essays. I think it was 2 essays, 1 research paper, and 1 oral report. Oral report is a group-based grade which sucks especially if you have bad speakers. But she is always there for help. Try to get an A in homework, that'll help your grade too.

She was a nice professor and all, but she grades TOO harsh on grammar. It gets pretty ridiculous, she constantly said that my essays were strong but because of comma splices I couldn't get an A or a B. She was helpful in class but her grading sucks ass.

Gives a lot of homework on top of reading. Very clear on what she expects from you. Her essays are very boring but easy enough. Group project is stupid but at least she grades people separate. Not a bad teacher, but glad I won't have to take her again.
I thought she was a great professor and was extremely helpful in Office Hours.

She seems like a nice person, but a horrible teacher. She grades based on how well you can use a comma. Her outlines for her essays are stupid and so is her homework. I didn't learn anything in her class other than how to please her and she didn't make me a better writer either.

Spaise was extremely difficult because there was such an attention to grammar & punctuation. In the long run, this helps a lot in other subjects; however, sometimes it does becomes too much. An entire grade may be taken off an essay for grammar alone. Overall, she's very helpful, but very particular. Not for those who want an easy A or B.
Approachable, clear & organized. She dislikes people being tardy!

She is an awesome professor! she cares about her students and if you attend her office hours she will definitely help you get an A on a paper. She cares a lot about grammar and punctuation, which will determine if she gives you a B or an A. Overall, great professor.

A brilliant pofessor! I learned a great deal in her class, and she made everything extremely clear. Just go to every class, do the work, and you'll get a good grade. She is very helpful and the book are all interesting. She grades on both context and grammar, not just grammar. Overall, a great professor!
Go to all her classes! And do all the reading assignments because she literally does quizzes on the majority of the assigned readings! Just pay attention in her class and don't get on her bad side.
She doesn't really care much about content in comparison to organization and grammar. If your papers have nearly perfect grammar and organization, it will automatically get a high B/low A.

I absolutely HATED her at first - but then I warmed up to her. She's actually a good teacher that explains really thoroughly. The only thing is she's really anal about grammar and punctuation, and esp. WORKS CITED. Other than that, she's an easy grader.

She is very old and when she got sick she was out 2 weeks!!! She is very difficult with grammar.Pay attention to your format of essays and grammar and you can get an easy "A". Seriously.Quizes are okay. But you must read, and she expects you to answer questions in class. IF you do not she will assume off the bat you didn't. ALWAYS PROOFREAD ESSAYS

Attendance is very important.  Reasonable amount of homework assigned weekly.  Extremely helpful during office hour.  Stresses on grammar, puncuation, and work citation.  Tip: read the assigned reading for she might give a quiz on it, try to finish your essay a week before it's due for it will be helpful to proofread your paper a couple times.
She was really nice and helpful. I thought her grading was fair. If you go to class and put some effort, then you should be fine.
I honestly thought she was a great professor. A bit tough and assigns a reasonable amount of work but she grades fair and is very helpful.

Oh my, I got my first C in college because of Professor Spaise. English 004 is the lowest english class offered at UCR and she's harder than my English 1A & 1B teachers! She would tell you to do one thing, but mark you off for doing what she said when she grades it. Ridiculous. >;( Try avoiding her. There's other English 4 teachers that are better.
This professor bases grades on grammar and works cited way more than on substance and uses a dumb medical ethics book that has nothing to do with english.

shes really nice and a fair grader, really obsessed with works cited. essay topics are easy, open notes open book on final. class is 4 essays and homework is really easy. theres also a group project on the topic of your choice. easy class, at least 10 classes got cancelled
Listen, if you want to get an A in her class, GO TO HER OFFICE HOURS. Don't be lazy and not go to class either because she does class work that counts heavily on your final grade.

She is the hardest, most ridiculous teacher you will ever have for English. She does not grade on content of your essay but your grammar. She is very biased and looks too deep into texts. IF YOU HAVE HER, PLEASE DROP THIS CLASS. She does not make you a better writer because she DOES NOT let you have the freedom of choice on your essays.

This professor is at times boring but at times interesting. Just read the question and make sure you understand it before you write the essay because if  you don't she'll lower your grade to c minus or D. You have to write four essays in this class. The Fourth is a research essay and it is kind of long so make sure you start it with time.

I started off strong in the class but she grades pretty hard, you just got to pay attention to the things she focuses on. She is sweet and helped my to become a better writer. GO TO HER OFFICE HOURS i didnt and never got higher than a c+ on the essays. She is the hardest eng4 teach, but you learn.

She is very hard and very picky...I learned how to write much better as the result of this course, but it cost me some points and a lot of energy. You HAVE to go to office hours if you want an A on a paper.

i never considered myself a good writer and i got a B+. all these ratings scared the hell out of me, but really she isn't that bad. she's actually a really good teacher. the 10 page paper is a ****, but you have plenty of time to work on it. and she gives you a lot of HW and CW, so that can help bring your grade up.

she loves grammar and really messes up your hard worked paper that you think is an A and turns out to be a C-, she is really hard. I wouldnt take her again..ever.., actually dont take her class haha to you who are reading this.

Took her for a summer course. Her emphasis on grammer is ridiculous. I've never had so many punctuation corrections in my life. She is in love with the comma and added about 200 to my paper. I would have laughed if I wasn't so mad. I say skip her if you can manage it. Professor, Spaise, loves, commas.

She grades very hard, so beware of that. It is difficuilt to write paper(s) that would keep her interested and mistake-free. Watch out for MLA format. She really puts an emphasis on writing the perfect paper. Other than the negatives, she is a pretty cool person. The class was entertaining, and I just wish she graded much more easier.

This teacher is unbelievably fixated on the tiny grammatical details. It doesn't matter if your overall paper is good, she will grade you down inordinately for every comma that's out of place. She's unfair, and she's rude. I would avoid her class, especially if you like English. I love english, but I hated her class.
for a professor to not look at your paper in detail, she is outspokenly horrible.
So long as you can pretend to enjoy the material, then her class should be some what enjoyable. The grammer emphasis leaves a little to be desired.

Being a Dr. doesn't mean anything. She doesn’t know how to teach grammar and she wrecks your future college English career. Also, most of what we read in her class was poorly written and by the same author.
She's a good teacher who's somewhat easy but she's very hard on grammar hence me taking the same class again in the fall.
normal professor, nothing special.
Horrible teaching! She grades too hard on the little things and makes a too much of a big deal about them. Plus, she's hard on people when it comes to ideas about the essays.

she's a very boring professor... she sometimes mumbles the words she said... she made the whole class confused that we did not know what to do...1st two essays are pretty easy... but later on, you'll get more confused... and watch out for Genetically modified foods topic...

She's clear, but despite participation she's really strict with grammer. 4 mistakes is an A-, plus you write 5 papers and a revision! soo much writing and if you're lucky you'll get an A, very tough to get an A. If no one reads, she starts quizzing you, try to change teachers.

She is a very nice professor. She is patient and kind to her students. But you got to go to her classes consistantly, because it will pay off at the end. The class will definitly help you to write better essays and pass English 4.

Easy grader for essays. But you gotta keep up with the attendance, she is heavy on attendance and in class work. Not a good teacher though. If you want to do better on your writings, go for a harder professor.

This lady literally stands up there and mumbles for an hour. beware of her topic: Genetically Modified Food. BORING! I would love to see her get mad often because she lets the class out early. Just don't do her reading assignments.
She is a good teacher. She is tough on grammar and mechanics though. However, if you participate and do the work, the class appears to be not as tough as one might expect.
she is okay. she is not so easy on the grading and sometimes don't clarify things well enough, also, i dont think she likes to give out A's, you can work your ass off and still end up  with a b.
arghhh!!!! she is soooo anal about grammar.Dangling modifiers, fused scentences....AHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHH!!!! She's nice though.
boring, she loves it if you participate, but she makes it that no one wants to.
Overall a decent teacher. You have to know your stuff to get a good grade. But its possible. She is boring though. Reminds me of a reincarnated version of my dead aunt, which is quite creepy.

good teacher, a little boring, but if you are into the class discussion you'll do good.  if you go to office hours, she will help you fix all of the problems with your essay and most likely you'll get an A

Lectures can be very boring, but if you are into reading articles and books, you will be okay in that class. If you read whatever she assigns, ask her questions once in awhile, and answer her questions in lecture, the class won't seem very difficult.
No Comments
Dull, dull class.  She's short, has thick glasses, is Greek and forces students to read Greek plays.  Spoon-feeds the most boring topics.  I hated her class.
No Comments

Her lectures can get pretty boring. Dr. Spaise is straight up though. There are about 4 essays for the quarter, and you can revise each essay. If you do not like Greek Mythology do no take this class. You have to read three of Euripides play.
her essay topics are not too easy, but she grades a bit on the lenient side.  i got a B+!  hehe, she gets annoyed when nobody does the reading assignment ^_^

On the first day, she said that the average grade she gives is a C and that this was considered “good.” If a professor chooses to grade that harshly, the course should at least be curved, but it was not. In addition, the feedback I received was unhelpful, so it was hard to improve. The class was unnecessarily discouraging for an introductory class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: SUPER NICE, she genuinely wants the best for you and makes sure you understand. She's very welcoming and will not judge you if you are wrong!! She makes the learning process easy

If you use ChatGPT to help you with your essay I recommend you to not taking her class. Once she finds out that you use AI, you are guaranteed not getting a B or above for the rest of your essays for the quarter. My friend who have her this year told me how she got the highest grade for one of the essay in her class and it was a B-.

Dr. Sullivan is a very great and caring professor who's willing to help improve her students writing and makes class engaging. However, I will not be taking her class again just for the sake of getting a good grade as she's a very hard grader and critiques harshly. Would not recommend if you want an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Great professor, but be prepared for a lot of reading and writing. There are four take-home essays plus an in-class final essay, so don't procrastinate since assignments pile up fast. She gives detailed feedback, is always willing to help, and grades fairly. Put in the effort, and you'll do well!
She is a great teacher. Very clear and very nice to students. She tries to make class interesting for students and wants them to pass. Overall loved her class.
Overall she's nice and caring of her students. Sometimes there will be tests but it's pretty easy if you did the reading
She is a super nice professor, when it comes up to grading essays or making comments, she says not to take it in the wrong way. For quizzes, they're really easy (if you did the reading) :)

Genuinely one of the kindest professors I've ever had; she cares about your writing and wants to help much as you allow her to. Grading can be a bit tough sometimes, but do the assignments (a lot of reading) and go to her office hours and she will tell you exactly what you can improve on.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Extremely harsh grader. Helps but then critiques that exactly help.
Received poor grades on every essay. She was a very hard grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Sullivan reminded me why I loved English. She assigns reading from the textbook daily but no more than 10pgs. The essays are challenging b/c they make you think, but a fun to write. You get one 72hr extension pass. When we got to the novel in week7 it was a good pick that allowed for lots of discussion. Sullivan is a great & helpful professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Sullivan reminded me why I loved English. She assigns reading from the textbook daily but it's no more than 10 pages. The essays are a little difficult as they make you think, but fun to write. When we got into the actual novel in week 7, it was a good pick that allowed for lots of discussion. Come to class, ask questions. She's nice & helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She is a very tough teacher at the school, but she is also very caring. As long as you put in the effort she will too. From my personal experience she is willing to put her family problems aside to help you better your writing. I'm really greatful for this teacher because I feel that my frustration gave her a hard time, yet she never held a grudge

A new professor so she's still trying new things. Some of those things you'll entirely forget about to do but she does give chances to make up for missed work. She is easy to work with. There was a quiz every day on the readings so be sure you did it. Also she uses movies in the class but you have to watch them on your own time. But she was helpful

Anne Sullivan is the nicest English teacher I've ever had. Aside from being nice, she also makes sure you are participating in class, and this helped students stay awake.  She also gives plenty of time for essays to be completed; however, no late work! Pop quizzes every now and then but no big deal.
