reviews.comment: Very paranoid about cheating/AI. Makes us show our edit history when writing, uses an over complicated lockdown browser, and has us turn our phones off and put them away on camera. Tests are kinda hard and mostly based on heavy readings and videos. Expect free responses on tests and lots of poll everywhere questions during lecture!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: The mere workload in this class was incredibly high and overwhelming for an intro class. Felt less like the needed amount for the class and more that the teacher acted like she was our only class. There was a lack of respect given to students and especially to those in need of academic accommodations. Do not recommend if you need those.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Mandatory lectures and PollEv questions are accuracy-based. Time consuming weekly annotations for readings and films. Discussions require you to actively participate with your camera on. A lockdown browser was required for the midterm and final (non-cumulative). There's also a four-week lifestyle change project. You have to put in a LOT of effort.

This class felt like it needed to use more of my time than any class I have taken here. We had to do a 4 week project on top of that we had to do annotations which included 2 readings and an hour film. We had a midterm and final. When we do polleverywheres she also grades you on what you get correct which isn't very fair plus participation points
I would not recommend. This course is an intro class that you need to treat it as double as your major class. Takes 6+ hours to do the assigned work each week.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: For an online course, this was pretty intense
This class is discriminatory towards students with disabilities please beware. She tried to refuse to give proper accommodations to students for the midterms/finals.

She started off todays class about lecturing us to be kind and not be rude when no one was. People were just coming up with suggestions because the midterm wasn't working. She made a whole presentation, wasting class time by the way. This is not only unnecessary but it is also very unprofessional. We are not children.

The entire class was made up of 2 group papers, 4-6 group activities, discussions, & a final group project. I don't usually like group work but it made the workload super bearable. There is a decent amount of reading every week but nothing unbearable. Lectures were nothing special. She offers extra credit. I've been at over 100% for a couple weeks.

Our class was on Tuesdays and Thursdays but was split in half so we only met once a week. Had to watch videos + quizzes on the day you don't meet (can go back and change answers). Videos had questions we had to answer in notebooks. 3 essays and 1 take home big exam. I got a B on my big exam and an A and 2 B's on my essays and still passed with an A
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Easy class. Almost everything rests on the midterms and final research paper. There's an attendance sheet (have seen people sign in and then leave though). Very boring in class (especially lectures, almost fell asleep several times). Would not recommend for feminists who already know about international issues since you'll probably fall asleep too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests? Not many

reviews.comment: She's such a sweetie and she cares about her students. Her Politics of Food class was very interactive. You can participate in your local community events. Her exam formats can be really weird. She'll actually ask for specific percentages and fill in the blanks. I've taken her for two classes but both classes are extremely easy.

Way too many group projects for my taste.... She seems like a nice woman but her assignments were annoying and not helpful at all. Her exams were super specific and dumb. Make sure to check your grade frequently bc she messed up on mine and I had to correct her a couple of times bc there's so many assignments. She's okay, I would not take her again

Food Studies class was a very informative and interactive experience.  From the readings and films to helping out in the R'Gardens, I feel this class can change one's perspectives of eating and make one more aware of the consequences people undergo for survival.  The course has two exams that are fairly easy.  The best part was the food events!
GSST 20 is a good class. It is relatively easy. As long as you go to class and just pay attention, do the forums and review before tests and do your paper. I would take this class again.

While she's not the best lecturer, she is very helpful if you have any questions! The class was indeed also very interesting! She is very sweet and just tries to help you out as much as possible, you just have to ask!

Easy class made hard by wordy ques that confuses even herself so what you know is not measured instead it is how u can master  her methods of testing.  Finals: group presentation. GPA n hands of grps(disussion/quizzes/grp presentation). Very hard 2 get A n EZ course. Students mostly self-taught. If she lectures,not so good lecturer. Disorganized.
this whole class was ridiculous. 6 papers a quiz every week in section and a final that was like 7 pages long (and most of questions weren't multiple choice they were short answers). do not take her!

Prof. Takeshita can be hard to understand at times and the concepts are very repetitive. However, if you go to lecture and section almost everytime, the class will not be too difficult. There was no midterm which made the final hard, but I studied for about 5 hours memorizing key concepts and vocab, and I got a 94% on my final.

Do not take this class. She sucks as a teacher. She treates this as an upper division class with 6 papers. The final is ridiculous. Her study guide has over 130 definitions plus 50 different readings. And its not multiple choice. All fill in. DO NOT TAKE HER AS A TEACHER!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

IF YOU ARE TAKIG THIS CLASS AS A REQUIREMET, YOU SHOULD RE-THINK YOUR DECISION. THE CLASS CALLS FOR 3 THREE PAGE ESSAYS 3 ONE PAGE ESSAYS AND CONSTANT READING ABOUT REPETITIVE CONCEPTS.. THE ONLY THING THIS CLASS WAS GOOD FOR WAS LOWERING MY GPA. TAKE RELIGIOUS STUDIES IF YOU CAN, I WISH I HAD..
She is a very interesting person but also pretty harsh if you don't do readings. She does make the effort to meet halfway but wants to see some effort from students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Do not hesitate to take her class! Her style to lecture is very pleasant to follow and I've never been bored in her class.

After her class I would always a better day. Very positive attitude and really listens and helps her students. She shows a lot of passion for the economics field and very smart. Recommend her ! Also do take advantage of her office hours, she explains with patience and in many details.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great lectures, I was never bored and it was a pleasure going to her class. I could listen to her lectures for hours. Its easy to learn from her. She has an accent but very easy to understand. I would take again! She uses her experience and travel stories as examples to make the lectures more interesting. Very intelligent and approachable.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: It was amazing experience taking her class. I would recommend her and I would to take another class with her. She has an eastern European accent but its a pleasure listening to her talk. Very inspirational and she has literary traveled the world almost. Whenever I went to her office hours she explained with patience everything until I understood.

Professor Balaj was very straightforward from the beginning of her course. She let her expectations known and works hard with students. Her class material applies to present economy times which was very interesting for me. I believe it helped me a lot her discussions and her personal experiences always added to making her class interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Amazing professor, she loves what she does. Very easy going. Do not skip class because she deducts points, but other than that she will be very flexible with turning in late assignments,  or making up missing homework.

She was very understanding and approachable. Class participation is basically inevitable. Don't think for a second that you can just go unnoticed in the back of the classroom. She will pick on you to participate. So, make sure to always stay current on all the readings so you actually have some productive input to contribute.

Dr. Toscano loves her class. I believe she has memorized all of her lectures. They are really boring but going to class is important because she does take roll every single day. Even though her class are 50 minutes long she will make sure she uses every single minute of class. She is easy as long as you do the hw you will get a good grade :)

She is a very easy professor. She does give multiple writing assignments, and also gives homework every day, but the homework is not very hard, and the writing assignments are not very long. She is very flexible with homework, and I recommend going to her office hours. Great professor over all, and truly cares about her students.

She is very nice and friendly in class, but this does not show when she grades any of your essays. She is extremely harsh on grading without a proper explanation as to why. If she explained why she is marking you down so much, you could actually learn from it and improve, but she fails to give you this chance. Overall, hw is easy, essays are hard.

Dr. Toscano is a great teacher if you make the effort to engage in the material. The grammar is of course rather dry but the stories are fun and interesting. I went to office hours regularly to chat with her in hopes of improving my fluency and she was always very patient. Basically, you get out of the class what you put into it.

I had a hard time understanding her speech. Most of all, I really hate speaking in class but if you don't, she docks you for participation. I got a B instead of an A because of it. She will do what she can to help you if you go to her. Really nice lady.

Had her for 101A and B. She is from Spain, so if a word is used in Spain as opposed to the US, use the word from Spain. Very nit-picky in grading and grading is hard to understand. Does not explain the material well, so background Spanish knowledge helpful. A "B" is not too hard to get in the class.

The course structure was ineffective. She lectures on grammatical points and then only chooses one out of many topics for the tests; there are 30 class meeting is a quarter (MWF) and she manages to test you on maybe four or five days worth of material. She's also very nit-picky. Would have been better to just study the book on own.

Nice lady.  Somewhat traditional.  Assignments are not too difficult and everything is outlined on the syllabus, so there are no surprises.  She is very clear and wants to make sure that the students understand the lecture.  She is kind of dull, nonetheless.  Not too lively.  The work is not that hard for upper-division Spanish.

She is extremely nice.  The only problem I had was that she doesn't always mark all the mistakes on the rough draft that she'll mark on the final. So you have to go meet with her during office hours to go over the paper if you want to avoid getting marked down  for those little mistakes.

Very nice lady... but don't be tardy, or she'll dock you!!!  Very strict attendance policy.  As far as grading, she lets you write your essay one time, corrects it, then returns it to you so you can turn it in a second time with corrections.  Nice.
Nice teacher but she grades hard on essays. A lot of homework but she is very helpfull
No Comments

No clear grading. Assignment instructions are obscure. He kept changing the weight of assignments/attendance it was hard to keep track. He randomly took attendance on canvas that needs a code. He's honestly too old to be teaching sadly. Assignments weren't too difficult but you almost had to guess what he wants.

Unclear grading criteria/no rubric, did not provide clear feedback unless u asked very specific questions (and sometimes no response), hard to reach outside of classes. Graded on two things: attendance, and one big project worth 80%. 8 am lectures, slide info sometimes wrong, and so boring. For an AIS class, prof was very tech unsaavy. Don't take.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: TMock is a nice guy BUT his teaching is horrible. His lectures are so boring. You try to pay attention but he goes on tangents and it's so hard to focus. He has 1 midterm and 1 final. He says he has in-class assignments/quizzes but he sometimes forgets about them. I don't even know how to study for this class. Avoid him if you can!
I don't know why he isn't retired
This professor inspired me to get a Master's in Accounting so I can teach this class to protect the next generation of Information Systems and Accounting students.

Excellent professor who truly loves the subject. Attendance isn't mandatory, but lecture was always fun and informative, plus he's a great guy to converse with. Professor Cogswell is amazing! He's loud, funny, and most importantly, he captures your attention. There was 1 midterm, 1 final, 2 quizzes, and an extra credit opportunity. Super passionate professor. His lectures are really really entertaining you can really tell he loves his job. Kind of an easy class just need to pay attention in lecture and do the readings. This man is amazing. He is like the funny old uncle at Christmas.

he is a great individual. he is very loud but his lectures are never boring. his midterm and final consist of 12 terms out of 46, you choose 6 to write detailed descriptions about and then you need to write an essay. you will need to write 2 movie reviews and that's about it. he gives two books that you may need to read. he has movie nights w/pizza

Professor Cogswell is an absolute doof. But that's what made him hilarious. I had Professor Cogswell for my entire 2 years of Undergrad in History and he was nothing but the sweetest, most caring, respected person I had ever had. I took every single European course that was offered by Cogswell, and he took me under his wing. He became a mentor and even after graduation, he has worked hard to still support me academically.

Dr. Cogswell is easily the best professor at UCR-- he is extremely caring (he'll provide pizza for all outside of class activities e.g study sessions), and his lectures are so interesting. Professor Cogswell is the best professor I have had at UCR. I've taken two upper division classes with him and both time it has been a great experience. Words cannot become to fathom how great of a professor this man is. His enthusiasm and passion for history is very contagious to his students. He truly cares for his students and just wants to help us in every way possible. He's an amazing lecturer with hilarious side stories. LOVE THIS MAN!!
One of the first, and nicest professors I've ever had! He truly wants everyone to pass his class, and will go out of his way to do so.

3. He tends to forget that the class is called "INTRO" to mechanical engineering calculations
4. Be prepared to learn linear algebra and java coding at the same time against your will! :)

The coding part of the midterm and final are done by an auto grader. That means that if you did 90% of the work correctly but the wrong 10% returns the wrong values, you will get 0% on that problem. The midterm was a bimodal peaking at 0% and 100%. No curves.

Whenever I found myself struggling I was always able to ask questions that would help me clarify the material. She gives clear instructions and always offers help if you need it. I enjoyed her lessons about culture!

This class is only easy to understand if you are actually majoring in Nordic Mythology or something along the lines. The reading load is heavy. The exams are very difficult to pass unless you already have the basic knowledge. Although the professor is very nice, she has no consideration towards those who are not actually interested in Mythology.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Sabine really cares about her students and will go out of her way to make sure they pass. She's great about helping students with their grammar blunders too. If you have a grammar question, she will always thoroughly answer it. As long as you put in a moderate amount of effort and have a good attitude, you will do great in this course.

It's a literature class so reading shouldnt be surprising or anything and there isnt much to go off of homework wise. A couple tests, an essay or two, and a presentation. Everything is laid out well in the syllabus.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Great teacher, so nice and willing to help. Homeowrk was just for  practice and points, vocab quizzes should be studied for, but as long as you try you should do fine.

Very easy if you have a basic understanding in german. I never studied and got an A, just listened and asked quest in class but you do have to take time to write the papers 3 long ones in german. Midterms are ridic easy. She cares but like anything else you have to reciprocate.

I have taken several classes with Sabine. Typically, she's wonderful, but I (and several students) had an awful experience with her for German 100. She was unhelpful, unclear, and her assignments were vague. She gave us very little to work with, the difficulty level was much higher than it should have been, and we never got study guides on time.

She was an absolute darling. Unfortunately only had her for German 001. Hoping to get her for German 003. She's so enthusiastic and fun, and her constant speaking in German (even though sometimes confusing) keeps you paying attention. Her nerdiness makes class even more fun.
Best Instructor at UCR. She is an incredibly sweet lady filled with passion for writing. I think this class was my best experience at UCR.
Super amazing! One of the nicest best teachers I have ever had. Super helpful.
Shes super nice, ridiculously easy class, actually had a lot of fun.
Sabine is great and extremely fair when it comes to grading.
i've had her for all of my german classes. simply awesome.

Sabine is an awesome teacher.  Her English is great for a non-native speaker and she keeps class very interesting.  The tests and homework aren't too bad as long as you keep up and study a little bit.  I'll be looking forward to 3, 4, and upper div.

I really want to consider Sabine as a long-lost mother that anyone would hope for. She is incredibly sweet and very knowledged in her area. Her tests are straight-forward and she grades fair, maybe too fair...and her finals (which in general are stressing) are just plain fun. My 4th review of her, and ill say it again, "best UCR teacher."

The best teacher in UCR has done it again. Every class was just plain fun and I have learned so much towards my Germanic Studies major. I cannot wait to have her in Ger 103A and 103B and any other classes in the future.
Best teacher in UCR. Absolutely loved her

A wondeful teacher. Very helpful, very passionate about her work. Prepares you well for the test and grades super fair. The German final can be challenging to some, but it was very fun. A great teacher, a definite recomendation.

Really nice and understanding guy, lectures decently but he goes on random tangents sometimes. Midterm and final are literal reflections of problem types he gives out every week, and he posts slides and sample problems for midterm/final on google drive. Straightforward class, just study the types of questions and you'll be fine.

Honestly a great class with a dedicated professor. Lectures can be confusing sometimes as he goes deeper than the content on the test. He does lectures concurrently on zoom so you don't have to show up in person. Homework can be weirdly difficult at times but it's good practice. Midterm felt surprisingly easy and final felt more challenging.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He responds to your emails in literally minutes. Best professor I have taken in terms of math.

He is an okay lecturer, but the class is easy. I barely went to lecture and got a 91% on the midterm. Has 4 things in the grading scale, classwork, homework, midterm, and final. Midterm was exactly like the class work, with very slight changes. Classwork was pretty easy, two of the lowest scores were dropped and there were only 4 assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The entire class is curved, no set grading criteria. The classworks are very easy and the midterm and final are the exact same thing with different numbers. I didn't attend lecture once and just youtubed the topics on the classwork. Homework can be very hard though

I liked him a lot. Grades were based on 4 in-class assignments(easy), webwork hw assignments(sometimes easy sometimes hard), midterm (study the in class assignments) and the final (study midterm and in class assignments. Sometimes was hard to understand, he is so much better than some other math professors I have had at UCR
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I learned this class almost entirely from the supplementary material the professor provided. His lectures were often unclear to me and I found myself falling behind and confused in class. Exams and tests are relatively easy if you understand the material.

One of the best math professors I had. Was effective as a lecturer and for a class that is known for being hard, he did a great job at it. Grade was based on four quizzes, midterm and final and homework. However, the homework was strangely disproportionally hard.

Professor Chow is a great professor for ODEs. He writes down the equations for every problem and delivers the content clearly and mathematically. The homework is worth a great amount of your grade and there's a lot of it so the problems were useful. The midterm and final are EXACTLY like the practice midterm and final but with different numbers.

Very caring professor. Discussion attendance with 10% and Hw, midterm, final worth 30% each. Exam questions are very straight forward and based off lecture notes and discussion worksheets. (Basically the same question but changed the numbers around)
Professor is a fantastic teacher, he truly cares about his students and their well-being. Offers great lectures and slides full of examples to follow along with during class.
Very caring and concerned about his students. Understanding about the situation with online classes. I crammed the material 3 days before the final since I had other classes to deal with.
His class is very chilling, and his teaching style is pretty fun
Great professor and overall person. He genuinely cares about your learning experience and is more than willing to help in any way he can.

I ended up withdrawling from his class for unrelated reasons, but stayed until the final. Ballard is very judgemental and moody. However, he is very accessible outside of class and offers a lot of help for essays. Attendence is important, a lot of reading quizzes and in class assignments that are graded. Easy pass for an active student
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Comments can be rude or condescending, making class uncomfortable. Quick to criticize or assume things before understanding students. He once falsely accused of cheating before even attempting to redo a body paragraph during his office hours. We worked this out after recalling the entire situation.

Overall grades is just essays, he only offer 1 reversion out of average and rlly strict on essays. If he's giving u feedback, he makes it feel like it's ur the problem. U have to learn by ur self. worst professor i have ever had and he gives no extra credit

The professor can come off as nice at times, but he intends to raise his voice toward students when giving feedback and would interrupt multiple times if you have something to say. Can be impatient at times. He has the right idea to be considered a "good professor" but the approach needs working on.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This professor is what you would call a "tough grader". He is suuuuuper nitpicky. You can give him your magnum opus and he'll probably give you a C+. He is also very intrusive. If possible do not take his class.
He is helpful and friendly. However, he is confusing sometimes. He makes a lot of compliments on my works, but I receive relatively low grades after I get them back from him.
Grades tough on the essays he assigns they can be confusing and hard to write for but doable if you try hard, theres about 3 or 4. In class essay for midterm, final is 2 in class essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Took this class in Fall 2022. While his lectures were a bit difficult to follow sometimes, I thoroughly enjoyed writing my choose-your-own-adventure story. I didn't have any experience contacting him outside of class because I asked any questions I had before or after lecture. Overall, I loved the class and still want to publish my game one day.

He is, like other students have claimed, outright impossible to reach off-campus. He did not reply to a single email from the entire quarter, and would regularly hold zoom meeting office hours he'd never attend or just stay silent during. His idea for class structure was more so about his niche interest in gamebooks rather than immersive media.

The class was easy, but the overall experience was frustrating. The professor is unresponsive to emails, so you have to speak with him in person. I did all my work and got an A+ in discussion yet I still ended up with an F. If you take this class, I recommend keeping records of your work. Be prepared to advocate for yourself if anything goes wrong.

I was lowkey lost all quarter, but the class was not difficult. At times the class felt like it was more about science fiction than it was about music. He took longer to grade assignments towards the end of the quarter.

The class I took was fairly easy, however, he did not grade and was impossible to reach outside of class. He gave me and other students a failing grade, regardless of perfect attendance and completed every assignment. It was insulting receiving this grade and to have it put on my transcript. Do not take this professor unless you want an unjust F!

This professor is horrible. He would not respond to any emails at all, and his class was confusing and disjointed. He did not grade and gave many students bad grades and when we reached out no response from him, even when staff emailed as well. Very rude do not take his class or support this teacher he should be fired.

Starts with small writing assignments using music vocab, focuses on making a student film for the final project. Expect timed assignments related to film music during discussions. Don't miss more than two days, attendance is brutal in lecture and discussion. Attend concert in week 8. Submit assignments on time, as Canvas locks them. You'll be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tim is an overall nice guy, but he seemed to be very unorganized. Class time was wasted by looking through books that ultimately made no difference in the course. And yes, I am referring to just flipping through pages. If you do the homework and show up it's and easy A. Just be prepared to be slightly confused all quarter.

Very confusing professor. I thought it was going to be an easy class, but I was wrong. Labor had us write a thesis statement every class, but was confusing on what he considered a good thesis. His requirements for the essay was hard to understand. He used music words that we did not know. The quizzes from discussion was difficult. Don't recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The class was very enjoyable and the examples he gave in class were interesting. 1 midterm, 2 papers, and a final. The test are pretty straightforward (study the vocab)and essays weren't that bad. This class really changed how I watch movies now.

This teacher is very passionate about music.  He tries to get through all he can in each class to emphasize the use of sound and music throughout movies. He's a really good teacher, but it's hard to hear him at times as a movie is playing.  Make sure to attend classes, or at least e-mail him about why you couldn't attend though.
awesome professor, easy class!
Awesome, fun class! Friendly professor.
Very patient and nice. Great teacher.
Very fun and interesting class

Tim Lindsey is my favorite teacher at UC Riverside. He is a very nice person and very accessible outside class. His exams are very fair, similar to his notes and homework, so you know what to study for the test without surprises. Effective Lecture and review notes for exams which are pretty helpful. Take his class you will never regret it!
He is very caring and engaging professor. He provided the class with a lot resources to do well in exams. Would take again!

Professor Lindsey is easily the most accessible prof at UCR. He responds to emails quickly and purposely wants students to succeed. Pacing in the class might be fast but the content isn't hard to digest if you do the homework. He also provided reviews for each chapter that he made. The effort he puts in the notes makes up for the pacing.
The Midterm was terrible 30 questions with only one hour to do which made no sense.

Very disorganized and wasn't the easiest to understand what exactly we needed to do all the time. BUT an understanding teacher that cared a lot, and hosted a final exam study session pizza party. Makes decisions in class so I'd say it's important to go. Attendance wasn't mandatory but if you wanted to know if you had due dates, you should go.

MY FAVORITE PROFESSOR EVER!!!

Professor Ballard is very accessible outside of class, including weekends. Furthermore, he clearly goes over sentence structures and word choices through in-class exercises. I think by taking his class I got a firmer grip on how I can become a better writers. Be sure to read because he does a lot of quizzes and small in-class timed writings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I liked his class because compared to other English teachers, hes not overbearing at all. Gave fair grades, amazing during office hours!!! One of the best English professors for sure, I recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Probably one of the toughest paper graders there is. All you do in class is watch films. But he never really helps you on the essays. He hands you the prompts and never touches on them again until they are do. If you want an A, go to office hours, he will tell you exactly what he wants in the essay. I thought Professor Ballard's class was easy and he really gives great feedback on how to get an A on your essay. You have to read but he gives you clear points to use in your essay.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: He was a great professor! He spends so much time in office hours with his students trying to help them with their papers. You just have to put in the effort and you'll be able to get a good grade.

Professor Ballard is a really nice professor. He gives great feedback on essays and is very helpful during office hours. He has a great sense of humor. In class, he goes over the assigned reading and there are pop quizzes and free writing. He is an easy grader. His class was very easy. Best English teacher!

Your average professor, not terrible. He gives a lot of feedback on essays, sometimes his own opinions that were not needed, but the actual feedback helps, and office hours are very helpful. He seems to be very nice and funny at first, but can be very rude and disrespectful. I would not want to have him as a professor ever again.

reviews.comment: Generally speaking, he is a good professor. Rarely, he could be rude or irony when he speaks.

reviews.comment: From my experience Professor Ballard is in fact very rude and disrespectful. He wants you to write according to his views and opinions. If you are a student who does not conform like other students who agree unquestionably to a professor's ideas just to pass do not take his class. He is insulting if you disagree with him.
really tough. he treats you like he is very kind but actually not. Failed every one in my class. Don't take his class
bad bad teacher. never give good grade
Worst teacher ever!!! Didn't learn anything from him! He doesn't teach you anything useful even though I went to his office hour.
BEST PROFESSOR EVER!! EASY A AND HE IS A VERY COOL GUY. REAL NICE AND ATTENDING OFFICE HOURS IMPROVES YOUR ESSAYS!

BEST ENGLISH TEACHER! I took him 4 years ago and I would take him again if I could. He was very helpful. Makes appointments if you couldn't make it to his O.H. He shows passion and explains things very well. I really enjoyed it. He's easy.

BEST ENGLISH PROFESSOR EVER! Super easy with grading. Very helpful during office hours. If you can't reach him during office hours, he arranges a meeting anywhere. I took him during freshmen year, 4 years ago. I would take him again, if I had the opportunity,
Very helpful, funny and witty

Ballard is such a nice guy. He is extremely helpful with office hours and he has a bit of a sense of humor. The first day of class we played a game to get to know everyone. Indeed, he is such a nice guy and the class is not hard as long as you go to office hours because he tells you what to fix meaning what to do to get an A.
Great professor.  He knows how to help with writing and adds extremely useful advice about how to write your papers.
he is quite funny (sometimes)
the best professor ever. he helped me on all my essays. he proof read my drafts, told me what i needed help on, and was an easy grader. he made me like english. By far, The best english teacher!
really means well. helpful with all your essays and will work with you. not a tough grader.
cool teacher, class is really easy not too tough of a grader just do your assignments and keep up with the reading
Fun class. Easy A.

Easy class, just do well on your essays and you will get an A. Ask for feedback on essays. Also, there are pop quizzes on the readings but they only makes up about 10% of your grade. We watched films and analyzed them so yeah if you don't like watching black and white or silent films,talking films towards the mid-end, its not the class for you.

Worse english teacher EVER! I've taken 1A and got an A+ in the class and I'm taking 1B right now and I'm getting A's on my papers as of now. But with him he's weird and a harsh grader. He corrects your paper to how he would write it but doesn't do much else.

He is a good guy, kind of strange, tells jokes that aren't really funny. He does grade hard, so make sure you try really HARD. He docks you on LITTLE things and is a stickler about MLA format. Overall though, good teacher.

Hey asked his students alot of question and he does assigned readings but if you do reading you will do well on quiz. He quizes are extremely easy and his grading was fair. Good teacher, so good I am taking him right now for 1B

Prof. Ballard truly loves his job, and makes class interesting, however he is a really tough grader. Prior to taking his class I had gotten only A's in English, and that was my major...that has changed. He is helpful, and did make me a better writer though...
Very nice, grades super easy. Remember to meet the length requirements on the essays, or else he docks off MAJOR points.

There are better english teachers out there..choose them before him. His first midterm was an in-class essay about the Declaration of Independence, it had NOTHING to do with what we were learning. Kinda strange, seems to favor males over females, unless you are a minority female then he favors you. Ask for help with essays, show effort.
Very good teacher. Cared about his students doing well in both of the courses I had him. Very easy as long as you do the readings and follow his paper corrections on the first draft.

Professor Ballard is a very nice teacher and asks a lot of questions to what other students think about a novel or other reading assignments. As long as you come to class on time, somewhat participate, and get above average grades on all of his essay assignments including final, then you can get a decent grade like a B for sure in his class.

he seemed really nice in the first day of class, but he does not give a crap about u doing well... -.-+ I had an idea of writing in different way in the first essay and he was like WTF r u doing... He made a puzzled face that was implyin that I'm a ****ing dumbass or some****.
really good

I think he's a great teacher. In 1A you have an essay due every other week, but he has the class do workshops and they really help. As long as you go to class and write your papers you're set. He may seem intimidating at first, but he's a pretty nice guy.

Had great interest in topic (film noir) but incredibly, he managed to ruin it for me.  Extremely unhelpful in terms of trying to make your paper better. Basically shat on my paper.  Had already run it by another instructor who said it was shaping up to be a great paper and have had professors comment positively on my level of writing so you decide

he's nice.. shortly the quarter ended he actually called me on my cell phone because he was missing one of my papers! and then he let me turn them in for a grade! that was pretty cool... but we did watch some movie and i have no idea what it had to do with the class...
this teacher is the coolest
kind of an ****. really tough grader. counts attendance towards your grade. hard to get an A in his class.
i found his in class work sometimes ptless. there's only one word i would use to describe him... annoying.

He didn't discuss the novel we read, just let us tell our opinions of what we think is happening. Grades essays sorta hard, doesn't help that much in improving. Makes time for office hours, but always seems to be in a rush. Tries to make class funny.

What's everyone talking about? HE'S THE BEST! I've had him for two quarters and I still think he's awesome. Very helpful, always makes room for office hours. Very understandable, and tries to make class fun! Those who criticize him should think about taking Wirz. You'll probably have a 2nd thought.

*ATTENTION EVERYONE* DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR! I REPEAT DO NOT TAKE HIM!! HORRIBLE CLASS...HORRIBLE GRADING SYSTEM...HORRIBLE PERSONALITY...NOT HELPFUL AT ALL...DIDNT LEARN A THING IN THAT CLASS...THE WORST ENGLISH PROFESOR EVER!!!
No Comments
extremely bad.  graded extremely tough.  not recommended to other students
yells at students. not helpful at all.  refuses to proof read anything.
Best english teacher!!
He does his very best to make lectures interesting and is very active. Get's pissed when someone interrupts his class. Fairly easy grader.
He is helpful. His class is very interesting.
Very nice, very friendly, and very approachable. Essays are graded kinda hard, but then again, eng 1B  requires quite a lot of work.
Very unhelpful. Doesn't really care about teaching

The lectures are long and he takes attendance, but offers a break in between. Lots of extra credit to make up for any days you miss! The class is a breeze if you know the basics of film and theater. Final paper on a film of your choice. Only met twice in the quarter for the "lab" portion.

I will give this course a 5 simply because it is very easy. You are almost guaranteed an A+. Prof. Baltierra obviously wants students to pass and does not want to bog anyone down with too much busywork. Discussion posts, 1 final paper, and some analysis of certain facets of production, along with PLENTY of extra credit. Boring lectures, though.

The only reason I didn't get an A in his class was my own fault, I forgot the class existed because I had other classes to worry about, but he managed to get me on the right track and passing. He's super caring and genuinely cares about his students. very interesting lectures. I have to warn you about his obsession with Taylor Swift, tho lol
I enjoyed learning about theatre, he covers every topic so well!!

Great professor- super funny and interesting and really cares about his students. Oddly obsessed with Taylor Swift for a married man, though. Would highly recommend any of his classes, whether you belong to the major or not. Textbooks are "required" for 149, but if you go to all the classes the readings are more supplemental.
Amazing teacher! He stuck to the syllabus, and everything thats on his lecture is the exact same as his test. I strongly recommend!!

Tony is a great professor. As long as you do the work youll pass. The midterm and final are fine. All the answers are on the powerpoints and he gives you an 80 question study guide for a 50 question exam. One warning he talks about the two TSs a lot (Taylor Swift and Tony Stark). Its funny at first but I got annoyed with it around week 8.

Professor Baltierra was a fantastic professor and was very happy I took the class. There was a decent amount of work in it, but very fair grader and offers tons of extra credit. The midterm and final were very easy to study due to him giving 80 questions on a study guide and would take 50 questions from that. Highly recommend taking him.

Professor Baltierra is an excellent professor. I took a fast track course and it was very heavy on reading the book as well as the plays assigned but the plays were interesting and the discussions were a good tool to use to participate with the other people taking the class.

Tony cares about his students. His class Stage Management and Stage Techniques are pretty easy. If you go to class, you'll get an A. He's not too work heavy. There are textbook which are nice to get and have but you can just borrow from someone else. Do all the extra readings though, those are important. He's a great teacher.
Professor Baltierra is one of the best professors I've had in college. He really cares about the students and does he best to make sure we understand and know how to apply the material.

Around 4 essays but doesn't publish the full prompt or assignment until the day before. A final quiz and a final paper. More than one right answer. The quiz will make or break your grade. If you ABSOLUTELY NEED to take this class, then be cautious but if not then I recommend looking for a class you would actually enjoy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Great professor in general, has a good lecturing-style with the professor providing in-depth explanations of the required texts/films during lecture. LOTS OF WRITING!! 4 short essays during the quarter, and a 10 page requirement for the final paper. Lots of reading, so come to class prepared.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Enjoyed the course and books assigned. He pushes you to expand your writing and think deeper about the texts he assigns. He's very kind and caring towards his students and also understanding. He wants you to do your best so he'll provide as much resources you need in order to be successful in the course. I would def take again!!!!

professor tobias was very passionate about what he spoke about, but the material was difficult to grasp. he wouldn't leave feedback on essay's. the final essay is 8-10 pages, so be prepared to write. there were books and textbooks we had to read and we didn't cover half of it in class. sorry, but wouldn't recommend.

Professor Tobias is very insightful when it comes to making your writing better. He is also very passionate about the topics he teaches, which makes the learning enjoyable. There is a lot of reading in the class, but it is manageable. The class is also primarily made up of writing assignments, so make sure to be prepared. I would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Tobias is extremely knowledgable and passionate about the subject he teaches. reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--So many papers

reviews.comment: Work, work, work. Took three upper division English classes at the same time, none of them provided the workload that this one did. Point knocked down for making a final essay due at 5 pm, which is honestly more insulting than just making it due a day earlier. Do not take as an "intro" class, but good insight bogged down by just how much there is.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Amazing Professor, was very lenient with everyone and graded very nicely

reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Please do not take his classes. It's an intro level class that's made purposely to make you not receive a grade higher than a B. Prof is wordy and unclear, the TAs are of little assistance bc they are confused too, essays/heavy reading every week.

reviews.comment: Professor Tobias can be a little intimidating at first, but he really warms up to his students. Don't be afraid to chat him up, he's super cool and can be really funny!
Professor Tobias gives GREAT feedback to help us improve our writing!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Tobias is one of the most intelligent professors at UCR. I agree with other comments in that his lectures are somewhat difficult to follow, but that's only if you go on your phone and don't pay attention. He is seriously brilliant and is invested in each of his students and their success.

Lectures were confusing af (I'm not used to his jargon) but he was always available to give clarification in office hours. Tons of writing during finals week. If you're having trouble with essays, he'll pretty much tell you where to go with the topic.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: He is a brilliant man but he doesn't spoon feed you answers. I am surprised to learn that he rarely gives As on papers because I got an A on every single one. All you need to do is analyze and use what he says during lectures as a spring board for your paper. He is not an easy grader but he gives a lot of good feedback and is very helpful.

I had Tobias for 20C and this class. I had to work for my grade, but I ended up getting an A- in this class and a B+ in 20C. The final was online and you were able to take it multiple times, so there was no excuse not to get a good grade. Hard grader, but doable

He is one of the most boring professors I have ever taken. Nothing is ever clear in his class. Everything was about interpretation and he definitely loves keeping it vague. The material he chooses is anything but interesting along with the terrible films we had to watch every week. No one in the class had any idea what was happening most of the tim

Professor Tobias is an intelligent, insightful, passionate professor. He genuinely cares about his students' progress in the class. He may be hard to follow during lecture at times, but that's what your TA is for. I learned so much about visual media narratives. Three 5-page essays and one 8-page essay. Final was MC. Take it if you love English.

A very strange class. To succeed in this class, you basically need to learn how to string together 2 or 3 technical terms into one long sentence broken up by many commas in your essays. While it's not hard to do, it's just not good English anymore...

The content of this class was very interesting and essay writing skills and grades depend on who your TA is. As 4 Prof. Tobias, he is very one-sided, not very open to other student's insights about the subject material during lecture,he only cares about his analysis.During the final exam he would shout out his answer to you, I don't recommend him.

Tobias is a very passionate and kind teacher. His lectures are a lot to take in, but they're very interesting if you're passionate about visual narratives. Provides a deeper understanding of visual media. A couple of novels must be read, but the focus is on film. From Charlie Chaplin to anime films like Akira. Fun and insightful.

Definitely not the conventional type, Tobias has a different yet interesting approach. Very intelligent and passionate about the material, introduces a lot of material that you may not expect to ever have in a class (in a good way). Sometimes a little confusing, but overall entertaining and interesting. Love the movies we watched!

I absolutely learned nothing in this class that is valuable towards life.  All he talked about were these abstract concepts about Focouly and bla bla bla.  Absolutely the worst English class I ever took in my entire life.  We didn't even read any literature (except maybe one novel).  Films were challenging and lectures were jsut plain bizarre.

I wasn't entirely thrilled to take this class at first, but upon taking it..wow. My favorite class I've taken at UCR so far (I'm about to be a third year). I learned to love to write in this class and the professor chose great films and literature. It's not the easiest class, but you learn and gain so much perspective. TAKE this class w/Tobias!!

Tobias is very passionate and knowledgeable. He talks A LOT. The class was about media and film, very different. Somewhat hard material but I enjoyed the class a little. 4 essays, 3 quizzes and 1 really hard final.

Tobias is a genius. He is so amazingly smart, and I loved attending class with him. Though the class was much more media and culturally oriented than I expected, I loved the way he approached the topics. Though the class was hard, and the material unfamiliar, I think this was exactly what a college class should be; a learning experience. He's rad.
This guy is brilliant and a wonderful professor. But truly only if you want to learn. If you're looking for an easy A, got to biology.

I thought Professor Tobias was quite challenging.  He covers material that you won't find in any other English class...because he makes you analyze films and music videos instead of literature.  I wish he was more clear because the concepts he teach are very deep.  Also, I was forced into this class due to budget cuts.

Tobias is extremely intelligent!He knows a lot of things that are not commonly known.He is very helpful during OH and is willing to explain things at the "avg. student level" if you don't get something.He has a sarcastic sense of humor that most do not get but if you do the reading & ask your TA for the "norm explanation" you should do fine!

Very matter-of-fact type of guy that comes across somewhat condescending. Covers some difficult and philosophical concepts. Although I admit it is not easy material to teach he seems to believe it is easy to understand becuase it makes sense to him. I would not recommend him to any english major, unless you have no choice like I did.
Great professor.
pretty difficult, very challenging and demanding but quite entertaining. Advice: Go to every class, go to office hours and have a clear mind.

I have taken him a few times, and I enjoy his classes a great deal. He can be a little hard to follow because it seems as if he forgets that we don't know everything he does, but still tends to do a good job of explaining things. I read the complaints others had, and all I can say is that, like in any class, if you don't try, you deserve to fail.

Absolutely wonderful professor. Although the material is difficult, as most of it is vested in philosophical concepts, it is rewarding to study and truly enlightening. He is also very helpful in office hours and does his best to help his students understand the concepts. Simply brilliant!

After taking this professor again, my opinion on him has since changed. He is actually pretty good in the field that he was supposed to teach. He is much better as a teacher in a higher class than lower division classes. He is still a hard grader and still rarely gives an A on papers.

Tobias presents a lot of interesting and eclectic material in his curriculum. He conveys complex ideas through understandable lectures and reading material. He is also very into the material he teaches, and it shows. His expectations on paper assignments are also clear-cut and he is fairly generous on grading. Highly recommended.
very smart, and for anyone who says that he is hard to follow that's probably a product of the system allowing unintelligent people to slip into the UC system through some crack.
Great professor, sometimes hard to follow. but he is willing to work with you.
Tobias is a fantastic professor.If only I could absorb a portion of his intelligence through some sort of osmosis.
Smart Motha ****a. I hardly went to class, did good on the final and got B.
He is a great professor, very kind, and caring about his students.  Highly recommended, easy workload.

James is a great teacher, his two best qualities being that he is very intelligent and is a greatly coherent speaker.  He very much expects you to come up to his level, which is challenging, but he's really openminded and willing to work with you to help you understand.  The workload is medium to light, and he is accessible.  Highly recommended.
No Comments

A very intelligent guy.  Discussions can get a little sidetracked sometimes and can also get so deep that you just get completely lost.  But, if you stop him and say, "What the heck are you talking about?" he will do his best to explain it to you.  By the second or third time, we usually get it.  He tries to teach some pretty difficult concepts, and he really wants you to understand them for yourself in your own way.  Hence, broad assignments and explainations.

this man is too smart for his own good. he was out sick for three weeks of the quarter. projects and assignments are SO broad. he tries to explain something to u and by the end of it, you're like waT??!? he doesnt let u know wat u have in the class, until class is over. ridiculous.
Complete waste of my life.  Unless you are into the film and visual culture thing, don't take this course.  All the information was completely useless and absolutely BORING!!!!!

Was terrible in office hours.  He did not try to help at all in office hours.  He also acted bored and in some type of hurry on several occasions when I was actually looking for assistance.  I was bothered by his total lack of care when it came to my questions.  It was very, very upsetting...

He lectured on usless subjects that do not matter in life.  Forget about this "elevated" learning and such matters of intelligence because he teaches about useless information.  Sure I may know a lot about paint peeling from a wall on a hot day, but I don't need to make a class out of it.

The class was certainly difficult, but highly informative. His language was elevated to the point that many students were lost. Very interesting class if you actually have a brain (unlike some of the **** below me). Also, very helpful during office hrs.
He is a drag on the UC system and a very useless instructor.  Seems to give certain students more preferance over others for some reason in the area of grades.  Make your own assumption...

The film theory courses that he teaches are useless.  It is like majoring in underwater basket weaving.  I understood what he was talking about, but I felt that it was useless.  He knew his material very well, but nobody cared out of boredom...

Tobias is amazing! He knows his theory cold. He is supportive, helpful, and truly seems to want to help students learn about film theory. His use of language is beautiful, but may be difficult for undergrads to comprehend--I loved it...
he was ok i got a b in the class i did not attend one class i think

yeah its true he switched up the course on us. we were supposed to be learning about film and gender but instead chose to teach about film and music (which was nonetheless interesting). he made me look at films in a different light, to which im grateful
wonderful professor.  amazing breadth of knowledge
Doesn't teach according to the catalog description; unorganized

Truly an amazing professor. I took her for ENGL021, Intro to Asian American studies, and she was great. Amazing discussions in class regarding the readings, very funny / interactive professor imo. If she ever seemed "mean" she moreso was just stressed out. Would totally take her again. Only had 2 essays + final project.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Absolutely loved Professor Yamato's class. Lots of reading, but if you keep up, you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Yamamoto was genuinely a wonderful teacher who actually sat down and went into detail for the books we read in class. Participation does matter but she fosters all ideas so you feel less anxious to speak up. I really enjoyed taking this class with her, and I will definitely be taking other classes with her if they arise.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Would definitely take again
Tough professor and grader
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: very tough grader and does not acknowledge open minded ideas
Writer's are not able to be open minded in this class. She demands one certain answer in Literature which is not possible with poetry in texts.

Definitely get ready to read. There are only two essays and two presentations worth your entire grade, the prompts are very straightforward but you definitely have to make sure you know what you read in the books. Otherwise she was an amazing professor, she was accessible outside class and gave great feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I enjoyed the readings for this class. The essays were very straightforward. Overall great class and great Prof. I wouldn't say she is an "easy" grader, but she is a fair one. Would definitely take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This was the most fun class I've ever taken. The texts were so interesting, and class discussions were really enjoyable. She was very helpful as well as funny and a pleasure to be around. Take this class if you enjoy reading and don't mind a lot of it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Heavy reading, but she makes the content interesting. She does a really good job of making sure you understand the content and is very helpful in office hours. She gladly helps critique essays and makes the material clear and concise. Funny, entertaining, and makes the content interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: It was a pretty challenging course as it forces you to think and analyze, but I learned a lot from this class. Grading:  Essays (two 6-7 & 7-8) page papers   60%  Quizzes, presentation & other assignments 15%  Discussion/participation/attendance  10%  Final exam     15%
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: I hated this class initially; however, by the end of the class, I can't wait to take another one! I loved the texts she chose, and I loved that the paper prompts were open to your own thoughts. You write about what interests you. She gave a few reading quizzes, but not every week. Final was reasonably challenging. Hope to take her again!

I'm on my 3rd class with this prof and she's amazing! It's a challenging class but in the best way. She gives quizzes to keep you on track with the reading. She has high but reasonable expectations for papers. She loves to have discussions so participate! She chooses interesting texts and really makes you think. Maybe tough for non-English majors.

She was a great lecturer and I loved going to class, but this class definitely had a lot of reading so make sure to keep up with it or else you will not do well on the quizzes and tests. She was so helpful and always available for feedback on essays. Just make sure you go to class because you can miss some crucial ideas that you need!

This class was by far, my least favorite taken at UCR.  The reading happens fast and is just seems way too critical and analytic, for what it really is. I feel that the analysis  of the books were stretched too much. And, the tests are HARD. You better memorize important quotes from the get-go. I just really disliked this class overall.

Lots and lots of reading. Analyses of the texts are the driving force of the course. Had trouble analyzing as in depth as she did. Gives pop quizzes often so you have to be on point with the assigned readings. Lectures were interesting and mostly full of discussion among the class. Definitely a challenging course, though. Takes attendance.

Definitely not the course to take for an easy A but if you want to really further yourself as a reader/writer I would highly recommend her. She really makes you analyze the heck out of texts, but it's good in the long run!

I absolutely love her! Not the class to take if you want an easy A. If you are willing to put in some work and want to be challenged and LEARN, she is your woman. Very clear on expectations and analysis. Also very available to students outside of class. I plan on taking as many classes as I can with her in my time at UCR!!

Prof. Yamamoto can be intimidating if you're not an English major or if you aren't 100% committed to the material. Also they're in the class I took they're were only 2 papers and a final (also a couple quizzes to make sure you were reading). That being said, If you mess up once you're going to have a write an awesome final!

Great professor! Great reading material. She really knows her stuff! I love her teaching style. She really gets the class to interact with her and makes you WANT to participate. It is important to keep up with the reading material, as she does call on people at random sometimes. She's also funny and makes a lot of spelling errors.
She is a nice professor and she makes lectures intresting and gives you good books to read.I would recomend her because she is an easy grader.

Dr. Yamamoto is amazing! Her choice in books and her level of analysis is perfect! She is incredibly intelligent and expects a lot from her students (as she should). I love this teacher would definitely take her again if I could.

One fact that can't be denied: Prof. Yamamoto has great taste in books!! She is charismatic and has passion for what she teaches. This professor LOVES her job and students need to take full advantage of her time. Her classes are not easy, but why should they be?!
Amazing.  I learned so much in such a short time.  Wonderful teacher, she genuinely cares about her students.  A++ teacher!

she is such an interesting professor. she is engaging in lectures and the books she chose for the course were all interesting. she's a hard paper grader though, but utilize office hours and she's incredibly helpful

I had her over summer school. There was a lot of work and reading to do but she was so passionate about teaching. She is probably one of the most challenging and interesting teachers I have had but well worth it. She is approachable, go to her office hours, it helps!!!

I was lucky to study with Traise at the University of Washington.  This was years ago but I have never forgotten her.  She is brilliant.  Too bad some of the kiddies here can't appreciate that kind of intellect.

She seems unapproachable sometimes because she (like most professors) has a stressful professional life and a home life in addition. She has a million things to do and not enough time to do them. Dr. Yamamoto will go to the mat for you, *but* not until you've earned her respect by being a thoughtful, hardworking, and professional student.

Yamamoto is fairly unapproachable and often gives students intimidating, blank stares in class. She does give somewheat helpful feedback on your work. However, in both class and on your papers, you have to be psychic. She wants students to fish around for the answers that she thinks are correct. I will not take another class from her.

Most ridiculous English class I have taken at UCR. Now I know that Literary Theory is just a class to make people sound smarter than they are. Yamamoto is also biased when grading, so unless your mind comes complete with fancy overloaded sophisticated psychoanalytic terminology, you're doomed. I've had her for other classes but this is horrible.
Professor Yamamoto is really interested in you getting the material and enjoying it. Fun and nice to look at too. Easy as long as you read. She calls on people randomly so be prepared!
She is a little strict on talking in class, but is really nice. She will give you a fair grade.

Not too difficult. She takes attendance everyday and counts it towards your grade. Had to post responses every week on blackboard. She's pretty understanding. Her lectures aren't the most interesting.

Tough professor, but I learned a lot. I think I almost get literary theory now. She's super helpful in office hours and really helped me in choosing and shaping my paper topic. Definitely recommend. One of the top professors I've had.
Great teacher, probably the best I had at Riverside.
Nice
No Comments
Learned more in her class than in several other classes combined.  Her expectations are high, and this pushes her students to do their best.
No Comments

Professor Trego is very thorough with answering any questions we may have, her lectures are very information dense but she makes it easy to understand and remember. I personally studied with the book but the lectures are clear enough to use on their own. Shes easy to reach, very nice and organized.

kind and witty professor. very flexible with the course schedule and whether or not an exam would be in-person or online. lectures were very straightforward. the 3 exams were mainly mcq and simple. you have ample time to complete the final project and she was very lenient with its submission times (barely a late penalty).
Understanding professor. Had one project, one midterm and a final, all online. Do the work and you will get an A

I went into this class not wanting to take it (was forced to as a Transfer student) but it quickly became my favorite class this quarter! The lectures are super interesting (mandatory too, but at least one gets dropped at the end). There is a quarter-long project but if you communicate with your TAs it is very easy. Highly recommend!

To pass the class you have to memorize every slide word for word-- undoable unless you want to orbit the entirety of your life around this class alone.

He will post the slides, but you have to go to the lectures to get all the material. Tests on lecture content, not just slides. ALSO GET THE BOOK.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This professor is extremely UNETHICAL as he forces students to purchase his own overpriced online textbook, clearly profiting off his class. He's consistently rude and dismissive during lectures, creating a hostile learning environment. His tests are absurdly difficult, packed with irrelevant content not covered in class. Avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Was pretty hard for a breadth course. His lectures were just him reading off the slides. His exams were based off of very minuscule details you'd likely only pick up from him saying it in lecture though so I suggest attending or having someone record. He actually caught someone recording and got upset about it though so keep this in mind.

Chill guy and you can tell he is passionate about his work. Class itself was pretty easy but it's scaled weird so its hard to get an actual A. He did end up curving so a lot so if you just read the textbook and actually study you should be able to get an A- or B+.
Attend his lectures because on the test there is questions from the lecture. Also a weekly quiz which is very easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Do not take if this is not your major requirement class. I took this as a GE class and this is so difficult and boring. This class is definitely not an intro-level class, there are so many concepts to remember and all we learn is highly theoretical and technical. After taking this class your passion for anthropology will get destroyed.

reviews.comment: 57% of the grade is from the 2 midterms and final. You have to buy HIS textbook new to get a code to take the quizzes. Lectures help a lot, but if you read and study the slides he uploads you'll be fine. Easy to pass the class, but an A will take some effort to get.

reviews.comment: definitely one of the worst professor I have ever had. His lectures were extremely heavy and unrelated to tests. Textbook is written by him and is $90 and is required. Terrible experience

reviews.comment: umm idk, hes just a normal teacher. he is not the greatest as his lectures only have like two words on it. you like reallllyyyyyy need to listen and write down what hes saying so yes very lecture heavy. he certainly knows what hes talking about though, his exams are very different and difficult
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lacture is not helpful in creating a clear concept of the ideas discussed. Not a good introduction to Archeology as a major. As interesting as ARCH is, this course will kill that passion as the expectation of this class is way too high for an introduction. If you care about how much you enjoy your classes, stay far away from this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment:
Stay away! 

For a Breadth requirement class, this feels more like a post grad class. Assistance is abysmal; lecture slides when posted on canvas do no include images with questionable reasonibg.

The way that his class operates does not serve as a warm welcome to this major.

He does great reviews of what's in the textbooks and is very light on homework only asking for small quizzes that are asked for barely every other week and gives you an entire week to complete them. He is very caring and is happy to help those who fear they need extra support in which he gives plenty in his zoom calls. Students will be very lucky!

57% of your grade are exams and they test on random stuff. Average on the exams is a D and he does not curve. Lectures are boring and completely useless, so is the $90 textbook he requires. TA gives no help. Just take another anthropology class that gives online & at home, open-note exams. Waste of time and a GPA killer!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Hard course in general, tests are hard and required us to remember many bs. Did not like the class or topic for the most part.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Nothing against the professor, I just hate archeology. Midterms are hard, study and do the extra credit. The textbook is like 85 dollars, and is REQUIRED. It has all the quizzes on it, and those are super easy. It's an easy class and easy A if you put in a little effort. Prof gives bad lectures, and its not worth going. Also, slides are posted.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You have to pay $90 to buy his textbook to do the homework. This type of predatory policy is abhorrent and needs to die out.

Lectures were a bit boring but if you show up and take notes (minimum effort) then you'll do well on the exams and get an A. He wants his students to pass. I really appreciated this class (GPA booster) and I think he and his TAs were very nice.
Terrible lecturer, did not know how to use zoom. Very boring and did not seem passionate about the subject matter.

Mixed feelings. It wasn't difficult and Stanton is not a hard grader. Also, Stanton clearly put effort into crafting this class. I respect a professor that works hard. Students do not have to attended class, but you will not gain prof's tips / help. Here's my hate - It's 95% group work and your peers have anonymous control 20% of your grade. FYI
