reviews.comment: I hated the lectures they were grouped together so literally its a lecture thats 4 hours long not much info really to see whats discussed in lecture. There is some lecture that are short. The lectures are just very unorganized just so lengthy these are aside from the actual lecture too.
His lectures are very boring and the tests are based on a combination of material in the textbook which is required and his monotone lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Overall a solid choice for an intro to archaeology class. Only downside is that final is cumulative. Attendance to lectures is not mandatory, he basically just repeats what is on slides. A lot of online quizzes that are due but very easy. Extra credit opportunities in discussion section. Repetitive if you are not interested in the subject matter.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Honestly a great professor and a great class. The book isn't really necessary at all. Follow the study guide and memorize a few vocabularies and an A is easy. His lectures are entertaining and he's a great professor.

First Midterm was easy. Second Midterm was spicy, but easy. Final was spicy, but easy. Study time for all exams were about 2 nights each. His lectures are amazing and you only have to take light notes. His grading is simple but leads to many A-'s and little A's.

Professor Stanton was overall good. His lectures can be very heavy if you are not interested in the material and can be hard to tune him in at times. You have to make sure to write down the notes from his slides as well as what he is saying because he does not post slides. Discussion is worth lots of points so that helps your grade if you attend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Stanton was very knowledgable on his topic, enhanced by his firsthand experience. If I were considering archaeology, his lectures would be fascinating- but i'm not, so it was hard to stay tuned in. Tons of content from his slides (which he does not post online) and he will test on things shared vocally as well as visually.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Stanton is a great professor! Basically everything thats in the lecture is directly put in the midterms (2). The grading criteria is pretty basic. 2 Midterms, 5 (very easy) homework assignments, and attendance/participation in discussion. The book is helpful, but not needed. Bonus questions on the midterms are based off the reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The class is more centered around the discussions. Having to do exercises mainly. There are 2 midterms and a final. Lectures theres no attendance but he doesn't put up slides on ilearn so you should go or at least have a friend that goes to get notes. Overall, not a hard class. He's clear with his knowledge of the subject.
reviews.rating_tags: Tests? Not many--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Usually doesn't assign homework, just readings. Class is based off of a midterm, a final paper, and a final exam. The exams can be a bit challenging ONLY if you don't pay attention or at least attempt to pay attention. Overall great professor but don't expect an easy A if you don't attend classes and/or do the readings
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Lectures were pretty boring and dont get me started on the professor! Dont need book, nothing posted online, must attend lectures. I attended lectures daily and did really well except when he messed up my grade. I aced the final but he forgot to input it so my grade was an F, I contacted him and it took him 8 months to fix it. Check your grades!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great professor and is very clear. Need to attend class

If you're used to teachers placing their presentations online, and zoning out in lecture, you're going to have a tough time. However, if you actually take notes and look over them before tests, you'll be fine. Memorize any lists of things, as  a significant portion of the tests are short answer. Go to discussion sections (gives bump in grade).

He's a good lecturer but the class is long and boring. He doesn't post any lecture slides online, so you have to go to class and take notes. He gives study guides for the exams which include every single topic he has lectured on. Flashcards are the best way to study. Going to discussion bumps up your grade with points for attendance and exercises.

It's obvious Professor Stanton loves Archaeology, but lecturing is not his strong suit. He spends a lot of time talking about his excavations while trying to explain information students will need for exams, but never clearly makes the connection. Luckily  the T.A.'s are amazing. The midterms (2) are not super difficult,  but final is cumulative!
Stanton is really nice. He'll help you when you ask. Only thing you need to pass the class easy is memorization because short answers are all listing things.

I took his class, I think he's a very good lecturer but he has admitted that his midterms and finals are defined by a randomizing program (which is not awesome if you care about relevance). He'll usually post a 5 point bonus at tests with a somewhat difficult fact to remember.

the powerpoint materials are harduninteresting to follow. Doesnt post online for review at home when you do need them. personally didn't find it very interesting. if you take this class you're better off reading the book. and going to the class for review.

-SUPER clear grading -a max of 1 homework assignment a week and they're pretty cool -tests are directly based off of the power points and he offers a bonus question each time and no essay questions - I recommend flash cards to study and practically guarantee an A if you actually try -attendance only mandatory for discussion
The lectures are sort of fast paced, but they aren't impossible
Doesn't post ANYTHING online and very hard to take notes in class. I would only recommend if you have a very strong interest in archeology.

Hard to take notes for. Doesn't post powerpoints online and doesn't let you record lectures but expects you to remember stuff from when he's speaking, even when you're writing down information from the powerpoint. Definitely not an easy A.

Simultaneously has high and low expectations for students. I agree that students should have taken the class more seriously than they were but there was also a lack of leeway for people who had unforeseeable issues with the class or material. The tests were easy and there was a lot of room for extra credit.

Professor Kahn is a pretty good professor and the "dirty 030" is actually a very useful class for everybody. Her lecture slides go by really fast because of 50 minute lecture times so prepare to read the textbook chapters. Be prepared to see some explicit pictures and talk about uncomfortable topics that need to be talked about in life anyway.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dirty 30 is an interesting class and is memed for a reason.  The content is easy, yes-- but also a lot.  It has a reputation of being easy but there's a lot to actually learn and you might even need to study a bit to get a good grade ( A+ is the only acceptable grade you should want ).  Prof is chill, cracks jokes about the content.  Take it.

Lectures were long and dragged at some points, but the quizzes and exams were very close to the practice exams she gave. If you do the learning objectives, that will also suffice. In discussion, ur TA should provide u with a study guide for the exams. Ur mostly tested on memorization abilities rather than application, so study ahead!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She's a good lecturer. There are a lot of extra credit opportunities through fun activities. Lectures are heavy content but as long as you know the learning objectives, you will be fine. Exams are straightforward and easy as long as you studied.

Her class was honestly so interesting and professor kahn loves what she does. I love when a professor really enjoys what they teach and she does that. She does fun little poll everyone questions that make class more enjoyable and get some giggles out of it. I def recommend this course if you can take it!! Also there's no lab, just discussion.

Course is very manageable, just a few quizzes and assignments and 2 exams. Exams are based off the slides so study them to prepare. Make sure to go over the practice questions as well because similar questions come up on the exam. Overall it is a fun class, you learn a lot of interesting facts.
Absolute beast! A must take at UCR. Such a sweet heart, amazing lecturer, and clearly passionate about the subject. 10/10 recommend and 15/10 would take again!

Tests were a lot of memorization and small details, wasnt bad but wasnt easy. Teacher was clearly enthusiastic and the TA's are also very happy. Decent chunk is pollev participation, and assignments and discussion section also had a lot.
She's cool.
Her class is an easy A and she answers emails pretty well. she also tries to make time to review for tests .

The grading scale in this class is heavily in your favor. I got mid-C's on midterm and final and still has an A in the course. You get points for attending and attempting. The material is fun and will probably be your only opportunity to learn such crazy topics in a higher institution. You'll leave this class with a lot of cool random knowledge.

I absolutely loved this class. She offers so many interesting lenses to look at sex and sexuality from, and she offers so many interesting and insightful guest lectures. The class is a really easy A, I passed with an A and I never had to use the textbook because all the info is in the lecture slides. Prof. Kahn is awesome, definitely recommend.

Tracy is an amazing professor, so caring and knowledgeable about the subject. Class is an Easy A if you do all the assignments and do the poll everywhere's she has each class. It's a light work load and she posts the slides and answers keys to exams after they're taken. You'll actually learn a lot in this class and she's fun 10/10 recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: A decent man, and an overall unengaging professor with lectures that move far slower than they have any right to. Homework is tolerable and is better than the main part of class. If you like group discussions (albeit online) take his class if unengaging lectures are not something that concerns you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took his class at CSUSB the class is decent in my opinion. There is a lot of work required for this course. The lectures are dreadfully long. He is straightforward and easy through. You have 9 out of 12 discussion posts to do, every lecture, and two essays. It is not that bad but it was a lot of work through. Class is straightforward and easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This is for Financial Economics he literally does not know what he is doing. I overheard him tell a TA he is still grasping the concepts of the course. The answer key of the homeworks had to be corrected upwards of 4 times because he kept getting them wrong. Yes the professor can't do the homework correct. Midterm study guides don't have answer key

Professor's grading criteria was very straight forward and clear. Gives 2 videos and 1 Discussion each week. Very organized. Some videos can be up to an hour long though. This class was very easy to pass and if you're falling behind, he is accommodating. He wants you to pass.

His class is very straightforward: weekly discussion board questions, video surveys, readings, and reflection papers. For the discussion boards, you only have to do 9 out of the 12 and 2 out of the 4 reflection papers, and all video surveys to pass. Take advantage of the extra credit! Put in the time and you'll get the grade you want.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I have no strong feelings about this professor, he gets the point across and has an engaging-enough online lecture. Overall, a safe option, just remember to do those discussion boards.

He is a very good professor! 10/10
This course consists of 12 discussion posts+responses (packback), 12 lecture surveys, and 4 essays. Although, you only have to do 9 discussion post+responses, 9 lecture surveys, and 3 short essays. 
He is very helpful and always available if you have any questions!
Definitely take this class, very easy!

This class was really interesting. His classwork is manageable, weekly hour-long video with questions and weekly pack back questions and reading. The reading is long but you can skim and get a good idea. There are also a few written essays but he gives you more than enough time to finish all of them. There is also extra credit, overall great prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Truby has a lot of experience teaching French and often offers her own opinions and experiences in the class which is hilarious more often than not. Class consists of weekly quizzes on movies watched and 3x weekly lectures and 2 midterms which are both online. If you watch the movies and analyze the scenes you will get an A. 10/10 Prof.

The class was fine, but the professor did come off as belittling at times, especially when it came to speaking the language. With any foreign language it is going to be difficult to pronounce, remember and practice no matter how much studying is done. But the professor moved really fast without helping those who were falling behind and struggling.
She's really nice, you'll do good in this course if you pay attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Had Prof Truby for french 1 and 3. Her classes are structured the same way. She can teach well and has videos for grammar. I'd recommend participating to get her to know you. Do not drive and zoom, she will be upset. Do not ask grammar questions before watching her videos she posts, bc she doesn't seem to like repeating herself, very understandable
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Truby writes a lot of helpful feedback on the daily assignments, so I recommend reading her comments and going to her optional classes. 2 midterms and a final in the same format as weekly tests, go to the presentation workshop, and bring questions for the review sessions. Try to speak in class, as she'll help you with pronunciation.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: An amazing professor! She really does care about her students. If you have trouble, just let her know! She's willing to help and is super funny.

Professor Truby is extremely intelligent, (which I like) but also funny and committed to her students. My only problem with her is that she never teaches two sections in a row, so if you can't take all of your classes with her, like you can with other language teachers. I'll miss her next quarter.

Not my favorite of the french instructors, but still very good. Follows the same format as the rest of the french classes. Towards the end you start to read a french book which was pretty cool. Nothing really to worry about here. Just show up, do the work, study for the tests, and you'll do fine. If you got this far into french you should pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof. Truby is a great  French teacher. She actually taught Jennifer Ramos who also teaches here, and so their styles are very similar. If you like Jennifer you will like Truby and vice versa. You just have to show up and listen and do the homework. Participation is important . She's really good at helping you learn.

Kelle was such an amazing professor, she really made me love French and I wish I had her for French 002 but unfortunately didn't have her. No other professor can compare to her, she made learning French fun and always clarified the lessons. If you have her you are lucky, no other teacher would want to help you succeed more than she does.

Updating my rating from 4/9/09. Now that I am a PhD student and looking back at my materials from 9A/9B, I am so grateful for Kelle and for the classes. They are SO helpful for translating. I am now UNFORTUNATELY enrolled in Elementary German (not at UCR), and it is terrible. Take languages from a linguist, NOT someone from an Education department.

The subject matter of the class is pretty interesting but the Professor likes to clown too much. She really likes being the center of attention. Laugh with her or she will become mean and put you down. Play along and it's an easy A. Just don't get bitten by the snake!

First of all, Kelle is hilarious. She's sharp as a tack and she's beyond spunky. Her style is all her own. Check out her shoes. They are always cool! But beyond the superficial, she is an exceptional professor with extensive knowledge of the french language considering it's not her native tongue. On top of that getting a good grade is a cinch!

Poor Professor Truby had to put up with some truly rude students who seemed to enjoy trying to  make her feel bad.  That wan't fun for anyone, but she still managed to teach a solid class and make it as useful and enjoyable as possible. I think she's amazing.  A beautiful woman too.  Take her class and hope for no meanies.

yes, she is entertaining. however, as a grad student, i would rather the lectures be clear and COHERENT than funny. also, as has been mentioned, she is INCREDIBLY condescending - seems sort of bitter. i am in 9B right now, and this seems to increase with every week. she treats 9A like a bi-weekly social hour, and then raises expectations in 9B.
I had Truby for French 1 and 2; she is a wonderful professor who is sincerely interested in making sure her students succeed. Go to class everyday, and you'll get an A... she's funny too.

I've had Truby for French 3, French 9A, French 15A, and French 101A and she is awesome. Super quirky and hilarious. I love her. You must study and do the homework and practice your french in order to do well, of course!
KELLE IS THE BEST IN THE WORLD!
Prof Truby was a fun teacher who still managed to get her lessons across.  Take her class if you have a chance.

I didn't enjoy Truby's 15A class because of the lack of homework assignments and the emphasis on phonetic transcription and conversation, but she's an interesting prof.  She's well-dressed and funny, but she does have condescending streak and, if you listen closely, behind most of her jokes is more than a hint of mocking.
Prof. Kelle is a truly great teacher. She is knowledgeable and always willing to help.  And she's hot!
Smart, sexy, sweet.
I love Prof. Truby! She is an awesome professor. Really knows her stuff. Very interesting and very funny! Also a great dresser! Highly recommend.

I took the French reading knowledge course woth Truby, and she was amazing.  She's witty, has a thorough knowledge of her subject, friendly, and gorgeous.  I would trade half the profs. in my home department for one like her.
Kelli was a fantastic prof. Especially for someone like me who dreads French class. She's sharp and is willing to help. Feel lucky if you take her class.

I wish I had the time to continue classes with her. She's an awesome teacher!  I learned more in her one class than the other 3 combined.  She's smart and stylish and sassy and really helps her students.
No Comments

This comment carries over to any class that Truby teaches. She is incredibly condescending, but people don't usually see it when she hides behind her humor and laughs. She thinks most riverside kids are lazy which is absolutely insulting. I don't understand how nobody has seen this. Despite her shortcomings, she's a somewhat thorough teacher.
No Comments
This teacher rocks and she sings really well. She TCBs.

I LOVE KELLE! Best Prof i've ever had. I only took 15a so i could have a class with her,  i'm not even a french minor. Fun class to go to, so refreshing. I missed one class in 15a and regreted it. Take anything she teaches!

Wonderful to hear that she's just as good (if not better)at UCR.  She was awesome as a grad student teaching intro French at UCD.  Had a very quick-witted and lively personality; made the course fun and challenging.
French has never been this much fun! Very lively lectures - you're sometimes surprised that the lecture is over already. Fairly easy too, if you put out the effort and do the work assigned.

Trubie is like a God compared to the French 9B teacher (some crazy round lady).  Trubie is sassy, smart, and has a great accent.  Additionally, she truly seeks to help the students in her class.  Her positive and zany attitude made learning French fun :-)
One of the coolest profs I've ever had!
I SUCK at french.. really, really, super badly. But this chicka is awesome and fun and VERY helpful. Wonderful schoolin' experience.. and she is an alum from my highschool! Rock On Trube!
awesome man , just awesome

I had to take this class for BREADTH. He is a very chill and respected professor. He uses PollEverywhere, but his midterms and finals are very straightforward. If you read, you will pass easily. There is a textbook required to purchase, which is a little pricey. Overall, I recommend him.

I'm not an Anth student by his class was my favorite of the semester. He can be a little monotone at times but you can still tell he genuinely loves what he does. He can sometimes have difficulties when it comes to answering questions but when it comes to grading you'll be golden if you take notes in lecture and suplement that with the textbook.

Failed both midterms and the final. pretty much all the info was random facts. PARTICIPATE IN POLLS, those absolutely saved my grade. Prof wasn't bad, I just was not super interested in the topic hence my lack of focus. Very personable professor.

I took this professor my first quarter as a first year and it wasn't overwhelming. The exams aren't that hard and they give you a lot of extra credit for just participating in lectures. Definitely take his intro to archaeology class.

Not a back-busting class, but not a easy as others claim. While heavy reading is implied, the midterms/finals really just rely a lot on the flashcards provided, besides the SAQs. There are a lot of terms you need to remember.

Dr. Tsukamoto is a cool guy though, just a thick accent that could make lectures a bit hard to follow.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment:
took this class because it was the only thing open and i actually enjoyed his class 10/10
exams were a bit difficult but there are bonus questions

Professor Tsukamoto seems really nice but is hard to understand with his thick accent. You kind of have to go to lectures for the polls he does which are graded. Just read the book (which you are required to get and it costs like $100) and you will be fine. The 2 midterms and final are straightforward and easy.

I got an 105% in the class by skimming the textbook and attending 60% of lectures. Very interesting course but definitely a lot of work for breadth, which is why I know a lot of people who failed. I would say the only inconvenience is that attendance is practically mandatory because you get PollEv credit where you need to answer correctly as well.

Professor Tsukamoto really cares for his students and is clear in what he expects you to know for each exam. There is readings for each lecture but I never did them and did very well on all exams. Make sure to study for the exams and you'll be fine. Offers extra credit which was pretty substantial and boosted me up a great deal, just go to lecture!

A bit hard to follow at times, but the content isn't hard, pretty easy A if you study a bit. Just pretend his study guides don't exist though, they're super useless. Also his textbook is like $100 and is required for the weekly quizzes, and you basically never use it. Content is pretty basic, but interesting, and the discussion activities are cool

Really easy and straightforward class. Two midterms and a final comprised of multiple choice, true/false, and short answer questions. SAQs were sometimes graded harshly, but each exam had at least 10% extra credit for a bonus question. Prof. has a relatively strong accent, but is clearly passionate. PollEv questions were hidden though, which sucks.

Very straightforward, had two midterms, weekly online quizzes, mandatory attendance, and a discussion with exercises (~5 of them). The prof is hard to understand at times but it is relatively easy to navigate. Was a large sentiment that the class was hard, but if you put in a solid amount of work you will do well. Overall easy class.

Very hard to understand his lectures. Midterms are very difficult and on paper. The study guide is the entire chapter of terms (100+ terms per chapter; not helpful). Study guides are 3 pages long with 2 columns on each page for TWO CHAPTERS, it's insane. You have to know the terms in full detail for the examines bc exam questions are obscure.

Amazing lectures, the tests are based on what is taught in the lecture and in the discussion. I never had to use to book but you still need it to do the weekly quizzes. Very easy class no much effort was needed.

Take for free ANTH credit, easy A. A Few essays and online exams all open notes. PollEV is used for extra grade booster. The textbook costs money I think it was around 100ish. If you need a 5-unit GPA booster take the class.

Has a very thick accent and is hard to understand. Assignments and quizzes are online and straight forward. Tests are taken on Canvas . You do have to buy his textbook though which is like $100. Polleverywhere is used pretty much every class and counts towards your grade. Class is reading heavy but if you attend lectures you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He would have his favorites and ended up giving "extra" credit to students who were always his favorite. It went as far as the discord was full of them bragging how he had given them more points then the normal. TA's are great but overall this course was only passable to his favorite students

Honestly the class was very easy. He presents the lecture slides and does polleverywhere. Assignments are only assigned at discussion so you would need to go to them. Quizzes every week, only four questions. Mid-term was open-notes.

Love Dr. Tsukamoto. He's really easygoing and it's clear he has a lot of passion for his field. Lectures are concise and interesting, and Tsukamoto is exceptionally reasonable. Super understanding, and just really wants you to succeed. Readings can be heavy, workloads are fine, midterms are moderately easy as long as you've been following along.

I took this class ANTH 005 and mostly everything, the quizzes, the homework, and sometimes lectures were online. It was a pretty easy class if you would attend lectures everything would come easy. He does have an accent but you understand through his slides. I would recommend taking him!! super interested and super kind!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: He has an accent which is a little hard to understand but the written information is on the slides and study guide. Hes funny and cares about the students. Also had him for ARCH001, for that class, make sure to do the quizzes!
A very easy class, he uses an online textbook quiz thingy and polleverywhere for lecture attendance

I loved having Professor Tsukamoto as a teacher. He's incredibly passionate about the subject matter, which made his lectures incredibly engaging. He has a great sense of humor as well. Definitely be ready to read from the textbook and to take notes during lecture to do well on the midterm and final. I'm not an anthro major but I loved this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Fantastic professor! His grading criteria is precise and he is accommodating to emergencies. He does have an accent, deal with it. He has so much to teach his students and he is the sweetest person. He is lecture heavy but everything not in lecture is in the textbook, which wasn't expensive. Show up, pay attention, you pass. Participation matters.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He calmly reviews the material
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Tsukamoto has some wonderful lectures. I enjoyed the coursework and the discussions. If you do the reading and study the vocabulary then that is the heart of the course. Outside of class he is thoughtful and extremely helpful and I found him to have the best advice on education as well as the academic journey. I would learn from him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Need the book to get access to the website where weekly quizzes are due, but can just purchase the code. Two midterms and one final. Multiple choice, true/false, and essay questions. Weekly assignments in discussion but they're easy and fun to complete. It is a fun class to attend if you like learning about the ancient Mexican civilizations!

An easy class. Just make sure to study for the two midterms and final. There are online quizzes that have to do with the reading. For discussions, there are activities that are due mostly each week. Lecture is not mandatory, but go to discussion.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Literally one of my favorite teachers! He gives chapters to read before lecture and I HIGHLY recommend you read the chapters and take notes before lecture because during lecture he presents very fast. The midterm and finals arent too bad, I was always over prepared for them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Easy class! Only thing is you have to get $100 textbook with access code to do the homework which are weekly quizzes. Lecture has polleverywhere clicker questions with questions only show on the screen. Pretty easy A if you do the work. 2 midterms 1 final!

Honestly, I love this class, and I don't even love archaeology. The class itself has the fairest grading system ever where you get a lot of easy opportunities to bump your grade up, it's very straightforward and as long as you pay attention and study, it's an EASY A. The professor himself is great. He's kind and non-judgmental and open to everyone.

Don't take the course if you're not willing to spend $100 on a book he wrote. Not sure about previous quarters but we were forced to buy the book in order to gain access to this special website where the lectures, notes, and quizzes (which are worth 50 points and not optional) are only available. Also, he has a VERY heavy accent.

Great professor. I am a transfer student and fall18 was my first quarter. I am an anthropology major but have always been alittle unsure if I really wanted to major in this. His excitement on the topic really inspired me to love anthropology. He gives 2 midterms and final,participate in class, he will give extra credit points at the end of quarter

The course was easy in general. You don't need the textbook. Just study off his slides and create group study guides for the midterm and final. Tests aren't difficult. He has an accent, so it's sometimes difficult to take notes. Purchase top hat for his course, sine he doesn't use clickers. Not an easy class if you don't study.

his lectures were great, he has an accent so it was kinda hard to understand him at times. There are 2 midterms and they are pretty straightforward, his study guides for midterms and the final help out a lot.

Professor Ken is an amazing professor who actively tries to engage his students in lecture. There can be a lot of readings, but they are all so interesting it is incredibly manageable. 10/10 Would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: The easiest class I ever took! I never even looked at the book. His tests are pretty straight forward, he'll give you a study guide prior, however it usually just the title of every powerpoint and slide. But his midterms are super straight forward and no trick questions. But show up to class everyday! He adds a lot of stuff that isn't written down.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I emailed him in regards to a question on the study guide and he said "I explained it in the lectures several times." First of all, he has a VERY Strong accent and it is very hard to understand him!!! You would prefer reading his books than attending his lecture. I struggled understanding what he had to say. He seems very welcoming, I guess.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He taught an identical course at UCSD during the summer and he's been a structured and generous professor despite the strict rigor and difficulty of the content.

This class is the hardest class I've taken at UCR but If you want to learn architecture this class is golden. Prof. Tseng puts an insane amount of effort to teach/construct the course. Usually system courses tend to be a lot of memorizing but his teaching style managed to turn new concepts into intuition and he proved concepts through live demos.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Very harsh professor. Like making Asian jokes no matter whether students like it or not. The attendance is compulsory. The experience is really bad

DON'T TAKE IT. YOU HAVE BEEN WARNED.
lab autograder sucks like hell. you gotta master mindreading to finish them.
gaslighting in lectures when you get bad grades.
emotionally unstable, rage outbursts from nowhere.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are good, but the auto-grading system wastes time on irrelevant details, and exams are unnecessarily hard. Despite the professor's self-identification as a bunny, he can be harsh and intimidating. For example, in the final, a student was disqualified for viewing the test paper early. The student was wrong, but the response was excessive.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He doesn't quiz you on what he teaches and straight up yaps during lecture. Would be fine if quizzes weren't 30% of your grade... Also his final project requirements were way too abstract and he basically left it up to us to figure out what he wanted - he made us design a GUI in an environment that doesn't even support them??

This class was harder than 141 and that's a high bar. The professor is out of his league to continue teaching and his TAs are out of touch. We had labs and a group project without any help from the TAs and they still graded harshly. The tests are alright except for the final which wasn't cumulative at all. Learn databases on your own if you can!

Professor can't teach at all. His slides were very confusing. Final project instructions were very unclear and TAs would take off points for things they never even asked for in the first place. Avoid mehnaz if you can. Because of the strike the TAs were MIA for 3 or so weeks so didn't get any help on the project and they still graded harshly.

Please skip him for the love of god. His explanations actually adds confusion to the materials. His accent is terrible and this is coming from an ESL student. Homework is never graded. He talks all the way from the beginning to the end of the class. I ended up learning by myself. I only showed up to the midterm and final.

I went into his class with a curiosity for database management and came out not despising database management. The course materials/slides are resourceful, but his explanation is not. His explanation adds no value or clarity to the slides but confusion to many students. He over-explains the simplest concept and gloss over the more difficult concept
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: Good experience in the COVID era. Understands the difficulty in online classes, and takes students requests into consideration each time. Extends deadlines and gives scope for scoring bonus points.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He is a very nice professor! The content is boring on the slides, especily when he is being very thorough and teaches some topics slowly. However, he gives a really good curve even though the midterm and final was as expected. All the content was reviewed to us before hand so the questions were fair. Practice the hw questions to get an A!

Lectures are pretty boring but some what useful especially if you read the material before coming to class.  Overall the class is easy and I guess that also made it enjoyable for me anyway.  He took a lot of questions from the book for the final and midterm but I hear he switches it up every quarter.

Class was fairly easy and straightforwards. However, the final was more difficult than the midterm so be sure to study. His slides are not entirely helpful so watching his demo on the board is a good idea.

Easy class... Not everything's on the Final, so pick and choose when to attend.  Can be boring, but explains things 10 times over, so it's easy to understand.  My friend got a B and went to 4 or 5 lectures all quarter (first, one or two more, midterm and final).  I got an easy A.

I took him over the summer and he was the best. His attendance wasn't mandatory and he posted all his lecture notes. Midterm and Final were pretty hard but he curves the class very heavily. Homework was graded based on completion and he was very patient during office hours and after class. Overall great experience with Professor Tsutsui.
Chill and fair professor. Quizes were very similar to lecture notes. HW was hard. Exams were fair and they were very similar to some of the homework questions.

Pro tip: Don't make the curriculum uneven. You should have quickly done Chapters 1 and 2 during week 1, 3 and 4 for Week 2, and 5 for Week 3, 6 for Week 4, and 8 and 9 for Week 5. I know you covered them in lecture, but you're bad at teaching. It's better to spend that time at home doing the homework and studying. Your homework solutions are trash.
final was something else

Quizzes are 20% & and mostly based on example problems done in class. Midterm exams are 40% and based mostly on HW problems. Attend the midterm review sessions because at least 1 of the problems worked out the sessions appear in the midterm. A lot homework problems are assigned and posted along with solutions but not graded/collected. Final is 40%
This class is overall pretty simple. He will go through problems step by step and is very straightforward. The exams are almost identical to the sample midterm.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He's a really nice guy. He gave me a lot of good career advises.

He honestly did pretty well in lecture. If you pay attention in class, the concepts are pretty simple. The quizzes are fair. Study the homework questions b/c the exam questions were generally very similar.
Hes not helpful in office hours and will make you feel stupid and his tests and homework are impossible.

He is not very clear in his concepts but takes some effort. Friendly guy and kind of lenient with grading but still the overall course experience was traumatic with the class being unclear all the time

Pretty bad teacher. Boring lectures. Homework that barely relates to class material. Office Hours were useless. He is very nice but just can't teach. Averages were extremely low and he barely curbed. If your'e an enve eng. major stay away.

Pretty good professor. Very straightforward in his exams. Practice a lot and pay attention in his lectures! He does care for his students. The truss project was really fun and I enjoyed it. Would not mind taking this professor later on in the future.

Very straight forward lecturing. No fluff, stay awake and there's no way you can't succeed. Goes through lots of examples in class and really solves things methodically. Weekly homework/quizzes. Fun group bridge project. Not too bad of an accent. He is kind of taken back when asked a question in class though. For an easy class, he does well.

One of the worst professors I have ever had. Looks down the entire lecture at his laptop & talks to it. When you ask a question, he either replies as if you are dumb, or just looks at you for a few seconds and then moves on with lecture. Claims he wants to help students but in reality only cares about his research. Teaching is his second priority.

This professor could be slightly boring during lecture. However, I found that when I really tried to pay attention this professor taught the material very thoroughly. She often tried to show us cool experiements as well to demonstrate what we were learning in class at the time. Additionally, the curve at the end of the class was massive.

This professor has no idea how to lecture the class in an understandable way. All she does are unhelpful derivations to the most simplest equations for absolutely no reason at all. Her sample midterms do not prepare you for the midterm and neither will the homework.

Decent Professor at UCR, He does care about his students. However, I felt I didn't learn much from the lectures. I went to discussions for assisted help and still didn't pass.

2 tests & homework. Material is kind of hard if you are not advanced in excel and this is not an easy class if you don't try. Professor is so empathetic to us student and being so flexible with us. He made this quarter a little more bearable for us.

Professor Tsuha is great! He's so nice and his grading is fair.

soc 1 . i dont care what the heck you are going through in life to pass this class you need to put in the work, do all the guided questions for all the chapters. he gives you 5 extra credits for doing 6 pages of guided questions. if you go to tutoring he gives you extra credit one point, if you attend 1 event u get 1 point.

Amazing professor! He's very into what he teaches and is a very down to earth guy. Super easy to talk to and there when you need help. Definitely recommend.
By far, one of the best professors I've had. You can really tell he cares about what hes teaching about.

Great professor. He cares about what he teaches, and actually deos something to improve the injustices that he is aware of. he knows his subject. the only down fall is the group paper--if one of the members doesn't do their work then its a down fall for all.

He is a really good professor.  He wants everyone to do well and learn the material, and still have fun. His class was very interesting. Overall he is a very nice and funny guy. Hes pretty SEXY too ;)   Take his class!

wow, this is the best class i've ever had.  plus, he's just so sexy, it made me want to go to class everyday.  plus, he's also so smart.  he was way better looking than the ta's that worked for him, but they were not bad either.  anyways, Go Clippers!
He explained the material very well and I got an A in the class. Go to class

She did a fantastic job teaching my GEO 009 class. Her class can be hard to understand, however if you attend office hours you should receive proper help.

Professor Turner's tests are difficult, but she allows you to bring a single double sided page of notes for the exam. This turned out to be an amazing studying technique I learned.

Professor KT is a cool professor! She is passionate about what she teaches and tries to make the course fun for all. The homework she assigned for Oceanography is very easy MC questions for the week, and she is always open to questions, including about your grades.

I wish I read all the reviews before taking this class for GE credit. The exams will definitely kill your grade and all the questions focus on super trivial stuff. Her exams have nothing to do with the notes, very specific and difficult class. Average was 50% on midterm and no curve was given. Talks very fast and lots of notes given. She is nice and the notes aren't bad but the exams destroy y0our grade because they are way too specific.

The course overall is just difficult but she definitely helps, also she goes through the slides kind of quick and its just information overload sometimes. Theres weekly quizzes and theyre open note so taking good notes will save you!! Also rlly watch the lectures in order if you dont attend bc by the time you get 1 think she'll be on the next alr.

reviews.comment: Honestly, a good breadth course for a PHYS requirement.  I do agree that some lessons are a little hard but just pay attention and ask questions (go to office hours) if you're stuck and you'll be fine. Overall, The professor is nice, but the class is HARD. Lots of information is being thrown at you for over an hour, homework has nothing to do with the lectures or content of the course, and the professor seems very disinterested. Her lecture notes aren't relatively that useful on exams.

reviews.comment: Honestly, some of the stuff was interesting. This class is not easy, it's a lot of information to take in especially if you're not familiar with oceanography so make sure you read the book and study!!! reviews.comment: A lot of information is given, be prepared to study! She talks really fast and her tests are very hard regardless of it being open note.

reviews.comment: Her tests aren't really are about specifics, but rather concepts.
Here lectures were hard to get through at times. You're over loaded with information. Just be ready to actually write down all the notes. You need the notes in order to pass the class.

Overall, professor Turner seemed fair. Oceanography definitely is a very informative class but assignments were not hard at all. Tests for sure require lots of studying but quizzes were really easy. Online made it better as everything was open note. Maybe lecture can get overwhelming but its a geoscience so its expected. (Online quarter)

She is an amazing teacher that seems passionate about what she is teaching. It rubs off and personally I found myself doing research on the ocean outside of class. This is a must take class, but the only thing I would complain about is that the lectures contain a lot of material so prepare to have a sore hand after class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Explains concepts in depth and well. Covers ALOT of info in a short amount of time, so effort is needed for a good grade. Grades on a curve for each exam. Need to actually pay attention in lecture and review slides on your own to get an A/B. No lie, very nerve racking class.

Oceanography 9 is not an easy breadth. There is tons of information you are expected to know. Answer the tophat questions during lecture its an easy grade bump. Her slides 40 % of the time are not self-explanatory, so go to lecture. IMO her exams can be hard b/c they go in depth and sometimes ask arbitrary details. The curve will save you.

Most important advice I will offer is record the lectures. There is a lot of content that is covered & she goes QUICK. Recordings are the best for studying by far in my experience. Course is not easy at all but record+read & youll be fine but being passionate/interested in the ocean helps earn that A+. Shes a knowledgeable & passionate professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Turner is an awesome professor. She's insanely intelligent and she's super passionate. I took Oceanography with her, and I loved going to her lectures. She made the course super interesting. BUT, don't be fooled. This class is WORK. I truly had to grind for my grade. If you're like me, and you don't want to do the reading, get ready to grind.

Tbh, I never listened to her lecture; I just showed up to do the top hat questions (she lets you "discuss" and change your answer) and crammed the night before the midterms and final. You can probably get away with skimming the book and reading her slides over. Make sure you go to discussion section though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Honestly, she is a very sweet person her really cares about her students which is crazy considering how many people are in lecture. There are two midterms and she drops the lowest grade then curves the one she keeps. Really if you just take notes and read the chapters (even if it is the night before the test) you will be fine.
She's a sweetheart. There are 2 midterms and she drops the lowest one. The midterms are also curved. I got a 63% on one of them and still got a B on that midterm.

Oceanography has very interesting material, but its just so much information. You absolutely must attend every lecture and every discussion. also, READ THE TEXTBOOK!!! I messed up the first midterm because I didn't read the corresponding chapters so take it from me, READ!

I should've got a D on a midterm but I got a B.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She's a good person I can tell, but as a professor, she isn't effective and goes way to fast. She puts way too much information on tests and lectures for an intro class. Her tests are hard and the average is around 50% every time. Her quizzes aren't easy too, she drops the lowest 2 quizzes and 1 midterm. Not an easy class and i wouldn't recommend

However, the midterm is all from the powerpoints & the quizzes are online. She drops 2 quizzes and 1 midterm and her curve is ridiculous. I got a D on the final but still an A in the class.

Prof Turner runs through her lectures very fast, almost too fast for everyone to keep up. Plus she crams way too much info into her lectures. She curves the grades because 90% of the class failed the tests. She's not a bad teacher, it's just that she needs some time to become a better one

Hard class for CHASS majors. It's almost as if she teaches this class for CNAS majors and upper-division. The average class grade was about a 40%. THANKFULLY she curves the grades at the end of the class and wound up with a B+ with about a 60%. Not an easy class but you have a curve to bank on. Be prepared for this class if you take it.

She grades on a curve and when you need help she will be there there to guide you through. I got an A+, but I work very hard for it. Everything she says in lecture is possibly going to be in the exam (a large part).
Covered too much material for a breadth course.

The main thing with this class is that you will learn so much more than expected! Many students complain that the class is hard, however, I passed with an A+ by just doing my readings, studying & not skipping class. The class ends up being curved a lot as many students have a failing average on tests. She's also drops your worst midterm & quizzes!

Dr. Kirtland Turner is knowledgeable but in terms of running a class, she could use some improvement.  She goes way too fast and rushes through material even when the class is clearly confused.  She asks lots of trick questions on the midterms and the final is 40 percent of your grade. Try to take a different class if possible

Finals are accumulative and account for 40% of your grade. There are 9 Discussion Quizes and your best 6 scores are averaged and account for 30% of your grade. There are two midterms. However, one gets dropped and the highest graded midterm counts for 25%. Five percent counts as lecture participation via TopHap. Use MindTap resources for quizzes.

If you thought Oceanography would be an easy GE, it's not with this professor. She tries to cram too much material into too little time, and is asked multiple times during lecture to slow down. She is not fun and lacks creativity. The test averages are a D-F range. However, if you go to her office hours with questions, she is helpful.

While its clear that she knows what she's talking about, she does not understand how to teach what so ever. She throws in terms with the expectation that you know what they are, she teaches insanely fast, skips around topics and gives no guidance for the tests. I would not recommend that anyone who has not taken a Chem, Physics or geo class before.

Prof. Turner is effective in identifying what she wants you to know in lecture. You must go to discussion sections to take the weekly quizzes. It's essential to record the lectures as she goes fast, and it doesn't always sink in the 1st time around.
Most students blame the tough course on the professor, but she is actually a great teacher.

Long lectures, talks too fast, tests are extremely in depth compared to what she lectures and have failing averages. Seems nice I guess, but I think the questions she asks us in class and on tests are a little unfair considering what she actually teaches us and asks us to learn beforehand.

her attitude is usually laid back, but don't make her mad! hard grader, but if you go to office hours, she is extremely helpful.
She is a good teacher, and although she grades hard but you know thats the grade you deserved. So I would recommend taking her class shes a cool teacher.
Alright class; little one the boring side.

very organized,chilled,relaxed professor. She is a HARD grader, but if you do all your work and go to her office hours for help you should be fine.
HAREST GRADER!

Professor Kim Turner was a great English teacher. Gives you a syllabus with a play by play of what assignments and tasks you are going to do the whole quarter. A fun class; however, she grade VERY hard!

She is quite funny. She tried to make conversations and relationships with students. She's open-minded and easy to joke around with. Materials were helpful to writing and reading. This teacher is really helpful and funny. Just follow the syllabus and put in work in your essays. She's an extremely hard grader, but I learned a lot.

Fun and Passionate Teacher. Weird at times. First Impression - very chill/relaxed. But a very hard grader and makes you do a lot of work in the class. It is worth it though. Learned a lot in her class. Just follow the syllabus and do your work everyday.

she'll definitely make you work, but it is totally worth it. i learned a lot - she's helpful in class, and always willing to set up office or email help. seems like a lot of work, but it's not too bad if you keep up with her syllabus time lines. amazing class
Amazingly awesome teacher. Makes english incredibly interesting. Hard grader though. Nontheless, take the class.

She seems easy, very easy going, but hard grader. She's good and fast in responding in emails.  I expected a better grade in her class, everyone did. I give her a C+

Good teacher, had a lot of fun in this class. This class is not for people who are squares. If you are, take History of Theoretical Quantum Physics, but for a fun and refreshing class, take hers. Imagination Required.

her class was relatively easy and it was really refreshing to have the fairytale theme in the class... I definitely recommend her to anyone... She'll make you read wicked which is a great book... good course
do not take her unless you want to pass your other classes; she just piles on the work.  she assigned 3 essays all due around the same time; whats with that?
She's very helpful.

Professor is a nice person, but he does lack in explanations in his lectures. The lecture examples and homework's are easy. This professor was kinda woke during the pandemic.

Easy grader. Tests are moderately tough.
He is a very easy going teacher and has open notes for finals Overall, he is one of the finest gentleman that I have had the chance to be taught by.

Be aware, he throws up hard questions in the final

relatively easy class. just show up to class and listen. he gives out the exam questions before hand and on exam day you pick the ones to answer, so prepare well and use that to your advantage. his lectures can be a bit boring but the topics are somewhat interesting. grading all depends on the TAs so go to discussion.

There were only 3 one page summary assignments and discussion attendance is mandatory. Study guides are posted, which are questions that will be on the written midterm and final

I took PHIL001, though that's not an option here. He really has a love for teaching and you can tell that he really enjoys the topic as well. The wording is quite confusing within his lectures, but philosophy is confusing so I guess that is not really his fault. Midterm and final are taken at home and easy if you understand the subject matter. Very interesting class, highly recommended.

reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

Be prepared to READ in this course, scoring high on her essays is almost impossible.

If you want to pass your will have to put in effort.
